title: 8 Ball
text: 8 Ball: 8 Ball (Joker). Effect: 1 in 4 chance for each played 8 to create a Tarot card when scored, (Must have room). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: On Scored. Probability-Based: Yes. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. 8 Ball is a Common Effect Joker that has a 1 in 4 chance to generate a Tarot card whenever an 8 is scored.

title: 8 Ball
text: 8 Ball: Synergies: Compared to other Tarot-generating jokers, 8 Ball is slow to begin with. You would need to draw and play all four 8s in your deck to simply match the expected value of a Cartomancer, and even then, it's not unlikely that you'll whiff every trigger and end up with no Tarots for your effort. However, if you're patient enough to play towards it, you'll find it's one of the most effective Tarot generators in the game. Unlike other Jokers of its kind, an 8 Ball at maximum efficiency can create multiple Tarots per hand without copy effects, outpacing even a Vagabond.

title: 8 Ball
text: 8 Ball: The deck-fixing properties that Tarot cards provide can make it easier to play more 8s and thus recursively create more Tarots. The enhancements can help with scoring as well, making up for the rank's relative lack of scoring Jokers. All of this is especially effective if the player is able to get a Red Seal on one of their 8s and then repeatedly copy it. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World work best with 8 Ball, as the smaller deck size allows for 8s to be played easier. Magic Deck's extra consumable slot is very helpful to hold useful Tarot cards.

title: 8 Ball
text: 8 Ball: Magic Deck's extra consumable slot is very helpful to hold useful Tarot cards. Ghost Deck and Zodiac Deck can potentially benefit from 8 Ball thanks to Spectral and Tarot cards that allow more 8s to be created. Blue Deck gives an extra hand, giving 8 Ball more chances to hit. Poker hands: Pair or Three of a Kind of 8s is good to start. Five of a Kind or Flush Five works well once the player has a lot of 8s. Jokers: DNA can be used to generate more 8s every blind.

title: 8 Ball
text: 8 Ball: Jokers: DNA can be used to generate more 8s every blind. 8s do not have a retrigger Joker associated with their rank. However, Hanging Chad, Dusk and Seltzer (and Sock and Buskin if Pareidolia is owned) can still be used to roll the dice for more Tarots. Hanging Chad is particularly effective, as even if the player is not playing towards 8 Ball, a stray High Card 8 is much more likely to provide value. Oops! All 6s boosts the chances of a Tarot card spawning to 1 in 2. A second copy guarantees a Tarot with every trigger, though this is usually excessive.

title: 8 Ball
text: 8 Ball: The Idol makes for a natural endgame for a good 8 Ball run, should the player fix their deck to consist mainly of 8s. Campfire can also scale faster if the Tarot cards that 8 Ball generates are not needed. Fortune Teller, Driver's License and Vampire can be built around using the Tarot cards that 8 Ball generates. Even Steven and Fibonacci also provide value for 8s. Consumables: Death, Strength and Cryptid can make more 8s. The Hanged Man can remove non-8 cards. Deja Vu can apply Red Seal to 8s, allowing more chances for 8 Ball to generate Tarot cards.

title: 8 Ball
text: 8 Ball: Deja Vu can apply Red Seal to 8s, allowing more chances for 8 Ball to generate Tarot cards. Vouchers: As 8 Ball can generate more than 2 Tarot cards per hand, Crystal Ball is integral to getting the most value out of it. Decks: Nebula Deck's fewer consumable slots makes it harder to hold and use Tarot cards from 8 Ball. Black Deck, Blast Off and Golden Needle do not work well with 8 Ball due to their lower amount of hands, which reduces the chances for 8 Ball to generate Tarot cards.

title: 8 Ball
text: 8 Ball: Jokers: Any Joker that limits the amount of 8s that can be played, such as Half Joker, will also reduce the chances for 8 Ball to generate Tarot cards. Card Modifiers: 8 Ball may prevent the player from maximizing value from Blue Seals, especially when the tarots generate during the last hand and fill up all consumable slots.

title: 8 Ball
text: 8 Ball: Trivia: The visual design of this card is based on the Magic 8 Ball, which itself is based on the 8 ball used in pool or billiards. The user holds the ball with the 8 facing them and asks the Magic 8 Ball a question. They then turn it over, and one of 20 answers (usually a variation on yes, no, or maybe) will appear in a window on the back of the ball. Billiards/Pool is also a common casino game like Poker among various other card games.

title: Abstract Joker
text: Abstract Joker: Abstract Joker (Joker). Effect: +3 Mult for each Joker card, (Currently +0 Mult). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Abstract Joker is a Common Additive Mult Joker that provides +3 Mult for every Joker card currently held, including itself.

title: Abstract Joker
text: Abstract Joker: Decks: Black Deck works well with the Abstract Joker, as it provides +1 Joker slot. Similarly, Five-Card Draw works even better with the Abstract Joker, as it provides +2 Joker slots. Poker hands: This Joker will increase the Mult of all types of hands by the same amount. Jokers: Near the beginning of the game, this Joker works best with Riff-Raff, which creates up to two Jokers per round. It gains additional Mult when using any type of Negative Joker.

title: Abstract Joker
text: Abstract Joker: It gains additional Mult when using any type of Negative Joker. This Joker can have anti-synergy with a lone Joker Stencil, since Abstract requires full slots, and Stencil requires empty ones. However, if there are multiple Joker Stencils, these two jokers can actually work quite well with each other, giving a good multiplicative bonus, which is backed up by the +mult from Abstract. Vouchers: Antimatter gives an additional Joker slot, and with it, the potential for another +3 Mult. Tags: The Negative Tag lets the player hold more Jokers irrespective of current Joker slots, especially if combined with one or more Double Tags.

title: Abstract Joker
text: Abstract Joker: Decks: Painted Deck and Blast Off are difficult to use with the Abstract Joker, as they have one Joker slot less than usual. Similarly, Cruelty is even more difficult to use with the Abstract Joker, as it has two Joker slots less than usual. Jokers: Ceremonial Dagger or Madness should not be used with this Joker, as they both destroy Jokers. Blinds: Verdant Leaf generally requires selling a Joker, meaning that Abstract Joker will lose 3 Mult. Trivia: During the first demo, this Joker only provided +2 Mult per Joker equipped, making it quite weak. It was buffed to +3 Mult per Joker equipped, making it on par with Mystic Summit without the need to use up all Discards.

title: Abstract Joker
text: Abstract Joker: The card design is likely a reference to the Abstract art style. The effect that this Joker gains +3 Mult for every other Joker card in possession could be a reference to an art gallery; the other Jokers would act as paintings in an art museum. Abstract Joker is one of the five Jokers to have a physical card from Balatro: Special Edition. The four other jokers where that is also the case are Joker, Ice Cream, Hack, and Throwback. The name "Jimbo" is written in tiny red letters in the center of the sprite, on the yellow portion below the eye. Abstract Joker appears on a t-shirt product from Playstack that is a special edition signed by LocalThunk.

title: Abstract Joker
text: Abstract Joker: Abstract Joker appears on a t-shirt product from Playstack that is a special edition signed by LocalThunk. In other media: Abstract Joker appeared as a cameo in a crossover collaboration between Balatro and Rusty's Retirement.

title: Acrobat
text: Acrobat: Acrobat (Joker). Effect: X3 Mult on final hand of round. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Play 200 hands. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Acrobat is an Uncommon Multiplicative Mult Joker that provides X3 Mult on the final hand of a round. This means Acrobat will only come into play when the player exhausts all of their available hands against a given Blind. This Joker is unlocked once the player plays 200 hands along all runs.

title: Acrobat
text: Acrobat: Decks: Black Deck reduces the available Hands for the player by -1, making it less punishing for the player to use their final hand. Similarly, Blast Off reduces the available Hands for the player by -2, making it less punishing for the player to use their final hand. Golden Needle reduces the player's Hands to 1, meaning Acrobat is automatically activated.

title: Acrobat
text: Acrobat: Golden Needle reduces the player's Hands to 1, meaning Acrobat is automatically activated. Poker hands: This Joker does not directly synergize with any hand. Strategies that involve winning the round with one high-scoring hand like Four of a Kind or Straight Flush can take advantage of this Joker by playing throwaway hands until the Acrobat is activated. Used like this, the Acrobat is virtually a X3 Mult on the entire round score. Conversely, a strategy revolving around playing multiple easy to make hands does not benefit as much. Jokers: Due to its condition of needing the final hand to be played, Acrobat does have some relevant synergies for other Jokers:

title: Acrobat
text: Acrobat: Dusk retriggers all cards of the final hand, increasing scoring power depending on card Enhancements. In general, any Joker that adds additive Mult will work well alongside Acrobat. Mystic Summit will usually be active alongside Acrobat as long as the player remembers to expend all remaining discards before the final hand. Scaling Jokers that require hands to be played (e.g. Square Joker and Wee Joker) also work well, as hands can be used to scale them before preparing the winning hand for Acrobat. Troubadour's -1 Hand penalty becomes mostly irrelevant as Acrobat only activates on the final hand.

title: Acrobat
text: Acrobat: Troubadour's -1 Hand penalty becomes mostly irrelevant as Acrobat only activates on the final hand. DNA using the first hand of the round is less troublesome if a build relies on the scoring from Acrobat on the final hand. Vouchers: Hieroglyph's -1 Hand penalty is less punishing as the player will need to exhaust all hands to make use of Acrobat regardless. Blinds: The Needle reduces the player's Hands to 1, meaning Acrobat is automatically activated. Decks: Green Deck: As expending all hands is necessary to activate Acrobat, it leaves no additional hands leftover for bonus Money, possibly less if all discards were used as well.

title: Acrobat
text: Acrobat: Jokers: Jokers that decrease in value when playing hands (e.g. Seltzer and Ice Cream) will likely be used up faster, as Acrobat requires the player to exhaust all hands to trigger. Blinds: If Crimson Heart debuffs Acrobat on the final hand, it cannot give its X3 Mult.

title: Acrobat
text: Acrobat: Blinds: If Crimson Heart debuffs Acrobat on the final hand, it cannot give its X3 Mult. Strategies: Acrobat is a useful Joker to have when playing against The Needle Blind, since The Needle will reduce the available hands for the player to only 1, ensuring the X3 Mult from Acrobat will be applied. It is also useful against The Wall and the Violet Vessel, since the player will often go through all of their available hands while trying to overcome the larger score thresholds from those two Blinds, and the X3 Mult may be just enough of a boost to get the player over the finish line.

title: Acrobat
text: Acrobat: Trivia: The acrobats in the artwork could be performing using aerial silks or aerial straps, or perhaps a variation of corde lisse. The lower acrobat seems to be holding an aerial hoop. Quite often performers doing these types of acts will have a 'big finish' trick to finish their performance, represented by the X3 Mult on the last hand. Acrobat's artwork is used for the "Rule Bender" achievement.

title: Ancient Joker
text: Ancient Joker: Ancient Joker (Joker). Effect: Each played card with [suit] gives X1.5 Mult when scored,, suit changes at end of round. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Ancient Joker is a Rare Multiplicative Mult Joker with highly variable power. At the end of each round, a new suit is chosen evenly amongst the 3 suits it is not currently using, regardless of the composition of the current deck. If multiple Ancient Jokers are held, they will all pick the same suit as each other. Each time a card of the current suit is scored, Ancient Joker applies X1.5 Mult.

title: Ancient Joker
text: Ancient Joker: This effect can vary from incredibly powerful to practically irrelevant. Ancient Joker can carry a run into the late Antes, but only if the deck is built specifically to take advantage of its effect. Decks: Black Deck allows for stronger Joker synergies to combine with and build around Ancient Joker and works well to mitigate the fewer hands Black Deck gives. Nebula Deck can level up Flushes very quickly, making Ancient Joker work off of a higher base Mult as well as providing modest Chip scaling.

title: Ancient Joker
text: Ancient Joker: Zodiac Deck allows you to see more Tarot cards, which can create more Wild cards or other strong enhancements, as well as more Jokers, giving more chances to see one that would work well with Ancient Joker. Painted Deck increases your hand size, making it easier to build flushes of the suit Ancient Joker has selected each round.

title: Ancient Joker
text: Ancient Joker: Poker hands: All Flush hands benefit greatly (though inconsistently) from Ancient Joker, since they will trigger its effect the maximum number of times compared to other hands. Unlike other Flush-based builds, it is best to not centralize around one suit, as Ancient Joker will only select it one in three times (1/4th on the first selection). Wild cards add flexibility in triggering Ancient Joker when other suits are chosen. Jokers: Ancient Joker provides good scoring by itself, but this can be significantly increased with the effects of other Jokers. Since Ancient Joker is a "When Scored" effect, retriggering cards will repeat the application of Ancient Joker, such as Dusk, Sock and Buskin, Hack, and Seltzer.

title: Ancient Joker
text: Ancient Joker: Similarly, Jokers that apply additive Mult effects when cards are scored, such as Fibonacci, Even Steven, and Walkie Talkie, can benefit from Ancient Joker. Most notable are other Jokers that trigger X Mult effects, though. Mostly, this will be Photograph, since the others require heavy centralization around suits and ranks, but they will all scale off the effects of retrigger Jokers. The Tribe can work especially well, since the player is ideally always playing Flushes, making it a smaller, consistent bonus.

title: Ancient Joker
text: Ancient Joker: The Tribe can work especially well, since the player is ideally always playing Flushes, making it a smaller, consistent bonus. Ways to level up Flushes are very strong in combination with Ancient Joker. The best ways to do this with Jokers are through Burnt Joker, Space Joker, and Astronomer, though other Jokers can help with planet scaling in other ways, like DNA to duplicate Blue Sealed cards. Smeared Joker makes the effect of Ancient Joker much more consistent to trigger, as well as allowing for easier Flush hands of either suit pair. Consumables: The Lovers works very well, as it makes Wild cards, which always trigger Ancient Joker.

title: Ancient Joker
text: Ancient Joker: Consumables: The Lovers works very well, as it makes Wild cards, which always trigger Ancient Joker. Deja Vu can apply a Red Seal to a card, giving retriggers for Ancient Joker. Trance can apply a Blue Seal to a card, allowing for easy planet scaling. Decks: Checkered Deck should be avoided, as it only has two suits, meaning Ancient Joker will be inactive half of the time. Erratic Deck will rarely have evenly distributed suits, making it harder to use Ancient Joker. Jokers: While Four Fingers can make Flushes easier to play, it enables the player to do so with fewer overall cards, therefore the scoring power of Ancient Joker is weakened if the player opts for a 4-card Flush.

title: Ancient Joker
text: Ancient Joker: It may be suitable to hunt for Planet cards if Four Fingers must remain in conjunction with Ancient Joker. Suit-based Jokers like Rough Gem or Lusty Joker will not get a lot of benefits since Ancient Joker changes the suit each round. Castle can be awkward to use, especially if they both choose the same suit. Additive Mult Jokers that trigger during the Joker scoring step, such as Mystic Summit, cannot benefit from the Multiplicative Mult Ancient Joker gives.

title: Ancient Joker
text: Ancient Joker: Blinds: The Goad, The Head, The Club, and The Window all debuff a specific suit, rendering Ancient Joker useless if it happens to pick the to-be-debuffed suit upon entering the Boss Blind. One trick to avoid this is to check the suit Ancient Joker chose before entering the Big Blind. If it is not the to-be-debuffed suit, skip the Blind to ensure Ancient Joker can be used during the Boss Blind. Consumables: The Sun, The Star, The Moon, and The World can be awkward to use, as Ancient Joker does not care about suit distribution. Sigil can be awkward to use due to the uneven suit distribution.

title: Ancient Joker
text: Ancient Joker: Sigil can be awkward to use due to the uneven suit distribution. Trivia: Unlike Castle, which chooses its suit proportionally to the composition of the current deck, Ancient Joker chooses evenly amongst the 3 suits it is not currently using, regardless of the current deck's composition. The artwork on the card is a reference to OLBAP, a face that Twitch streamer "michaelalfox" (MALF) would often sketch when streaming games that involve drawing. This is confirmed by both Localthunk and michaelalfox.

title: Arrowhead
text: Arrowhead: Arrowhead (Joker). Effect: Played cards with Spade suit give +50 Chips when scored. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Have at least 30 cards with Spade suit in your deck. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Chips. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Arrowhead is an Uncommon Spades-oriented Chips Joker. Arrowhead provides +50 Chips per Spade when scored.

title: Arrowhead
text: Arrowhead: Arrowhead thrives when playing Spade Flushes, providing +250 Chips, and more if any retrigger effects, such as Red Seals, are present. This makes Arrowhead a good reason to opt in to Flushes, although 50 Chips per Spade can supplement any build. Usage notes: Unlocking Arrowhead is easiest on the Checkered Deck, which starts with 26 Spade cards, making it substantially easier to reach 30 Spade cards total. Non-spade Wild cards or Club cards with Smeared Joker do not count towards Arrowhead's unlock condition. Decks: Checkered Deck is the easiest Deck to pair with Arrowhead, since it starts with 26 Spades, allowing the player to play Spade Flushes consistently.

title: Arrowhead
text: Arrowhead: Plasma Deck is arguably the strongest Deck to pair with Arrowhead, as the innate advantage Chips have on it makes Arrowhead's 50 Chips per Spade an immense boon. However, the viability of this playstyle can heavily depend on if the player has already fixed their Deck toward Spade cards. Black Deck appreciates having such a strong Chips Joker, as it frees up slots for more Mult/Effect Jokers. Poker hands: Although a potential source of chips for any hand due to its high output, Arrowhead is strongest with Flush hands. These are: Flush Straight Flush Flush House Flush Five Jokers: Retrigger Jokers can greatly increase Arrowhead's scoring power.

title: Arrowhead
text: Arrowhead: Flush Straight Flush Flush House Flush Five Jokers: Retrigger Jokers can greatly increase Arrowhead's scoring power. Hanging Chad is a relatively easy Joker to pair with Arrowhead on account of being a Common. Other retrigger Jokers include Sock and Buskin, Seltzer, and Dusk, although all of these are conditional, unlike Hanging Chad. Wrathful Joker provides +3 Mult per Spade, giving a small complementary boost to Arrowhead's Chips. Smeared Joker allows Arrowhead to benefit from Club cards, increasing the scope of its usage. Club-based Jokers like Gluttonous Joker and Onyx Agate may be useful in this context.

title: Arrowhead
text: Arrowhead: Club-based Jokers like Gluttonous Joker and Onyx Agate may be useful in this context. Blackboard may be useful with Arrowhead once the player has sufficiently removed enough Hearts and Diamonds from the Deck, allowing its X3 Mult condition to activate consistently. This may be a reason to play hands other than Flush, for the ability to throw away Red-suited cards as non-scoring cards. As a precaution, it may be useful to obtain Luchador (or on rarer occasions, Chicot) to ensure that Arrowhead may function properly against certain Boss Blinds. Card modifiers: Arrowhead works well with Wild cards. This can allow base Heart, Club, and Diamond cards to benefit from Arrowhead.

title: Arrowhead
text: Arrowhead: Mult cards, Lucky cards, and Glass cards also work well due to Arrowhead already providing a substantial amount of Chips. Red Seals can increase the scoring power of Arrowhead, as with all other retrigger effects. Consumables: The World can turn some non-Spade cards into Spade cards allowing the player to see Spade cards easier. The Lovers can turn some non-Spade cards into Wild cards which trigger Arrowhead. Death can turn some non-Spade cards into Spade cards. The Hanged Man can remove some non-Spade cards. Deja Vu can apply Red Seals onto Spade cards allowing for more Arrowhead triggers.

title: Arrowhead
text: Arrowhead: Deja Vu can apply Red Seals onto Spade cards allowing for more Arrowhead triggers. Jokers: Castle as a fellow Chips Joker may be awkward to use alongside Arrowhead, especially if the current suit required for the round is Spades. While Four Fingers can make Flushes easier to play, it enables the player to do so with less overall cards, therefore the scoring power of Arrowhead is weakened if the player opts for a 4-card Spade Flush. It may be suitable to hunt for Planet cards and/or scaling Mult Jokers if Four Fingers must remain in conjunction with Arrowhead. Blinds: The Goad will debuff all Spade cards, meaning Arrowhead cannot activate.

title: Arrowhead
text: Arrowhead: Blinds: The Goad will debuff all Spade cards, meaning Arrowhead cannot activate. The Pillar debuffs previously played cards in the Ante, which may debuff a substantial amount of the player's Spade cards if Arrowhead is essential to the current Joker Build. Trivia: An arrowhead is a rough approximation of the shape of a spade. LocalThunk's artwork is based on an arrowhead he found on a beach, which was eventually donated to a museum. An arrowhead is a symbol of anger, relating this joker to the Wrathful Joker, a Spade-based joker. Arrowhead is one of four stone/mineral-themed jokers unlocked by having 30 of that suit in your deck. The others are Rough Gem (diamonds), Bloodstone (hearts), and Onyx Agate (clubs).

title: Arrowhead
text: Arrowhead: Arrowhead's original design featured a more rounded design, but was scrapped due to being too suggestive.

title: Astronomer
text: Astronomer: Astronomer (Joker). Effect: All Planet cards and Celestial Packs in the shop are free. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Discover every Planet card. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Astronomer is an Uncommon Effect-type Joker that sets the cost of all Planet cards and Celestial Packs to $0, making them free to purchase.

title: Astronomer
text: Astronomer: To unlock this Joker, the player must have discovered every Planet card. This Joker shares an unlock requirement with the Astronomy achievement. Decks: Zodiac Deck works best with Astronomer thanks to the increased Planet card frequency in the shop. Nebula Deck makes Celestial Packs always give a planet card of your most played hand, which may make the free Celestial Packs more useful. Blast Off starts with an Eternal Constellation and Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon vouchers, which Astronomer can help proc the given Constellation, and is doubly helpful with the provided Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon vouchers. Poker hands: Any poker hand can benefit from Astronomer.

title: Astronomer
text: Astronomer: Poker hands: Any poker hand can benefit from Astronomer. Jokers: Constellation: The free planet cards and packs allow players to buff this Joker up very fast. Satellite: The free planet cards and packs allow it to reach its cap faster. Campfire: Buying and selling Planet cards will gain you some money while also scaling Campfire. Red Card: Since Celestial Packs are now completely free, the player can get it scaled up quickly by buying and skipping packs without hurting their economy. Vouchers: Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon make Planet cards appear more often. Telescope guarantees a specific planet in every Celestial Pack, making Astronomer more useful to keep in return.

title: Astronomer
text: Astronomer: Telescope guarantees a specific planet in every Celestial Pack, making Astronomer more useful to keep in return. Overstock, Overstock Plus, Reroll Surplus, and Reroll Glut all allow the player to see more cards (and thus more Planet cards) in the shop. Anti-Synergies: The High Priestess: Although planet cards and Celestial Packs are free, the High Priestess isn't, making the Tarot card less valuable. Strategies: As planet cards still sell for $1, Astronomer can be used to make money by buying and selling all planet cards instead of using them. Trivia: During the first playtest build, Astronomer only provided free Planet cards in the shop. Upon release, it was buffed to provide free planet cards and free Celestial Packs.

title: Astronomer
text: Astronomer: This joker's art is stylised to mimic a Planet card, mirroring Cartomancer, which has comparable unlock requirements to Astronomer and is stylised to mimic a Tarot card. In versions before 0.9.0l-DEMO the background of Planet cards were grey instead of the cyan used since, Astronomer reflected this by also having a grey background.

title: Banner
text: Banner: Banner (Joker). Effect: +30 Chips for each remaining discard. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Banner is a Common Chips Joker that provides +30 Chips for each remaining discard when a hand is played.

title: Banner
text: Banner: Decks: Red Deck's +1 Discard provides more benefits for Banner. Plasma Deck benefits significantly from the large amount of chips Banner provides, which, when balanced, greatly boost the score for the played hand. Green Deck discourages discarding, increasing the amount of Chips that Banner gives. Painted Deck has a larger hand size, which increases the likelihood of drawing a strong Poker Hand without discarding. Five-Card Draw and Golden Needle both start with 6 discards, which means Banner can supply up to 180 Chips if no Discards are used. Poker hands: Playing more common hands like High Card, Pair, Two Pair, or Three of a Kind can reduce the need to discard and thus increase this Joker's effectiveness.

title: Banner
text: Banner: Jokers: Works well with any Jokers that reward you for not discarding, especially Delayed Gratification, Green Joker, and Ramen. Any Joker that increases the number of discards, for example, Drunkard or Merry Andy, will benefit Banner. Though, Merry Andy decreases hand size, which could make it harder to form hands. Jokers that make poker hands easier to make, like Shortcut, Four Fingers, or Smeared Joker, make it easier to assemble a hand without discarding. Jokers that affect hand size, like Juggler, Turtle Bean, and Troubadour, make it significantly easier to form hands without discarding. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy each provide an additional +1 Discard when redeemed, buffing Banner.

title: Banner
text: Banner: Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy each provide an additional +1 Discard when redeemed, buffing Banner. Decks: Black Deck: The -1 hand penalty means players will have to rely on Discards to find winning hands, decreasing Banner's effectiveness. Blast Off is even worse than above, as this deck not only starts with 2 hands, which already encourages the player to rely on Discards to find winning hands, but it also only starts with 2 discards, which means Banner gives fewer Chips than usual. Poker hands: Without heavy deck modifying, strong hands like Flush, Straight, and Full House will be hard to assemble without using Discards. Jokers: Burglar removes all discards, rendering Banner useless.

title: Banner
text: Banner: Jokers: Burglar removes all discards, rendering Banner useless. Any Jokers that incentivize discarding, like Burnt Joker, Castle, Mail-In Rebate, Faceless Joker, and Yorick, will decrease Banner's effectiveness. Banner will never give chips if Mystic Summit is activated, as it requires having no discards remaining. Card modifiers: A card with a Purple Seal needs to be discarded in order to get value from it, which lowers Banner's Chips. Vouchers: Hieroglyph and Petroglyph have anti-synergy with Banner due to their -1 hand and -1 discard punishments, respectively. Blinds: The Water will always start with 0 Discards, making Banner useless. The Needle sets hands to 1 and may force a discard to be used, lowering Banner's chips.

title: Banner
text: Banner: The Needle sets hands to 1 and may force a discard to be used, lowering Banner's chips. Stakes: On Blue Stake and higher, having one less discard means that Banner provides fewer Chips by default. Trivia: Banner is a reference to the banner, a specific type of card in Swiss adapted cards, which is represented as a flag (banner is the German word for flag) and equivalent to rank 10 in common playing cards. Its art also resembles the design of banner cards in Swiss adapted cards. Banner is the only joker to appear on the front of Jumbo Buffoon Packs. At the bottom edge, Banner's flagpole overlaps the white border surrounding the card's background.

title: Baron
text: Baron: Baron (Joker). Effect: Each King held in hand gives X1.5 Mult. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: On Held. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Baron is a Rare Multiplicative Mult Joker that provides X1.5 Mult for each King in the player's hand after playing a hand. Cards that are discarded or debuffed by certain Blinds do not trigger this effect.

title: Baron
text: Baron: Decks: Painted Deck has a larger hand size, making this Joker easier to use. Poker Hands: If the player builds their deck to be mostly Kings, it is best to level up smaller hands such as High Card or Pair to keep as many Kings in hand as possible. Jokers: Mime doubles this card's multiplier per King (to X2.25 Mult per King). Reserved Parking has a 50% chance of giving $1 for each King (or other face card) held in hand. Midas Mask can add a buff to scored Kings, providing an additional benefit thereafter when Kings are held in hand.

title: Baron
text: Baron: Midas Mask can add a buff to scored Kings, providing an additional benefit thereafter when Kings are held in hand. Steel Joker can potentially have synergy with Baron if you're able to make Steel Kings to provide even more XMult. Shoot the Moon makes a great pair with Baron, as the +13 Mult from the Queens will each be multiplied by X1.5 Mult. However, for the Queens to trigger before the Kings, you must physically move the Queens to the left of your Kings. Raised Fist effectively does the same thing. Both of these Jokers' +Mult effects are retriggered by Mime, allowing for double the +Mult before the Baron starts giving XMult

title: Baron
text: Baron: If the player's deck is mostly comprised of Kings, Juggler and/or Troubadour can increase the maximum number of cards held in hand and thus allow Baron to trigger more times. Tarot generating Jokers like Vagabond can help trim your deck using The Hanged Man to draw Kings more reliably, or replicate Kings with Death. The Chariot can also create Steel Kings for more XMult when you hold your Kings in hand, and The Devil can provide Gold Kings, providing economic support whilst using Baron. Trading Card can help reduce your deck size to draw Kings reliably. DNA works very well with baron, as it is able to temporarily increase your hand size when combined with Blueprint and/or Brainstorm.

title: Baron
text: Baron: Consumables: Death and Strength can turn some cards into Kings. The Hanged Man can remove non-King cards. The Chariot can create Steel Kings for more XMult when you hold your Kings in hand. Deja Vu can apply Red Seal to Kings, allowing for more Baron triggers. Cryptid can create more copies of Kings, as well as temporarily increase hand size. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette can permanently increase your hand size, allowing you to hold more Kings. Blinds: The Serpent is by far the most popular boss blind to go against a Baron build thanks to the ability to temporarily increase hand size. With the aid of Burglar and multiple copies of Blueprint/ Brainstorm, it is possible to achieve Naneinf.

title: Baron
text: Baron: Decks: On Abandoned Deck, Medusa, and Mad World, Baron should be avoided, as they do not naturally contain any Kings. Five-Card Draw does not work well with this Joker due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers. Jokers: Merry Andy and Stuntman reduce hand size, which means the player holds fewer Kings. Blinds: The Plant is a run killer; debuffed Kings render Baron completely useless. The Psychic can be a run killer as well—scoring is reliant on playing 5 cards, therefore significantly reducing hand size. The Ox sets your money to zero if you play your most often played hand. This is especially detrimental in deep endless runs, where money is essential.

title: Baron
text: Baron: The Mark draws all face cards face down, making it hard to tell which card is a King. Cerulean Bell may force a King to be played or discarded.

title: Baron
text: Baron: Cerulean Bell may force a King to be played or discarded. Strategies: On first glance, Baron might seem like a small amount of Mult. However, what makes Baron so incredibly strong is that every King or Steel card in hand multiplies your score exponentially. For example, one King only multiplies your score by 1.5x. But two Kings multiplies it by 1.5x twice, which is a 2.25x increase. If an ideal card for Baron is held in hand (a steel King with a red seal), it will produce x1.5⁴ = ~x5.1 Mult. With Mime, this increases to x1.5⁶ = ~x11.4 Mult; with one Blueprint/Brainstorm copying Mime, it increases to x1.5⁸ = ~x25.6 Mult, and with two cards copying each Mime and Baron it rises further to x1.5¹² = ~x130 Mult.

title: Baron
text: Baron: If a player manages to find these four Jokers and enough steel Kings with red seals to fill a hand, they will be able to play far into Endless mode. For example, with a Hand size of eight, the base Mult would be multiplied by ~x619 trillion; with a Hand size of nine this increases to ~80 quadrillion; and with a Hand size of ten it further increases to ~10 quintillion (1.0x10¹⁹). With some base chips and mult, this is enough to finish the first 16 Antes. Using this strategy, players can achieve the elusive Naneinf score, most often on Plasma Deck due to its score balancing mechanic lowering the amount of cards necessary, or on Ghost Deck due to easier access to Spectral cards such as Deja Vu to apply a Red Seal and Cryptid to copy cards, as well as temporarily bypass the hand size limit.

title: Baron
text: Baron: The formula of total x1.5s per card is (x1.5s each trigger) x (total trigger times). Since multiple retriggers stack additively, for each red seal steel King in your hand, the formula becomes (1 steel + number of Baron equivalents) x (1 base + 1 red seal + number of Mime equivalents). If the player can arrange Blueprints/Brainstorms to copy these Jokers, they can reach the best possible score by having 1 more Baron equivalents than Mime equivalents.

title: Baron
text: Baron: For lower antes, Shoot the Moon or Raised Fist are some of the best ways to get mult that scores before your jokers score. However, because cards in hand trigger from left to right, you must physically move your Queens/lowest rank card to the left of your Kings, in order for their mult to be multiplied. Trivia: Baron and Baroness are titles of nobility, usually lower than a king or count, but higher than a knight or lord.

title: Baseball Card
text: Baseball Card: Baseball Card (Joker). Effect: Uncommon Jokers each give X1.5 Mult. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: On Other Jokers. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Baseball Card is a Rare Multiplicative Mult Joker that provides X1.5 Mult for each Uncommon Joker held by the player. The effect is multiplicative. The more Uncommon Jokers that the player holds, the more times Baseball Card will be triggered.

title: Baseball Card
text: Baseball Card: Importantly, Baseball Card does not trigger from a "minimum" rarity requirement of Uncommon; it only triggers specifically from Uncommon Jokers. Rare or Legendary Jokers do not grant the multiplier. Baseball Card's effect triggers after the Uncommon Joker's effect. Therefore, placing +Mult Jokers left of Uncommon Jokers is best to maximize score. Decks: Black Deck's +1 Joker slot is beneficial for Baseball Card, allowing the player to hold an extra Uncommon Joker for an additional X1.5 Mult. Five-Card Draw works very well with Baseball Card, as this deck not only starts with an Uncommon Joker, but it also gives +2 Joker slots, allowing the player to hold two extra Uncommon Jokers for two additional X1.5 Mult.

title: Baseball Card
text: Baseball Card: Ghost Deck has easier access to multiple useful Spectral cards, including Ectoplasm, which can allow the player to take more Uncommon Jokers to scale Baseball Card. Anaglyph Deck's double tags can be used to generate a large amount of Uncommon Jokers in a shop, allowing the player more choices on Uncommon Jokers via the Uncommon Tag, and the Negative Tag can potentially generate Uncommon Jokers without the need for empty Joker slots. Fragile starts with 2 Negative Oops! All 6s, earning the player X2.25 Mult if Baseball Card is acquired. Blast Off starts with Constellation and Rocket, earning the player X2.25 Mult if Baseball Card is acquired, although it also starts with one fewer Joker slot.

title: Baseball Card
text: Baseball Card: 15 Minute City, On a Knife's Edge, Mad World, Medusa, Bram Poker, and Monolith all start with 1 Uncommon Joker, earning the player X1.5 Mult if Baseball Card is acquired. Poker hands: With Uncommon Jokers like Marble Joker and Stone Joker, High Card builds can work well, provided the base Mult has been scaled sufficiently.

title: Baseball Card
text: Baseball Card: Jokers: Baseball Card is a bit of an odd Joker, since its effect is triggered by only Uncommon Jokers. This effect happens after each Uncommon Joker is activated. Any Uncommon Joker is inherently synergistic with Baseball Card (aside from Madness), and having four Uncommon Jokers totals to X5.0625 Mult, a rather large amount, but this restricts you to only using Uncommon Jokers or having more Joker slots. This bonus grows exponentially with more Joker slots, making Baseball Card one of only two Jokers that scale with total Jokers, the other being Abstract Joker. Other XMult Uncommon Jokers work incredibly well with Baseball Card, like Blackboard, Hologram, and Glass Joker. Pairing these with Baseball Card exponentially increases their scoring power.

title: Baseball Card
text: Baseball Card: Uncommon Mult Jokers, such as Spare Trousers, have excellent synergy with Baseball Card, being able to contribute a higher base Mult while also benefitting from Baseball Card. Effect or economy Uncommon Jokers are more useful with Baseball Card, like To the Moon and Rocket, since they usually would have no direct scoring bonus. Retrigger and luck-based builds can use Baseball Card to great effect, since Jokers like Oops! All 6s and Lucky Cat, and most retrigger Jokers are uncommon. Séance and Sixth Sense can generate Ectoplasm, which allows the player to hold more Uncommon Jokers, making Baseball Card stronger. Not only that, but these two Jokers are also Uncommons.

title: Baseball Card
text: Baseball Card: Baseball Card is compatible with Blueprint and Brainstorm. Using a copy Joker will reduce the total amount of Uncommon Jokers but can provide more total XMult. Consumables: Ectoplasm adds Negative to a random Joker, which allows the player to hold more Uncommon Jokers. Vouchers: Antimatter gives +1 Joker slot, allowing the player to hold an extra Uncommon Joker for an additional X1.5 Mult. Boss Blinds: When playing against Crimson Heart, Baseball Card will still trigger on debuffed Uncommon Jokers, as long as Baseball Card is not debuffed itself.

title: Baseball Card
text: Baseball Card: Stakes: On Orange Stake and higher, Uncommon Perishable Jokers that have been debuffed will still be granted XMult by Baseball Card, making it potentially worthwhile to hold onto a Joker even after it perishes. Decks: Painted Deck is difficult to use with Baseball Card due to its -1 Joker slot, which allows fewer Uncommon Jokers to be held at once. Similarly, Cruelty is even more difficult to use with Baseball Card due to the -2 Joker slots, which allows even fewer Uncommon Jokers to be held at once. Trivia: Baseball cards are a type of collectable trading card, with uncommon baseball cards being worth more than common cards. This Joker plays on this theme, with uncommon Jokers granting a bonus.

title: Baseball Card
text: Baseball Card: The signature at the bottom of the card reads "Jim Joker". The exact depiction of the Joker/Jimbo icon/logo on the top right corner of this Joker's art can also be found on Riff-Raff, as well as there being a similar version in the center of Seltzer.

title: Blackboard
text: Blackboard: Blackboard (Joker). Effect: X3 Mult if all cards held in hand are Spades or Clubs. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Blackboard is an Uncommon Multiplicative Mult Joker that provides a large X3 Mult boost when all drawn cards remaining (after playing a hand) are Spades or Clubs. The boost also activates when there are no cards left in hand.

title: Blackboard
text: Blackboard: Any Wild cards will also count as a Spade/ Club. Stone cards have no suit and will prevent the effect from activating if left in hand. Decks: Five-Card Draw works well with Blackboard, as this deck only has a hand size of 5, making it easier to hold Clubs or Spades. Poker hands: Blackboard can potentially work in Flush builds if you can convert the entire deck into Spades and Clubs. However, having one Heart/ Diamond card in hand will make Blackboard useless, making this strategy risky. Blackboard is extremely powerful for High Card and Pair builds. A small hand allows you to play leftover Hearts and Diamonds in your hand and easily trigger Blackboard.

title: Blackboard
text: Blackboard: Modifiers: Wild cards in hand will be treated as a Club or Spade by the Blackboard. With Blackboard, it's more beneficial to add card modifiers that trigger upon holding cards of Spade and Club, as they are more often left in hand: Steel cards can give X1.5 Mult, combining on Blackboard to produce high scores. Gold cards and Blue Seal cards can be held until the end of the round for a bonus. Jokers: Stuntman greatly reduces hand size, significantly increasing the player's chances of their hand containing no Diamond and Heart cards. Similarly, Merry Andy reduces hand size and increases discards, making it easier to hold only Spades or Clubs.

title: Blackboard
text: Blackboard: Similarly, Merry Andy reduces hand size and increases discards, making it easier to hold only Spades or Clubs. Spectrals: Ouija and Ectoplasm have a permanent -1 hand size penalty, making it easier to hold all Spades and Clubs. Blinds: The Manacle reduces hand size, making it easier to hold all Spades and Clubs. The Hook discards 2 cards held in hand, allowing a chance for Blackboard to trigger even if 1 or 2 Diamond or Heart cards are held in hand. Consumables: The Moon and The World can turn some Hearts and Diamonds into Clubs or Spades, allowing Blackboard to trigger easier. The Lovers can turn Hearts or Diamonds into Wild cards, which triggers Blackboard.

title: Blackboard
text: Blackboard: The Lovers can turn Hearts or Diamonds into Wild cards, which triggers Blackboard. The Hanged Man and Death can help remove Hearts and Diamonds, which allows Blackboard to trigger easier. Decks: Painted Deck's +2 hand sizes makes it slightly harder to hold only Clubs or Spades in your hand to trigger Blackboard. Enhancements: Stone cards have no suit and will prevent Blackboard from activating if left in hand. Jokers: Troubadour, Turtle Bean, and Juggler have an anti-synergy with Blackboard, as the increased hand size provided by these Jokers makes it harder to hold only Spades or Clubs in your hand. Notably, Mime will not retrigger Blackboard, despite the ability being "held in hand".

title: Blackboard
text: Blackboard: Notably, Mime will not retrigger Blackboard, despite the ability being "held in hand". Wrathful Joker, Gluttonous Joker, and Seeing Double all rely on playing Spades or Clubs, which can make it harder to hold only Spades/Clubs in hand. Jokers that rely on playing Hearts or Diamonds, such as Lusty Joker and Rough Gem, do not benefit with Blackboard. Flower Pot and Ancient Joker both rely on having all 4 suits together, making a bad combo with Blackboard without a lot of Wild cards.

title: Blackboard
text: Blackboard: Blinds: When playing against debuffing Boss Blinds, debuffed Wild cards revert to their original suit, debuffed Stone cards prevent Blackboard from activating, and debuffed base cards behave as normal. This means that e.g. a debuffed (wild) diamond card will prevent Blackboard from activating. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette have a slight anti-synergy with Blackboard, as the increased hand sizes provided by these vouchers make it harder to hold Clubs or Spades in your hand.

title: Blackboard
text: Blackboard: Trivia: The art is reminiscent of blackboards (sometimes called chalkboards) found in schools and other learning environments, including the piece of chalk used to draw and write on it. Despite the name, they are not always made of black material and can often be found in grey, green, or dark blue. In many situations, they have been replaced with whiteboards (also called dry-erase boards).

title: Bloodstone
text: Bloodstone: Bloodstone (Joker). Effect: 1 in 2 chance for played cards with Heart suit to give X1.5 Mult when scored. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Have at least 30 cards with Heart suit in your deck. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: On Scored. Probability-Based: Yes. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Bloodstone is an Uncommon Hearts-oriented Multiplicative Mult Joker which has a 1 in 2, or a 50% chance to immediately provide X1.5 Mult for each Heart scored.

title: Bloodstone
text: Bloodstone: Usage Notes: Non-heart Wild cards and Diamond cards with Smeared Joker do not count towards Bloodstone's unlock condition. To unlock Bloodstone, Checkered Deck can make it substantially easier to reach 30 Heart cards total, as it already starts with 26 Heart cards. Decks: Checkered Deck is the easiest Deck to pair with Bloodstone, as it starts with 26 Heart cards, which makes playing Heart Flushes consistently an easy task. Blue Deck's extra hand makes it easier to get a winning amount of Bloodstone triggers. Poker hands: Any Flush hand with the Heart suit works with Bloodstone, such as: Flush Straight Flush Flush House Flush Five Although, any 5-card hand that includes 2-3 Heart cards can benefit greatly as well.

title: Bloodstone
text: Bloodstone: Straight Flush Flush House Flush Five Although, any 5-card hand that includes 2-3 Heart cards can benefit greatly as well. Jokers: Lusty Joker also triggers when Hearts are scored, giving the player a small boost scoring power if the Poker Hand's base Mult is not scaled highly, rendering Bloodstone's X1.5 Mult relatively weak. Oops! All 6s is incredibly useful, guaranteeing that this Joker's effect triggers. Because Bloodstone works so well with Oops! All 6s, stacking other chance-based Jokers, like Lucky Cat, Business Card, and Hallucination, can be helpful to maximize the value of Oops! All 6s. Retrigger Jokers are very useful, as they make Bloodstone's inconsistency matter less with more overall triggers.

title: Bloodstone
text: Bloodstone: Retrigger Jokers are very useful, as they make Bloodstone's inconsistency matter less with more overall triggers. Other XMult and +Mult on-score Jokers, like The Idol, Triboulet, Fibonacci, and Even Steven, are very helpful, as they push Mult even higher when combined with Bloodstone's effect and other retrigger Jokers. Smeared Joker allows both Diamonds and Hearts to trigger Bloodstone. Additionally, Smeared Joker allows you to pair Bloodstone with Diamond-oriented Jokers, like Greedy Joker and Rough Gem. When there are multiple Bloodstones (or when copied by Blueprint or Brainstorm), their triggers are calculated separately. This can provide more consistent scoring. Consumables: The Sun can turn some non-Heart cards into Heart cards. The Hanged Man can remove some non-Heart cards.

title: Bloodstone
text: Bloodstone: Consumables: The Sun can turn some non-Heart cards into Heart cards. The Hanged Man can remove some non-Heart cards. Death can turn some cards into Heart cards. The Lovers can turn some non-Heart cards into Wild cards which trigger Bloodstone. Deja Vu can apply a Red Seal to Heart cards allowing more chances for Bloodstone triggers. Decks: Golden Needle makes it very risky to use Bloodstone (unless with Oops! All 6s), as this deck only starts with 1 hand, which means scoring too little at any point will lead to game over.

title: Bloodstone
text: Bloodstone: Jokers: While Four Fingers can make Flushes easier to play, it enables the player to do so with less overall cards, therefore the scoring power of Bloodstone is weakened if the player opts for a 4-card Heart Flush. It may be suitable to hunt for Planet cards and/or scaling Mult Jokers if Four Fingers must remain in conjunction with Bloodstone. Blinds: The Head will debuff all Heart cards, meaning Bloodstone cannot activate. The Pillar debuffs all previously played cards of the Ante, which may debuff a substantial amount of the player's Heart cards if Bloodstone is vital to the current Joker Build.

title: Bloodstone
text: Bloodstone: Trivia: Bloodstone is one of four stone/mineral-themed jokers unlocked by having 30 cards of that suit in your deck. The others are Arrowhead (spades), Rough Gem (diamonds), and Onyx Agate (clubs). A bloodstone (also known as a Heliotrope) is a typically green stone with distinctive red spots resembling drops of blood, hence the name. Bloodstone's design originally sported a large red squiggle in the background, but was changed to the modern pinkish background later on. Bloodstone could be connected to Lusty Joker, with the name relating to the term "bloodlust" or "lust for blood".

title: Bloodstone
text: Bloodstone: Bloodstone could be connected to Lusty Joker, with the name relating to the term "bloodlust" or "lust for blood". Before Update 1.0.1f, this was the only chance-based Joker to have a 1 in 3 chance, and therefore required two Oops! All 6s to have a 100% activation chance. It has since been changed to a 1 in 2 chance of triggering.

title: Blue Joker
text: Blue Joker: Blue Joker (Joker). Effect: +2 Chips for each remaining card in deck, (Currently +104 Chips). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Blue Joker is a Common Chips Joker that adds 2 Chips for every card still in the deck — cards that have not been played/discarded nor are currently held in hand. Its value starts high and decreases as the round continues and cards are drawn.

title: Blue Joker
text: Blue Joker: Decks: Plasma Deck benefits more from the large number of chips Blue Joker provides, which, when balanced, greatly boosts the score for the played hand. Green Deck can encourage saving Hands or Discards, which can keep the Chips from Blue Joker higher during the round. Medusa and Monolith both work well with Blue Joker, as these decks both start with a Marble Joker, which means Blue Joker gains +2 Chips for free each blind. Five-Card Draw's reduced hand size has slight synergy with Blue Joker since fewer cards are drawn to hand, meaning more cards remain in the deck, allowing Blue Joker to stay a bit stronger.

title: Blue Joker
text: Blue Joker: Poker hands: Hands that use fewer cards, are easier to draw, and have fewer base chips benefit more from Blue Joker: High Card Pair Jokers: Blue Joker naturally becomes more powerful as more cards are added to the deck and thus synergizes with Jokers such as: DNA Certificate Marble Joker Hologram Consumables: Familiar, Grim, and Incantation add cards to the deck and thus increase the value from Blue Joker. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World don't work as well with Blue Joker due to their lower total card count.

title: Blue Joker
text: Blue Joker: Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World don't work as well with Blue Joker due to their lower total card count. Fragile doesn't work well with Blue Joker, as the player starts with a 52 card deck full of Glass cards that are guaranteed to break by virtue of having 2 Oops! All 6s upon starting the challenge, which makes Blue Joker quickly fall off in value on this deck. Jokers: Erosion gains Mult for having fewer cards in the deck. Blinds: The Hook discards two random cards every hand played, potentially weakening Blue Joker.

title: Blue Joker
text: Blue Joker: Blinds: The Hook discards two random cards every hand played, potentially weakening Blue Joker. Strategies: While Blue Joker does get stronger the more cards are in the deck and weaker the fewer cards are in the deck, this might not be the best way to think about Blue Joker. Instead, it is best to think about Blue Joker as if it gave +70 Chips on average, as it often gives this amount of chips within a normal deck. From that perspective, Blue Joker is one of the strongest and most reliable chip jokers at common, especially in the early game.

title: Blue Joker
text: Blue Joker: Trivia: Despite being similarly named to the Green Joker, the art for the Blue Joker is completely original rather than being a recolor of the original Joker. The name and colour for Blue Joker may be because Chips are blue. In other media: In Black Mirror, there is a scene in "Hotel Reverie" where a character is seen playing Balatro, and Blue Joker is a card shown onscreen. Joker, Campfire, Sixth Sense, The Empress, and Uranus are shown onscreen as well.

title: Blueprint
text: Blueprint: Blueprint (Joker). Effect: Copies ability of Joker to the right. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Win a run. Buy Price: $10. Sell Price: $5. Type: Effect. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Blueprint is a Rare Effect Joker that copies the effect of the Joker to its immediate right. Not all Jokers are compatible with Blueprint, as Blueprint cannot copy any "passive modifier" effects, but Blueprint itself is compatible. Blueprint's compatibility with other Jokers can be seen under its effect. This Joker is unlocked once the player wins their first run. This Joker shares an unlock requirement with the Heads Up achievement.

title: Blueprint
text: Blueprint: In general, Blueprint will not copy the following effects: Anything that triggers at the end of a round (ex. Golden Joker) Debuffed Jokers Card Edition effects Sticker effects Card destruction (ex. Trading Card) Joker scaling (only the final result is copied) Changes to hands, discards, hand size or hand typing (except for Burglar, which triggers after the blind starts) Passive effects (like Chicot or Pareidolia) See Incompatible Jokers for a full list.

title: Blueprint
text: Blueprint: Passive effects (like Chicot or Pareidolia) See Incompatible Jokers for a full list. Usage Notes: If the player presses "Play Hand", then quickly attempts to move Blueprint to a different position in the joker panel while the hand is scoring, the Blueprint will copy the effect of the joker that it was to the left of before the hand is played. For example, if a player has three jokers, positioned in this way before playing this hand: Blueprint, Greedy Joker, and Fibonacci, then attempted to move the Blueprint to the right of Greedy Joker and to the left of Fibonacci immediately after the "Play Hand" button is triggered, the Blueprint will trigger the effect of Greedy Joker instead of Fibonacci.

title: Blueprint
text: Blueprint: However, the copy order changes once the round is complete. For example, if the player moves your Blueprint to copy Mime while your winning hand is scoring, then the player will receive the benefits of multiple copies of Mime during the end-of-round effects (such as Gold cards or Blue Seal). Players should move all of their copies of Blueprint and Brainstorm onto Mime while their final hand is scoring for maximum Gold card and Blue Seal value. Decks: By its nature, any deck can make effective use of Blueprint. Its effect is highly flexible and can benefit nearly any archetype of deck, aside from Madness without Eternal Stickers.

title: Blueprint
text: Blueprint: Poker Hands: Any hand can benefit from Blueprint in the usual ways. The only hand-specific Jokers that are incompatible with Blueprint are independent effects such as Shortcut. Jokers: Blueprint is an essential Joker and combines well with virtually any other Joker to double its effect. When stacked with Brainstorm or another Blueprint, each will add one more copy of the copied effect. When combining Blueprint with Brainstorm, Blueprint can be placed to the left of Brainstorm or to the left of the leftmost Joker (to be copied), depending on the desired order of Joker activation.

title: Blueprint
text: Blueprint: As a rule of thumb, copying a Joker with X Mult or retrigger is usually better than copying +Chips or +Mult. The optimal placement for maximum score can be difficult to determine, so consider all possible options. When multiple copies are combined with Baron and Mime, while using Plasma Deck, players can achieve the elusive Naneinf score. Copying a Joker that earns $money or creates cards (especially Tarot) is a great option when boosting score is not necessary. When copying chance-based Jokers like Space Joker, the chance is rolled independently for each copy of that Joker. This means if one Joker triggers, the copies are not guaranteed to trigger at the same time.

title: Blueprint
text: Blueprint: A few Jokers have both "trigger" effects that Blueprint can copy and "passive" ones that it cannot. Stuntman, for example, gives +250 Chips, a "trigger" effect, and -2 Hand Size, a "passive" effect. Therefore, Blueprint copies the +250 Chips, but not the -2 Hand Size. If jokers that take effect upon selling them (Luchador and Diet Cola, not including Invisible Joker) get copied, Blueprint can be sold to trigger the effect. However, on mobile devices, dragging Blueprint to sell it could change the order of Jokers, changing its effect.

title: Blueprint
text: Blueprint: However, on mobile devices, dragging Blueprint to sell it could change the order of Jokers, changing its effect. Moving Blueprint can often maximize its potential by always copying the most important Joker for the next action taken. Once a Poker hand is played, Blueprint will continue copying the last Joker to its right, even if it is moved around afterward. For example, one round could involve copying: Hallucination when opening a Booster Pack. Perkeo when exiting the shop Cartomancer or Burglar when starting the Blind Burnt Joker during the first discard DNA during the first hand Business Card during the following hands while playing face cards Mail-In Rebate during the following discards Acrobat during the final hand

title: Blueprint
text: Blueprint: Mail-In Rebate during the following discards Acrobat during the final hand Mime during the calculation of the winning hand, doubling the bonus from Blue Seals and Gold cards at the end of the round Decks: On a Knife's Edge starts with a copy of Ceremonial Dagger pinned in the leftmost position, which means it can't be copied by Blueprint (unless it's copying Brainstorm), limiting it's usage. Incompatible Jokers: There are 29 Jokers that are entirely incompatible with Blueprint:

title: Blueprint
text: Blueprint: Incompatible Jokers: There are 29 Jokers that are entirely incompatible with Blueprint: Blinds: Amber Acorn: This boss blind flips and shuffles Jokers around, which can make Blueprint copy the incorrect Joker, or copy nothing at all if it happens to be moved to the rightmost position or to the left of an incompatible Joker, for at least one hand. Trivia: Certain visuals upon triggering a Joker effect, like the "Level Up!" from a copied Space Joker, have a blue background instead of the standard orange one. At $10 each, Blueprint and its sibling Brainstorm are the most expensive Jokers able to be purchased. (Legendary Jokers would cost $20 if they were ever purchasable.)

title: Blueprint
text: Blueprint: The card art depicts a deliberate, professionally-produced blueprint. This is in contrast with the rough 'back of the napkin' sketching of Brainstorm. The background art used to span the whole card pre-release. The Joker in the art is looking to its left (the right of the card), at the Joker it is copying. If the collection were a set of joker slots, Blueprint would be copying Wee Joker. Blueprint is one of the four jokers that is featured in the official physical playing card deck. The 3 others are Joker, Juggler, and Gros Michel. It was the only Rare Joker to have any physical merchandise before the Vagabond Joker got a Youtooz Collectible figurine from a merchandise collaboration.

title: Bootstraps
text: Bootstraps: Bootstraps (Joker). Effect: +2 Mult for every $5 you have, (Currently +0 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Have at least 2 Polychrome Jokers at the same time. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Bootstraps is an Uncommon Additive Mult Joker that grants +2 Mult for every $5 the player has. It does nothing if the player has $4 or less.

title: Bootstraps
text: Bootstraps: Usage Notes: While Bootstrap's unlock condition may appear difficult to achieve, under the right circumstances it can be surprisingly easy. Ghost Deck starts the player with a Hex, allowing any of the run's first purchased Jokers to become Polychrome. In addition to this, Hex cannot destroy Eternal Jokers, making the requirement even easier on Black Stake and above. As long as the player uses the given Hex on an Eternal Joker, the unlock can be achieved by finding a second Hex in the shop due to Ghost Deck's innate ability. Alternatively, the player can use Ankh or Invisible Joker to duplicate the Polychrome Joker to unlock the requirement.

title: Bootstraps
text: Bootstraps: Alternatively, the player can use Ankh or Invisible Joker to duplicate the Polychrome Joker to unlock the requirement. Decks: Yellow Deck's starting Money bonus makes it easier to build up money quickly. Rich get Richer also encourages the player to have a lot of money, similar to Bootstraps. Blast Off starts with an Eternal Rocket, which allows Bootstraps to get a lot of value pretty quickly. Poker hands: Any hand can benefit from Bootstraps. Jokers: Bull similarly provides a Chips boost for having Money. All Economy Jokers, like Rocket or Golden Ticket help accumulate money quickly. Midas Mask, while not directly being an Economy Joker, can create Gold cards which can then earn money.

title: Bootstraps
text: Bootstraps: Midas Mask, while not directly being an Economy Joker, can create Gold cards which can then earn money. Modifiers: Gold cards give $3 at the end of the round, and can be doubled when combined with Mime. Lucky cards have a 1 in 15 chance to give $20. Retrigger Jokers or Oops! All 6s are recommended. Gold Seal gives $3 when triggered, which is especially useful when combined with retrigger Jokers like Hanging Chad. Consumables: The Hermit can give up to $20. Temperance can also give up to $50 and works very well with Egg or Gift Card. The Devil can make Gold cards which give money at the end of the round.

title: Bootstraps
text: Bootstraps: The Devil can make Gold cards which give money at the end of the round. The Magician can make Lucky cards which have a small chance to give $20. Talisman can apply the Gold Seal to a card, which gives money. Immolate destroys cards and gives $20. Vouchers: Seed Money and Money Tree raise the interest cap, allowing Bootstraps to scale much faster.

title: Bootstraps
text: Bootstraps: Vouchers: Seed Money and Money Tree raise the interest cap, allowing Bootstraps to scale much faster. Tags: Investment Tag, Handy Tag, Garbage Tag, Economy Tag, Speed Tag all give money if the player is willing to skip blinds for them. Investment and Economy though are the best ones for Bootstraps, as Investment will add a hefty +10 Mult to Bootstraps's Mult value once the Boss blind is defeated, and Economy can grant up $40. Decks: Green Deck has poor synergy because it encourages the player to spend money as they earn it. Luxury Tax encourages the player to not have too much money, which can make it harder to use Bootstraps effectively.

title: Bootstraps
text: Bootstraps: Luxury Tax encourages the player to not have too much money, which can make it harder to use Bootstraps effectively. The Omelette, while not being a direct counter, makes it very hard to get money, making Bootstraps weaker. Jokers: Vagabond will never generate any Tarot cards if the player has a lot of money. Credit Card is useless as going into debt makes Bootstraps do nothing. Blinds: The Ox can neutralize Bootstraps if the most played hand is played, resetting money to $0. The Tooth subtracts money for how many cards are played in a given hand, potentially weakening Bootstraps. Consumables: Wraith should not be used as it sets money to $0, making Bootstraps useless.

title: Bootstraps
text: Bootstraps: Consumables: Wraith should not be used as it sets money to $0, making Bootstraps useless. Stake: On Gold Stake, each Rental Joker owned will weaken Bootstraps. Trivia: This might be a reference to the phrase "pulling yourself up by your bootstraps", or to Bootstrap funding. The phrase originally described an impossible task, first used mockingly in an 1834 newspaper. Over time, it evolved to mean self-reliance, despite its ironic origins. As of Update 1.0.1f, having $-5 or less causes Bootstraps to erroneously show negative Mult (eg. +-2 Mult). This is purely visual, as Bootstraps does not do anything while this is in effect.

title: Brainstorm
text: Brainstorm: Brainstorm (Joker). Effect: Copies the ability of leftmost Joker. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Discard a Royal Flush. Buy Price: $10. Sell Price: $5. Type: Effect. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Brainstorm is a Rare Effect Joker that copies the effect of the player's leftmost Joker. Unlike Blueprint, moving Brainstorm around will not change what it copies, only when it does so. To change the Joker that is being copied, a different Joker will need to be moved to the leftmost position. There are some Jokers that cannot be copied, and putting Brainstorm itself in the leftmost position will cause it to do nothing. If Blueprint is in the left-most position, Brainstorm will copy the same joker Blueprint is copying. Brainstorm's compatibility with other Jokers can be seen in its tooltip.

title: Brainstorm
text: Brainstorm: In general, Brainstorm will not copy the following effects: Anything that triggers at the end of a round (ex. Golden Joker) Debuffed Jokers Card Edition effects Sticker effects Card destruction (ex. Trading Card) Joker scaling (only the final result is copied) Changes to hands, discards, hand size or hand typing (except for Burglar, which triggers after the blind starts) Passive effects (like Chicot or Pareidolia) See Incompatible Jokers for a full list.

title: Brainstorm
text: Brainstorm: Passive effects (like Chicot or Pareidolia) See Incompatible Jokers for a full list. Usage Notes: If the player presses "Play Hand", then quickly attempts to change the leftmost Joker while the hand is scoring, then Brainstorm will copy the effect of the leftmost Joker before the hand is played. For example, if a player has three Jokers, positioned in this way before playing this hand: Lusty Joker, Smiley Face, and Brainstorm, then attempting to move the Smiley Face to the leftmost position immediately after the "Play Hand" button is pressed, the Brainstorm will copy the effect of Lusty Joker instead of Smiley Face.

title: Brainstorm
text: Brainstorm: However, the copy order changes once the round is complete. For example, if the player moves Mime to the leftmost position while the player's winning hand is scoring, then the player will receive the benefits of multiple copies of Mime during the end-of-round effects (such as Gold cards or Blue Seal). Players should move all of their copies of Blueprint and Brainstorm onto Mime while their final hand is scoring for maximum Gold card or Blue Seal value. Unlocking Brainstorm can be done easily on either Red Deck, Checkered Deck, or Painted Deck by simply starting a run below Blue Stake and intentionally expending Hands as Discards before drawing a Royal Flush to discard.

title: Brainstorm
text: Brainstorm: Decks: By its nature, any deck can make effective use of Brainstorm. Its effect is highly flexible and can benefit nearly any archetype of deck, aside from Madness without Eternal Stickers. Poker Hands: Any hand can benefit from Brainstorm in the usual ways. The only hand-specific Jokers that are incompatible with Brainstorm are independent effects such as Shortcut. Jokers: Due to the difference in the way it copies a card, and the nature of Jokers triggering left to right, Brainstorm will always be in Blueprint's shadow — by a small amount.

title: Brainstorm
text: Brainstorm: Brainstorm's disadvantage is that xMult Jokers (such as Cavendish) must be placed all the way to the left to be copied by Brainstorm, meaning the player cannot multiply the Mult from +Mult Jokers such as Supernova twice. For example, Supernova + Blueprint + The Trio will score more than The Trio + Supernova + Brainstorm. However, a Polychrome Brainstorm can copy a +Mult Joker to its left while still allowing the full benefit of its edition effect. Some notable targets for copying include Jokers that make money mid-Blind such as Mail-In Rebate, retrigger Jokers such as Dusk, and xMult Jokers that trigger before most +Mult jokers anyways, such as Baron, Photograph or Bloodstone.

title: Brainstorm
text: Brainstorm: When multiple copies are combined with Baron and Mime, usually while using Plasma Deck, players can achieve the elusive Naneinf score. When copying a Blueprint, Brainstorm will copy whichever effect Blueprint is copying, not the Blueprint itself. While it will not work with them, Jokers such as Smeared Joker and Four Fingers can be used to unlock Brainstorm more easily. See the Blueprint page for more general copying strategies. Decks: On a Knife's Edge starts with a copy of Ceremonial Dagger pinned to the leftmost position, which means Brainstorm can only copy that Joker, limiting its usage. Incompatible Jokers: There are 29 Jokers that are entirely incompatible with Brainstorm:

title: Brainstorm
text: Brainstorm: Incompatible Jokers: There are 29 Jokers that are entirely incompatible with Brainstorm: Blinds: Amber Acorn: This Showdown Blind flips and shuffles Jokers around, potentially causing Brainstorm to copy the incorrect Joker, or copy nothing at all if it happens to be moved to the leftmost position or the leftmost Joker is incompatible for at least one hand. However, this can be easily mitigated, by holding the Joker which the player wants to copy in hand, before Amber Acorn starts shuffling. This allows for the player to put the designated Joker in the leftmost position regardless of shuffling, ensuring that Brainstorm copies the right Joker.

title: Brainstorm
text: Brainstorm: Trivia: Certain visuals upon triggering a Joker effect, like the "Level Up!" from a copied Space Joker, have a red background instead of the standard orange one. At $10 each, Brainstorm and its sibling Blueprint are the most expensive Jokers able to be purchased since the Legendary Jokers are never purchasable. On the artwork, the leftmost bauble on the hat, the leftmost eye, and the leftmost bauble on the bottom are highlighted in some way, referencing how Brainstorm copies the leftmost Joker.

title: Brainstorm
text: Brainstorm: The card art depicts a messy "back of the napkin" sketch, a rough calculation or idea quickly sketched out during a conversation at a bar or restaurant, which could be seen as the conception of the Joker being copied. This also reflects its limitations compared to the more versatile Blueprint, which depicts a more deliberate and detailed technical drawing. This is the only Joker that has a 90-degree corner (top left) in its card art, as all other Jokers have a rounded radius in all their corners. According to LocalThunk, this represents the unfolded corner of the napkin. If the collection were a set of joker slots, Brainstorm would be copying Stuntman.

title: Brainstorm
text: Brainstorm: If the collection were a set of joker slots, Brainstorm would be copying Stuntman. The texture of this Joker has protruding areas on the right and down sides, slightly exceeding the boundaries of a standard Joker. This may represent the ragged edge of the napkin after being torn off. The other Joker with this similar property is Hallucination. Brainstorm appears on the artwork of the Mega Buffoon Pack.

title: Bull
text: Bull: Bull (Joker). Effect: +2 Chips for each $1 you have, (Currently +0 Chips). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Chips. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Bull is an Uncommon Chips Joker that grants +2 Chips for every $1 the player has. It does nothing if the player has $0 or less.

title: Bull
text: Bull: Decks: Yellow Deck starts the player off with $14, giving Bull a boost not granted by any other Deck. Plasma Deck focuses more on Chips than Mult, meaning that Bull can become a strong Joker even into the late-game assuming the player doesn't spend too much money. Blast Off starts with an Eternal Rocket, which allows Bull to get a lot of value pretty quickly. Poker hands: Bull's bonus chips work well with any Hand, but it might be easier to start with high Mult Hands such as Full House. Jokers: Bootstraps similarly provides a Mult boost for having money. All Economy Jokers, like Rocket or Golden Ticket help accumulate money quickly.

title: Bull
text: Bull: All Economy Jokers, like Rocket or Golden Ticket help accumulate money quickly. Midas Mask, while not directly being an Economy Joker, can create Gold cards which can then earn money. Modifiers: Gold cards give $3 at the end of the round, and can be doubled when combined with Mime. Lucky cards have a 1 in 15 chance to give $20. Retrigger Jokers or Oops! All 6s are recommended. Gold Seal gives $3 when triggered, which is especially useful when combined with retrigger Jokers like Hanging Chad. Consumables: The Hermit can give up to $20. Temperance can also give up to $50 and works very well with Egg or Gift Card.

title: Bull
text: Bull: Temperance can also give up to $50 and works very well with Egg or Gift Card. The Devil can make Gold cards which give money at the end of the round. The Magician can make Lucky cards which have a small chance to give $20. Talisman can apply the Gold Seal to a card, which gives money. Immolate destroys cards and gives $20. Vouchers: Seed Money and Money Tree raise the interest cap, allowing Bull to scale much faster.

text: Bull: Vouchers: Seed Money and Money Tree raise the interest cap, allowing Bull to scale much faster. Tags: Investment Tag, Handy Tag, Garbage Tag, Economy Tag, Speed Tag all give money if the player is willing to skip blinds for them. Investment and Economy though are the best ones for Bull, as Investment will add a hefty +50 Chips to Bull's Chips value once the Boss blind is defeated, and Economy can grant up $40. Decks: In Rich get Richer, Bull gives fewer chips than usual due to the cap on Chips, although it does always ensure Chips are maximised. Green Deck has poor synergy because it encourages the player to spend money as they earn it.

title: Bull
text: Bull: Green Deck has poor synergy because it encourages the player to spend money as they earn it. Luxury Tax encourages the player to not have too much money, which can make it harder to use Bull effectively. The Omelette, while not being a direct counter, makes it very hard to get money, making Bull weaker. Jokers: Vagabond will never generate any Tarot cards if the player has a lot of money. Credit Card is useless as going into debt makes Bull do nothing. Blinds: The Ox can neutralize Bull if the most played hand is played, resetting money to $0. The Tooth subtracts money for how many cards are played in a given hand, potentially weakening Bull.

title: Bull
text: Bull: The Tooth subtracts money for how many cards are played in a given hand, potentially weakening Bull. Consumables: Wraith should not be used as it sets money to $0, making Bull useless. Stake: On Gold Stake, each Rental Joker owned will weaken Bull. Trivia: This Joker is most likely a reference to a bull market, which is a stock market trend where stock prices tend to rise for an extended period of time.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: Burglar (Joker). Effect: When Blind is selected, gain +3 Hands and lose all discards. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: On Blind Select. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Burglar is an Uncommon Effect Joker that gives 3 extra hands in exchange for all of the player's discard(s), doubling up as money generation if the player defeats the blind in 3 hands or less.
