Do note that it will always give 3 hands no matter the amount of discards the player has.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: Usage Notes: Unlike other jokers related to hands and discards (such as Merry Andy), the effect of Burglar triggers when selecting the Blind. This means that if Burglar gets disabled during a round (by Crimson Heart) or sold during a round, the hands and discards will not be changed. In other words, the player will still have 0 discards and get to keep the 3 extra hands for the rest of the round. Since Ceremonial Dagger destroys the Jokers on the right side, Burglar would be destroyed before taking effect. For Madness, the order of Burglar and Madness does not matter, as Burglar always activates before Madness. The Blast Off and Golden Needle Challenge Decks both ban Burglar.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: The Blast Off and Golden Needle Challenge Decks both ban Burglar. Decks: Green Deck: As leftover hands and discards act as a pseudo-Interest, Burglar essentially trades $1 from each removed discard for $2 for each of the 3 extra hands. Black Deck: Burglar mitigates the -1 Hand downside while also adding 2 extra hands, but removes all discards. Poker Hands: Burglar's extra hands make use of poker hands that can be played at a high frequency, such as High Card, Pair, or Two Pair. On a deck that concentrates on one specific rank, this can also be Three of a Kind, Five of a Kind, or Flush Five.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: Jokers: Ride the Bus, Green Joker, Square Joker, Spare Trousers, or Supernova all scale from playing hands, which is made way easier thanks to Burglar. Burglar removing all discards allows Mystic Summit to always trigger its +15 Mult effect. Burglar, unlike its discard counterpart Merry Andy, can be copied by Blueprint/ Brainstorm for an extra 3 hands each copy. This effect also poses no downside because of how the copying effects can be used on another Joker afterwards without any consequences.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: Additionally, because of how Burglar triggers when blind is selected, the player can abuse this by setting the game speed down and swapping Burglar with other Jokers that also trigger at the start of round, such as Marble Joker or Certificate for Blueprint/ Brainstorm to copy after Burglar has done its job. Note that while the game speed being slower makes this trick much easier, it still requires decent concentration and reflexes. Vagabond can generate more Tarot cards if the added hands are used. Card Sharp can get more triggers thanks to the fact that more hands can be played, therefore increasing the chance of the poker hand being played twice or more.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: Loyalty Card (almost) always guarantees a trigger every round. The aforementioned Green Joker and Ramen can no longer be reduced since there are no discards to be used, except during The Hook's forced discard effect. Blinds: Burglar neutralizes the following Boss blinds remarkably well: The Needle (Play only 1 hand): Burglar only triggers after The Needle has taken effect, which lets the player gain 3 extra hands at the expense of all discards. The Water (Start with 0 discards): The Water functionally does nothing as Burglar already covers its effect, making it a glorified Small Blind with a higher score requirement.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: Verdant Leaf (All playing cards debuffed until 1 Joker sold): On Ante 8 runs, selling this Joker to remove this Blind's debuff does nothing to hurt your build since its effect only goes away when the next Blind is selected. Tags: Handy Tag will give extra money. Stakes: On Blue Stake and above, the -1 discard effect can safely be ignored when using Burglar. Vouchers: Burglar can mitigate Hieroglyph's -1 hand penalty, and Petroglyph's -1 discard penalty can safely be ignored when using Burglar. Decks: Red Deck and Five-Card Draw: The extra discards provided by them are negated when a blind is selected. Jokers: Any Joker that triggers off of discards like Banner and Delayed Gratification will have no effect.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: Jokers: Any Joker that triggers off of discards like Banner and Delayed Gratification will have no effect. Jokers that need cards to be discarded to scale, like Yorick and Castle, can no longer scale. Jokers that give extra discards like Drunkard and Merry Andy will have no effect. The Merry Andy, in particular, with the Burglar, will only decrease hand size by 1. Jokers that activate on discard, like Mail-In Rebate, Trading Card, and Burnt Joker, can no longer function. Jokers that decrease in value when playing hands like Seltzer and Ice Cream will likely be used up faster.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: Jokers that decrease in value when playing hands like Seltzer and Ice Cream will likely be used up faster. Jokers that activate on the final hand, such as Acrobat and Dusk. Given that Burglar provides more hands, it would delay the chances for these jokers to come into effect. DNA and Sixth Sense may have anti-synergy with Burglar if the first hand does not have the wanted card to be played. This is especially bad with a small hand size. Card modifiers: Purple Seal will no longer function. Tags: Garbage Tag's money no longer increases. Blinds: Some bosses affect the player in such a way that makes not having discards highly detrimental, crippling the run's potential by a wide margin:

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: The Hook's forced discard effect makes building specific poker hands significantly harder if the played hands are also throwaway hands. Using a high amount of hands on this Boss blind, with or without a small deck, can lead to an instant game over when the playing deck runs out of cards. The Mouth: The player is locked into only playing the poker hands that can be formed from the starting hand. If there are no ways of altering the playing cards first drawn, like Death or Strength, this may be a dead end on builds that only function when playing a specific poker hand.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: The Fish: After drawing the starting cards, all playing cards will be drawn face down, effectively making the player fight while blind. The Tooth: Since the player will often play throwaway hands as pseudo-discards, this Boss blind can potentially be a deficit of $3 - 15. As mentioned earlier, the effect of Burglar on the current round cannot be undone by selling it. Therefore, any method that can avoid specific Boss Blinds (e.g., Luchador, Chicot, or Director's Cut) should be considered. Otherwise, Burglar should be sold before choosing the Boss Blind if it would be difficult to deal with. Vouchers: The +1 discard effect given by Wasteful and Recyclomancy is negated when a blind is selected.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: Vouchers: The +1 discard effect given by Wasteful and Recyclomancy is negated when a blind is selected. Strategies: Burglar allows Jokers that scale off of played hands to scale much faster, such as Ride the Bus, Green Joker, Square Joker, Spare Trousers, or Supernova. Burglar lets the player generate much more resources with Jokers that generate value off of played hands, such as Reserved Parking, Space Joker, or Vagabond. A build capable of scoring the elusive Naneinf score typically consists of playing on the Plasma Deck while on the Boss Blind The Serpent, after copying Burglar with Blueprint and Brainstorm, and holding both Baron and Mime.

title: Burglar
text: Burglar: Trivia: The Burglar wears the classic black-and-white stripes of an American prison uniform, first introduced in the New York prison system in the 1820s. This suggests the Burglar is also currently an inmate of a jail or perhaps an escapee.

title: Burnt Joker
text: Burnt Joker: Burnt Joker (Joker). Effect: Upgrade the level of the first discarded poker hand each round. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Sell 50 cards. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Effect. Activation: On Discard. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Burnt Joker is a Rare Effect Joker that upgrades the level of the first discarded Poker Hand each round.

title: Burnt Joker
text: Burnt Joker: Usage notes: Burnt Joker can be triggered as normal by debuffed cards. The Hook's forced discards will not activate Burnt Joker. Decks: Red Deck - The +1 discard makes the Burnt Joker have less of a downside. Checkered Deck - Only having two suits makes it significantly more likely to have a Flush in hand at all times. Abandoned Deck - The lack of face cards makes it easier to find certain hands for Burnt Joker to discard without using a lot of hands. Poker hands: Simple hands such as Pairs or High Cards are more likely to naturally occur, thus making them easier to discard and level up.

title: Burnt Joker
text: Burnt Joker: Jokers: Blueprint or Brainstorm - Synergizes incredibly well, as after the desired hand is discarded it can be moved to copy a different Joker before a hand is played. Drunkard and Merry Andy increase the number of Discards, making the first Discard for Burnt Joker inconsequential. Jokers that make a particular hand easier to produce, such as Four Fingers, Shortcut, and Smeared Joker, can make it easier to discard their related hands, especially if you then want to be able to play the same hand immediately afterwards; Four Fingers and Shortcut also allow you to hit the relevant hand when discarding fewer cards, for situations when there are cards in your hand you want to keep.

title: Burnt Joker
text: Burnt Joker: Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy both increase discards, making the first discards for Burnt Joker inconsequential. Decks: Painted Deck starts with -1 Joker Slot, which makes it harder to carry Burnt Joker alongside other scoring Jokers, though its bigger hand size makes it easier to find the hand to discard. Similarly, Cruelty is even more difficult to carry Burnt Joker alongside other scoring Jokers due to the -2 Joker Slots. Blast Off not only starts with one less Joker Slot, but also starts with 2 discards, making Burnt Joker more committal to utilize. Poker hands: Five-card hands that are hard to draw naturally like Straight, Full House, Straight Flush can make it hard to benefit from Burnt Joker.

title: Burnt Joker
text: Burnt Joker: Jokers: Jokers that discourage Discarding such as Green Joker, Delayed Gratification or Ramen can make it harder to benefit from Burnt Joker. Burglar removes all Discards, nullifying Burnt Joker. May or may not have anti-synergy with Trading Card since this Joker requires discarding a single card to benefit and thus can only level-up High Card. Stakes: Blue Stake and above removes a discard, making Burnt Joker more committal to utilize. Blinds: The Water will always set your discards to 0.

title: Burnt Joker
text: Burnt Joker: Blinds: The Water will always set your discards to 0. Trivia: In early demo versions, the effect of Burnt Joker was "gains +1 hand size per 4 tarot/planet cards sold". This is still reflected by the unlock requirement being related to selling cards, and in the 1.0.1o version of the game, Burnt Joker still gives +0 hand size internally. Space Joker is similar, but it may provide an upgrade for playing hands instead of discarding them. Unlike Trading Card, Burnt Joker does not shake even if a discard was not used yet.

title: Business Card
text: Business Card: Business Card (Joker). Effect: Played face cards have a 1 in 2 chance to give $2 when scored. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Economy. Activation: On Scored. Probability-Based: Yes. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Business Card is a Common Economy Joker that can reward the player financially for playing face cards, with a 1 in 2 chance to earn $2 every time a face card is scored.

title: Business Card
text: Business Card: Usage notes: The Mad World challenge starts the player with an Eternal copy of Business Card.

title: Business Card
text: Business Card: Usage notes: The Mad World challenge starts the player with an Eternal copy of Business Card. Poker hands: Business Card wants you to play many face cards all at once. Therefore, the best hands you could play with this are ones that have the most face cards in them (preferably 5). Full House is the easiest to access early on and can be fairly consistent. Later on in the game, Four of a Kind or Five of a Kind hands can give just as much of a chance for money but can often score higher as long as your Full House isn't upgraded as much. Later in the game you can also access Flush House and Flush Five for an even bigger increase in score.

title: Business Card
text: Business Card: Jokers: Pareidolia enables Business Card to pay out on any played card. Oops! All 6s guarantees payout from Business Card. Retrigger jokers that affect face cards, such as Sock and Buskin or Seltzer, allow Business Card to pay out more than once. Splash allows Business Card to affect all face cards played by making them all score. Midas Mask's ability turns all face cards gold, resulting in more income. Other jokers that increase the scoring of played face cards (e.g. Scary Face for + Chips, Smiley Face for + Mult, and Triboulet for XMult) provide additional benefit when face cards are played.

title: Business Card
text: Business Card: Reserved Parking provides income on unplayed face cards, so having both this Joker and Business Card in a face card focused deck can provide a steady stream of money.

title: Business Card
text: Business Card: Consumables and card modifiers: Adding more face cards to your deck can be helpful when using this joker. Therefore, cards like Cryptid or Death, can copy your face cards and their enhancements to make a much stronger and more consistent deck. Death can also be used as a way to "remove" a non-face card by changing it into a face card. The Hanged Man is also useful for removing any non-face cards from your deck and slimming your deck to make it more consistent. Familiar also works to add more enhanced face cards to your deck as well as potentially remove non-face cards.

title: Business Card
text: Business Card: The best way to get new face cards from the shop is likely going to be through Standard Packs. A Red Seal works quite well with Business Card as any face card with a red seal on it will trigger itself twice when played, enabling it to have another chance at triggering Business Card for more money. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Medusa start with no face cards, making Business Card pretty much useless unless the player has Pareidolia. Jokers: Ride the Bus requires face cards to not be played in order to grow its Mult bonus. Canio's ability activates only upon destroying face cards, resulting in fewer cards able to trigger Business Card.

title: Business Card
text: Business Card: Canio's ability activates only upon destroying face cards, resulting in fewer cards able to trigger Business Card. Blinds: The Mark draws all face cards face down, making it more difficult to assemble a good hand for Business Card. The Plant debuffs all face cards, rendering Business Card useless for the round. Trivia: Business cards often show the name, contact details, and other information of the person handing them out. They may even include imagery, watermarks or QR codes. In some industries, the quality and style of an individual's business card directly impact the perception of the said person among colleagues and peers, as can be seen in this (slightly exaggerated) scene from the film American Psycho.

title: Business Card
text: Business Card: This Joker has a smaller width than standard Joker cards when face up. However, when it is flipped face-down, it uses the same standard size of card back as the rest. The other Joker with this similar property is Golden Ticket. This may be a reference to the fact that the standard size of business cards (2 × 3.5 inches) is smaller than that of playing cards (2.5 × 3.5 inches).

title: Campfire
text: Campfire: Campfire (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains X0.25 Mult for each card sold, resets when Boss Blind is defeated, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $9. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Campfire is a Rare scaling Multiplicative Mult Joker that gains X0.25 Mult per sold card, which can theoretically be scaled infinitely. However, it resets itself to X1 Mult after defeating a Boss Blind.

title: Campfire
text: Campfire: Selling any Joker or consumable (Tarot, Planet, or Spectral card) will add X0.25 Mult to Campfire's bonus. They must be deliberately sold—destroying them through use of other cards (such as Hex or by the effect of Ceremonial Dagger) does not count. Note that unlike most non-retroactive positively scaling jokers, Campfire can be Perishable, likely due to the fact that it will reset at least once before it perishes. Decks: Zodiac Deck starts you with the Tarot Merchant and Planet Merchant Vouchers, which make consumable cards appear more often, and the Overstock Voucher, which makes more cards appear in the shop. This combines to provide a vast amount of cards you can sell every shop.

title: Campfire
text: Campfire: Yellow Deck lets you build money much faster, which is needed to scale Campfire. Black Deck's extra Joker slot lets you have five Jokers while still having room to buy and sell with the final slot. Poker hands: Since Campfire provides a strong XMult bonus, any Poker Hand with a high base Mult like Flush, Straight, Full House, will benefit greatly. Jokers: The cornerstone of Campfire's functioning is economy. It is best paired with at least one money-generating Joker, the more powerful the better. It doesn't necessarily need this, though, if it is added late-game when you already have a large amount of money.

title: Campfire
text: Campfire: Jokers that generate other cards, like Cartomancer, Riff-Raff and Perkeo, can then have those cards be sold for extra scaling. A strong source of + Mult is near required to make Campfire work. The single best Joker for this is Flash Card, as you will want to be rerolling anyway to find more cards to sell, but other strong options include Onyx Agate and Spare Trousers. Astronomer allows you to buy planet cards for free and sell them for a profit, which allows for more buying and selling of other cards. Chaos the Clown gives you a free reroll in every shop, allowing you to buy more consumables.

title: Campfire
text: Campfire: Chaos the Clown gives you a free reroll in every shop, allowing you to buy more consumables. Diet Cola, Luchador and Invisible Joker are intended to be sold in the first place, as (to a lesser extent) is Egg, making them easily combo with Campfire. Invisible Joker works pretty well if it copies Campfire, since selling the Invisible Joker will not only scale the first copy, but also the second one at the same time. With careful planning, Gift Card can recover some of the cost of buying all those items to feed to the fire. Notably, due to Credit Card's low cost, it can be bought and then immediately sold to scale Campfire with no economic downside.

title: Campfire
text: Campfire: Consumables: All consumables will work with campfire, however The Emperor and The High Priestess work particularly well, since they both create 2 cards to sell. Vouchers: Clearance Sale and Liquidation make it cheaper to constantly buy and sell cards, the latter reducing the purchase and sell value of all consumables to 1 and effectively allowing you to scale Campfire for free. Overstock and Overstock Plus make more cards appear in the shop to buy and sell. Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut make it cheaper to reroll to find more cards to sell. Tarot Merchant, Planet Merchant, Tarot Tycoon and Planet Tycoon make Tarot and Planet cards appear in shop more frequently, allowing repeated buying & selling them.

title: Campfire
text: Campfire: Crystal Ball provides +1 Consumable Slot, which allows the player to hold 2 Consumables while still having a room to sell. Antimatter provides +1 Joker Slot, which allows the player to hold 5 Jokers while still having a room to sell. Blinds: If Crimson Heart disables Campfire on the last hand the player needs to win, Campfire will not reset, allowing it to be scaled for another Ante. Modifiers: Purple Seal can generate some Tarot cards which can be sold if they are not necessary. Blue Seal can generate some Planet cards at the end of the round, allowing Campfire to scale faster.

title: Campfire
text: Campfire: Blue Seal can generate some Planet cards at the end of the round, allowing Campfire to scale faster. Stakes: On Gold Stake buying a Rental Joker and selling it immediately thereafter allows you to scale Campfire with no economic downside. Decks: Painted Deck's -1 Joker Slot and Nebula Deck's -1 Consumable Slot can make it harder to have a room for Jokers to sell and hold onto Consumables to sell, respectively, to increase its effectiveness between antes. This also applies to Blast Off and Cruelty. Ghost Deck allows for Spectral cards to appear in the shop, but they're more expensive than Tarots or Planets, and selling them is not always something the player would want to do.

title: Campfire
text: Campfire: Jokers: Fortune Teller and Constellation encourage the player to use Tarot cards and Planet cards, respectively, which is the opposite of what Campfire does. Throwback and Diet Cola rely on skipping blinds, which results in Campfire being reset faster. Trivia: Like a real campfire, this Joker needs a continuous source of fuel to keep burning brightly. This Joker's art also references how the selling animation looks like the sold card is burning. Campfire is the only Joker with a buy price of $9. In other media: In Black Mirror, there is a scene in "Hotel Reverie" where a character is seen playing Balatro, and Campfire is a card shown onscreen.

title: Campfire
text: Campfire: Joker, Blue Joker, Sixth Sense, The Empress, and Uranus are shown onscreen as well.

title: Canio
text: Canio: Canio (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains X1 Mult when a face card is destroyed, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Legendary. Unlock Requirement: Find this Joker from the Soul card. Buy Price: 20 (cannot be found in shop). Sell Price: $10. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Canio is one of the five Legendary Jokers that can be generated from using The Soul Spectral card, which in itself has a 3 in 1000 (0.3%) chance to replace any given card in a Spectral Pack or an Arcana Pack.

title: Canio
text: Canio: Canio starts at X1 Mult and gains an extra X1 Mult whenever a face card is destroyed. This makes Canio perhaps one of, if not the best, multiplicative Mult Joker, as scaling by X2 Mult with just a single use of The Hanged Man is unfathomably powerful, and utilizing different Jokers as well as consumables can let it reach X10 Mult and higher quite easily, sometimes even pushing the boundaries at X25 Mult or X50 Mult, potentially even higher.

title: Canio
text: Canio: Synergies: Canio gives multiplicative Mult to all hands once at least 1 face card is destroyed. Because of its run-winning potency, the player should try to build into Canio whenever possible. However, with builds relying on face cards, destroying them for Canio might drastically affect the run's safety. Balancing destroying face cards for Canio and not succumbing to the temptation of scaling it is the key to winning a run with Canio.

title: Canio
text: Canio: Decks: Most decks can benefit greatly from Canio, as they all have face cards. Although, it is noteworthy that some decks grant easier access to Tarot cards, which includes The Hanged Man, making it an important factor to consider when the goal of the run is obtaining and maximizing Canio. The Ghost Deck grants easier access to the otherwise hard to find Spectral cards via The Shop, in which 4 of them can help Canio scale by destroying playing cards, those being Familiar, Grim, Incantation, and Immolate. 15 Minute City starts with 24 face cards, allowing this Joker to scale easier.

title: Canio
text: Canio: 15 Minute City starts with 24 face cards, allowing this Joker to scale easier. Mad World starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which allows this Joker to scale easier, but be wary not to destroy too many cards due to the small size of this deck. Poker hands: Because of how Canio provides a strong source of multiplicative Mult, poker hands that have a higher base Mult and scaling tend to work better with it. The player may want to keep one or two Chips Jokers around though, to compensate for the lower Chips count numbered cards offer.

title: Canio
text: Canio: Jokers: Pareidolia: Because every playing card now counts as a face card, Canio gains X1 Mult when any playing card is destroyed. This allows the player to choose which ranks to destroy and which ranks to keep. Trading Card: By sacrificing a discard every round to destroy a face card, Canio can gain Mult at a much more consistent rate. Erosion: This Joker and Canio is a reasonably strong combo due to the fact that focusing on destroying face cards often leads to a smaller deck than the starting size, which boosts Erosion by +4 Mult for every playing card below that starting amount.

title: Canio
text: Canio: Glass Joker: Due to the fact that Glass cards can destroy themselves when scored, Canio pairs amazingly well with Glass Joker, which gains X0.75 Mult when a Glass card is destroyed. Whenever a Glass face card is destroyed, both Jokers will scale. Due to a bug, when Glass cards are destroyed by Spectral cards, Glass Joker will not scale, so it is recommended for the player to try and find Oops! All 6s or The Hanged Man when using this combination. DNA can create a copy of a face card, allowing the player to destroy more face cards.

title: Canio
text: Canio: DNA can create a copy of a face card, allowing the player to destroy more face cards. Any Joker that creates Tarot cards will enable two crucial things for strengthening Canio: firstly, easier access to either Justice to enhance face cards into Glass cards or The Hanged Man to destroy face cards, and secondly, holding unwanted Tarot cards in the consumable slots to increase the chances that the aforementioned two will appear in Booster Packs; among them, Cartomancer and Vagabond are the easiest to activate and gain large amounts of Tarot cards from. The Legendary Joker Perkeo can make the Justice and The Hanged Man even more common by duplicating them every round.

title: Canio
text: Canio: Sixth Sense can also work with Canio, but only if the player has Pareidolia. Consumables: Any card destruction effects can boost Canio, including Glass cards. As such, the following consumables are useful for scaling Canio: Tarot cards: The Hanged Man can be used to destroy face cards. Justice can enhance face cards into Glass cards, which have a 1 in 4 chance to be destroyed after scoring. Death, Strength, and The Tower do not count as destroying face cards when used, since the original face card is not actually destroyed. The former two, however, can be used to create more face cards to be destroyed. Spectral cards:

title: Canio
text: Canio: Spectral cards: Familiar has a chance to destroy a random face card and adds 3 additional face cards to the deck for the player to destroy. Immolate can destroy up to 5 face cards in hand while also giving an immediate burst of money that can be spent to further enhance the quality of the deck. Grim and Incantation both have a chance to destroy a random face card. Ouija is capable of converting a large number of playing cards into face cards at once, but due to its low chance to do so (a fixed 3/13 or ~23.1% chance), it should be used with caution when taking into account its downside of -1 Hand size.

title: Canio
text: Canio: Cryptid can be used to create more face cards to be destroyed. Vouchers: Omen Globe allows Spectral cards to appear in Arcana Packs, which can be helpful to scearch for those mentioned in Synergetic Spectral cards section. Magic Trick can have a chance for face cards to appear in the shop, which can be bought to get destroyed to scale Canio. This can be further increased with help from Overstock and Overstock Plus to increase the shop selection, plus Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut to make rerolling cheaper. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Medusa are not recommended due to their default lack of face cards, making it significantly harder to scale Canio.

title: Canio
text: Canio: Jokers: Jokers that synergize with face cards, such as Baron, Sock and Buskin, and Triboulet, do not work well with Canio because you're destroying many face cards, which will hurt the collective output. Boss Blinds: The Plant makes it so that all face cards are debuffed, and face cards destroyed during this Boss blind will not scale Canio.

title: Canio
text: Canio: Trivia: Canio is a reference to the 1892 Italian opera Pagliacci by Ruggero Leoncavallo. The opera tells the tale of Canio, an actor and the leader of a theatrical company who murders his wife Nedda and her lover Silvio on stage during a performance. The destruction of face cards (which feature people on them) to increase Canio's power is likely in reference to these murders. This Joker is animated, with Canio himself hovering just above the silver card face. Only the other Legendary Jokers and Hologram share this trait. The other legendary Jokers are Chicot, Perkeo, Triboulet, and Yorick.

title: Canio
text: Canio: The other legendary Jokers are Chicot, Perkeo, Triboulet, and Yorick. In some early versions of the game, the card was misspelled as "Caino". This is still true in internal references to the card within the game's code. Canio is a certain type of jester or clown called a Pierrot, which is defined as a French male character dressed in a loose white costume with a sad-painted white face and a pointed hat. In other media: Canio appears as a playable character in the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors. Canio appears as an artifact in Monster Train 2.

title: Card Sharp
text: Card Sharp: Card Sharp (Joker). Effect: X3 Mult if played poker hand has already been played this round. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Card Sharp is an Uncommon Multiplicative Mult Joker that provides X3 Mult when a hand is played again during the same round.

title: Card Sharp
text: Card Sharp: Usage Notes: Card Sharp only applies to the scoring hand, not the hands that it contains. For example, playing a Straight Flush after a Flush or Straight does not give X3 Mult. The Five-Card Draw challenge starts the player with a copy of Card Sharp. Decks: Checkered Deck: Start run with 26 Spades and 26 Hearts, making repeated flushes easier. Blue Deck: +1 hand per round, allowing more chances to play repeated hands. Red Deck: +1 discard, allowing more chance to assemble desired hands. Poker hands: Strong 5-card hands like Flush, Straight, Full House, etc... benefit the most from Card Sharp, provided they can be played at least twice per blind.

title: Card Sharp
text: Card Sharp: Players may opt to buff weaker hands like High Card, Pair, Two Pair, etc... with Planet cards to make their base Mult stronger, allowing repeated play for each blind to score larger. Jokers: Burglar: +3 hands, allowing more chances to play repeated hands. Juggler: +1 hand size, allowing strong hands to be assembled more easily. Drunkard: +1 discard, allowing more chances to assemble desired hands. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong both give additional hands, giving the player more chances to play the same hand. Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give additional discards, allowing the player more opportunities to assemble the desired hand. Deck: Black Deck starts with one less hand, which makes it harder to work around Card Sharp.

title: Card Sharp
text: Card Sharp: Deck: Black Deck starts with one less hand, which makes it harder to work around Card Sharp. Similarly, Blast Off starts with two less hands, which makes it even harder to work around Card Sharp. Golden Needle only starts with one hand, rendering Card Sharp useless. Jokers: Troubadour is not recommended as the -1 hand each round which means less chances to play the same hand. Vouchers: Hieroglyph is not recommended as the -1 hand each round which means less chances to play the same hand.

title: Card Sharp
text: Card Sharp: Vouchers: Hieroglyph is not recommended as the -1 hand each round which means less chances to play the same hand. Boss Blinds: The Needle: This boss hard counters Card Sharp as it only allows 1 hand to be played. Burglar is an effective safety against this, as discards are converted after the blind effect is applied. The Eye: This boss also hard counters Card Sharp as it does not allow repeated hand types, making it impossible to play a second hand for the X3 Mult effect.

title: Card Sharp
text: Card Sharp: The Arm: Does not hard counter Card Sharp unlike the other two bosses, but if the player relies on the X3 Mult to win, they must decrease the level of the hand at least two times. Trivia: Card sharps, sometimes known as card sharks, are people who use skill and/or deception to win poker games. The hoodie + sunglasses outfit derives from Phil Laak, a professional poker player nicknamed "the Unabomber" due to the outfit's resemblance to police sketches of Ted Kaczynski. Laak's use of this outfit popularized it among poker players in general; it is unclear whether LocalThunk was referencing Laak specifically or simply riffing on the outfit more broadly.

title: Cartomancer
text: Cartomancer: Cartomancer (Joker). Effect: Create a Tarot card when Blind is selected, (Must have room). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Discover every Tarot card. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: On Blind Select. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Cartomancer is an Uncommon Effect Joker that creates a random Tarot each time a Blind is selected. The wide-ranging effects of Tarot cards allow the player to easily manipulate their deck in a variety of directions, but this same variance can also make it slightly unreliable. Because of this, Cartomancer tends to be much stronger in the early game than later on.

title: Cartomancer
text: Cartomancer: To unlock this Joker, the player must have discovered every Tarot card. This Joker shares an unlock requirement with the Cartomancy achievement. Decks: Black Deck: Its inherent +1 Joker slot allows Cartomancer to be used alongside 5 other scoring Jokers. Moreover, acquiring The Hermit or Temperance early from this Joker's effect can help this Deck reach its ceiling sooner by overstepping its largest weakness: its poor early-game economy.

title: Cartomancer
text: Cartomancer: Magic Deck: This 52-stack of wizardry starts the player with the Crystal Ball Voucher, giving an extra consumable slot to hold more Tarot cards. This serves several functions when combined with this Joker: scoring-oriented Tarot cards like Justice can be stored to save a run in a pinch; the starting copies of The Fool will have easier access to more desirable targets, and potentially unwanted Tarot cards can be stored to prevent them from reappearing elsewhere. Obtaining earlier access to the Omen Globe Voucher can be of potential interest, too - by allowing Spectral cards to appear in Arcana Packs, they can be viewed as potential mini-Spectral Packs, as there would already be a reliable source of Tarot cards.

title: Cartomancer
text: Cartomancer: Poker hands: Cartomancer does not synergize directly with any poker hand. It provides very slight favor to the 5-card hands, however, as they provide more opportunities for Enhancements (applied by Tarot cards) to pump up the score. Jokers: The following Jokers have synergy with Cartomancer:

title: Cartomancer
text: Cartomancer: Jokers: The following Jokers have synergy with Cartomancer: Fortune Teller: Perhaps the strongest synergy that either of these two have, it will gain +1 Mult for each Tarot card used. Skipping as few Blinds as possible, while maximizing on Arcana Packs and copies of The Fool and The Emperor, can easily shoot it up to +40 Mult or more. To strengthen the case, Fortune Teller scales retroactively, meaning that it will not be any weaker if Cartomancer is acquired first than if they were simultaneously.

title: Cartomancer
text: Cartomancer: Jokers that scale based on hands/cards played are a good choice, as using this Joker means wanting to see as many Blinds as possible. These include Green Joker, Ride the Bus, Runner, Square Joker, Supernova, Spare Trousers, Wee Joker, and Obelisk. The Enhancement series Jokers (Glass Joker, Golden Ticket, Lucky Cat, Steel Joker, and Stone Joker) all become more accessible while using this Joker. If focusing on a specific type of Enhancement, Cartomancer can more easily balloon their high power by finding the relevant Tarot card, as well as copies of The Fool. Of these, Lucky Cat is perhaps the most synergistic, as more Blinds played means more Tarot cards created, and also more chances to trigger Lucky cards.

title: Cartomancer
text: Cartomancer: Blueprint and Brainstorm: These two can copy Cartomancer's effect at the start of a Blind, meaning 2 or possibly even 3 unique Tarot cards to choose from, or at the very worst, a bit of extra money for the next Shop. The Joker lineup can also be rearranged immediately afterward to assist with scoring. Campfire: In the event the Tarot cards are unneeded, this Joker can provide an X0.75 Mult boost to Campfire on each Ante, which can shoot even higher if The Emperor or The High Priestess are generated. Driver's License and Vampire are the two best jokers for converting all of the enhanced cards that Cartomancer has made into a powerful endgame strategy.

title: Cartomancer
text: Cartomancer: Perkeo: Perkeo has awkward timing and mild anti-synergy with Cartomancer, as Perkeo copies a consumable immediately after the shop while Cartomancer generates a Tarot card after entering a blind. If Cartomancer generates an ideal Tarot card, the player will have to keep it during the entirety of the next shop, potentially blocking the card from showing up in said shop (unless the player has Showman). Nonetheless, Cartomancer is still a useful consumable generator for Perkeo if better options do not come up, and can help supercharge the player's deckfixing. Vouchers: The aforementioned Crystal Ball pairs very nicely with this Joker, for all the same reasons (run-saving, ease of deck fixing, and Shop RNG manipulation).

title: Cartomancer
text: Cartomancer: Hieroglyph and its upgraded counterpart Petroglyph allow the player to see up to 3 additional Blinds each, which means even more Tarot cards to enhance Deck quality. These should be avoided when using the Black Deck, however, as having only 2 hands and, in the case of Petroglyph, 2 discards every round (only 1 on Blue Stake and above), is a very risky position unless the other held Jokers and poker hand levels are contributing enough raw score. Decks: Nebula Deck's -1 consumable slot can make it harder to hold and use Tarot cards from Cartomancer.

title: Cartomancer
text: Cartomancer: Decks: Nebula Deck's -1 consumable slot can make it harder to hold and use Tarot cards from Cartomancer. Anaglyph Deck: With emphasis placed on skipping Blinds for duplication of powerful Tags, it has slight anti-synergy with this Joker. It can still be very useful early on, however, especially in the absence of particularly strong Tags. Jokers: Throwback: A Joker that encourages skipping Blinds. Cartomancer will have fewer opportunities to create Tarot cards if scaling Throwback is more of a priority. Trivia: This Joker's art is stylised to mimic a Tarot card, mirroring Astronomer, which has comparable unlock requirements to Cartomancer and is stylised to mimic a Planet card.

title: Cartomancer
text: Cartomancer: Despite this, the brightest color of the background (and second-brightest of the frill) is off-color compared to Tarot cards, including on the third bauble of the frill. This color is also only ever found on a single pixel of the Vagabond.

title: Castle
text: Castle: Castle (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains +3 Chips per discarded [suit] card, suit changes every round, (Currently +0 Chips). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Chips. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Castle is an Uncommon scaling Chips Joker that adds Chips to played hands. The amount of Chips added begins at +0 and is permanently increased by +3 for each time a card of the specified suit is discarded.

title: Castle
text: Castle: The suit is chosen proportionally to the suit composition of the current deck and changes each round. For example, in a deck of 20 Clubs and 10 Spades, Castle would select Clubs two-thirds of the time, and Spades for the remaining third. If the deck has no card with any suit (i.e., full of Stone cards) Castle will default to +3 Chips per discarded Spade. Decks: Checkered Deck works well with Castle due to the lower suit diversity. Red Deck can use its +1 discard for more scaling. Plasma Deck gets more value from the chips than any other deck.

title: Castle
text: Castle: Plasma Deck gets more value from the chips than any other deck. Painted Deck increases the player's hand size by two, which allows players to see and discard more cards desired by Castle. Erratic Deck can start with a lot of cards of a certain suit, making it easier to fix the deck for Castle. Five-Card Draw can use the +3 discards per round for more scaling. Poker hands: Because Castle scales based on discarding cards, it means that weaker, easier hands like High Card and Pair allow for the effect to be used more consistently.

title: Castle
text: Castle: Alternately, when players manage to shape their deck down to a single suit, Flush-based hands like Flush, Straight Flush, Flush House, and Flush Five become much more viable. Jokers: Drunkard and Merry Andy both provide additional discards, allowing Castle to scale more per round. Yorick will also scale alongside Castle. Smeared Joker makes Castle twice as easy to scale. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette increase the player's hand size, allowing players to see more of their deck and give them more chances to discard cards chosen by Castle. Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give 1 extra discard, allowing Castle to scale faster.

title: Castle
text: Castle: Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give 1 extra discard, allowing Castle to scale faster. Blinds: The Hook automatically discards 2 cards held in hand, which can trigger Castle's scaling if one or both cards are of the chosen suit. Tarot cards: Wild cards count towards any suit as the bonus, so The Lovers can be helpful. Removing all cards of a certain suit using tarot cards gives Castle more chance to trigger (like Checkered Deck). Decks: Green Deck incentivizes not discarding, as it basically means throwing money away, which can make Castle difficult to use. Blast Off doesn't work well with Castle, as this deck only starts with 2 discards. Jokers: Burglar prevents this Joker entirely from scaling.

title: Castle
text: Castle: Jokers: Burglar prevents this Joker entirely from scaling. Banner, Delayed Gratification, Green Joker, and Ramen conflict with this Joker, as their effects rely on not using discards. Similarly, Trading Card and Burnt Joker place restrictions on discards, which interferes with triggering Castle's effect optimally. Blinds: The Goad, The Head, The Club, and The Window all debuff a specific suit, preventing Castle from scaling if it happens to pick the to-be-debuffed suit upon entering the Boss Blind. One trick to avoid this is to check Castle's chosen suit before entering Big Blind: if it's not the to-be-debuffed suit, skip the Blind to ensure it can scale normally during the boss blind.

title: Castle
text: Castle: The Water will always set your discards to 0, meaning Castle Joker does not scale. The House, The Fish, The Wheel and The Mark all draw cards face down, which makes it difficult to tell if the cards are the same suit as the one that Castle wants to discard. Stakes: Blue Stake and above hinder Castle's potential because they have 1 less discard by default. Trivia: As a part of the Ghost Deck Playing Cards set by Fangamer, Castle is one of the four Jokers to be featured next to Mr. Bones, Séance, and Sixth Sense.

title: Cavendish
text: Cavendish: Cavendish (Joker). Effect: X3 Mult, 1 in 1000 chance this card is destroyed at the end of round. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Spawn Condition: Only obtainable if Gros Michel has gone "extinct" during the current run. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Probability-Based: Yes. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: ✗ No. Cavendish is a Common Multiplicative Mult Joker that provides an immediate and unconditional X3 Mult to all hands played. With many other similar cards having an activation requirement or warranting scaling, this Mult bonus makes Cavendish among the best in its class, arguably the best Common Joker, and potentially one of the best in the game.

title: Cavendish
text: Cavendish: Obtaining this joker first requires Gros Michel to destroy itself via its own 1 in 6 chance during the same run. It also comes with a minuscule but potentially devastating risk in the form of a 1 in 1000 chance to destroy itself at the end of the round (denoted by the word "Extinct!" displaying as it vanishes), which can deprive the player of most of their scoring power. Usage Notes: The Non-Perishable challenge bans Cavendish. While Cavendish can also go "Extinct!", it is still able to show up in the shop again, unlike Gros Michel. Decks: This Joker works well with any of the Decks, as it gives X3 Mult to every hand played.

title: Cavendish
text: Cavendish: Decks: This Joker works well with any of the Decks, as it gives X3 Mult to every hand played. Poker hands: Any hand can benefit from this Joker for the same reasons that any of the Decks can. Jokers: Cavendish, as any Multplicative Mult Joker, pairs incredibly well with Additive Mult Jokers and other Multiplicative Mult Jokers, especially scaling ones. This includes Jokers such as Green Joker, Fortune Teller and Flash Card. Copying Cavendish with Blueprint and Brainstorm does not increase the probability of self-destruction of Cavendish or cause the copying Joker to self-destruct, so they can be used without additional risks.

title: Cavendish
text: Cavendish: Anti-Synergies: Oops! All 6s doubles Cavendish's destruction chance to a 2 in 1000 chance. This can safely be ignored in most cases. To guarantee that Cavendish gets destroyed, the player would need 10 copies of Oops! All 6s (which would display as a 1024 in 1000 chance). Trivia: After the real world Gros Michel was devastated by a fungal pandemic in the 1950s-1960s, the Cavendish replaced it as the most commercially common banana due to its resistance to the fungus. A similar disaster could wipe out Cavendish bananas, as they are vulnerable to a relative of the fungus that wiped out the Gros Michel, but more care and preventative measures are in place to stop this from reoccurring.

title: Cavendish
text: Cavendish: These traits are represented by the Joker's requirement for Gros Michel to first go extinct, common rarity, powerful bonus, and the highly unlikely chance of self-destruction by going "Extinct!". The waves of energy radiating from the banana in Cavendish's art may be a reference to how bananas are very faintly radioactive. Cavendish's 1 in 1000 chance to destroy itself is the least likely probability-based event in the game. This Joker is part of the group of "Consumable" Jokers that can be destroyed with usage, dubbed "Food Jokers" due to their shared theme. The other Jokers in this group are Ice Cream, Popcorn, Gros Michel, Egg, Seltzer, Turtle Bean, Ramen, and Diet Cola.

title: Cavendish
text: Cavendish: Cavendish is one of the few Jokers to be found in a recently released pin collection by Makeship, including Jimbo and a The Wheel of Fortune's "Nope!" Cavendish appears on an Ante Up! shirt in a merch collaboration with Fangamer. The two other jokers that appear on the same shirt include Joker and Popcorn. In other media: Cavendish appears as a weapon in the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors. The card art of this joker specifically appears upon the activation of the "Bananastrophe" event. Cavendish appears as an artifact in Monster Train 2.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Ceremonial Dagger (Joker). Effect: When Blind is selected, destroy Joker to the right and permanently add double its sell value to this Mult, (Currently +0 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Ceremonial Dagger is an Uncommon scaling Additive Mult Joker. It starts at +0 Mult, and at the beginning of each round, it will destroy the Joker immediately to its right and gain Mult equal to twice the destroyed card's sell value. If it is the rightmost Joker, it will not destroy anything. If the Joker to the right of it is Eternal, the Eternal joker will not be destroyed, and no Mult will be added to the total.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Since the destruction happens only on Blind selection, Ceremonial Dagger can be safely reordered with other jokers during a Blind to apply its Mult bonus in the most beneficial order. Usage Notes: This Joker is the main star in the On a Knife's Edge Challenge. It receives the Eternal Sticker and a unique Pinned property, which makes it permanently stuck at the leftmost side. As a result, players must constantly "feed" the dagger during this challenge, and it cannot benefit from Blueprint (but it works with Brainstorm normally). Decks: Yellow Deck is a good option, as the early bonus money allows players to get to $25 quickly and be able to save up a lot for the Dagger.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Black Deck's extra Joker slot is very helpful, as one can still have four safe Jokers while scaling Dagger. Similarly, Five-Card Draw's 2 extra Jokers slots is even better, as one can still have six Jokers while scaling Dagger. Anaglyph Deck is occasionally a good choice, as the Double Tag can provide lots of economic buffs when presented. However, skipping a blind means skipping a level of scaling. Inflation might work with Ceremonial Dagger, as this deck permanently increases prices by $1 on every purchase, including the sell price. This Joker can scale very fast thanks to Jokers' inflated sell prices.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Poker hands: This Joker can sometimes make it more difficult to change your deck due to needing a constant supply of money to fuel its destruction of other Jokers. As a result, it might be best to prioritize easier-to-play hands. However, the hand you play doesn't really matter, as the Mult Dagger provides will always apply. Jokers: Ceremonial Dagger is, at its core, an economy-based scaling Joker. Therefore, having more money makes it better, as one can afford more expensive Jokers to scale it. There are many options, but it's recommended to go for more powerful ones, like Cloud 9 or Golden Ticket, as Joker slots are limited with Dagger.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Jokers that expire gradually are economically great choice to be fed to Dagger, especially Turtle Bean, which provides hand size increasing before being destroyed. Egg's sell value grows by $3 per round, which can be a big windfall when fed to a Ceremonial Dagger. Gift Card adds $1 of sell value to all owned Jokers at the end of a round, getting some more power out of Jokers before they're put to the altar. Swashbuckler, which also benefits from higher sell values, can act as a sort of mini-Dagger until you find it. Riff-Raff can supply joker cards to scale the Dagger. This alleviates the economic strain before one can obtain strong sources of money.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Joker Stencil will provide increased XMult when Ceremonial Dagger consumes one Joker at the start of each blind, since an empty slot is created. Chaos the Clown grants a free reroll, making it a bit cheaper to hunt for Jokers to feed to the Dagger. Credit Card has a buy and sell value of $1, which translates to a very efficient conversion rate of money into +Mult. Strong sources of XMult are very much appreciated, as they push Ceremonial Dagger's Mult even higher and allow one to win faster, therefore getting more money.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Note that if Ceremonial Dagger is to the left of a different Joker that triggers "When Blind is selected" (such as Cartomancer, Riff-Raff, or Burglar), the Ceremonial Dagger will destroy the other joker before it can trigger. Vouchers: Reroll Surplus, Reroll Glut, Overstock, and Overstock Plus all make it easier to look for more expensive Jokers to scale Ceremonial Dagger. Hone and Glow Up make it more likely for editioned Jokers to appear, which have a higher sell value, helping Ceremonial Dagger gain +Mult. Antimatter provides +1 Joker slot, allowing the player to have five Jokers while scaling Dagger.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Antimatter provides +1 Joker slot, allowing the player to have five Jokers while scaling Dagger. Stakes: On Gold Stake difficulty, Rental Jokers offer the most efficient cost-to-mult ratio of 1:2, similar to Credit Card. This can make scaling the Dagger more affordable in the early game. Boss Blinds: During Amber Acorn, Ceremonial Dagger will take effect between flipping and shuffling, so it will still destroy the Joker on the right side (rather than randomly one). Decks: Painted Deck's reduced Joker amount is bad to combo with Ceremonial Dagger, as the player will only have three Jokers while scaling Ceremonial Dagger.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Similarly, Cruelty's reduced Joker amount is even more difficult to combo with Ceremonial Dagger, as the player will only have two Jokers while scaling Ceremonial Dagger. Non-Perishable does not work with Ceremonial Dagger, as all Jokers are Eternal, and it cannot destroy them and doesn't gain + Mult. Jokers: Abstract Joker depends on having many Jokers to boost its +Mult, which it can't do very well with Ceremonial Dagger destroying Jokers left and to the right, which reduces the total Joker count. Throwback depends on skipping Blinds, and when a Blind is skipped, Ceremonial Dagger cannot be upgraded.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Throwback depends on skipping Blinds, and when a Blind is skipped, Ceremonial Dagger cannot be upgraded. Vouchers: Clearance Sale and Liquidation are very bad to combo with Dagger. Their reduced prices also affect sell value, and sell value rounds down, making Dagger much less effective. It is impossible to get more than +4 per Joker after Liquidation except from a few Editioned Rare Jokers, Legendaries, or from scaling sell value effects such as Egg and Gift Card.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Strategies: Ceremonial Dagger has high growth potential, while this requires an additional Joker Slot (used to place the Joker to be destroyed) to achieve. However, outside of the On a Knife's Edge Challenge, Ceremonial Dagger can be used alongside other Jokers once it's buffed up significantly. Simply move it to the rightmost slot at the end of each blind, start a new blind, and move it back to the leftmost side so it can provide maximum effect for other Multiplicative Jokers. This ensures Ceremonial Dagger doesn't consume any other Jokers while still providing +Mult for the round. On Black Stake difficulty or higher (and in some Challenges), it is also possible to put an Eternal Joker to the right of it and prevent Ceremonial Dagger from destroying Jokers.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: Trivia: Ritual weapons, including knives and daggers, are used in many forms of ceremonial sacrifice in the real world, and as such are found in many fictional works. The name and design of this card are references to the Ceremonial Dagger item from the Risk of Rain series. In those games, its effect required an enemy to be slain to trigger, similar to how this Joker requires another Joker to be sacrificed. Ceremonial Dagger has a unique slicing sound effect when it destroys a Joker, which is recorded by LocalThunk with a kitchen knife. The pitch of the sound effect changes slightly each time. On Balatro's Steam Page an early design of Ceremonial Dagger appears which contains a different border.

title: Ceremonial Dagger
text: Ceremonial Dagger: On Balatro's Steam Page an early design of Ceremonial Dagger appears which contains a different border. Further down on the page, an alternate design shows up where not only the different border appears, but the green aura of the dagger appears to be a bluish-black as well. Furthermore, in the Friends of Jimbo 1 Trailer, this bluish-black version of Ceremonial Dagger reappears, this time losing the inlaid border. If the collection were a set of joker slots, Dagger would be destroying Banner. The art of this card in pre-release had a thinner inner border instead of the full border it has now.

title: Certificate
text: Certificate: Certificate (Joker). Effect: When round begins, add a random playing card with a random seal to your hand. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Have a Gold playing card with a Gold Seal. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Certificate is an Uncommon Effect Joker that adds a playing card with a random rank, suit, and random Seal to the hand of the player when a round begins. The card stays in the deck for future rounds.

title: Certificate
text: Certificate: Much of the power Certificate provides comes from it being able to generate a large amount of Seals, which are very difficult to get normally. Seals are incredibly powerful if built around, which makes an early Certificate incredibly valuable to shaping a run. The Seals are random, so it may be less valuable to buy Certificate in the hopes of generating only one out of the four Seals. All of the Seals can be useful, though, and even undesired Seals can be built around. To unlock this Joker, the player must have a Gold card with a Gold Seal.

title: Certificate
text: Certificate: To unlock this Joker, the player must have a Gold card with a Gold Seal. Usage notes: When Certificate adds a sealed card at the beginning of the round, it is put directly into your hand, bypassing the normal hand size temporarily. Certificate does not prevent the player from dying when they have a hand size of zero or below, since the game checks the hand size before Certificate can activate.

title: Certificate
text: Certificate: Unlike other Jokers that activated "When a blind is selected", Certificate activates "when a round begins", which is when the initial hand is drawn. This means Blueprint / Brainstorm can be used to copy for example Cartomancer, then immediately moved over to copy Certificate after clicking Select Blind (best done at lower game speeds). The Fragile challenge bans Certificate. Decks: Because Magic Deck starts with Crystal Ball, it allows the player to make better use of Blue Seals and Purple Seals. Painted Deck's extra hand size allows the player to hold more cards created by Certificate, as well as finding a desired hand whilst holding onto those cards more easily.

title: Certificate
text: Certificate: Zodiac Deck can use its extra Tarot cards to more easily manipulate the Sealed cards from Certificate. Abandoned Deck's and Mad World's reduced deck size make it easier to find the produced cards after they have been added to the deck. It is also easier to flood these decks with high-quality cards, since there are fewer bad cards to potentially draw. Poker hands: No specific poker hand directly benefits from Certificate, but any of them can be leveled up with its generated Blue Seals. Hands that benefit more from planet cards therefore indirectly benefit more.

title: Certificate
text: Certificate: If Certificate is held for only a couple of rounds, the generated cards are generally high-value duplication targets, and it can be easier to make powerful Five of a Kinds or Flush Fives. If Certificate is held for a long time or is Eternal, then lower value poker hands like High Card and Pair that do not rely on finding specific cards can be easier to find with many extra random cards in the deck. Jokers: Hologram scales with each card Certificate adds. DNA is better when copying valuable cards, like a Gold Seal Lucky card for example.

title: Certificate
text: Certificate: DNA is better when copying valuable cards, like a Gold Seal Lucky card for example. Gold Seal: Jokers that retrigger cards, like Hanging Chad make gold seals considerably stronger. As well as jokers that rely on the player having stronger income, like Flash Card are boosted by Gold seals. Red Seal: Jokers that adds effects to cards, like Fibonacci and Reserved Parking are better on cards with Red seals. Along with jokers that scale from scoring cards, like Lucky Cat appreciate the extra trigger. Blue Seal: Constellation scales from the player using Planet Cards which the Blue seal provides many of.

title: Certificate
text: Certificate: Blue Seal: Constellation scales from the player using Planet Cards which the Blue seal provides many of. Purple Seal: Jokers like Fortune Teller and Vampire scale from the Tarots the Purple seal provides. Furthermore, jokers like Steel Joker can be more powerful when the player has more access to Tarots. Decks: Nebula Deck makes it significantly harder to use Blue and Purple Seals due to the starting 1 consumable slot. On Checkered Deck Certificate can still create Club and Diamond cards, which can make it harder to play flushes.

title: Certificate
text: Certificate: On Checkered Deck Certificate can still create Club and Diamond cards, which can make it harder to play flushes. Poker hands: If Certificate is held for a long time or is Eternal, then higher value poker hands like Straight and Four of a Kind that rely on finding specific cards can be much harder to find with many extra random cards in the deck. Jokers: Erosion relies on a small deck size, which is more difficult to get when 1 card is added per round from Certificate. Blue Seal: Cards that decrease the players hand size, like Stuntman and Ouija can make finding and holding Blue seals more difficult.

title: Certificate
text: Certificate: Purple Seal: Burglar prevents the player from discarding, and jokers like Banner and Ramen heavily discourage the player from discarding. Trivia: The Joker art is a typical style of real-life certificates, with a seal and signature (J. Joker). According to LocalThunk, the art of Certificate used to include a seal (the marine mammal), which is an obvious pun. In early demos, the effect of Certificate was X2 mult for each Gold Seal card when played and scored. This is reflected by that its unlock condition is related to the Gold Seal.

title: Chaos the Clown
text: Chaos the Clown: Chaos the Clown (Joker). Effect: 1 free Reroll per shop. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Chaos the Clown is a Common Joker that provides one free Reroll every time you visit the shop.

title: Chaos the Clown
text: Chaos the Clown: Usage Notes: The next reroll still starts at the same price it would have been without the extra reroll, so Chaos the Clown effectively saves $ equal to Rerolls+4. With Reroll Surplus, this becomes Savings=Rerolls+2, and with Reroll Glut, it becomes Savings=Rerolls. If Chaos the Clown is obtained while in a shop, the price for the current shop reroll will be brought down to $0, regardless of whether it is the first reroll in that shop or not. The next reroll will cost where it previously left off. If the player sells Chaos the Clown whilst the once-per-shop free reroll is active, the reroll cost will immediately revert to the regular value.

title: Chaos the Clown
text: Chaos the Clown: As Chaos the Clown costs $4 but a standard re-roll costs $5, it can be cheaper to buy him to reroll the shop, and the player can sell him again later for an extra $2 back. If Chaos the Clown is sold after using its one free reroll and another one is found, it can be purchased again for another free reroll. Multiple copies of Chaos the Clown (obtained through Ankh, Invisible Joker, or Showman) do stack, allowing the player to get 2 free rerolls. However, it cannot be copied Blueprint or Brainstorm. Decks: Zodiac Deck works well with this Joker, as you will want to be rerolling more to see more Tarot and Planet cards.

title: Chaos the Clown
text: Chaos the Clown: Black Deck is decent for this Joker, as rerolling a lot allows you to see more Jokers that you can take. Jokers: Flash Card: use the free reroll to boost this after every shop visit. Campfire: can scale quicker, as the free reroll can let you find more Jokers or Consumables to buy and sell. Constellation: can scale very quickly, as the free reroll can let you find more planet cards each shop. Astronomer: can let you find more free planet cards. Vouchers: Overstock and Overstock Plus can make Chaos's free reroll much more significant. Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut combined with Chaos is practically equivalent to a D6 Tag.

title: Chaos the Clown
text: Chaos the Clown: Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut combined with Chaos is practically equivalent to a D6 Tag. Stakes: On Gold Stake, Chaos the Clown can be Rental, allowing the player to purchase it for $1, get a free re-roll, and then sell it back again for $1 to remain money neutral.

title: Chaos Theory
text: Chaos Theory: Chaos Theory (Joker). Effect: Unknown. Unlock Requirement: Unknown. Buy Price: Missing data. Sell Price: Missing data. Type: Unknown. Activation: Unknown. Copyable: ?. Perishable: ?. Eternal: ?. Chaos Theory is an unused Joker. The name "Chaos Theory" is shown in the video Lumpy Touch made about this Joker. It never had a name or effect in the game files.

title: Chaos Theory
text: Chaos Theory: Trivia: This Joker is drawn by Lumpy Touch who also created the art for Vagabond. The art for this Joker was found in the files of the 0.9.2 version of Balatro.

title: Chicot
text: Chicot: Chicot (Joker). Effect: Disables effect of every Boss Blind. Rarity: Legendary. Unlock Requirement: Find this Joker from the Soul card. Buy Price: 20 (cannot be found in shop). Sell Price: $10. Type: Effect. Activation: On Blind Select. Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Chicot is one of the five Legendary Jokers that can be generated from using The Soul Spectral card, which in itself has a 3 in 1000 (0.3%) chance to replace any given card in a Spectral Pack or an Arcana Pack.

title: Chicot
text: Chicot: Chicot eliminates all Boss Blind effects, reducing their required win conditions to 2x base chips (besides The Needle, which won't have its score increased). Decks: Black Deck has +1 Joker slot, which leaves more room for scoring Jokers. Jokers: Boss Blinds can affect almost every Joker in the game, and thus be helped by Chicot, but many Jokers have notable weaknesses to particular Boss Blinds. Chicot can negate the holes in these Jokers' defenses: Photograph, Smiley Face, and other face card Jokers no longer fear The Plant or The Mark. In this context, Pareidolia becomes less punishing to use. Bloodstone, Seeing Double, and other Card Suit Jokers can ignore their respective Boss Blinds.

title: Chicot
text: Chicot: Bloodstone, Seeing Double, and other Card Suit Jokers can ignore their respective Boss Blinds. In particular, Flower Pot and Ancient Joker can safely rely on Wild cards with Chicot. Card Sharp, Supernova, and other Jokers limited by poker hand-limiting Boss Blinds. Burglar is no longer weak against The Mouth or The Fish. Any Oops! All 6s based run will no longer fear The Wheel. Jokers that rely on discards (by either keeping them or using them), such as Banner or Castle, can safely ignore The Water. Boss Blinds: Disabling a boss blind reverses its effect, and due to the timing involved, multiple copies of Chicot will all disable the Boss Blind, resulting in a net positive effect:

title: Chicot
text: Chicot: The Wall: Score requirement is reduced by a factor of 2 for each copy of Chicot. The Water: Gains the number of discards originally as extra discards for each copy of Chicot. The Manacle: +1 extra Hand size for each copy of Chicot (permanently). This can be useful for using Ectoplasm more times in the same run than usually possible. The Needle: Gains (the number of hands originally - 1) extra hands for each copy of Chicot. Violet Vessel: Score is reduced by a factor of 3 for each copy of Chicot.

title: Chicot
text: Chicot: Violet Vessel: Score is reduced by a factor of 3 for each copy of Chicot. Since Chicot is not compatible with Blueprint/ Brainstorm, this occurrence can only be achieved through Joker duplicating means like Invisible Joker or Ankh, or by using another copy of The Soul with a Showman in hand. This interaction may actually be a bug, and might be patched in the future. Vouchers: Because of its distinctive effect as a utility Joker, Chicot normally does not benefit from any particular voucher. However, if the player has multiple copies of Chicot, Director's Cut and Retcon can be considered for the positive effects mentioned above.

title: Chicot
text: Chicot: Decks: Painted Deck, Blast Off and Cruelty penalize holding non-scoring Jokers like Chicot with their reduced Joker slots. Jokers: As Luchador also disable Boss blinds, functionally overlapping with Chicot, Luchador becomes a redundant pickup. Matador also does not work, as it activates based on Boss Blind effects. Vouchers: The Director's Cut and Retcon vouchers are usually made obsolete with the possession of Chicot, since Boss Blind effects are no longer a concern. Blinds: While normally it's not too big of a problem, do note that Amber Acorn shuffles Jokers before Chicot disables it, which can be annoying sometimes. Any run that relies on The Serpent's effect will no longer work with Chicot.

title: Chicot
text: Chicot: Any run that relies on The Serpent's effect will no longer work with Chicot. Trivia: Chicot (c. 1540–1591), real name Jean-Antoine d'Anglerais, was the jester of King Henry III of France, and later Henry IV. He was sharp-tongued, very cunning, spoke with the king without formalities, and often participated in battle. Chicot disabling Boss Blinds in the game is likely a reference to this. This Joker is animated, with Chicot hovering just above the red card face. The other Legendary Jokers are Canio, Perkeo, Triboulet and Yorick. Chicot's eyes are positioned slightly higher on his face than the other 4 Legendary Jokers. This is the only Legendary joker that is not Blueprint or Brainstorm compatible.

title: Chicot
text: Chicot: This is the only Legendary joker that is not Blueprint or Brainstorm compatible. It is possible Chicot's appearance is based on the 1862 painting Stańczyk, which depicts the real life Polish jester of the same name. Similarities between the paintings depiction of Stańczyk and Chicot (the Joker) include red hats with bells lined in the middle and stern expressions. The painting in question is often confused as a depiction of Chicot. In other media: Chicot appears as a playable character in the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors. Chicot appears as an artifact in Monster Train 2.

title: Clever Joker
text: Clever Joker: Clever Joker (Joker). Effect: +80 Chips if played hand contains a Two Pair. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Clever Joker is a Common Chips Joker that provides +80 Chips when the played hand contains a Two Pair. This does not include hands like Four of a Kind, but it does include hands like Full House.

title: Clever Joker
text: Clever Joker: Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World work well with this Joker thanks to their smaller deck, allowing you to find a Two Pair easier. Erratic Deck can work well with this Joker if it randomizes a lot of cards with the same rank. Plasma Deck benefits from the large amount of chips, which, when balanced, greatly boost the score for the played hand. Poker hands: Any Poker Hand that contains a Two Pair will benefit from Clever Joker. These are: Two Pair Full House Flush House Flush - only if the flush contains a Two Pair Four of a Kind and similar hands do not trigger Clever Joker. Jokers: Spare Trousers gains Mult when playing a Two Pair.

title: Clever Joker
text: Clever Joker: Jokers: Spare Trousers gains Mult when playing a Two Pair. Square Joker gains Chips any time a played hand consists of exactly 4 cards. Since a standard Two Pair is exactly four cards, the player can strengthen Square Joker while getting Chips from Clever Joker. Jolly Joker and Mad Joker give Mult on a Pair and Two Pair respectively. Sly Joker gives Chips if the played hand contains a Pair. The Duo provides a X2 Mult boost when playing a Two Pair. Trivia: This joker is part of a series which provide a Chips boost for a specific hand. The others are Sly Joker, Wily Joker, Devious Joker and Crafty Joker.

title: Clever Joker
text: Clever Joker: Much like the other Jokers in this series, this Joker has blue face paint over the mouth, indicating that they provide a bonus of Chips and not Mult like the red face paint Jokers.

title: Cloud 9
text: Cloud 9: Cloud 9 (Joker). Effect: Earn $1 for each 9 in your full deck at end of round, (Currently $4). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Economy. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Cloud 9 is an Uncommon Economy Joker. It pays out an additional $1 at the end of every round for each 9 in the player's complete Deck - regardless of whether they were scored, drawn, or discarded that round.

title: Cloud 9
text: Cloud 9: Assuming no Deck modification, or skewing by an Erratic Deck seed, it will generate $4 every round - which makes it just as effective as the Common Golden Joker, but slightly worse to start as it costs a dollar extra. However, with the right amount of Deck manipulation, this Joker can earn substantial amounts of money. Decks: Any Deck can use Cloud 9 effectively, as it pays out whenever a round is completed as long as the player has at least one 9 in their full Deck. Black Deck can benefit from Cloud 9 thanks to its +1 Joker Slot. Because of the -1 hand per blind penalty, Cloud 9 can help offset the lower income from early games.

title: Cloud 9
text: Cloud 9: Green Deck: This Deck likes to have extra income sources in the absence of interest, so something like Cloud 9 is a natural inclusion. Yellow Deck: This Joker will help maintain the interest cap when acquired in the mid-game, further increasing the already-strong buying power it has. Ghost Deck, Magic Deck, and Zodiac Deck: All these Decks have easier access to Deck fixing to include a higher amount of 9s in the Deck. Of these, Ghost Deck is probably the best to choose, as its starting Hex Spectral card makes it more practical to keep this Joker for the long run by allowing it to help with scoring.

title: Cloud 9
text: Cloud 9: Poker hands: Since players are encouraged to create lots of 9s to increase Cloud 9's benefit, hands which use many of the same rank are recommended. Three of a Kind Four of a Kind Five of a Kind Flush Five Jokers: Tarot card generation is extremely important if the maximization of Cloud 9's value is the goal. Cartomancer is the most effective one, creating a Tarot card whenever a Blind is selected (a Cloud 9 build would not want to skip in the first place in order to gain the most money from the end-of-round payouts). If it can be found, the Legendary Joker Perkeo is a must-keep, allowing infinite duplication of key Deck-fixing consumables.

title: Cloud 9
text: Cloud 9: Fortune Teller: Providing a retroactively-scaling +1 Mult for every Tarot card used in the current run, it can richly reward the player with strong scoring for building into this Joker's niche. Odd Todd: With its extra shot of Chips whenever an odd-ranked card is scored, it can dish out up to an extremely high +155 Chips boost when five 9s are scored in the same hand (and even more with retrigger effects). Bull and Bootstraps: Giving extra Chips and Additive Mult, respectively, as the player's held money grows, these are a good choice if high amounts of spending is not particularly valuable.

title: Cloud 9
text: Cloud 9: Hologram: A potential consideration if making use of Standard Packs to buff the number of 9s, this gives a Multiplicative Mult boost that grows as more playing cards are added to the Deck. DNA: The only direct synergy this Joker has with another. It can be used to duplicate tons of 9s to sharply increase the end-of-round payout. It also synergizes with the aforementioned Hologram. The Trio and The Family: Cloud 9 already makes it more advisable to build into hands with repetitive ranks, which these cards reward richly with high Multiplicative Mult boosts.

title: Cloud 9
text: Cloud 9: Consumables: The Death and Strength Tarot cards, and the Cryptid Spectral card, can be used to quickly boost the number of 9s, thus increasing the value of Cloud 9. Vouchers: Tarot Merchant, its upgraded counterpart Tarot Tycoon, and Omen Globe all make it easier to find Deck manipulation consumables. Clearance Sale and its upgraded counterpart Liquidation allow easier ballooning of Cloud 9's value by making Booster Packs cheaper. Magic Trick can be considered, as it allows players to buy more 9s directly from The Shop. Decks: Painted Deck, Blast Off and Cruelty: The reduced Joker slots makes it difficult to carry Cloud 9 since players may need more scoring Jokers to survive and beat Ante 8.

title: Cloud 9
text: Cloud 9: Trivia: This is the only Economy Joker in the game without a true cap on its money generation - most of the others have a fixed amount (like Golden Joker), are limited by the number of hands/discards per round (like Faceless Joker and To Do List), or have a hard cap by some other means (like Satellite and To the Moon). As long as the player has a large number of 9s, Cloud 9 will continue to pay out $1 for each. There are exactly nine clouds on the card art for this Joker. The name of this Joker is possibly a reference to the phrase 'on cloud 9', referring to being in a state of euphoria.

title: Constellation
text: Constellation: Constellation (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains X0.1 Mult every time a Planet card is used, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes.
