Constellation is an Uncommon scaling Multiplicative Mult Joker that gains X0.1 Mult each time a Planet card is used. It does not scale retroactively, and always starts at X1 Mult.

title: Constellation
text: Constellation: It should be noted that using a Planet card is technically distinct from the act of leveling up a Poker Hand; the Black Hole Spectral card and the Orbital Tag do not trigger Constellation, since they are not Planet cards. Similarly, Burnt Joker and Space Joker also do not increase Constellation. Usage notes: The Blast Off challenge starts the player with an Eternal copy of Constellation. Decks: Nebula Deck begins with the Telescope Voucher, allowing the player to purchase a Planet card of the most played Poker Hand each time a Celestial Pack is opened. Zodiac Deck begins with the Planet Merchant Voucher making Planet cards have a x2 chance of appearing.

title: Constellation
text: Constellation: Zodiac Deck begins with the Planet Merchant Voucher making Planet cards have a x2 chance of appearing. Poker Hands: Since Constellation levels up regardless of the Planet cards' type, any poker Hand has synergy with it. Jokers: Economy Jokers (ex. Business Card, Golden Joker, Cloud 9, etc.) are important to help scale Constellation, since they allow the player to purchase more Celestial Packs and Planet cards from the Shop. Notably, Satellite provides more money for each unique Planet card used. Chaos the Clown gives a free reroll in the Shop allowing for more Planet cards to be found. Mime is able to retrigger a Blue Seal, allowing for two Planet cards to be created, instead of one.

title: Constellation
text: Constellation: Mime is able to retrigger a Blue Seal, allowing for two Planet cards to be created, instead of one. Astronomer makes every Planet card and Celestial Pack in the Shop free, thus giving free upgrades to Constellation. Certificate can generate cards with a Blue Seal, granting a repeatable source of Planet cards. As Perkeo gives a copy of a random consumable at the end of the Shop, the player should keep a Planet card of their best poker hand to obtain more, and scale Constellation. Vouchers: Overstock and Overstock Plus respectively add a 3rd and 4th card slot in the Shop, giving the player more chances to find Planet cards to buy and use.

title: Constellation
text: Constellation: Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut make it cheaper to reroll to find more Planet cards to buy and use. Clearance Sale and Liquidation reduce the price of Planet cards and Celestial Packs. Telescope guarantees that the player's most played poker hand will appear in Celestial Packs. Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon make it more likely for Planet cards to appear more often in the Shop. Observatory gives X1.5 Mult for poker hands corresponding to Planet cards in the consumable area. Modifiers: Blue Seal can generate Planet cards at the end of the round, allowing Constellation to scale faster. Consumables: The High Priestess provides two Planet cards. The Fool can copy Planet cards to use.

title: Constellation
text: Constellation: Consumables: The High Priestess provides two Planet cards. The Fool can copy Planet cards to use. Trance creates a Blue Seal, allowing the player to create more Planet cards. Jokers: Red Card encourages skipping Celestial Packs instead of using the Planet cards in them. Campfire incentives the player to sell Planet cards instead of using them. Skipping for Throwback or Diet Cola likely means fewer Planet cards to find or use, although this becomes viable if the Meteor Tag is involved. Vouchers: Tarot Merchant, Tarot Tycoon, and Magic Trick reduce the probabilities of Planet cards appearing in the shop. Trivia: Constellation is a space-themed joker, continuing the space association with Planet cards like Supernova, Satellite, Space Joker, and Astronomer.

title: Constellation
text: Constellation: Trivia: Constellation is a space-themed joker, continuing the space association with Planet cards like Supernova, Satellite, Space Joker, and Astronomer. In astronomy, a "constellation" is an alignment of stars in a certain pattern that form a shape that help us recognize where certain stars are in the sky. The constellation in the art has stars that form the joker's hat, its head, and its ruffle.

title: Crafty Joker
text: Crafty Joker: Crafty Joker (Joker). Effect: +80 Chips if played hand contains a Flush. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Crafty Joker is a Common Chips Joker that provides +80 Chips when playing a Flush. This includes hands that include any Flush, such as a Flush House.

title: Crafty Joker
text: Crafty Joker: Decks: Checkered Deck works best with Crafty Joker thanks to its 2 suits, allowing Flushes to be reliably formed. Plasma Deck benefits from the large amount of chips, which, when balanced, greatly boost the score for the played hand. Poker hands: Playing any kind of Flush will trigger Crafty Joker. This includes: Flush Straight Flush Flush House Flush Five Jokers: Smeared Joker and Four Fingers make it easier to play Flushes. Droll Joker gives +10 Mult when playing a Flush. The Tribe gives X2 Mult when playing a Flush. Consumables: Tarot cards:

title: Crafty Joker
text: Crafty Joker: The Tribe gives X2 Mult when playing a Flush. Consumables: Tarot cards: The Moon, The Star, The Sun, and The World turn cards into Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, and Spades, respectively, which can be useful if the player wants their deck to focus on one or two suits. The Hanged Man can be useful for cutting unwanted cards out the deck if the player wants to focus on one particular card suit. The Lovers turns a card into a Wild card, which can be useful for forming a Flush if the player needs another card.

title: Crafty Joker
text: Crafty Joker: Trivia: This joker is part of a series which provide a Chips boost for a specific hand. The others are Sly Joker, Wily Joker, Clever Joker and Devious Joker. Much like the other Jokers in this series, this Joker has blue face paint over the mouth, indicating that they provide a bonus of Chips and not Mult like the red face paint Jokers.

title: Crazy Joker
text: Crazy Joker: Crazy Joker (Joker). Effect: +12 Mult if played hand contains a Straight. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Crazy Joker is a Common Additive Mult Joker that provides +12 Mult when the hand contains a Straight. This also includes Straight Flush and Royal Flush.

title: Crazy Joker
text: Crazy Joker: Decks: Red Deck is good with this joker, as more discards can help you get a Straight. Nebula Deck can be good, as having your hands be mainly Straight means having your planet packs contain Saturn helps. Abandoned Deck and Mad World both have fewer cards than a standard deck, which makes Straights easier to make. Painted Deck gives extra hand size, which can help the player with forming Straights. 15 Minute City starts with an Eternal Shortcut, which allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand. Poker hands: Crazy Joker affects both Straights and Straight Flushes.

title: Crazy Joker
text: Crazy Joker: Poker hands: Crazy Joker affects both Straights and Straight Flushes. Jokers: Devious Joker, Runner, and The Order will always activate at the same time as this Joker, as well as possibly Superposition and Séance, though those are more specific. Four Fingers and Shortcut both help in making Straights easier. As you are mainly just going for the same hand constantly, Supernova, Space Joker, and Card Sharp are good. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy give additional discards, allowing the player to search for Straight hands easier. Paint Brush and Palette both increase hand size, which can help players with forming Straights. Telescope can help upgrade Straights using Saturn.

title: Crazy Joker
text: Crazy Joker: Telescope can help upgrade Straights using Saturn. Decks: Erratic Deck has anti-synergy, as it is generally harder to create Straights with this deck. Five-Card Draw's -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straights. Jokers: Jokers that reduce hand size, like Stuntman and Merry Andy, have anti-synergy with Crazy Joker, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Consumables: Ectoplasm and Ouija have anti-synergy with Crazy Joker, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Not only that, but Ouija converts all cards held in hand into one single rank, which makes assembling Straights less consistent. Blinds: The Manacle's -1 hand size makes it hard to assemble Straights.

title: Crazy Joker
text: Crazy Joker: Blinds: The Manacle's -1 hand size makes it hard to assemble Straights. The Water will always start with 0 discards, making it very hard to assemble Straights. Trivia: This joker is part of a series that provide a Mult boost for a specific hand. The others are Jolly Joker, Zany Joker, Mad Joker and Droll Joker. In demo versions of the game, Crazy Joker had a different color scheme, more resembling Jolly Joker or Odd Todd. The Steam page for Balatro still shows this old art in some screenshots.

title: Credit Card
text: Credit Card: Credit Card (Joker). Effect: Go up to -$20 in debt. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $1. Sell Price: $1. Type: Economy. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Credit Card is a Common Economy Joker which allows you to have up to $20 in debt. It means you can spend an additional $20, even if your money is $0.

title: Credit Card
text: Credit Card: Note that if you're in debt and you sell the Credit Card, you cannot purchase anything until you climb out of the negatives. Usage notes: The Inflation and Golden Needle challenges start the player with a copy of Credit Card. Decks: Green Deck does not generate interest based on current money, which means being in debt does not hinder your income. Luxury Tax: When playing this challenge deck, hand size decreases by 1 for every $5, meaning that with a single credit card, the hand size can be increased by up to 4. Additionally, having a credit card makes it easier to avoid the hand size penalty while still being able to buy items from the shop.

title: Credit Card
text: Credit Card: Jokers: Vagabond allows you to get Tarot cards every time you play a hand with $4 or less. Staying in debt with the Credit Card assures you will create many Tarot cards. Credit Card: Although the wording may make it seem otherwise, multiple copies do stack, allowing you to go up to $40 in debt with two, up to $60 with three, etc., if that's something you would want. Credit Card cannot be copied by Blueprint or Brainstorm, but multiple copies can be obtained via Showman, Invisible Joker, or Ankh. Blinds: The Ox: Playing your most played hand this run sets money to $0, which can be used to wipe out Credit Card's debt.

title: Credit Card
text: Credit Card: The Tooth: Losing money is less detrimental with the ability to go into debt, but be careful, as you may lose a lot of money and go deeply below -$20. Consumables: Wraith sets your money to $0 after use, meaning you gain money if your balance was below $0. Decks: Rich get Richer: Since chips cannot exceed the current money, being in debt will prevent the player from scoring any points at all. Jokers: To the Moon: Without any money, no interest can be generated. Bull does not have any effect if you don't have any money. Bootstraps also has no effect for the same reason.

title: Credit Card
text: Credit Card: Bootstraps also has no effect for the same reason. Vouchers: Seed Money and Money Tree: No interest can be earned if the player is in debt. Consumables: The Hermit Tarot card (which normally doubles your money) gives no money if you have $0 or less.

title: Credit Card
text: Credit Card: Consumables: The Hermit Tarot card (which normally doubles your money) gives no money if you have $0 or less. Trivia: During the second demo, Credit Card cost $2 to buy. This was changed to $1 upon release, making Credit Card the cheapest Joker without using any Vouchers. It is also unique in that it can be bought and sold for the same price, meaning players can pick it up and later sell it and get a full refund. This may be a reference to the fact that in real life, most common credit cards are often free to apply for and have no annual fees.

title: Credit Card
text: Credit Card: Unlike other displayed money in game, the -$20 in the effect of credit card is in red. This is a reference to the red ink used in ledgers to show negative balances or losses. The card number on the card is entirely fictional, and does not correspond with any real-world providers. However, it can be broken down into: 867-5309, the phone number featured in the popular song of the same name by Tommy Tutone. 420 and 69, two numbers commonly used in memes and Internet-based humor. 1234, simply the first four numerals, often used in dummy credit card numbers. Interestingly, a 2012 study found that the 4-digit PIN 1234 is the most widely used out of all other combinations.

title: Credit Card
text: Credit Card: The full name of J. Joker Jr. on the credit card is Jerry Joker Jr according to LocalThunk. Credit Card is one of the few non-effect Jokers to have a consistent, unconditional, unchanging effect. The others are Joker and Golden Joker.

title: Delayed Gratification
text: Delayed Gratification: Delayed Gratification (Joker). Effect: Earn $2 per discard if no discards are used by end of the round. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Economy. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Delayed Gratification is a Common Economy Joker that provides $2 per discard if no discards are used during a round.

title: Delayed Gratification
text: Delayed Gratification: With the average deck giving 3 discards, Delayed Gratification will likely pay off $6 per blind early on. Blue Stake lowers this to 2 discards, making Delayed Gratification significantly worse for higher stakes. Usage notes: The Hook's forced discards will not prevent Delayed Gratification from taking effect. Decks: Red Deck provides an additional discard, which increases the money earned when this Joker is triggered. Painted Deck has a larger hand size, which increases the likelihood of drawing a strong Poker Hand without discarding. Green Deck already incentivizes using few discards.

title: Delayed Gratification
text: Delayed Gratification: Green Deck already incentivizes using few discards. Five-Card Draw and Golden Needle both start with 6 discards, which means Delayed Gratification can provide $12 if no discards are used. However, Golden Needle starts with only 1 hand, which can make it awkward to use Delayed Gratification. Poker hands: This Joker disincentivizes discarding, so it is recommended to play more common poker hands like High Card, Pair, Two Pair, or Three of a Kind. Jokers: Works well with any Jokers that reward you for not discarding, especially Banner, Green Joker, and Ramen. Any Joker that increases the number of discards (for example, Drunkard or Merry Andy) will benefit Delayed Gratification.

title: Delayed Gratification
text: Delayed Gratification: Any Joker that increases the number of discards (for example, Drunkard or Merry Andy) will benefit Delayed Gratification. Though Merry Andy decreases hand size, which could make it harder to form hands. Jokers that make poker hands easier to make, like Shortcut, Four Fingers, or Smeared Joker, give the player an opportunity to win the round without using discards. Jokers that affect hand size, like Juggler, Turtle Bean, and Troubadour, make it significantly easier to form hands without discarding. However, Troubadour has a -1 hand penalty, which increases the player's dependence on discards. Tags: Garbage Tag also rewards not using discards. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy each provide an additional +1 Discard when redeemed, allowing Delayed Gratification to generate more money.

title: Delayed Gratification
text: Delayed Gratification: Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy each provide an additional +1 Discard when redeemed, allowing Delayed Gratification to generate more money. Grabber and Nacho Tong each provide an extra hand, which lowers the player's dependence on discards. Decks: Black Deck makes it difficult to use Delayed Gratification due to its -1 hand per round. Blast Off is even worse due to its -2 hands and -1 discard per round. Poker hands: Without heavy deck modification, strong five-card hands like Flush, Straight, or Full House will be hard to assemble without using any discards. Jokers: Burglar removes all discards, rendering Delayed Gratification useless. Jokers that encourage discarding, like Castle, Mail-In Rebate, Faceless Joker, Burnt Joker, and Yorick, all have anti-synergy with Delayed Gratification.

title: Delayed Gratification
text: Delayed Gratification: Jokers that encourage discarding, like Castle, Mail-In Rebate, Faceless Joker, Burnt Joker, and Yorick, all have anti-synergy with Delayed Gratification. Mystic Summit is especially bad, as it requires having no discards remaining. Jokers that decrease hand size, like Merry Andy and Stuntman, could make it much harder to form hands, as Delayed Gratification heavily encourages not discarding. Card modifiers: A card with a Purple Seal needs to be discarded in order to get value from it, which disables Delayed Gratification. Vouchers: Telescope can work somewhat poorly with Delayed Gratification when playing towards big hands, as the player will constantly use hands as pseudo-discards, resulting in hands like High Card or Pair to be the most played hand.

title: Delayed Gratification
text: Delayed Gratification: Blinds: Starting with no discards, The Water prevents Delayed Gratification from taking effect. The Needle sets player's hands to 1 and may force a discard to be used, disabling Delayed Gratification. Stakes: On Blue Stake and higher, having one less discard means Delayed Gratification generates less money by default. Trivia: The hourglass is an ancient method of measuring time, with sand falling from the top bulb to the bottom. An hourglass symbol was also used by many computer systems to tell the user the system is busy and that they should wait until it is finished.

title: Delayed Gratification
text: Delayed Gratification: "Delayed gratification" is the act of resisting an immediate reward in favor of a longer-lasting, more substantial reward that will come later. This ties in with the ability of the Joker; the player is given extra money at the end of a blind by keeping all of their discards instead of immediately using them. This Joker has the longest name between all Jokers, with a total of 21 characters.

title: Devious Joker
text: Devious Joker: Devious Joker (Joker). Effect: +100 Chips if played hand contains a Straight. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Devious Joker is a Common Chips Joker that provides +100 Chips when playing a Straight. This also includes Straight Flush and Royal Flush.

title: Devious Joker
text: Devious Joker: Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World both work best with Devious Joker thanks to their smaller card count, allowing Straights to be formed easier. Painted Deck also works well with Devious Joker thanks to its larger hand size, allowing Straights to be formed easier. Plasma Deck benefits from the large amount of chips, which, when balanced, greatly boost the score for the played hand. 15 Minute City starts with an Eternal Shortcut, which allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand. Poker hands: Playing any Straight will trigger Devious Joker, including Straight Flush and Royal Flush. Jokers: Shortcut allows gaps in Straights, making them easier to find and play.

title: Devious Joker
text: Devious Joker: Jokers: Shortcut allows gaps in Straights, making them easier to find and play. Four Fingers allows Straights of length 4, making them easier to find and play. Runner gains Chips when playing a Straight. Crazy Joker gives +12 Mult when playing a Straight. The Order gives X3 Mult when playing a Straight. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy give additional discards, allowing the player to search for Straight hands easier. Paint Brush and Palette both increase hand size, which can help players with forming Straights. Decks: Erratic Deck's randomness can make it harder to assemble Straights. Five-Card Draw's -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straights.

title: Devious Joker
text: Devious Joker: Five-Card Draw's -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straights. Jokers: Jokers that reduce hand size, like Stuntman and Merry Andy, have anti-synergy with Devious Joker, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Consumables: Ectoplasm and Ouija have anti-synergy with Devious Joker, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Not only that, but Ouija converts all cards held in hand into one single rank, which makes assembling Straights very difficult. Blinds: The Manacle's -1 hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. The Water will always start with 0 discards, making it very hard to assemble Straights.

title: Devious Joker
text: Devious Joker: The Water will always start with 0 discards, making it very hard to assemble Straights. Trivia: This joker is part of a series that provides a Chips boost for a specific hand. The others are Sly Joker, Wily Joker, Clever Joker, and Crafty Joker. Much like the other Jokers in this series, this Joker has blue face paint over the mouth, indicating that they provide a bonus of Chips and not Mult like the red face paint Jokers.

title: Diet Cola
text: Diet Cola: Diet Cola (Joker). Effect: Sell this card to create a free Double Tag. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: ✗ No. Diet Cola is an Uncommon Effect Joker that creates a free Double Tag if it is sold, allowing the player to create a copy of the next tag they gain by skipping blinds.

title: Diet Cola
text: Diet Cola: Usage notes: The Non-Perishable challenge bans Diet Cola. Decks: Black Deck: The +1 Joker slot gives more chances to get Diet Cola without having to sell another Joker. Anaglyph Deck: Diet Cola's Double Tag can stack with the ones obtained after defeating a boss blind.

title: Diet Cola
text: Diet Cola: Anaglyph Deck: Diet Cola's Double Tag can stack with the ones obtained after defeating a boss blind. Jokers: Diet Cola synergizes with just about every build as long as the player has an open Joker slot. It is, in effect, a $3 Double Tag, if it is bought and sold immediately. Any build that is empowered by a tag is inherently empowered by buying and selling Diet Cola, unless the act of selling another Joker to make room for it temporarily is a negative act that outweighs the benefits the Double Tag gives. It is recommended to read up on all the Tags available to see all the potential synergies, as there are too many to list here.

title: Diet Cola
text: Diet Cola: Some particular Jokers that work well with Diet Cola: By definition, it is very strong with Throwback, as the player can get even more value out of skipping blinds (though Throwback does not receive additional scaling for each double tag spent). Diet Cola very mildly synergizes with Gift Card, as if the player waits a few rounds before selling the cola, they will lose less money overall. Selling Diet Cola can also help proc Campfire. Blueprint and Brainstorm are compatible with Diet Cola, selling either one while they are copying Diet Cola will also create a Double Tag. This would not be advisable, however, as Blueprint and Brainstorm are far more valuable than the Double Tag selling them would create.

title: Diet Cola
text: Diet Cola: Stakes: On Gold Stake, gaining a Rental Diet Cola and selling it immediately after buying it essentially gives the player a free Double Tag. Trivia: The design of the bottle on the card with the label reading "JOKE" resembles an old-fashioned glass bottle of Coca-Cola with their "COKE" branding. The circular patterned background of Diet Cola could resemble fizzy bubbles that form when carbon dioxide is released inside the drink. Diet Cola's design could have been red, but an oranger hue was chosen due to red being too "litigious." This card's effect may be referencing the fact that Tags superficially resemble bottle caps. Diet Cola is the only Joker with the ability to acquire a Tag.

title: Diet Cola
text: Diet Cola: Diet Cola is the only Joker with the ability to acquire a Tag. This Joker is part of the group of "Consumable" Jokers that can be destroyed with usage, dubbed "Food Jokers" due to their shared theme. The other Jokers in this group are Ice Cream, Popcorn, Gros Michel, Cavendish, Egg, Seltzer, Turtle Bean, and Ramen.

title: DNA
text: DNA: DNA (Joker). Effect: If first hand of round has only 1 card, add a permanent copy to deck and draw it to hand. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Effect. Activation: On Played. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. DNA is a Rare Effect Joker that adds a copy of a card to the deck (including all of its modifiers and additional chips from Hiker), given that it is the only card played on the first hand. After scoring, the original card is discarded, and the copy is drawn to hand. On its own, DNA provides minimal benefit and uses up a hand to copy a card. However, when synergized with card duplication strategies, DNA can power a machine that pushes scores way up.

title: DNA
text: DNA: Decks: Blue Deck gives an additional hand to play, which can be used to trigger DNA with fewer consequences. Red Deck gives an additional discard, which can help in finding a specific card for DNA to copy. Erratic Deck starts with uneven ranks and suits, so copying cards with DNA can help further inflate specific ranks/suits, which can allow the player to play higher ranking hands, like Four of a Kind, more consistently. Poker Hands: DNA works best with High Card, since it requires a High Card on the first hand to trigger. DNA also works especially well with strong hands that use duplicate cards, like Four of a Kind, Five of a Kind, Flush Five, or Flush House.

title: DNA
text: DNA: Jokers: Hologram increases by X0.25 Mult for every card copied by DNA. As a result, DNA can increase Hologram by X0.75 Mult per ante, on top of whatever other cards can be added to your deck. Blue Joker adds Chips based on the number of cards in the deck, which can be increased by DNA.

title: DNA
text: DNA: Blue Joker adds Chips based on the number of cards in the deck, which can be increased by DNA. Blueprint and Brainstorm can be combined with DNA to duplicate a card twice (or thrice if all three Jokers are used together), allowing the player to quickly fill the deck with high value cards. Additionally, it allows the player to immediately use more copies of the card they played. With all three jokers, playing one card will put three copies in hand, for a net of two extra copies available to use.

title: DNA
text: DNA: Trading Card pairs with DNA in deck manipulation, removing unwanted cards from the deck while DNA copies the necessary cards. It also increases the chances, through thinning the deck, of a specific card being drawn for DNA to copy. Drunkard and Merry Andy both give extra discards, which benefit DNA. While Merry Andy reduces hand size, which normally makes desired cards harder to find, the extra discards will make that punishment pretty much meaningless, as long as the player does not reduce their hand size much lower.

title: DNA
text: DNA: Anything that increases hand size will make it easier to find the desired card for DNA to copy. Juggler may be the best one, as even though it only increases hand size by 1, it has no punishments or limits. Troubadour and Turtle Bean can be used too, but the first one removes a hand, which makes it more punishing to use DNA, and the second one can only be used temporarily as it will give less hand size until it reaches 0. Acrobat and Dusk require playing to the final hand of the round to activate, making it less of a problem for DNA to monopolize the first hand.

title: DNA
text: DNA: In general, DNA synergizes with any Joker that requires specific cards: Steel Joker - Through duplication of Steel cards. Baron - Through duplication of Kings. Stone Joker - Through duplication of Stone cards. Shoot the Moon - Through duplication of Queens. Driver's License - Through duplication of cards with enhancements. Lucky Cat - Through duplication of Lucky cards, then playing them to trigger them. Golden Ticket - Through duplication of Gold cards, then playing them. Hit the Road - Through duplication of Jacks, then discarding them. Notably, for Jokers that consume cards, DNA can replicate the consumed cards, allowing them to be used multiple times:

title: DNA
text: DNA: Notably, for Jokers that consume cards, DNA can replicate the consumed cards, allowing them to be used multiple times: Sixth Sense also share triggering condition with DNA, so if the first hand is a single 6, DNA will replicate the 6 to be destroyed, effectively generating spectral cards with no cost. (The order of the two makes no difference. If DNA is on the right, the 6 will still be replicated after being destroyed.)

title: DNA
text: DNA: Vampire can be upgraded without cost through duplication of cards with enhanced effects. To achieve this, DNA needs to be placed on the left of Vampire, otherwise it will replicate card without enhancement. Note that the combination of the two will generally add many cards without enhancement to deck, hindering the effect of Vampire. Glass Joker - DNA can replenish broken Glass cards. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong both give additional hands to play, which can be used to trigger DNA with fewer consequences. Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give additional discards, which can help in finding a specific card for DNA to copy.

title: DNA
text: DNA: Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give additional discards, which can help in finding a specific card for DNA to copy. Paint Brush and Palette both increase hand size, which makes it easier to find the desired card for DNA to copy. Blinds: Any blind that disables cards in your deck (The Plant, The Club, etc.) will not prevent DNA from triggering, allowing you to still copy a disabled card for that round. This Joker is very easy to locate when playing against Amber Acorn, as it still shakes even when flipped face-down. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle all reduce the number of hands to play, which can discourage using DNA while a player's hands aren't strong enough.

title: DNA
text: DNA: Golden Needle is especially bad, as it only starts with one hand, which means that without a strong High Card build, DNA is unlikely to be a useful purchase. Poker Hands: DNA is weakest when building for Straight or Straight Flush, because it is harder to duplicate cards into runs than it is to duplicate cards into sets. Jokers: Erosion's effect depends on having fewer cards than you started with, and the cards added by DNA make it very difficult to get and stay under that limit. Unless with a build around High Cards, triggering DNA will waste one hand per round, which means Ice Cream and Seltzer will be depleted more quickly.

title: DNA
text: DNA: While Burglar gives extra hands to play with, it also removes discards. If the first hand of the round does not have the wanted card, DNA will miss its effect. Stuntman reduces hand size, which makes it harder to find the desired cards for DNA to copy. Vouchers: Telescope will likely identify High Card as the most-played hand because of all the card duplication being done, making it harder to find Planet cards for the player's preferred hand—unless that preferred hand is High Card. Hieroglyph's -1 hand makes it more punishing to use DNA, and Petroglyph's -1 discard makes it harder to find the desired cards for DNA to copy.

title: DNA
text: DNA: Blinds: The Needle limits the player to 1 hand which heavily discourages the use of DNA, unless the player can score high enough playing a single card. The Mouth only allows 1 hand type, so unless players build around High Cards, they must play a winning hand type first, missing DNA's effect. The Psychic requires 5 cards to be played, therefore disabling DNA as the illegal hand will not trigger its effect. The Pillar will debuff the copy of the card that DNA copied after playing the first hand, even if the card played isn't debuffed, preventing benefits from modifiers and seals. If Crimson Heart debuffs DNA on the first hand, it cannot duplicate any card.

title: DNA
text: DNA: If Crimson Heart debuffs DNA on the first hand, it cannot duplicate any card. Stakes: On Blue Stake difficulty or higher, there is a -1 Discard penalty which can make it harder to find the specific card for DNA to copy. Trivia: DNA is one of only three Jokers that add cards to your deck. The others are Marble Joker and Certificate.

title: DNA
text: DNA: DNA, short for Deoxyribonucleic acid, is one of the "building blocks" of life, involved in the growth and development of all known organisms and many viruses. The card image is a typical representation of a double-helix, a section of a DNA strand. The four different colors connecting the strands together represent the four key ingredients of DNA: adenine, cytosine, thymine, and guanine. DNA is tied with Egg for the shortest Joker name in Balatro, containing only 3 letters.

title: Driver's License
text: Driver's License: Driver's License (Joker). Effect: X3 Mult if you have at least 16 Enhanced cards in your full deck, (Currently 0). Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Enhance 16 cards in your deck. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Driver's License is a Rare Multiplicative Mult Joker that provides X3 Mult if your full deck contains at least 16 enhanced cards. It is unlocked using this same condition.

title: Driver's License
text: Driver's License: It has little to no utility early on in a run due to its steep activation requirement, but by stacking a lot of enhancements early using other Jokers and Tarot cards, or opening lots of Standard packs, it can help secure a win by providing a significant boost in Mult, especially when stacked with other multiplicative Jokers. It is important to note that it only provides X3 Mult once no matter how much enhanced cards you have in deck (having 32 enhanced cards will not trigger the effect twice). Decks: Yellow Deck: The bonus $10 allows for better econ in early to mid game to afford Booster packs.

title: Driver's License
text: Driver's License: Decks: Yellow Deck: The bonus $10 allows for better econ in early to mid game to afford Booster packs. Magic Deck: Starting with two copies of The Fool, this can get the player's number of enhanced cards up to 6 at the first shop, nearly half of the required amount to activate Driver's License. Zodiac Deck: Increased Tarot cards in shop means more chance to get enhancement cards. Anaglyph Deck: Skipping for Charm Tag, Ethereal Tag or Standard Tag can accelerate Driver's License. Fragile starts with all 52 cards as Glass cards, meaning that Driver's License will be immediately activated, but be aware if your deck reaches to 15 or less cards.

title: Driver's License
text: Driver's License: On a similar note, Medusa starts with 12 Stone cards and an Eternal Marble Joker, meaning that Driver's License will become active after Round 4 Jokers: Jokers that add enhanced cards to your deck or change cards into enhanced ones like Marble Joker, Midas Mask, or DNA can help activate Driver's License a lot sooner. Combining Midas Mask with Pareidolia is extremely effective for this instance as it can turn all scored cards into Gold cards, activating Driver's License at a record pace. Vagabond can also create many enhanced cards very quickly. Any Joker that relies on specific enhancements, such as Lucky Cat and Steel Joker, work well with Driver's License.

title: Driver's License
text: Driver's License: Any Joker that relies on specific enhancements, such as Lucky Cat and Steel Joker, work well with Driver's License. Glass Joker in particular can make up for Glass cards breaking. Consumables: Driver's License requires a large amount of enhanced cards, therefore consumables that adds enhancement are important to get this Joker online fast: The Magician, The Empress, and The Hierophant are preferred as they enhance up to 2 cards at once. The Lovers, The Chariot, The Devil, Justice, and The Tower are alternative Tarot cards that enhance 1 card each. Death can be used to duplicate an enhanced card as well.

title: Driver's License
text: Driver's License: Death can be used to duplicate an enhanced card as well. Familiar, Grim, and Incantation are useful to increase the number enhanced cards in your deck, but be wary that they could destroy an enhanced card as well, subtracting one from the net gain. Cryptid can be used on an already enhanced card. Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon may also prove useful to find more tarot cards to apply enhancement with.

title: Driver's License
text: Driver's License: Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon may also prove useful to find more tarot cards to apply enhancement with. Illusion allows the player to buy enhanced playing cards in the Shop, which can be useful to help get Driver's License online faster. This can be further increased with help from Overstock and Overstock Plus to increase the shop selection, and Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut to make rerolls cheaper. Crystal Ball gives an extra consumable slot, allowing the player to hold more consumables that are useful for Driver's License. Omen Globe allows for the Spectral cards mentioned above to appear in Arcana packs.

title: Driver's License
text: Driver's License: Omen Globe allows for the Spectral cards mentioned above to appear in Arcana packs. Decks: Nebula Deck works somewhat poorly with Driver's License, as its -1 consumable slot penalty does not allow for many useful consumables to be held at once. Blast Off makes Driver's License harder to activate due to the starting Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon vouchers, which reduce the probabilities of Tarot cards appearing in the shop. Jokers: Vampire is not a good Joker to combine with Driver's License, as any played enhanced card will get the enhancement removed and leave Driver's License useless. Vouchers: Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon reduce the probability of Tarot cards appearing in the shop.

title: Driver's License
text: Driver's License: Vouchers: Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon reduce the probability of Tarot cards appearing in the shop. Trivia: The name of the driver in this Joker is "Jen Joker", with her date of birth being December 3, 1995. The license expired on January 24, 2025. In the Balatro demo, the name used to read "Jeb Joker" instead (which can still be seen in the signature on the license). The art of this joker also displays some information that provided on common driver's licenses of the US/Canada: DD number, the Document Discriminator which is a unique number on license to determine its authenticity, is 1104961341. Height (HT) is 6'0". Eye color (EY), usually represented by 2-3 letter abbreviations, is BRN (brown).

title: Driver's License
text: Driver's License: Height (HT) is 6'0". Eye color (EY), usually represented by 2-3 letter abbreviations, is BRN (brown). Organ donor status, displayed as a red symbol (usually a heart shape in reality) and the "donor" on it. Jen Joker has a degree from Lehigh University in Electrical Engineering and works in Aurora, Colorado. Jen has never met Jimbo. The number of enhanced cards needed to activate this Joker might be a reference to a common age required to be able to obtain a real driver's license. In Colorado, Jen's likely state of residence, the minimum age to obtain a driver's license is 16. Likewise, in LocalThunk's home province of Saskatchewan, the minimum eligible driving age without an educational course is 16.

title: Droll Joker
text: Droll Joker: Droll Joker (Joker). Effect: +10 Mult if played hand contains a Flush. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Droll Joker is a Common Additive Mult Joker that gives +10 Mult if the hand contains a Flush. This includes hands that include any Flush, such as a Flush House.

title: Droll Joker
text: Droll Joker: Decks: Magic Deck helps a fair amount in getting flushes, as multiple tarot cards can change a card into a certain suit. Ghost Deck, like the Magic Deck, helps as a lot of Spectral cards may help in getting a lot of your cards into one Suit. Checkered Deck may be the best deck for this Joker, as flushes are extremely easy due to the deck only containing two suits to start with. Zodiac Deck can help you buy tarot cards to change your deck into one suit. Erratic Deck can sometimes be extremely good for flushes, depending on the contents of your deck.

title: Droll Joker
text: Droll Joker: Erratic Deck can sometimes be extremely good for flushes, depending on the contents of your deck. Poker hands: This Joker works with Flush and Straight Flush as well as 2 of the hidden hands, Flush House and Flush Five. Jokers: Crafty Joker and The Tribe always activate at the same time as this Joker. Four Fingers and Smeared Joker help in making it easier to create flushes. Depending on your deck and which suit you are playing off of, one of the pairs of Greedy Joker/ Rough Gem, Lusty Joker/ Bloodstone, Wrathful Joker/ Arrowhead or Gluttonous Joker/ Onyx Agate can work for diamonds, hearts, spades and clubs respectively. Consumables: Tarot cards:

title: Droll Joker
text: Droll Joker: Consumables: Tarot cards: The Moon, The Star, The Sun, and The World turn cards into Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, and Spades, respectively, which can be useful if the player wants their deck to focus on one or two suits. The Hanged Man can be useful for cutting unwanted cards out the deck if the player wants to focus on one particular card suit. The Lovers turns a card into a Wild card, which can be useful for forming a Flush if the player needs another card. Spectral cards: Sigil turns all cards in hand into a particular suit, which can make creating Flushes a lot more consistent.

title: Droll Joker
text: Droll Joker: Sigil turns all cards in hand into a particular suit, which can make creating Flushes a lot more consistent. Trivia: This joker is part of a series which provide a Mult boost for a specific hand. The others are Jolly Joker, Zany Joker, Mad Joker and Crazy Joker. While in modern times, "droll" means "humorous in an odd way", it is also an archaic name for "joker" or "buffoon". Droll Joker can thus be read as the tautology "joker joker".

title: Drunkard
text: Drunkard: Drunkard (Joker). Effect: +1 discard each round. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Drunkard is a Common Effect Joker that provides +1 discard each round, making it easier to search for specific cards.

title: Drunkard
text: Drunkard: Decks: Green Deck in particular synergizes well as the player earns money for leftover discards. Poker hands: All hands can benefit from Drunkard, as it makes it easier to search for the desired cards. Jokers: Drunkard has synergy with: Jokers that activate when discarding specific cards, suits, or hands: Trading Card when discarding a single card. Hit the Road when discarding Jacks. Faceless Joker when discarding 3+ face cards. Burnt Joker when discarding any Poker Hand. Mail-In Rebate when discarding the random rank chosen. Castle when discarding the random suit chosen. "Remaining discards" Jokers: Banner gives more chips if the player has more discards. Delayed Gratification provides $2 per discard if no discards are used.

title: Drunkard
text: Drunkard: Delayed Gratification provides $2 per discard if no discards are used. Jokers that want to play a specific, difficult to find hand: Séance wants to play a Straight Flush. Superposition wants to play a Straight that includes an Ace. Card Sharp wants you to play the same Poker Hand twice. The Family wants to play a Four of a Kind. Yorick to help scale Yorick faster. Modifiers: Purple Seal: The extra discard provides more opportunities to generate more Tarot cards. Stakes: Drunkard restores a discard lost from playing Blue Stake and above. Jokers: Burglar as it removes all discards (no matter the order of the 2 Jokers). Green Joker as it gets -1 Mult for every discard used.

title: Drunkard
text: Drunkard: Green Joker as it gets -1 Mult for every discard used. Ramen as any discard reduces its XMult. Blinds: The Water will always set your discards to 0, making Drunkard useless. Trivia: According to LocalThunk, Drunkard is throwing the bottle, as if discarding it. It has a very similar theme to Juggler, both in effect and card design.

title: Dusk
text: Dusk: Dusk (Joker). Effect: Retrigger all played cards in final hand of the round. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Retrigger. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Dusk is an Uncommon Retrigger Joker that triggers all played cards in the final hand twice, effectively doubling their scored chips and any potential enhancement they have, like Bonus, Mult, Foil, Holographic, and Polychrome. Note that Dusk does not retrigger a Red Seal. A card with a Red Seal will only activate three times: once for the initial trigger, once for the Red Seal, and then lastly, for Dusk.

title: Dusk
text: Dusk: Decks: Black Deck reduces the available Hands for the player by -1, making it less punishing for the player to use their final hand. Similarly, Blast Off reduces the available Hands for the player by -2, making it less punishing for the player to use their final hand. Golden Needle reduces the player's Hands to 1, meaning Dusk is automatically activated. Poker hands: Dusk works best with five card hands, such as Flushes and Straights, due to these giving Dusk more cards to retrigger, thus giving a higher score. Jokers: Dusk synergizes well with Hack when playing low-ranked cards, as they allow each card to be triggered three times.

title: Dusk
text: Dusk: Jokers: Dusk synergizes well with Hack when playing low-ranked cards, as they allow each card to be triggered three times. Similarly to Hack, Sock and Buskin synergizes well with Dusk, as it allows face cards to be triggered more. Acrobat is a good pair with Dusk, provided players have a lot of Mult cards and +Mult Jokers ready for the final hand. Troubadour's -1 Hand penalty becomes mostly irrelevant as Dusk only activates on the final hand. As with all retrigger Jokers, any Joker that cares about certain cards being scored goes well with Dusk. Notable examples are Bloodstone and Triboulet, as their XMult effects stack.

title: Dusk
text: Dusk: Hiker has incredible synergy with Dusk, as not only will Hiker scale cards twice as fast, but the retriggering of the cards will also give their chips again. Lucky Cat can scale twice as fast since the Lucky cards it will be using to scale have twice as many chances to earn +20 Mult or $20. As Glass cards are substantially powerful with Dusk's retriggers, Glass Joker can be a nice addition to still get value when they break. Vouchers: Hieroglyph's -1 Hand penalty is less punishing as the player will need to exhaust all hands to make use of Dusk regardless. Blinds: The Needle will reduce hands available to 1, meaning Dusk will always trigger.

title: Dusk
text: Dusk: Blinds: The Needle will reduce hands available to 1, meaning Dusk will always trigger. Decks: Green Deck gives no interest, instead gaining $2/Hand and $1/Discard remaining. Using all your hands to trigger Dusk means losing most of your income. Jokers: Dusk will deplete Seltzer and Ice Cream faster, as Dusk requires the player to exhaust all hands to trigger. Blinds: If Crimson Heart debuffs Dusk on the final hand, it cannot retrigger any card. Trivia: Dusk is usually considered to be the time near the end of twilight, before night begins. There are technically three 'stages' of dusk and twilight, depending on the light levels being considered: civil dusk, nautical dusk, and astronomical dusk.

title: Dusk
text: Dusk: The card art depicts saguaro cacti, which grow only in the Sonoran Desert, an area known for its brilliant sunsets. It is based on LocalThunk's tour in the Sonoran Desert.

title: Egg
text: Egg: Egg (Joker). Effect: Gains $3 of sell value at end of round. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Economy. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Egg is a Common Economy Joker which gains $3 of sell value each round, and has no other effect. It can help with some joker synergies, or simply be cashed in after a few rounds for a small profit.

title: Egg
text: Egg: Usage Notes: The Omelette challenge starts the player with 5 copies of Egg. Decks: The Green Deck cannot generate interest, and can especially benefit from alternative income sources like Egg. Poker hands: This Joker does not add Chips or Mult, so no hand benefits or suffers from it. Jokers: Swashbuckler can combo with Egg to gain Mult each round, but will lose it if Egg is sold. While Debuffed, Egg will still provide Mult for Swashbuckler. Ceremonial Dagger can be used to sacrifice Egg for a permanent Mult bonus.

title: Egg
text: Egg: Ceremonial Dagger can be used to sacrifice Egg for a permanent Mult bonus. Tarot cards: The money given by Temperance scales with the sell value of the player's Jokers. The longer players have Egg, the more money they'll get from Temperance, even potentially hitting the maximum value of $50 they can get from the Tarot card. Vouchers: Hieroglyph and Petroglyph send the player back an Ante, giving players more time to scale Egg's sell value. Decks: Anaglyph Deck incentives skipping blinds due to its Double Tag gimmick, which gives Egg less chances to increase its sell value.

title: Egg
text: Egg: Since Painted Deck and Blast Off only have 4 Joker slots instead of the typical 5, taking Egg is much more risky since it doesn't immediately help the player score and its only purpose is to be sold. Cruelty makes it even more difficult and risky to use Egg, as this deck only has 3 Joker slots. Non-Perishable makes every Joker Eternal, including Egg, which means it cannot be sold. Jokers: Throwback encourages skipping blinds to scale the XMult of the Joker, once again giving Egg less opportunity to increase its sell value.

title: Egg
text: Egg: Stakes: On Black Stake and above, there is a chance for an Egg to be Eternal, which makes it impossible to sell if picked up, nullifying the main point of the Joker. On Gold Stake, an Egg can be Rental, taking away $3 from the player every round, which is usually not worth the sell value increase. Trivia: LocalThunk has confirmed Egg is a reference to: Northernlion, a Twitch streamer and YouTuber who has played Balatro. The term "nest egg", which is a reserve or investment of money for the future, fitting for the Joker's gimmick of its sell value gradually increasing each round. Egg is tied with DNA for the shortest Joker name in Balatro, containing only 3 letters.

title: Egg
text: Egg: Egg is tied with DNA for the shortest Joker name in Balatro, containing only 3 letters. This Joker is part of the group of "Consumable" Jokers that can be destroyed with usage, dubbed "Food Jokers" due to their shared theme. The other Jokers in this group are Ice Cream, Popcorn, Gros Michel, Cavendish, Seltzer, Turtle Bean, Ramen, and Diet Cola. Egg is one of the few "food jokers" to get merch from Makeship in the recently campaigned Food Joker Pin Set alongside Popcorn and Ice Cream.

title: Erosion
text: Erosion: Erosion (Joker). Effect: +4 Mult for each card below [the deck's starting size] in your full deck, (Currently +0 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Erosion is an Uncommon Additive Mult Joker that gains +4 Mult for each card that's removed from the current deck from its original starting size (52 cards in general, 40 cards for the Abandoned Deck, and 32 cards for Mad World). For example, Erosion will give +40 Mult if there are 10 cards missing from the original deck. If the deck is equal to or greater than the original deck size, it gives +0 Mult.

title: Erosion
text: Erosion: Decks: Erosion has synergy with all decks, since most players generally want to reduce their deck size anyway in order to draw more reliably. However, it is especially powerful when used with these decks: Zodiac Deck can provide more Tarot cards in the Shop with its starting Tarot Merchant, potentially increasing the odds of getting The Hanged Man. Ghost Deck allows for Spectral cards to appear in the Shop, which can potentially include Immolate. Erosion works extremely well on Fragile, as the player starts with a 52 card deck full of Glass cards that are guaranteed to break by virtue of having 2 Oops! All 6s upon starting the challenge.

title: Erosion
text: Erosion: Poker hands: If the player can choose which cards to destroy, it may be useful to build towards higher-scoring hands, such as Four of a Kind or Full House. If not, it may be best to focus on smaller hands, such as Two Pair or Three of a Kind. Jokers: Trading Card is able to destroy one card once per round giving Erosion +4 Mult each time. Sixth Sense can destroy a 6 once per round, and potentially provide an Immolate card. Tarot generating Jokers like Cartomancer or Vagabond can give access to The Hanged Man and Justice, or The Fool to copy them.

title: Erosion
text: Erosion: Glass Joker gains X0.75 Mult every time a Glass card is destroyed. Reducing the deck size by breaking glass cards can benefit both these Jokers. Canio gains an additional X1 Mult for every face card destroyed, making it an especially powerful partner with Erosion. Consumables: The Hanged Man and Immolate destroy 2 and 5 cards respectively, boosting Erosion's effect significantly. Justice can create Glass cards, which can break and be destroyed. Vouchers: Omen Globe allows for Spectral cards to appear in Arcana Packs, which potentially increases the odds of getting Immolate.

title: Erosion
text: Erosion: Vouchers: Omen Globe allows for Spectral cards to appear in Arcana Packs, which potentially increases the odds of getting Immolate. Decks: Abandoned Deck might have anti-synergy with Erosion, as it has only 40 cards instead of 52. Since there are less cards, erosion has a lower ceiling on the maximum mult it can give. Mad World starts with a 32 card deck, making it extremely difficult to earn value from Erosion with a ceiling even lower than the Abandoned Deck. Medusa and Monolith don't work well with Erosion, as these decks both start with an Eternal Marble Joker, which makes Erosion very hard to scale.

title: Erosion
text: Erosion: Jokers: Blue Joker gives additional + Chips based on the size of player's deck, so it will provide less benefit as the player reduces their deck size for Erosion. Jokers that add playing cards to the player's deck reduce the amount of + Mult Erosion can provide. This includes: Certificate, DNA, and Marble Joker. Hologram wants the player to add more cards to their deck, which reduces Erosion's mult. Consumables: The Spectral cards Familiar, Incantation, Grim, and Cryptid add playing cards to the deck, lowering Erosion's + Mult.

title: Erosion
text: Erosion: Consumables: The Spectral cards Familiar, Incantation, Grim, and Cryptid add playing cards to the deck, lowering Erosion's + Mult. Trivia: Erosion is the environmental process of the removal (and subsequent deposition) of material due to natural forces, typically weather. The removal of cards from a deck could thus be considered a kind of erosion of the deck.

title: Even Steven
text: Even Steven: Even Steven (Joker). Effect: Played cards with even rank give +4 Mult when scored, (10, 8, 6, 4, 2). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Even Steven is a Common Additive Mult Joker that provides +4 Mult when cards with an even rank are scored. In Balatro, the even ranks are 2s, 4s, 6s, 8s, and 10s.

title: Even Steven
text: Even Steven: Synergies: Even Steven is a decent source of +Mult that triggers through cards, effectively being +20 Mult if all played cards are even and trigger once. It works very well as an early-game source of Mult, but can fall off unless heavily built around (and even then, it isn't the best Joker to build around). Decks: Abandoned Deck works very well with Steven, since it allows the player to find even ranks more easily. It makes even cards about 20% more common to draw (in an unaltered deck). Mad World will also work as well, although this deck doesn't start with any 10s.

title: Even Steven
text: Even Steven: Mad World will also work as well, although this deck doesn't start with any 10s. Magic Deck's Fools can be used to turn many odd cards into evens with Strengths, or copy a strong even card with Deaths. Poker hands: Steven works best with hands that play five even cards. This is mainly Full House, though Four of a Kind may work well with its higher base chips, and later Five of a Kind. Flushes can serve as a decent alternative, since they can be easier to find and will still (ideally) contain some even cards.

title: Even Steven
text: Even Steven: Jokers: Even Steven is, in essence, a more effective version of the sinful Jokers (the ones that give +3 Mult per scored card of a certain suit). In an unaltered deck, the chance an even card is drawn is ~38%, compared to the 25% of a specific suit, and it gives more Mult. In exchange, it's harder to build around since there are fewer rank-changing methods than suit changers, and it can be harder to make a Full House than a Flush due to the specific even cards being harder to find.

title: Even Steven
text: Even Steven: As with every Joker that triggers an effect when a card is scored, retrigger Jokers increase the effect of Steven by an order of magnitude. Steven itself isn't a great Joker to build a retrigger strategy around, but combined with a source of X Mult from played cards, like Ancient Joker or Glass cards, it can be a valid strategy. Tarot generators also work well with Steven, because of Glass cards and even rank preference from Even Steven.

title: Even Steven
text: Even Steven: Tarot generators also work well with Steven, because of Glass cards and even rank preference from Even Steven. Because Steven is best used as an early-game method of boosting Mult, combining it with Economy Jokers is very beneficial. The earlier Antes can be easily cleared in 1 or 2 hands with Steven, meaning you will be looking for more powerful Jokers or other forms of scaling, which is what Economy Jokers help you afford. Walkie Talkie lets you give another boost to 10s and 4s, though without retriggers having both can be a bit of a waste of Joker slots.

title: Even Steven
text: Even Steven: Wee Joker gets buffed for every 2 that scores. Comboing it with Steven lets you play weaker 2-based hands and still gain a decent score. Ride the Bus provides a decent source of scaling that uses Steven very effectively, since even cards are already more desirable with Bus. Consumables: Tarot cards: The Hanged Man can be used to destroy non-even numbered cards in order to make the even numbered ones easier to find. Death can be used to turn other cards into even numbered cards in order to maximize the Mult value. Strength can be used to turn odd numbers into even numbers and Aces into 2s.

title: Even Steven
text: Even Steven: Strength can be used to turn odd numbers into even numbers and Aces into 2s. The Hierophant and Justice provide a lot of Chips and Multipicative Mult to help boost Even Steven's Mult bonus. Spectral cards: Deja Vu can apply a Red Seal onto some even cards, which allows for more Even Steven triggers. Cryptid can create more copies of even cards. Incantation also has the possibility to make more even-ranked cards with random enhancements at the cost of sacrificing a card to be destroyed. Trivia: "Even Steven" is a way of saying something is evenly matched or evenly split between things. "I split the cake with my friend even-steven".

title: Even Steven
text: Even Steven: Even Steven has a single red off-color pixel on the third bauble of his frill; this color does not appear anywhere else in the Balatro palette. Even Steven is similar in style to Odd Todd, which gives Chips for odd ranks instead. Due to his theming of even numbers, Even Steven's hat baubles, frill baubles, and eyes are all even, the opposite from Odd Todd. Specifically, Even Steven has two sides to his hat and two baubles and has four frill baubles. Even Steven being red as opposed to Odd Todd's blue ties into his ability to provide additive Mult to your score.

title: Even Steven
text: Even Steven: Even Steven is another Joker to get merchandise from Makeship alongside Odd Todd as part of a Combo Pack mini-plush set.

title: Faceless Joker
text: Faceless Joker: Faceless Joker (Joker). Effect: Earn $5 if 3 or more face cards are discarded at the same time. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Economy. Activation: On Discard. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Faceless Joker is a Common Economy Joker which provides $5 if 3 or more face cards are discarded simultaneously. Debuffed face cards do not count towards this total.

title: Faceless Joker
text: Faceless Joker: Decks: Red Deck gives +1 Discard, allowing more chances to discard and dig for face cards. Golden Needle removes money when discarding, and Faceless Joker is an effective counter to this. Poker hands: Because this Joker requires discarding face cards, which provide lots of Chips, it's recommended to build toward weaker hands like High Card, Pair, or Two Pair. Jokers: Pareidolia makes it so that all cards are considered face cards, effectively guaranteeing $5 per every 3 cards discarded. Drunkard gives +1 Discard, allowing more chances to find and discard face cards. Merry Andy gives +3 Discards, allowing more chances to find and discard face cards.

title: Faceless Joker
text: Faceless Joker: Merry Andy gives +3 Discards, allowing more chances to find and discard face cards. Blueprint and Brainstorm can copy Faceless Joker to effectively double/triple amount of money gained with no downside as they can be moved around to buff scoring Jokers afterward. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy give additional discards, allowing more chances to find and discard face cards. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Medusa start with no face cards, making Faceless Joker useless at the beginning unless paired with Pareidolia. Blast Off doesn't work well with Faceless Joker, as this deck only starts with 2 discards.

title: Faceless Joker
text: Faceless Joker: Blast Off doesn't work well with Faceless Joker, as this deck only starts with 2 discards. Jokers: Jokers that benefit from playing or keeping face cards, such as Scary Face or Baron, are worse as Faceless Joker incentivizes discarding face cards. Possible exceptions are if Pareidolia is used or if the deck is heavily manipulated for face cards. Any Jokers that benefit from not using Discards like Delayed Gratification or Banner have anti-synergy with Faceless Joker. Burglar removes all discards, effectively disabling Faceless Joker. Blinds: The Water starts with 0 discards, making Faceless Joker useless for the round. The Plant debuffs all face cards, rendering Faceless Joker useless for the round.

title: Faceless Joker
text: Faceless Joker: The Plant debuffs all face cards, rendering Faceless Joker useless for the round. Stakes: Blue Stake and above hinder Faceless Joker's potential because of how they have 1 less discard by default. Trivia: The art is identical to the basic Joker in all ways, except for the lack of facial features.

title: Fibonacci
text: Fibonacci: Fibonacci (Joker). Effect: Each played Ace, 2, 3, 5, or 8 gives +8 Mult when scored. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Fibonacci is an Uncommon Additive Mult Joker that gives +8 Mult every time an Ace, 2, 3, 5, or 8 scores.

title: Fibonacci
text: Fibonacci: Decks: Thanks to the absence of face cards, Abandoned Deck has a greater concentration of cards favorable by Fibonacci, and thus works really well with it. Mad World will also work as well, although this deck doesn't start with any Aces. Poker hands: As Three of a Kind, Full House and Four of a Kind all utilize a number of the same rank, they often work really well with Fibonacci. Low-ended Straight also makes great use of Fibonacci. Flush is difficult early on, but can earn +40 Mult from Fibonacci in an unmodified deck, and diligent suit conversion can make triggering Fibonacci a simple matter of picking ranks.

title: Fibonacci
text: Fibonacci: Jokers: Hack retriggers 2s, 3s and 5s, giving at least +8 Mult when one of the ranks is played and scored. Scholar also triggers off of Aces. Wee Joker gains +8 Chips when a 2 is scored, on top of the +8 Mult provided by Fibonacci. Hanging Chad retriggers the first scoring card in a played hand twice, giving +16 Mult if the first scored card triggers Fibonacci. Ride the Bus accumulates +Mult very easily when paired with Fibonacci, since the player wants to use ranks that are not face cards, boosting Ride the Bus in the process.

title: Fibonacci
text: Fibonacci: Shortcut lets the player utilize the rare scenario of the Straight A 3 5 7 8 or A 2 3 [4] 5 [6/7] for maximum Fibonacci value. A 2 3 5 8 is, unfortunately, not a valid Straight even with Shortcut. Splash allows tossing Fibonacci cards into a poker hand that otherwise wouldn't score them for extra Mult. Smeared Joker can make Flush builds easier early on by enabling such hands as ♦️A ♦️3 ♥️A ♥️5 ♥️8. Odd Todd gives +31 Chips for Aces, 5s and 3s. Even Steven gives +4 Mult for 8s and 2s.

title: Fibonacci
text: Fibonacci: Odd Todd gives +31 Chips for Aces, 5s and 3s. Even Steven gives +4 Mult for 8s and 2s. Consumables: Suit Tarots (The Moon, The World, The Star, and The Sun) can convert Fibonacci cards into a single suit, making it simpler to play them in Flushes, and The Lovers can assist this strategy early on before the suits are sufficiently uniform. Grim adds 2 Aces to the deck but might destroy a useful card for Fibonacci in the process. Incantation can add 2s, 3s, 5s or 8s to the deck but might destroy a useful card for Fibonacci in the process.

title: Fibonacci
text: Fibonacci: Decks: 15 Minute City doesn't work well with Fibonacci due to lack of Aces, 2s, and 3s by default. Trivia: The Fibonacci sequence is a mathematical pattern where the next number in the pattern is found by adding the two previous numbers together. It can be found in nature, such as in how certain plants flower or fruits grow. If the pattern is started with zero/one, it goes: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, and so on. This is represented by the ranks Ace (1), 2, 3, 5 and 8 triggering it, its effect of +8 Mult for those cards, and its price of $8.

title: Fibonacci
text: Fibonacci: The card art shows a Fibonacci spiral, an approximation of the Golden spiral. The distance between the center and the spiral gets multiplied by a certain factor for every quarter turn it makes. This factor approaches the golden ratio (≈1.618) as the Fibonacci numbers approach infinity. There's a single green off-color pixel between the spiral and the small blue square, which has been present since the very first public release. In other media: Fibonacci is referenced as a weapon in the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors, albeit with the appearance of Seltzer.

title: Flash Card
text: Flash Card: Flash Card (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains +2 Mult per reroll in the shop, (Currently +0 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Flash Card is an Uncommon scaling Additive Mult Joker that permanently gains +2 Mult every time the player reroll in the shop. The increase is not retroactive and will only start scaling after purchase, meaning it is always +0 Mult initially.

title: Flash Card
text: Flash Card: Decks: Decks that generate more money than usual are stronger with Flash Card, mainly Yellow Deck and Green Deck. Green Deck in particular is good with it early, as one can spend as much money on rerolls as they want without worrying about losing interest. Zodiac Deck may work well with Flash Card, as the player may want to reroll frequently to see more Tarot and Planet cards. Poker hands: No poker hands inherently work better than others with Flash Card. All potential benefits come from other synergies. Jokers: Chaos the Clown grants 1 free reroll per shop, effectively giving Flash Card +2 Mult gain per shop visit on top of paid rerolls.

title: Flash Card
text: Flash Card: Economy Jokers are critical to Flash Card's success. Being able to get more money translates directly into more Mult. Particularly helpful are scaling Economy Jokers, like Cloud 9 and Rocket, though most of them will work. Campfire is very good with Flash Card, as the large amount of rerolls being performed and strong economy allows many cards to be sold, scaling Campfire very high. Buying and selling planets from Astronomer found with rerolls will allow you to recuperate some of the money spent from rerolling. Other Jokers that give XMult are helpful, as they allow Flash Card's scaling to be more effective. Particularly, Constellation can scale very quickly, as every reroll can create a planet card.

title: Flash Card
text: Flash Card: As the player will be spending lots of money to scale Flash Card, Vagabond can be a good addition to the build, especially considering that it can generate Temperance to further increase Flash Card's value. Vouchers: Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut both make rerolls cheaper, allowing for Flash Card to scale more. Hieroglyph and Petroglyph allow you to see more shops and play more blinds, allowing for greater scaling. Overstock and Overstock Plus Vouchers make rerolls more valuable, as you get to see more cards when doing so. Hone and Glow Up will create more Editioned Jokers, making good Editioned Jokers have a higher chance to show up.

title: Flash Card
text: Flash Card: Hone and Glow Up will create more Editioned Jokers, making good Editioned Jokers have a higher chance to show up. Planet Merchant, Planet Tycoon, Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon can be strong with builds that benefit from those cards, as they provide cards to buy even when your Joker slots are full. Modifiers: Gold cards, Lucky cards, and Gold Seal generate money mid-round, allowing Flash Card to scale more. Tags: D6 Tag while skipping one shop, makes reroll start at $0 at the next shop, saving up to $5 on every reroll in that shop.

title: Flash Card
text: Flash Card: Decks: Black Deck starts with -1 Hand per round, making Economy more difficult to set up early game. This directly limits Flash Card's scaling opportunities as less Hands per round earns the player less Money overall when defeating Blinds. Similarly, Blast Off starts with -2 hands per round, limiting the player's money even more. Golden Needle only starts with 1 hand per round, which means the player will not get money from extra hands under normal circumstances. Jokers: Bull and Bootstraps respectively gain Chips and Mult relative to the player's current Money. Spending Money on rerolls to scale Flash Card will therefore weaken the scoring power of these Jokers.

title: Flash Card
text: Flash Card: Blinds: The Ox sets the player's Money to 0 upon playing the most played Poker Hand of the run, making it potentially difficult to recover Economy for Flash Card scaling. Trivia: Flash cards, or flashcards, are cards normally used as memory aids for learning new topics, often by repeatedly cycling through them to be effective, similar to how rerolling improves this card's effect. The type of flash card this Joker is referencing is based on alphabetical flash cards being used to teach uppercase and lowercase letters as well as a picture and/or word based on the letter being taught.

title: Flash Card
text: Flash Card: In early demo versions, the color of Flash Card was blue. This is changed later to match the color of the reroll button in shop.

title: Flower Pot
text: Flower Pot: Flower Pot (Joker). Effect: X3 Mult if poker hand contains a Diamond card, Club card, Heart card, and Spade card. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Reach Ante level 8. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Flower Pot is an Uncommon Multiplicative Mult Joker that rewards the player with X3 Mult for playing at least one scoring card of every suit. Flower Pot can only trigger when at least 4 cards are scored in a given hand.

title: Flower Pot
text: Flower Pot: Cards with multiple suits (such as Wild cards or cards affected by Smeared Joker) will only count for a single suit per card, but they can replace missing suits the player needs to activate its effect. Debuffed cards still count for their suit. Debuffed Wild cards don't count at all, though this seems to be a bug. To unlock this Joker, the player must reach Ante 8 for the first time. Do note that the condition is only to reach Ante 8 and not necessarily beating it. This Joker shares an unlock requirement with the Ante Upper! achievement. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World are easier to sift through with discards due to their smaller size.

title: Flower Pot
text: Flower Pot: Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World are easier to sift through with discards due to their smaller size. Painted Deck and Red Deck are also easier to sift through due to a larger hand size and extra discard, respectively.

title: Flower Pot
text: Flower Pot: Card modifiers: Wild cards work fantastically with Flower Pot as they can count as any suit. However, it should be noted that Wild cards will only count as one suit per card, meaning that a single Wild card cannot earn Flower Pot's X3 Mult on its own. Four Wild cards, or three Wild cards and any non-Wild suited card on the other hand, will always trigger Flower Pot's effect (unless the Wild cards are debuffed, this seems to be a bug). Re-triggering a Wild card does not make it count for multiple suits.

title: Flower Pot
text: Flower Pot: Poker hands: Four of a Kind is one of the best poker hands with Flower Pot as it needs four cards of every suit to begin with assuming the player doesn't heavily modify their deck. Straights are a five-card hand that only cares about rank, meaning it's easy to get at least one card of every suit in a hand. Full Houses require five cards to be played, meaning it's easier to get four different suits. Two Pairs require four cards and is easier to assemble than a Four of a Kind. Though, when compared to the other hands, it may be harder to get all four suits in a hand.

title: Flower Pot
text: Flower Pot: Jokers: Splash is easily one of the best Jokers to use with Flower Pot, since it lets the player play smaller hands like Pairs or High Cards and still obtain the X3 Mult from Flower Pot. Smeared Joker is another powerful Joker for Flower Pot as loosens the requirements from one card of each suit to just two of each color. Smeared Joker can also negate Flower Pot's anti-synergy with Checkered Deck as that deck doesn't naturally contain any clubs or diamonds. Seeing Double also works great alongside Flower Pot assuming the player plays a proper hand that's capable of triggering both.

title: Flower Pot
text: Flower Pot: Seeing Double also works great alongside Flower Pot assuming the player plays a proper hand that's capable of triggering both. The Family and The Order grant incredible XMult to a Four of A Kind and a Straight respectively, the poker hands that work best with Flower Pot. Decks: Checkered Deck only has two suits instead of the typical four, meaning that it's impossible to trigger Flower Pot's effect without buying diamond and club cards, creating Wild cards, converting cards to other suits, or using Smeared Joker. Poker hands: Flush-based hands require all 5 cards to be of the same suit. Without using at least 3 Wild cards, or 2 Wild cards and Four Fingers/ Splash, Flower Pot will never trigger.

title: Flower Pot
text: Flower Pot: Without Splash, High Card, Pair, Three of a Kind will never trigger Flower Pot's X3 Mult as they contain less than four cards. Jokers: Half Joker will never trigger alongside Flower Pot, as the former one wants to play hands with less than 4 cards. Consumables: Sigil can be awkward to use due to the uneven suit distribution, making it harder to get all four suits in a scoring poker hand without rigorous deck fixing.

title: Flower Pot
text: Flower Pot: Trivia: In poker, the pot is the chips that have been bet, and therefore the money to be won, likely derived from the word "jackpot". In this way, Flower Pot is a play on this term, given that Flower Pot helps grow the "pot" with its X3 Mult. The art of the Flower Pot card could also be a direct reference to the 1st version of Vincent Van Gogh's famous painting, "Sunflowers". In other media: Flower Pot makes an appearance as an enemy in Vampire Survivors.

title: Fortune Teller
text: Fortune Teller: Fortune Teller (Joker). Effect: +1 Mult per Tarot card used this run, (Currently +0). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Fortune Teller is a Common scaling Additive Mult Joker that gives +1 Mult per Tarot card used. It starts at +0 Mult. The effect is retroactive, meaning players immediately benefit from all the Tarot cards they utilized before buying this Joker.

title: Fortune Teller
text: Fortune Teller: Decks: Zodiac Deck, with its Tarot Merchant already equipped, benefits greatly from Fortune Teller, as players have more chances to buy and use Tarot cards without having to rely on Booster Packs. Yellow Deck extra $10 may allow for more Tarot cards to be bought. Poker Hands: Any Poker hand can benefit from Fortune Teller.
