Jokers: Vagabond, Cartomancer, Hallucination, 8 Ball, and Superposition can all provide Tarot cards with which to nourish Fortune Teller. Chaos the Clown gives a free reroll in the Shop allowing for more Tarot cards to be found. Certificate can generate cards with a Purple Seal, granting a repeatable source of Tarot cards.

title: Fortune Teller
text: Fortune Teller: Certificate can generate cards with a Purple Seal, granting a repeatable source of Tarot cards. Vampire consumes Enhancements from played cards, making it a good combo with Fortune Teller. Consumables: Naturally, every Tarot card benefits Fortune Teller, but there are 2 in particular that benefit the most. The Emperor provides two Tarot cards. The Fool can copy a Tarot card to use. Using these two in conjunction with each other can be a quick way to increase Fortune Teller's Mult. In addition: The Wheel of Fortune will scale Fortune Teller regardless if the 1 in 4 chance successfully activates, making it beneficial regardless of the outcome. Medium creates a Purple Seal, allowing the player to create more Tarot cards.

title: Fortune Teller
text: Fortune Teller: Medium creates a Purple Seal, allowing the player to create more Tarot cards. Vouchers: Overstock and Overstock Plus respectively add a 3rd and 4th card slot in the Shop, giving the player more chances to find Tarot cards to buy and use. Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut make it cheaper to reroll to find more Tarot cards to buy and use. Clearance Sale and Liquidation reduce the price of Tarot cards and Arcana Packs. Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon make it more likely to find Tarot cards in the shop. Crystal Ball gives +1 consumable slot, so you can purchase more Tarot cards in the shop for the next round.

title: Fortune Teller
text: Fortune Teller: Crystal Ball gives +1 consumable slot, so you can purchase more Tarot cards in the shop for the next round. Modifiers: Purple Seal can generate Tarot cards when discarding, allowing Fortune Teller to scale faster. Tags: Charm Tag lets the player choose up to two Tarot cards for free if the player is willing to skip blinds for it. Decks: Blast Off makes Fortune Teller harder to scale due to the starting Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon vouchers, which reduce the probability of Tarot cards appearing. Jokers: Red Card wants to skip Arcana Packs instead of using them, which removes scaling for Fortune Teller.

title: Fortune Teller
text: Fortune Teller: Jokers: Red Card wants to skip Arcana Packs instead of using them, which removes scaling for Fortune Teller. Campfire requires selling Tarot cards instead of using them, which is the opposite of what Fortune Teller does. Skipping for Throwback or Diet Cola mean fewer Tarot cards to use, although this isn't too bad if the Skip Tag itself is the Charm Tag. Vouchers: Planet Merchant, Planet Tycoon, and Magic Trick reduce the probabilities of Tarot cards appearing in the shop. Omen Globe reduces the amount of Tarot cards in Arcana Packs, although it can still be used to find Medium easier. Trivia: Tarot card readings are occasionally used by fortune tellers to help them make predictions.

title: Fortune Teller
text: Fortune Teller: Trivia: Tarot card readings are occasionally used by fortune tellers to help them make predictions. The color of "Tarot" in Fortune Teller's description is incorrectly formatted as {C:purple} instead of {C:tarot}, which is only used correctly in Medium. This makes the text appear as a slightly darker purple than other cards that reference Tarot cards. Vagabond has the same issue. Of all of the scaling +Mult Jokers, Fortune Teller is the only one to not include a "Mult" in the "(Currently +# Mult)" area.

title: Four Fingers
text: Four Fingers: Four Fingers (Joker). Effect: All Flushes and Straights can be made with 4 cards. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Four Fingers is an Uncommon effect-type Joker that allows you to make Straights or Flushes using four cards instead of five. (Five cards can still be used for higher-scoring hands.)

title: Four Fingers
text: Four Fingers: Straights can score the same number multiple times using this card. For example, a hand with a 2, 3, 4, and two 5's will score all five cards as a straight. Straight Flushes become more achievable with this joker, as a five-card hand that contains a 4-card Straight and a 4-card Flush will be considered to be a Straight Flush. For example, in a hand of 2♠️ 3♠️ 4♦️ 5♠️ 10♠️, the 2 3 4 5 make a straight of four cards, and the 2 3 5 10 make a flush of four cards, together being counted as a Straight Flush.

title: Four Fingers
text: Four Fingers: Decks: Black Deck: The +1 Joker Slot allows Four Finger to function as a utility Joker while still providing space for 5 other Jokers to score. Checkered Deck: Having only two suits allows a Straight Flush to be formed much easier. For Flush builds on Checkered Deck, a minimum hand size of 9 is required to guarantee every hand contains a flush, but with Four Fingers, a hand size of only 7 is required.

title: Four Fingers
text: Four Fingers: Poker hands: Straights and flushes become easier to make as you can score them with only 4 cards, but the biggest benefit will be with the highest scoring, flush-based hands like Straight Flush, Flush House, or Flush Five. Straight flushes, especially, become much easier with Four Fingers as both the "flush" and "straight" parts can be made with 4 different cards out of the 5 played, as described above.

title: Four Fingers
text: Four Fingers: Specifically, with Four Fingers, Royal Flush can be made from A K Q J or K Q J 10 of the same suit, or any four of A-10 when combined with Shortcut. This doesn't have much influence on the score but can be used for unlocks like the Royale achievement and Brainstorm's unlock condition. Similar things occur with Flush House and Flush Five, where only 4 of the cards need to be of the same suit. However, unlike straight flushes, the 5th card does still matter in terms of rank in order for the Full House/Five of a Kind hand type to be made.

title: Four Fingers
text: Four Fingers: Jokers: Shortcut makes straights and straight flushes easier to make as your straights can begin skipping ranks. Crazy Joker and The Order give additive and multiplicative Mult respectively when a Straight is played. Devious Joker and Runner both give Chips when a Straight is played. Jokers that give bonuses from playing a Flush, like Crafty Joker, Droll Joker, and The Tribe, all become easier to activate. Square Joker can be scaled with straights and flushes when four cards are played. Séance can be easier to trigger since straight flushes are easier to get. Marble Joker adds stone cards to the deck, which are extra useful, since they can now be used with 4-card flushes or straights to boost chip counts.

title: Four Fingers
text: Four Fingers: Splash enables playing a 4-card hand with an additional card, such as a glass or lucky card. The Duo, as well as other Jokers that activate if a hand contains a pair, have limited synergy with this Joker, as the effect of Four Fingers allows you to play Straights that include a Pair (ex: 10 9 9 8 7). Multiple Four Fingers do not stack. Multiple copies still require four cards to make straights and flushes. Enhancements: With Four Fingers, one Stone card can be scored when playing a Straight, Flush, or Straight Flush, as they can be made with 4 cards.

title: Four Fingers
text: Four Fingers: Strategies: Four Fingers is slightly weaker than Shortcut in creating Straights and weaker than Smeared Joker in creating Flushes. However, it can serve these purposes with just one Joker. The player can choose from these Jokers based on the play style of a run. Trivia: In poker, card sets are called "hands", and the relevant hands here are normally five cards each, so "Four Fingers" is a reference to a hand that's short by one card/finger. The drawing on the joker is very similar to common cartoon hands, which often have only four fingers.

title: Four Fingers
text: Four Fingers: The drawing on the joker is very similar to common cartoon hands, which often have only four fingers. According to LocalThunk, in the beta version of Balatro, Four Fingers is forced to show up on the tutorial seed, because it was an important joker to showcase the features of the game. This joker is thought by some players to be a reference to a popular "Loss" meme which originates from the Ctrl+Alt+Del webcomic by Tim Buckley. LocalThunk claims it is an unintentional reference.

title: Gift Card
text: Gift Card: Gift Card (Joker). Effect: Add $1 of sell value to every Joker and Consumable card at end of round. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Economy. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Gift Card is an Uncommon Economy Joker that increases the sell value of all Jokers (including itself) and Consumables by $1 at the end of each blind. Gift Card will still raise the value of debuffed jokers at the end of round.

title: Gift Card
text: Gift Card: Decks: Black Deck and Magic Deck can benefit from Gift Card thanks to increased Joker and Consumable slots, allowing more items to be stored. Five-Card Draw's increased Joker slots also benefits from Gift Card, as it allows even more items to be stored. Poker hands: This Joker doesn't synergise with any Poker Hand. Jokers: Swashbuckler combined with Gift Card, can be used for scaling Mult. Ceremonial Dagger can consume Gift Card or other jokers scaled by Gift Card for Mult.

title: Gift Card
text: Gift Card: Ceremonial Dagger can consume Gift Card or other jokers scaled by Gift Card for Mult. Cartomancer (and all other jokers that create Tarot cards): Can create the Temperance card, which can generate money equal to the sell value of each of your jokers. Additionally, the tarot cards created this way sell for $1 dollar extra per round because of Gift Card. Tarot cards: The money given by Temperance scales with the sell value of the player's Jokers. The longer players have Gift Card, the more money they'll get from Temperance, even potentially hitting the maximum value of $50 they can get from the Tarot card.

title: Gift Card
text: Gift Card: Vouchers: Crystal Ball adds an additional Consumable slot, allowing for more consumables to gain sell price per round. Antimatter similarly adds an additional Joker slot, allowing for another joker to gain sell price per round. In longer games, Gift Card can offset the negative effects of Clearance Sale and Liquidation, ensuring Temperance value while simultaneously keeping shop purchases cheap. Hieroglyph and Petroglyph send the player back an Ante, giving Gift Card more time to scale the sell value of Jokers and Consumables. Decks: Anaglyph Deck incentivizes skipping blinds due to its Double Tag gimmick, which gives Gift Card less chances to scale the sell value of Jokers and Consumables.

title: Gift Card
text: Gift Card: Painted Deck, Blast Off, and Nebula Deck don't synergize well with Gift Card due to -1 Joker slot and -1 Consumable slot, respectively. Cruelty makes it even more difficult to use Gift Card due to -2 Joker slots. Jokers: Throwback encourages skipping blinds to scale the XMult of the Joker, once again giving Gift Card less opportunity to increase the sell value of Jokers and Consumables. Trivia: Gift cards are pre-paid cards that can be used at participating store as a substitute for money, they are usually given as gifts, especially when it may be seen as rude or lazy to gift money.

title: Glass Joker
text: Glass Joker: Glass Joker (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains X0.75 Mult for every Glass Card that is destroyed, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Have at least 5 Glass Cards in your deck. Spawn Condition: Only obtainable if there is at least 1 Glass card currently in the player's deck. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Glass Joker is an Uncommon scaling Joker that provides Multiplicative Mult to all played hands. It starts at X1 Mult and gains X0.75 Mult every time a Glass card is destroyed, be it breaking after being played in a hand, or the effects of Sixth Sense, Trading Card, or The Hanged Man Tarot card. It is important to note that Spectral cards that can destroy Glass cards, such as Immolate, Familiar, Grim, and Incantation, do not increase Glass Joker. This is a bug.

title: Glass Joker
text: Glass Joker: Among the Multiplicative Mult Jokers that can have their value increased, Glass Joker is one of the fastest-scaling; after breaking just 3 Glass cards, it will give X3.25 Mult to all played hands, making it stronger than Cavendish (only Canio and Yorick, both exceedingly rare Legendary Jokers, have greater per-interval scaling values). This Joker will only appear once players have at least one Glass card currently in their deck. Usage Notes: Glass Joker will only appear in the shop after you have at least one Glass card in your deck. To unlock this Joker, the player must have at least 5 Glass cards in the deck

title: Glass Joker
text: Glass Joker: To unlock this Joker, the player must have at least 5 Glass cards in the deck Decks: Zodiac Deck gives more opportunity to buy both Justice and The Hanged Man directly from the shop. Anaglyph Deck, with its Double Tag provided after each Boss Blind, may allow players to gain many Charm Tags, or buff up their money to invest in Arcana Packs later in the run. Fragile works very well with Glass Joker, as this deck starts with two Oops! All 6s and all cards are Glass cards, which makes Glass Joker scale much faster. Poker hands: Any hand that contains a scoring Glass card will have a chance to buff Glass Joker.

title: Glass Joker
text: Glass Joker: Poker hands: Any hand that contains a scoring Glass card will have a chance to buff Glass Joker. Jokers: Splash: This allows up to five Glass cards to be played at once, in the event that the Glass cards cannot form an ideal poker hand. While also giving more X2 Mult boosts that can potentially make or break a run, it most importantly gives extra chances at breaking Glass cards, thereby scaling Glass Joker at a faster rate.

title: Glass Joker
text: Glass Joker: Erosion: An Additive Mult Joker that scales remarkably fast as the number of cards in your full deck drops below the starting amount. Even destroying single-digit numbers of Glass cards can give it up to +36 Mult, which, in turn, will pair very nicely with this Joker's at-times simultaneous Multiplicative Mult scaling. Oops! All 6s: With this Joker equipped, Glass cards will break half of the time, making the rate at which Glass Joker scales much faster. This comes at the downside of exhausting your deck at the same accelerated rate, so consider finding additional ways to add cards to it, like certain Cryptid, the aforementioned DNA, Certificate, or Standard Packs.

title: Glass Joker
text: Glass Joker: Trading Card: As long as a Glass card is drawn in the opening hand, this can potentially lead to a X0.75 Mult boost every Blind, while also earning some value on the side. Sixth Sense can also work well with Glass Joker as long as the player draws a Glass 6. DNA: This Joker allows duplicating Glass cards easier, and they could break in the process, immediately providing a buff for Glass Joker.

title: Glass Joker
text: Glass Joker: Canio: Although getting both of these two Jokers is unlikely, they can both have their Multiplicative Mult scaled greatly and simultaneously, by destroying Glass face cards. Pareidolia will make all cards count as face cards, meaning that each Glass card that breaks or gets destroyed will scale both Jokers at once.

title: Glass Joker
text: Glass Joker: Any Joker that creates Tarot cards will enable two crucial things for strengthening Glass Joker: firstly, easier access to either Justice to enhance cards into Glass cards or The Hanged Man to destroy them, and secondly, holding unwanted Tarot cards in the consumable slots to increase the chances that the aforementioned two will appear in Booster Packs; among them, Cartomancer and Vagabond are the easiest to activate and gain large amounts of Tarot cards from. The Legendary Joker Perkeo can make the Justice and The Hanged Man even more common by duplicating them every round! Consumables: Justice and Death can turn some cards into Glass cards. The Hanged Man can destroy Glass cards. Cryptid can make more Glass cards.

title: Glass Joker
text: Glass Joker: The Hanged Man can destroy Glass cards. Cryptid can make more Glass cards. Vouchers: Illusion can have a chance for Glass cards to appear in the shop, which can be bought to get destroyed to scale Glass Joker. This can be further increased with help from Overstock and Overstock Plus to increase the shop selection, plus Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut to make rerolling cheaper. Decks: Bram Poker starts with an Eternal Vampire, which means Glass Joker will not gain anything unless you use The Hanged Man or Trading Card. Jokers: Vampire is not recommended, as it removes any Glass enhancement when scored, and players might need to destroy Glass cards by using The Hanged Man or Trading Card.

title: Glass Joker
text: Glass Joker: Consumables: Due to a bug, Immolate, Grim, Incantation, and Familiar destroying Glass cards will NOT scale Glass Joker, wasting the Enhancement while not providing any value, although the latter 3 can be used to create more Glass cards to destroy. Trivia: The card art is semi-transparent. This Joker is part of a series, along with Stone Joker, Steel Joker, Golden Ticket, and Lucky Cat, where the Joker only appears once players have at least one card with the relevant enhancement currently in their deck.

title: Gluttonous Joker
text: Gluttonous Joker: Gluttonous Joker (Joker). Effect: Played cards with Club suit give +3 Mult when scored. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Gluttonous Joker is a Common Joker that provides conditional Additive Mult to played hands. One of the four 'sinful' Jokers made to support specific Card Suits, it gives +3 Mult each time a Club card is scored. If the played card is retriggered, either by a Joker effect or by its own Red Seal, Gluttonous Joker's effect will activate again.

title: Gluttonous Joker
text: Gluttonous Joker: Decks: Magic Deck's Fool Tarots can be used to mass-convert cards to have Club suits. Ghost Deck can find a Sigil Spectral card in the shop, which may convert cards into Clubs. Poker hands: This Joker works best with Flush hands, if they contain only Club suit cards. These hands are as follows: Flush Straight Flush (and Royal Flush) Flush House Flush Five Other hands that score more cards are generally better to play with Gluttonous Joker, as they allow more Club cards to be scored. Jokers: As Gluttonous Joker's effect triggers when a Club card is scored, retrigger Jokers that allow cards to be scored multiple times are very good to combo with Gluttonous.

title: Gluttonous Joker
text: Gluttonous Joker: Flush Jokers, like Crafty Joker and Droll Joker, work well with Gluttonous Joker, as you want to be playing flushes to maximize its effect anyways. Onyx Agate also triggers off of Club cards scored, forming a natural synergy with Gluttonous Joker. As Onyx Agate is a strict upgrade to Gluttonous, it can be used as a replacement, but it also can be used in builds that have high X Mult from hands from Jokers like, sometimes, Ancient Joker, or The Idol. This combo also benefits from a strong Chip Joker, ideally one that also benefits from Flushes. Castle is the best example of this kind of Joker.

title: Gluttonous Joker
text: Gluttonous Joker: Because Gluttonous Joker's Mult is applied during the scoring of your played cards, Jokers that focus on creating Tarot cards are helpful to Gluttonous Joker's viability. They can both allow more Clubs to be created, and create certain Enhancements (particularly Glass and Steel) that work well with high hand-scoring Mult builds. Smeared Joker effectively turns all Spade cards into Clubs for the purpose of Gluttonous Joker's effect. Decks: Checkered Deck starts with no Clubs, making Gluttonous Joker less useful. Blinds: When facing The Club, all Club cards are debuffed, meaning Gluttonous Joker cannot activate.

title: Gluttonous Joker
text: Gluttonous Joker: Blinds: When facing The Club, all Club cards are debuffed, meaning Gluttonous Joker cannot activate. Trivia: Gluttony is one of the traditional seven deadly sins. The four basic Jokers that provide +3 Mult for each suit are each based on these. The other Sinful Jokers are Greedy Joker, Lusty Joker and Wrathful Joker. Gluttonous Joker's uncommon counterpart, Onyx Agate, gives +7 Mult instead of +3 Mult, which could perhaps play into the "acquiring things especially beyond the point of necessity" definition of gluttony. Unlike the other Sinful Jokers, there appears to be no correlation between the suit and the sin chosen. In the game's code, Gluttonous Joker is misspelled as "gluttenous".

title: Gluttonous Joker
text: Gluttonous Joker: In the game's code, Gluttonous Joker is misspelled as "gluttenous". In demo versions of the game, the color of Gluttonous Joker was dark blue instead of green. This was changed in the release version (update 1.0.0h) to match the color of the suit better.

title: Golden Joker
text: Golden Joker: Golden Joker (Joker). Effect: Earn $4 at end of round. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Economy. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. The Golden Joker is a Common Economy Joker that provides an extra $4 at the end of each blind. It pays for itself after only one blind, as selling it nets $3. It is considered the "standard" Economy Joker, being a decent generator of money. Many other Economy Jokers can be considered by how well they stack up to Golden Joker.

title: Golden Joker
text: Golden Joker: Usage notes: The Omelette challenge bans Golden Joker. Decks: Green Deck appreciates other sources of income, especially if you are using all of your hands/discards. Black Deck can synergy with Golden Joker thanks to the +1 Joker Slot, plus its -1 hand per round means players need something to boost their income anyway. Zodiac Deck generally wants to reroll a lot, meaning Golden Joker's money can help with that. Poker hands: This Joker doesn't synergize with any poker hands. Jokers: Economy-based scalers, like Bull and Flash Card, appreciate the extra money brought in by Golden Joker.

title: Golden Joker
text: Golden Joker: Jokers: Economy-based scalers, like Bull and Flash Card, appreciate the extra money brought in by Golden Joker. Golden Joker can be used to help jump start To the Moon, achieving higher interest levels sooner. To the Moon is, with $25 held, a strict upgrade to Golden Joker. Tarot generators can be useful with Golden Joker, since the money Golden provides can increase the value of The Hermit. Temperance also likes Golden Joker, as it has a base sell value of $3.

title: Golden Ticket
text: Golden Ticket: Golden Ticket (Joker). Effect: Played Gold cards earn $4 when scored. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Play a 5 card hand that contains only Gold cards. Spawn Condition: Only obtainable if there is at least 1 Gold card currently in the player's deck. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Economy. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Golden Ticket is a Common Economy Joker that gives $4 for every scoring Gold card, effectively turning them into more powerful Gold Seal cards.

title: Golden Ticket
text: Golden Ticket: For this Joker's unlock requirement's "5 card hand", the hand's 5 cards do not need to score. For example, the player can unlock this Joker by playing a High Card hand of one scoring card with four non-scoring cards. All cards do need to be gold cards before any joker effects, so Golden Ticket will not unlock if one or more of the cards was changed to gold by Midas Mask. This Joker will only appear once players have at least one Gold card currently in their deck. Decks: The Zodiac Deck works best with Golden Ticket thanks to its increased Tarot card frequency, allowing Gold card conversion more frequent.

title: Golden Ticket
text: Golden Ticket: Poker hands: Playing 5-card hand such as Flush or Full House with as many Gold cards as possible will ensure maximum income. Jokers: "On scored" retrigger Jokers will reactivate Golden Ticket's effect. So Hanging Chad, Dusk, and Seltzer are great with this Joker. Hack and Sock and Buskin can also be great if the Gold cards have the relevant ranks. Midas Mask turns all face cards into Gold cards when scored. It will be even stronger if paired with Pareidolia, as all cards now can be converted into Gold cards. Bull and Bootstraps benefit from the high money making capabilities of this joker. Card modifiers: A Gold Seal will earn $3 when scored, giving $7 total per Gold card.

title: Golden Ticket
text: Golden Ticket: Card modifiers: A Gold Seal will earn $3 when scored, giving $7 total per Gold card. A Red Seal will retrigger Golden Ticket, giving $8 per Gold card. Consumables: The Devil can make more Gold cards. Death can turn some cards into Gold cards. The Hanged Man can remove non-Gold cards. Deja Vu can apply Red Seals onto Gold cards allowing Golden Ticket to generate more money. Jokers: Vampire has anti-synergy, as the Gold Enhancement gets removed before it can score. However if the player is also using Midas Mask this becomes a non-issue. This innately applies to the Bram Poker as it starts with an Eternal Vampire.

title: Golden Ticket
text: Golden Ticket: This innately applies to the Bram Poker as it starts with an Eternal Vampire. Vagabond can have anti-synergy, as having more than $4 during a round will disable its effect. It may be better to keep Gold Enhancement cards in hand and let them trigger when the round ends. Mime has slight anti-synergy, since a Gold card held in hand with Mime will give $6, more than what Golden Ticket gives for playing Gold cards. Trivia: The numbers 16180339 used in the artwork are the first digits of the Golden ratio, perhaps because of the shared "golden" thread.

title: Golden Ticket
text: Golden Ticket: This Joker is part of a series, along with Stone Joker, Steel Joker, Glass Joker and Lucky Cat, where the Joker only appears once players have at least one card with the relevant enhancement currently in their deck. Interestingly, Golden Ticket is the only Common Joker in this list. This Joker has a smaller width than standard Joker cards when face up. However, when it is flipped face-down, it uses the same standard size of card back as the rest. The other Joker with this similar property is Business Card.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: Greedy Joker (Joker). Effect: Played cards with Diamond suit give +3 Mult when scored. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Greedy Joker is a Common Joker that provides conditional Additive Mult to played hands. One of the four 'sinful' Jokers made to support specific Card Suits, it gives +3 Mult each time a Diamonds card is scored. If the played card is retriggered, either by a Joker effect or by its own Red Seal, Greedy Joker's effect will activate again.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: As Diamonds have the least meaningful support of all the suits, and Flush already has one of the slowest Planet scaling curves in the game, Greedy Joker is often not worth keeping past the first few Antes, unless better Additive Mult options are never encountered. Decks: Magic Deck: This Deck has the only innate advantage with this one, as one can turn the starting copies of The Fool into The Star to more rapidly convert their Deck into Diamonds. Death and The Lovers also help build towards this goal, albeit at a slower pace, but in the latter's case, Wild cards synergize with many more Jokers.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: Red Deck, Blue Deck, and Painted Deck: These Decks all have bonuses that make it marginally easier to find that key Diamonds Flush, making them slightly more practical overall, but not by a large margin. Poker hands: The most obvious plan with this Joker is to play hands that contain only Diamonds. As a result, Flush-type hands are the most optimal, to guarantee at least +15 Mult to all played hands: Flush Straight Flush (and subsequently Royal Flush) Flush House Flush Five Other hands that score more cards, like Straight, are generally better to play with this Joker than, say, High Card or Pair, as they allow more Diamond cards to be scored.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: Jokers: Retrigger Jokers work best with this one. To maximize the Additive Mult boost to +30 Mult on a Flush-type hand, priority should be given to those that can very easily affect the entire hand of played cards, such as Hack (for cards with 5 or lower rank) or Sock and Buskin (for face cards). Tarot card generation is also a must if Greedy Joker is to be at the core of the build. Cartomancer is an obvious choice, but building into Straight Flushes can also lend well to including Superposition. Additionally, Spectral cards can be created with Séance if a build is centered around Straight Flushes.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: Additionally, Spectral cards can be created with Séance if a build is centered around Straight Flushes. Crafty Joker and Droll Joker: Providing +80 Chips and +10 Mult, respectively, when scoring a Flush-type hand, these can be beneficial in tandem with this Joker, primarily in the early game. In Crafty Joker's case, since Chip sources are overall rarer than Additive Mult, keeping it later is more practical.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: Castle: A Chip Joker that scales by +3 Chips for every discarded card of a random suit determined by deck distribution. It can easily cover the other side of the equation once the deck has been manipulated enough to mostly include Diamonds, by just tossing away lower-ranked or otherwise less desirable cards of the suit. Rough Gem: Forming the most natural synergy with this Joker, it will make each Diamonds Flush you play also give $5, which can help compensate for the lack of raw damage Diamond Decks can output by increasing purchasing power, thereby granting indirect access to higher strength.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: Smeared Joker: By making Hearts also count as Diamonds, and vice versa, this not only makes deck-fixing and finding Flushes twice as easy, but opens up access to more cards, like more consistent hits of Ancient Joker, as well as Bloodstone. Ancient Joker and The Idol: These are more difficult to include thanks to their inherent randomness, but with enough Wild cards (in the former's case) or duplication (for the latter), they could easily be activated every few hands later on in the run.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: The Tribe: A natural include in a Flush build to give an extra X2 Mult to the most practical of scored hands. However, if it is possible to deck fix into a Flush Five build, The Family should be prioritized. Decks: Checkered Deck has anti-synergy with this Joker, since it includes no Diamonds to start. This Joker is better off avoided if encountered while playing this Deck. Boss Blinds: Care should be taken when playing a Diamonds Flush build, as they are hard countered by two Boss Blinds, and soft countered by one of the Showdown Blinds. The Director's Cut voucher is a smart choice as a result.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: The Window is a debilitating encounter, since it makes it so that all Diamond cards go unscored and thus activate no Joker or card effects. A Diamonds Flush deck is only a safe consideration early on if this Boss Blind has already came and went; in any other case, it is very likely to end the run.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: The Ox can also be crippling later on in the run, especially when playing predominantly regular Flushes, by killing the player's economy on the spot. While it is possible to mitigate the loss with other money generation, or even avoid it entirely by veering into another hand like a Flush House, this is not always possible. In the event it is not, seriously consider whether the money is best spent right before to lessen the need for it for the rest of the run.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: The Cerulean Bell can prove to be a mild or major annoyance; if its effect forcibly selects a non-Diamond card and prevents scoring a Flush as a result, it must either be discarded, or played in a 'burner hand' as a makeshift discard, which can both lessen consistency and overall odds of winning. Trivia: Greed is one of the traditional seven deadly sins. The four Common Jokers that give Additive Mult for each suit are based on these. The other 'sinful Jokers' (as named by LocalThunk in the Balatro patch notes) are Lusty Joker, Wrathful Joker and Gluttonous Joker. Greed is typically applied to being greedy for money, hence it is associated with Diamonds, which as jewelry, symbolizes wealth.

title: Greedy Joker
text: Greedy Joker: Greed is typically applied to being greedy for money, hence it is associated with Diamonds, which as jewelry, symbolizes wealth. Greedy Joker's Uncommon counterpart, Rough Gem, generates money, which plays into the theme of greed.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Green Joker (Joker). Effect: +1 Mult per hand played, -1 Mult per discard, (Currently +0 Mult). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Green Joker is a Common Joker that provides Additive Mult to all played hands. It is one of many scaling Additive Mult Jokers which grows in power with specific actions, gaining +1 Mult whenever a hand is played and scored. This very strong and unconditional strength is offset by a noticeable downside: it loses -1 Mult whenever a card(s) get discarded - either by the player or game mechanics, which currently only applies in the case of The Hook. It starts at, and will never go below, +0 Mult.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Green Joker is often touted as one of the best Common Jokers in the game, primarily for its strength in the foundational early Antes of a run, which snowballs into huge power later as long as the build is not dependent on discarding cards. This is largely a nonissue, as hands are strictly superior to discards anyway regarding point scoring, and can only prove troublesome when the player's money pool is weak. Assuming it is obtained at the start of Ante 2, with an average of 3 hands played per round and no discards or skips, Green Joker will give +60 Mult going into the Showdown Blind, equivalent to three fresh copies of Popcorn.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Decks: Green Joker works with any Deck, with its strength being more pronounced the earlier it is acquired into the run. Decks that have noteworthy synergy include: Blue Deck: An extra hand means Green Joker can reach even greater heights by the end of the run. At the very worst, if the player's build is strong enough that a few High Cards are sweeping the Blinds, it translates to an extra $1 at the end of each round.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Green Deck: This deck benefits from this Joker mainly in the early game when money is low and all hands are used to scale Green Joker, taking advantage of the $1 gained per unused discard. However, other decks would be able to provide more money long-term if the player holds $25 and continues using all hands to scale Green Joker.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Poker Hands: Green Joker works best with hands that can be reliably made without discarding and also played repeatedly, with the rarer hands being less and less reliable. Green Joker wants weaker hands earlier anyway so it can scale more per round, as ending the Blind in one hand will make it scale to about the same size as a fresh Popcorn by the end of a run, far inferior to its usual capabilities. This means it works best when playing: High Card (especially so, as it is always assembled) Pair Two Pair

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: This means it works best when playing: High Card (especially so, as it is always assembled) Pair Two Pair Another possible strategy is to scale up one of the stronger hands like Straight or Four of a Kind, then use all but one of the hands as makeshift discards to try and craft that hand, leading to an even stronger end result. This strategy can lead to very high scores, and works best when paired with Jokers like Acrobat and Dusk, but it is a lot less reliable and may necessitate discards, thereby weakening Green Joker.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Jokers: Chip Jokers help Green Joker form an important core that can bolster the strength of most, if not all hands, very reliably. Banner is the most obvious choice, giving +30 Chips for each unused discard in the round; in the same rarity, however, Blue Joker is more favorable at higher difficulties, as it is not affected by the -1 discard penalty of Blue Stake and higher, and would not be having its power significantly dampened by discards. Other reliable options include Square Joker for consistent scaling, and Stuntman for an extraordinary boost at a negligible downside for builds Green Joker is oriented towards anyway.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Multiplicative Mult Jokers are key, not only to powering through the higher Stakes, but to amplifying this Joker's strengths, and many of them synergize very well with it. Some examples include: Acrobat: With its X3 Mult boost triggering on the final hand of the round, it can be easier to use when playing large volumes of hands, as is optimal in this Joker's case. It can also lead to much more explosive plays with bigger hands. Card Sharp: Giving a strong X3 Mult boost if the poker hand was scored previously in the round, it is almost impossible not to benefit from it due to the ease of simply playing multiple High Cards.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Hologram: High Card/Pair builds do not necessarily care about overall consistency or individual card quality as much, as most of the scoring is sourced from the Jokers as well as the Planet scaling. This allows the player to very easily take advantage of Hologram's fast scaling rate. Ramen: An unconditional X2 Mult boost, it and Green Joker go together greatly, as they are only weakened by discards - something the player would not be doing in the first place in ideal scenarios if they had both.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Vampire: While it does not scale as fast as it would in builds playing full 5-card hands when paired with Green Joker (as a general rule of thumb), it is still a great option to consider, as it removes mostly insignificant buffs for much more generally useful Multiplicative Mult boosting. Delayed Gratification: Paying out $2 per discard at the end of the round as long as none were used, this Joker helps significantly with the economy problems playing large amounts of hands usually incurs, while being cheaper to acquire than more generic alternatives. It is slightly less valuable past Black Stake due to the -1 discard penalty.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Burglar: Forming the best synergy with this Joker by a country mile, trading in discards for an extra three hands provides a huge power ceiling boost, allowing this Joker to reach even higher levels of Mult before key points in the run. It also gives more consistency to finding stronger hands, which can be leveraged to an effect mentioned in the Poker Hands section. However, it does turn off synergy with Banner and Delayed Gratification, so consider other options if these are key to the current build.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Matador: It can pay out tremendously if the right Boss Blind is encountered, as just playing repeated High Cards of debuffed cards (for example) can net $24 or more, enough to approach the default interest cap on its own. Only do this if the scoring provided by other sources is sufficient, however. Space Joker: With the high volumes of hands Green Joker builds play, this can help to periodically tune the scaling even higher.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Vagabond: Another very seamless synergy, generating a Tarot card after every hand played as long as no more than $4 is held. Creating 3 or more in a single round can lead to very rapid deck enrichment and manipulation, allowing pivots into much stronger hands that will appreciate the sea of Mult that Green Joker will give. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong give additional hands per round, allowing Green Joker to scale even higher. Tags: Handy Tag rewards the player with Money equal to the amount of hands they have currently played during the run. Green Joker (especially in the earlier antes) incentivizes playing as many hands as possible in order to scale its Mult.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Garbage Tag also rewards the player for not using their discards. Blinds: The Water will set the player's discards to 0, meaning Green Joker cannot lose mult. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle all have poor synergy with Green Joker due to their reduced number of hands. Red Deck: The +1 discard bonus is completely redundant to a Green Joker build, which should only be using discards in emergencies anyway. Anaglyph Deck: Skipping Blinds to get extra Tags means not getting those extra Mult points on this Joker, which, in very extreme circumstances, could spell the player's demise. Given the power of stacking Tags, however, this is usually a nonissue.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Jokers: Green Joker has anti-synergy with any Joker related to using discards in almost every circumstance. This includes Jokers such as: Burnt Joker Faceless Joker Mail-In Rebate Trading Card Mystic Summit (without Burglar) Another anti-synergy arises from Troubadour, which even though it increases hand size and makes hands easier to find, it also makes the player play one hand short, thus making Green Joker scale slower.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Green Joker also has anti-synergy with both Drunkard and Merry Andy, two Jokers that provide extra discards, so in a Green Joker build, these two Jokers are useless. A possible exception can be if the player also has Banner or Delayed Gratification, but since this combo requires 3 Jokers it can be somewhat unneficient, so the player should avoid these two Jokers, especially Merry Andy as it decreases hand size.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Blinds: The Hook: This boss blind counters Green Joker's scaling potential as it discards 2 random cards every hand played, causing only a net neutral at the end. It is recommended to try to win as fast as possible against The Hook so players can have some money leftover as they cannot scale Green Joker against this boss blind. The Needle: This boss blind sets hands to 1 and may force a discard to be used, lowering Green Joker's mult. Burglar can be used to mitigate this, however. Card modifiers: A card with a Purple Seal needs to be discarded in order to get value from it, which lowers Green Joker's Mult.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy are not recommended as Green Joker de-incentivizes discarding. However, the vouchers can be worth it if Green Joker is paired with Delayed Gratification and/or Banner. Telescope can be less useful if the player is specializing in a hand other than High Card, as Green Joker's scaling mechanics tend to cause High Card to be the most played hand.

title: Green Joker
text: Green Joker: Trivia: This Joker has a direct counterpart in Ride the Bus: both are Additive Mult Jokers that gain power whenever a hand (regardless of type) is played, and both have ways to lose their power as well, which encourages the player to not perform a specific action (using discards in this Joker's case, or playing face cards in the other's).

title: Gros Michel
text: Gros Michel: Gros Michel (Joker). Effect: +15 Mult, 1 in 6 chance this card is destroyed at end of round. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Spawn Condition: Only obtainable while Gros Michel has not yet gone "extinct" during the current run. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Probability-Based: Yes. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: ✗ No. Gros Michel (French for "big Mike" or "big Michael"; pronounced in American English as grows mee-shel, and in British English as grow mih-chel) is a Common Additive Mult Joker that gives an unconditional +15 Mult to any poker hand played.

title: Gros Michel
text: Gros Michel: Unfortunately, all good things must come to an end, and it might so happen that when the run needs him most, he'll vanish. At the end of every round, there is a 1 in 6 chance that Gros Michel will destroy itself (denoted by the word "Extinct!" displaying as it vanishes). Once this occurs, Gros Michel cannot be obtained for the rest of the current run. Instead Cavendish, a Multiplicative Mult Joker, is able to spawn. Note that Cavendish will not replace Gros Michel in its Joker slot; it must be obtained through means like the Shop, Judgement, Riff-Raff, Buffoon Tag, etc.

title: Gros Michel
text: Gros Michel: If Gros Michel is either sold or destroyed through non-extinction means, such as with Ankh, Hex, Ceremonial Dagger, or Madness, it will continue to appear throughout the run until it has gone extinct. Cavendish will only appear if Gros Michel destroys itself naturally. Usage Notes: The Non-Perishable challenge bans Gros Michel. If a Perishable Gros Michel gets extinct at the 5th round, there will be an "Extinct!" pop-up first, followed by a "disabled!" in a blank space.

title: Gros Michel
text: Gros Michel: Jokers: Oops! All 6s: Obtaining these two Jokers simultaneously can either be an immense boon or a huge risk, depending on the state of the run. Increasing the self-destruction odds to a 2 in 6 chance allows for Cavendish to appear faster, at the cost of a potentially run-saving Additive Mult bonus. Copying Gros Michel with Blueprint and Brainstorm does not increase the probability of self-destruction of Gros Michel or cause the copying Joker to self-destruct, so this can be used without additional risks. Decks: Gros Michel does not work as well on Plasma Deck compared to other decks, as Additive Mult is not as powerful on this deck.

title: Gros Michel
text: Gros Michel: Strategy: Gros Michel is essentially a must take in the early Antes; with it, most Two Pairs (16 combined rank or higher), any Three of a Kind, or any higher ranked hand is guaranteed to clear each Blind of Ante 1, and any of the common 5-card hands (Straight, Flush, and Full House) can clear up to the Big Blind of Ante 2 on any difficulty without help, provided the chip value is at least 79. Seeing it early also increases the odds of destroying it early, and gaining quick access to Cavendish, a cheap and guaranteed source of Multiplicative Mult. Multiplicative Mult is essentially mandatory to clear the later Antes on any difficulty past Red Stake.

title: Gros Michel
text: Gros Michel: Building around Gros Michel will usually end up being a fruitless endeavor, as it can disappear at any moment. However, any build, regardless of synergy, will be happy to pick it up; not only does it provide a powerful bonus before expiry, but exhausting it unlocks the even more powerful Cavendish. Thus, it can supplement any build. Although, if it remains for far too long, it may be necessary to ditch its secret potential in order to pick up a Joker that is more immediately beneficial.

title: Gros Michel
text: Gros Michel: It's best to avoid adding any editions to this Joker, since it will be lost when it becomes extinct. Consider holding onto The Wheel of Fortune or Ectoplasm in the consumable area until this Joker destroys itself in order to maximize their value. Trivia: In the 1950s-1960s, the real-world Gros Michel was devastated by a fungal pandemic called Panama disease, which led the Cavendish to replace it as the most commercially common banana. These traits are represented by the Joker's high chance of self-destruction, its need to be destroyed for Cavendish to appear, and its common rarity.

title: Gros Michel
text: Gros Michel: Gros Michel is one of the four jokers that are featured in the official physical playing card deck. The 3 others are Joker, Juggler, and Blueprint. This Joker is part of the group of "Consumable" Jokers that can be destroyed with usage, dubbed "Food Jokers" due to their shared theme. The other Jokers in this group are Ice Cream, Popcorn, Cavendish, Egg, Seltzer, Turtle Bean, Ramen, and Diet Cola. Gros Michel is the fifth Joker after Jimbo, Odd Todd, and Even Steven, as well as Vampire, to get an official plush toy due to a merch collaboration with Makeship. The product is labeled Balatro Gros Michel Longboi.

title: Gros Michel
text: Gros Michel: The "Longboi" name could be a reference to the unusually tall mallard of the same name. In other media: Gros Michel appears as a weapon in the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors. Gros Michel appears as an artifact in Monster Train 2.

title: Hack
text: Hack: Hack (Joker). Effect: Retrigger each played 2, 3, 4, or 5. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Retrigger. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Hack is an Uncommon Retrigger Joker that can retrigger played scoring low-rank cards, more specifically, 2s, 3s, 4s, and 5s. This can mitigate the lower chip count provided by low-rank cards, since they will be triggered twice.

title: Hack
text: Hack: Hack is similar to Sock and Buskin, but works with specific numbered cards instead of faces. Similar to Sock and Buskin, it also does not retrigger a Red Seal. For example, a Red Seal 3 will only activate three times: once for the initial trigger, once for the Red Seal, and then lastly, for Hack. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World only have number cards, making it much easier to find low-rank cards. Zodiac Deck can be used to find more Tarot cards to enhance low-rank cards or ways to copy them. Ghost Deck can find powerful seal-applying Spectral cards and Aura, which can make your low-rank cards more impactful.

title: Hack
text: Hack: Ghost Deck can find powerful seal-applying Spectral cards and Aura, which can make your low-rank cards more impactful. Poker hands: Using large hands that have multiple low-rank cards that can trigger Hack is generally the best option, allowing the player to maximize its potential. Notably, Five of a Kind and Flush Five are easily feasible after duplicating powerful and/or modified low-rank cards. This also includes Full House and Flush House, although they are slightly weaker than the initially mentioned hands. A Straight using Ace, 2, 3, 4, and 5 is also a good way to utilize Hack, although it will not retrigger the Ace.

title: Hack
text: Hack: Jokers: Jokers that are able to give bonuses based on the type of playing card, whether it is suit-based or rank-based, can benefit from Hack. This allows the player to double that Joker's effectiveness. Suit-based Jokers like Greedy Joker, Arrowhead, Gluttonous Joker, etc. can be retriggered if a low-rank card of the corresponding suit is played. Rank-based Jokers like Even Steven, Walkie Talkie, or Odd Todd can benefit from a second trigger. Fibonacci is particularly strong with Hack, as it gains +8 Mult for each scored 2, 3, and 5, and will trigger twice. Wee Joker can scale twice as fast utilizing the retriggered 2s.

title: Hack
text: Hack: Wee Joker can scale twice as fast utilizing the retriggered 2s. Tarot generating Jokers, like Cartomancer and Vagabond, are needed for deck manipulation to draw low-rank cards more reliably. It will also help modify low-rank cards to make them more valuable during the retrigger (ex. retriggering a Bonus 4). Jokers that give XMult from cards are very useful, as the cards that trigger them will do so twice. There aren't as many that work with low-rank cards, but some examples are Bloodstone and Ancient Joker.

title: Hack
text: Hack: If one has enough XMult from their cards, another retrigger Joker is very useful to combine with Hack. This will usually be either Dusk or Seltzer, though Blueprint and Brainstorm can also be used to copy Hack for a less conditional retrigger. One can also use Showman to try and find another Hack. Trading Card and DNA make it easier to draw your useful low-rank cards. DNA is particularly useful, as it can copy a powerful low-rank card with an enhancement, edition, and seal. Hiker has incredible synergy with Hack, as not only will Hiker scale cards twice as fast, but the retriggering of the cards will also give their chips again.

title: Hack
text: Hack: Lucky Cat can scale twice as fast since the low-rank Lucky cards it will be using to scale have twice as many chances to earn +20 Mult or $20. As Glass cards are substantially powerful with Hack's retriggers, Glass Joker can be a nice addition to still get value when they break. Certificate can be used to try and find a low-rank card (or a King/Ace that can be Strengthened) with a powerful seal, or a Purple Seal to generate Tarots for the low-rank cards. However, if it adds too many high-rank cards, Hack will become less valuable, so the risk and reward must be carefully assessed. Consumables: Tarot cards:

title: Hack
text: Hack: Consumables: Tarot cards: The Hierophant, The Empress, The Magician and Justice add enhancements to the low-ranking cards that makes retriggering them more worthwhile. The Hanged Man can be used to thin out the deck and the low-ranking cards easier to draw. Death can be used to turn other cards into low-rank cards, especially low-rank cards that already have an enhancement or edition on them. Strength can be used to Aces back into 2s. Strength can also be used if be used if the player only wants to focus on one rank (such as turning all 3s into 4s). Spectral cards:

title: Hack
text: Hack: Spectral cards: Aura can add a Foil, Holographic, or Polychrome effect to a low-ranking card, giving the player more of a reason to play them. Cryptid can be used to create more low-ranking cards that already have enhancements or editions on them. Deja Vu can add a Red Seal to a low-rank card for an additional retrigger. Immolate can destroy up to five cards, potentially making the low-ranking cards easier to find. Talisman can apply a Gold Seal to a low-rank card, allowing it generate $6 when played. Incantation can add 2s, 3s, 4s and/or 5s to the deck, at the cost of a random card being destroyed.

title: Hack
text: Hack: Incantation can add 2s, 3s, 4s and/or 5s to the deck, at the cost of a random card being destroyed. Decks: 15 Minute City doesn't work well with Hack due to a lack of 2s and 3s by default. Trivia: A "hack" is a slang term to refer to both a mediocre comedian and/or re-used, obvious, or stolen jokes from other comedians (explaining the presence of the comedian in the card's artwork). This repetition of low-quality jokes is reflected in the retriggering of low-rank cards. According to LocalThunk, the outfit of this joker is loosely based on Joe Rogan.

title: Hack
text: Hack: According to LocalThunk, the outfit of this joker is loosely based on Joe Rogan. It is one of the five Jokers to have a physical card from Balatro: Special Edition. The four other jokers where that is also the case are Joker, Ice Cream, Abstract Joker, and Throwback. Hack is one of the two Jokers to appear on the front of a regular-sized Buffoon Pack. The other Joker is Juggler. According to LocalThunk, the joke that Hack told is as follows:Fun fact about me, I'm a trysexualI'll try ANYTHING in bed once!1. Missionary2.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Half Joker (Joker). Effect: +20 Mult if played hand contains 3 or fewer cards. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Half Joker is a Common Joker. It is a conditional Additive Mult Joker that adds +20 Mult to played hands containing 3 or fewer cards. Note that this does not take into account whether the excess cards are scored.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Synergies: This Joker is very good in the earliest of Antes, with most Pairs and Three of a Kinds able to clear the first one on their own, and is one of the strongest flat Additive Mult Jokers in the game. However, due to the weak base power of the hands it enables, it is usually best replaced by other Additive Mult Jokers in later Antes. Decks: Blue Deck: This Joker works best when repeatedly playing the hands it enables. Therefore, this Deck provides natural synergy, since the small size of all three valid poker hands warrant fewer discards to consistently find and score them.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Nebula Deck: Since this Deck emphasizes the quick scaling of a single poker hand, it can greatly balloon the power of Half Joker, which already rewards the player for playing the same few hands, with its built-in Telescope Voucher guaranteeing that each Celestial Pack gives a much needed Pluto, Mercury, or Venus, as the three hands this Joker empowers are very weak at base. However, the -1 consumable slot malus can prevent the player from capitalizing on strong consumables like The Chariot Tarot card, or, if somehow generated by Séance or Sixth Sense in the same run, the Deja Vu, Ouija, and Trance Spectral cards.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Ghost Deck: The aforementioned Spectral cards (Deja Vu, Ouija, and Trance) all become more accessible by becoming potential Shop presences. Moreover, the starting Hex card can also give Half Joker a noteworthy X1.5 Mult bonus, making it much more feasible to hold later into the run. Poker hands: Half Joker only synergizes with hands that can be formed with three or fewer cards: High Card Pair Three of a Kind Jokers: Half Joker uniquely encourages the user to go big with small hands. As a result, many of the Jokers it synergizes with will ideally play into this trait:

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Blue Joker: Giving +2 Chips to all hands played for each card remaining in your Deck, this one is ideal in the early-to-mid-game for empowering the hands this Joker already enables, as their low card count and lessened dependency on discards means its power is not dampened as much as it is by the 5-card hands. Delayed Gratification: The high amount of + Mult can allow the player to play using whatever they draw in their opening hand since they can play three cards that do not form a hand, rather than just discarding them to cycle for new cards.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Green Joker, Ride the Bus and Supernova: These Additive Mult Jokers will give even more score for playing repeated hands, which is something this Joker already encourages. Their downsides (-Mult on discard, reset when playing face card and single-hand focus, respectively) matter very little, as discards are less crucial, and only a small number of hands benefit in the first place. Juggler, Troubadour, and Turtle Bean: All three of these provide passive bonuses to hand size, allowing for easier assembly of Three of a Kinds, and most importantly, more opportunity to trigger 'held in hand' abilities, which scale particularly well with this Joker.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Raised Fist, Shoot the Moon, and Baron: These Jokers provide Mult bonuses based on the cards held in your hand (singular variable + Mult, multiple flat + Mult, and multiple flat XMult, respectively), which meshes very well with the need to play fewer cards. Reserved Parking: By repeatedly scoring numbered cards and Aces in small hands, while keeping face cards in hand, a large amount of money can potentially be earned. Sly Joker and Wily Joker: These both provide a flat number of Chips for hands containing a Pair or a Three of a Kind, respectively. Since Three of a Kind also contains a Pair, it can benefit from both of these Jokers simultaneously to reap a near-universal +150 Chips.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Card Sharp: A flat Multiplicative Mult Joker that gives X3 Mult if the played poker hand has been played previously in the round. Since all of the hands this Joker enables are easy to score, this suave fellow is nearly guaranteed to give his impressive bonus on all subsequently played hands. Certificate: A unique utility Joker that gives a technical hand size bonus by adding a playing card with a random Seal to the hand at the start of a round. This allows for even greater scaling of the hands this card enables. It also works particularly well with the aforementioned Blue Joker.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Mime: Allowing all 'held in hand' abilities to trigger an additional time, it gives a huge boost to the power ceiling of this Joker by allowing additional scoring from Steel cards and 'held in hand' Mult Jokers, money generation from Reserved Parking and Gold cards, and Planet card generation from Blue Seals. Ramen: Similarly to Green Joker, this card is essentially a free X2 Mult boost for a Half Joker build, as discards are less necessary in the first place. Space Joker and Burnt Joker: These both allow for easy poker hand level scaling, as they can easily be assembled and thus repeatedly played or discarded, respectively.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Steel Joker: Since this Joker already benefits greatly from a large number of Steel cards due to the lesser number of played cards, the bonus it gives just by adding Steel cards to the build makes it a natural choice. Stuntman: One of the strongest Chip Jokers in the game, providing an astounding +250 Chips to all played hands, at the cost of a passive -2 hand size penalty. While its drawback detracts from one of this Joker's primary strengths - holding onto more cards to activate 'held in hand' abilities - oftentimes the sheer power it provides will be more than enough to compensate.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: The Duo and/or The Trio: These are the strongest Multiplicative Mult Jokers to pair with this one, as only High Card is excluded from their effects (which is only sub-optimal in the Endless Antes). Much like the hand-specific Chip Jokers, Three of a Kinds can benefit from both simultaneously to pump out a staggering X6 Mult. The following Jokers could potentially have synergy with this Joker, but have noticeable downsides:

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: The following Jokers could potentially have synergy with this Joker, but have noticeable downsides: Splash: This Joker allows all played cards to count in scoring. When using this Joker, High Card and Pair can be used as makeshift discards while utilizing otherwise non-scoring cards that could have a nice card modifier to help with scoring, or another trait to mesh with unique Joker synergy. However, Three of a Kind is completely incapable of benefiting if Half Joker is being emphasized, and in the event that it is the focused hand, Splash would do nothing (like depicted in most other media).

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Marble Joker: Adding a Stone card to the Deck at the start of a round can sound enticing, and is especially so if the hands being scaled are High Card or Pair due to allowing more cards to be scored than usual, but the shot of Chips they provide usually is not enough to outweigh the large amassment of Jokers that provide score based on rank or suit - Stones lack both of these. On top of that, more cards in the deck means less of a chance of finding crucial Steel cards or Blue Seals. With a large number of Stones, Stone Joker can form a very potent Chip engine with it, but one should carefully consider all their options before picking this up.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Blackboard: While its Multiplicative Mult bonus is impressive, it can be difficult to trigger by only scoring 3 cards at a time without suit fixing. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong allow for the three poker hands Half Joker enables to be played more and more often and further increasing the power of cards like Green Joker, Ride the Bus and Supernova. Paint Brush and Palette provide passive hand size bonuses without necessitating the consumption of a Joker slot, allowing for easier capitalization on 'held in hand' effects. Telescope is a wonderful pickup in a build featuring this Joker, for the same reason that the Nebula Deck is a good choice.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Boss Blinds: This Joker is easily distinguishable when played against Amber Acorn, as it retains its unique shape even when flipped face-down. Poker hands: The following poker hands are formed of more than three cards, and thus gain no benefit from Half Joker: Two Pair Straight Flush Full House Four of a Kind Straight Flush Five of a Kind Flush House Flush Five

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Two Pair Straight Flush Full House Four of a Kind Straight Flush Five of a Kind Flush House Flush Five Jokers: Jokers oriented towards larger hands will contribute nothing to a Half Joker build. Some of the numerous examples include not being able to get its benefit while also scaling Square Joker, and being unable to capitalize on The Family, which is one of the strongest flat Multiplicative Mult Jokers in the game, and would otherwise be easy to pivot into from a Three of a Kind build.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Merry Andy: The +3 discards it provides are nice for most other builds, but for Half Joker builds, they are largely irrelevant for the reasons stated multiple times before. The -1 hand size penalty it provides can make it just hard enough to find Pairs and Three of a Kinds to be a severe detriment, as well as making Steel cards and Blue Seals harder to find (although it can be useful if the player also wants to play towards Banner or Delayed Gratification). Flower Pot also does not work well with Half Joker as the four suits are impossible to reach with 3 cards.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Boss Blinds: There is 1 Boss Blind that counters Half Joker, and a few others that can provide a noticeable challenge but do not directly counter it: The Psychic: Hands with less than 5 played cards will not score at all. Unless the player has scaled their build well enough, this is a definite run-ender for a Half Joker build. The Eye: Hands that have been played previously this Blind will not score at all. Half Joker only empowers 3 of the 12 hands in the game, so once these options are exhausted, it will not assist in scoring whatsoever. This can potentially cause a guaranteed run loss, but is less detrimental when encountered earlier.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: The Ox: Playing the poker hand that was the most played at the start of the same Ante will set the player's money to $0. This Joker struggles with it especially, as it encourages focusing on a small number of hands. Since the Jokers and card modifiers Half Joker bounces off of best are hard to come by consistently, this Boss Blind can potentially cause irreversible damage to the run by making them virtually inaccessible. The Wall and Violet Vessel: With their doubled and tripled Boss Blind size, respectively, they prove an extreme challenge to a Half Joker build without extreme amounts of scaling, as all three hands it enables have very low base Chips and Mult.

title: Half Joker
text: Half Joker: Trivia: This Joker is part of a set that doesn't adhere to the standard joker size, along with Wee Joker, Photograph, and Square Joker

title: Hallucination
text: Hallucination: Hallucination (Joker). Effect: 1 in 2 chance to create a Tarot card when any Booster Pack is opened, (Must have room). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Probability-Based: Yes. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Hallucination is a Common Effect Joker that has a 1 in 2 chance of creating a Tarot card any time you open a Booster Pack.

title: Hallucination
text: Hallucination: Decks: Magic Deck's extra consumable slot is very useful for saving Tarot cards. Green Deck encourages the player to spend money as they earn it, which works well with Hallucination. Jokers: Oops! All 6s will guarantee a Tarot card when used with Hallucination. Fortune Teller scales with the amount of Tarot cards used, and it's better when used on an Arcana Pack. Red Card also has synergy with Booster Packs. Blueprint and Brainstorm can copy Hallucination's effect when opening the Booster Packs, meaning there is a chance for 2 or even 3 Tarot cards.

title: Hallucination
text: Hallucination: Campfire can gain X0.25 Mult if the Tarot card that is generated is not necessary, and can be even higher if The Emperor or The High Priestess are generated. Driver's License and Vampire can be built around using the Tarot cards that Hallucination generates. Vouchers: Crystal Ball gives +1 consumable slot, allowing the player to hold more useful Tarot cards. Clearance Sale and Liquidation lower the price of booster packs, making it easier to purchase and generate more Tarot cards. Decks: Nebula Deck's missing consumable slot makes it significantly harder to hold and use the Tarots from Hallucination. Trivia: This is the only Joker to activate when opening a pack.

title: Hallucination
text: Hallucination: Trivia: This is the only Joker to activate when opening a pack. The art on this card is skewed and imperfect, like how many people report hallucinations to be. The texture of this Joker has protruding areas on the left and right sides, slightly exceeding the boundaries of a standard Joker. The only other Joker with this property is Brainstorm. When Hallucination is being copied by Blueprint or Brainstorm and manages to generate two Tarot cards, the "+1 Tarot" appears on Hallucination twice instead of once for Copy Joker and once for Hallucination. This is likely a visual bug.

title: Hanging Chad
text: Hanging Chad: Hanging Chad (Joker). Effect: Retrigger first played card used in scoring 2 additional times. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Beat a Boss Blind with a High Card. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Retrigger. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Hanging Chad is a Common Retrigger Joker that can retrigger the first scoring played card in a poker hand twice. This includes any card modifiers and/or extra+ Chips from Hiker, making these cards effectively three times more potent.

title: Hanging Chad
text: Hanging Chad: Usage Notes: Hanging Chad will not retrigger a Red Seal. A card with a Red Seal that is played as the first scoring card will only trigger for a total of four times (once for the initial trigger, twice for Hanging Chad, and once more for the Red Seal). DNA will not be triggered another two times by Hanging Chad and will only produce one copy of the played card. To unlock this Joker, the player must beat a Boss Blind with a High Card. Decks: The need for powerful enhanced cards to use with Hanging Chad makes it important to utilize Tarot cards and/or Spectral cards.

title: Hanging Chad
text: Hanging Chad: The Zodiac Deck increases the rate of Tarot cards in the Shop with its starting Tarot Merchant voucher. The Ghost Deck allows for Spectral cards to be found in the Shop, allowing for cards like Aura, Talisman, etc. to be more likely to acquire. The Yellow Deck and Green Deck can improve the player's early economy to purchase Booster Packs. These include Standard Packs which may have modified cards, reducing the need for further modification.

title: Hanging Chad
text: Hanging Chad: Poker hands: Cards in a Poker Hand can be rearranged in a player's hand before it is played, such that their highest scoring or most Modified card gets retriggered by Hanging Chad (i.e. the left-most card in a played hand). It does not matter how the cards are re-ordered in a player's Poker Hand. For example, a Straight will still count as one even if its played as Queen, Ace, King, Jack, 10. The Queen, in this case, will have triple its effect this way (e.g. it was a Polychrome Bonus card).

title: Hanging Chad
text: Hanging Chad: Smaller hands like High Card or Three of a Kind can help mitigate their lack of played scoring cards, by using Hanging Chad. A singular especially powerful card can make triple its impact with this Joker. Jokers: Photograph is one of the best duos with Hanging Chad, since it's also a common Joker, making it much more attainable. If a face card is the first scored card in a hand, it gives X8 Mult to the player's base mult, making it a strong early game to late game combination. When paired with Hiker, the first played scoring card will be permanently upgraded thrice, adding +15 Chips to the card, instead of the usual +5 Chips.

title: Hanging Chad
text: Hanging Chad: Any Jokers that are reliant on a specific type of played card to trigger can benefit from Hanging Chad, as it allows it to be triggered two additional times. Face-card Jokers like Scary Face, Triboulet, Smiley Face, etc. will be more effective with the additional triggers. Business Card can provide up to $6, with a face-card being the first card played (which can be guaranteed with Oops! All 6s). Suit-based Jokers like Greedy Joker, Gluttonous Joker, Onyx Agate, Ancient Joker, etc. can become even more powerful. Bloodstone can provide up to X3.375 Mult with a Heart card being played first (which can be guaranteed with Oops! All 6s).

title: Hanging Chad
text: Hanging Chad: Other rank-based Jokers such as Fibonacci, Odd Todd, Scholar, Walkie Talkie, etc. can benefit from the additional triggers. If the first played card is a 2, Wee Joker can scale three times faster, by gaining +24 Chips instead of +8 Chips. Lucky Cat can gain more XMult, by having a Lucky card be played first, allowing it to potentially trigger more often. Tarot and Spectral generating Jokers like Vagabond, 8 Ball, Séance, etc. can provide the necessary consumables to empower playing cards, and help in triggering the above mentioned Jokers (ex. changing the suit of a card with The Sun for Bloodstone). Modifiers: Gold Seal can give a total of $9.

title: Hanging Chad
text: Hanging Chad: Modifiers: Gold Seal can give a total of $9. Glass card benefits greatly as it can provide a whopping X8 Mult base Mult. Lucky card has a higher chance to proc with three triggers. Polychrome cards also greatly benefit as it can provide X3.375 Mult base Mult. Trivia: The dot and line markings along the left edge of the card are binary numbers, where a dot represents 0 and a dash represents 1. The four visible numbers are, from top to bottom, 1, 2, 4, and 5. The hanging chad presumably obscures the symbols "••||" or "0011", which is binary for 3.

title: Hanging Chad
text: Hanging Chad: A "chad" is the fragment of paper created when a hole is made in paper or similar substances, such as with a hole punch. A "hanging" chad is one that hasn't fully separated, remaining attached at a single corner. This became a major issue during the 2000 U.S. presidential election, where hanging chads on punch card ballots led to controversy and multiple recounts, ultimately requiring a court decision on whether such ballots should be counted. A visual reference to this appears in "How I Met Your Mother", where Ted Mosby wears a "Hanging Chad" costume in Season 1, Episode 6. This specific depiction of a "Hanging Chad" closely resembles the design of the card.

title: Hanging Chad
text: Hanging Chad: Despite being see through from the front, this Joker has the default face down texture. This is the only retrigger joker that is not uncommon.

title: Hiker
text: Hiker: Hiker (Joker). Effect: Every played card permanently gains +5 Chips when scored. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Hiker is an Uncommon Chips Joker that permanently adds +5 Chips onto every played scoring card for the entirety of the run. The additional chips stack onto each other, so the next time a card is scored that has been boosted by Hiker, it will get an additional +5 Chips for a total of +10 Chips, etc. These bonus chips attached to the playing card cannot be removed and will be retained even if Hiker is sold, the card's suit/enhancement is changed, etc.

title: Hiker
text: Hiker: This also works with any Bonus cards or Stone cards; they will get an additional +5 Chips on top of the additional + Chips they already had. If a card with Hiker's additional chips was copied with Death, Cryptid or DNA, it will retain the bonuses from the copied card. Decks: The Abandoned Deck and Mad World both have fewer cards than the standard 52 card deck, making finding the desired cards to level up with Hiker much easier. It also benefits from centralization around certain ranks, as those cards will already be played more often. The Red Deck allows for +1 discard to find cards more reliably.

title: Hiker
text: Hiker: The Red Deck allows for +1 discard to find cards more reliably. The Blue Deck gives a +1 hand allowing the player to score more cards for Hiker. The Painted Deck increases the player's hand size, making it easier to find desired cards, in addition to making better hands easier to find for those cards. The Erratic Deck starts with uneven ranks and suits, which can allow the player to score more cards, allowing Hiker to add more bonus chips to said cards. The Plasma Deck benefits the most from Hiker thanks to its balancing feature, as Chips scale a lot faster than Mult.

title: Hiker
text: Hiker: Poker hands: Hiker upgrades whenever cards are scored. Naturally, hands with more scoring cards will perform better with Hiker. In particular, Full House, Four of a Kind, Five of a Kind, Flush House, and Flush Five work well as they allow playing multiple of the same rank, upgrading multiple cards of that rank at the same time and making them more appealing and powerful to play in the future. Jokers: Retrigger Jokers are invaluable to Hiker's success, as they allow cards to be scored multiple times and get upgraded multiple times. In addition, each scoring will add multitudes of chips to the final score, as the cards played ideally have dozens, even hundreds of bonus chips.

title: Hiker
text: Hiker: Sock and Buskin and Hack work best for these purposes, as their retriggers are only rank-reliant. Splash has an interesting synergy with Hiker. Because it scores all cards played, certain cards can be upgraded with Hiker that normally would not be due to the hand. This dual combo can act as a strong chip provider for High Card and Pair builds, as one can focus on playing the same cards again and again to continuously upgrade them without caring about rank.
