Jokers that give Mult based on scored cards are helpful, such as Smiley Face and Fibonacci, especially if they also benefit from the retriggers Hiker loves.

title: Hiker
text: Hiker: Vagabond can work well with Hiker, as it requires many hands to be played to work the best. A number of other Jokers like this benefit as well, like Ride the Bus and Spare Trousers. Vampire can occasionally work well with Hiker. The bonus chips Hiker provides makes up for the lack of enhancements on cards. This idea also combos well with Vagabond, as one can end up playing many hands to get as much value from Vampire and Vagabond as possible while also upgrading all their cards. This does weaken one of Hiker's main draws, though, that being buffing already powerful modified cards to even greater heights.

title: Hiker
text: Hiker: DNA, ironically, works best with Hiker after Hiker has been sold. Creating copies of cards will usually end up flooding the deck with too many cards to upgrade in a round, and takes away a hand that could otherwise be used upgrading cards. It is better to copy an already powerful card after Hiker is sold to retroactively make it as if Hiker buffed an additional card each round it was used. Wee Joker needs 2s to be played to upgrade it, however, 2s are weak early game due to their low base chip count. Hiker can buff a player's 2s to 12 Chips from just 2 triggers, which is higher than a base face card value of 10 Chips.

title: Hiker
text: Hiker: Seals: Red Seals can also retrigger cards for Hiker, giving an additional permanent +5 Chips, for a total of +10 Chips, each time the card is played. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give +1 discard, which helps the player to find cards more reliably. Grabber and Nacho Tong both give +1 hand, allowing the player to score more cards for Hiker. Paint Brush and Palette both increase the player's hand size, making it easier to find desired cards, in addition to making better hands easier to find for those cards. Decks: Fragile makes Hiker useless, as every played card will be destroyed once played. Double or Nothing debuffs all cards when scored, which makes it impractical to use Hiker.

title: Hiker
text: Hiker: Double or Nothing debuffs all cards when scored, which makes it impractical to use Hiker. Poker hands: High Card and Pair are generally the worst to play with Hiker, as the fewest cards are scored. There are some circumstances where they are decent, but those circumstances are uncommon. High Card and Pair have the least amount of scored playing cards, making it less useful with Hiker since only those cards will be enhanced. However, it is possible to make these poker hands work if the circumstances are right (ex. Splash). Blinds: The Pillar debuffs previously played cards of the Ante, potentially reducing Hiker's value.

title: Hiker
text: Hiker: Blinds: The Pillar debuffs previously played cards of the Ante, potentially reducing Hiker's value. Trivia: This Joker's name and art is a pun on the word "hike", as it can also mean a sudden price increase, similar to how its effect increases a playing card's Chips. Hiker is the only Joker that can permanently and repetitively buff playing cards.

title: Hit the Road
text: Hit the Road: Hit the Road (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains X0.5 Mult for every Jack discarded this round, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Discard 5 Jacks at the same time. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Hit the Road is a Rare scaling Multiplicative Mult Joker which provides an additional temporary X0.5 Mult per discarded Jack. This Joker starts with X1 Mult and is reset back to X1 Mult at the end of each round.

title: Hit the Road
text: Hit the Road: Usage Notes: If the player has multiple copies of Hit the Road, they will all level up if one Jack is discarded. Decks: Red Deck may work well with Hit the Road thanks to the +1 discard per round it provides, allowing more Jacks to be discarded. Painted Deck makes drawing Jacks easier thanks to its +2 hand size. Five-Card Draw offers +3 discards per round, allowing a larger amount of Jacks overall to be discarded.

title: Hit the Road
text: Hit the Road: Five-Card Draw offers +3 discards per round, allowing a larger amount of Jacks overall to be discarded. Poker hands: Hit the Road can work with any hand, but with less deck fixing, it is better to play small hands, like High Card, Pair, or Three of a Kind. This ensures that you can discard Jacks while keeping cards in hand to score. Jokers: DNA can create 1 Jack per round (or more with copy effects), increasing the amount that Hit the Road can be scaled. It is especially beneficial to duplicate Purple Seal Jacks. Drunkard's +1 Discard allows more Jacks to be found and discarded.

title: Hit the Road
text: Hit the Road: Drunkard's +1 Discard allows more Jacks to be found and discarded. Juggler allows for more Jacks to be found and good cards to be held in hand for scoring. Merry Andy gives +3 Discards, allowing more Jacks to be discarded, with the caveat of -1 hand size. The hand size can make Jacks harder to find and force the player to discard fewer Jacks to hold on to scoring cards. Mail-In Rebate is one of the best Jokers to pair with Hit the Road, as the player is already most likely using all of their discards. It can generate an absurd amount of money with good deck fixing.

title: Hit the Road
text: Hit the Road: Faceless Joker is more reliable money with less deck fixing required, although it has far less potential profit than Mail-In Rebate. Yorick scales slower than Hit the Road, but its mult never resets, making it better in the long run. Once Yorick has scaled enough, Hit the Road may no longer be necessary. Trading Card can destroy cards that are not Jacks, allowing for Jacks to be found more consistently to discard. However, Trading Card takes a discard to use, so it should only be utilized if scoring is not an issue.

title: Hit the Road
text: Hit the Road: Troubadour allows for more Jacks to be found and for scoring cards to be kept in hand. With a strong enough build, the -1 hand's downside can be minimal. Consumables: Death and Cryptid can be used to create more Jacks. The Hanged Man can remove non-Jack cards, allowing for Jacks to be found and made more easily. Medium and Purple Seal are best placed on Jacks with Hit the Road, as you want to discard them anyway, and the Tarot cards generated also synergize with Hit the Road. Strength can be used to turn 10s (or possibly 9s) into Jacks. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy each give +1 discard per round, allowing for more Jacks to be discarded.

title: Hit the Road
text: Hit the Road: Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy each give +1 discard per round, allowing for more Jacks to be discarded. Paint Brush and Palette allows for +1 hand size each, making it easier to draw Jacks into the hand. Blinds: The Hook discards 2 random cards every hand played, which will scale Hit the Road if the discarded card(s) are Jacks. If Hit the Road is debuffed on the final hand against Crimson Heart, it will not reset, allowing it to scale for another round. Decks: Abandoned Deck, Mad World, and Medusa don't work well with Hit the Road due to lack of initial Jacks. Blast Off doesn't work well with Hit the Road, as this deck only starts with 2 discards.

title: Hit the Road
text: Hit the Road: Blast Off doesn't work well with Hit the Road, as this deck only starts with 2 discards. Poker hands: Hands that work with multiple numbered cards, like Straight, Full House, Straight Flush, and Flush House, don't work well with Hit the Road because in an ideal deck you would only have Jacks; if not, you have no discards left to find these hands. Jokers: Burglar removes all Discards, making Hit the Road useless. Any Jokers that disincentivize discarding, like Delayed Gratification, Banner, Green Joker, and Ramen, have poor synergy with Hit the Road. Blinds: The Water starts with 0 Discards and therefore renders Hit the Road useless.

title: Hit the Road
text: Hit the Road: Blinds: The Water starts with 0 Discards and therefore renders Hit the Road useless. The Mark makes it difficult to see if a given card is a Jack or another face card. The Plant debuffs face cards and therefore renders Hit the Road useless. Stakes: Blue Stake and above hinder Hit the Road's potential because they have 1 less discard by default. Trivia: The name and effect of this Joker are based on the 1961 hit song "Hit the Road Jack", written by Percy Mayfield and originally recorded by Ray Charles. The border for Hit the Road is a slightly different shade from all other Jokers. Hit the Road's hex code is #C2C7C9, whereas the standard is #B9C2D2.

title: Hologram
text: Hologram: Hologram (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains X0.25 Mult every time a playing card is added to your deck, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Hologram is an Uncommon scaling Multiplicative Mult Joker that gains X0.25 Mult when new playing cards are added to the deck. It starts at X1 Mult and gains an additional X0.25 Mult for each playing card added after its acquisition. The effect is based solely on gaining cards; keeping the cards afterwards is not required.

title: Hologram
text: Hologram: Decks: Ghost Deck offers upside to Hologram thanks to its easier access to Spectral cards, especially those mentioned in the Synergetic Consumables section. Abandoned Deck and Mad World work well with Hologram thanks to their low amount of starting cards. Medusa and Monolith both work well with Hologram, as these decks both start with a Marble Joker, which means Hologram gains X0.25 Mult for free each blind. Poker hands: Hologram can be used with any Poker Hand, but small hands such as High Card or Pair are affected the least when constantly adding new cards to the deck. Jokers: DNA duplicates the first card played if it is the only card.

title: Hologram
text: Hologram: Jokers: DNA duplicates the first card played if it is the only card. Certificate adds a random playing card to hand when a round starts. Marble Joker adds a Stone card when a Blind is selected. Blueprint and Brainstorm are powerful on any build, but they are especially useful with Hologram, as they can copy all of DNA, Certificate, Marble Joker, and Hologram itself. Blue Joker gives Chips for every remaining card in your deck. However, Blue Joker does need to keep cards in the deck. Trading Card allows you to destroy cards at will, thus preventing the deck from becoming too bloated while keeping the benefit of this Joker.

title: Hologram
text: Hologram: Vagabond and Cartomancer create Tarots, some of which are useful for handling added cards that aren't meant to be kept. Sixth Sense and Séance can create useful spectral cards (see the Consumables section), which can give this Joker a sizable boost. Additionally, Sixth Sense can slightly alleviate deck bloating by destroying 6s. Perkeo can then create copies of said spectral cards, scaling your Hologram by up to X1 Mult per round (or more with Blueprint and Brainstorm). Consumables: Familiar, Grim, Incantation, and Cryptid add cards to the deck and buff Hologram at the same time. Immolate removes 5 cards and gains $20, which is a good way to trim the deck at no cost to Hologram.

title: Hologram
text: Hologram: Glass cards from Justice have a chance to shatter, so they won't clog the deck forever, and they'll be useful for XMult in the meantime. The Hanged Man allows destroying any miscellaneous junk cards that were only added to pump Hologram. Vouchers: Magic Trick adds playing cards to the Shop, effectively allowing players to scale Hologram at X0.25 Mult per $1. More playing cards can be purchased per shop with help from Overstock and Overstock Plus to increase the shop selection, plus Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut to make rerolling cheaper. Omen Globe makes it easier to find the Familiar, Grim, Incantation, and Cryptid Spectral cards, all of which add playing cards into the deck and thus scale Hologram.

title: Hologram
text: Hologram: Decks: Fragile doesn't work well with Hologram due to all sources of adding playing cards besides Cryptid and DNA being banned in this deck. Poker hands: Hologram is probably weakest when paired with strategies that prioritize Straights and Straight Flushes, because it is harder to gain cards into runs than it is to gain cards into sets. Jokers: Erosion has anti-synergy as it gives mult for having a small deck. Since one of the primary ways to scale Hologram is with the use of Booster Packs, Red Card can be hard to use alongside Hologram.

title: Hologram
text: Hologram: Trivia: This card is animated, like the Legendary Jokers (the Joker face is hovering above the card), but it is also flickering like an old CRT television screen. This hovering effect can also be seen on the placeholder image for undiscovered Jokers in the Collection. When Hologram turns Negative, the sprite colors of the Joker itself aren't inverted because the animated sprite is separated from the card itself. On Gold Stake, the Rental Sticker is mostly obscured by the Joker's hat, which may catch players by surprise.

title: Ice Cream
text: Ice Cream: Ice Cream (Joker). Effect: +100 Chips, -5 Chips for every hand played. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: ✗ No. Ice Cream is a Common +Chips Joker that initially provides a large Chips boost which slowly fades over time. When this boost reaches 0 Chips, it is destroyed, denoted by the text "Melted!"

title: Ice Cream
text: Ice Cream: Usage Notes: Ice Cream starts at 100 Chips and will decrease by 5 Chips after each hand played, so the first hand will provide the full 100 Chips, not 95. The sell value of Ice Cream does not depend on its current chip value, so it is best to sell Ice Cream when it is at +5 Chips, instead of letting it get destroyed (worth $0). The Non-Perishable challenge bans Ice Cream. Decks: Plasma Deck benefits the most from Ice Cream, as the large amount of chips, when balanced, greatly boost score for the played hand.

title: Ice Cream
text: Ice Cream: Poker hands: It's recommended to play strong, 5-cards hand to score large with Ice Cream. If you can beat blinds with fewer hands, then Ice Cream will last longer. However, when paired with other jokers, Ice Cream can be part of a strategy that makes low-chip hands, like High Card or Pair, high scoring. Jokers: Ice Cream can synergize with the following jokers: Throwback: Ice Cream melts with every hand played, and Throwback wants to skip blinds. As a chips-type Joker, Ice Cream pairs well with any additive mult or multiplicative mult Jokers. Boss Blinds: If a hand that is not allowed is played during The Psychic, The Mouth or The Eye, Ice Cream will still lose 5 Chips.

title: Ice Cream
text: Ice Cream: Strategy: Ice Cream is one of the best early-game Jokers. Most chips-type Jokers have significant tradeoffs, or require more hands to boost properly, which makes them unsuitable for the early-game.

title: Ice Cream
text: Ice Cream: Without any other jokers, enhanced cards, or leveled hand types, the best hand is a Royal Flush, worth 100 Chips, plus 50 Chips for the cards, and 8 Mult. A fully topped ice cream is worth the equivalent of x1.66 Mult for this hand. For a more typical good hand (like a KKKQQ full house), worth 40 Chips, plus 50 Chips for the cards, and 4 Mult, a fully topped ice cream is worth the equivalent of x2.2 Mult! There are no jokers in the deck this effective for a starting build.

title: Ice Cream
text: Ice Cream: As Ice Cream melts, it becomes significantly less valuable. If you depend on Ice Cream, keep an eye out for its replacement. Try not to add editions to it, as you'll lose them when it melts away. In the early game, when paired a strong global + Mult joker, like Mystic Summit or Gros Michel, Ice Cream can allow otherwise low-value hands to score big, letting you beat blinds without using hands or discards, thereby racking up an early economy. Once you get past Ante 2 or 3, Ice Cream loses its relative effectiveness, compared to other build strategies.

title: Ice Cream
text: Ice Cream: Trivia: Ice cream is a cold dairy product eaten as a treat. As it heats up, it becomes less solid and melts over time, reflected in game by the Ice Cream losing potency as hands are played. Ice Cream's blue background, and the blue-colored scoop at the top of the cone, tie into its ability to give Chips to your score. The text "Melted!" will flash under Ice Cream when it disappears. Ice cream is also a concession dessert commonly served at carnivals, circuses, and fairgrounds, which are also places where clowns and jesters are known to perform.

title: Ice Cream
text: Ice Cream: This Joker is part of the group of "Consumable" Jokers that can be destroyed with usage, dubbed "Food Jokers" due to their shared theme. The other Jokers in this group are Popcorn, Gros Michel, Cavendish, Egg, Seltzer, Turtle Bean, Ramen, and Diet Cola. It is one of the five Jokers to have a physical card from Balatro: Special Edition. The four other jokers where that is also the case are Joker, Hack, Abstract Joker and Throwback. While it is unknown what flavors the Ice Cream joker's scoops are, the blue, orange, and red colors are a reference to Jimbo's--or a Joker's--traditional color scheme in Balatro.

title: Ice Cream
text: Ice Cream: Ice Cream is one of the few "food jokers" to get merch from Makeship in the recently campaigned Food Joker Pin Set alongside Popcorn and Egg.

title: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker: Invisible Joker (Joker). Effect: After 2 rounds, sell this card to Duplicate a random Joker, (Currently 0 /2), (Removes Negative from copy). Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Win a run without ever having more than 4 Jokers. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: ✗ No. Invisible Joker is a Rare Effect Joker that can be sold after two rounds to duplicate a random Joker in the player's inventory.

title: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker: The copied Joker will retain almost all the properties of the original, including any scaling, Edition, and Stickers. There are only 2 exceptions: Negative Editions, which are removed from the copy, and copying a second Invisible Joker, which will have its counter reset to 0/2. When Invisible Joker is debuffed by either its own Perishable Sticker or the Crimson Heart Boss Blind, it can still be sold for the normal sell price, but will no longer duplicate another Joker. Usage Notes: Unlocking Invisible Joker is done easiest on the Painted Deck since it has -1 Joker slot, but only if the player does not purchase any Negative Jokers, or the Antimatter Voucher.

title: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker: Invisible Joker can duplicate a second Invisible Joker if players manage to acquire one via Showman. However, the duplicated Invisible Joker will have its rounds played status reset to 0/2. An Invisible Joker that is duplicated by the Ankh Spectral card will be created with the same number of "round played" status as the original. Any copies created by selling a second Invisible Joker will still have 0/2 rounds played, however.

title: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker: A duplicated Joker from a Negative edition Invisible Joker can let the player have 1 more Joker than the number of slots. If the player manages to acquire a negative Invisible Joker and sell it with all joker slots filled, the player will still gain a copy of a random joker. Doing so, however, will add -1 to the Joker Slots (example: 6/5), preventing other Negative Jokers from being bought. If Invisible Joker copies a debuffed Joker, the copied Joker will also be debuffed. The same applies for temporary debuff caused by Crimson Heart, while in next hand they will both recover.

title: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker: Specifically, if an Invisible Joker copies a debuffed Negative Joker (whether it obtains negative earlier and then debuff, or vice versa), though the copied Joker does not have a negative effect, selling it will still result in a decrease in Joker Slot, which may be a bug. Copying a Joker does not copy the card back - the copied Joker will always be created with the Red Deck's card back and can thus be identified even when turned face down by the Amber Acorn boss blind. This is presumed to be a bug. The line (Removes Negative from copy) in the Joker's effect only shows if the player already has a negative Joker.

title: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker: The line (Removes Negative from copy) in the Joker's effect only shows if the player already has a negative Joker. Selling an active Invisible Joker while having no other Jokers will show a "No other Jokers!" message in place of the normal "Duplicated!" text. Selling an active Invisible Joker when the player has more Jokers than Joker slots (example: 6/5) will show an exceedingly rare "No Room!" message, despite the Joker description not explicitly stating (Must have room). The Non-Perishable challenge bans Invisible Joker.

title: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker: The Non-Perishable challenge bans Invisible Joker. Decks: Any deck can benefit from Invisible Joker, but the Black Deck offers more rooms to maneuver thanks to its +1 Joker Slot. That said, having an extra joker slot makes Invisible Joker less likely to pick a specific joker. Poker hands: Invisible Joker does not synergize with any poker hand. Jokers: Invisible Joker does not synergize with any other Joker, other than whatever joker you have that's the "best". To provide the best result, players are advised to sell any unimportant Jokers they don't want before selling Invisible Joker, to ensure they get a duplicate of the intended Joker.

title: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker: Blinds: Because Verdant Leaf requires selling one Joker to neutralize its effect, Invisible Joker can benefit players if carried from the start of Ante 8, which can then be sold to disable Verdant Leaf and still retain 5 Jokers. Decks: On a Knife's Edge: Invisible Joker might duplicate the Eternal, Pinned Ceremonial Dagger, leaving one permanently stuck behind the other and thus unable to scale. Jokers: Generally, passive effect Joker like Four Fingers or Pareidolia do not benefit from being copied by Invisible Joker. There are also some Jokers that might be expected to work well when copied but can behave unexpectedly with multiple copies. This includes:

title: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker: Sixth Sense: Only one Spectral card will be created, even with multiple copies of it. To Do List: Unlike Jokers like Mail-In Rebate, where multiple copies will always choose the same rank, multiple copies of To Do List may want different hands to be played. Vampire: Only the leftmost Vampire will scale when removing Enhancements. Trivia: The card art is semi-transparent. The art of Invisible Joker is actually the outfit of Jimbo (or in other words, Jimbo becomes invisible). This can be more clearly seen from the art in the demo version, which lacks the transparent effect.

title: Invisible Joker
text: Invisible Joker: Of the three jokers with sell effects (the other two being Diet Cola and Luchador), this is the only joker that cannot be copied by Blueprint or Brainstorm. It is also the only Rare Joker that cannot be copied by Blueprint or Brainstorm. In the second demo, duplicating Invisible Joker using a second Invisible Joker preserved the "round played" status (2/2), thus it could be immediately sold, creating another ready-to-sell copy. This process effectively allowed players to farm infinite money by duplicating and selling Invisible Joker over and over. In other media: The Spectral Joker from Vampire Survivors is likely based on this joker.

title: Joker
text: Joker: Joker (Joker). Effect: +4 Mult. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $2. Sell Price: $1. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Joker is a Common Additive Mult Joker. It provides +4 Mult to all played hands.

title: Joker
text: Joker: The Five-Card Draw challenge starts the player with a copy of Joker.

title: Joker
text: Joker: The Five-Card Draw challenge starts the player with a copy of Joker. Overview: In spite of its pitiful Mult bonus, Joker is a deceptively strong pickup in the early Antes due to its nature as an unconditional and extremely cheap score booster. It doubles the score of the most common 5-card hands at Level 1 (Straight, Flush, and Full House), making it so that every Blind in Ante 1 can be cleared with just one of these hands, provided the base Chips add up to 75 or more. Assuming the player spends $2 in the first Shop to buy Joker, buys/sells nothing else, and scores a sufficient 5-card hand (or Four of a Kind) in all three Blinds without using any more hands, they would enter Ante 2 with a minimum of:

title: Joker
text: Joker: $19 on Black Deck $27 on Blue Deck $29 on Green Deck $40 on Yellow Deck $23 on all other Decks

title: Joker
text: Joker: $27 on Blue Deck $29 on Green Deck $40 on Yellow Deck $23 on all other Decks While Ante 1 can be cleared without spending any money, the Big and Boss Blind generally require 2 or even 3 hands to beat without Jokers, depending on luck of the draw, and being able to clear them in a single hand with Joker generally means saving $1 more than usual, while also having a little bit of no-frills scoring help for the future Antes. Joker's extremely cheap buying price (which is only bested by Credit Card) also gives easier access to a decent lineup of 3 or more Jokers at the start of Ante 2, which can help save even more money by consistently putting out lethal hands.

title: Joker
text: Joker: With all that said, a quick glance at the Blind requirements past Ante 1 makes it incredibly clear that Joker does not scale well to the later Antes at all; Abstract Joker, for example, is a direct upgrade to it while holding more than 1 Joker card, and several other cards like Green Joker, Ride the Bus, and Supernova can put out power equivalent to dozens of this Joker with their Additive Mult scaling capabilities. As a result, it should generally be sold once the player has the rest of their Joker slots filled with more impactful Jokers, or perhaps even earlier if gaining its sell value means earning more interest next round.

title: Joker
text: Joker: It can potentially be kept many Antes later if it has an Edition, or even permanently if it ends up being Negative, but even then, its help as a baseline is exactly the same as a single Mult card provided by The Empress Tarot card, so its impact will be at best marginal. Trivia: This Joker resembles Jimbo, and is provided to the player during the Tutorial. Coming in at an extremely succinct 7 characters, Joker has the shortest description of all cards in the game. It even has a shorter description than the basic numbered cards ranked 2 through 9, all of which have 8-character descriptions.

title: Joker
text: Joker: Joker is one of the few non-effect Jokers to have a consistent, unconditional, unchanging effect. The others are Credit Card and Golden Joker. Joker is one of the four jokers that is featured in the official physical playing card deck. The 3 others are Juggler, Blueprint, and Gros Michel. It is also available as a physical joker card in Balatro: Special Edition. It is one of the five Jokers to have a physical card from Balatro: Special Edition, with the four other jokers being Ice Cream, Hack, Abstract Joker and Throwback.

title: Joker
text: Joker: When the game tries to generate a Joker of a given Rarity, if all Jokers of that Rarity are unavailable (already owned without Showman, banned by a Challenge Deck, unmet requirements, etc), it will generate Joker instead as a fallback. The only exception to this is the Rare Tag, which will instead "Nope!" and do nothing. Joker is the only Joker with a cost of $2. Joker appears on an Ante Up! shirt in a merch collaboration with Fangamer. The two other jokers that appear on the same shirt include Popcorn and Cavendish. Before the main menu shows up, Joker will pop up from the bottom of the screen.

title: Joker
text: Joker: Before the main menu shows up, Joker will pop up from the bottom of the screen. If the player used Joker to win a certain Stake and had the "Display Stake Stickers during Run" setting turned on, the Joker will show up with its corresponding Stake Sticker. In other media: In Black Mirror, there is a scene in "Hotel Reverie" where a character is seen playing Balatro, and Joker is a card shown onscreen. Campfire, Blue Joker, Sixth Sense, The Empress, and Uranus are shown onscreen as well.

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: Joker Stencil (Joker). Effect: X1 Mult for each empty Joker slot, Joker Stencil included, (Currently X1). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Joker Stencil is an Uncommon Multiplicative Mult Joker that gives the player X1 Mult per empty Joker slot, including this Joker.

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: Decks: Black Deck is good with this Joker, as this deck gives +1 Joker slot, which basically gives it an extra X1 Mult. Similarly, Five-Card Draw is even better with this Joker, as this deck gives +2 Joker slots, which basically gives it an extra X2 Mult. Ghost Deck can be potent with Joker Stencil thanks to its easier access to Spectral cards, especially those mentioned in the Synergetic Spectral cards section. Nebula Deck is really good with this Joker, as it relies less on having many Jokers, thus freeing up slots. Zodiac Deck can be good with this Joker, as it gives more chances for cards other than Jokers to appear.

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: Zodiac Deck can be good with this Joker, as it gives more chances for cards other than Jokers to appear. Poker hands: Strong five-card hands like Flush, Straight, or Full House synergize well with Joker Stencil thanks to their high base Mult. Jokers: Any Negative Joker works well with this, as they do not take up a Joker slot.

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: Jokers: Any Negative Joker works well with this, as they do not take up a Joker slot. Because the Joker Stencil counts itself as an empty slot, multiple Joker Stencils combine brilliantly. If you have five slots, two Joker Stencils, and no other Jokers, they both provide X5 Mult for a combined total of X25 Mult. A negative joker stencil gives an extra X1 Mult to each Joker Stencil (the formula being XMult = Empty Joker slots + # of Joker Stencils). Invisible Joker can be very good for duplicating the Joker Stencil, provided you can play around the loss of X1 Mult for two rounds before selling it.

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: While Blueprint and Brainstorm both copy the main XMult effect of Joker Stencil, they do not take on the secondary effect of acting as an empty joker slot. This makes their synergies inadvisable if buying them takes the Joker Stencil down to X1 Mult, rendering it useless. However, as long as the Joker Stencil stays above X1 Mult, multiple copies of its XMult effect will provide a higher combined XMult than a singular copy of it, even if that means the XMult being copied is slightly lower (for example, X3 Mult < X2 Mult * X2 Mult).

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: Any Joker giving Mult is good, as it's better to have a bigger base Mult to multiply off of. Jokers that can reach high levels of Mult by themselves, like Red Card, Flash Card, or Bootstraps, are really good, as you don't have to rely on multiple Jokers to get large amounts of Mult. Ceremonial Dagger in particular always empties out a Joker slot when it gains +Mult. Spectral cards: Ectoplasm makes one of your Jokers Negative, adding +1 Joker slot and therefore adding X1 Mult.

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: Spectral cards: Ectoplasm makes one of your Jokers Negative, adding +1 Joker slot and therefore adding X1 Mult. Ankh can duplicate Joker Stencil, effectively raising your XMult Mult by the 2nd power. If you only have 1 Joker Stencil and 5 total Joker slots, this would be X5 Mult ^2, which equals X25 Mult. This can be done multiple times if your Joker Stencil is Eternal. Vouchers: Antimatter provides +1 Joker Slot and therefore gives it an extra X1 Mult. Blinds: Selling a Joker to disable Verdant Leaf will give Joker Stencil an extra X1 Mult (unless the Joker is Negative).

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: Stakes: On Black Stake and higher, the Eternal sticker can allow for Ankh to make multiple copies of Joker Stencil, which is made more powerful when combined with the Polychrome from Hex. Or, if combined with Perkeo and Ectoplasm, the elusive naneinf score can be achieved with hundreds of Negative Joker Stencils. Because of the hand size reduction, however, you will immediately lose the next round. Decks: Painted Deck hamstrings Joker Stencil with its -1 Joker Slot, giving it X1 Mult less. Similarly, Cruelty hamstrings Joker Stencil even more with its -2 Joker Slots, giving it X2 Mult less.

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: Similarly, Cruelty hamstrings Joker Stencil even more with its -2 Joker Slots, giving it X2 Mult less. Plasma Deck is also generally not good with this Joker, as usually the player either wants a lot of chips for early antes or needs a lot more mult for later antes, more than what this Joker gives. 15 Minute City and Blast Off do not work well with Joker Stencil, as these decks both start with two Eternal Jokers, which means Joker Stencil gives less XMult than usual. Not only that, but Blast Off also reduces a Joker slot, which means Joker Stencil gives even less XMult than usual.

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: Typecast sets your Joker Slots to 0 after ante 4, which sets Joker Stencil to X0 Mult or less. Poker hands: Weaker hands with low base Mult, like High Card, Pair, or Two Pair, have poor synergies with Joker Stencil, unless heavily leveled up using Planet cards. Jokers: Abstract Joker requires filling up all Joker Slots to maximize its effect, and thus has anti-synergy with Joker Stencil. Riff-Raff adds two jokers per blind selected, reducing empty slots for Joker Stencil to use.

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: Riff-Raff adds two jokers per blind selected, reducing empty slots for Joker Stencil to use. Trivia: A "stencil" is a thin piece of material, usually paper, metal, or plastic, that has letters or patterns cut out of it. The stencil is then used to print a design or sentence on a surface by applying ink or paint through the cut-out holes. This is reflected in the Joker's design, as the card has a joker that's been cut out of the middle of it. The center of the Joker Stencil texture is transparent, allowing you to see through it when moving this Joker around. However, when it is flipped face-down, it uses the same intact card back as the rest.

title: Joker Stencil
text: Joker Stencil: Of all of the scaling Multiplicative Mult Jokers, Joker Stencil is the only one to not include a "Mult" in the "(Currently x# Mult)" area.

title: Jolly Joker
text: Jolly Joker: Jolly Joker (Joker). Effect: +8 Mult if played hand contains a Pair. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Jolly Joker is a Common Joker that conditionally provides Additive Mult to played hands. It will give +8 Mult if the played hand contains a Pair (i.e., 2 or more cards of the same rank). This is not the same as being a Pair; Two Pair, Three of a Kind, Full House, Four of a Kind, Five of a Kind, Flush House, and Flush Five always contain a Pair, while Flush, Straight, and Straight Flush can contain a Pair under the correct circumstances.

title: Jolly Joker
text: Jolly Joker: The rationale for using this Joker is mostly comparable to that of the standard Joker, with its effect being stronger at the cost of a mild condition and a higher buy price. While cheap, and a reasonable pickup in the first few Antes, its Additive Mult bonus is overall insignificant, compared to what some scaling or more specialized Jokers can offer. Unless better options are encountered, it should be sold the moment a better Joker contends for its spot.

title: Jolly Joker
text: Jolly Joker: Decks: Virtually all of the Decks work comparably well with Jolly Joker, as Pair is the easiest hand to assemble - barring High Card (which always is assembled), and it is all but guaranteed to find one after a discard or two outside of the most extreme circumstances. Abandoned Deck and Mad World: These Deck are favored by this Joker, as they contain less overall ranks, and total cards, which makes it that much easier to find a Pair. Nebula Deck: Scaling Mercury using this Deck's integral Telescope Voucher can make it a worthwhile choice.

title: Jolly Joker
text: Jolly Joker: Nebula Deck: Scaling Mercury using this Deck's integral Telescope Voucher can make it a worthwhile choice. Plasma Deck: Has very slight anti-synergy with this Joker, as Additive Mult is overall not a good complement to the Deck's strength; Chips are preferred in the non-Endless Antes, and past that, several sources of Multiplicative Mult are preferred. Poker hands: Jolly Joker can trigger on any hand except for High Card. Through deck manipulation, even Flushes can benefit. Straight Flushes can benefit under very specific cases when combined with Four Fingers; Straight can benefit under similar circumstances if these two Jokers are also combined with Splash, although this is a highly impractical combo and should be avoided.

title: Jolly Joker
text: Jolly Joker: Jokers: Sly Joker and The Duo pair well with this, as both will trigger on the same activation as this joker. Half Joker can be easily triggered along with this joker. Square Joker also becomes easier to use, as playing a pair doesn't require playing five cards. Spare Trousers pairs well with this joker, as triggering it will always trigger Jolly Joker. Jokers that discourage discarding, such as Banner, Delayed Gratification, or Green Joker, work well with this joker, as pairs are easier to achieve than most other hands. Similarly, Jokers that rely on having no discards between hands, such as Burglar or Mystic Summit also work well.

title: Jolly Joker
text: Jolly Joker: Similarly, Jokers that rely on having no discards between hands, such as Burglar or Mystic Summit also work well. Stuntman can also work well due to the hand size not mattering as much. Trivia: Jolly Joker can never trigger on a High Card, even with Splash. This joker is part of a series of Common Jokers which provide a Mult boost for playing a specific hand type. The others are Zany Joker for Three of a Kinds, Mad Joker for Two Pairs, Crazy Joker for Straights, and Droll Joker for Flushes. In demo versions of the game, Jolly Joker had a different color scheme, resembling Joker. The Steam Page for Balatro still shows this old art in some screenshots.

title: Juggler
text: Juggler: Juggler (Joker). Effect: +1 hand size. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Juggler is a Common Effect Joker that gives +1 Hand Size when equipped, allowing the player to hold one more card in their hand. This makes it easier to search for poker hands that require five cards, and is a counter to Boss Blinds that reduce hand size.

title: Juggler
text: Juggler: Usage notes: The Five-Card Draw challenge bans Juggler. Decks: Juggler synergizes with all decks, as +1 hand size is always useful. It is somewhat less useful on Painted Deck, however, due to the missing Joker Slot and that this deck already increases hand size. Poker hands: Any strong 5 card hands can benefit from Juggler, as the increased hand size means higher chance to draw needed cards to form the hand. Juggler can also be good in High-card builds which rely on cards being in hand to score, such as with Steel cards. Jokers: Baron: gives XMult for kings held in hand. Shoot the Moon: gives +13 Mult for each queen held in hand.

title: Juggler
text: Juggler: Shoot the Moon: gives +13 Mult for each queen held in hand. Mime: more cards held in hand means more cards for Mime to retrigger. Reserved Parking: has a 1 in 2 chance to give $1 for every face card held in hand. Troubadour: +2 hand size, coupled with Juggler, will provide a whooping 11 cards in hand. Merry Andy: Juggler can offset its -1 hand size penalty. Stuntman: Juggler can partially offset its -2 hand size penalty.

title: Juggler
text: Juggler: Merry Andy: Juggler can offset its -1 hand size penalty. Stuntman: Juggler can partially offset its -2 hand size penalty. Blinds: If Crimson Heart disables Juggler, the hand size will return to normal but current hand will stay intact until the next discard (ex: 9/8). By quitting to Main Menu and returning, the hand size actually permanently increases (ex: 9/9), giving players a permanent hand size upgrade. The Manacle gets countered by Juggler. Consumables: Juggler can offset the downside of using Ectoplasm once. Sigil and Ouija will transform more cards at once. Juggler also offsets Ouija's downside. Modifiers: The increased hand size can allow for more Gold cards, Steel cards, and Blue Seals to be utilized.

title: Juggler
text: Juggler: Modifiers: The increased hand size can allow for more Gold cards, Steel cards, and Blue Seals to be utilized. Jokers: Blackboard can be harder to trigger, as the increased hand size can make it harder to hold only Clubs and Spades in your hand. The increase hand size will make it hard for Raised Fist to give more score from high-ranked cards. Trivia: During the first demo, Juggler provided +2 hand size with no penalty, making it very powerful. It was nerfed to only provide +1 hand size upon release, and the +2 hand size is given to Troubadour with a -1 hand per round penalty as a caveat.

title: Juggler
text: Juggler: Juggler is one of the four jokers that is featured in the official physical playing card deck. The 3 others are Joker, Blueprint, and Gros Michel. Juggler has a very similar theme to Drunkard, both in effect and card design. Juggler is one of the two Jokers to appear on a regular-sized Buffoon Pack. The other Joker is Hack. In other media: Juggler appeared as a cameo in a crossover collaboration between Balatro and Rusty's Retirement.

title: Loyalty Card
text: Loyalty Card: Loyalty Card (Joker). Effect: X4 Mult every 6 hands played, 5 remaining. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Loyalty Card is an Uncommon Multiplicative Mult Joker that provides X4 Mult once every six hands. A countdown in its description begins at 5 and decreases with each hand played. Once five hands have been played, the card will begin to shake, signaling that the next played hand will receive the Mult bonus. After applying it, the countdown returns to 5.

title: Loyalty Card
text: Loyalty Card: Usage Notes: The text on the bottom of the Loyalty Card will change to "Active!" and the card will wiggle if the multiplier effect will be applied. If Loyalty Card is copied (for example, with Ankh), it keeps the same number of rounds played. When a disallowed hand is played during Boss Blinds that restrict hand type (like The Psychic) or when Loyalty Card is disabled (by Crimson Heart), Loyalty Card still counts down internally and will trigger every 6 hands, but there is no shaking animation nor does the visual counter in the description get reduced, which is a bug. Decks: Blue Deck works well with this Joker, as the +1 hand makes it easier to activate.

title: Loyalty Card
text: Loyalty Card: Decks: Blue Deck works well with this Joker, as the +1 hand makes it easier to activate. Poker hands: Any poker hand can benefit from Loyalty Card, but it tends to work best with large hands like Straight and Full House since they tend to struggle against more boss blinds than smaller hands, e.g. The Water, The House, The Fish and The Mouth, and their higher power compensates for Loyalty Card’s long downtime. Jokers: Burglar's +3 hands usually allow Loyalty Card to trigger every blind.

title: Loyalty Card
text: Loyalty Card: Jokers: Burglar's +3 hands usually allow Loyalty Card to trigger every blind. The Order, The Trio and Flower Pot provide XMult that can be triggered every round, and appreciate Loyalty Card's ability to blow through boss blinds like The Water and The House that make the hands necessary to trigger them harder to assemble. Bloodstone, Smiley Face, Hiker, and all other Jokers that trigger on playing cards appreciate Loyalty Card defeating boss blinds that debuff the required playing cards, like The Head, The Plant, and especially The Pillar.

title: Loyalty Card
text: Loyalty Card: Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong give you extra hands per round, helping you trigger this more often. With Nacho Tong (or Grabber + Blue Deck), Loyalty Card can trigger every blind if the player opts to use every hand for it, making it significantly stronger. Blinds and Antes: This Joker is easy to locate when playing against Amber Acorn, as it still shakes if it meets the condition, even when flipped face-down. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle all have anti-synergy with Loyalty Card due to their reduced number of hands. Jokers: Troubadour has anti-synergy with Loyalty Card, as the -1 hand each round makes it difficult to reach the 6 hands requirement to activate Loyalty Card.

title: Loyalty Card
text: Loyalty Card: Vouchers: Hieroglyph has anti-synergy with Loyalty Card, as the -1 hand each round makes it difficult to reach the 6 hands requirement to activate Loyalty Card. Strategies: The "critical hit" nature of Loyalty Card makes it suitable for dealing with Boss Blinds that punish multiple plays (The Needle, The Tooth, The Eye, or The Fish) and blinds with high score requirements (The Wall and Violet Vessel), as long as it triggers at the appropriate time. Therefore, with Loyalty Card, sometimes it is not better to play fewer hands in a round, but rather to adjust the hands played so that the Loyalty Card can be triggered when needed.

title: Loyalty Card
text: Loyalty Card: Trivia: Many delis and coffee shops provide frequent customers with loyalty cards like this, which may be punched, stamped, or otherwise marked every time the customer makes a purchase. This usually comes with a reward, and the completed card can be handed in for a free coffee, a discount, or some other reward. The Loyalty Card's associated business, Joker's Deli, appears on a shirt as part of the Playstack merchandise for Balatro. The product is labeled as Jimbo's Fish & Chips T-Shirt, which hints at Joker's Deli selling fries and types of seafood. The art of Loyalty Card has a little mistake, as the card's remaining punch holes amount to seven instead of the six relating to the card's effect.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: Luchador (Joker). Effect: Sell this card to disable the current Boss Blind. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: ✗ No. Luchador is an Uncommon Effect Joker. It is one of just three Jokers that has a consumable-like function - namely, when this Joker is carried into a Boss Blind, it can be sold at any time during that round to disable its condition. For example, selling it against The Psychic allows the player to score hands with fewer than 5 cards, and selling it against The Wall or Violet Vessel returns the score requirement to that of a standard Boss Blind. Note that Luchador needs to be sold during the Boss Blind to take effect.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: However, Luchador does not score you any points directly, and the Blind still has to be won by scoring the requirement. For this reason, it is generally more useful in the early game than the late game, as it can prevent untimely losses before you have time to sufficiently enhance the quality of your current build. While it theoretically can keep a build alive in a pinch in the late game, the scaling of later Antes (especially on Green Stake and higher) means playing down a scoring Joker can be extremely detrimental, and as such, Luchador offers little in this regard.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: When Luchador is debuffed, either by its own Perishable Sticker or the Crimson Heart Boss Blind, it can still be sold for the normal sell price, but will not disable the current Boss Blind. Usage Notes: Luchador will only take effect if sold after entering the Boss Blind. Luchador does not disable the current Boss Blind if it is debuffed. Selling Luchador against The Needle will give the player their hands back, but will not increase the score requirement. The Non-Perishable challenge bans Luchador.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: The Non-Perishable challenge bans Luchador. Decks: Black Deck: The +1 Joker slot makes carrying this Joker less taxing, as it can be played alongside 5 scoring Jokers. The much less forgiving economy of this Deck in the early game also gives many more opportunities for this card to keep a run alive, allowing for proper capitalization on the benefits of an extra Joker slot later on. Magic Deck: If the Judgement Tarot card is discovered early in the run, the two starting copies of The Fool can be used to duplicate them, therefore allowing for a quick replacement of this Joker once its effect is activated.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: Ghost Deck: This Deck has easier access to the Wraith Spectral card, which serves as a higher-risk but higher-reward version of the aforementioned Judgement. It can also use its starting Hex card to turn Luchador into scoring assistance, but this should only be done as a last resort. Poker hands: Luchador doesn't benefit any poker hands directly. However, certain hands can occasionally appreciate the assistance it provides (such as Flush against one of the suit-debuffing Boss Blinds, or, less frequently, a High Card/Pair/Three of a Kind build against The Psychic).

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: Jokers: Being a utility Joker, Luchador does not directly synergize with any build. However, it can enable a wealth of Jokers that are otherwise soft or hard countered by specific Boss Blinds, in the event they are encountered. Cartomancer: This card has the potential to create Judgement at the start of a Blind, allowing this Joker to be immediately replaced upon activating its ability. In the interim, it can also serve as a soft 'scoring' Joker by creating such cards as The Empress, The Hierophant, and Justice.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: Gift Card: An economy Joker that increases the sell value of all held cards, including itself, by $1 at the end of each round. Should these two be acquired simultaneously, it allows this Joker to serve both as a last-second run-saver and a potentially huge burst of money to keep it going in the next Shop.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: Blueprint and Brainstorm: Selling either of these Jokers while they are copying Luchador will also disable the current Boss Blind, giving you two 'charges' of the effect negation to use. Boss Blinds can only be disabled once per round, so be sure to hold onto this Joker for a potential second save. This should only be done in extreme desperation, such as a boss effect preventing a lethal score on the final hand of a round, as both of these have immeasurably more power when copying scoring Jokers.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: Campfire: By selling Luchador, not only is the Boss Blind's effect disabled, but it also gives this card an additional X0.25 Mult, thereby directly improving score and making it even easier to clear the requirement. Joker Stencil: Selling Luchador creates an empty Joker slot, therefore immediately provides an X2 Mult for Joker Stencil. Decks: Painted Deck: This Deck has innate anti-synergy due to the -1 Joker slot penalty, and is generally not worth considering anyway due to the +2 hand size bonus allowing for easier assembly of more potent hands. This also applies to Blast Off and Cruelty. Jokers: Matador cannot earn money from a disabled Boss Blind.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: This also applies to Blast Off and Cruelty. Jokers: Matador cannot earn money from a disabled Boss Blind. Chicot disables the effect of every Boss Blind while it is held. It is a direct upgrade over Luchador in most cases. Due to the role overlap, these two should not be used together. Boss Blinds: Amber Acorn flips and shuffles all Jokers, so the player doesn't know which of their Jokers is Luchador. Trying to pick a Joker to sell could likely result in selling the wrong card by mistake. If Crimson Heart debuffs this card, it can still be sold, but will not disable the Blind.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: If Crimson Heart debuffs this card, it can still be sold, but will not disable the Blind. Strategies: Luchador can be useful when the play style of a round is extremely fragile to certain Boss Blinds, for example: With a deck mostly consisting of a certain suit, or with Smeared Joker: The Club, The Goad, The Window, and The Head. With a deck mostly consisting of face cards, or with Pareidolia: The Plant, The Mark. With a high-leveled hand: The Flint. Relying on a certain hand type, or with Card Sharp: The Eye and The Arm. Relying on using discards to build hands: The Wheel, The Water, Cerulean Bell. Relying on combination of all held Jokers: Verdant Leaf, Crimson Heart.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: Relying on combination of all held Jokers: Verdant Leaf, Crimson Heart. Relying on good economy: The Ox and The Tooth. Relying on hands that are hard to play, or with Burglar: The Mouth and The Fish. Being relatively weak and relying on multiple hands to defeat blinds: The Needle, The Wall, and Violet Vessel. With a big hand size: The House.

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: With a big hand size: The House. In fact, for most runs, players are only vulnerable to 1-2 specific Boss Blinds and one Showdown Blind. In an Ante 8 run, excluding Ante 1 and 2 (at which point a specific gameplay style is unlikely to be formed), the probability of encountering both detrimental Boss Blinds, or a Boss Blind combined with a Showdown Blind is relatively low (both around 6%). Therefore, Luchador is sufficient to handle the risk. However, in endless mode, the player will face many Boss Blinds, so it would be better to have a method that can avoid multiple Boss Blinds (such as Chicot and Director's Cut).

title: Luchador
text: Luchador: Trivia: A Luchador is a Mexican wrestler. The joker image depicts a luchador wearing a typical wrestling mask and with a championship belt slung over his shoulder. When playing against Verdant Leaf and selling Luchador, Luchador will disable the Blind before Verdant Leaf can disable itself. This can be inferred from the ordering of getting the sell value and the Blind being disabled, and is confirmed by the source code. This is one of the few Jokers that has a consumable-like effect, in which disposing of it is necessary to reap its benefits. The others are Diet Cola and Invisible Joker.

title: Lucky Cat
text: Lucky Cat: Lucky Cat (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains X0.25 Mult every time a Lucky card successfully triggers, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Spawn Condition: Only obtainable if there is at least 1 Lucky card currently in the player's deck. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Lucky Cat is an Uncommon scaling Multiplicative Mult Joker that gains X0.25 Mult each time a Lucky card successfully triggers, and starts at X1 Mult. A card that triggers both the Money and Mult effects at the same time will only count as one activation for Lucky Cat.

title: Lucky Cat
text: Lucky Cat: This Joker will only appear once players have at least one Lucky card currently in their deck. Decks: Zodiac Deck starting with Overstock and Tarot Merchant improves the chances of finding The Magician in shop. Magic Deck starts with two copies of The Fool, increasing the player's initial amount of Lucky cards when finding The Magician. Poker hands: While Lucky Cat technically affects all hands evenly, five-card hands allow more Lucky cards to be played at once, increasing the potential for a successful trigger, such as: Straight Flush Full House Jokers: Oops! All 6s doubles the odds of Lucky cards' effects activating. Three copies will guarantee the Mult activation, and therefore, the Xmult for Lucky Cat.

title: Lucky Cat
text: Lucky Cat: Splash allows five Lucky cards to be scored in case they can't form a five-card poker hand. Driver's License may benefit with enough Lucky cards in the Deck to activate its conditional X3 Mult. Retrigger Jokers are very beneficial, as they increase the odds of a successful trigger, further scaling Lucky Cat. Hack and Sock and Buskin both retrigger cards of certain ranks. Seltzer retriggers all cards played for 10 hands. Dusk retriggers all cards played on the final hand. Hanging Chad retriggers the first card played twice, benefiting the player as long as the Lucky card is placed first. Seals: Red Seals double the opportunities for the Lucky card to trigger. Consumables: The Magician can make more Lucky cards.

title: Lucky Cat
text: Lucky Cat: Seals: Red Seals double the opportunities for the Lucky card to trigger. Consumables: The Magician can make more Lucky cards. Death can turn some cards into Lucky cards. The Hanged Man can remove non-Lucky cards. Deja Vu can apply Red Seals onto Lucky cards, increasing their chance to activate. Decks: Bram Poker makes Lucky Cat useless due to the Eternal Vampire this deck starts with. Jokers: Vampire is not recommended, as it removes the Lucky enhancement when scored, making Lucky Cat impossible to scale. Midas Mask converts all face cards into Gold cards, therefore overriding the previous Enhancement.

title: Lucky Cat
text: Lucky Cat: Midas Mask converts all face cards into Gold cards, therefore overriding the previous Enhancement. Vagabond may be risky to use, as just one $20 trigger will prevent it from creating more Tarot cards (unless the player has $-16 or less, which is pretty unlikely). Blinds: The Pillar debuffs previously played cards of the Ante, which may make some Lucky cards unusable. The Fish can potentially make it hard to play hands with Lucky cards if multiple hands are required to defeat the Boss Blind.

title: Lucky Cat
text: Lucky Cat: Trivia: Many Asian countries have superstitions about cats being lucky, specifically the Maneki-neko (or 'waving cat'), which is a figurine based on the calico Japanese Bobtail cat breed, which is believed to give good luck to the owner. This Joker is part of a series, along with Stone Joker, Steel Joker, Glass Joker, and Golden Ticket, where the Joker only appears once players have at least one card with the relevant enhancement currently in their deck.

title: Lusty Joker
text: Lusty Joker: Lusty Joker (Joker). Effect: Played cards with Heart suit give +3 Mult when scored. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Lusty Joker is a Common Joker that provides conditional Additive Mult to played hands. One of the four 'sinful' Jokers made to support specific Card Suits, it gives +3 Mult each time a Heart card is scored. If the played card is retriggered, either by a Joker effect or by its own Red Seal, Lusty Joker's effect will activate again.

title: Lusty Joker
text: Lusty Joker: Decks: Magic Deck's Fool Tarots can be used to mass-convert cards to have Heart suits. Ghost Deck can find a Sigil Spectral card in the shop, which may convert cards into Hearts. This Joker is easier to take with Checkered Deck, as the deck starts with 26 Heart playing cards. Poker hands: This Joker works best with Flush-type hands that only contain Hearts: Flush Straight Flush (and Royal Flush) Flush House Flush Five Other hands that score more cards are generally better to play with Lusty Joker, as they allow more Heart cards to be scored.

title: Lusty Joker
text: Lusty Joker: Jokers: As Lusty Joker's effect triggers when a Heart card is scored, retrigger Jokers, that allow cards to be scored multiple times, are very good to combo with Lusty. Flush Jokers, like Crafty Joker and Droll Joker, work well with Lusty Joker, as you want to be playing flushes to maximize Lusty's effect anyways. Bloodstone also triggers off of Heart cards scored, forming a natural synergy with Lusty Joker. As Bloodstone gives X Mult on a chance basis, Lusty Joker can be a natural addition to Oops! All 6s builds, which tend to use Lucky cards and other chance-based Joker effects, or other "X Mult from cards played" Jokers, like The Idol or, sometimes, Ancient Joker.

title: Lusty Joker
text: Lusty Joker: Because Lusty Joker's Mult is applied during the scoring of your played cards, Jokers that focus on creating Tarot cards are helpful to Lusty Joker's viability. They can both allow more Hearts to be created, and create certain Enhancements (particularly Glass and Steel) that work well with high hand-scoring Mult builds. Smeared Joker effectively turns all Diamond cards into Hearts for the purpose of Lusty Joker's effect. Blinds: When facing The Head, all Heart cards are debuffed, meaning Lusty Joker cannot activate. Trivia: Lust is one of the traditional seven deadly sins. The four basic Jokers that provide +3 Mult for each suit are each based on these. The other Sinful Jokers are Greedy Joker, Wrathful Joker and Gluttonous Joker.

title: Lusty Joker
text: Lusty Joker: Lust is considered a more shallow or primal version of love, and hence, is associated with Hearts. Lusty Joker's uncommon counterpart, Bloodstone, could be based on the phrase "bloodlust" and therefore be connected to Lusty Joker.

title: Mad Joker
text: Mad Joker: Mad Joker (Joker). Effect: +10 Mult if played hand contains a Two Pair. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Mad Joker is a Common Additive Mult Joker that provides +10 Mult when the played hand contains a Two Pair. This does not include hands like Four of a Kind, but it does include hands like Full House

title: Mad Joker
text: Mad Joker: Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World work well with this Joker thanks to their smaller deck, allowing you to find a Two Pair easier. Erratic Deck can work well with this Joker if it randomizes a lot of cards with the same rank. Poker hands: Any Poker Hand that contains a Two Pair will benefit from Mad Joker. These are: Two Pair Full House Flush House Flush - only if the flush contains a Two Pair Four of a Kind and similar hands do not trigger Mad Joker. Jokers: Spare Trousers gains Mult when playing a Two Pair.

title: Mad Joker
text: Mad Joker: Jokers: Spare Trousers gains Mult when playing a Two Pair. Square Joker gains Chips any time a played hand consists of exactly 4 cards. Since a standard Two Pair is exactly four cards, the player can strengthen Square Joker while getting Mult from Mad Joker. Sly Joker and Clever Joker give Chips on a Pair and Two Pair respectively. Jolly Joker gives Mult if the played hand contains a Pair. Trivia: This joker is part of a series which provide a Mult boost for a specific hand. The others are Jolly Joker, Zany Joker, Crazy Joker and Droll Joker.

title: Mad Joker
text: Mad Joker: In demo versions of the game, Mad Joker had different art to correspond with its ability involving a played Four of a Kind (see #Update History), resembling the standard Joker's colors if they had swapped around. The Steam page for Balatro still shows this old art in some screenshots.

title: Madness
text: Madness: Madness (Joker). Effect: When Small Blind or Big Blind is selected, gain X0.5 Mult and destroy a random Joker, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Madness is an Uncommon scaling Multiplicative Mult Joker. It starts at X1 Mult, and when a Small Blind or Big Blind is selected, it gains X0.5 Mult and destroys another Joker at random.

title: Madness
text: Madness: The gain of X0.5 Mult is not dependent on the destruction of another Joker, meaning that if no Joker is destroyed (whether because there are no other Jokers or because they are all Eternal), it will still gain X0.5 Mult. Madness cannot destroy itself, but can destroy other copies of Madness. If there are both Eternal and non-Eternal Jokers present, Madness will always destroy a non-Eternal Joker. Madness will not destroy any Joker upon selecting a Boss Blind, allowing players to buy a spare Joker to temporarily buff their scoring during said Boss Blind, then sell it right afterward.

title: Madness
text: Madness: Decks: Madness adds multiplicative Mult at a prodigious rate, but the player will need more than multiplicative Mult to win a run. For that reason, it's best to choose decks that can feasibly feed into Madness from an early point. Ghost Deck on some occasions, can be potent with Madness. If the player is playing on Black Stake or above and Madness is Eternal, the player can safely use the given Hex to give it Polychrome or even Ankh it to create multiple copies of Madness that cannot destroy each other, scaling the player's scoring power at an astounding rate.

title: Madness
text: Madness: On occasions where the player opts for a Madness-only Joker run, Painted Deck and Cruelty may feasibly work well, as their reduced Joker slots are rendered moot in most cases. Non-Perishable works well with Madness, as all Jokers are Eternal, and Madness cannot destroy them but is still able to scale. Typecast might work well with Madness, as after defeating Ante 4's boss, all Jokers will become Eternal, allowing Madness to scale freely without destroying other Jokers. Some Challenge Decks that start with Eternal Jokers, such as 15 Minute City, Bram Poker, Blast Off, etc., may work well with Madness.

title: Madness
text: Madness: Poker hands: Madness synergizes poorly with hands that have low native Mult and rely on Jokers for bonuses, but quite well with hands that have high native Mult: Flush Straight Full House Four of a Kind Straight Flush Jokers: Riff-Raff can reduce the likelihood that Madness will destroy an important Joker by providing a steady supply of weak Jokers, although it is possible for Madness to destroy Riff-Raff. Ensure Riff-Raff is placed to the left of Madness so it activates before Madness does. Modifiers: As Madness' destructive nature inhibits the player's ability to take other Jokers reliably, card Modifiers are vital to maximizing the scoring power of Madness. Eternal Jokers cannot be destroyed by Madness, completely negating the downside.

title: Madness
text: Madness: Eternal Jokers cannot be destroyed by Madness, completely negating the downside. Mult cards, Lucky cards, and Holographic cards work reasonably well, as they can provide additive Mult to feed into Madness. Steel cards, Glass cards, and Polychrome cards are stronger options, provided the player already has enough base Mult. Blue Seals provide the most consistent source of planet scaling. Gold cards and Gold Seals provide one of the only ways to gain more money without economy Jokers. Purple Seals provides a source of Tarot cards without Jokers. Vouchers: Hieroglyph and Petroglyph lower the Ante by 1, giving another Small Blind and Big Blind each to beat, and thus, two more opportunities to increase Madness' multiplier.

title: Madness
text: Madness: Telescope can provide consistent planet scaling. Stakes: On Black Stake difficulty and higher (and in some Challenges), Eternal Jokers synergize greatly with Madness, as Madness cannot destroy them. This means that any strategy that would normally have bad synergy with Madness can have its anti-synergy be completely avoided if the requisite Jokers are Eternal. Not only that, if Madness is Eternal, the player can safely duplicate it by using either Ankh to create multiple copies of Madness that cannot destroy each other, scaling the player's scoring power at an astounding rate. Decks: Anaglyph Deck has slight anti-synergy with this Joker, as it encourages the player to skip blinds, which remove an opportunity to scale Madness.

title: Madness
text: Madness: On Plasma Deck the player nearly always wants to take advantage of the easy early Antes by using a few chips Jokers and as many value generators as possible. However, taking Madness early makes it very difficult to do so, as well as preventing the player from pivoting their Chips to Mult if they took any Eternal Jokers. Jokers: Any Joker that cannot receive the Eternal sticker is inherently anti-synergistic with Madness, such as Gros Michel, as it has the potential to be destroyed before the player can get full value from the Joker.

title: Madness
text: Madness: Trivia: Madness is one of three "spooky" Jokers that came as a part of a pin set alongside Mr. Bones and Scary Face as a merch collab between LocalThunk and Makeship. In other media: Madness serves as inspiration to a cosmetic head piece (referred to in-game as the Unknown Madness) for The Unknown in Dead by Daylight.

title: Mail-In Rebate
text: Mail-In Rebate: Mail-In Rebate (Joker). Effect: Earn $5 for each discarded [rank], rank changes every round. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Economy. Activation: On Discard. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Mail-In Rebate is a Common Economy Joker that gives $5 for every card discarded of a certain rank. The rank changes every round, choosing from a random rank in the player's deck (this chooses more common ranks in the deck more often).

title: Mail-In Rebate
text: Mail-In Rebate: Usage Notes: If the deck has no card with any rank (i.e., full Stone cards), Mail-In Rebate will default to +$5 per discarded Ace. All copies of Mail-In Rebate (whether created using Invisible Joker or Ankh, or found using Showman) will always choose the same rank. Decks: Red Deck grants an extra discard, allowing more cards of the selected rank to be discarded. Painted Deck allows the player to have more cards in hand, letting the player discard more cards without sacrificing good hands.

title: Mail-In Rebate
text: Mail-In Rebate: Black Deck can more easily take Mail-In Rebate, as it has more Joker slots, and it is recommended to discard more with Black Deck anyway, as the player must play better hands to compensate for having fewer hands. Black Deck can also hold more Jokers that help with discarding, like Drunkard. Abandoned Deck and Mad World both contain fewer ranks and total cards, making it easier to find the selected rank and discard it. Golden Needle removes money when discarding, and Mail-In Rebate is an effective counter to this.

title: Mail-In Rebate
text: Mail-In Rebate: Golden Needle removes money when discarding, and Mail-In Rebate is an effective counter to this. Poker Hands: Hands that need fewer cards are better if the player has a smaller hand size, like Three of a Kind, which allows them to discard 5 cards if they have the default hand size. For this reason, Straight, Flush, and Full House are less valuable with Rebate. However, Five of a Kind and Flush Five are sometimes better in highly centralized decks, as with more of that rank, Mail-In Rebate will likely choose that rank, and discarding them will be fine, as the player is more likely to draw more to form a Five of a Kind still.

title: Mail-In Rebate
text: Mail-In Rebate: Jokers: Jokers that add more discards work great with Mail-In Rebate, those being Drunkard and Merry Andy. It is recommended to be cautious with Merry Andy, though, as the lowered hand size can sometimes result in the player discarding fewer cards by virtue of wanting to save a strong poker hand. Jokers that give an effect when discarding, like Castle, Faceless Joker, and Hit the Road, synergize well with Mail-In Rebate, as the player can use them to get even more value out of discards. Blueprint and Brainstorm can copy the money generation effect, then copy a different Joker's effect for scoring hands, effectively allowing the player to double Mail-In Rebate's effect for free.

title: Mail-In Rebate
text: Mail-In Rebate: Sixth Sense and DNA usually work well with Rebate, as the player will want to discard to find the card desired to play the first hand. DNA particularly works well, as by adding more cards of the same rank, the chance of Rebate selecting that rank is higher. Blinds: The Hook discards 2 random cards every hand played, potentially triggering Mail-In Rebate if discarded cards are chosen for this blind. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy give additional discards, allowing more chances to find the cards of selected rank and generate more money. Decks: Blast Off doesn't work well with Mail-In Rebate, as this deck only starts with 2 discards.

title: Mail-In Rebate
text: Mail-In Rebate: Decks: Blast Off doesn't work well with Mail-In Rebate, as this deck only starts with 2 discards. Jokers: Any Jokers that benefits from not using Discards, like Delayed Gratification or Banner, have anti-synergy with Mail-In Rebate. Burglar removes all discards, effectively disabling Mail-In Rebate. Blinds: The Water sets your discards to 0, making Mail-In Rebate useless for the round. Since debuffed cards do not have a rank, any blind that debuffs cards makes it less likely for the player to make use of Mail-In Rebate. Stakes: Blue Stake and above hinder Mail-In Rebate's potential because they have 1 less discard by default.

title: Mail-In Rebate
text: Mail-In Rebate: Stakes: Blue Stake and above hinder Mail-In Rebate's potential because they have 1 less discard by default. Strategy: Mail-In Rebate has an extremely high potential cash output. The player should try and maximize its potential by ensuring that all the cards in your deck are the same rank. This can be done through a variety of methods. Copying Mail-In Rebate with Blueprint or Brainstorm while discarding 5 cards gives a total of $50, and adding more copies just adds more money per discard. The player should be careful not to discard too much, as completely running out of cards is an instant loss.

title: Mail-In Rebate
text: Mail-In Rebate: The player should be careful not to discard too much, as completely running out of cards is an instant loss. Trivia: In real life, a "mail-in rebate" (MIR) is a special type of rebate usually done as a form of sales promotion. Typically, the customer buys a product at full price, and by mailing in a coupon or a receipt to the manufacturer, they receive a partial refund (or in some cases a full refund) on the product. This mirrors the Joker's ability in Balatro. By purchasing Mail-In Rebate and discarding certain cards, players can get a refund on their purchase. This Joker is addressed to Jerry Seinfeld's apartment from the show Seinfeld.

title: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker: Marble Joker (Joker). Effect: Adds one Stone card to the deck when Blind is selected. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: On Blind Select. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Marble Joker is an Uncommon Effect Joker that adds a Stone card to the deck at the beginning of each Blind.

title: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker: Unlike Certificate, cards given by Marble Joker will be added to the deck instead of directly to the hand, and they need to be drawn like other cards in deck to be played. Usage Notes: When playing against Verdant Leaf, the Stone card generated by Marble Joker will not be debuffed. The Fragile challenge bans Marble Joker. The Medusa challenge starts the player with an Eternal copy of Marble Joker. The Monolith challenge starts the player with an Eternal, Negative copy of Marble Joker. Decks: Plasma Deck can use the Stone cards created to great effect. Marble's Stone cards could win the entire run in combination with only a few other Chip Jokers and/or Planet cards.

title: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker: Abandoned Deck and Mad World have fewer cards than other decks, meaning the player will be able to draw a mixture of Stone and non-Stone cards more consistently. Red Deck allows you to find Stone cards easier, letting the player play more hands with as many Stone cards as possible. Blue Deck's extra hand allows the player to play more Stone card hands and scale hand-based mult-scaling Jokers. Black Deck's extra Joker slot makes it easier to take Marble, as there will be more Jokers to carry it as it starts to create Stone cards.

title: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker: Poker hands: High Card is the best hand to use with Stone cards, as you can end up playing five of them. Besides that, Pair and Three of a Kind still allow you to play a few Stone cards, and Two Pair and Four of a Kind allow you to play one. Straight, Flush, and Straight Flush can also be played with one stone card with Four Fingers. No other hand can be played with Stone cards. You will want to end up focusing on High Card, as it is the most reliable and plays the most Stone cards.

title: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker: Jokers: Marble Joker will only work with some way to scale Mult. This can be scaling based on hands played, like from Ride the Bus or Supernova, scaling from leveling up High Card, like from Burnt Joker or Space Joker, or even scaling from economy, like from Bootstraps or Flash Card, but it must exist in some form. There aren't many flat + Mult Jokers that will be able to beat the final Boss Blind. This doesn't need to be from a Joker necessarily, getting enough Pluto cards from Celestial Packs, blue seals, etc. can act as this scaling, but Joker scaling is easier to pull off generally.

title: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker: Stone Joker possesses a very strong combo with Marble Joker. The worst part about Marble is that after the fifth Stone card it adds, you have maxed out on the Chips from Stone cards you can play in a single hand, and every additional Stone just makes that hand easier to play (or lets you play it multiple times). Stone Joker adds consistent Chips scaling that will give Marble Joker value after it would begin to lose it. It can also serve as a late replacement for Marble, giving it value postmortem. Driver's License will become active very quickly with Marble Joker adding an enhanced card every Blind.

title: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker: Driver's License will become active very quickly with Marble Joker adding an enhanced card every Blind.
