Hologram is an extremely strong combo, as it will gain X0.25 Mult every Blind from the Stone card added. It can very rapidly reach a huge XMult, which can affect whichever +Mult scaler you have to a large extent. Vampire can use Marble as an enhancement generator to scale easier. Builds using Vampire often don't care about the cards in its deck besides enhancements, either, meaning the added cards don't massively hinder it, only making it slightly harder to find other enhanced cards (which is, again, not too bad since you get one automatically every Blind).

title: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker: Blueprint and Brainstorm can copy Marble Joker at the start of the blind, allowing players to create more Stone cards and can be helpful to scale Jokers like Stone Joker or Hologram. Blue Joker can be useful due to the fact that every blind adds an extra card. Blue Jokers is better if Marble Joker is paired with Blueprint or Brainstorm because then it adds 2 card to the deck every blind. Poker hands: If Marble Joker is held for a long time or is Eternal, higher value poker hands like Straight and Four of a Kind that rely on finding specific cards are much harder to find with many Stone cards in the deck.

title: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker: Jokers: Erosion relies on a small deck size, which is more difficult to get when 1 card is added per round from Marble Joker. Since the Stone cards given by Marble Joker always score no matter what, Splash becomes unnecessary.

title: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker: Since the Stone cards given by Marble Joker always score no matter what, Splash becomes unnecessary. Strategies: Generally, Marble Joker isn't a strong Joker. Stone cards only really work with High Card and Pair builds, and you need a large amount of them in your deck to consistently draw and play them. Marble Joker ends up in an awkward state early where it takes up a Joker slot that could be used for another Chips provider like Stuntman or Castle that can work better with High Card builds. However, the Stone cards it adds can end up supplanting a Chips Joker entirely, meaning you can sell Marble after getting value from it and go into the final Boss Blind with an extra Mult or effect Joker you'd be missing otherwise. With that said, Marble joker can be great when it's fueling some specific other jokers.

title: Marble Joker
text: Marble Joker: Trivia: Like many real-life marble statues, the art of Marble Joker is partially missing. If the Stone enhancement is removed or replaced, it can be seen that the card created by Marble Joker has a random rank and suit. This doesn't impact the type of a played hand if Vampire removes it.

title: Matador
text: Matador: Matador (Joker). Effect: Earn $8 if played hand triggers the Boss Blind ability. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Defeat a Boss Blind in 1 hand without using any discards. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Economy. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Matador is an Uncommon Economy Joker that provides a cash boost whenever you play a hand that triggers a Boss Blind's ability (such as attempting to score debuffed cards). This effect doesn't work with all Boss Blinds due to an oversight, though, and can occasionally give results inconsistent with what one might expect. As a general rule, any hand that contains a debuffed card, or will not score, will trigger Matador.

title: Matador
text: Matador: Blinds that can trigger Matador: Suit-debuffing Blinds: The Window (Diamonds) The Head (Hearts) The Club (Clubs) The Goad (Spades) The Plant (debuffed face cards) The Pillar (debuffed previously-played cards) The Flint (halved base chips and mult) The Eye, The Mouth, or The Psychic, if hand is a non-scoring hand (repeat hand type, non-repeat hand type, less than 5 cards) The Arm, if played hand's level could be decreased (when it is level 2 or higher) The Ox, if hand sets money to zero (the Ox sets the money to zero, then triggers Matador's effect, allowing you to keep the money earned, provided you don't trigger it again) Verdant Leaf, if no Joker has been sold yet

title: Matador
text: Matador: Verdant Leaf, if no Joker has been sold yet No other blinds can trigger Matador's effect. Usage Notes: Matador only triggers if the debuffed card is played and "scored". This means e.g. a High Card with one non-debuffed scoring card and some debuffed cards that do not "score" will not trigger Matador. Synergies: Matador gains the most value out of being used during applicable Boss Blinds the most amount of times. This generally means you want more hands, and Blind reroll abilities if the boss won't trigger Matador. Decks: Blue Deck allows you to play more hands, allowing Matador to trigger more often.

title: Matador
text: Matador: Decks: Blue Deck allows you to play more hands, allowing Matador to trigger more often. Anaglyph Deck appreciates a way to make money that isn't hindered by needing to play Blinds instead of skipping them. Double or Nothing will trigger Matador when attempting to score debuffed cards, even during Small and Big Blinds. Jokers: Burglar is the best Joker to combine Matador with, as with ideal draws you can obtain an additional $24 from each Boss Blind. To the Moon can benefit from the mid-round money earning, as this money will count toward interest. Jokers such as Bull or Bootstraps that directly scale off of money enjoy the extra cash that Matador brings in.

title: Matador
text: Matador: Jokers such as Bull or Bootstraps that directly scale off of money enjoy the extra cash that Matador brings in. Jokers such as Flash Card or Red Card that scale off of actions that require money to be spent can also benefit from the extra spendable cash. Mr. Bones makes Matador less punishing. Using Pareidolia during The Plant will debuff every single card, which means playing any hand will always trigger Matador. Similarly, using Smeared Joker during any of the four suit-debuffing Boss Blinds will double the amount of cards debuffed, doubling the chances for Matador to trigger.

title: Matador
text: Matador: Vouchers: As with many mid-round economy Jokers, Seed Money and Money Tree are very helpful, as they allow more interest to be gained off of that money. Director's Cut and Retcon are useful vouchers to reroll into a Boss Blind that triggers Matador, however, spending too much money on rerolling will negate the benefits given by Matador. Grabber and Nacho Tong both allow you to play more hands, allowing for more Matador triggers Other Synergies: Wild cards are debuffed by all four suit-debuffing Boss Blinds, causing them to always trigger Matador when scored in a hand.

title: Matador
text: Matador: Deck: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle don't allow the player many chances for Matador to trigger due to their reduced number of hands. Checkered Deck starts with 0 Clubs and 0 Diamonds in the deck, which makes it significantly harder for the player to earn money when playing against The Club or The Window. Abandoned Deck and Medusa start with no face cards, meaning the player will struggle to make use of Matador if the upcoming Blind is The Plant. Jokers: Boss-Blind-disabling Jokers like Luchador and Chicot should generally be treated as mutually exclusive with Matador, as their abilities to disable Boss Blinds' abilities leave Matador useless.

title: Matador
text: Matador: Boss Blinds: Blinds which cannot trigger Matador (The Wheel, The House, The Fish, The Water, The Wall, The Manacle, The Serpent, The Needle, The Tooth, The Mark, The Hook, Amber Acorn, Violet Vessel, Crimson Heart, Cerulean Bell) are obviously no good for it; Matador should usually not be purchased if one of these Blinds is the upcoming boss. Inversely, if Matador is already possessed, an Ante with these blinds is usually a good time to sell out of it.

title: Matador
text: Matador: Trivia: Matadors, or bullfighters, are the main performers with the bull in bullfighting. The lead matador is dressed in gold, like on the Joker card, with other matadors dressed in silver. Matadors often wave a red cloth to attract or anger the bull, which is represented in the card's background by the folds of the cloth. Similarly, this Joker rewards the player for provoking the Boss Blind's ability. In an interview with Bloomberg, Localthunk has confirmed that he will overhaul "the confusing Matador Joker" in the upcoming gameplay update. Internally, The Hook, The Tooth, and Crimson Heart actually do set the Blind.triggered flag Matador looks for, but with the wrong timing, so Matador will fail to trigger in response.

title: Merry Andy
text: Merry Andy: Merry Andy (Joker). Effect: +3 discards each round,, -1 hand size. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Win a run in 12 or fewer rounds. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Merry Andy is an Uncommon Effect Joker that provides +3 discards at the cost of -1 Hand Size.

title: Merry Andy
text: Merry Andy: To unlock this Joker, the player must reach Ante 8 in 12 rounds or less. This Joker shares an unlock requirement with the Speedrunner achievement. Usage Notes: If you generate Merry Andy through a Judgement, you will get the extra discards for the current hand without cards being discarded from your hand but will drop your hand size when you next draw.

title: Merry Andy
text: Merry Andy: Decks: Merry Andy is a good Joker early game for the economy of the Green Deck, since it gains no interest and instead earns money only based on discards and hands remaining, extra discards are pretty valuable. Merry Andy can also be useful early game for the Painted Deck, as its hand size penalty is completely negated by the Painted Deck's bonus hand size. Poker Hands: Straights usually require more discards to set up. If the player needs to draw a specific enhanced card to win, Merry Andy enables the player to sift through up to 15 more cards every round. Although, the reduced Hand Size makes it harder to hold multiple Steel cards and Gold cards at once.

title: Merry Andy
text: Merry Andy: Although, the reduced Hand Size makes it harder to hold multiple Steel cards and Gold cards at once. Jokers: Juggler helps with negating this Joker's downside. Banner can combo with Merry Andy to provide additional chips early game. Castle and Yorick can scale much faster since Merry Andy allows you to discard 15 more cards per blind. It also works well with Delayed Gratification for economy, increasing the payout by an extra $6. However, the smaller hand size will make it harder to play certain hands. Blackboard benefits from reduced hand size, making it easier to hold only Spades or Clubs for its Mult bonus. Raised Fist becomes easier to use with high-ranked cards.

title: Merry Andy
text: Merry Andy: Raised Fist becomes easier to use with high-ranked cards. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette can mitigate Merry Andy's -1 hand size penalty. Blinds: If Crimson Heart disables Merry Andy, the hand size will return to normal, but the current Hand will stay intact until the next discard (e.g., 8/7). By quitting to the main menu and returning, the hand size will actually permanently increase (e.g., 8/8), giving players a permanent hand size upgrade. Modifiers: Purple Seal: The extra discards provides more opportunities to generate more Tarot cards. Stake: On Blue Stake and higher, Merry Andy can mitigate the -1 discard penalty. Decks: Five-Card Draw's reduced hand size may make it impossible to play certain poker hands.

title: Merry Andy
text: Merry Andy: Decks: Five-Card Draw's reduced hand size may make it impossible to play certain poker hands. Jokers: Jokers with held in hand abilities vary with Merry Andy's effectiveness. Baron, Shoot the Moon, and Reserved Parking are all weakened due to holding fewer face cards in hand. Inversely, Raised Fist actually benefits, as the player is less likely to hold a card with a low rank at any moment. Burglar always removes all discards, effectively making Merry Andy -1 Hand Size with no upside. Stuntman adds an additional -2 hand size, making it difficult to feasibly form 5-card poker hands. Green Joker and Ramen discourage discarding due to weakening with each used discard.

title: Merry Andy
text: Merry Andy: Green Joker and Ramen discourage discarding due to weakening with each used discard. Consumables: Ectoplasm should not be used more than once with Merry Andy, as its permanent hand size reduction can make even hands like Pair harder to assemble. Sigil and Ouija will transform fewer cards at once. Not only that, but Ouija also reduces hand size even further, making it significantly more punishing to use. The Devil, The Chariot and Trance become weaker, for reasons stated below. Modifiers: The decreased hand size doesn't allow many Gold cards, Steel cards, and Blue Seals to be utilized. Blinds: The Water will always set discards to 0.

title: Merry Andy
text: Merry Andy: Blinds: The Water will always set discards to 0. Strategy: As skipping is usually a high-risk strategy, it can be tricky to win a run in 12 or fewer rounds, meaning the player must skip at least 12 Blinds, averaging at 1.5 Blinds per Ante skipped. A basic Deck, such as Red Deck or Blue Deck, is likely the best, as an additional discard/hand makes it more feasible to play more risky as is the case with skipping. Plasma Deck can skip more in the early game due to its balancing ability, making the need to obtain Jokers early less of a priority.

title: Merry Andy
text: Merry Andy: Anaglyph Deck earns the player a Double Tag upon defeating a Boss Blind, making skipping slightly more viable. Tags in general to look out for are Investment Tag and Speed Tag, as earning Economy is critical since the player sees fewer Shops and Blind payouts overall. Throwback will have scaled to a minimum of X4 Mult by the end of the run, making it a very consistent source of scaling multiplicative mult. The Uncommon Tag may be a quick way to obtain Throwback early, on top of retroactively scaling it. Trivia: A "merry andrew" is a term for a jester who entertains by supplying a steady stream of jokes, much like how Merry Andy supplies a steady stream of discards.

title: Midas Mask
text: Midas Mask: Midas Mask (Joker). Effect: All played face cards become Gold cards when scored. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: On Played. Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Midas Mask is an Uncommon Effect Joker that enhances scoring face cards into Gold cards. It will overwrite other Enhancements.

title: Midas Mask
text: Midas Mask: Usage Notes: The Fragile challenge bans Midas Mask. Decks: Mad World starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which makes it so that all cards are upgraded to Gold cards when scored. Poker hands: Any five-card hand with five face cards will benefit Midas Mask the most. This includes Flush, Full House, Five of a Kind, Flush House, and Flush Five. Since it is slightly more difficult to make a Straight or Straight Flush with face cards than other cards, Midas Mask is slightly less useful if you have invested in those hands. Late game, playing small hands like High Card means you can keep more Gold cards in hand. Jokers: Mime means the Gold cards make twice as much money.

title: Midas Mask
text: Midas Mask: Jokers: Mime means the Gold cards make twice as much money. Midas Mask naturally synergizes with Smiley Face, Scary Face, and Business Card when playing the face cards. However, you're not going to want to play your golden face cards later in the game. It has an extremely strong synergy with Pareidolia, which makes it so that all cards are upgraded to Gold cards when scored. Beware of using Stone cards with this strategy, as they will also be turned into regular Gold cards, which may ruin a run based on Stone cards. Golden Ticket makes Gold cards give +$4 when played.

title: Midas Mask
text: Midas Mask: Golden Ticket makes Gold cards give +$4 when played. Vampire removes card enhancements in exchange for X0.1 Mult per enhancement removed, making it a potent combination with Midas Mask as it creates a steady stream of XMult scaling.

title: Midas Mask
text: Midas Mask: Where Midas Mask is placed relative to the Vampire can affect this. Assuming a five-card hand of only face cards is played, when placed to the left of Vampire, it guarantees that Vampire will gain X0.5 Mult, as it will apply the Gold card effect, then Vampire's enhancement removal effect. However, when Midas Mask is placed to the right, Vampire's enhancement removal applies before Midas Mask, guaranteeing that all face cards are Gold cards when reshuffled into the deck. This can be helpful to prepare additional face cards for future Vampire scaling.

title: Midas Mask
text: Midas Mask: Midas Mask is inherently anti-synergistic with Ride the Bus and Reserved Parking, however, if the player is able to convert most of the face cards in the deck with Midas Mask before acquiring these Jokers, then they may be able to benefit substantially. Finally, Driver's License becomes a nearly free X3 Mult when all face cards are gold. Blinds: The Pillar does not consider the cards turned gold to be "previously played", allowing the player to use them as normal against this Boss. Decks: This Joker is close to useless on the Abandoned Deck and Medusa since it has no face cards. Blinds: The Plant debuffs all face cards, preventing Midas Mask from making any gold cards for the round.

title: Midas Mask
text: Midas Mask: Blinds: The Plant debuffs all face cards, preventing Midas Mask from making any gold cards for the round. Trivia: Midas Mask's name and ability are a reference to King Midas, a king of Greek myth who was cursed to turn anything he touched to gold (often referred to as the "Midas touch"). The effect of turning only face cards gold reflects how it's a mask.

title: Mime
text: Mime: Mime (Joker). Effect: Retrigger all card held in hand abilities. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Retrigger. Activation: On Held. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Mime is an Uncommon Retrigger Joker that can retrigger all held in hand effects (cards that are not played but remain in hand).

title: Mime
text: Mime: Mime can retrigger Gold and Steel cards, as well as Blue Seals. Mime will also retrigger other Jokers that activate from held in hand cards, such as Baron. It is important to note that Mime will not reactivate a Red Seal a second time. For example, a Red Seal Gold card, will only activate three times with Mime, giving a total of $9 after the round ends. Decks: The Painted Deck gives an additional +2 to the player's hand size, allowing Mime to activate more cards. The Ghost Deck allows for Spectral cards to be readily available in the Shop, making Seals more attainable.

title: Mime
text: Mime: The Ghost Deck allows for Spectral cards to be readily available in the Shop, making Seals more attainable. Poker hands: High Card is arguably the best hand with Mime, since it requires the least amount of cards to play. This allows for more cards to be held in hand. Pair and Three of a Kind can be used for the same reasons, although slightly less effectively. Jokers: Held in hand Jokers synergize the best with Mime, since it enables them to be activated twice. These include: Reserved Parking will generally give $0.25 more on average. This can change depending on retriggers and held in hand effects, see the Reserved Parking page for an explanation on the specific interactions and numbers.

title: Mime
text: Mime: Raised Fist and Shoot the Moon: Provides double their + Mult to the score. Baron: Potentially the strongest duo with Mime by giving an additional X1.5 Mult for each retrigger. This, paired with the Plasma Deck, can also allow the player to possibly reach the elusive Naneinf score. Steel Joker: Steel cards are exceptionally strong with Mime, and attaining more Steel cards will also scale this Joker. Constellation: Blue Seals are retriggered by Mime, creating more planets and scaling this Joker faster. Tarot generating Jokers (ex. 8 Ball, Cartomancer, etc.) can help maximize the effectiveness of Mime by providing the necessary means to manipulate the deck and modify cards.

title: Mime
text: Mime: Vagabond can benefit the most from Mime, since it can activate Gold cards a second time after the round ends, allowing the for player to still maintain their economy without hampering Vagabond's trigger condition. Having a larger hand size allows for more cards to be held in hand. Jokers like Turtle Bean, Juggler and Troubadour can be beneficial to have. Blueprint/ Brainstorm: If Blueprint or Brainstorm is copying a different joker when a hand is played, and then moved to copy Mime as the hand is being scored, the Blueprint/Brainstorm will copy Mime when it retriggers Blue Seals/Gold cards.

title: Mime
text: Mime: Hanging Chad can help retrigger modified played cards, making them more effective, especially so since smaller hands are generally used with Mime. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette each increase your hand size by +1, allowing for more cards to be held in hand. Playing cards: Mime works extraordinarily well with Gold cards, Steel cards and cards with Blue Seal as it is able to retrigger their effects. Decks: Medusa can be difficult to use with Mime due to the Eternal Marble Joker adding more Stone cards to the deck, making finding cards that Mime works with more difficult.

title: Mime
text: Mime: Five-Card Draw does not work well with this Joker due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers, though it can still be used with Raised Fist. Jokers: Mime suffers from Jokers that reduce hand size, such as Stuntman and Merry Andy, due to them lowering the number of cards with "Held in Hand" abilities able to be active at once. Notably, Mime does not affect Blackboard despite its ability having the "held in hand" description. Golden Ticket encourages the player to play Gold cards instead of keeping them in hand, making Mime weaker. 8 Ball may fill up the player's consumable slots with Tarot cards, preventing the player from receiving Planet cards from blue seals.

title: Mime
text: Mime: Blinds: The Hook activates before Mime does, and can remove desirable cards from a player's hand during scoring. Trivia: The word "Mime" comes from the Greek word "mimos" (μῖμος) which means "imitator" or "actor", as well as the Greek adjective "mimikos" (μιμικός) which roughly translates to "of or pertaining to imitation/mimicry". This is well reflected in the Mime's ability to imitate the effects of some card modifiers. Although mimes originated in Ancient Greece and Rome, Mime's design is based on the modern French mime, likely because that depiction is more universally recognized. This is reflected in the card's artwork, which features stereotypical French elements such as a beret and a red scarf.

title: Misprint
text: Misprint: Misprint (Joker). Effect: +0-23 Mult. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Misprint is a Common Additive Mult Joker. It provides a random amount of Mult ranging from +0 to +23 Mult (inclusive) to all played hands, and the Mult is randomized for every hand. Misprint's description is constantly changing and glitching to represent this.

title: Misprint
text: Misprint: Decks: Blue Deck: +1 hand per round means one more opportunity for Misprint to save the run with a high roll. Poker hands: This Joker provides unconditional +Mult, so it works for all played hands. Hands with low Mult at base and low Mult from levelling, such as High Card, Pair, and Two Pair, benefit from +Mult sources more than faster scaling hands such as Straight and Four of a Kind. Jokers: Multiple Misprints, or Misprint copied with Blueprint/ Brainstorm: The Mult given by these jokers will be generated independently, which reduces the randomness of the total Mult.

title: Misprint
text: Misprint: Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong each give +1 hand per round, which means one more opportunity for Misprint to save the run with a high roll. This is especially valuable earlier on. Decks: Painted Deck: This Deck should avoid Misprint outside of absolute emergencies; consistency is the key to making the most out of a Joker roster that is one slot short. Golden Needle makes it very risky to use Misprint because this deck only has 1 hand, which mean scoring too little at any point will lead to game over.

title: Misprint
text: Misprint: Strategy: The average Mult added by Misprint is +11.5 Mult, which is statistically better on paper than other Common +Mult Jokers (Joker, Jolly Joker, Mad Joker, and Droll Joker to name a few). This and the unconditionality of Misprint make it very suitable for the early stage of a run, when the player lacks powerful Jokers and specific gameplay style—for example, it is possible for Misprint to give +23 Mult, which is roughly equivalent to X6.75 Mult even for the high hands (Straight, Flush, or Full House), if the player does not have any other Mult Jokers or hand upgrades.

title: Misprint
text: Misprint: However, due to randomness of Misprint, it is hard to rely on it for scoring. In later stages of a run, Misprint is very replaceable in favor of Specialized Additive Mult Jokers, such as Fibonacci or Onyx Agate, or ones capable of very fast scaling, such as Red Card or Spare Trousers, based on the play style of this run. Also, in a 'sink or swim' scenario where the player needs a consistent source of scoring, a Joker that provides less +Mult on average but has a lower capacity to low roll may be favorable.

title: Misprint
text: Misprint: Both low rolls and high rolls from Misprint can be harmful; a low roll can lead to you not scoring enough to beat a blind, and while a high roll may enable you to beat a blind with fewer hands, it can also hinder scaling hand-based Jokers like Green Joker and Square Joker as a result. Trivia: This Joker is a reference to playing cards (or any other printed object) that have been printed incorrectly or misaligned during manufacture, resulting in the art being off-centered. The assorted blocks between the two Joker labels represent colored test bars used to perform calibration or quality assurance on printed media.

title: Misprint
text: Misprint: During early playtest versions of the game, Misprint could give negative mult down to -3 Mult, resulting in players directly losing score, which was later changed to give ≥ 0 Mult. The glitchy description of Misprint consists of two parts: the first half contains random mult values (+0-23), independent of the Mult that Misprint will actually give, and the second half switches between the following: The usual "Mult". "rand()", the random function in C++. According to LocalThunk, this is an homage to his past game development in C++.

title: Misprint
text: Misprint: "rand()", the random function in C++. According to LocalThunk, this is an homage to his past game development in C++. A special text revealing the next card to be drawn: "#@[2-14][C/D/H/S]". The number corresponds to the rank of the card to be drawn (2-10 for numbered cards, 11 for Jack, 12 for Queen, 13 for King, and 14 for Ace), and the letter corresponds to the suit of the card (Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, Spades). During a run, even if Misprint is not held, it can still be seen in the collection in the option panel, as long as Misprint has been discovered for the first time. However, when outside a run, in the collection of main menu, Misprint does not display cards drawn in a new or continued run, but rather always displays "#@11D" (Jack of Diamonds) as the default.

title: Misprint
text: Misprint: In other media: Misprint cameoed in a collaboration between Balatro and Rusty's Retirement.

title: Mr. Bones
text: Mr. Bones: Mr. Bones (Joker). Effect: Prevents Death if chips scored are at least 25% of required chips, self destructs. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Lose 5 runs. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: ✗ No. Mr. Bones is a unique Uncommon Effect Joker. While this Joker is equipped, the player can survive a blind without scoring the required amount of chips, provided they manage to score at least 25% of the target amount. Upon playing all of their hands, Mr. Bones will perish and consider the blind as won, with the result screen saying "Saved by Mr. Bones". However, the player will not receive any reward money for clearing the blind, but they will still gain interest.

title: Mr. Bones
text: Mr. Bones: Mr. Bones will not save the player when they run out of cards, even if the player has reached 25% of the chips requirement for the blind. Usage Notes: Anaglyph Deck still grants a Double Tag when the player is saved by Mr. Bones. The Investment Tag still rewards $25 when the player is saved by Mr. Bones. The Non-Perishable challenge bans Mr. Bones. Decks: Black Deck gives 1 extra Joker slot in exchange for 1 fewer hand, which can be used by Mr. Bones, as 1 less hand makes it harder to get to the required score. Poker hands: This Joker does not affect any poker hand but may be slightly more useful for certain builds.

title: Mr. Bones
text: Mr. Bones: Poker hands: This Joker does not affect any poker hand but may be slightly more useful for certain builds. Jokers: Showman can let the player pick up multiple Mr. Bones, which they would likely need the effects of due to missing 3 scoring Jokers by that point. Blueprint and Brainstorm can't copy this Joker, so don't try to get multiple extra lives out of it. Matador becomes less punishing with Mr. Bones. This can be useful for the player to get a lot of money with little to no consequences.

title: Mr. Bones
text: Mr. Bones: Boss Blinds: Being saved by Mr. Bones will still award the player a win on Ante 8, effectively making this joker divide the final round's chip requirement by 4. Note that being saved by this Joker will not allow it to gain a stake sticker. Boss Blinds: If Mr. Bones gets debuffed on the final hand of Crimson Heart, it will not save the player. Strategies: Mr. Bones can be useful when the play style of a round is extremely fragile to certain Boss Blinds, for example: With a deck mostly consisting of a certain suit, or with Smeared Joker: The Club, The Goad, The Window, and The Head.

title: Mr. Bones
text: Mr. Bones: With a deck mostly consisting of face cards, or with Pareidolia: The Plant, The Mark. With a high-leveled hand: The Flint. Relying on a certain hand type, or with Card Sharp: The Eye and The Arm. Relying on using discards to build hands: The Wheel, The Water, Cerulean Bell. Relying on combination of all held Jokers: Verdant Leaf, Crimson Heart. Relying on good economy: The Ox and The Tooth. Relying on hands that are hard to play, or with Burglar: The Mouth and The Fish. Being relatively weak and relying on multiple hands to defeat blinds: The Needle, The Wall, and Violet Vessel. With a big hand size: The House.

title: Mr. Bones
text: Mr. Bones: With a big hand size: The House. In fact, for most runs, players are only vulnerable to 1-2 specific Boss Blinds and one Showdown Blind. In an Ante 8 run, excluding Ante 1 and 2 (at which point a specific gameplay style is unlikely to be formed), the probability of encountering both detrimental Boss Blinds, or a Boss Blind combined with a Showdown Blind is relatively low (both around 6%). Therefore, Mr. Bones is sufficient to handle the risk. However, compared with other methods that can avoid specific Boss Blind (e.g. Luchador and Director's Cut), Mr. Bones still needs at least 25% of the score, so it cannot handle specific situations, such as encountering The Psychic with a hand size below 5. And in endless mode, the player will face many Boss Blinds, so it would be better to have a method that can avoid multiple Boss Blinds (such as Chicot).

title: Mr. Bones
text: Mr. Bones: When dealing with Crimson Heart, a possible strategy is to sell all Jokers except for the one being debuffed and Mr. Bones when there are two hands left. As Crimson Heart will not select a Joker consecutively, this ensures that Mr. Bones will not be debuffed during the last hand. Trivia: The name "Mr. Bones" is based on the meme "Mr. Bones' Wild Ride", which was a car ride made in RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 that was 30,696 feet long and took 4 in-game years to ride to completion, with the riders exclaiming "I want to get off Mr. Bones' Wild Ride".

title: Mr. Bones
text: Mr. Bones: Mr. Bones can bail the player out of any round before Ante 39. This is because at ante 39 the required score is "NaN" (Not a Number) and the game will not recognize any number as at least 25% of the requirement.

title: Mr. Bones
text: Mr. Bones: Normally, Mr. Bones cannot save the player if they run out of cards in their deck. However, if the player has two Mr. Bones, running out of cards puts the game in a glitched state where it ends the round every frame, with very strange results. Alternately, instead of a second Mr. Bones, this glitched state can be achieved by selling Luchador against The Wall or Violet Vessel immediately after playing a losing hand to reduce the blind requirement below the achieved score. Using this glitch, it is possible to progress past ante 39. If done on a boss round, it ups the ante constantly.

title: Mr. Bones
text: Mr. Bones: Mr. Bones is one of three "spooky" Jokers that came as a part of a pin set alongside Madness and Scary Face as a merch collab between LocalThunk and Makeship. As a part of the Ghost Deck Playing Cards set by Fangamer, Mr. Bones is one of the four Jokers to be featured next to Séance, Sixth Sense, and Castle. In other media: Mr. Bones makes an appearance as an enemy in Vampire Survivors.

title: Mystic Summit
text: Mystic Summit: Mystic Summit (Joker). Effect: +15 Mult when 0 discards remaining. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Mystic Summit is a Common additive Mult Joker that gives +15 Mult when the player has 0 discards remaining, either by using them all or through other means (such as Jokers like Burglar).

title: Mystic Summit
text: Mystic Summit: In general, Mystic Summit can be useful in the early game during Ante 1 or 2, but its inability to scale makes it less useful in later Antes, and it will likely be replaced as other better Jokers are found. Jokers: Burglar is a good combination with Mystic Summit, as it trades all discards for +3 hands. This allows Mystic Summit to be in effect as soon as the round starts. If the player is able to find Yorick, Mystic Summit is a great choice as both incentivize using all of the player's discards. In addition, Mystic Summit provides + Mult to be boosted by Yorick's XMult.

title: Mystic Summit
text: Mystic Summit: Decks: Mystic Summit has anti-synergy with the Green Deck, since one of the ways to get money with the Green Deck is to retain discards, and Mystic Summit is only effective when all discards are gone. Golden Needle removes $1 for every discard used, which means Mystic Summit costs $6 to activate during this challenge. Five-Card Draw has a hand size of 5, which might force the player to discard a wanted card to activate Mystic Summit. Jokers: Green Joker and Ramen are likely a bad choice, due to having to spend discards for Mystic Summit. This can be mitigated with Burglar but as this combo requires three Jokers it may be best to ignore it.

title: Mystic Summit
text: Mystic Summit: Any Joker that benefits from retaining discards, such as Banner or Delayed Gratification are not a good combination with Mystic Summit. Trivia: According to LocalThunk, Mystic Summit requires the player to use all discards and play what they have, because it is similar to how there's nowhere left to go on top of a summit.

title: Obelisk
text: Obelisk: Obelisk (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains X0.2 Mult per consecutive hand played without playing your most played poker hand, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Obelisk is a Rare scaling Multiplicative Mult Joker that provides an additional X0.2 Mult each time a hand that is not one of the player's most-played hands is played. This Joker starts at X1 Mult and will reset to X1 Mult if the most-played hand is played. The Obelisk resets before the hand is scored.

title: Obelisk
text: Obelisk: You can safely play any hand type until it is tied to your most-played hand type. Obelisk will only reset once you break the tie between those hands (i.e., you play one of those hands one more time). The Monolith Challenge Deck starts the player with an Eternal copy of Obelisk. Decks: Red Deck's extra discards, Painted Deck's higher hand size, and Abandoned Deck's smaller deck size all allow the player to find more unique hands, which helps with keeping the XMult on Obelisk without risking playing the most played hand. Painted Deck also appreciates having such a high-value XMult Joker. Blue Deck's extra hands allow Obelisk to scale faster per round.

title: Obelisk
text: Obelisk: Blue Deck's extra hands allow Obelisk to scale faster per round. Checkered Deck makes Flush easier to play, as the deck only has Spades and Hearts. Using this deck allows another option for the most played hand type other than Pair and Two Pair to build around and then pivot out of. It also helps the player after pivoting if the build does not revolve around Flush beforehand, as having another hand type that's easy to hit reduces the chance of resetting Obelisk accidentally.

title: Obelisk
text: Obelisk: Poker hands: No particular poker hand is better with Obelisk. The Pair or Two Pair strategy mentioned below could be considered a synergy, but the bulk of the game will be spent playing as many different hands as possible to keep options open in the future.

title: Obelisk
text: Obelisk: Jokers: Jokers that produce Mult without hand-based conditions are what you always want to use with Obelisk. These can be flat + Mult Jokers, like Fibonacci and Gros Michel, but the most success comes from scaling ones, like Bootstraps, Erosion, Ride the Bus, or Fortune Teller. Having one of these scaling Jokers will usually allow you to play all your hands per round, since you can place Obelisk before them for all but the last hand, and the last hand will have a large amount of extra Mult. Spare Trousers and Runner will often naturally set up a stack of Two Pairs/Straights, making a smooth transition to other hands.

title: Obelisk
text: Obelisk: Jokers that provide scaling + Chips, like the aforementioned Runner, Square Joker or Bull, are very important to play Obelisk effectively, as few Chips will be provided from Planet cards. Vagabond and other Jokers that benefit from many hands being played per round work well with Obelisk, as you already want to play many hands per round to scale Obelisk. All of these kinds of Jokers in turn benefit from Acrobat, as it provides a safety net for the last hand of the round.

title: Obelisk
text: Obelisk: Boss Blinds: When a poker hand is not allowed to be played by The Psychic, The Eye, or The Mouth, Obelisk will not reset or gain Mult. However, the hand counter in the Run Info will increase by 1. This theoretically allows a method of always increasing Obelisk. Alternately, when Obelisk gets disabled by Crimson Heart, the most played hands can be safely played without resetting Obelisk. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong give additional hands per round, allowing Obelisk to scale even higher. Wasteful and Recyclomancy give additional discards, which allows the player to find more unique hands, which helps with keeping the XMult on Obelisk without risking playing the most played hand.

title: Obelisk
text: Obelisk: Paint Brush and Palette both increase hand size, which can help players to find and form more unique hands to keep the XMult on Obelisk without risking playing the most played hand. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle all have poor synergy with Obelisk due to their reduced number of hands. Nebula Deck has slight anti-synergy with Obelisk, as Telescope encourages building around a single most-played hand type, which Obelisk discourages. Jokers: Burglar removes all discards and may force the most played hand to be played, resetting Obelisk. All Jokers that rely on playing specific hands, including Superposition, Crazy Joker, and The Order, will not be able to be used as much.

title: Obelisk
text: Obelisk: Planet cards and Jokers that upgrade hands, like Space Joker and Burnt Joker, are far less effective because the hand can only be used a limited number of times. Vouchers: Telescope encourages focusing on a single poker hand, which is the opposite of what Obelisk needs to scale. Strategies: Obelisk can become a very powerful Scaling XMult Joker, but it cannot be used in every build. It works best on builds that don't rely on playing specific hands to score, as if too many of any one hand are played, you can no longer play it without resetting the Obelisk.

title: Obelisk
text: Obelisk: The most effective strategy with Obelisk is to play Pair or Two Pair until around 15 have been played, then pivoting in the later antes to playing any other hand. It is not recommended to use Obelisk if the most played hand is High Card, as the player runs a higher risk of being forced to reset the Obelisk. Trivia: The inspiration for Obelisk comes from the movie 2001: A Space Odyssey, which features alien monoliths. LocalThunk once revealed an old design of Obelisk, with a more vibrant background.

title: Obelisk
text: Obelisk: LocalThunk once revealed an old design of Obelisk, with a more vibrant background. During the second demo, Obelisk scaled at X0.5 Mult per played hand, making it as strong as Madness. It was later nerfed twice, resulting in only X0.2 Mult per played hand, the second weakest among scaling Multiplicative Jokers per scaling trigger (only after Constellation, at X0.1 Mult per Planet card used).

title: Odd Todd
text: Odd Todd: Odd Todd (Joker). Effect: Played cards with odd rank give +31 Chips when scored, (A, 9, 7, 5, 3). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Odd Todd is a Common Chips Joker that provides +31 Chips when played cards with an odd rank are scored. These odd ranks are Aces, 3s, 5s, 7s, and 9s.

title: Odd Todd
text: Odd Todd: Decks: Red Deck's extra discard makes finding strong hands with many odd ranks easier. Abandoned Deck works best with Odd Todd thanks to having no face cards, allowing players to find odd ranks easier. Mad World will also work as well, although this deck doesn't start with any Aces. Magic Deck's Fool Tarots can be used as Strengths, converting even ranks or Kings into odd ranks. Plasma Deck can use the large influx of Chips to win a large number of early hands, allowing one to search for better Jokers easier.

title: Odd Todd
text: Odd Todd: Poker hands: Any poker hand can benefit from Odd Todd provided it is comprised of mainly odd cards. Todd works the best with five-card hands that encourage repeating ranks, like Full House and Five of a Kind. Jokers: Odd Todd generates +155 Chips when five odd ranks are scored, and more if any of those cards retrigger. This amount of Chips encourages taking more + Mult and X Mult Jokers to balance Chips and Mult. Many of them work well, though notable ones include Fibonacci and Scholar, as both also trigger on certain odd ranks.

title: Odd Todd
text: Odd Todd: Retrigger effects increase the amount of Chips Odd Todd produces. Notably, Hack works very well, as it offers unconditional retriggers on Threes and Fives (which also are triggered by Fibonacci). Cloud 9 scales its money generation off having more Nines in your deck. These Nines become better to play with Odd Todd's extra chips. Trading Card and DNA allow the changing of your deck to include more odd ranks and fewer non-odd ranks. Ride the Bus is able to scale very well, as you never want to play non-odd ranks with Odd Todd.

title: Odd Todd
text: Odd Todd: Ride the Bus is able to scale very well, as you never want to play non-odd ranks with Odd Todd. Shortcut can let you make Straights primarily from odd cards. However, Straights already have a high amount of chip scaling from Saturn/ Neptune and certain other Jokers like Runner. Consumables: Tarot cards: The Hanged Man can be used to destroy non-odd numbered cards in order to make the odd numbered ones easier to find. Death can be used to turn other cards into odd numbered cards or Aces in order to maximize the Chips value. Strength can be used to turn even numbers into odd numbers and Kings into Aces.

title: Odd Todd
text: Odd Todd: Strength can be used to turn even numbers into odd numbers and Kings into Aces. The Empress and Justice provide flat and multiplicative Mult scaling respectively to help balance Odd Todd's Chips bonus. Spectral cards: Deja Vu can apply a Red Seal onto some odd and Ace cards, which allows for more Odd Todd triggers. Cryptid can create more copies of odd and Ace cards. Grim can provide more Ace cards to play in exchange for destroying 1 random card. While an odd numbered card could be destroyed in the process, Aces provide the highest number of Chips when played, making the risk worth it.

title: Odd Todd
text: Odd Todd: Incantation could also create more odd-ranked cards with random enhancements despite having to destroy a random card in your hand as a drawback. Trivia: It is similar in style to Even Steven, with that being Mult and even ranks. Due to his theming of odd numbers, Odd Todd's clothes are different from other jokers. He wears a hat with an odd number of baubles on top and has only three frill baubles below instead of four. Out of all the baubles, three of them are white and one of them is black. He also only has one eye open, as opposed to other jokers, who usually have both of their eyes open.

title: Odd Todd
text: Odd Todd: Odd Todd's ability to give +31 Chips whenever an odd ranked card is scored is self-evident, with 31 being an odd number itself. Odd Todd being blue as opposed to Even Steven's red is in relation to his ability to add Chips to your score. He is another Joker to get merchandise from Makeship alongside Even Steven as part of a Combo Pack mini-plush set.

title: Onyx Agate
text: Onyx Agate: Onyx Agate (Joker). Effect: Played cards with Club suit give +7 Mult when scored. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Have at least 30 cards with Club suit in your deck. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Onyx Agate is an Uncommon Clubs-oriented Additive Mult Joker that gives +7 Mult per Club card scored. For a Club Flush, this adds up to a whopping +35 Mult, making Onyx Agate an easy choice for a source of Mult in the early to mid game, or if the player prefers playing Flush-type builds.

title: Onyx Agate
text: Onyx Agate: Usage Notes: Unlike unlocking Arrowhead and Bloodstone, fulfilling the condition of 30 Club cards in a Deck is trickier, as it doesn't allow for an easy strategy such as using the Checkered Deck for the aforementioned Jokers. Magic Deck starts the player with two copies of The Fool, allowing for easier Deck manipulation early on by finding The Moon or Death. Any Jokers that synergize with Flush builds are likely to be useful during the unlock attempt, such as Droll Joker, Crafty Joker, and The Tribe. Economy Jokers are likely to be beneficial to find more Tarots for Deck manipulation, such as Mail-In Rebate and Golden Joker.

title: Onyx Agate
text: Onyx Agate: Non-club Wild cards or Spade cards with Smeared Joker do not count towards Onyx Agate's unlock condition. Poker hands: Playing any Flush-type hand full of Clubs will benefit greatly from Onyx Agate, those being: Flush Straight Flush Flush House Flush Five Jokers: Gluttonous Joker also triggers when Club cards are played, though the bonus is strictly inferior. Smeared Joker allows Spade suit to benefit from Onyx Agate as well. In this context, Arrowhead can be a substantial addition as the player will gain both Chips and Mult. Blackboard can be an easy addition, as if the player as the deck set up to have a lot of Clubs, Blackboard will benefit too.

title: Onyx Agate
text: Onyx Agate: Retrigger Jokers work very well with Onyx Agate, as the extra triggers adds more Mult, on top of other card Enhancements that could benefit scoring power. For a Flush build, The Tribe will capitalize on Onyx Agate's Mult bonus. Photograph can work reasonably well as long as the face card is placed to the far right, activating its XMult after Onyx Agate's Additive Mult. Enhancements: Wild cards count as Clubs, which will activate Onyx Agate's Mult bonus. As Onyx Agate already provides a hefty Mult bonus, Bonus cards fit quite nicely to double as a source of Chips.

title: Onyx Agate
text: Onyx Agate: Glass cards may be the most potent synergy as it directly synergizes with Onyx Agate's Additive Mult, however, there is always the risk of the Glass breaking. This could potentially be capitalized on if the player obtains a Glass Joker, which gains XMult on Glass breaking. Consumables: The Moon can turn some non-Club cards into Club cards allowing the player to see Club cards easier. The Lovers can turn some non-Club cards into Wild cards which trigger Onyx Agate. Death can turn some non-Club cards into Club cards. The Hanged Man can remove some non-Club cards. Deja Vu can apply Red Seals onto Club cards allowing for more Onyx Agate triggers.

title: Onyx Agate
text: Onyx Agate: Deja Vu can apply Red Seals onto Club cards allowing for more Onyx Agate triggers. Decks: The Checkered Deck cannot benefit from Onyx Agate due to lack of Clubs, unless combined with the Smeared Joker. Jokers: Seeing Double will only activate if a Club and another suit score, rendering it useless for Flush builds which is where Onyx Agate shines best. Although, the bonus may still be activated if a Wild card is used. While Four Fingers can make Flushes easier to play, it enables the player to do so with less overall cards, therefore the scoring power of Onyx Agate is weakened if the player opts for a 4-card Club Flush.

title: Onyx Agate
text: Onyx Agate: It may be suitable to hunt for Planet cards and/or scaling Chip Jokers if Four Fingers must remain in conjunction with Onyx Agate. Blinds: When facing The Club, all Club cards are debuffed, meaning Onyx Agate cannot activate. The Pillar may be problematic as previously played Club cards of the Ante will be debuffed, rendering them useless for Onyx Agate. Trivia: Onyx Agate is one of four stone/mineral themed jokers unlocked by having 30 cards of that suit in your deck. The others are Arrowhead (spades), Bloodstone (hearts), and Rough Gem (diamonds). In demo versions, the effects of Bloodstone (+ Mult) and Onyx Agate (XMult on probability) are swapped.

title: Onyx Agate
text: Onyx Agate: In demo versions, the effects of Bloodstone (+ Mult) and Onyx Agate (XMult on probability) are swapped. Like Arrowhead, this joker is inspired from an Onyx agate LocalThunk found on beach.

title: Oops! All 6s
text: Oops! All 6s: Oops! All 6s (Joker). Effect: Doubles all listed probabilities, (ex: 1 in 3 -> 2 in 3). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: In one hand, earn at least 10,000 chips. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Oops! All 6s is an Uncommon Effect Joker that doubles all listed probabilities (generally distinguished by green text in game). For example, a 2 in 5 chance would become a 4 in 5 chance.

title: Oops! All 6s
text: Oops! All 6s: To unlock this Joker, the player must score 10,000 chips or more. This Joker shares an unlock requirement with the 10K achievement. Oops! All 6s works on almost every shown X in Y chance, including potentially undesirable effects, such as Cavendish going extinct. The only listed probability Oops! All 6s does not affect is the 1 in 4 chance of flipping a card during the X-ray Vision challenge. Usage notes: The Fragile challenge starts the player with two Eternal Negative copies of Oops! All 6s, while all cards are Glass cards. Jokers: This Joker benefits Jokers that have probability effects: 8 Ball's effect becomes a 2 in 4 chance to generate a Tarot card when an 8 is scored.

title: Oops! All 6s
text: Oops! All 6s: 8 Ball's effect becomes a 2 in 4 chance to generate a Tarot card when an 8 is scored. Space Joker's effect becomes a 2 in 4 chance to upgrade any hand when played. Reserved Parking and Business Card become guaranteed to give money on held face cards and scored face cards respectively. Hallucination guarantees a tarot card when opening a booster pack. Bloodstone becomes guaranteed to apply its multiplier effect. Gros Michel's chance of extinction increases to a 2 in 6 chance, which can speed up the process of having one break to spawn a Cavendish. This comes at the downside of an increased risk to lose out on +15 Mult.

title: Oops! All 6s
text: Oops! All 6s: This comes at the downside of an increased risk to lose out on +15 Mult. Oops! All 6s can also benefit Jokers that indirectly use probability effects: Lucky Cat can scale faster, as Lucky cards have an increased chance to trigger. Glass Joker, Canio, and Erosion can scale faster due to the increased chance of Glass cards breaking.

title: Oops! All 6s
text: Oops! All 6s: Glass Joker, Canio, and Erosion can scale faster due to the increased chance of Glass cards breaking. Oops! All 6s's effect stacks with multiple copies of itself. With two copies of Oops! All 6s, probabilities are effectively quadrupled. For example, The Wheel of Fortune will always trigger, and Glass cards will always break when played. Oops! All 6s is incompatible with Blueprint and Brainstorm, but multiple copies can be obtained in normal play by using Showman, Invisible Joker, or Ankh. Consumables: The Wheel of Fortune cards' chances improve to 2 in 4. Decks: Painted Deck, Blast Off and Cruelty reduce the amount of Joker Slots, which makes it less convenient to use Oops! All 6s.

title: Oops! All 6s
text: Oops! All 6s: Jokers: Driver's License can suffer slightly from Glass cards' increased chance of destruction, but it also benefits from Lucky Cards increased chance of triggering, especially the Mult chance. Cavendish's chance to destroy itself is doubled to a 2 in 1000 chance. Card modifiers: While the increased chance of Glass breaking is beneficial for deck thinning, it also can pose an issue if they are crucial for survival. Boss Blinds: The Wheel will have an increased chance of flipped cards, becoming 2 in 7. With 3 copies of Oops! All 6s, this chance is increased to 8 in 7, causing all playing cards to be drawn face down.

title: Oops! All 6s
text: Oops! All 6s: Trivia: This Joker's name is a reference to Cap'n Crunch cereal, specifically the "Oops! All Berries" variant. It has become a popular meme online to refer to something excessive in this way. The Joker art depicts a unique cubic die with six pips on every visible face, the highest roll one can get on a standard 6-sided die. The six-pip pattern is also shown in the background. The example from the description (1 in 3 chance to 2 in 3) is now hypothetical - there are no 1 in 3 chances in the game since Bloodstone was updated in Update 1.0.1f.

title: Oops! All 6s
text: Oops! All 6s: According to LocalThunk, Oops! All 6s' design used to be in red, but it was changed to keep consistent with the color of listed probabilities. The original red design for Oops! All 6s can still be seen on the icon for the achievement "You Get What You Get". The art of this card in pre-release had a thinner inner border instead of the full border it has now.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Pareidolia (Joker). Effect: All cards are considered face cards. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Pareidolia is an Uncommon Effect Joker that makes all playing cards be counted as face cards. This is also applicable to Blinds' and other Jokers' effects. The cards will still retain their original rank, suit, and chip value.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Despite the in-game description saying "all cards", this only applies to playing cards (i.e., Tarot cards and Planet cards do not have this effect applied to them). Usage notes: The Mad World challenge starts the player with an Eternal, Negative copy of Pareidolia. Decks: Black Deck: This deck provides an extra Joker slot, making it easier to work with Pareidolia since it does not directly improve the player's build, without having other face card orientated Jokers to leverage it. Abandoned Deck: Potentially benefits from having Pareidolia by giving access to face card bolstering Jokers.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Abandoned Deck: Potentially benefits from having Pareidolia by giving access to face card bolstering Jokers. Poker hands: A larger poker hand is generally more ideal to play, since it can trigger more Jokers that trigger off of face cards, including Four of a Kind, Full House, Flush, etc.. The type of poker hand it is counted as is unaffected by the played cards counting as "face cards", since Pareidolia does not change a rank or suit. Card modifiers: Pareidolia also lets Stone cards be treated as face cards, thus able to work with effects triggered from face cards.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Jokers: Because Pareidolia does not change the rank of the card (rather, it just makes all playing cards count as face cards), it does not interfere with the effects of Jokers like Fibonacci which trigger on specific ranks. Generally, Pareidolia has synergy with any Joker that is triggered from face cards. Some specific Jokers it works well with include: Business Card: All cards scored have a 1 in 2 chance to generate $2. This means a played hand with any 5 scoring cards will generate an average of $5, as much as Rough Gem when playing a Diamonds Flush. Faceless Joker: Gives $5 for every discard that has at least 3 cards.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Faceless Joker: Gives $5 for every discard that has at least 3 cards. Reserved Parking: All cards held in hand will have a 1 in 2 chance to generate $1. This translates to an average of $0.5 per held card on every played hand, and becomes stronger as the player's hand size increases or their played hands begin containing fewer cards. Smiley Face: All scored cards get +5 Mult each (up to +25 Mult with no other effects). Scary Face: All scored cards get +30 Chips each (up to +150 Chips with no other effects).

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Scary Face: All scored cards get +30 Chips each (up to +150 Chips with no other effects). Sock and Buskin: All scored cards trigger twice. Pairing this with the aforementioned Business Card, Smiley Face, and/or Scary Face means twice as much money, +Mult, and Chips, respectively. Midas Mask: All scoring cards become Gold cards when played, which allows for huge amounts of money generation as the run progresses and the player's hand size increases (as much as $21 with the base hand size of 8 and a round-ending High Card). These two Jokers alongside Vampire can combine to boost Vampire by X0.5 extra Mult per hand played, as long as each hand has 5 scoring cards.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Notably, since Pareidolia also makes Stone cards treated as face cards, they will also be turned to Gold cards. Canio: Destroying any card gives it X1 Mult. Note that only playing cards count as face cards and not Jokers or consumables. Thus, the effects of Ceremonial Dagger and Madness, or the 'food' Jokers that can destroy themselves (such as Popcorn) will not trigger Canio's scaling. Splash: All played cards trigger any Jokers that apply to scored face cards.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Splash: All played cards trigger any Jokers that apply to scored face cards. Photograph: Despite it buffing face cards, combining it with this Joker typically has somewhat limited effectiveness, as it gives its X2 Mult when the first card in the played poker hand is scored, meaning it happens before any of the other scored cards have a chance to activate their own "when scored" effects. However, pairing it with the aforementioned Smiley Face and/or Sock and Buskin makes it a bit stronger, and it also allows for far easier ballooning of the power of Glass cards, cards with a Red Seal, and/or Polychrome playing cards.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Luchador, Mr. Bones, and Chicot: In the absence of another way to circumvent select Boss Blinds, any of these Jokers will let the player avoid almost certain death when faced with The Mark or The Plant. Investing in an Ectoplasm, a Negative Tag, or Blank (leading to Antimatter) can all be worth considering in these cases, as being down two scoring Jokers can make a run very dangerous, much more so than just one would.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Vouchers: Pareidolia is one of the few Jokers in the game that almost necessitates the use of a specific Voucher(s). Director's Cut and its upgraded counterpart Retcon are one of the only ways to boost a Pareidolia build's stability, by allowing the near-guaranteed avoidance of two run-enders Blinds (discussed below) so long as the player has money. Seed Money and Money Tree can also synergize with this card, if you have jokers like Business Card, Reserved Parking and Midas Mask. These jokers can generate extra money, and combining them with these vouchers can enable extremely high amounts of interest.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Decks: Avoid this Joker on the Painted Deck, Blast Off, and Cruelty, as their inherent reduced Joker slots makes Pareidolia extremely hard to use without going out of your way to hold more Jokers or scale certain poker hands with Planet cards. Jokers: Ride the Bus will reset back to +0 Mult on every hand played when Pareidolia is present. Blinds: There is one Boss Blind that weakens Pareidolia-based builds, and another that is extremely run-threatening:

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Blinds: There is one Boss Blind that weakens Pareidolia-based builds, and another that is extremely run-threatening: The Mark: All cards are drawn face-down, making it far more difficult to assemble a sufficiently-scoring hand. This can be somewhat remedied by carrying Enhancing or Suit-changing Tarot cards into this Boss Blind, allowing a few cards to be identified at a time. Similarly, and more effectively, albeit much rarer, the Ouija and Sigil Spectral cards can completely negate the power of this Boss Blind, by guaranteeing that a potentially lethal hand can be scored (Five of a Kind/Flush Five and Flush/Straight Flush/Flush House, respectively).

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: The Plant: All cards are debuffed, meaning they cannot provide 'when scored' or 'held in hand' effects at all and utterly crippling the player's score. This is an almost guaranteed run-ender against a Pareidolia build unless the player can reroll the Boss Blind, or the player's other Jokers and poker hand levels provide enough raw scoring independent of it (in which case replacing it may be a better move than keeping it).

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: Depending on a player's strategy, selling Pareidolia before entering these Boss Blinds may be beneficial (selling Pareidolia after The Mark has begun does not flip over non-face cards). At other times, however, encountering either of these can mean certain death, which makes means of rerolling or disabling the Boss Blind imperative to keeping a build like this stable. Trivia: Pareidolia can be defined as "the perception of apparently significant patterns or recognizable images in random or accidental arrangements of shapes and lines", which can include faces. This plays into its ability to make all cards count as face cards; it makes the Blinds the player is up against perceived face cards where there may otherwise be none.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: The art of this card references its name as it is a set of playing cards arranged to appear like a face. The counter of the R in the top left "Joker" text is the wrong shade of green, as it is a solid color and does not follow the gradient shown by the rest of the card. All but four jokers either provide some benefit by themselves, or simply require having literally any other joker (such as Swashbuckler or Invisible Joker); the exceptions are Pareidolia, Baseball Card, Blueprint and Brainstorm. Of these, Pareidolia has by far the smallest pool of compatible jokers with only nine.

title: Pareidolia
text: Pareidolia: The art of this card in pre-release had a thinner inner border instead of the full border it has now.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Perkeo (Joker). Effect: Creates a Negative copy of 1 random consumable card in your possession at the end of the shop. Rarity: Legendary. Unlock Requirement: Find this Joker from the Soul card. Buy Price: 20 (cannot be found in shop). Sell Price: $10. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Perkeo is one of the five Legendary Jokers that can be generated from using The Soul, which in itself has a 3 in 1000 (0.3%) chance to replace any given card in a Spectral Pack or an Arcana Pack.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Perkeo creates a Negative copy of any random consumable card held by the player when leaving The Shop, be it a Tarot card, a Planet card, or a Spectral card. Thanks to the Negative modifier that gives a +1 consumable slot to the applied card, Perkeo will always create a new consumable, even if all consumable slots are filled. This extra copy can then be used like normal, or sold for a higher value than usual because of the Negative modifier.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Decks: Having access to many consumables is one of the most important aspects when owning Perkeo, as it grants a wider selection of choices for Perkeo to duplicate, allowing the player to make better decisions depending on what they can get it to copy. Perkeo fits well in any deck, but notable standouts are:

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Ghost Deck is undoubtedly the deck that works best with Perkeo, as Spectral cards are, by nature, a huge game-changer due to their drastic effects at various degrees. The ability to buy Spectral cards directly from the Shop can be unfathomably powerful, allowing the player to create copies of powerhouses like Cryptid to duplicate powerful cards, or the likes of Deja Vu and Aura to enhance existing cards in their deck. Without it, the only way to get Spectral cards into the consumable slots to copy will be Séance or Sixth Sense, which is way harder to make use of.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Zodiac Deck due to the increased consumable rate in the Shop coming from both the Tarot Merchant and Planet Merchant vouchers, as well as easier access to their upgrades, Tarot Tycoon and Planet Tycoon, and just more shop items in general thanks to the Overstock voucher, and again, easier access to its upgraded version, the Overstock Plus voucher. Poker hands: Perkeo can benefit any unlocked poker hand equally. Acquiring the desired poker hand's Planet and keeping it in the consumable slot can let the player get a Planet every shop, which can make scaling very easy and comfortable compared to trying to find it in the shop.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Perkeo also has a natural synergy with the Observatory Voucher, which has been colloquially dubbed together as the "particle accelerator" build. This is because Observatory grants X1.5 Mult for each Planet held in the consumable slots matching the poker hand played. By stacking multiple copies of a particular planet, the player gains a massive boost to their score which can accumulate at a rapid pace, especially when using jokers capable of copying Perkeo. This is helpful for runs that go deep into endless, though even with several copy jokers it will eventually become outpaced by the scaling of blind scoring requirements each ante. Additionally, this can be useful in helping the player achieve naneinf as a supplementary form of scoring, so there is a slight bias for High Card (as a High Card build is the most consistent way to achieve naneinf).

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Jokers: Any Joker that is compatible with Blueprint and/or Brainstorm performs amazingly when paired with them, and Perkeo is no exception. It is in fact one of the best Jokers to copy, allowing players to generate multiple Negative consumables every blind, which is not to mention that Perkeo activates at a separate time from all other Jokers - when exiting a Shop - allowing the player to freely copy other Jokers when Perkeo has done its job for maximum benefit. Note that each trigger of the ability may select a different consumable to copy if the player has different consumables available to be duplicated.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Jokers like Superposition, Cartomancer, Hallucination, Vagabond, and 8 Ball all generate Tarot cards, which can be used as the copy target for Perkeo. Sixth Sense and Séance are the only ways to put a Spectral card in the consumable slot outside of Ghost Deck, which makes them a powerful combination with Perkeo, provided their conditions can be fulfilled consistently. Even just getting one or two Spectral cards from them can be good enough value. Duplicating random Planets or Tarot cards becomes way more viable of a strategy when paired with Constellation which gains X0.1 Mult when a Planet is used, or Fortune Teller, gaining +1 Mult when using a Tarot card.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Perkeo has a natural synergy with Campfire, which gains X0.25 Mult every time a card is sold. Holding a consumable at the end of the shop creates a copy that can be sold for cash and a guaranteed X1.75 Mult on Campfire for the Boss Blind, provided neither the Small Blind or Big Blind are skipped. Gift Card works well with Perkeo by keeping consumables for multiple rounds, gaining lots of money than what was initially worth. The added sell value does not drop with Clearance Sale or Liquidation, allowing this combo to be used in full effect even with the mentioned Vouchers purchased. Consumables: Tarot cards:

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Consumables: Tarot cards: The Fool has a respectable synergy with Perkeo. By having multiple copies of The Fool, one can generate multiple copies of the desired Tarot card or Planet all at once, whether it be a suit-changing Tarot card for poker hands containing a Flush, Death/ The Hanged Man for deck building, or a specific Planet to use. The Hanged Man has perhaps one of the best combos with Perkeo, as the synergy can repeatedly trim the deck by 2 cards each round, allowing specific poker hands or playing cards, that are difficult to come across with a bloated deck, much easier to find.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Death can turn the whole deck into a specific playing card, which is best used on cards that already have a useful Enhancement, Edition or Seal. The High Priestess and The Emperor are great ways to generate Planets and Tarot cards, allowing the players to find certain consumables much easier. They also have an apparent synergy with the aforementioned Jokers Constellation and Fortune Teller. The Judgement and The Wheel of Fortune Tarot cards, while not the best targets for Perkeo to duplicate, can still generate new Jokers or Editions for your Jokers, which is best when there's not much money to be spent. In most scenarios though, their best use is to be sold.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Temperance is one of the best cards to copy due to Perkeo alone having a high sell value of $10. Spectral cards: Cryptid and Immolate are some of the best consumables to be used with Perkeo. They have immense deck building value, with Cryptid creating multiple copies of a playing card and Immolate thinning the deck down quite significantly while also giving a decent chunk of money, equal to that of The Hermit. When used in bulk, which is made far more accessible thanks to Perkeo, they allow the deck to be composed of only one specific card quite easily, opening the gates for quite a few strategies, most notably High Card and Flush Five builds.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Aura and Ectoplasm are quite good match-ups with Perkeo to enhance the player's cards. Aura can be used repeatedly for the specific Edition wanted, or at certain times bail the player out of sticky situations. Ectoplasm lets the player cover their Joker roster with the Negative Edition, allowing more Jokers to join in the build, in turn generating way more score or letting duplicates of strong Jokers in with the use of Showman, Invisible Joker and/or Ankh. Though, it is noteworthy that it is never recommended to use too many Ectoplasms, since the additive deduction to Hand size makes it a run killer.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: This issue can be negated partly by building towards High Card or Pair. Even then, it is recommend that the player never use more than 3 Ectoplasms without certain methods to obtain more Hand sizes than normally available. Deja Vu, Talisman, Trance, and Medium allows the player to make Seals on playing cards easily, providing lots of value. However, one of the better strategies is to only use them a few times on important cards and then makes more copies of it using Death, DNA and/or Cryptid. Planets:

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Planets: All poker hands benefit from Perkeo's ability evenly as its effect treats all Planets equally. The player can use the copies to level up the poker hand, keep them for extra score with Observatory, or form synergies with Gift Card/ Campfire as described in the #Synergies section above.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Vouchers: The Observatory voucher has one of the most powerful synergies with Perkeo. By keeping multiple copies of a Planet in the consumable slots and focusing on playing that one particular hand, the player gets a great boost to their scoring, which is almost always better than just leveling up the poker hand itself, making this a really viable strategy. The deck can be built to work with any poker hand, but the most notable and consistent, especially for Endless Mode, will be High Card, Five of a Kind and Flush Five. With extra copies of Perkeo, or the beloved Blueprint/ Brainstorm, every Shop can guarantee at least 2 extra Planets for a much better scaling.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: The Tarot Merchant and Planet Merchant vouchers makes Tarot cards and Planets way more accessible for duplication, which is doubly true so with their upgrades, the Tarot Tycoon and Planet Tycoon vouchers. The Zodiac Deck starts with both of those vouchers, as well as the Overstock voucher and access to its upgraded version, Overstock Plus, allowing the player to see many more shop items, including the Tarot cards and Planets aforementioned, making it a better candidate to use with Perkeo than most other decks.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Decks: Painted Deck can be harder to utilize due to its -1 Joker slot penalty, since Perkeo generally provides no direct benefits for scoring. In most cases this isn't really an issue though, as the benefits that Perkeo provides generally far outweigh the downside. Jokers: Madness should not be used, since Perkeo is a Legendary and therefore cannot have an Eternal sticker outside of challenge decks.

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: Trivia: Perkeo of Heidelberg (born Clemens Pankert, according to other sources Giovanni Clementi; 1702–1735) was a notable jester of Elector Palatine Charles III Philip in Heidelberg. As guardian of the Great Heidelberg Tun, he has since become an unofficial mascot of the city and region. His name, story, and image have been connected with a variety of festivals, traditional songs, cultural and scientific institutions, hotels, restaurants, and private companies (in and out of the region) ever since. Perkeo's ability to hold infinite consumable cards is a reference to the real jester's penchant for allegedly consuming between five and eight US gallons of wine a day (possibly due to a case of Diabetes Insipidus).

title: Perkeo
text: Perkeo: This Joker has 2 differently shaped eyes: Perkeo's left eye is slightly deviated, resembling cross-eyes, specifically a condition known as exotropia. Perkeo is the only way to get consumables with the Negative Edition applied. This Joker, like the other Legendary Jokers, is animated, with Perkeo hovering just above the green card face. The other Legendary Jokers are Canio, Chicot, Triboulet, and Yorick. More information about them can be found in the page Legendary Jokers. Perkeo is the only Joker that triggers when exiting the Shop. In other media: Perkeo appears as a playable character in the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors. Perkeo appears as an artifact in Monster Train 2.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: Photograph (Joker). Effect: First played face card gives X2 Mult when scored. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Photograph is a Common Joker that can give Multiplicative Mult. This Joker activates on the first played scoring face card in a poker hand and gives X2 Mult after the played cards' Enhancement and Edition trigger. Photograph will get retriggered by either a Joker effect (ex. Sock and Buskin) or if said face card had a Red Seal.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: It's generally better to place scoring face cards on the rightmost side of the poker hand so that they activate later (unless paired with Hanging Chad). This is because of the sequence scoring activation. By having Photograph activate its X2 Mult later, Jokers that give + Mult from played scoring cards, the Holographic edition, and/or the Mult enhancement from playing cards will contribute to the Mult of the score before it's doubled by Photograph. Decks: The Ghost Deck can be a good choice since it gives easier access to Deja Vu for Red Seals, and Familiar for more face cards.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: Poker hands: Full House, Two Pair, Straight, and Flush are the best early game, as they give additional opportunity for Enhanced and/or Edition Aces and numbered cards to activate their effects first. Additionally, all of these except Two Pair have relatively high starting raw Mult stats, enabling more benefit from Photograph's xMult early on. Straight, Four of a Kind, and Secret Hands are the best late game, as the high base Mult from Saturn, Mars, and the Secret Hand Planet cards far outscale any + Mult effects.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: Jokers: Hanging Chad: Popularly known together as "Photochad", these are one of the most reliable duos in the game, with a powerful early game combo that has the potential to stay relevant in the late game.
