Due to their low rarity, it makes it easy to create this pair with a low total cost of $9, providing X8 Mult and +20 Chips on their own if the first scored card in a hand is a face card.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: For example: A Flush will score a minimum of 2,528 (Fa 5 4 3 2), a Full House 2,752 (Fa Fa 2 2 2), and a Straight 3,008 (J 10 9 8 7). This means, with a little luck, Ante 2 on any Stake can be cleared in a single hand per Blind with just this combo, while saving cash to make stronger purchases. The only exception is if The Wall Boss Blind is encountered at Ante 2, requiring 2 hands or something extra.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: Wrathful Joker, Fibonacci, Walkie Talkie, and other Jokers that give + Mult when cards are scored are one of the few ways to add Mult before Photograph activates, and can provide high scores early game if the + Mult cards are placed before the first face card. Sock and Buskin: By retriggering all played face cards, Photograph's effect is doubled. This combo is most effective when the player has stacked up many Glass cards and/or Polychrome face cards, as they can shoot the Mult value way higher even after Photograph is done triggering.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: Dusk and Seltzer: These two are generally more effective than Sock and Buskin in bolstering this Joker, but instead of unconditionally applying to face cards, they are either conditional (Dusk) or temporary (Seltzer). They allow for 'when scored' effects of Aces and numbered cards (ex. Scholar, Mult cards, and Holographic cards) to trigger twice before Photograph quadruples the Mult at the time the face card gets scored, leading to an overall higher score.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: The Idol: Providing X2 Mult when a card of a specific rank and suit is scored, it can double the rate at which this Joker skyrockets the score. At base, it only has a 3/13 (~23.1%) chance of choosing any face card at the end of a round, but deck manipulation through the likes of Tarot cards such as Strength, The Lovers, and especially Death (which can unify suits while also copying other card Modifiers stronger than the Wild Enhancement) can make it significantly easier to activate.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: Ancient Joker gives X1.5 when cards played match the suit that Ancient Joker targets in that round, effectively making the first played face card give X3 Mult when triggered. Though, due to Ancient Joker being based on random suits and not the specific cards in your deck, it can be less consistent in the later antes or when your deck is sufficiently fixed through Tarot cards like Strength and Death. The Lovers can also be useful with this Joker, allowing it to always trigger.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: Triboulet: An exceedingly rare Legendary Joker that gives X2 Mult when a King or Queen is scored. Pairing this with one of the aforementioned retrigger Jokers makes for an absurd amount of Mult when scoring a King or Queen. Pareidolia: A situational synergy with Photograph, since it causes the X2 Mult to be activated on the first scoring card played regardless of rank. This means that any + Mult that could have been added beforehand will not get doubled. Splash: Can help with activating Photograph if the played hand does not contain any scoring face cards. For example, a Four of a Kind with 5, 5, 5, 5, Queen.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: Boss Blinds: Since Photograph retains its unique square shape, it is easy to identify despite being flipped face-down by the Amber Acorn. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Medusa should not be used with Photograph, as they have no face cards by default. A possible exception is if Pareidolia is used alongside. Jokers: Faceless Joker incentivizes discarding face cards, making it harder to preserve one for Photograph. Ride the Bus: As scoring a face card resets it back to +0 Mult, this Joker is unable to use its own effect without decimating many rounds' worth of Additive Mult scaling. Canio encourages the player to destroy face cards, which doesn't work well with Photograph.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: Canio encourages the player to destroy face cards, which doesn't work well with Photograph. Boss Blinds: The Plant debuffs all face cards, rendering Photograph useless. The Mark may be an issue if your poker hand relies on particular ranks, such as Straights. Trivia: This Joker is square-shaped, rather than the typical rectangle. It evokes the style of the Polaroid camera film.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: Trivia: This Joker is square-shaped, rather than the typical rectangle. It evokes the style of the Polaroid camera film. The Joker in the image has red eyes. This is a reference to the red-eye effect that was especially common when Polaroid cameras were the standard, but can still occur with digital cameras assuming no correction is used. It is caused when the camera's flash feature reflects all the blood cells in one's retina; this is best seen in low-light areas as the pupils dilate in darkened conditions. Photograph is one of only two Common Jokers that can provide Multiplicative Mult, along with Cavendish.

title: Photograph
text: Photograph: Photograph is one of only two Common Jokers that can provide Multiplicative Mult, along with Cavendish. This Joker is part of a set that doesn't adhere to the standard joker size, even when flipped over by Amber Acorn, along with Wee Joker, Square Joker, and Half Joker.

title: Popcorn
text: Popcorn: Popcorn (Joker). Effect: +20 Mult, -4 Mult per round played. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: ✗ No. Popcorn is a Common +Mult Joker that provides +20 Mult, decreasing by 4 per round. When Popcorn reaches 0 Mult, it is destroyed (denoted by the text "Eaten!").

title: Popcorn
text: Popcorn: The sell value of Popcorn does not depend on its current Mult value, so it is best to sell it at +4 Mult instead of letting it get destroyed. Usage notes: The Non-Perishable challenge bans Popcorn. Decks: Any deck can benefit from Popcorn. However, Plasma Deck benefits the least due to its balancing feature, where Chips are better than Mult. Poker hands: Any poker hand can benefit from Popcorn. Jokers: Throwback benefits Popcorn the most, as it gets stronger when skipping blinds, allowing Popcorn to stay alive for more rounds.

title: Popcorn
text: Popcorn: Trivia: Popcorn is a snack food created from heating up corn kernels to which they expand and eventually pop. The Popcorn joker losing its potency overtime is symbolic of eating the popcorn until it is gone. Popcorn's red background, including the red stripes on the bucket, tie into its ability to provide additive Mult to your score. The text "Eaten!" will flash under Popcorn when it disappears. Popcorn is also a concession snack commonly served at carnivals, circuses, and fairgrounds, which is also a place where clowns and jesters are known to perform. Because Popcorn lasts exactly 5 rounds, the Perishable sticker has no effect on it, as it will disappear immediately before it is set to be debuffed.

title: Popcorn
text: Popcorn: This Joker is part of the group of "Consumable" Jokers that can be destroyed with usage, dubbed "Food Jokers" due to their shared theme. The other Jokers in this group are Ice Cream, Gros Michel, Cavendish, Egg, Seltzer, Turtle Bean, Ramen, and Diet Cola. Popcorn is one of the few "food jokers" to get merch from Makeship in the recently campaigned Food Joker Pin Set alongside Egg and Ice Cream. Popcorn appears on an Ante Up! shirt in a merch collaboration with Fangamer. The two other jokers that appear on the same shirt include Joker and Cavendish.

title: Raised Fist
text: Raised Fist: Raised Fist (Joker). Effect: Adds double the rank of lowest ranked card held in hand to Mult. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: On Held. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Raised Fist is a Common Additive Mult Joker that makes the lowest ranked card held in hand give double its rank in Mult. For face cards it gives +20 Mult, and for Aces it gives +22 Mult.

title: Raised Fist
text: Raised Fist: Since its maximum bonus is +22 Mult, Raised Fist is typically most helpful in the early stages of a run. It often makes way for stronger jokers later on. However, it can remain fairly effective into the mid or late game if the rest of the hand is filled with Steel cards. Usage Notes: In case there are multiple lowest-rank card held in hand, Raised Fist triggers on the rightmost card with that rank.

title: Raised Fist
text: Raised Fist: Because the cards held in hand can be moved around before pressing play, any held cards with an XMult multiplier should be placed to the right of the lowest-ranked card(s) to get the most value. Similarly, if the player holds multiple cards of the lowest rank, and one is debuffed or has a Red Seal, placing the stronger card to the right will yield a better score. Raised Fist provides +0 Mult for debuffed cards. Stone cards do not have a rank and can never trigger Raised Fist. Raised Fist does not give extra Mult from cards upgraded by Hiker. Decks: Five-Card Draw's reduced hand size makes it easier to hold only high-ranked cards.

title: Raised Fist
text: Raised Fist: Decks: Five-Card Draw's reduced hand size makes it easier to hold only high-ranked cards. Poker hands: High Card and Pair allow playing low-value cards without forcing them to be part of the scoring hand. Jokers: Baron multiplies the Mult from Raised Fist if the lowest card is positioned to the left of any held Kings. Mime retriggers Raised Fist because its ability activates on cards held in hand. Stuntman shrinks hand size, making it easier to hold only high-ranked cards, and provides extra Chips to pair with Raised Fist's Mult. Merry Andy also reduces hand size for better card control and offers more discards to remove low-ranked cards.

title: Raised Fist
text: Raised Fist: Merry Andy also reduces hand size for better card control and offers more discards to remove low-ranked cards. Card modifiers: Steel cards multiplies the Mult from Raised Fist if the lowest card is placed to the left of any Steel cards in hand. If the lowest-ranked card itself is Steel, the X1.5 Mult multiplier applies first, which actually results in a lower total score. Red Seals will retrigger Raised Fist if it activates on a card with a Red Seal. Consumables: Strength can be used to raise card ranks. The Hanged Man can remove lower-ranked cards completely, making higher ranks more likely to appear in hand. Death can transform low-ranked cards into higher ones.

title: Raised Fist
text: Raised Fist: Death can transform low-ranked cards into higher ones. The Chariot can turn some cards into Steel cards, which can multiply Raised Fist's Mult. Blinds: The Manacle reduces hand size, making it easier to hold only high-ranked cards. The Hook discards two random cards after playing a hand, which can boost Raised Fist's value if low-value cards are removed. Decks: Painted Deck's larger hand size can make it difficult to hold only high-ranked cards. Poker hands: Five-card hands like Straight and Full House make it harder to control what's left in hand, since no extra non-scoring cards can be included. Jokers: Juggler, Troubadour, and Turtle Bean increase hand size, with which holding only high-ranked cards becomes harder.

title: Raised Fist
text: Raised Fist: Jokers: Juggler, Troubadour, and Turtle Bean increase hand size, with which holding only high-ranked cards becomes harder. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette both increase hand size, which can make holding only high-ranked cards harder. Trivia: The raised fist is an image often linked to socialist or communist movements. It is also a symbol of solidarity and has been used in workers' rights and trade union advocacy. This Joker's effect is a reference to empowering the lower class by amplifying the value of the lowest-ranked card.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Ramen (Joker). Effect: X2 Mult, loses X0.01 Mult per card discarded. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: ✗ No. Ramen is an Uncommon Joker that provides Multiplicative Mult to all hands played. When first acquired, it serves as a middling but unconditional X2 Mult. However, as luck favors the user less and the rounds drag on, this Joker decreases in power, decreasing by X0.01 Mult per card discarded. Ramen cannot maintain or go below X1 Mult; once 100 cards are discarded, it will automatically destroy itself, with the text "Eaten!" flashing on the screen when it does.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: The Mult decrease triggers both on the player's per-round discards and cards discarded by other sources - the latter currently only being The Hook. Ramen will not trigger if the played hand in a round contains a card(s) that did not score, as they are not considered to have been discarded. This Joker's sell value is also never decreased regardless of its current Mult value, so it is advised to sell it once it reaches or goes below around X1.25 Mult, at which point its scoring assistance will be minimal.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Ramen has extremely limited utility past Ante 8 due to its middling base power and reverse power scaling. However, in the absence of another Multiplicative Mult Joker, it can still serve most builds very well. Usage notes: The Non-Perishable challenge bans Ramen. Decks: Green Deck: Perhaps the most obvious synergy exists with this Deck; conserving discards for money gives a mild source of income to compensate for the extra hands required to capitalize on Ramen's power. Blue Deck: The extra hand every round makes it less punishing to play 'throwaway' hands as makeshift discards that also ease a bit of scoring tension, which better preserves this Joker's power.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Nebula Deck: With Ramen skewed more towards easier-to-find hands in desperate need of scaling, the built-in Telescope Voucher this Deck provides makes it a natural choice. All Decks with consistency-based bonuses allow them to form better hands in the absence of discards, which helps make much more out of Ramen than usual. These include the Painted Deck (+2 hand size), the Checkered Deck (only Hearts and Spades), and especially the Abandoned Deck (no face cards), which can very easily leverage the fast scaling of Straights with the Saturn Planet card in tandem with this Joker. Even certain Erratic Deck seeds can lend themselves well to consistently finding high-performing hands.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Poker hands: This Joker works best with weaker hands that can be more reliably made without discarding (or by using a hand as a makeshift discard), such as High Card, Pair, Two Pair, and Three of a Kind. To that end, this will force the player to become more dependent on Planet card scaling than with most other builds, as all these hands are very weak at a baseline. Three of a Kinds should be prioritized if possible, as they have slightly more base + Mult and gain twice as much through Venus as the others do (Pluto, Mercury, and Uranus, respectively).

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Jokers: This Joker is the only Multiplicative Mult Joker that objectively gets weaker over time. On top of its already average X2 Mult multiplier, it is best used in the earlier Antes as a 'transitional' Joker to be used while saving up money to gain more dependable sources of scoring. The following Jokers synergize well with Ramen:

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: The following Jokers synergize well with Ramen: Any Common Joker that can provide consistent shots of + Mult will benefit a build with this Joker greatly, allowing rounds to be solved faster, and as a result, more money to be conserved for longer-term options. Some of the better options include Abstract Joker (which is viable even in the later Antes), Popcorn (itself a temporary addition), and Half Joker, Scholar, and Walkie Talkie (which are all Jokers that can easily be built around while still being strong).

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Banner: Providing +30 Chips to all hands played for each unused discard, these two can cover both sides of the equation with almost any hand in the early game. The -1 discard malus inflicted by Blue Stake and higher makes this a less viable combo in the later difficulties, but it is still worth considering. Blue Joker: Providing +2 Chips to all hands played for each card remaining in the deck, this essentially beats out Banner on the higher Stakes and can go even higher by adding cards to the deck, albeit this is ill-advised in combination with this Joker due to an absolute need for consistency.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Delayed Gratification: This economy Joker rewards the user with $2 for each discard the player has at the end of the round, as long as no discards were used during the round. This can much more quickly help the player access more build stability when combined with the unique property of this Joker. Much like Banner, however, it is far less viable on Blue Stake or higher, as it essentially becomes a Golden Joker with an inconvenient activation condition.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Green Joker: A steady-scaling Additive Mult Joker that gains +1 Mult for every hand played but loses -1 Mult for every discard action (including The Hook). This is the only other anti-discard Joker that ignores the number of remaining discards, making it far more effective on all Stakes. Adding onto this, its Additive Mult pairs extremely well with the Multiplicative Mult this Joker gives, allowing them to comprise a respectable amount of your score alone, even into the late game!

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Burglar: An amazing partner with this Joker, replacing the player's discards with 3 extra hands at the start of the round. This effectively turns Ramen into an X2 Mult with no drawbacks, which, with enough Additive Mult, can serve well even into Ante 8 when it otherwise would not. It also enables synergy with Mystic Summit, which normally has anti-synergy with this Joker, giving a respectable shot of +15 Mult to more easily clear the Blinds. However, it does turn off synergy with Banner and Delayed Gratification, so consider other options if these are key to the current build.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Astronomer: One of the few effect Jokers that Ramen has synergy with, making Planet cards and Celestial Packs in The Shop free. In doing so, it becomes easier to lean on poker hand level scaling in the event that scoring Jokers prove too inaccessible due to bad luck. Space Joker: With each played hand having a 1 in 4 chance to have its level upgraded before scoring, it can serve as a source of long-term scaling, especially while playing the large number of hands per round this Joker encourages. Vouchers: Grabber and its upgraded counterpart, Nacho Tong, provide an extra hand with each acquisition, giving more opportunities to find higher-scoring hands to play.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Telescope guarantees that the Planet card for the most played poker hand will always appear in Celestial Packs. Due to the very low base Mult of High Card, Pair, and Two Pair, this is a good addition to any build keeping Ramen for the long term. For similar reasons, Planet Merchant and Tarot Merchant, as well as their upgraded counterparts Planet Tycoon and Tarot Tycoon, are also possible considerations, albeit not as strongly recommended since they take notable Shop space away from Jokers, which are usually the main source of scoring. Blinds: The Water will always set your discards to 0, making it impossible to decrease Ramen.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Blinds: The Water will always set your discards to 0, making it impossible to decrease Ramen. Amber Acorn: If there are too many Jokers to keep track of otherwise, a single-card discard will trigger Ramen, revealing its location. Crimson Heart: If this blind debuffs Ramen, the player can safely discard without making it lose its value. Decks: Red Deck: This Deck has anti-synergy with this Joker, as it encourages the player to discard more to find better hands. Black Deck makes it very difficult to use Ramen, as it suffers from -1 hand per round. This forces more dependency on discards while disallowing liberal use of 'throwaway' hands.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Similarly, Blast Off makes it even more difficult to use Ramen, as this deck only has 2 hands. This forces much more dependency on discards while disallowing liberal use of 'throwaway' hands. Golden Needle starts with only one hand and 3 extra discards, which means Ramen will rarely see its full value in this deck. Jokers: Drunkard and Merry Andy: The extra discards these two provide are almost useless in a Ramen build, except when considering the potential presence of Banner or Delayed Gratification. Using 3 Joker slots for such a combination can badly dampen scoring, so these two discard giving Jokers should generally be avoided, especially Merry Andy as it decreases hand size.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Faceless Joker, Mail-In Rebate, and Trading Card: These Jokers cannot give their payout unless Ramen gets decreased. Money does lead to better scoring, but the risk of depreciating Mult even a little is huge. Troubadour: While its hand size bonus provides opportunity to more consistently find hands with higher base Mult, it has a debilitating -1 hand per round penalty, meaning it forces more dependency on discards that would weaken this Joker. Burnt Joker: Though a source of much-needed level scaling, it does this through discarding the poker hand in question, which actively worsens Ramen. Castle cannot gain chips if the player doesn't discard.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Castle cannot gain chips if the player doesn't discard. Hit the Road and Yorick: The power of these cards both depends on discarding large quantities of cards, meaning they will both greedily slurp your Ramen right up. Yorick is usually worth keeping over this Joker, however, as it has the potential to reach very high XMult values if acquired early. Mystic Summit has anti-synergy with Ramen unless the player has Burglar, as it wants to get rid of all discards and therefore weaken Ramen. Card modifiers: A card with a Purple Seal needs to be discarded in order to get value from it, which lowers Ramen's Mult.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy: the extra Discards provided by these two vouchers are almost useless in a Ramen build, except when considering the potential presence of Banner or Delayed Gratification. Hieroglyph should be avoided while using this Joker, as its -1 hand per round penalty increases dependence on discards. Blinds: The Hook will cause Ramen to lose X0.02 Mult per hand played, unless hand size is small enough to leave fewer than 2 cards in hand after playing. The Needle sets player's hands to 1 and may force a discard to be used, which lowers Ramen's mult.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: The Needle sets player's hands to 1 and may force a discard to be used, which lowers Ramen's mult. Trivia: Ramen is a popular Japanese noodle dish consisting of Chinese-style wheat noodles served in a flavorful, savory broth and topped with ingredients like sliced meats, seaweed, and vegetables. This Joker is part of the group of "Consumable" Jokers that can be destroyed with usage, dubbed "Food Jokers" due to their shared theme. The other Jokers in this group are Ice Cream, Popcorn, Gros Michel, Cavendish, Egg, Seltzer, Turtle Bean, and Diet Cola.

title: Ramen
text: Ramen: Of the five Food Jokers that scale down, Ramen is the only Joker that can avoid being scaled down throughout a run. The others are scaled down after hands are played or rounds are passed, both of which are necessary for progress.

title: Red Card
text: Red Card: Red Card (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains +3 Mult when any Booster Pack is skipped, (Currently +0 Mult). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Red Card is a Common scaling Additive Mult Joker that gains +3 Mult every time any Booster Pack is skipped by the player pressing the "Skip" button in the Booster Pack. It does not retroactively count the player's skipped Booster Packs before it was purchased and always begins at +0 Mult. Only Booster Packs purchased at the Shop or obtained through tags afterwards add to this multiplier. Mega Booster Packs are only able to trigger this Joker once per pack, allowing the player to pick up the first card and skip the second to trigger Red Card.

title: Red Card
text: Red Card: Decks: Anaglyph Deck can build up many tags, then copy any tag that gives a Mega Booster Pack. Green Deck encourages the player to spend money as they earn it, which works well with Red Card. In Typecast, after Ante 4, Buffoon Packs will continue to spawn in the shop despite it being impossible to take Jokers from them. Red Card can be used to extract value from what would otherwise be a wasted booster slot. Jokers: Red Card synergizes well with most economy Jokers that provide money, like Business Card or Rocket. Astronomer can provide free Celestial Packs that can be used to scale. Hallucination can allow you to still get tarot cards even while skipping packs.

title: Red Card
text: Red Card: Hallucination can allow you to still get tarot cards even while skipping packs. Vouchers: Clearance Sale and Liquidation lower the price of booster packs, making it easier to purchase and skip more. Hieroglyph and Petroglyph send the player back an Ante at the cost of -1 Hand and -1 Discard respectively, allowing them to open more booster packs to skip. Tags: Skipping for these Tags works best when the player is on the Anaglyph Deck or has taken lots of Diet Colas. Standard Tag, Charm Tag, Meteor Tag and Buffoon Tag all give access to Mega Booster Packs, which can be used by taking 1 card, then skipping to scale Red Card.

title: Red Card
text: Red Card: Ethereal Tag gives access to a Spectral Pack, which can optionally be skipped to scale Red Card. Anti-Synergies: There are a lot of Jokers that, when combined with Red Card, leave the player in a dilemma between whether to scale Red Card or whether to scale the other joker. However, it is worth emphasizing again that skipping a Booster Pack specifically to scale up Red Card (instead of skipping a Booster Pack that already had very little value) might not be a good idea. Moreover, it is debatable whether these are true anti-synergies (rather than complements), since pairing the Red Card with any of these lessens the punishment of opening Booster Packs that don't have what you want:

title: Red Card
text: Red Card: Jokers that care about Tarot cards, such as Fortune Teller, Driver's License, and Vampire. Jokers such as Steel Joker and Lucky Cat, which care about specific Tarot cards. Jokers that care about Planet cards, such as Constellation and Satellite. As for Standard Packs (and Spectral Packs in some cases), one would face a choice between scaling Hologram and Red Card — choose the one that increases the score more. Some other dilemmas: Jokers that care about the base Mult of a played hand, such as Bloodstone, can lose out on the scaling provided by planets that the player skipped to scale Red Card. Skipping blinds for Throwback means fewer packs to open. However, some skip tags themselves give Booster Packs.

title: Red Card
text: Red Card: Skipping blinds for Throwback means fewer packs to open. However, some skip tags themselves give Booster Packs. Vouchers: The Telescope voucher can make skipping Celestial Pack undesirable.

title: Red Card
text: Red Card: Vouchers: The Telescope voucher can make skipping Celestial Pack undesirable. Strategies: When playing with Red Card, it's better not to skip Booster Packs specifically just to scale the Red Card. Opening a Booster Pack is more like rolling for a chance to get a good item — Booster Packs are not guaranteed to provide value, and the player would skip many Booster Packs anyway due to not getting a card that is sufficiently valuable. What Red Card does is that it provides +3 Mult in all of the cases where the player would have skipped anyway, so it is better to think of Red Card as an additional Booster Pack slot and to only skip if none of the options are better than +3 mult.

title: Red Card
text: Red Card: For instance, with 9 Planet cards available at the beginning of a run and three of those being visible in a regular Celestial Pack, assuming no Telescope, there is only a 1 in 3 chance for a Celestial Pack to contain the Planet card that one actually wants. The other two-thirds of the time, the player would just skip or take a Planet card of an undesirable hand, gaining little to no value out of it. But with the Red Card, the player would get a minimum of +3 Mult — it might be more reasonable to think of it as a fourth Planet card that gives +3 Mult for every hand (assuming no XMult triggered on played or held cards).

title: Red Card
text: Red Card: If the player opens a Mega Booster Pack, the player can still use the first card and then skip to scale up Red Card. Trivia: A red card in sports is usually used to signal a large penalty, often for some kind of rule infraction. In most forms of association football, for example, a red card signals that a player must leave the pitch after causing a foul or acting unsportsmanlike, causing their team to be one player short for the rest of the match.

title: Red Card
text: Red Card: A red card may also refer to a bright red plastic card used in blackjack, where the player inserts the card in the middle of the deck after the dealer shuffles it to mark where the deck should be cut.

title: Reserved Parking
text: Reserved Parking: Reserved Parking (Joker). Effect: Each face card held in hand has a 1 in 2 chance to give $1. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Economy. Activation: On Held. Probability-Based: Yes. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Reserved Parking is a Common Economy Joker that has a 1 in 2 chance to provide $1 for each face card held in hand after a hand is played. Cards which are discarded or debuffed by certain Blinds do not trigger this effect.

title: Reserved Parking
text: Reserved Parking: Usage Notes: Reserved Parking rolls a 1 in 2 on each face card held in hand, so the expected value per face card per hand is $0.5. Mime and Red Seals will only attempt to retrigger this effect if the initial roll was successful. As a result, one retrigger will raise the expected value to $0.75 per card per hand, and two retriggers raises the expected value to $1.

title: Reserved Parking
text: Reserved Parking: If the player also already has another held in hand effect that triggers on every hand, like Baron, Shoot the Moon or Steel cards, then Mime and Red Seals will always retrigger this effect, and therefore this card. As a result, Reserved Parking can be retriggered even if the initial roll was unsuccessful. In this case, one retrigger raises expected value to $1 per hand, two retriggers raises expected value to $1.5. Decks: Painted Deck's larger hand size potentially allows for Reserved Parking to activate more often. Blue Deck’s extra hand allows for more hands that can be used to yield money and dig for face cards.

title: Reserved Parking
text: Reserved Parking: Blue Deck’s extra hand allows for more hands that can be used to yield money and dig for face cards. Mad World starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which makes it so that all cards are considered face cards, causing Reserved Parking to potentially activate on all cards held in hand. Poker hands: Since it's best to keep as many face cards in hand as possible, smaller hands like High Card and Pair work well. Jokers: Oops! All 6s guarantees that Reserved Parking will trigger. Mime retriggers all card held in abilities, including Reserved Parking’s effect. Pareidolia makes it so that all cards are considered face cards, causing Reserved Parking to potentially activate on all cards held in hand.

title: Reserved Parking
text: Reserved Parking: Shoot the Moon also wants the player to keep face cards (Queen) in hand. Baron also wants the player to keep face cards (King) in hand. Ride the Bus also does not want to play face cards. Note that having these 2 jokers at the same time can be very dangerous, as there's a small chance of drawing a hand of only face cards. Juggler and Troubadour increase hand size, allowing the player to hold more cards in hand. Burglar gives 3 extra hands, allowing more chances for Reserved Parking to give more money. Modifiers: Gold cards also generate money for holding in hand. Steel cards give X1.5 Mult for holding in hand.

title: Reserved Parking
text: Reserved Parking: Modifiers: Gold cards also generate money for holding in hand. Steel cards give X1.5 Mult for holding in hand. Red Seals retrigger face cards held in hand for an extra chance to generate money. Blue Seals on face cards allow them to generate Planet cards while held in hand. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette can increase hand size, allowing more face cards to held at once. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Medusa start with no face cards, meaning Reserved Parking Joker is useless. Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle all have fewer hands to be used for yielding money. Five-Card Draw does not work well with this Joker due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers.

title: Reserved Parking
text: Reserved Parking: Poker hands: Five-card hands like Flush, Straight or Full House leaves fewer cards held in hand so it doesn't benefit Reserved Parking much. Jokers: Merry Andy and Stuntman reduce hand sizes, which means the player hold less face cards. Faceless Joker encourages discarding lots of face cards. Canio encourages destroying face cards. Business Card encourages playing face cards instead, although this could actually be a synergy if the player has a lot of face cards in the deck or Pareidolia. Blinds and Antes: The Plant debuffs all face cards, rendering Reserved Parking useless.

title: Reserved Parking
text: Reserved Parking: Blinds and Antes: The Plant debuffs all face cards, rendering Reserved Parking useless. Trivia: This Joker was cut from the second Demo, being only present in a specialized version for the Jimbo Invitational Tournament. Instead of the 1 in 2 chance, it was guaranteed to give $1 per face card held in hand. The artwork for this Joker may have been inspired by this "Reserved Parking for Law Enforcement Officer" sign, or one similar to it. This Joker's sprite art has the least amount of unique colors out of every Joker, having a total of two unique colors.

title: Reserved Parking
text: Reserved Parking: Reserved parking is a parking space that is reserved for someone important or to people who bought a special pass. An unpermitted person using a reserved parking space usually results in their vehicle being towed and them being given a ticket. This is reflected by the Joker's ability to give every face card held in hand a 1 in 2 chance to grant $1, as if the cards are being fined for taking up space.

title: Ride the Bus
text: Ride the Bus: Ride the Bus (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains +1 Mult per consecutive hand played without a scoring face card, (Currently +0 Mult). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Ride the Bus is a Common Joker that provides a slow but steady source of scaling Mult. It starts at +0 Mult and gains +1 Mult added for every hand played without a scoring face card, and it resets to +0 Mult if a face card is scored.

title: Ride the Bus
text: Ride the Bus: Acquiring it early and carefully avoiding scoring face cards will lead to a high amount of Mult in the late game, especially if an Edition like Polychrome can be applied to it. Face cards can be played safely as long as they do not score. For example, playing an Ace and a Queen will not count as playing a face card (because it is an Ace High Card). Playing a hand with debuffed face cards also does not reset Ride the Bus. Usage notes: The 15 Minute City challenge starts the player with an Eternal copy of Ride the Bus. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Medusa start with no face cards, so this Joker will almost never reset.

title: Ride the Bus
text: Ride the Bus: Decks: Abandoned Deck and Medusa start with no face cards, so this Joker will almost never reset. Blue Deck gives +1 hands every round, allowing for more scaling per round. Poker Hands: Any hand will work with this Joker. However, the smaller the hand type, the better Ride the Bus is. This makes it ideal for High Card or Pair builds, while Straights and Flushes builds can be more difficult. Jokers: Jokers whose effects trigger based on numbered cards can be more useful, such as Even Steven, Odd Todd, Fibonacci, and Hack. Canio scales greatly from destroying face cards, thus both thinning the deck and providing a significant XMult to complement the additive Mult of Ride the Bus.

title: Ride the Bus
text: Ride the Bus: Though, Canio encourages adding face cards to the deck in order to destroy them, which can make it harder to work around Ride the Bus. Trading Card can destroy face cards, making it easier for the player to avoid resetting Ride the Bus. Burglar adds 3 extra hands and removes all discards, allowing Ride The Bus to scale faster. However, missing out on discards can be dangerous, as the player might be forced to reset Ride The Bus. It is especially important to remove face cards from the deck when running Burglar and Ride the Bus.

title: Ride the Bus
text: Ride the Bus: Blinds: The Plant, The Goad, The Head, The Club, The Window, The Pillar, Verdant Leaf: When face cards are debuffed, it's safe to play them without resetting Ride The Bus. Crimson Heart: If Ride The Bus gets disabled, it's safe to play a hand with face cards. Consumables: Strength can help turn your Kings into Aces, and reduce your face cards in the deck. Death and The Hanged Man can help remove some face cards in the deck. The Tower can turn face cards into Stone cards and reduce your face cards in your deck.

title: Ride the Bus
text: Ride the Bus: The Tower can turn face cards into Stone cards and reduce your face cards in your deck. Incantation, Grim, and Cryptid can add non-face cards to your deck, lessening the chance of drawing face cards. Not only that, the former two might also destroy a face card as well. Immolate can destroy face cards. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong give additional hands per round, allowing Ride The Bus to scale even higher. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle all have poor synergy with Ride the Bus due to their number of reduced hands.

title: Ride the Bus
text: Ride the Bus: Mad World doesn't work with Ride the Bus, as this Deck starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which means Ride the Bus will never scale or gain + Mult. X-ray Vision randomly flips cards, which can cause players to accidentally play a face card. Jokers: Pareidolia will ruin Ride the Bus' multiplier as soon as any hand is played. Splash can trigger a face card that otherwise would have done nothing. The following Jokers' effects rely on scoring face cards, meaning they cannot be utilized without resetting Ride the Bus. Business Card Midas Mask Photograph Scary Face Smiley Face Sock and Buskin Triboulet

title: Ride the Bus
text: Ride the Bus: Business Card Midas Mask Photograph Scary Face Smiley Face Sock and Buskin Triboulet Baron and Hit the Road require a lot of face cards in the deck to work well, which does not synergize with Ride the Bus. Blinds: The following Boss Blinds flip cards, which can cause players to accidentally play a face card: The House The Wheel The Fish Cerulean Bell can force a face card to be picked. If you don't have any discards and you can't play at least a Ace or a numbered pair, Ride The Bus will be forced to lose its mult. Consumables: Familiar adds face cards to the deck and might destroy a non-face card while at it.

title: Ride the Bus
text: Ride the Bus: Consumables: Familiar adds face cards to the deck and might destroy a non-face card while at it. Trivia: According to LocalThunk, the name of the card is a reference to the drinking game Ride the Bus. A bus usually keeps driving until it has to stop to pick up passengers. In Balatro, the face cards — Jacks, Queens, and Kings — represent people, and the "Route 210-A" could be read as allowing cards 2-10 and Ace to continue onward. The design of this Joker is based on a bus stop sign near LocalThunk's apartment in Regina, Saskatchewan, Canada.

title: Ride the Bus
text: Ride the Bus: The design of this Joker is based on a bus stop sign near LocalThunk's apartment in Regina, Saskatchewan, Canada. During the first demo, Ride the Bus provided +2 Mult per consecutive hand played without scoring face cards, making it as strong as Spare Trousers without any hand requirement. Upon release, it was nerfed to only provide +1 Mult for balancing purposes. On the artwork of Rocket, inside the rocket itself, there is a person that is similar to the one that appears on the artwork for Ride the Bus.

title: Riff-Raff
text: Riff-Raff: Riff-Raff (Joker). Effect: When Blind is selected, create 2 Common Jokers, (Must have room). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: On Blind Select. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Riff-Raff is a Common Effect Joker that generates up to two more Common Jokers whenever a Blind is selected, as long as there is space in the player's Joker slots. If the player has no room, Riff-Raff will not generate anything (except in certain scenarios as seen in the interactions section).

title: Riff-Raff
text: Riff-Raff: Usage Notes: Notable interactions with other Jokers/game mechanics include: Jokers generated by Riff-Raff can potentially come with Editions, including Negative. When playing on higher Stakes, Riff-Raff will not create Jokers with in-run Stickers, such as the Rental sticker. Jokers generated during the Non-Perishable will still receive an Eternal sticker. Riff-Raff is able to spawn Cavendish as long as Gros Michel went extinct (destroyed itself) earlier in the run. Riff-Raff can create Jokers that are undiscovered in the player's collection. When the player possesses Showman, Riff-Raff can create a second Riff-Raff.

title: Riff-Raff
text: Riff-Raff: When the player possesses Showman, Riff-Raff can create a second Riff-Raff. If all Joker slots are currently filled when the Blind is selected, and then Ceremonial Dagger consumes a Joker, Riff-Raff will create another Joker, as long as it's on the right of Ceremonial Dagger. If all Joker slots are currently filled when the Blind is selected, and either Ceremonial Dagger or Madness destroys a Negative Joker, Riff-Raff will be able to create a non-Negative Joker. This is similar to selling a Negative Invisible Joker, which leads to a -1 Joker Slot situation. Decks: Black Deck works well with Riff-Raff, as it gives an additional Joker slot at the cost of losing a hand.

title: Riff-Raff
text: Riff-Raff: Similarly, Five-Card Draw works even better with Riff-Raff, as it gives two additional Joker slots at the cost of only having a hand size of 5. On a Knife's Edge starts with an Eternal, Pinned Ceremonial Dagger, which means Riff-Raff can provide disposable Jokers to feed the Dagger. Make sure to keep a disposable Joker in between them so Riff-Raff can be kept after selecting a blind. Poker hands: Since Riff-Raff is a utility Joker, it does not have specific synergy with any hand. Jokers: Ceremonial Dagger: By providing free fodder to feed it, this Joker can scale its +Mult much more reliably. Campfire: Similarly, having free Jokers to sell allows Campfire to scale easily.

title: Riff-Raff
text: Riff-Raff: Campfire: Similarly, having free Jokers to sell allows Campfire to scale easily. Abstract Joker: Riff-Raff ensures the player's Joker slots are filled, so it makes it easy to get +Mult for Abstract Joker. Gros Michel: If the player is lucky enough to get this Joker from Riff-Raff, it can be a good way to get the powerful Cavendish later. Due to the random nature of Riff-Raff, it has the potential to either have great or poor synergy with the player's other Jokers depending on what Common Jokers it provides. Vouchers: Purchasing Blank and then Antimatter gives the player an additional Joker slot, which could be beneficial for Riff-Raff.

title: Riff-Raff
text: Riff-Raff: Vouchers: Purchasing Blank and then Antimatter gives the player an additional Joker slot, which could be beneficial for Riff-Raff. Decks: Painted Deck reduces Joker slots by one, making it harder to have extra space for Riff-Raff to spawn Jokers. Similarly, Cruelty reduces Joker slots by two, making it even harder to have extra space for Riff-Raff to spawn Jokers. Non-Perishable makes it very risky to use Riff-Raff, as it spawns Eternal Common Jokers on this deck. Jokers: Joker Stencil: Since Riff-Raff constantly adds Jokers, it reduces the XMult it can get. Swashbuckler: Common Jokers generally don't have a high selling value, so they will add less +Mult to Swashbuckler.

title: Riff-Raff
text: Riff-Raff: Swashbuckler: Common Jokers generally don't have a high selling value, so they will add less +Mult to Swashbuckler. Baseball Card: This Joker only scales its XMult from owning Uncommon Jokers, meaning the Jokers provided by Riff-Raff are useless to it. Trivia: The word riff-raff (sometimes spelled as riffraff) has the meaning of "people with a bad reputation or of the common class", which is fitting in how Riff-Raff only creates Common Jokers. The exact depiction of the Joker/Jimbo on the card art of this joker can also be found on the top right corner of the Baseball Card, while a slightly different version is in the center of Seltzer.

title: Riff-Raff
text: Riff-Raff: Riff-Raff will always say "+1 Joker" even if it generates 2 Jokers. This seems to be a visual bug.

title: Rocket
text: Rocket: Rocket (Joker). Effect: Earn $1 at end of round. Payout increases by $2 when Boss Blind is defeated. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Economy. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Rocket is an Uncommon scaling Economy Joker that gives $1 at the end of every round, and the payout increases by $2 upon defeating a Boss Blind.

title: Rocket
text: Rocket: Usage notes: The increment for defeating a Boss Blind is added before it pays out for the end of that round. The Omelette challenge bans Rocket. The Blast Off challenge starts the player with an Eternal copy of Rocket. Jokers: Bootstraps increases its Mult provided as players have more money. Bull increases its Chips provided as players have more money. Decks: Painted Deck and Cruelty: The reduced Joker slots makes it difficult to carry Rocket since players may need more scoring Jokers to survive and beat Ante 8. Anaglyph Deck: As the player ideally wants to avoid skipping to make use of Rocket's payout at the end of the round, this Deck has a slight anti-synergy with it.

title: Rocket
text: Rocket: Jokers: Throwback: Skipping Blinds is less than ideal for most Economy Jokers, to which Rocket is no exception. Blinds: If Crimson Heart disables Rocket upon playing a winning hand, it will not gain $2 nor any accumulated money upon cashing out. Trivia: Unlike other space-themed jokers such as Constellation or Astronomer, Rocket has no effect on Planet cards or hand levels. The artwork of this Joker shows someone inside the rocket, which is pretty similar to the person that appears on the artwork of Ride the Bus. In other media: The rocket from this joker, alongside all non-secret planet cards, are referenced in Vampire Survivors, specifically in a weapon called the "Celestial Booster."

title: Rocket
text: Rocket: The Negative depiction of the rocket is referenced in another weapon from the game, the Negative Space, which is the evolved version of the Celestial Booster.

title: Rough Gem
text: Rough Gem: Rough Gem (Joker). Effect: Played cards with Diamond suit earn $1 when scored. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Have at least 30 cards with Diamond suit in your deck. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Economy. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Rough Gem is an Uncommon Diamonds-oriented Economy Joker which gives the player $1 for each Diamond scored.

title: Rough Gem
text: Rough Gem: Usage Notes: Unlike unlocking Arrowhead and Bloodstone, fulfilling the condition of 30 Diamond cards in a Deck is trickier, as it doesn't allow for an easy strategy such as using the Checkered Deck for the aforementioned Jokers. Magic Deck starts the player with two copies of The Fool, allowing for easier Deck manipulation early on by finding The Star or Death. Any Jokers that synergize with Flush builds are likely to be useful during the unlock attempt, such as Droll Joker, Crafty Joker, and The Tribe. Economy Jokers are likely to be beneficial to find more Tarots for Deck manipulation, such as Mail-In Rebate and Golden Joker.

title: Rough Gem
text: Rough Gem: While Smeared Joker allows Heart cards to count as Diamonds for the purpose of scoring, those cards do not count as Diamonds for the purpose of unlocking the joker. This also applies to non-diamond Wild cards. Poker hands: Any Flush-type hand with Diamonds benefits from Rough Gem, those being: Flush Straight Flush Flush House Flush Five Jokers: Greedy Joker provides a small boost in Mult for scoring Diamond cards, which may be useful as Rough Gem does not directly increase scoring power. Bull and Bootstraps directly benefit as they gain scoring power based on the player's current Money. Jokers that require a steady Economy to scale efficiently such as Flash Card and Red Card also benefit substantially.

title: Rough Gem
text: Rough Gem: Jokers that require a steady Economy to scale efficiently such as Flash Card and Red Card also benefit substantially. As Rough Gem produces money mid-round, it works very well with To the Moon, as the money produced counts towards interest earned at the end of the round. Any Retrigger Joker will synergize with Rough Gem as it allows the player to earn more Money. Dusk, Hack, Seltzer, Sock and Buskin, or Hanging Chad. Smeared Joker allows all Heart cards to count as Diamonds for scoring, letting Rough Gem work on more cards. Lusty Joker and Bloodstone may be useful in this context, as Rough Gem does not provide direct scoring power.

title: Rough Gem
text: Rough Gem: Lusty Joker and Bloodstone may be useful in this context, as Rough Gem does not provide direct scoring power. Splash can occasionally be useful, as the scoring of an additional Diamond that wouldn't otherwise score is extra Money. However, the player ideally would be playing Flushes, which Splash is useless for. Consumables: The Star can turn some non-Diamond cards into Diamond cards allowing the player to see Diamond cards easier and generate more money. The Lovers can turn some non-Diamond cards into Wild cards which trigger Rough Gem. Death can turn some non-Diamond cards into Diamond cards The Hanged Man can remove some non-Diamond cards.

title: Rough Gem
text: Rough Gem: Death can turn some non-Diamond cards into Diamond cards The Hanged Man can remove some non-Diamond cards. Deja Vu can apply Red Seals onto Diamond cards allowing Rough Gem to generate more money. Decks: Checkered Deck cannot benefit from Rough Gem without adding Diamonds to the deck. Jokers: While Four Fingers can make Flushes easier to play, it enables the player to do so with less overall cards, therefore Rough Gem will generate less money if the player opts for a 4-card Diamond Flush. It may be suitable to hunt for Planet cards and/or scaling Mult Jokers if Four Fingers must remain in conjunction with Rough Gem.

title: Rough Gem
text: Rough Gem: Blinds: The Window will debuff all Diamond cards, meaning Rough Gem cannot give any Money. The Pillar can be detrimental as previously played Diamond cards will not be able to score, earning no Money. Trivia: Rough Gem is one of four stone/mineral themed Jokers unlocked by having 30 cards of that suit in your deck. The others are Arrowhead (Spades), Bloodstone (Hearts), and Onyx Agate (Clubs). The effect of the Joker giving money could connect it to Greedy Joker, the other Joker pertaining only to Diamonds.

title: Runner
text: Runner: Runner (Joker). Effect: Gains +15 Chips if played hand contains a Straight, (Currently +0 Chips). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Runner is a Common scaling Chips Joker that adds Chips to played hands. The amount of Chips added begins at +0 and is permanently increased by +15 when the player plays a hand that contains a Straight (including Straight Flush and Royal Flush).

title: Runner
text: Runner: Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World both have fewer cards than the standard Deck, making it easier to locate specific cards for Straights. Painted Deck with its increased Hand Size, can make Straights easier to form with more cards held in hand. Plasma Deck significantly benefits from early Chips value. This makes Runner an easy choice for the early to mid game, although it can be carried into late game if the player builds around Straights. 15 Minute City starts with an Eternal Shortcut, which allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand. Poker hands: Straight, Straight Flush, and Royal Flush are recommended to scale Runner consistently.

title: Runner
text: Runner: Poker hands: Straight, Straight Flush, and Royal Flush are recommended to scale Runner consistently. Jokers: Shortcut allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand. Four Fingers allows Straights to be scored with only four cards instead of the usual five, making it easier to get that hand. The Order will give X3 Mult as long as the played hand contains a Straight, making it a strong partner with Runner for both scaling Chips and XMult. Crazy Joker gives +12 Mult on Straights, being especially useful to increase Mult during the early game. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong give additional hands, allowing Runner to scale faster.

title: Runner
text: Runner: Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong give additional hands, allowing Runner to scale faster. Wasteful and Recyclomancy give additional discards, allowing the player to search for Straight hands easier. Paint Brush and Palette both increase hand size, which can help players with forming Straights. Telescope can help upgrade Straight using Saturn. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle all have poor synergy with Runner due to their reduced number of hands. Erratic Deck can make it difficult to use Runner as the randomized rank and suit makes it harder to form Straights. Five-Card Draw's -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straights.

title: Runner
text: Runner: Five-Card Draw's -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straights. Jokers: Jokers that reduce hand size, like Stuntman and Merry Andy, have anti-synergy with Runner, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Consumables: Ectoplasm and Ouija have anti-synergy with Runner, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Not only that, but Ouija converts all cards held in hand into one single rank, which makes assembling Straights less consistent. Blinds: The Manacle's -1 hand size makes it hard to assemble Straights. The Water will always start with 0 discards, making it very hard to assemble Straights.

title: Runner
text: Runner: The Water will always start with 0 discards, making it very hard to assemble Straights. The Eye will only allow the player to play any given Poker Hand once, limiting the scaling opportunities for Runner. Trivia: This is the only Chip Joker that scales by playing a hand of a specific type; in this case, Straights (which can include Straight Flushes). Its counterpart, Spare Trousers, scale its +Mult by playing hands that contain Two Pairs. The runner's ID number, #345, is itself a (short) Straight. The name is a reference to how in some games, straights are called "runs".

title: Satellite
text: Satellite: Satellite (Joker). Effect: Earn $1 at end of round per unique Planet card used this run. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Have at least $400. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Economy. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Satellite is an Uncommon Economy Joker that gives $1 at the end of each round per unique Planet card used in the run. Players can earn up to $9 from it by using the normal Planet cards, and an additional $3 can be earned in a run by playing the three secret hands.

title: Satellite
text: Satellite: To unlock this Joker, the player must reach $400 in a run. This Joker shares an unlock requirement with the Nest Egg achievement. Each planet card only needs to be used once in a run to count for Satellite. Black Hole is a Spectral card, and will not increase the $ gained from Satellite, even if opened from within a Celestial booster pack. Usage Notes: Without a steady Economy, unlocking Satellite may prove to be a difficult task. The Yellow Deck is a decent choice for the run to unlock Satellite as it starts the player with an extra $10, earning the player Interest from defeating the first Blind of the run, and setting up for further Economic gain.

title: Satellite
text: Satellite: Another option is to choose the Anaglyph Deck, save up the Double Tags until hitting a money-giving Tag such as Investment Tag, Economy Tag or Handy Tag, then skip for a massive profit. Economy Jokers such as Golden Joker, Mail-In Rebate, etc. are directly helpful in reaching the unlock condition. The Bull and Bootstraps Jokers both gain scoring power relative to the player's Money, which would be useful to have in a run that attempts to unlock Satellite as hoarding Money to reach $400 will also give it scoring power. Egg and Gift Card add sell value, making it possible to hold onto the Egg or a useless Joker/Consumable to sell later for a substantial boost in Money.

title: Satellite
text: Satellite: Swashbuckler would quantify the sell value into Mult, which may help the player continue the run. To the Moon, Seed Money, and Money Tree allow the player to earn more Interest, which may contribute to reaching the unlock condition faster. All 3 of these combined allow for the player to earn a maximum of $40 from Interest alone, merely one-tenth of the required amount. The Omelette challenge bans Satellite. Decks: Checkered Deck works well with Satellite as it requires fewer Deck modifications to unlock the secret Poker hands. Erratic Deck may require no Deck modifications at all to unlock the secret Poker hands.

title: Satellite
text: Satellite: Erratic Deck may require no Deck modifications at all to unlock the secret Poker hands. Poker hands: Playing the three secret hands (Flush House, Five of a Kind and Flush Five) to unlock their planets allows players to maximize this Joker's value. Jokers: Since Satellite is maximized through the use of Planet cards, it synergizes with Constellation, which gains X0.1 Mult per planet card used. Satellite benefits from Astronomer, which makes planet cards and Celestial booster packs free. Smeared Joker can make it much easier to unlock the secret hands, thereby maximizing Satellite's value. Consumables: The High Priestess can potentially spawn Planet cards not yet used by the player if found early, boosting Satellite.

title: Satellite
text: Satellite: Consumables: The High Priestess can potentially spawn Planet cards not yet used by the player if found early, boosting Satellite. Vouchers: Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon increase the frequency of planet cards in the shop, making it easier to find different planet cards. Jokers: Showman can have anti-synergy with Satellite, since it will allow duplicate planet cards to appear, and Satellite requires unique planet cards. Vouchers: Telescope can make it harder to achieve max rewards with Satellite, as it lends itself to the same planet card repeating. This innately applies to the Nebula Deck as it starts with the Telescope Voucher.

title: Satellite
text: Satellite: This innately applies to the Nebula Deck as it starts with the Telescope Voucher. Trivia: In real life, satellites (also known as "artificial satellites" or "orbiters") are used to collect data and relay signals about the planet it orbits. This plays into the Joker's main effect of rewarding money for each unique planet "discovered" by obtaining their card. Although there have been many satellites sent to orbit other planets, most of them have been retired due to lost contact. Currently, the only planets that have active artificial satellites are Earth and Mars, which is why the art of the Joker depicts a satellite above a planet that resembles Earth.

title: Satellite
text: Satellite: Satellite is a space-themed Joker, continuing the space theme of Jokers like Supernova, Constellation, Astronomer, and Space Joker.

title: Scary Face
text: Scary Face: Scary Face (Joker). Effect: Played face cards give +30 Chips when scored. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Scary Face is a Common Chips Joker that adds +30 Chips for each scored face card in a hand.

title: Scary Face
text: Scary Face: Decks: Red Deck’s extra discard can be used to dig for more face cards in the player’s deck. Painted Deck has a larger hand size, allowing for more face cards to appear. However, the -1 Joker slot means Scary Face may not be as viable as some other options. Plasma Deck can use the large influx of Chips to win a large number of early hands, allowing one to search for better Jokers easier. Mad World starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which causes Scary Face to trigger on all played cards.

title: Scary Face
text: Scary Face: Mad World starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which causes Scary Face to trigger on all played cards. Poker hands: Scary Face requires face cards (King, Queen, and Jack) to trigger, so hands with more face cards in them will allow Scary Face to award more Chips. For example, a Full House consisting of K K K Q Q will trigger Scary Face five times. Jokers: If the first card of the hand is a face card, Hanging Chad will cause Scary Face to trigger thrice, giving +90 Chips. Pareidolia causes Scary Face to trigger on all played cards, effectively making every card a Bonus card. Sock and Buskin will add an additional +30 Chips per face card scored.

title: Scary Face
text: Scary Face: Sock and Buskin will add an additional +30 Chips per face card scored. Triboulet provides a Mult multiplier for each played King or Queen. Business Card gives each face card played a 50% chance to provide $2 when scored. Smiley Face provides additional Mult for each face card played. Splash allows non-scoring cards to trigger Scary Face (by making them score). Decks: Abandoned Deck and Medusa are not recommended due to lack of face cards. Jokers: Baron, Shoot the Moon, Hit the Road and Reserved Parking encourage not playing face cards. Ride the Bus actively punishes playing face cards. Canio's ability activates only upon destroying face cards, resulting in fewer cards able to trigger Scary Face.

title: Scary Face
text: Scary Face: Canio's ability activates only upon destroying face cards, resulting in fewer cards able to trigger Scary Face. Blinds: The Plant will debuff all face cards, meaning Scary Face Joker cannot trigger. Trivia: Scary Face is one of three "spooky" Jokers that came as a part of a pin set alongside Mr. Bones and Madness as a merch collab between LocalThunk and Makeship. The art of this card in pre-release had the art span the whole card, without the border.

title: Scholar
text: Scholar: Scholar (Joker). Effect: Played Aces give +20 Chips and +4 Mult when scored. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips and Additive Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Scholar is a Common Chips and Additive Mult Joker which gives +20 Chips and +4 Mult per Ace scored.

title: Scholar
text: Scholar: Decks: Abandoned Deck can reliably find Aces more often due to the smaller deck size. Blue Deck and Red Deck give an extra hand or discard respectively, allowing for more opportunities to dig for Aces. Poker hands: Any Poker hand containing Aces can be valuable to Scholar. Jokers: Fibonacci gives you +8 Mult per Ace. Odd Todd adds +31 Chips per Ace. Aces do not have a retrigger Joker associated with their rank. However, Hanging Chad, Dusk and Seltzer (and Sock and Buskin if Pareidolia is owned) can still be used to trigger Aces multiple times. DNA can copy an Ace every first hand. Superposition creates a Tarot card if the played hand is a Straight which contains an Ace.

title: Scholar
text: Scholar: Superposition creates a Tarot card if the played hand is a Straight which contains an Ace. Trading Card can help thin the deck out, so you can draw Aces more reliably. Any jokers requiring multiples of the same rank cards like The Trio, Zany Joker, etc.. Consumables: The Hanged Man and Immolate can be used to thin out the deck and make Aces easier to find. Death, Strength and Cryptid can all be used to make Aces. Aura can add the Foil, Holographic, or Polychrome edition to an Ace, making the Chips or Mult bonus even stronger. Deja Vu can add a Red Seal to Aces and allow Scholar to trigger them multiple times.

title: Scholar
text: Scholar: Deja Vu can add a Red Seal to Aces and allow Scholar to trigger them multiple times. Grim adds two enhanced Aces to the deck in exchange for destroying a random card. Decks: 15 Minute City and Mad World are not recommended, as these decks don't contain any Aces by default. Trivia: The A+ mark is reminiscent of a teacher marking their student's homework with a red ballpoint pen. The original design for Scholar differs heavily from the modern day version, solely featuring the words "The A" on it. It is currently unknown what this is a reference to, if anything.

title: Scholar
text: Scholar: The effect triggering upon scoring an ace may be a reference to the verb "ace," which means to get perfect marks on something. Scholar's sprite is missing a pixel on the "E" in the Top Left "Joker" label and on the "K" in the Bottom Right label. There are two Scholar sprites in the game files: one with shading on the hair and one without. Scholar is one of only two Jokers to provide both Chips and Mult buff to scored cards, the other being Walkie Talkie.

title: Seeing Double
text: Seeing Double: Seeing Double (Joker). Effect: X2 Mult if played hand has a scoring Club card and a scoring card of any other suit. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Play a hand that contains four 7 of Clubs. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Seeing Double is an Uncommon Multiplicative Mult Joker that gives X2 Mult when a hand is scored with one Club card and any other suit card. Seeing Double will not activate if all Club cards or all non Club cards are debuffed.

title: Seeing Double
text: Seeing Double: Usage notes: Wild 7s of any suit and 7s of Spades with Smeared Joker will also count towards the unlock condition. Decks: Erratic Deck may start with more Clubs than a standard deck, and allows for more X of a Kind, like Pair or Three of a Kind, to be played, which could activate Seeing Double's condition more easily. Poker hands: Straight and Full House both generate X2 Mult a large majority of the time, making Seeing Double great for those strategies. Jokers: Smeared Joker means Clubs can also count as Spades and vice-versa. This means that playing any hand (even High Card) containing a Club or Spade will trigger Seeing Double.

title: Seeing Double
text: Seeing Double: This interaction is a bug. This interaction doesn't apply if the card is Wild. Splash allows triggering the bonus by adding an extra card that would otherwise be ineligible for scoring; e.g. ♣️A ♣️A ♣️A ♣️A ♥️4. Almost any hand that triggers Flower Pot will also trigger Seeing Double, providing a total of X6 Mult. If some cards are debuffed, Flower Pot may trigger without Seeing Double, as Seeing Double requires at least 1 non debuffed Club and at least 1 non debuffed non Club, while Flower Pot still counts debuffed cards.

title: Seeing Double
text: Seeing Double: Card modifiers: Wild cards can count as either the Club or the non-Club, but not both. Generally this means adding any second scoring card (including a second Wild card) will trigger the bonus, though Stone cards will not qualify, having no suit at all. Decks: Checkered Deck makes it significantly harder to activate Seeing Double, as it contains no Club cards naturally. Poker hands: Flush-based hands are hard to use, requiring a Wild card, Smeared Joker or an off-suit card via Four Fingers and Splash. Blinds: The Club renders Seeing Double useless, as all Club cards are debuffed and debuffed Club cards will not trigger Seeing Double.

title: Seeing Double
text: Seeing Double: The Pillar can make Seeing Double difficult to trigger if players already played some Club cards in the previous round, making them debuffed upon facing this boss blind. This can be remedied by carrying Tarot cards that provide enhancements into the boss blind to "revive" debuffed Club cards. Strategies: Unlocking Seeing Double may prove to be challenging at first due to its condition being oddly specific towards a specific rank and suit. In particular, there are no Jokers that directly have synergies with 7s, the sole exception being Odd Todd. Here are some approaches that can help with unlocking Seeing Double:

title: Seeing Double
text: Seeing Double: Magic Deck starts with two copies of The Fool, allowing the player to copy Tarots to make more 7 of Clubs, such as Death, The Moon, Strength, or even The Lovers. Erratic Deck can generate with more 7 of Clubs from the start. Wild 7s of any suit and 7s of Spades with Smeared Joker can also be used. Trivia: LocalThunk has said the name of this Joker is based on the album Seeing Double from 2002 by the British pop group S Club 7. Its effect in demo version used to be, and its current unlock condition is still related to 7 of Clubs.

title: Seltzer
text: Seltzer: Seltzer (Joker). Effect: Retrigger all cards played for the next 10 hands. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Retrigger. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: ✗ No. Seltzer is an Uncommon Retrigger Joker that temporarily boosts played hands' effect by re-triggering each scored card. It lasts for a total of 10 hands and will disappear after the 10th hand is played and retriggered (denoted by the text "Drank!").

title: Seltzer
text: Seltzer: Usage Notes: Seltzer does not retrigger a Red Seal. A card with a Red Seal will only activate three times: once for the initial trigger, once for the Red Seal, and then lastly, for Seltzer. The Non-Perishable challenge bans Seltzer. Decks: Zodiac Deck is helpful for finding tarot cards to make the enhanced cards that make Seltzer work effectively. Red Deck is able to find better hands on average, so Seltzer will last longer, as less hands need to be played per round.

title: Seltzer
text: Seltzer: Black Deck is able to stack more Jokers that benefit from Seltzer's effect. Adding even a single XMult Joker like Ancient Joker can be an extra X7.5 Mult normally, but with Seltzer it becomes an extra X57 Mult. Plasma Deck gains a huge boost from stacking XMult modifiers, which Seltzer enables very well. Poker hands: Any 5-card hands like Flush, Straight, or Full House will provide more retriggers from Seltzer. In particular, Flush Fives, with five of the same very strong duplicated card, work very well. Jokers: Any Joker that triggers on scoring will have its effect doubled, for instance Scary Face for Chips, Fibonacci for +Mult, The Idol for XMult, or Rough Gem for money.

title: Seltzer
text: Seltzer: Jokers that scale based on cards played, like Lucky Cat and Hiker, work very well with Seltzer, as the cards they scale with will always retrigger, and the scaling will remain after Seltzer is consumed. Jokers like 8 Ball (in particular, due to its on scoring nature) and Cartomancer can provide frequent Tarot cards to buff up playing cards. Throwback rewards you for skipping blinds, making Seltzer last longer and into more difficult Boss Blinds. Glass cards are very powerful with Seltzer, so Glass Joker can be a useful addition to compliment their usage. Certificate's Red Seals lend themselves well to the late-game endless runs Seltzer is often used on, and the Gold Seal effect can be retriggered.

title: Seltzer
text: Seltzer: If you have enough XMult from other Jokers, Polychrome cards or Glass cards, adding another retrigger Joker like Sock and Buskin can be more valuable than adding another XMult Joker. Blueprint and Brainstorm can also be used for this purpose, more flexibly even. Jokers: Copying cards with DNA will quickly use up Seltzer's retriggers. Similarly, destroying 6s with Sixth Sense will also quickly use up Seltzer's retriggers. Jokers that incentivize playing many hands per round, such as Green Joker or Vagabond, will similarly cause Seltzer to be spent quickly. Using Burglar does not always guarantee winning in one hand, so the player will have to play hands as pseudo-discards, which will quickly deplete Seltzer.

title: Seltzer
text: Seltzer: Boss Blinds: If a hand that is not allowed is played during The Psychic, The Mouth or The Eye, Seltzer will still lose a retrigger. Strategies: In a build with many enhanced cards, Seltzer can be a powerful joker, especially in the late game. Due to Seltzer's limited lifespan, it is often used to get the highest scoring single hand possible in endless mode. Trivia: The Joker's art depicts a seltzer bottle, also known as a soda siphon. These were historically used by clowns to spray soda water as a prank, which was the initial inspiration for the Joker. Despite this, the pop-up before disappearing will say "Drank!", tying in with its status as a Food Joker instead.

title: Seltzer
text: Seltzer: Despite this, the pop-up before disappearing will say "Drank!", tying in with its status as a Food Joker instead. The center of the bottle features a small Jimbo logo, similar to those on Riff-Raff and Baseball Card. Seltzer's effect to retrigger all scoring cards in a played hand could be a reference to its real life function of needing to pull the bottle's trigger repeatedly to effectively spray water from the nozzle. In early demos of the game, Seltzer is referred to as "Selzer", which seems to be a spelling error. This is still true in internal references to the card within the game's code.

title: Seltzer
text: Seltzer: This Joker is part of a group of "Consumable" Jokers that can be destroyed with usage, dubbed "Food Jokers" due to their shared theme. The other Jokers in this group are Ice Cream, Popcorn, Gros Michel, Cavendish, Egg, Turtle Bean, Ramen, and Diet Cola. In other media: Seltzer appears as a weapon in the Ante Chamber DLC of Vampire Survivors, albeit with the movement mechanics of Fibonacci.

title: Shoot the Moon
text: Shoot the Moon: Shoot the Moon (Joker). Effect: Each Queen held in hand gives +13 Mult. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Play every Heart card in your deck in one round. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: On Held. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Shoot the Moon is a Common Additive Mult Joker that provides +13 Mult for each Queen in the player's hand. Played cards do not trigger this Joker, regardless of whether they score. Queens that are debuffed by certain Blinds also do not trigger.

title: Shoot the Moon
text: Shoot the Moon: Usage Notes: Stone cards, non-heart Wild cards and Diamond cards with Smeared Joker do not need to be played to unlock Shoot the Moon. Decks: The Painted Deck has a larger hand size, making this Joker easier to use. Poker hands: All hands that do not use Queens benefit from this Joker. In decks with a hand limit of 8 or less, hands that require 5 cards make this Joker more difficult to use. Conversely, smaller hands, such as High Card, can use this Joker effectively every hand. This Joker may not be good when trying to make Straights, as the Straight cannot exceed a Jack unless Shortcut is in use. Jokers: Mime doubles the trigger of this Joker's effect.

title: Shoot the Moon
text: Shoot the Moon: Jokers: Mime doubles the trigger of this Joker's effect. Midas Mask can add a buff to played Queens, providing an additional benefit thereafter when Queens are held in hand. Reserved Parking provides cash when face cards are held in hand. Baron increases the amount of Mult gained by X1.5 Mult per held King, which can ride off of Shoot the Moon's Additive Mult for additional value. Shoot the Moon can also be used as a stepping stone for strengthening Queens to Kings for a Baron build. As previously mentioned, the player must physically move the Kings to the right of the Queens for maximum scoring value. Trading Card can remove non-Queen cards, allowing you to see and hold Queens easier.

title: Shoot the Moon
text: Shoot the Moon: Trading Card can remove non-Queen cards, allowing you to see and hold Queens easier. Consumables: Death and Strength can turn some cards into Queens. The Hanged Man can remove non-Queen cards, allowing you to see and hold Queens easier. The Chariot can turn some cards into Steel cards, which can multiply Shoot the Moon's additive Mult. As previously mentioned, the player must physically move the Steel cards to the right of the Queens for maximum scoring value. Deja Vu can apply Red Seals to Queens, allowing for more Shoot the Moon triggers. Cryptid can make more Queens. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette will permanently increase the player's hand size, enabling more Queens to be held at once.

title: Shoot the Moon
text: Shoot the Moon: Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette will permanently increase the player's hand size, enabling more Queens to be held at once. Decks: Abandoned Deck, Mad World, and Medusa can be difficult to use, as they naturally contain no Queens. Five-Card Draw does not work well with this Joker due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers. Jokers: Jokers that reduce hand size, like Stuntman and Merry Andy, will make the player hold fewer Queens. Blinds: The Hook discards 2 random cards after playing a hand, which may render Shoot the Moon useless if the Queens were discarded. The Plant debuffs all face cards, rendering Queens useless for the round.

title: Shoot the Moon
