text: Shoot the Moon: The Plant debuffs all face cards, rendering Queens useless for the round. The Mark draws all face cards face down, which makes the player unable to tell which card is a Queen. Cerulean Bell may force a Queen to be played or discarded. Verdant Leaf debuffs all cards, including Queens, until a Joker is sold.

title: Shoot the Moon
text: Shoot the Moon: Verdant Leaf debuffs all cards, including Queens, until a Joker is sold. Strategies: If the player has any cards in hand that give X1.5 Mult, either Steel cards or owning a Baron, it is ideal to manually drag the Queens to the far left so as to make Shoot the Moon's +Mult trigger before the XMult, maximizing the scoring power for the poker hand played. The reason for this is that any held-in-hand abilities are triggered from left to right. Therefore, placing any card far left will prioritize that specific held-in-hand effect. However, when enhancing a Queen itself to be a Steel card, the XMult will always apply before Shoot the Moon's +Mult.

title: Shoot the Moon
text: Shoot the Moon: The unlock requirement for Shoot the Moon does not necessarily mean to play one card of each rank with the Heart suit, so having just one Heart card in the deck and playing it will unlock Shoot the Moon. A suitable strategy to unlock it is with an Erratic Deck configuration with few Hearts, or Abandoned Deck, since it only has 10 Heart cards. Conversely, it is harder to unlock on Checkered Deck due to the big amount of Heart cards.

title: Shoot the Moon
text: Shoot the Moon: Trivia: "Shooting the Moon" is a term used in the popular card game "Hearts" for winning a hand by taking every Heart card and the Queen of Spades. Normally these cards give the players points - which you aim to avoid in Hearts, as the lowest scorer wins - but if a player can take all of them, their opponents get hit with a points penalty instead. It is a risky play to attempt, as missing just one card ruins the attempt and will cause that player to take a lot of points. The +13 Mult refers to the Queen of Spades in Hearts being 13 points.

title: Shoot the Moon
text: Shoot the Moon: The +13 Mult refers to the Queen of Spades in Hearts being 13 points. The unlock requirement is also a reference to Hearts, since it requires collecting and playing every Heart card in the deck. In demo versions, Shoot the Moon only worked for the Queen of Spades, as it does in Hearts. The art of Shoot the Moon is based on the Queen of Spades, most noticeable by the design of their staves being the same.

title: Shortcut
text: Shortcut: Shortcut (Joker). Effect: Allows Straights to be made with gaps of 1 rank, (ex: 10 8 6 5 3). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Shortcut is an Uncommon Effect-type Joker that allows Straights to be made with one or more gaps of 1 rank between cards (ex: 2 4 5 7 9). Like normal, Shortcut still does not allow "wrapping" Straights, so Aces remain either high or low and not both.

title: Shortcut
text: Shortcut: Usage notes: The 15 Minute City challenge starts with an Eternal copy of Shortcut. Decks: Black Deck: The +1 Joker Slot allows Shortcut to function as a utility Joker while still providing space for 5 other Jokers to score. Abandoned Deck lowers the range of card values from A-K to A-10, making it significantly more likely to draw a Straight, especially with Shortcut. Checkered Deck in tandem with Shortcut increases the likelihood of finding a playable Straight Flush. Poker hands: Straight Straight Flush (or Royal Flush)

title: Shortcut
text: Shortcut: Poker hands: Straight Straight Flush (or Royal Flush) Jokers: Four Fingers is a great combination with Shortcut, as this allows for a 4-length Straight with gaps, and Straight Flushes become even easier to make since the Straight and Flush don't need to be on the same 4 cards. (e.g. Q♠️ J♠️ 9♥️ 7♠️ 3♠️ is a valid Straight Flush with both Jokers in effect) Crazy Joker and The Order give additive and multiplicative Mult respectively when a Straight is played. Devious Joker and Runner both give Chips when a Straight is played. Superposition and Séance create Consumables when a Straight or Straight Flush is played.

title: Shortcut
text: Shortcut: Superposition and Séance create Consumables when a Straight or Straight Flush is played. Space Joker and Burnt Joker appreciate Shortcut’s effect allowing for multiple straights to be formed in one round, and can make use of Straights having incredibly strong Planet scaling. Playing cards: Obtaining Saturn from cards with a Blue Seal becomes much easier due to the decreased difficulty of forming a straight allowing more discards to be used to find them.

title: Shortcut
text: Shortcut: Strategies: Mathematically, Shortcut is slightly better than Four Fingers in creating Straights. However, Four Fingers is better at helping create Flushes and Straight Flushes. The player can consider choosing between the two, or combining the two to gain more Straights (in which case, Straights are almost always present in the 8 cards), but at the risk of losing two scoring Jokers. Trivia: A shortcut is a quicker route from one place to another than the usual path, often taken by skipping across roads through side paths. Shortcut's effect is inspired by this; it allows players to 'skip' a number while still preserving the Straight.

title: Showman
text: Showman: Showman (Joker). Effect: Joker, Tarot, Planet, and Spectral cards may appear multiple times. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Reach Ante level 4. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Showman is an Uncommon Effect Joker that removes the restriction on Jokers, Planet cards, Tarot cards and Spectral cards from appearing when already in the player's possession. This can lead to multiple copies of the same card appearing in Booster Packs or the Shop, or allow card generators such as Riff-Raff to generate multiple copies of the same card.

title: Showman
text: Showman: Showman is one of the few ways that the player can obtain multiple copies of a single Joker (the others being the Invisible Joker and Ankh cards), and is often used to enable extremely high score set-ups. To unlock this Joker, the player must reach Ante 4 during any run. This Joker shares an unlock requirement with the Ante Up! achievement. Usage Notes: Showman can make The Emperor and Riff-Raff generate themselves. Although the probability is extremely low, Showman can even make multiple copies of The Soul or Black Hole appear in Booster Packs.

title: Showman
text: Showman: If the player has Showman and finds a duplicate of any of their Jokers in the shop, if they sell that Joker and replace it with the shop duplicate, (as they might do if it has a better Edition) that Joker will be able to appear as a duplicate again even if the Showman is sold. Decks: Showman is effective with any deck, but is particularly strong on Black Deck due to the +1 Joker slot bonus.

title: Showman
text: Showman: Poker hands: Showman has no direct effect on any specific poker hands. It does, however, make Celestial Packs less reliable, as its effect allows them to give duplicate planets. This decreases the chances of a Celestial Pack containing your desired Planet card, as well as preventing Planet Blocking (holding useless Planets in your consumable slots so they can't appear elsewhere). Jokers: Showman has no direct Joker synergies. However, its main benefit lies in it being one of very few ways to obtain multiple copies of the same Joker. Cavendish is a powerful common Joker, making it likely to appear again before ante 8. Photograph and Hanging Chad have notable synergy and are also common Jokers, making them appear more often.

title: Showman
text: Showman: Photograph and Hanging Chad have notable synergy and are also common Jokers, making them appear more often. Blueprint and Brainstorm are strong in long endless runs. The Idol is also powerful in endless runs. Vouchers: Because it allows for duplicated Planet cards to appear, Showman synergizes with the Observatory by allowing for planet cards to appear in the shop whilst they are in the consumable space. However, this is easier achieved with Blue Seal. Showman can also create problems when Telescope is not yet redeemed, as Celestial Packs will often contain multiple copies of irrelevant planet cards.

title: Showman
text: Showman: Trivia: This Joker was present in the initial playtest build, but was not present within the first two public demos. Numerous glitches that produced the same effect were, however, present during the time the demo was available. This has led players to believe that Showman was influenced, or inspired by these glitches. This Joker used to be named "Ring Master" in some of Balatro's early builds. It is still referred to by this name in the programming, and most translations. According to LocalThunk, the reason for renaming is that Showman is more in line with the effect of this joker.

title: Showman
text: Showman: According to LocalThunk, the reason for renaming is that Showman is more in line with the effect of this joker. The bug of Showman is so difficult to pin down that LocalThunk had taken to calling it his "White Whale", after the fanatical obsession of Captain Ahab in the novel Moby Dick. In the extreme event that all Rare Jokers are owned, Rare Tag will "NOPE" and do nothing. Unlike most interactions with blocking, Showman will not override this, which is believed to be a bug.

title: Sinful Jokers
text: Sinful Jokers: Sinful Jokers refers to these four Common Jokers, which give +3 Mult when specific suits are scored: Greedy Joker, gives +3 Mult when Diamonds are scored. Lusty Joker, gives +3 Mult when Hearts are scored. Wrathful Joker, gives +3 Mult when Spades are scored. Gluttonous Joker, gives +3 Mult when Clubs are scored. If the played card is retriggered, either by a Joker effect, like Hanging Chad, or by its own Red Seal, the Sinful Joker's effect will activate again. Trivia: These 4 Jokers were referenced as 'Sinful Jokers' by LocalThunk in patch notes. All 4 of these Jokers are one of the traditional seven deadly sins.

title: Sinful Jokers
text: Sinful Jokers: All 4 of these Jokers are one of the traditional seven deadly sins. In demo versions of the game, the color of Sinful Jokers backgrounds were less vibrant. This was changed in the release version (update 1.0.0h) to match the color of the suits better.

title: Sixth Sense
text: Sixth Sense: Sixth Sense (Joker). Effect: If first hand of round is a single 6, destroy it and create a Spectral card, (Must have room). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Sixth Sense is an Uncommon Effect Joker that will provide the player with Spectral cards, as long as it is fed with a 6 as the only played card in the first hand of a round. It activates after all scoring is completed and therefore still works if the 6 is debuffed, and does not get influenced by retriggers. It does not activate if the hand is not allowed under the current Boss Blind (e.g. The Psychic).

title: Sixth Sense
text: Sixth Sense: Sixth Sense cannot give the Spectral cards The Soul or Black Hole, as both can only be found in Booster Packs. Decks: Red Deck gives +1 Discard which makes it easier to find a 6. Blue Deck gives +1 Hand which allows the player more freedom to utilize Sixth Sense, as there are more remaining Hands to defeat the Blind. Abandoned Deck and Mad World increase the chance to draw a 6 as they have less overall cards. Painted Deck gives +2 hand size, making it easier to find 6s. However, the -1 joker slot makes Sixth Sense riskier to use. Poker Hands: High Card is the only poker hand directly relevant to Sixth Sense.

title: Sixth Sense
text: Sixth Sense: Poker Hands: High Card is the only poker hand directly relevant to Sixth Sense. Jokers: Perkeo can copy any Spectral card created by Sixth Sense. DNA can create copies of playing cards, allowing the player to infinitely farm Spectral cards as long as the Deck contains at least one 6. The order of the two makes no difference—If DNA is on the right, the 6 will still be replicated after being destroyed. Erosion will also scale after Sixth Sense destroys 6s.

title: Sixth Sense
text: Sixth Sense: Erosion will also scale after Sixth Sense destroys 6s. Drunkard and Merry Andy both give extra discards, which makes it easier to find a 6. While Merry Andy reduces hand size, which normally makes 6s harder to find, the extra discards will make that punishment pretty much meaningless, as long as the player does not reduce their hand size much lower. Juggler increases hand size and makes it easier to find a 6 to play. Troubadour and Turtle Bean can be used too, but Troubadour removes a hand, which makes it more punishing to use Sixth Sense, and Turtle Bean can only be used temporarily, as it will reduce its value until it reaches 0.

title: Sixth Sense
text: Sixth Sense: Consumables: Strength can be used to turn 5s (and possibly 4s) into 6s to be destroyed and converted into Spectral cards. This also helps remove cards in order to shape the deck. Death can turn some cards into 6s to be destroyed and converted into Spectral cards. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong both give additional hands to play, which can be used to trigger Sixth Sense with fewer consequences. Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give additional discards, which can help in finding 6s. Paint Brush and Palette both give extra hand size, which can make it easier to find a 6.

title: Sixth Sense
text: Sixth Sense: Paint Brush and Palette both give extra hand size, which can make it easier to find a 6. Blinds: Any blind that disables cards in deck (like The Club, The Pillar, etc.) will not prevent Sixth Sense from triggering. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle all reduce the number of hands to play, which can discourage using Sixth Sense while a player's hands aren't strong enough. Nebula Deck only starts with one Consumable Slot, which makes it harder to hold onto Sixth Sense's Spectral cards. Jokers: Obtaining a second copy of Sixth Sense does not stack with itself, creating only 1 Spectral card when destroying 6s.

title: Sixth Sense
text: Sixth Sense: While Burglar gives more hands to play with, it also removes all discards. If the first hand of the round does not contain a 6, Sixth Sense will miss its effect. Stuntman reduces hand size, which makes it harder to find a 6. Blinds: The Psychic forces the player to play a 5-card hand, meaning Sixth Sense cannot activate. The Needle sets the player's hands to 1. Therefore, to still benefit from Sixth Sense, the player would have to beat the blind with nothing but a single High Card. The Mouth only allows 1 hand type, so unless players build around High Cards, they must play a winning hand type first, missing Sixth Sense's effect.

title: Sixth Sense
text: Sixth Sense: If Crimson Heart debuffs Sixth Sense on the first hand, it cannot destroy any 6 or create a Spectral card. Stakes: On Blue Stake difficulty or higher, there is a -1 Discard penalty which can make it harder to find a 6. Strategies: As Sixth Sense requires having 6s in the deck to activate, it has limited use as the player will likely destroy all 6s in the Deck before reaching Ante 8. However, this is usually ideal, as 6s do not have any particularly strong synergies with other Jokers, and the Spectral card given may help further enhance the player's deck and hasten the Deck manipulation process. In general, Spectral cards to look out for are:

title: Sixth Sense
text: Sixth Sense: Any of the Seal-adding cards. Deja Vu, Trance, Medium, and Talisman. Aura for farming the Polychrome Edition. Cryptid to make copies of a useful card, which can be used in conjunction with the above Spectral cards. Immolate to further hasten Deck manipulation and for a boost in Money. Ectoplasm for when the player has their final Joker lineup. Any other Spectral card is still worth keeping so as to prevent it from appearing in the shop, either from a Spectral Pack or from playing on the Ghost Deck, as they are either too niche or hard to make use of.

title: Sixth Sense
text: Sixth Sense: When using Sixth Sense, it can be worth opening Standard Packs to directly add 6s for later destruction; while this usually isn't as good as opening a Spectral Pack directly, Standard Packs are much more common than Spectral Packs, and Spectral cards can be quite impactful. Additionally, Sixth Sense makes it more reasonable to fish for specific or highly-upgraded cards in Standard Packs, grabbing a six to be later traded for a Spectral card if nothing better presents itself. Trivia: A sixth sense, also known as extrasensory perception, is the power of perception beyond the five senses of sight, hearing, touch, smell, or taste.

title: Sixth Sense
text: Sixth Sense: In early demo versions, the effect of Sixth Sense was "Each played 6 permanently gains +6 Chips when scored". This is changed in later versions. As a part of the Ghost Deck Playing Cards set by Fangamer, Sixth Sense is one of the four Jokers to be featured next to Mr. Bones, Séance, and Castle. Unlike DNA, Sixth Sense does not shake during the first hand. In other media: In Black Mirror, there is a scene in "Hotel Reverie" where a character is seen playing Balatro, and Sixth Sense is a card shown onscreen. Joker, Campfire, Blue Joker, The Empress, and Uranus are shown onscreen as well.

title: Sly Joker
text: Sly Joker: Sly Joker (Joker). Effect: +50 Chips if played hand contains a Pair. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. Type: Chips. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Sly Joker is a Common Chips Joker that provides +50 Chips when playing a Pair. This includes hands that include any two cards with the same rank, such as a Three of a Kind or a Full House.

title: Sly Joker
text: Sly Joker: Decks: The Abandoned Deck and Mad World, having fewer total cards in the deck, gives a higher chance of drawing a pair. The Erratic Deck will have cards of a certain rank appear more than others. Plasma Deck benefits from the large amount of chips, which, when balanced, greatly boost the score for the played hand. Poker hands: Sly Joker triggers whenever there are two duplicate scoring cards, regardless of whether the hand itself is a "Pair". This means you can trigger Sly Joker if you play a Flush that contains two of the same card. In an unmodified deck, Sly Joker triggers off of every hand in the game except for High Card, Flush, Straight, or Straight Flush.

title: Sly Joker
text: Sly Joker: Jokers: Jolly Joker and The Duo pair well with this, as both will trigger on the same activation as this joker. Trivia: This joker is part of a series that provides a Chips boost for a specific hand. The others are Wily Joker, Clever Joker, Devious Joker, and Crafty Joker. Much like the other Jokers in this series, this Joker has blue face paint over the mouth, indicating that they provide a bonus of Chips and not Mult like the red face paint Jokers.

title: Smeared Joker
text: Smeared Joker: Smeared Joker (Joker). Effect: Hearts and Diamonds count as the same suit, Spades and Clubs count as the same suit. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Have at least 3 Wild Card in your deck. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Smeared Joker is an Uncommon Effect Joker which makes Diamonds and Hearts count as the same suit, and Clubs and Spades count as the same suit. This effect applies to all Jokers and Blinds which have an effect based on suit.

title: Smeared Joker
text: Smeared Joker: To unlock this Joker, the player must have at least 3 Wild cards in the deck. Usage Notes: Despite Smeared Joker counting suits as other suits, Jokers that unlock based on a certain suit won't count the other suit for their unlock condition, which includes the following Jokers: Rough Gem won't count Heart cards for its unlock condition. Bloodstone won't count Diamond cards for its unlock condition. Arrowhead won't count Club cards for its unlock condition. Onyx Agate won't count Spade cards for its unlock condition. Shoot the Moon does not need to play Diamond cards in order to get unlocked.

title: Smeared Joker
text: Smeared Joker: Shoot the Moon does not need to play Diamond cards in order to get unlocked. There is one exception, however, which is Seeing Double, which can be unlocked by playing 7s of Spades with Smeared Joker. Decks: Black Deck: The +1 Joker Slot allows Smeared Joker to function as a utility Joker while still providing space for 5 other Jokers to score. Checkered Deck is split between two suits that do not combine due to the Smeared Joker, so it loses out on some benefits. However, it allows the deck to benefit from effects that involve Clubs and Diamonds, including very powerful Jokers like Ancient Joker, so it can still be quite valuable.

title: Smeared Joker
text: Smeared Joker: Painted Deck's hand size of 10 guarantees a Flush with Smeared Joker and no Stone cards. However, with Painted Deck's fewer Joker slots, keeping effect Jokers like Smeared Joker can be risky. Poker hands: Works best with the following hands if you are trying to go for a flush build. Flush Straight Flush Flush House Flush Five Jokers: Generally, any Joker that takes effect upon cards of certain suits will benefit from Smeared Joker, by activating on more cards, including: Lusty Joker and Greedy Joker - Each Diamond or Heart provides +3 Mult. Wrathful Joker and Gluttonous Joker - Each Club or Spade provides +3 Mult.

title: Smeared Joker
text: Smeared Joker: Wrathful Joker and Gluttonous Joker - Each Club or Spade provides +3 Mult. Bloodstone - Each Diamond or Heart has a 1 in 2 chance to provide a X1.5 Mult. Rough Gem - Each Diamond or Heart provides $1. Onyx Agate - Each Club or Spade provides +7 Mult. Arrowhead - Each Club or Spade provides +50 Chips. Ancient Joker - Diamonds and Hearts can be played interchangeably. Clubs and Spades can be played interchangeably. Castle - Diamonds and Hearts can be discarded interchangeably. Clubs and Spades can be discarded interchangeably. Seeing Double - playing any hand (even High Card) containing a Club or Spade will trigger the X2 Mult effect, unless the card is Wild.

title: Smeared Joker
text: Smeared Joker: Flower Pot - Only two Clubs or Spades and two Diamonds or Hearts need to be played to trigger the X3 Mult effect. There are other Jokers that work together well with Smeared Joker: Jokers that are effective with Flushes, such as Droll Joker, Crafty Joker, and The Tribe all become easier to activate. As with Painted Deck, with Jokers like Juggler, Troubadour and Turtle Bean, increasing hand size can usually guarantee a Flush. Séance - Since playing Straight Flushes becomes a lot more common with Smeared Joker, you can create Spectral cards much easier this way. Vouchers: Paint Brush once again increases hand size, guaranteeing a Flush with Smeared Joker under most circumstances.

title: Smeared Joker
text: Smeared Joker: Vouchers: Paint Brush once again increases hand size, guaranteeing a Flush with Smeared Joker under most circumstances. Palette's increase to 10 is less valuable since Flushes are already guaranteed, but still gives more room to find specific cards if that's desirable for some reason. Blinds: Smeared Joker doubles a player's vulnerability to suit bosses: The Head and The Window both debuff all Diamond and Heart cards. The Club and The Goad both debuff all Club and Spade cards.

title: Smeared Joker
text: Smeared Joker: The Club and The Goad both debuff all Club and Spade cards. Trivia: This card's name and design are a reference to how in a normal playing card deck, Club and Spade are the same color, just like Diamond and Hearts. As such, if the actual symbol of the suit was smeared and illegible, it would be difficult to tell them apart. Due to the letters being smeared, this Joker is the only non-Legendary Joker to not legibly contain the word "Joker" in its sprite.

title: Smiley Face
text: Smiley Face: Smiley Face (Joker). Effect: Played face cards give +5 Mult when scored. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Smiley Face is a Common Additive Mult Joker that adds +5 Mult for each scored face card in a hand.

title: Smiley Face
text: Smiley Face: Decks: Red Deck's extra discard can be used to dig for more face cards in the player's deck. Painted Deck has a larger hand size, allowing for more face cards to appear. However, the -1 Joker slot means Smiley Face may not be as viable as some other options. Mad World starts with an Eternal Pareidolia, which makes every card scored provide +5 Mult. Poker hands: Two Pair and especially Full House work best with this Joker in the early game. Four of a Kind, Five of a Kind, and Flush Five work well with this Joker in the late game. Jokers: Pareidolia makes every card scored provide +5 Mult, effectively making every card a slightly better Mult card.

title: Smiley Face
text: Smiley Face: Jokers: Pareidolia makes every card scored provide +5 Mult, effectively making every card a slightly better Mult card. Sock and Buskin will add an additional +5 Mult per face card scored. Triboulet provides a Mult multiplier for each played King or Queen. Business Card gives each face card played a 50% chance to provide $2 when scored. Scary Face provides additional Chips for each face card played. Splash causes all face cards played to provide +5 Mult. Jokers: Baron, Shoot the Moon, and Reserved Parking encourage not playing face cards. Ride the Bus actively punishes playing face cards. Canio's ability activates only upon destroying face cards, resulting in fewer cards able to trigger Smiley Face.

title: Smiley Face
text: Smiley Face: Canio's ability activates only upon destroying face cards, resulting in fewer cards able to trigger Smiley Face. Blinds: The Plant debuffs all faces, which prevents Smiley Face from giving any mult. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Medusa do not work well with Smiley Face, due to their initial lack of face cards.

title: Sock and Buskin
text: Sock and Buskin: Sock and Buskin (Joker). Effect: Retrigger all played face cards. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Play a total of 300 face cards. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Retrigger. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Sock and Buskin is an Uncommon Retrigger Joker that retriggers all face cards - Jacks, Queens, and Kings - that are scored in a hand. It does not retrigger face cards held in hand or a Red Seal. For example, a Red Seal Jack will only activate three times: once for the initial trigger, once for the Red Seal, and then lastly, for Sock and Buskin. This Joker is unlocked after playing a total of 300 face cards.

title: Sock and Buskin
text: Sock and Buskin: Decks: Mad World works well with Sock and Buskin, as this deck starts with Pareidolia and Business Card, allowing all cards to retrigger and generate more money from Business Card. Poker Hands: 5-card hands such as Full House, Five of a Kind, Flush, Flush House, and Flush Five will let you retrigger the most amount of face cards. Jokers: Hiker will permanently add an additional +5 Chips per face card, for a total of +10 Chips. Pareidolia will make it so all cards are retriggered. Business Card can retrigger and give you an additional $2 for each proc. Smiley Face will add an additional +5 Mult per face card. Scary Face will add an additional +30 Chips per face card.

title: Sock and Buskin
text: Sock and Buskin: Scary Face will add an additional +30 Chips per face card. Triboulet will add an additional X2 Mult per King or Queen. Photograph will add an additional X2 Mult on the first face card, for a total of X4 Mult. Bloodstone might give an additional X1.5 Mult for each Heart face card, which can be guaranteed with Oops! All 6s. Other suit-based Jokers like Onyx Agate, Greedy Joker, Arrowhead, etc. can benefit if your face cards have the corresponding suit. Tarot generating Jokers, like Cartomancer and Vagabond, are needed for deck manipulation to draw face cards more reliably. It will also help modify face cards to make them more valuable during the retrigger (ex. retriggering a Bonus Jack).

title: Sock and Buskin
text: Sock and Buskin: If one has enough XMult from their cards, another retrigger Joker is very useful to combine with Sock and Buskin. This will usually be either Dusk or Seltzer, though Blueprint and Brainstorm can also be used to copy Sock and Buskin for a less conditional retrigger. One can also use Showman to try and find another Sock and Buskin. Trading Card and DNA make it easier to draw your useful face cards. DNA is particularly useful, as it can copy a powerful face card with an enhancement, edition, and seal. Lucky Cat can scale twice as fast since the Lucky face cards it will be using to scale have twice as many chances to earn +20 Mult or $20.

title: Sock and Buskin
text: Sock and Buskin: As Glass cards are substantially powerful with Sock and Buskin's retriggers, Glass Joker can be a nice addition to still get value when they break. Certificate can be used to try and find a face card (or a 10 that can be Strengthened) with a powerful seal, or a Purple Seal to generate Tarots for the face cards. However, if it adds too many non-face cards, Sock and Buskin will become less valuable, so the risk and reward must be carefully assessed. Consumables: Tarot cards: The Hierophant, The Empress, The Magician and Justice add enhancements to the face cards that makes retriggering them more worthwhile.

title: Sock and Buskin
text: Sock and Buskin: The Hierophant, The Empress, The Magician and Justice add enhancements to the face cards that makes retriggering them more worthwhile. The Hanged Man can be used to thin out the deck and the face cards easier to draw. Death can be used to turn other cards into face cards, especially face cards that already have an enhancement or edition on them. Strength can be used to turn 10s into Jacks. Strength can also be used if be used if the player only wants to focus on one rank (such as turning all Queens into Kings). Spectral cards: Aura can add a Foil, Holographic, or Polychrome effect to a face card, giving the player more of a reason to play them.

title: Sock and Buskin
text: Sock and Buskin: Cryptid can be used to create more face cards that already have enhancements or editions on them. Deja Vu can add a Red Seal to a face card for an additional retrigger. Immolate can destroy up to five cards, potentially making the face cards easier to find. Talisman can apply a Gold Seal to a face card, allowing it generate $6 when played. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Medusa both have anti-synergy since they contain no face cards by default. Jokers: Canio encourages the player to destroy face cards, which doesn't work well with Sock and Buskin. Ride the Bus totally discourages playing face cards, making Sock and Buskin useless.

title: Sock and Buskin
text: Sock and Buskin: Ride the Bus totally discourages playing face cards, making Sock and Buskin useless. Poker Hands: Straights, although being a five-card hand, can only let you play up to 3 face cards. Blinds: The Plant debuffs all face cards, rendering Sock and Buskin useless for the round. Trivia: Sock and buskin are ancient symbols of comedy and tragedy. Traditionally, the two masks of Comedy and Tragedy are known as Thalia and Melpomene. The art of this card in pre-release had the art span the whole card, without the border on the right side.

title: Space Joker
text: Space Joker: Space Joker (Joker). Effect: 1 in 4 chance to upgrade level of played poker hand. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: On Played. Probability-Based: Yes. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Space Joker is an Uncommon Effect Joker that has a 1 in 4 chance of upgrading the poker hand that is played. The upgrade is triggered before scoring of the hand, thus the hand will get a higher score itself.

title: Space Joker
text: Space Joker: Decks: Blue Deck gives an extra hand, meaning more chances to level up a poker hand. Poker hands: Simple hands such as Pair or Two Pair are easier to find and play, allowing the player to consistently level these hands up. Jokers: Oops! All 6s increases your chances of upgrading the hand to 1 in 2, or 50%. Two copies of Oops! All 6s makes it guaranteed. Burglar's +3 Hands are perfect for trying to level up easy-to-assemble hands like High Card and Pair. Supernova pays out Mult based on the number of times you've played a hand previously, which can enable a player to consistently build huge Mult values with simpler hands like Pair and Two Pair.

title: Space Joker
text: Space Joker: When there are multiple Space Jokers (or when copied with Blueprint and Brainstorm), their triggers are calculated separately. This provides more opportunities and consistency for leveling up poker hands. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong both provide an extra hand, giving the player more chances to level up a specific poker hand. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle don't allow the player many chances to level up a poker hand due to their reduced number of hands. Trivia: Burnt Joker is similar, but it provides an upgrade when discarding hands instead of playing them. The reason why an astronaut joker was chosen for this effect might be because planet cards are the primary way of upgrading poker hands.

title: Space Joker
text: Space Joker: The fact that Space Joker is triggered by chance may be a reference to the fact that space launches carry risks and may not always succeed. However, according to NASA's data, the average historical success rate of spacecraft launches is about 80%, way higher than Space Joker.

title: Spare Trousers
text: Spare Trousers: Spare Trousers (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains +2 Mult if played hand contains a Two Pair, (Currently +0 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Spare Trousers is an Uncommon scaling Additive Mult Joker that adds Mult to played hands. The amount of Mult added begins at +0 and is permanently increased by +2 when the player plays a hand that contains a Two Pair (including Full House and Flush House).

title: Spare Trousers
text: Spare Trousers: Decks: Red Deck: +1 Discard, making it easier to assemble Two Pairs. Blue Deck: +1 Hand per round, allowing more chances to scale. Painted Deck: The +2 hand size makes it much more likely to draw Two Pairs. Abandoned Deck and Mad World: Easier to assemble Two Pairs thanks to their lower number of cards.

title: Spare Trousers
text: Spare Trousers: Abandoned Deck and Mad World: Easier to assemble Two Pairs thanks to their lower number of cards. Poker hands: Spare Trousers's additive Mult increases by +2 any time the player plays a Poker Hand that contains a Two Pair. A Two Pair, a Full House, or a Flush House will always trigger this increase, even if any of the cards are debuffed by a Boss Blind. A Flush may also trigger this increase if it is assembled in such a way that it also contains a Two Pair; for example, a valid Flush for Spare Trousers would be K K J 9 9 with a matching suit.

title: Spare Trousers
text: Spare Trousers: Jokers: Square Joker: +4 Chips any time a played hand consists of exactly four cards. Since a standard Two Pair is exactly four cards, the player can strengthen both Square Joker and Spare Trousers at the same time. Space Joker: Like with Supernova, the repeated playing of Two Pair synergizes well with this Joker. Card Sharp: Because it's unlikely to win with one Two Pair hand, Card Sharp will provide an additional X3 Mult on subsequent Two Pair hands.

title: Spare Trousers
text: Spare Trousers: Obelisk: While potentially a detriment if acquired alongside Spare Trousers at the start, this Joker will allow for an extreme power spike in the mid-to-late game, where it is much easier to pivot from an overplayed Two Pair to hands like Flushes and Full Houses. The Duo: The Duo will always trigger and provide X2 Mult on a Two Pair, Full House and a Flush House poker hand, synergizing will with the flat Mult provided by Spare Trousers. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong give additional hands, allowing Spare Trousers to scale faster. Wasteful and Recyclomancy give additional discards, which allows the player to search for Two Pair hands easier.

title: Spare Trousers
text: Spare Trousers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy give additional discards, which allows the player to search for Two Pair hands easier. Paint Brush and Palette both increase hand size, which can help players with forming Two Pairs. Telescope can help upgrade Two Pair using Uranus. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle all have poor synergy with Spare Trousers due to their reduced number of hands. Poker hands: 5 of a kind, Four of a Kind, Three of a Kind, Pair, Straight, Royal Flush, and Flush Five cannot activate the +Mult ability. Blinds: The Eye will only allow the player to play any given Poker Hand once, limiting the scaling opportunities for Spare Trousers.

title: Spare Trousers
text: Spare Trousers: Strategies: Spare Trousers' usefulness is comparable to a bell curve over time. Initially, Spare Trousers has no bonus, and the player needs to play a Two Pair hand for it to have any benefit at all. Since any played hand can only ever include one Two Pair at a time, it can potentially take numerous hands and rounds of a run to build up Spare Trousers to a point where it feels strong. In other words, Spare Trousers requires a significant time investment, plus a conscious effort to play as many Two Pair hands as possible.

title: Spare Trousers
text: Spare Trousers: Furthermore, since it can only be increased by +2 Mult per hand at most, in the late game (beginning around Ante level 7 and higher) the player runs the risk of being unable to increase Spare Trousers quickly enough to keep it viable. Usually, the player can raise Spare Trousers to around +40 Mult by the time they reach Ante level 8, but if Spare Trousers was the centerpiece of their build, they may struggle against the Showdown Blind and any subsequent Boss Blinds. Using Planet cards to level up Spare Trousers' applicable hands can partially compensate for the joker's late-game strength falloff.

title: Spare Trousers
text: Spare Trousers: Using Planet cards to level up Spare Trousers' applicable hands can partially compensate for the joker's late-game strength falloff. Trivia: The background of the card art consists of a pattern of little trousers (also called pants in some parts of the world). The name of this Joker could be a play on the fact that having a spare pair of trousers also means that you have Two Pairs of trousers, hence its effect revolving around Two Pair hands.

title: Splash
text: Splash: Splash (Joker). Effect: Every played card counts in scoring. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Splash is a Common Effect Joker that makes all the cards you play count when scoring, not just the ones that make up the formal Poker Hand. This includes triggering seals and enhancements on each of the additional cards, and these will also trigger any Joker effects.

title: Splash
text: Splash: If the player is very desperate for chips, Splash can also provide an extra 20-40 chips for low-scoring hands like High Card. Decks: Blue Deck may see some more value out of this card due to its extra hand each round. While Black Deck removes a hand, it also adds an extra Joker Slot, making it easier to keep Splash alongside other scoring Jokers. Poker hands: This Joker especially helps High Card and Pair builds which otherwise lose out on the ability to stack effects from enhanced cards or triggering jokers such as Fibonacci multiple times in a hand.

title: Splash
text: Splash: Jokers: Any Jokers that trigger their effect when certain cards are scored synergize well with Splash. This includes Scholar, Greedy Joker, The Idol, Onyx Agate, and any other Joker that gives played cards a bonus when scored. Flower Pot is arguably the best synergy with Splash, since you will almost always be able to play and score every suit in one hand, though that hand will probably counts as a Pair or High Card. Seeing Double and Splash makes it very easy to get the X2 Mult for low-scoring hands. Pareidolia boosts Splash's synergy with all Jokers that buff scored face cards.

title: Splash
text: Splash: Pareidolia boosts Splash's synergy with all Jokers that buff scored face cards. Hiker is very good with Splash, as the cards played will always score and therefore always upgrade. This makes it easier to upgrade specific cards, as they can score even if the hand they would normally be played in is unavailable. It also makes it easier to add a high-chip card onto an otherwise low-chip hand.

title: Splash
text: Splash: Jokers that scale Mult based on hands played, like Green Joker, are usually good to use with Splash, as they also help out many of the High Card and Pair builds that Splash is used most often in. In this case, Splash is best used as a Chip provider, scoring Bonus cards and Foil card that wouldn't otherwise be scored. (Stone cards perform like this already, but you could use Splash as a transitional Joker while you build up the amount of Stones in your deck.) Splash can help out Burglar, as the throwaway hands that one will usually need to play with it will score more Chips.

title: Splash
text: Splash: Fibonacci and Splash lets you easily get an extra 24 - 40 Mult per each hand. Decks: Painted Deck, Blast Off and Cruelty punish having effect Jokers like Splash due to their reduced Joker slots. During Double or Nothing and Fragile, Splash will result in cards being debuffed and destroyed prematurely, respectively. Poker hands: The following hands are already made up of five cards, and thus get no benefit from Splash: Straight* Flush* Full House Straight Flush (and Royal Flush)* Five of a Kind Flush House Flush Five *Unless holding Four Fingers. Jokers: Ride the Bus is anti-synergistic, as it can be reset by a face card that would have otherwise had no effect.

title: Splash
text: Splash: Marble Joker adds Stone cards, which count to the score regardless of the hand, making Splash unnecessary. Trivia: This joker was available since the first demo of the game and has never been changed. In poker, splashing is the act of carelessly dropping or throwing chips into the pot, causing them to scatter, rather than neatly moving or piling them. This joker similarly allows you to carelessly play cards, since they will all score regardless of poker hands.

title: Splash
text: Splash: In collectible card games such as Magic: The Gathering, a "Splash" is a term for the practice of using only a very small amount of cards of a color in a deck which is filled with cards of other colors. In a similar vein, this Joker allows the player to "Splash" a small amount of cards that wouldn't normally score into their deck.

title: Square Joker
text: Square Joker: Square Joker (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains +4 Chips if played hand has exactly 4 cards, (Currently 0 Chips). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Square Joker is a Common scaling Chips Joker that adds Chips to played hands. The amount of Chips added begins at +0 and is permanently increased by +4 when the player plays a hand that contains only four cards. The four cards played do not have to score, and all four can be debuffed.

title: Square Joker
text: Square Joker: Decks: Plasma Deck: Due to the balancing feature, Square Joker can be very beneficial if picked up early and scaled adequately throughout the run. Blue Deck: Having one extra hand allows more scaling for Square Joker. Poker hands: The following hands are made up of no more than four cards, and thus can scale Square Joker: Four of a Kind Three of a Kind Two Pair Pair High Card Hands that require fewer than four cards can be padded with non-scoring cards to scale anyway. Flushes, Straights, and Straight Flushes can synergize with this Joker if Four Fingers is also present. Jokers: Four Fingers: Allows Straights and Flushes to be made with only four cards.

title: Square Joker
text: Square Joker: Jokers: Four Fingers: Allows Straights and Flushes to be made with only four cards. Splash: Allows High Cards to score with all 4 cards, providing more bonus. Spare Trousers: Requires Two Pairs hand to scale, which is exactly 4 cards. Burglar: Provides three extra hands, allowing Square Joker to scale more. Other scaling Additive mult Joker based on hands, like Green Joker, Ride the Bus, or Supernova, can be used alongside with Square Joker. Voucher: Grabber and Nacho Tong give additional hands per round, allowing Square Joker to scale even higher. Boss Blinds: This Joker is easily distinguishable when played against Amber Acorn, as it retains its unique shape even when flipped face-down.

title: Square Joker
text: Square Joker: In general, the only time Square Joker will not scale or score is when a hand is not allowed. Boss Blinds that can prevent specific hands are: The Eye: No repeat hand types this round The Mouth: Only one hand type can be played this round The Psychic: Must play 5 cards Deck: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle all have poor synergy with Square Joker due to their reduced number of hands. Poker hands: The following hands are made up of five cards, and thus cannot scale Square Joker: Straight* Flush* Full House Straight Flush (and Royal Flush)* Five of a Kind Flush House Flush Five *Unless holding Four Fingers.

title: Square Joker
text: Square Joker: Flush* Full House Straight Flush (and Royal Flush)* Five of a Kind Flush House Flush Five *Unless holding Four Fingers. Boss Blind: The Psychic forces the player to play five cards, which means that Square Joker cannot scale. Trivia: The artwork of this Joker is an exaggerated version of pixel art, which is slightly ironic considering all the artwork in this game is in that style. Even the "Joker" text on the card has been squared off, with chunky letters. The value 4 is a square number, which are numbers made by multiplying one number with itself. 4 is 22, or 2×2. The Joker's sprite is also exactly a square, being 138x138 pixels.

title: Square Joker
text: Square Joker: The Joker's sprite is also exactly a square, being 138x138 pixels. This Joker is part of a set that doesn't adhere to the standard joker size, along with Wee Joker, Photograph, and Half Joker. In early versions, Square Joker had the same size as other Jokers. This was changed in 1.0.1f. The Steam Trading Card of Square Joker still retains its old shape. Of all of the scaling Chip Jokers, Square Joker is the only one to not include a plus in the "(Currently +# Chips)" area.

title: Steel Joker
text: Steel Joker: Steel Joker (Joker). Effect: Gives X0.2 Mult for each Steel Card in your full deck, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Spawn Condition: Only obtainable if there is at least 1 Steel card currently in the player's deck. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Steel Joker is an Uncommon Multiplicative Mult Joker that gives X0.2 Mult for each Steel card in your full deck.

title: Steel Joker
text: Steel Joker: It can be a top-tier multiplier card, assuming you can put lots of Steel cards into your deck. The combination of Steel cards in hand plus the high multiplier of Steel Joker can easily create high scoring hands. Getting Steel cards into your deck is the biggest challenge with this Joker. You will need to invest heavily in booster packs. This Joker can only appear if you currently have at least one Steel card in your full deck.

title: Steel Joker
text: Steel Joker: This Joker can only appear if you currently have at least one Steel card in your full deck. Synergies: To synergize with the Steel Joker, there are two approaches: one is to maximize the number of Steel cards in the deck, and the second is to maximize the scoring potential of the Steel cards that will be in your hand. In general, Steel cards benefit from having a high base multiplier after scoring the cards, since Steel cards act before any Jokers. As such, Planet cards and Jokers that add multiplier upon scoring cards can help boost scores.

title: Steel Joker
text: Steel Joker: Decks: Steel Joker works well with all decks, but Steel Joker is particularly well suited to the Plasma Deck. Since the combination of multipliers between Steel Joker and Steel cards can significantly boost mult well beyond any possible chip combinations, Plasma helps turn that high mult into a much higher score. Poker hands: Steel cards tends to work best with smaller hand types (high card, pair, etc.). This allows you to keep more cards in hand, capitalizing on the many Steel cards in the deck. Jokers: There are only a few good direct synergies with Steel Joker: DNA is very helpful, as it can be used to duplicate Steel cards each round.

title: Steel Joker
text: Steel Joker: DNA is very helpful, as it can be used to duplicate Steel cards each round. Mime retriggers all "in hand" cards, which should include many Steel cards. Tarot creating Jokers such as Vagabond, Cartomancer or Hallucination can create some of the tarot cards described in the Consumables section below. Some other potential synergies include: Burnt Joker will upgrade the level of the first discarded Poker hand. This allows you to easily level up a hand without buying planet cards, increasing the base multiplier. This can be useful if you're going for a High Card build.

title: Steel Joker
text: Steel Joker: Any + Mult joker that triggers before the steel multipliers, such as Fibonacci, Onyx Agate or Smiley Face can help with scoring when not having a lot of Steel cards yet. Consumables: Steel Joker requires lots of Steel cards to maximize its value. Use Tarot and Spectral cards to boost the amount of Steel cards you have: The Chariot enhances one card into a Steel card. Death can be used to duplicate a Steel card. Familiar, Grim, and Incantation all have a chance to create Steel cards but might destroy a Steel card in the process. Cryptid can be used to create copies of a Steel card. All Standard Packs have a chance to contain Steel cards.

title: Steel Joker
text: Steel Joker: All Standard Packs have a chance to contain Steel cards. Apart from turning cards into steel, there are other consumable cards that pair well with the Steel enhancement: Deja Vu can add a red seal to a Steel card. This will retrigger the card, adding another X1.5 Mult to the multiplier. Vouchers: Illusion can have a chance for Steel cards to appear in the shop, which can be bought to scale Steel Joker. This can be further increased with help from Overstock and Overstock Plus to increase the shop selection, plus Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut to make rerolling cheaper. Jokers: Vampire might be harder to scale when trying to keep Steel cards in the deck.

title: Steel Joker
text: Steel Joker: Jokers: Vampire might be harder to scale when trying to keep Steel cards in the deck. Trivia: Steel Joker's image is identical to the base Joker, but with a Steel card skin applied. Unlike playing cards, which retain their color when steeled, Steel Joker is entirely grayscale. This Joker is part of a series, along with Stone Joker, Glass Joker, Golden Ticket and Lucky Cat, where the Joker only appears once players have at least one card with the relevant enhancement currently in their deck.

title: Stone Joker
text: Stone Joker: Stone Joker (Joker). Effect: Gives +25 Chips for each Stone Card in your full deck, (Currently +0 Chips). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Spawn Condition: Only obtainable if there is at least 1 Stone card currently in the player's deck. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Chips. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Stone Joker is an Uncommon Chips Joker that gains +25 Chips for every Stone card in the player's deck. It scales very quickly if players manage to acquire a lot of Stone cards, either via Tarot cards or from purchasing Booster Packs.

title: Stone Joker
text: Stone Joker: This Joker will only appear once players have at least one Stone card currently in their deck. Decks: Plasma Deck works best with this Joker thanks to its balancing feature, as Chips scale a lot faster than Mult. Medusa and Monolith both work well with Stone Joker, as these decks both start with a Marble Joker, which means Stone Joker gains +25 Chips for free each blind. Not only that, Medusa also starts with twelve Stone cards.

title: Stone Joker
text: Stone Joker: Poker hands: Any hands can benefit from Stone Joker, as it provides a flat Chips bonus; however, any build based around hands that require 5 cards can be made more difficult due to the increasing number of stone cards in the deck. As such, hands with 4 or fewer cards tend to work best. A hand of five stone cards is considered a High Card, making this one of the best types of hands to build around with Stone Joker. Jokers: Marble Joker provides one Stone card every blind, effectively scaling Stone Joker at the same time.

title: Stone Joker
text: Stone Joker: Jokers: Marble Joker provides one Stone card every blind, effectively scaling Stone Joker at the same time. Blueprint or Brainstorm can be paired with Marble Joker to add up to 2 Stone cards every blind, providing 50 Chips for Stone Joker, or even 75 Chips if both are owned. Blueprint or Brainstorm can be reordered after completing a blind but before selecting a new blind, allowing it to both create a second Stone card through Marble Joker and double the chip bonus of Stone Joker (or doubling a more valuable joker if you have one). DNA lets you duplicate Stone cards to increase this card's chip bonus quicker.

title: Stone Joker
text: Stone Joker: DNA lets you duplicate Stone cards to increase this card's chip bonus quicker. Pareidolia can be used to make the Stone cards added to increase Stone Joker's value more useful by allowing them to count as face cards for effects such as Scary Face, Smiley Face and Sock and Buskin. Consumables: The Tower and Death can turn some cards into Stone cards, which increases Stone Joker's chips. Cryptid can be used to generate more Stone cards.

title: Stone Joker
text: Stone Joker: Cryptid can be used to generate more Stone cards. Vouchers: Illusion can have a chance for Stone cards to appear in the shop, which can be bought to scale Stone Joker. This can be further increased with help from Overstock and Overstock Plus to increase the shop selection, plus Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut to make rerolling cheaper. Jokers: Vampire will remove the Stone enhancement from played cards, reducing Stone Joker's chips. While Stone Joker does not necessarily needs to play Stone cards to work, care should still be taken when combining these two Jokers together.

title: Stone Joker
text: Stone Joker: Trivia: This Joker is part of a series, along with Steel Joker, Glass Joker, Golden Ticket, and Lucky Cat, where the Joker only appears once players have at least one card with the relevant enhancement currently in their deck.

title: Stuntman
text: Stuntman: Stuntman (Joker). Effect: +250 Chips,, -2 hand size. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Earn at least 100 million (100,000,000) Chips in a single hand. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Chips. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Stuntman is a Rare Chips Joker that gives +250 Chips at the cost of -2 hand size.

title: Stuntman
text: Stuntman: While Stuntman may appear to be weak at first, it provides an absolutely incredible amount of chips. Given its downside, Stuntman is one of the largest payoffs for running low-scoring hands such as High Card and Pair. To unlock this Joker, the player must score 100,000,000 chips or more. This Joker shares an unlock requirement with the 100,000K achievement. Usage Notes: When obtaining Stuntman within a round, the hand size will decrease, but the current number of cards held remains unchanged. When Stuntman is lost in a round, the hand size will increase while drawing cards immediately. This can be utilized to hold cards far exceeding the hand size (see Strategies).

title: Stuntman
text: Stuntman: Decks: Plasma Deck works very well with Stuntman, as the +250 Chips, when balanced, guarantee players a significant score each hand. Having two Stuntmen can practically clear antes 1-8 by themselves with the Plasma deck, as long as the player does not find themselves with The Psychic. Painted Deck starts with +2 hand size, thus Stuntman's penalty is completely neutralized. However, the -1 Joker Slot penalty makes it harder to build +Mult. Poker Hands: Because Stuntman greatly reduces hand size, smaller hands like High Card and Pair are considered the best option. Jokers: Juggler: +1 hand size, partially offsetting the -2 hand size penalty. Turtle Bean: The +5 hand size completely removes Stuntman's penalty but is only temporary.

title: Stuntman
text: Stuntman: Turtle Bean: The +5 hand size completely removes Stuntman's penalty but is only temporary. Troubadour: +2 hand size, which completely removes Stuntman's penalty, at the cost of -1 hand per round. Blueprint and Brainstorm can both copy Stuntman's 250 Chips bonus without the -2 hand size penalty. Blackboard: A smaller hand size makes it easier to trigger Blackboard's condition. Raised Fist: The reduced hand size makes it easier to play all the smaller ranked cards from your hand. An early Stuntman + Raised Fist can score over 5,000 for each high card played, making it arguably the most efficient money-to-score ratio that two jokers have together.

title: Stuntman
text: Stuntman: Green Joker: Stuntman wants you to play easier to make hands, such as High Card or Pair, which you don't need to discard for, making Green Joker's downside harder to trigger. Consumables: If Stuntman is generated through a Judgement or Wraith, the hand size will only drop during the next card draw. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette vouchers both increase hand size by one, counteracting Stuntman's hand size debuff.

title: Stuntman
text: Stuntman: Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette vouchers both increase hand size by one, counteracting Stuntman's hand size debuff. Blinds: When playing against Crimson Heart, any Joker that gets disabled other than Stuntman will return hand size to normal, but the current hand will stay intact until the next discard (ex 8/6). By quitting to the Main Menu and returning, the hand size will actually permanently increase (ex 8/8), and Stuntman will keep gaining hand size every time another Joker gets disabled. Decks: Five-Card Draw's reduced hand size may make it impossible to play certain poker hands. Jokers: Merry Andy's additional -1 hand size penalty may make it impossible to play certain poker hands. Jokers with held-in-hand abilities vary with Stuntman's effectiveness.

title: Stuntman
text: Stuntman: Jokers with held-in-hand abilities vary with Stuntman's effectiveness. Baron, Shoot the Moon, and Reserved Parking are all weakened due to holding fewer face cards in hand. Consumables: Ouija and Ectoplasm both reduce hand size, which further debuffs the player along with Stuntman. Modifiers: The decreased hand size doesn't allow many Gold cards, Steel cards, and Blue Seals to be utilized. Blinds: The Manacle: -1 hand size can make assembling hands even harder. The Psychic: Must play 5 cards. Stuntman, along with another -2 hand size debuff, can reduce hand size to 4, making the Psychic impossible to beat. If necessary, Stuntman can be sold during the round, and the Hand Size will immediately recover, with the missing cards being drawn.

title: Stuntman
text: Stuntman: Strategies: Stuntman can be used to score naneinf by creating many negative copies of Ankh with Perkeo to repeatedly clone and sell a Stuntman. Each Stuntman sold increases hand size by 2, and because no other scoring Jokers can be used, about 400 Red Seal Steel cards must be used. Trivia: This Joker's appearance might be in reference to the costume worn by the American stuntman Evel Knievel. The "-2 hand size" effect could be a reference to how real-life stuntmen will often perform tricks hands-free, i.e., without both of their hands on the controls to their vehicles. Stuntman has the shortest in-game description of any Uncommon or Rare Joker, at only 23 characters.

title: Stuntman
text: Stuntman: Stuntman has the shortest in-game description of any Uncommon or Rare Joker, at only 23 characters. In other media: Stuntman appeared as a cameo in a crossover collaboration between Balatro and Rusty's Retirement.

title: Supernova
text: Supernova: Supernova (Joker). Effect: Adds the number of times poker hand has been played this run to Mult. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Supernova is a Common Additive Mult Joker that adds Mult based on the number of times that the scoring hand has been played in the current run. Consistently playing the same hands will result in a constantly increasing Mult boost, which can stay useful until late game. The effect is retroactive, meaning players immediately benefit from all the past hands they played before buying this Joker.

title: Supernova
text: Supernova: Decks: Supernova works well with all decks, though it can find particular synergy when playing with a strategy that matches the deck to the poker hand, like Checkered Deck and Flush. Poker hands: The key to Supernova is to play the same hand consistently. Hands that can reliably be made, especially in the early game, help Supernova flourish. Furthermore, the more hands played, the better, so a build focusing on high base mult and chips hands (like straight flush) can prevent you from using all your hands to boost Supernova. This makes Supernova particularly powerful when matched with hands like High Card or Pair. Jokers: Supernova has synergy with the following Jokers:

title: Supernova
text: Supernova: Jokers: Supernova has synergy with the following Jokers: Burglar replaces discards with hands, resulting in more available hands, thus allowing Supernova to scale faster. Green Joker is an additive mult card that grows as more hands are played (however, Green Joker also loses mult with discards, and having multiple additive mult cards can limit your run's potential above Ante 9 or 10). Card Sharp gives X3 Mult when the same hand is played more than once in a round. Space Joker gives a 1 in 4 chance of upgrading a hand when it's played. By playing only one hand type consistently to boost Supernova, you can achieve very high levels for said hand.

title: Supernova
text: Supernova: Burnt Joker easily allows leveling up a poker hand without planet cards (at the effective cost of 1 discard), which is extra beneficial when a single poker hand type is being played. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong give additional hands per round, allowing Supernova to scale faster. Telescope also encourages focusing on a single poker hand, similar to Supernova. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle all have poor synergy with Supernova due to their reduced number of hands. Jokers: If the player only ever plays one hand type, Obelisk will never provide anything above X1 Mult.

title: Supernova
text: Supernova: Jokers: If the player only ever plays one hand type, Obelisk will never provide anything above X1 Mult. If the player skips blinds to level up Throwback, the player will have fewer opportunities to play hands in order to increase Supernova's power. To Do List will always pick random hands to play, making a weird combo with Supernova. Trivia: A supernova is a star exploding at the end of its life. This is somewhat connected with the planet theming for poker hands.

title: Superposition
text: Superposition: Superposition (Joker). Effect: Create a Tarot card if poker hand contains an Ace and a Straight, (Must have room). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Effect. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Superposition is a Common Effect Joker that will gift you a Tarot card whenever you can play a Straight that contains Aces: either Ace/K/Q/J/10 or Ace/2/3/4/5. This also includes Straight Flush and Royal Flush.

title: Superposition
text: Superposition: Decks: Red Deck gives an extra discard, allowing the player to search for Straights with an Ace easier. Blue Deck gives an extra hand, allowing the player to generate more Tarot cards. Painted Deck gives extra hand size, which can help the player with forming Straights with an Ace. Abandoned Deck makes it impossible to get an A/K/Q/J/10 Straight, but about three times easier to assemble an A/2/3/4/5 Straight. Poker hands: Straight with an Ace. Straight Flush (and Royal Flush) with an Ace.

title: Superposition
text: Superposition: Poker hands: Straight with an Ace. Straight Flush (and Royal Flush) with an Ace. Jokers: Shortcut: Normally, there are only two possible straights that contain an ace: A/2/3/4/5 and 10/J/Q/K/A. This makes it relatively difficult to trigger Superposition. Shortcut, however, allows straights to skip single cards, vastly increasing the number of ways this joker can be triggered. Four Fingers: Similarly, though to a lesser extent, Four Fingers makes it easier to trigger Superposition by reducing the requirements for a straight to just 4 consecutive cards instead of 5.

title: Superposition
text: Superposition: Mathematically, assuming a standard 52-card deck: the number of 5-card hands that trigger Superposition increases by a factor of 12 with the addition of Four Fingers, a factor of 16 with the addition of Shortcut, and a factor of 84 with both. Meanwhile, the chance of getting any straight at all increases by a factor of 12.2 with the addition of Four Fingers, a factor of 12.8 with the addition of Shortcut, and a factor of 76.3 with both. Be aware that the Ace must score for Superposition to trigger. 5/6/7/8/A will not trigger Superposition with only Four Fingers, though it will with both Four Fingers and Splash.

title: Superposition
text: Superposition: Jokers that give bonuses from playing Straights, like Devious Joker, Runner, Crazy Joker, and The Order, all work well with Superposition. Scholar and Walkie Talkie: Will give additional chips and Mult, as Straights triggering the Superposition effect will always contain an Ace, plus a 10 or 4. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong give additional hands, allowing the player to generate more Tarot cards. Wasteful and Recyclomancy give additional discards, allowing the player to search for Straights with an Ace easier. Paint Brush and Palette both increase hand size, which can help players with forming Straights with an Ace. Decks: Erratic Deck can make it difficult to use Superposition, as the randomized rank and suit makes it harder to form Straights.

title: Superposition
text: Superposition: Black Deck has slight anti-synergy, as 1 less available hand makes it slightly harder to find Straights. However, it is easier to take Superposition, as it is less likely to take up a crucial Joker slot needed for survival. 15 Minute City and Mad World are not recommended, as these decks don't contain any Aces by default. Five-Card Draw's -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straights with an Ace. Nebula Deck starts with one fewer Consumable Slot, making it harder to hold onto Superposition's Tarot Cards. Jokers: Jokers that reduce hand size, like Stuntman and Merry Andy, have anti-synergy with Superposition, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights with an Ace.

title: Superposition
text: Superposition: Consumables: Ectoplasm and Ouija have anti-synergy with Superposition, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straight with an Ace. Not only that, but Ouija converts all cards held in hand into one single rank, which makes assembling Straights with an Ace less consistent. Blinds: The Manacle's -1 hand size makes it hard to assemble Straights with an Ace. The Water will always start with 0 discards, making it very hard to assemble Straights with an Ace.

title: Superposition
text: Superposition: The Water will always start with 0 discards, making it very hard to assemble Straights with an Ace. Trivia: In quantum mechanics, superposition is the ability of a quantum system to be in multiple states at the same time until it is measured. In Balatro, Aces can be either high or low depending on the rest of the hand. The sprite of this Joker resembles an electron, which can only have +1/2 or -1/2 spin, similar to how Aces can only form high or low straights.

title: Superposition
text: Superposition: The background of the Joker art for Superposition contains a repeating pattern of 𝜓 (psi) and λ→ (lambda with right arrow above). According to LocalThunk, this is a reference to eigenvalue equation A^ψi=λiψi, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics about measurement and the nature of quantum states. 𝜓 is the eigenfunction/eigenstate (a specific quantum state of the system), and 𝜆 is the eigenvalue (value of measuring the observable quantity under this state), which could be a vector. Superposition means the system can be in multiple eigenstates at the same time.

title: Swashbuckler
text: Swashbuckler: Swashbuckler (Joker). Effect: Adds the sell value of all other owned Jokers to Mult, (Currently +1 Mult). Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Sell a total of 20 Joker cards. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Swashbuckler is a Common Additive Mult Joker that provides + Mult equal to the sum of the sell value of all other owned Jokers. This Joker is unlocked once the player sells 20 Jokers.

title: Swashbuckler
text: Swashbuckler: Decks: Black Deck gives an extra Joker slot, meaning Swashbuckler gets more Mult. Similarly, Five-Card Draw gives two extra Joker slots, meaning Swashbuckler gets even more Mult. Swashbuckler generally works well with negative Jokers, as they will increase the amount of Joker slots while also having substantial sell values of their own. Therefore, the Anaglyph Deck can synergize with Swashbuckler, where many players will opt to use their accumulating Double Tag on a Negative Tag. The Omelette works very well with Swashbuckler, as this deck starts with multiple Eggs. With 4 Eggs, this Joker gains +12 Mult at the end of every Blind.

title: Swashbuckler
text: Swashbuckler: Inflation also works well with Swashbuckler, as this deck permanently increases prices by $1 on every purchase, including the sell price. This Joker can provide a high amount of + Mult since it will scale when other Jokers' prices inflate. Poker hands: Any poker hand can benefit from Swashbuckler. Jokers: Generally, Swashbuckler gets more benefits when it is with higher-rarity Jokers due to their higher sell values. In particular, the Legendary Jokers have a massive sell value of $10, which is double that of the next highest base sell value. Some other notable synergies are: Gift Card adds to the sell value for all other jokers at once, effectively scaling Swashbuckler over time.

title: Swashbuckler
text: Swashbuckler: Gift Card adds to the sell value for all other jokers at once, effectively scaling Swashbuckler over time. Egg increases its sell value by $3 per blind, effectively scaling Swashbuckler over time. When either of the two previous Jokers has been paired with Swashbuckler for long enough, Ceremonial Dagger is a very effective pivot away from Swashbuckler; because it will multiply built-up sell values by X2, it can both increase immediate scoring and open up a Joker Slot (or more) for other purposes. Vouchers: Hone and Glow Up make it more likely for editioned Jokers to appear, which have a higher sell value, helping Swashbuckler gain +Mult. Antimatter gives an extra Joker slot, meaning Swashbuckler gets more Mult.

title: Swashbuckler
text: Swashbuckler: Antimatter gives an extra Joker slot, meaning Swashbuckler gets more Mult. Decks: Swashbuckler's effectiveness can be decreased when using the Painted Deck, Blast Off, and Cruelty due to their reduced Joker slots. Jokers: Credit Card. Joker, Jolly Joker, Sly Joker and Splash all have a sell value of $1, which is not good for Swashbuckler. Vouchers: Clearance Sale and Liquidation are not recommended, as they reduce the sell price of all Jokers and thus reduce the +Mult of Swashbuckler. Blinds: Verdant Leaf requires selling a Joker, which means that unless the player does not rely on enhanced cards to win, Swashbuckler will lose +Mult. Stakes: Gold Stake introduces Rental Stickers, which only have a sell value of $1.

title: Swashbuckler
text: Swashbuckler: Stakes: Gold Stake introduces Rental Stickers, which only have a sell value of $1. Trivia: Swashbucklers in fiction tend to be heroic types skilled in swordplay, acrobatics, and charm, ready to rescue princesses and with a strong sense of honour. Famous swashbucklers include Robin Hood, The Three Musketeers, and the Princess Bride's Dread Pirate Roberts. Swashbuckler's default Mult value is +1 Mult, which can be seen when checking it in the collection of Main Menu. It still gives +0 Mult during a run if there are no other Jokers.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Séance (Joker). Effect: If poker hand is a Straight Flush, create a random Spectral card, (Must have room). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Séance is an Uncommon Effect Joker that gives a Spectral card whenever a Straight Flush is played. This also includes Royal Flush.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Séance cannot provide The Soul or Black Hole, as both can only be found in Booster Packs. Synergies: Séance is a bit of an odd Joker, as very few Spectral cards benefit from full Straight Flush builds. It is best used as a temporary Spectral generator that does not have limited uses, like Sixth Sense does, to create useful Spectrals that can then facilitate other builds. Anything that benefits from certain Spectral cards, theoretically, has some synergy with Séance. For this reason, the synergies listed are split into two sections: ways to make more Straight Flushes, to maximize the Spectral cards Séance can give; and ways to use those Spectral cards to their maximum effect.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Decks: Checkered Deck is by far the best one to use Séance, as it is much easier to create Straight Flushes with fewer differing suits. Red Deck, Blue Deck, and Painted Deck all make it slightly easier to find Straight Flushes. Magic Deck's Fool cards are incredibly helpful, as they can be used to create a Suit-changing Tarot that can be used in a round to guarantee a Straight Flush. Starting with an extra consumable slot is also great for holding more Spectral cards. 15 Minute City starts with an Eternal Shortcut, which allows Straight Flushes to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Poker hands: Straight Flushes (and Royal Flushes) are the only hands relevant to this Joker. Helping Séance: Four Fingers and Shortcut both make Straight Flushes easier to play, allowing Séance to trigger more often. Smeared Joker is also helpful for making Straight Flushes, as it doubles the amount of cards one can use for a Straight Flush of any given suit. Jokers that give bonuses when Straights are scored, like Devious Joker and Crazy Joker, can be helpful to make the Straight Flushes Séance needs better to play.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Troubadour and Juggler make Straight Flushes easier to find with their increases in hand size. Drunkard and Merry Andy do the same by adding more discards. Merry Andy is slightly less effective at this unless the player has more hand size, though, as you may be discarding fewer cards.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Perkeo allows you to duplicate the Spectral card created in the consumable slots at the end of the shop. This can be very strong for a multitude of different strategies, such as using Cryptids to create large amounts of cards whenever needed, holding multiple Wraiths to see many rare Jokers at once, copying Sigils to guarantee a Straight Flush as long as a Straight is present, using Immolate many times to thin massive amounts of the deck, and many more. Burglar allows the player to play more Straight Flushes each round, thus generating additional spectral cards.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Burglar allows the player to play more Straight Flushes each round, thus generating additional spectral cards. Making use of Séance's Spectral cards: A number of Spectral cards add enhanced cards to the deck, which can let Hologram and Vampire scale more. Due to being able to add so many enhanced cards so quickly, Driver's License can become an easy addition as well. If one can create a Hex/ Ankh and Ectoplasms, Joker Stencil can become very strong, as you can massively increase the effective Mult given by applying Polychrome to it or duplicating it (or both), then add other Jokers that do not decrease Stencil's value.

title: Séance
text: Séance: DNA can be used to copy better cards, as Séance can create the Aura Spectral card and Seal-applying Spectral cards. These Spectral cards can be saved until a desirable card is drawn, then used on it, then the card can be copied with DNA. As many Spectral cards can be used to make Five of a Kind or Flush Five more likely, mainly Ouija and Cryptid, Jokers that work better in these kinds of builds, like The Family, or rank-specific ones like Fibonacci, Scholar, Wee Joker, Hit the Road, etc., can become better.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Early Sigils can be used to convert many cards in your deck to the same suit, making suit-based Jokers like Arrowhead, Onyx Agate, Bloodstone, etc. better if their suit is the one chosen. Erosion very much appreciates an Immolate from Séance. It does conflict with other Spectral cards that add cards, though. Because you can hold onto a Wraith, Credit Card becomes very valuable, as you can spend the $20 of debt, sell Credit Card, then use Wraith to eliminate the debt and obtain a Rare Joker. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong both give +1 hand, allowing the player to play more Straight Flushes and generate more Spectral cards.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give +1 discard, allowing the player to search for Straight Flushes easier.
