Paint Brush and Palette both give +1 hand size, which can help the player to form Straight Flushes easier. Decks: Erratic Deck can make it difficult to use Séance, as the randomized rank and suit makes it harder to form Straight Flushes. Black Deck has slight anti-synergy, as 1 less available hand makes it slightly harder to find Straight Flushes. However, it is easier to take Séance, as it is less likely to take up a crucial Joker slot needed for survival. Five-Card Draw's -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straight Flushes.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Five-Card Draw's -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straight Flushes. Nebula Deck starts with one fewer Consumable Slot, making it harder to hold onto Séance's Spectral Cards. Jokers: Jokers that reduce hand size, like Stuntman and Merry Andy, have anti-synergy with Séance, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straight Flushes. Glass Joker has slight anti-synergy with Séance, since due to a bug, Spectral Cards that destroy cards (such as Immolate) will not scale Glass Joker when destroying Glass cards.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Consumables: Ectoplasm and Ouija have anti-synergy with Séance, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straight Flushes. Not only that, but Ouija converts all cards held in hand into one single rank, which makes assembling Straight Flushes less consistent. Blinds: The Manacle's -1 hand size makes it hard to assemble Straight Flushes. The Water will always start with 0 discards, making it very hard to assemble Straight Flushes. Trivia: A séance is a traditional method for communicating with spirits or the dead. Often, but not necessarily, a group is seated around a table with a medium leading the ritual.

title: Séance
text: Séance: Séance is the only Joker in Balatro that uses a letter with a diacritic in its English name. The letter é is an e with an acute accent, or l'accent aigu in French. As a part of the Ghost Deck Playing Cards set by Fangamer, Séance is one of the four Jokers to be featured next to Mr. Bones, Sixth Sense, and Castle.

title: The Duo
text: The Duo: The Duo (Joker). Effect: X2 Mult if played hand contains a Pair. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Win a run without playing a Pair. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. The Duo is a Rare Multiplicative Mult Joker that grants X2 Mult any time a hand containing a Pair is played. It can be unlocked by winning a run without playing a Pair, though playing other hands that contain pairs, such as Three of a Kind, are allowed.

title: The Duo
text: The Duo: Since The Duo offers only X2 Mult and has no scaling potential, it has limited utility past Ante 8. Usage Notes: Winning a run without playing a Pair is not difficult as hands played that contain Pairs do not count towards the unlock requirement. Nonetheless, there is a clear winner in which Deck to use to unlock The Duo: Checkered Deck allows the player to play Flushes consistently throughout the run, being able to avoid Pairs a large majority of the time.

title: The Duo
text: The Duo: The played Pair does not need to score for The Duo to activate. The only way to have this happen is when playing a Flush with Four Fingers that also has a differently suited Pair (ex: 10 9 4 3 of Spades and 10 of Diamonds). The Duo can also activate on a Straight with Four Fingers when there is a repeated rank (ex: 10 10 9 8 7). Revealing a pair of matching ranks via Vampire removing Stone from a card will not activate The Duo; the determination is made when the hand is played, not when the Joker effect activates.

title: The Duo
text: The Duo: Decks: All Decks work equally well, though Erratic Deck is slightly better, because the odds of a finding a Pair are higher given the unequal distribution of the Deck. Poker hands: Although only a X2 Mult boost, this Joker can trigger on every hand except High Card: Pair, Two Pair Three of a Kind, Four of a Kind, Five of a Kind Full House, Flush House Flush Five Flush, when a pair is present in the played hand Straight and Straight Flush, when containing a pair using Four Fingers (ex: 10 9 9 8 7) Jokers: Any Joker that provides benefits to hands that contain Pairs provide direct synergy, such as: Pair: Jolly Joker and Sly Joker.

title: The Duo
text: The Duo: Pair: Jolly Joker and Sly Joker. Two Pair: Mad Joker, Clever Joker, and Spare Trousers. Three of a Kind: Zany Joker and Wily Joker. Half Joker works reasonably well to provide some base Mult to feed into The Duo, although it does limit the player to only playing a maximum of 3 cards per hand. Supernova and Card Sharp are also decent choices if the player wishes to lean into a specific poker hand type. Seeing Double is another option provided the player always includes a Club and Non-Club in the hand that contains the Pair.

title: The Duo
text: The Duo: Space Joker or Burnt Joker can level up Pairs to steadily increase its scoring power, which is relatively weak compared to harder to form poker hands. Pairs of specific ranks can be useful for the following Jokers: Fibonacci: Aces, 2s, 3s, 5s, and 8s. Scary Face and Smiley Face: Kings, Queens, and Jacks. Scholar: Aces. 8 Ball: 8s. Even Steven: 2s, 4s, 6s, 8s, and 10s. Odd Todd: Aces, 3s, 5s, 7s, and 9s. Walkie Talkie: 4s and 10s. Triboulet: Kings and Queens.

title: The Duo
text: The Duo: Odd Todd: Aces, 3s, 5s, 7s, and 9s. Walkie Talkie: 4s and 10s. Triboulet: Kings and Queens. Trivia: This Joker is part of a set that gives strong Mult boosts for playing specific hands, which are unlocked by winning a run without playing that hand. The others are The Trio, The Family, The Order and The Tribe. Though all 5 Jokers have identical, color-swapped backgrounds, The Duo has small portions in the center that differ from every other in the set. This Joker has similar colors to Jolly Joker and Sly Joker, two other Jokers that give bonuses if the played hand contains a Pair.

title: The Family
text: The Family: The Family (Joker). Effect: X4 Mult if played hand contains a Four of a Kind. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Win a run without playing a Four of a Kind. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. The Family is a Rare Multiplicative Mult Joker that grants a powerful X4 Mult any time you play a hand that contains a Four of a Kind.

title: The Family
text: The Family: It can be unlocked by winning a run without playing a Four of a Kind (though playing other hands that contain four cards of the same rank, such as Five of a Kind, are allowed for the unlock condition). Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World work well with this Joker thanks to their smaller deck, making searching for Four of a Kind easier. Erratic Deck can work well with this Joker if it randomizes a lot of cards with the same rank. Poker hands: The Family will trigger on any hand containing a Four of a Kind: Four of a Kind Five of a Kind Flush Five

title: The Family
text: The Family: Four of a Kind Five of a Kind Flush Five Jokers: Any jokers that trigger with Three of a Kind hands and Pair hands, such as Zany Joker and The Duo. Drunkard and Merry Andy give extra discards, which makes it easier to find a Four of a Kind. Merry Andy's hand size downside is pretty much meaningless with the extra discards, as long as the player does not reduce their hand size much further.

title: The Family
text: The Family: Juggler and Troubadour increase hand size, which makes it easier to find a Four of a Kind. Troubadour's -1 hand punishment is pretty much meaningless on early antes as a single X4 Mult can beat some antes with good + Mult. Turtle Bean can also be used, but not permanently like the other 2 Jokers. Trivia: This Joker is part of a set that gives strong Mult boosts for playing specific hands, which are unlocked by winning a run without playing that hand. The others are The Duo, The Trio, The Order and The Tribe.

title: The Family
text: The Family: This Joker has similar colors to Mad Joker and Clever Joker, two Jokers that give bonuses if the played hand contains a Two Pair. It is the only such XMult Joker to not share its preferred hand type with the preceding pair of +Chips and +Mult Jokers. The basis for this Joker's name likely comes from the term "nuclear family", which describes a family unit that traditionally consists of four people: the father, the mother, and two children (usually both a son and daughter).

title: The Idol
text: The Idol: The Idol (Joker). Effect: Each played [rank] of [suit] gives X2 Mult when scored, Card changes every round. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: In one hand, earn at least 1,000,000 chips. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. The Idol is an Uncommon Multiplicative Mult Joker that provides X2 Mult when a card with a chosen rank and suit is scored. For example, the card may be an Ace of Spades, or 7 of Diamonds. The chosen card is decided at the end of each round by selecting a random card from your deck.

title: The Idol
text: The Idol: To unlock this Joker, the player must score 1,000,000 chips or more. This Joker shares an unlock requirement with the 1,000K achievement. Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World can make it easier to manipulate the deck into one type of card due to the reduced number of starting cards. Zodiac Deck starts with Tarot Merchant, which can be helpful to manipulate the deck in your favor using Tarot cards. Checkered Deck starts with 2 of every card rather than 1, making The Idol slightly more consistent to activate in the early game. Poker hands: Flush Five works exceptionally well with The Idol because it can trigger the effect 5 times, plus any additional retriggers from Jokers or Red Seal.

title: The Idol
text: The Idol: If using The Idol, it's best to play a Flush Five as soon as possible in order to unlock its respective Planet card, Eris. In the early to midgame, one can make do with Three of a Kind and Four of a Kind, assuming the correct card is chosen by The Idol. Due to the highly random nature of the card, you will likely want more reliable sources of score before you can fully utilize it. That said, using this Joker in the early to midgame is nearly impossible. Jokers: Jokers that retrigger scored cards, such as Dusk or Hack, will compound the multiplication immensely.

title: The Idol
text: The Idol: Jokers: Jokers that retrigger scored cards, such as Dusk or Hack, will compound the multiplication immensely. Jokers that help manipulate the deck to fewer types of cards will make the randomly chosen card more likely to be desirable. DNA or Trading Card are the most important jokers for accomplishing this. Smeared Joker effectively halves the number of unique cards in any given deck (aside from Checkered Deck) and may be worth considering on some runs. Tarot cards: The Hanged Man and Death can be used to remove undesired card(s), making The Idol more consistent. Thus, Vagabond can be one of the best ways to enable The Idol. The Lovers can generate Wild cards, which can trigger The Idol.

title: The Idol
text: The Idol: The Lovers can generate Wild cards, which can trigger The Idol. The Tower can also be used to make The Idol more consistent, as The Idol cannot choose Stone cards to buff. Spectral cards: Immolate will destroy 5 random cards in hand, making it easier to get The Idol trigger. Jokers: Hologram requires you to add cards to your deck for Joker scaling, making this Joker more inconsistent in scoring, unless you add your desired cards with DNA. Certificate always adds cards with a random rank and suit, making an awkward combo with The Idol.

title: The Idol
text: The Idol: Certificate always adds cards with a random rank and suit, making an awkward combo with The Idol. Strategies: The rank and suit are decided by pulling a random non- Stone card from your deck. Thus, if you have multiples of a particular rank or suit, it will be proportionally likely for that value to be chosen. While it can be underwhelming early game, it excels late game when the proper deck manipulation can be put into place. A Flush Five containing five of The Idol's target card yields X32 Mult, retriggers notwithstanding. However, it is one of the more difficult Jokers to extract the most use out of.

title: The Idol
text: The Idol: The best cards to build around are those that can be retriggered more times by other Jokers. 2's, 3's, 4's, and 5's can be retriggered by Hack, while face cards (J, Q, K) can be retriggered by Sock and Buskin. Trivia: The card art depicts a colorful wood carving of a head, also known as a tiki idol. If the deck has no card with any rank and suit (i.e., full Stone cards), The Idol will default to X2 Mult per played Ace of Spades.

title: The Order
text: The Order: The Order (Joker). Effect: X3 Mult if played hand contains a Straight. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Win a run without playing a Straight. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. The Order is a Rare Multiplicative Mult Joker that grants X3 Mult any time you play a Straight. It can be unlocked by winning a run without playing a Straight (though playing other hands that contain straights, such as Straight Flush, are allowed).

title: The Order
text: The Order: Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World both have fewer cards than usual, which makes it easier to make Straights. Painted Deck's extra hand size makes Straights easier to find. 15 Minute City starts with an Eternal Shortcut, which allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand. Poker hands: The Order will trigger on Straights and Straight Flushes. As all Straight hands have high Chip scaling from Planet cards, The Order can lend itself well to high-level Straight or Straight Flush runs. Jokers: Four Fingers and Shortcut both allow Straights to be made more easily. Having either of these will make Straight builds much more reliable, making The Order easier to trigger.

title: The Order
text: The Order: Jokers that give bonuses when Straights are played, like Crazy Joker and Devious Joker, work well with The Order. Runner is the primary example of this, as it gives scaling Chips when the player plays the hand they already want to play if they have The Order. Sources of easy +Mult are useful in the early antes, such as Mystic Summit, as they allow The Order to multiply a larger amount of Mult without having to level Straights first.

title: The Order
text: The Order: Séance, if it can be properly utilized, can be a source of Spectral cards that can help Straight builds, like Aura, Incantation/ Familiar & Grim (depending on which Straights one is playing more often), and Immolate to destroy certain ranks not used in your Straights. In the same vein, Superposition gives mild synergy by giving a Tarot card from high and low Ace Straights, but this isn't very strong compared to the benefits of many other Jokers.

title: The Order
text: The Order: Deck thinning is more useful to Straight builds than others, as adding cards doesn't necessarily make Straights more likely. For this reason, Trading Card and Erosion can form a strong combo with The Order, as the player can destroy all cards that aren't in your chosen Straight, making them more likely, and provide scaling Mult for The Order to work off of. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy give additional discards, allowing the player to search for Straight hands easier. Paint Brush and Palette both increase hand size, which can help players with forming Straights. Telescope can help upgrade Straight using Saturn.

title: The Order
text: The Order: Telescope can help upgrade Straight using Saturn. Decks: Erratic Deck can make it difficult to use The Order, as the randomized rank and suit makes it harder to form Straights. Five-Card Draw's -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straights. Jokers: Jokers that reduce hand size, like Stuntman and Merry Andy, have anti-synergy with The Order, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Consumables: Ectoplasm and Ouija have anti-synergy with The Order, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Not only that, but Ouija converts all cards held in hand into one single rank, which makes assembling Straights less consistent.

title: The Order
text: The Order: Blinds: The Manacle's -1 hand size makes it hard to assemble Straights. The Water will always start with 0 discards, making it very hard to assemble Straights. Trivia: This joker is part of a set that gives XMult boosts for playing specific hands, which are all unlocked by winning a run without playing that hand. The others are The Duo, The Trio, The Family and The Tribe. This Joker has similar colors to Crazy Joker and Devious Joker, two other Jokers that give bonuses if the played hand contains a Straight.

title: The Tribe
text: The Tribe: The Tribe (Joker). Effect: X2 Mult if played hand contains a Flush. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Win a run without playing a Flush. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. The Tribe is a Rare Multiplicative Mult Joker that offers X2 Mult any time you play a Flush. It can be unlocked by winning a run without playing a Flush (though playing other hands that contain flushes, such as Flush House, are allowed).

title: The Tribe
text: The Tribe: Since The Tribe only offers X2 Mult and has no scaling potential, it has limited utility past Ante 8. Compared to the other hand-specific multiplicative mult cards, The Tribe is probably the weakest, because it only works with 4 possible hands (and only 2 of those are accessible without deck modification). However, if you have a deck that lends itself to flushes with the occasional high-value flush (like Flush House or Flush Five), The Tribe may be a better option. Usage Notes: The Flush does not need to score for The Tribe to activate. This can happen when playing a Four of a Kind with 5 cards of the same suit (ex: K K K K 8 of Spades).

title: The Tribe
text: The Tribe: Decks: Checkered Deck will almost always get value from The Tribe, since it excels at making Flushes. Poker hands: Flush: The hand this Joker is specifically made for. Straight Flush: A much more valuable hand, use Tarot cards and Standard Packs to make playing a Straight Flush easier. Flush House/Flush Five: The two most valuable base hands in the game, which both contain Flushes. Try to pick up cards that make playing these possible. Jokers: Four Fingers and Smeared Joker make it easier to play Flushes and trigger this Joker's multiplier. Any Joker that adds multiplier based on played cards of certain suit, such as Gluttonous Joker.

title: The Tribe
text: The Tribe: Any Joker that adds multiplier based on played cards of certain suit, such as Gluttonous Joker. Troubadour gives extra hand size, making it easier to find cards of the same suit. Crafty Joker and Droll Joker trigger on the same condition, giving them natural synergy. Consumables: Tarot cards: The Moon, The Star, The Sun, and The World turn cards into Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, and Spades, respectively, which can be useful if the player wants their deck to focus on one or two suits. The Hanged Man can be useful for cutting unwanted cards out the deck if the player wants to focus on one particular card suit.

title: The Tribe
text: The Tribe: The Lovers turn a card into a Wild card, which can be useful for forming a Flush if the player is down a card or two needed. Trivia: Out of all the cards that give multipliers for specific hands, this shares the weakest bonus alongside The Duo. This joker is part of a set that gives strong Mult boosts for playing specific hands, which are unlocked by winning a run without playing that hand. The others are The Duo, The Trio, The Family and The Order. This Joker has similar colors to Droll Joker and Crafty Joker, two other Jokers that give bonuses if the played hand contains a Flush.

title: The Tribe
text: The Tribe: A "tribe" is a unit of people that share common ancestry, beliefs, language, etc. This ties in with the Joker's ability, as Flushes are only able to be played if all the cards share the same suit.

title: The Trio
text: The Trio: The Trio (Joker). Effect: X3 Mult if played hand contains a Three of a Kind. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Win a run without playing a Three of a Kind. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. The Trio is a Rare Multiplicative Mult Joker that grants X3 Mult any time you play a hand that contains a Three of a Kind.

title: The Trio
text: The Trio: It can be unlocked by winning a run without playing a Three of a Kind (though playing other hands that contain three cards of the same rank, such as Full House, are allowed for the unlock condition). Usage Notes: The Three of a Kind does not need to score for The Trio to activate. The only way to have this happen is when playing a Flush with Four Fingers that also has a differently suited Three of a Kind (ex: ♠️10 ♠️10 ♦️10 ♠️4 ♠️3). Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World work well with this Joker thanks to their smaller deck, allowing assembling a Three of a Kind easier.

title: The Trio
text: The Trio: Erratic Deck can work well with this Joker if it randomizes a lot of cards with the same rank. Poker hands: This Joker can trigger on any played hand containing three cards of the same rank: Three of a Kind, Four of a Kind, Five of a Kind Full House, Flush House Flush Five Flush, when a Three of a Kind is present in the played hand Jokers: Wily Joker gives +100 Chips when played hand contains a Three of a Kind. Zany Joker gives +12 Mult when played hand contains a Three of a Kind. Playing a Three of a Kind or above will also trigger Jokers that trigger with Pair hands such as Jolly Joker and The Duo.

title: The Trio
text: The Trio: Trivia: This joker is part of a set that gives strong Mult boosts for playing specific hands, which are unlocked by winning a run without playing that hand. The others are The Duo, The Family, The Order and The Tribe. This Joker has similar colors to Zany Joker and Wily Joker, two other Jokers that give bonuses if the played hand contains a Three of a Kind.

title: Throwback
text: Throwback: Throwback (Joker). Effect: X0.25 Mult for each Blind skipped this run, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Continue a saved run from the main menu. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Throwback is an Uncommon scaling Multiplicative Mult Joker that gains X0.25 Mult for each Blind skipped in a run. It starts at X1 Mult. This effect is retroactive in that Blinds skipped before picking it up count towards its XMult. It is unlocked by going to the main menu and continuing an ongoing run.

title: Throwback
text: Throwback: Decks: Anaglyph Deck can be useful when running Throwback, as the Double Tags it generates make skipping Blinds more appealing. Fragile can work with Throwback, as this deck encourages the player to preserve as many Glass cards as possible to beat ante 8, for which skipping blinds can be useful. Jokers: Jokers that have powerful up-front effects generally work great with Throwback, as they allow you to skip blinds and boost Throwback without compromising the other Jokers' scaling. Flat +Mult jokers in particular, such as Half Joker, Mystic Summit, etc., can provide a larger base mult for Throwback, though depending on the hand type, per-card mult boosts may be stronger.

title: Throwback
text: Throwback: Since Throwback can boost mult to very high values, it can be worth investing in a +Chips joker, like Stuntman or Bull, to improve that side of the equation. Since Throwback prioritizes skipping blinds, consumable Jokers (Popcorn, Ice Cream, Seltzer, and similar) go through fewer hands, allowing them to be useful for more Antes. Diet Cola empowers the skips you do, allowing you to double the bonus from a strong tag. Card modifiers: Glass cards work very well with Throwback, as you can gain X2 Mult, and the risk of losing the cards is reduced because you are playing fewer hands.

title: Throwback
text: Throwback: Vouchers: Hieroglyph and Petroglyph lower the Ante by 1, giving another Small Blind and Big Blind each to skip, and thus, two more opportunities to increase Throwback's multiplier. Tags: Speed Tag gives $5 for every skipped blind, which is what Throwback already incentivizes. Jokers: Because Throwback needs to skip Blinds to scale, it is usually a poor combination with Jokers that require action taken in Blinds or the shop to scale. For example, Hologram, Vampire, Supernova, and Madness. It can be decent if a couple of blinds were skipped in the past as a temporary midgame choice, but there are often better alternatives for builds that use these kinds of scaling.

title: Throwback
text: Throwback: Trivia: The name Throwback is possibly a reference to the 80s styling of this Joker, with the arcade carpet detailing in the background lending a retro feel. It may also be a reference to the vaporwave internet phenomenon. It is one of the five Jokers to have a physical card from Balatro: Special Edition. The four other jokers where that is also the case are Joker, Ice Cream, Hack and Abstract Joker. It is the only Joker that is unlocked by actions performed outside of a run.

title: To Do List
text: To Do List: To Do List (Joker). Effect: Earn $4 if poker hand is a [Poker Hand], poker hand changes at end of round. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Economy. Activation: On Played. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. To Do List is a Common Economy Joker that rewards the player financially for playing specific hands. However, the hand changes after every round, so the player needs to be flexible.

title: To Do List
text: To Do List: Usage Notes: To Do List only applies to the scoring hand, not the hands that it contains. For example, playing a Full House if the chosen hand is Two Pair does not give $4. Each copy of To Do List picks its Poker Hand independently of every other copy. For example, if one were to copy a held To Do List that is on Straight Flush using Ankh, they will both start at Straight Flush. However, once they reset, it is possible that one is on Full House and the other is on High Card. This is unlike all other Jokers with similar random effects (such as Mail-In Rebate, Castle, or Ancient Joker), as all of their copies are "synced".

title: To Do List
text: To Do List: Much like the appearance of planet cards, it has a chance to choose Secret hands if they have been played at least once during the current run. Decks: Red Deck gives +1 Discard, allowing the player more chances to dig through their deck if To Do List requires a more difficult hand to play. Blue Deck gives +1 Hand, meaning that the player has more chances to get more Money from To Do List. Ghost Deck and Zodiac Deck have increased access to Spectral cards and Tarot cards respectively, which can make some of the more difficult hands easier to achieve if To Do List chooses them.

title: To Do List
text: To Do List: Erratic Deck can make hands like Four of a Kind easier to play. However, it can also make it harder to play hands like Straight. Poker hands: The target hand will change randomly every round, so it doesn't synergise with any specific hand. Jokers: Burglar adds 3 extra hands allowing To Do list to generate more money. Drunkard and Merry Andy add more discards which can help the player to find the hand that To Do List chose. Blueprint and Brainstorm can copy To Do List to effectively double/triple amount of money gained with no downside as they can be moved around to buff scoring Jokers afterward. Four Fingers, Shortcut and Smeared Joker all make certain hands easier to play.

title: To Do List
text: To Do List: Four Fingers, Shortcut and Smeared Joker all make certain hands easier to play. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong both give extra hands allowing To Do List to generate more money. Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give extra discards allowing the player to find the hand that To Do List chose. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle don't allow the player many chances for To Do List to trigger due to their reduced number of hands. Jokers: Any joker which incentivizes playing a consistent hand type throughout a run like Runner, Supernova or Spare Trousers has a slight anti-synergy with To Do list. When running Obelisk, it is possible for To Do List to land on your most played hand.

title: To Do List
text: To Do List: When running Obelisk, it is possible for To Do List to land on your most played hand. Trivia: The first letters of each item on the card are an acrostic that spells "J-O-K-E-R".

title: To the Moon
text: To the Moon: To the Moon (Joker). Effect: Earn an extra $1 of interest for every $5 you have at end of round. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Economy. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. To the Moon is an Uncommon Economy Joker that gives an extra $1 of interest for every $5 held at the end of a round. Extra interest earned by the card is based on how much money the player is holding and limited by the current interest cap ($5 by default). The interest cap can be increased by buying Seed Money and Money Tree. It is worth noting that the effect of To The Moon stacks with multiple copies of itself, gaining an extra $2 interest for every $5 held with two copies, an extra $3 with three copies, and so on and so forth.

title: To the Moon
text: To the Moon: Usage notes: The Omelette challenge bans To the Moon. Decks: Yellow Deck, as this deck tends to allow the player to reach the initial Interest cap earlier. Jokers: Jokers that rely on Money, like Bull and Red Card, are boosted from the extra Interest To the Moon offers. Money generating jokers that provide Money during the round, like Rough Gem and Mail-In Rebate can help the player reach Interest thresholds. Modifiers: Gold cards and Gold Seal allow money generation mid-round, meaning the money they make counts toward interest earned at the end.

title: To the Moon
text: To the Moon: Vouchers: Seed Money and Money Tree have one of the strongest synergies with To The Moon, as they raise the base interest cap. With both vouchers, To the Moon can end up producing $40 at the end of every round. Decks: Avoid this Joker on Green Deck and Mad World, as those decks cannot gain interest at any time. Luxury Tax receives little benefit from To The Moon, as in order to take advantage of its high interest, the player would want high starting money, which this deck punishes. Jokers: Vagabond encourages playing without earning interest, making To The Moon useless. Credit Card enables going $20 in debt, well below the minimum interest level.

title: To the Moon
text: To the Moon: Credit Card enables going $20 in debt, well below the minimum interest level. Blinds: The Ox sets money to $0 when playing most played hand, which totably disables To the Moon (unless the player has Matador) The Tooth deducts money for every card played, so try not to play any 5-card hand if possible. Trivia: "[Going] to the moon" is a common phrase used by cryptocurrency traders to describe a stock that is rising incredibly fast. The card art depicts the price of a stock going up exponentially.

title: Trading Card
text: Trading Card: Trading Card (Joker). Effect: If first discard of round has only 1 card, destroy it and earn $3. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Economy. Activation: On Discard. Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Trading Card is an Uncommon Economy Joker that gives $3 from discarding a single card on their very first discard each round, once per Blind. The discarded card will be destroyed, allowing the player to thin their deck and find their desired cards more easily.

title: Trading Card
text: Trading Card: Usage Notes: If the player holds multiple copies of Trading Card, they still only apply to the first discard, and each gives $3. Trading Card cannot be copied by Blueprint or Brainstorm, but multiple copies can be obtained via Showman, Invisible Joker, or Ankh. Decks: Red Deck gives +1 Discard, allowing Trading Card to be used with fewer consequences. Poker hands: In the early game, Trading Card tends to work best with hands that are more likely to be drawn, since it requires "wasting" a discard.

title: Trading Card
text: Trading Card: However, Trading Card is one of the strongest enablers for more difficult hands by the mid/late game, as removing a third to a half of the deck makes certain difficult hand types significantly easier to assemble. Jokers: Drunkard gives +1 Discard, allowing Trading Card to be used with fewer consequences. Merry Andy gives +3 Discards, making the discard used for Trading Card inconsequential. Glass Joker increases by X0.75 Mult for every destroyed Glass card. Canio increases by X1 Mult for every destroyed face card, dramatically improving the value of Trading Card. Erosion gives +4 Mult for every card less than the deck's starting amount. Ride the Bus is easier to keep the effect of, as face cards can be destroyed.

title: Trading Card
text: Trading Card: Ride the Bus is easier to keep the effect of, as face cards can be destroyed. DNA pairs well with Trading Card for deck manipulation. Hologram scales on adding cards. By using Trading Card, cards can be added without bloating the deck. Mystic Summit gains +15 Mult after using up all discards, making the discard used for Trading Card less consequential. Other: Purple Seal activates before the destruction, resulting in both a Tarot card and $3. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give +1 discard, allowing Trading Card to be used with fewer consequences.

title: Trading Card
text: Trading Card: Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give +1 discard, allowing Trading Card to be used with fewer consequences. Blinds: The Hook's discard can activate Trading Card after playing a hand if there is only one card held in hand. Because this discard does not count toward the player's discards, Trading Card will activate every time players play a hand that leaves only one card held in hand, making this the only time Trading Card can be used multiple times in a blind. This Joker is very easy to locate when playing against Amber Acorn, as it still shakes even when flipped face-down. Decks: Blast Off starts with 2 discards, making Trading Card harder to use.

title: Trading Card
text: Trading Card: Decks: Blast Off starts with 2 discards, making Trading Card harder to use. Fragile makes it risky to use Trading Card without Glass Joker. Jokers: Jokers that discourage discarding do not benefit from the required discard to activate Trading Card. These include Green Joker, Ramen, Banner, and Delayed Gratification. Burglar removes all discards, rendering Trading Card unusable. May or may not have anti-synergy with Burnt Joker since Trading Card requires discarding a single card to activate meaning Burnt Joker can only level-up High Card. Blinds: The Water starts with 0 discards, meaning Trading Card cannot be used. Stakes: Blue Stake starts with -1 discard, making Trading Card harder to use.

title: Trading Card
text: Trading Card: Stakes: Blue Stake starts with -1 discard, making Trading Card harder to use. Trivia: The effect of Trading Card references the practice of selling single trading cards for money. In this case, "selling" (discarding) a single card for $3. However, it's still considered as destroying rather than selling in game, thus it has no interaction with Campfire. The design of this Joker mimics the card layout typical of Trading Card Games, including design elements such as numerical stats, a text box, and a collector number. The numbers on Trading Card's artwork are the same as the default amount of Hands and Discards.

title: Triboulet
text: Triboulet: Triboulet (Joker). Effect: Played Kings and Queens each give X2 Mult when scored. Rarity: Legendary. Unlock Requirement: Find this Joker from the Soul card. Buy Price: 20 (cannot be found in shop). Sell Price: $10. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Triboulet is one of the five Legendary Jokers that can be generated from using The Soul Spectral card, which in itself has a 3 in 1000 (0.3%) chance to replace any given card in a Spectral Pack or an Arcana Pack.

title: Triboulet
text: Triboulet: Triboulet gives X2 Mult whenever a King or Queen is scored. Decks: Most decks benefit equally from Triboulet as most start with the same amount of Kings and Queen. The Ghost Deck has easier access to Spectral cards, which simplifies deck building, allowing the deck to be more concentrated on Kings and Queens, but also because of Red Seals, which can retrigger Triboulet's effect. Poker hands: To make the most value out of Triboulet, bigger poker hands are preferred, such as Full House, Flush House, Five of a Kind or Flush Five. This also means that, inversely, smaller poker hands like High Card or Pair get less triggers of Triboulet, and therefore are not recommended.

title: Triboulet
text: Triboulet: Jokers: As Kings and Queens are considered face cards, any Jokers triggering off of face cards naturally make a combo with Triboulet. Retriggers are by far the most valuable, as seen with Sock and Buskin, activating the multiplicative Mult up to 5 times more. This skyrockets gain from Triboulet when playing a 5-card hand containing only scoring Kings and Queens which is X32 Mult to X1024 Mult, a staggering difference. Hanging Chad, Dusk, and Seltzer are also good due to the same reasoning. Splash allows Kings and Queens to score on poker hands they otherwise would be unable to, such as an Ace-high High Card hand. Consumables: Tarot cards:

title: Triboulet
text: Triboulet: Consumables: Tarot cards: The Empress can enhance Queens or Kings into Mult cards, which provides extra flat + Mult to be boosted by Triboulet. Death can turn some cards into powerful Queens or Kings. The Hanged Man can remove non-Queen and non-King cards. Strength can turn Jacks into Queens or even turn Queens into Kings depending on the build. Justice can enhance Queens or Kings into a Glass cards, granting powerful XMult when paired with Triboulet. Spectral cards: Cryptid can make more Queens or Kings. Deja Vu can apply Red Seals onto Queens or Kings, allowing for more Triboulet triggers. Familiar can add enhanced Queens or Kings into the player's deck.

title: Triboulet
text: Triboulet: Familiar can add enhanced Queens or Kings into the player's deck. Decks: Abandoned Deck, Medusa, and Mad World are not recommended due to the lack of initial Kings and Queens. Jokers: Canio requires many face cards to be destroyed, the majority of which tend to be Kings and Queens. This isn't too much of a problem if the player decides to destroy just Jacks or if they have Pareidolia. Baron, Shoot the Moon and Reserved Parking require having Kings and Queens held in hand instead of playing them, making a bad combination with Triboulet. Though Reserved Parking isn't too much of an issue if the player leaves just Jacks or have Pareidolia.

title: Triboulet
text: Triboulet: Though Reserved Parking isn't too much of an issue if the player leaves just Jacks or have Pareidolia. Ride the Bus grows with every consecutive hand played that contains no face cards, meaning consistently playing Kings or Queens renders it useless. Boss Blinds: The Plant can be a run killer as debuffed Queens and Kings do not trigger Triboulet.

title: Triboulet
text: Triboulet: Boss Blinds: The Plant can be a run killer as debuffed Queens and Kings do not trigger Triboulet. Trivia: Little biographical information is available about the jester Triboulet. It is known that in France, there have been at least three jesters referred to as "Triboulet", with the first one serving René of Anjou and also being a playwright, the second serving Louis XII, and the third one serving Francis I (and possibly also Louis XII). The second Triboulet died during Louis XII's reign, and he and the Third Triboulet later became confused as one person.

title: Triboulet
text: Triboulet: The effect of this Joker is likely in reference to a story in which a court jester slapped the King on the buttocks. As the tale goes, the King told the jester he would be allowed to live if he could give an answer more offensive than the act itself. In response, the jester said, “I’m sorry, your majesty- I mistook you for the Queen!” This would explain why the effect of the joker specifically applies to only Kings and Queens. Although the historical accuracy of this story and quote is questionable, it is commonly attributed to Triboulet. This Joker is animated, with Triboulet hovering just above the blue card face.

title: Triboulet
text: Triboulet: This Joker is animated, with Triboulet hovering just above the blue card face. The other legendary Jokers are Canio, Chicot, Perkeo, and Yorick. In other media: Triboulet appears as an artifact in Monster Train 2.

title: Troubadour
text: Troubadour: Troubadour (Joker). Effect: +2 hand size,, -1 hand each round. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Win 5 consecutive rounds by playing only 1 hand. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Troubadour is an Uncommon Effect Joker that provides +2 hand size at the cost of 1 Hand being taken away when Blind is selected.

title: Troubadour
text: Troubadour: To unlock this Joker, the player must win 5 consecutive rounds by playing only 1 hand. Usage Notes: The Five-Card Draw challenge bans Troubadour. Because the hand is taken away when Blind is selected, gaining Troubadour during a round will not reduce the amount of hands until the next Blind, and selling Troubadour during a blind will only remove the extra Hand Size while keeping the -1 hand effect for that Blind. Troubadour can never decrease the total amount of hands below 1, even with multiple copies or when used during The Needle or Golden Needle.

title: Troubadour
text: Troubadour: Decks: Blue Deck works best with Troubadour thanks to its +1 hand per round bonus, offsetting the -1 hand penalty of this Joker. This effectively transforms the Blue Deck into a more flexible Painted Deck. Golden Needle starts with 1 hand, and Troubadour cannot reduce hands below one, turning Troubadour into a +2 hand size without any penalty. Poker Hands: Any strong 5 card hands can benefit from Troubadour, as the increased hand size means a higher chance to draw needed cards to form the hand. Troubadour can also be good in High-card builds that rely on cards being in hand to score, such as with Baron or Steel cards.

title: Troubadour
text: Troubadour: Jokers: Any held-in-hand effect Joker will be improved by Troubadour by virtue of holding more cards in hand. This includes Baron, as mentioned previously, Shoot the Moon, and Reserved Parking. Mime: More cards in hand means more cards for Mime to retrigger. Mail-In Rebate: With increased hand size, it can be easier to find the card rank required for that round. Burglar: Add three extra hands, offsetting the -1 hand penalty of this Joker at the cost of no discards. Merry Andy and Stuntman: Troubadour offsets the hand size penalty of these two Jokers.

title: Troubadour
text: Troubadour: Merry Andy and Stuntman: Troubadour offsets the hand size penalty of these two Jokers. Card modifiers: With Troubadour's increased hand size, it can make it easier to draw into Steel cards and/or Gold cards, as well as cards that have a Blue Seal. Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong can mitigate Troubadour's -1 hand penalty. Blinds: With The Needle, it effectively provides +2 hand size without penalty, as players always start with 1 hand per round.

title: Troubadour
text: Troubadour: If Crimson Heart disables Troubadour, the hand size will return to normal but the current hand will stay intact until the next discard (ex: 10/8). By quitting to the Main Menu and returning, the hand size actually permanently increases (ex: 10/10), giving players a permanent hand size upgrade. Decks: Black Deck makes it difficult to use Troubadour on, as its -1 hand per round penalty means players will only have 2 hands to beat each blind. Similarly, Blast Off makes it even more difficult to use Troubadour on, as its -1 hand per round penalty means players will only have 1 hand to beat each blind.

title: Troubadour
text: Troubadour: Jokers: Overall, any scaling Joker that requires hands to be played is impeded by the -1 hand penalty, giving fewer opportunities to scale them efficiently. This includes Green Joker, Ride the Bus, Supernova, Runner, Square Joker, Spare Trousers, and Obelisk. Vagabond and Space Joker suffer from the -1 hand penalty, as Jokers that generate a resource or trigger when a hand is played have fewer opportunities to trigger. Card Sharp can activate one less time. Loyalty Card becomes harder to activate. Blackboard can be harder to trigger, as the increased hand size can make it harder to hold only Clubs and Spades in your hand.

title: Troubadour
text: Troubadour: The increased hand size will make it hard for Raised Fist to give more score from high-ranked cards. Tags: Handy Tag will give less money. Vouchers: Hieroglyph, as it gives an additional -1 hand, should be avoided if Troubadour is essential to the current Joker build. Coupled with the Black Deck, it can reduce the total number of hands to as low as 1. Blinds: The House is particularly bad for big hand size, as it means that more cards will be drawn face down. Trivia: A troubadour was someone who composed music and performed poetry during the Middle Ages. Troubadour songs were mainly about chivalry and courtly love.

title: Turtle Bean
text: Turtle Bean: Turtle Bean (Joker). Effect: +5 hand size, reduces by 1 each round. Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $6. Sell Price: $3. Type: Effect. Activation: N/A (Passive). Copyable: ✗ No. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: ✗ No. Turtle Bean is an Uncommon Effect Joker that initially provides +5 Hand Size, but decreases by 1 every blind until it destroys itself, indicated by the word "Eaten!" appearing under the Joker, after which it has bean and gone.

title: Turtle Bean
text: Turtle Bean: Usage Notes: The Non-Perishable and Five-Card Draw challenges ban Turtle Bean. Decks: Any deck can benefit from Turtle Bean. Poker hands: Any 5-card hand can benefit from Turtle Bean. In particular, the extra hand size makes finding matching cards for high-value hands, like Straight Flush or Flush Five, much easier. Jokers: If your goal is huge hand sizes, then: Juggler: +1 hand size. Troubadour: +2 hand size, at the cost of -1 hand per round. Turtle Bean has particular synergies with: Any Joker that provides held in-hand bonuses like Baron, Shoot the Moon, or Reserved Parking benefits, since Turtle Bean allows larger hand sizes. Throwback: Since Throwback benefits from skipping blinds, this extends the life of Turtle Bean.

title: Turtle Bean
text: Turtle Bean: Throwback: Since Throwback benefits from skipping blinds, this extends the life of Turtle Bean. Consumables: Note that the increased Hand Size from Turtle Bean also applies to Tarot and Spectral packs. Thus: Tarot and Spectral cards with selected card effects have a wider selection of cards to choose from your deck. Ouija and Sigil convert substantially more cards if used early in Turtle Bean's duration. Card modifiers: Because Turtle Bean lasts exactly 5 rounds, the Perishable sticker has no effect on it, as it will get disappear immediately before it is set to be debuffed.

title: Turtle Bean
text: Turtle Bean: Blinds: If Crimson Heart disables Turtle Bean, the hand size will return to normal, but current cards in hand will stay intact until the next discard (ex: 13/8). By quitting to Main Menu and returning, the hand size actually permanently increases (ex: 13/13), giving players a permanent hand size upgrade. Jokers: Blackboard can be harder to trigger, as the increased hand size can make it harder to hold only Clubs and Spades in your hand. The increased hand size will make it hard for Raised Fist to give more score from high-ranked cards.

title: Turtle Bean
text: Turtle Bean: The increased hand size will make it hard for Raised Fist to give more score from high-ranked cards. Strategies: The sell value of Turtle Bean does not depend on its current Hand Size value, so it is best to sell Turtle Bean when it is at +1 Hand Size, instead of letting it get destroyed (worth $0). Trivia: The black turtle bean is the only type of turtle bean. It is used in Latin American and Indian cuisine, to name a few. LocalThunk drew inspiration for this Joker from Mexican food. The turtle bean is often referred to as a black bean in some areas.

title: Turtle Bean
text: Turtle Bean: The turtle bean is often referred to as a black bean in some areas. This Joker is part of the group of "Consumable" Jokers that can be destroyed with usage, dubbed "Food Jokers" due to their shared theme. The other Jokers in this group are Ice Cream, Popcorn, Gros Michel, Cavendish, Egg, Seltzer, Ramen, and Diet Cola.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Vagabond (Joker). Effect: Create a Tarot card if hand is played with $4 or less. Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Effect. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Vagabond is a Rare Effect Joker that spawns a Tarot card when a hand is played, provided players have a free consumable slot and $4 or less when the hand is played.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Money generation like the 1/15 $20 payout from Lucky cards, Gold Seal on scoring cards, or money generated by Jokers such as Golden Ticket or Business Card that take the player over $4 upon playing will still generate the Tarot card along with their additional money effect. Decks: Green Deck isn't reliant on Interest to gain money, so spending everything you have to trigger Vagabond won't impact your ability to buy from the Shop as much. However, some of Green Deck's income is from leftover Hands/Discards, which can be harder to save if the player wants to get max value from Vagabond by playing all their hands. Blue Deck allows more hands to be played, meaning more triggers of Vagabond.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Blue Deck allows more hands to be played, meaning more triggers of Vagabond. Magic Deck's extra consumable slot is very helpful for saving useful Tarots. Zodiac Deck's unique shop makes it easier to spend money to reach the $4 threshold and generally helps the Tarot-stacking builds Vagabond tends to form. Luxury Tax encourages the player to not have too much money when entering blinds, similar to Vagabond. Poker Hands: Weaker hands like High Card or Pair allow the player to farm more Tarot cards per round. Later in the game, these Tarot cards can enable hands built around one rank, such as Four of a Kind and Five of a Kind.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Jokers: Jokers that scale based on hands played, like Ride the Bus, Square Joker, and Obelisk, are helpful to pair with Vagabond, as they grow more powerful in the process of using Vagabond to its full potential. Furthering this idea, Burglar allows more hands to be played to both generate more Tarots and scale these Jokers. Jokers that want the player to use many Tarot cards benefit well from Vagabond, these include: Enhancement-based Jokers like Steel Joker and Glass Joker Suit-based Jokers like Bloodstone and Ancient Joker Rank-based Jokers like Walkie Talkie and Wee Joker

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Suit-based Jokers like Bloodstone and Ancient Joker Rank-based Jokers like Walkie Talkie and Wee Joker Fortune Teller is a useful scaling Joker Vagabond can pair with. It can end up scaling faster than Jokers like Green Joker as the Tarots used elsewhere still scale it. Acrobat is very helpful, as it provides a safety net for the final hand of the round. This final hand will, ideally, always be reached, as using every hand to maximize Tarot production is the main goal of Vagabond. One does not usually need to discard with Vagabond, so Jokers that want to save discards, like Ramen, Banner, and Delayed Gratification can be useful additions to builds using Vagabond.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Money generation that triggers at cashout, like Golden Joker and Satellite, are very helpful, as it allows the player to make money after utilizing Vagabond. Egg and Gift Card increase your Joker sell value, which pairs well with Temperance. Driver's License and Vampire allow the player to turn Enhancements into xmult. Campfire can be scaled by X0.25 Mult or more per hand played by selling the Tarots generated. Credit Card allows the player to go up to $-20 in debt which can allow them to purchase cards in the shop they otherwise could not, as well as staying below $4 without as much difficulty.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Vouchers: Grabber and Nacho Tong both add 1 extra hand, allowing Vagabond to generate more Tarot cards. Crystal Ball gives you an additional +1 consumable slot, which is helpful since you may want to save some Tarot cards from Vagabond instead of using them immediately. This applies notably to Temperance, since you want to collect the money after the Blind is over. Consumables: Wraith can be helpful as it sets money to $0, allowing Vagabond to activate. Blinds: The Tooth and The Ox can lower the amount of money the player has, allowing them to activate Vagabond. Stakes: On Gold Stake, any Rental Jokers may help the player maintain Vagabond's conditional requirement.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Stakes: On Gold Stake, any Rental Jokers may help the player maintain Vagabond's conditional requirement. Other synergies: Be careful when playing Lucky cards with Vagabond, as winning $20 from it will prevent Vagabond from generating any more Tarot cards for future hands during the current blind. Using The Devil to create Gold cards can be beneficial since the $3 you gain from it happens just before the Blind ends. Decks: Black Deck, Blast Off, and Golden Needle don't work as well with Vagabond due to their reduced number of hands. Nebula Deck's fewer consumable slots make it significantly harder to use the Tarots from Vagabond.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Nebula Deck's fewer consumable slots make it significantly harder to use the Tarots from Vagabond. Rich get Richer doesn't work well with Vagabond, as this deck encourages the player to have a lot of money. Jokers: Jokers which generate money during a round, as opposed to at cashout, can quickly pass Vagabond's shutoff point. Rough Gem, To Do List, Mail-In Rebate, Business Card, Reserved Parking and Matador all can pass Vagabond's requirement during the round. Trading Card's $3 does not go over the limit on its own, but it does require the player make sure they have no more than one dollar before each Blind. Golden Ticket provides $4 when scoring Gold cards, which can quickly turn off Vagabond.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Golden Ticket provides $4 when scoring Gold cards, which can quickly turn off Vagabond. Bootstraps and Bull grow stronger when the player has more money, which directly conflicts with Vagabond's low-money requirement. To The Moon becomes considerably harder to utilize, unless the player has some way of making a significant amount of money at the end of the round. Seals: Because Vagabond generates 1 Tarot card per hand played, Blue Seal becomes harder to use as players may not have enough consumable slots to hold both. Gold Seal generates money when played, which can quickly turn off Vagabond.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Gold Seal generates money when played, which can quickly turn off Vagabond. Vouchers: Seed Money and Money Tree encourage the player to have a lot of money to gain interest, which directly conflicts with Vagabond's low-money requirement. Trivia: The card art for this Joker was made by Pixel Artist, Animator, and YouTuber Lumpy Touch. This was the only card in the game whose pixel art was not done by LocalThunk, until some of the Friends of Jimbo arrived. Lumpy Touch also did the art for Chaos Theory, though that Joker is unused. The Joker resembles a clown character named Weary Willie, created by the late circus performer Emmett Leo Kelly.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: The Joker resembles a clown character named Weary Willie, created by the late circus performer Emmett Leo Kelly. Vagabonds are wandering people who have no set home or job, often associated with being poor. This fits the design of the Joker, being a poor-looking man with worn clothes and the effect based on having low or no money. The card's "material" also makes it look like it's made of cardboard, referencing how vagabonds sometimes live in cardboard boxes. The color of "Tarot" in Vagabond's description is incorrectly formatted as {C:purple} instead of {C:tarot}, which is only used correctly in Medium. This makes the text appear as a slightly darker purple than other cards that reference Tarot cards.

title: Vagabond
text: Vagabond: Fortune Teller has the same issue. Vagabond had a Youtooz Collectible figurine through a merchandising collaboration in addition to Jimbo/ Joker and The Wheel of Fortune.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Vampire (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains X0.1 Mult per scoring Enhanced card played, removes card Enhancement, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Uncommon. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $7. Sell Price: $3. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Vampire is an Uncommon scaling Multiplicative Mult Joker that removes Enhancements from your scored cards and permanently gains X0.1 Mult for each Enhancements when it does. It starts at X1 Mult. It removes Enhancements before their effect occurs, meaning that the enhancement will not affect your hand's score.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Usage Notes: Vampire removes Enhancements before their effect occurs, meaning the Enhancements cannot activate. All scored cards will get their Enhancements removed. Vampire also cannot change the type of Poker Hand retroactively, for example removing Wild would still keep the Poker Hand as Flush. There are a few notable playing card interactions: Debuffed: Debuffed cards are considered not to have any Modifier including Enhancements, so Vampire cannot remove Enhancements from debuffed cards. Wild card: wild enhancement gets removed, the card scores if it would have scored for the original hand, and the type of hand played is not affected. Glass card: glass enhancement gets removed, no X2 Mult, and there is no chance for the card to break.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Glass card: glass enhancement gets removed, no X2 Mult, and there is no chance for the card to break. Stone card: stone enhancement gets removed and card returns to what it originally was, no +50 Chips, but card will always score for this hand (the type of hand played is not affected). Editions: Editions are not Enhancements, will not get removed by Vampire, and work normally. Seals: Seals are not Enhancements, will not get removed by Vampire, and work normally. The Joker order matters significantly when using certain other Jokers with Vampire: A second Vampire: only the left-most Vampire can remove enhancements and scale at any time (regardless of how many Midas Masks are used). Midas Mask:

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Midas Mask: Putting Midas Mask before Vampire results in all scoring face cards turning Gold, then feeding vampire, leaving them unenhanced. Putting Vampire before Midas Mask results in all scoring enhanced face cards feeding vampire, then turning gold. Putting a Midas Mask before Vampire, and a second Midas Mask after Vampire results in all scoring face cards turning gold, then feeding Vampire, then turning gold again. DNA copies an enhanced card if Vampire is after DNA, but copies the unenhanced card if Vampire is before DNA. Ride the Bus resets if Vampire is before Ride the Bus and removes the Stone enhancement from a face card. Ride the Bus does not reset if Vampire is positioned after Ride the Bus.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Golden Ticket only works if there is a Midas Mask positioned after Vampire, with the positioning of Golden Ticket itself having no impact. Bram Poker challenge starts the player with an Eternal copy of Vampire. and Fragile challenge bans Vampire. Decks: Zodiac Deck, Magic Deck or the Ghost Deck work well for the vampire, as these decks have more opportunities to obtain Tarots and Spectral cards (see Consumables below) that can provide enhanced cards to feed the Vampire. Black Deck's additional Joker slot can be used for effect Jokers (like Midas Mask) to generate enhanced cards.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Black Deck's additional Joker slot can be used for effect Jokers (like Midas Mask) to generate enhanced cards. Medusa and Monolith Challenge Decks both starts with a Marble Joker, which Vampire can use it as an enhancement generator to scale easier. Not only that, Medusa also starts with 12 Stone cards. Poker Hands: Since this joker will consume the Enhancements before they get applied, hands with a high base mult are preferred. Flush Five Flush House Five of a Kind Straight Flush Full House Flush Four of a Kind Jokers: Vampire combos well with jokers that either generate Tarot cards, or enhancements themselves (such as Midas Mask) to generate a steady supply of Enhancements to eat.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: If using the Midas Mask combo, the order will affect this. If the Midas Mask is placed first, face cards will be changed to Gold cards, and the Vampire will immediately consume the effect to increase its multiplier. However, if the Midas Mask is placed after the Vampire, the cards are made golden without consuming the effect. Thus, players could create infinite enhancement supplies for Vampire either by having Midas Mask turn face cards to Gold cards first then Vampire consumes them, or have some Gold cards in advance and have Vampire consume them, and they immediately turns into Gold cards again by Midas Mask. Pareidolia can be used with Midas Mask so that all scored cards turn into Gold cards, giving Vampire even more mult.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Jokers such as DNA or Marble Joker also provide a good source of Enhancements (as you can play a single enhanced card with DNA before Vampire to copy it with its enhancement before feeding the Vampire). Splash is a useful supporting Joker that guarantees five enhanced cards to be scored, in the event that they can't form a five-card hand. If used with Midas Mask and Pareidolia, all 5 scored cards can become gold and give Vampire X0.5 Mult per hand. Since only the left-most of two held Vampires can scale, it is recommended to continuously swap them around, keeping them at the same Mult to get the best score possible.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Tarot cards are useful to enhance cards and get Vampire scale faster, so look out for Jokers like Cartomancer, Vagabond and/or Hallucination. Sixth Sense and Séance can be used to create any of the 3 Spectral cards that destroy cards but add Enhanced cards in exchange, as well as Cryptid to scale Vampire faster. They can also create Spectral cards that give Seals (like Talisman) or Aura, since Seals and Editions are not affected by Vampire. Consumables: Vampire requires a large amount of enhanced cards to scale, therefore consumables that adds enhancement are important to scale this Joker fast: The Magician, The Empress and The Hierophant are preferred as they enhance up to 2 cards at once.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: The Magician, The Empress and The Hierophant are preferred as they enhance up to 2 cards at once. The Lovers, The Chariot, The Devil, Justice, and The Tower are a good alternate pick up that enhance 1 card. Death can be used to duplicate an enhanced card as well. Familiar, Grim, and Incantation are useful to increase enhanced cards number, but be wary that they could also destroy an enhanced card in your hand as well. Cryptid can be used on an already enhanced card.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Cryptid can be used on an already enhanced card. Notably, with Ghost Deck or Jokers that generates Spectral cards (like Séance), it is possible to using above-mentioned cards during a round, which means multiple enhanced cards generated are in the hand and can be played at once to obtain lots of upgrades. Aura also provide utility in that the edition of a card does not get eaten by the vampire: a Holographic card stays holographic after the hand is played, hence increasing the base mult of the hand. Talisman, Deja Vu, Trance and Medium provide Seals to cards, which are not affected by Vampire, so they can be used without any problem.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon may also prove useful to find more tarot cards to apply enhancement with. Illusion allows the player to buy enhancement cards in the Shop, which can also be useful to provides additional enhancement cards to feed the Vampire with. This can be further increased with help from Overstock and Overstock Plus to increase the shop selection, plus Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut to make rerolling cheaper. Jokers: Jokers that rely on specific card enhancements become harder to use when combined with Vampire. These include Lucky Cat, Glass Joker, Golden Ticket, Steel Joker and Stone Joker. Driver's License limits the players to not play any enhanced card, making a risky combo with Vampire.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Driver's License limits the players to not play any enhanced card, making a risky combo with Vampire. Vouchers: Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon reduce the probabilities of Tarot cards appearing in the shop, and therefore, the XMult from Vampire. Magic Trick also applies here, but this one isn't too bad at all since it's required to get Illusion. Trivia: Vampire's effect reflects vampirism. It drains enhancements from cards, growing stronger while leaving them weaker. As compared to Joker, the coloring of Vampire's eye and mouth makeup are swapped. This is likely to make his fangs more distinct. Vampire is the fourth Joker after Jimbo, Odd Todd, and Even Steven to get a plush as merchandise from Makeship.

title: Vampire
text: Vampire: Vampire is the fourth Joker after Jimbo, Odd Todd, and Even Steven to get a plush as merchandise from Makeship. In other media: This specific joker is depicted in the cover art of the Ante Chamber DLC of the bullet heaven game Vampire Survivors. This joker makes a reference to Bisconte Draculó, the vampire depicted in the box art and main menu of Vampire Survivors (though not really otherwise appearing in the game.)

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Walkie Talkie (Joker). Effect: Each played 10 or 4 gives +10 Chips and +4 Mult when scored. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips and Additive Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Walkie Talkie is a Common Joker that uniquely gives a boost to Chips and Additive Mult simultaneously. Whenever a 10 or a 4 is scored, this Joker will give an immediate +10 Chips and +4 Mult; if the 10 or 4 is retriggered either by a Joker effect or its own Red Seal, the effect of Walkie Talkie will activate again on that same card.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Even without additional assistance, this Joker represents a +50 Chips and +20 Mult bonus on a hand full of scoring 10s and 4s. For reference, a Level 1 Full House (10 10 10 4 4) would normally yield 312 score; this Joker increases it to a whopping 3,072 all by itself. The score increase is even higher on hands that allow for high amounts of 10s and 4s to score while having even higher base Chips and Mult.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: With the amount of Deck manipulation present in the game thanks to the presence of certain Tarot cards and Spectral cards, Walkie Talkie is especially appetizing for its rarity and is definitely worth building around if acquired early, as it can allow for pivots into the very strong secret hands. Decks: Any Deck synergizes well with Walkie Talkie due to its versatility. However, these have a slightly easier time using it than the others: Abandoned Deck: Has the highest state of advantage with this Joker, due to having less cards in the Deck overall, thereby making it easier to find 10s and 4s.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Painted Deck: This Joker serves as good role compression, providing Chips and Additive Mult while taking up just 1 of the 4 Joker slots. On top of this, the increased hand size allows easier finding of higher quantities of 10s and 4s. Ghost Deck, Magic Deck, and Zodiac Deck: All these have more overall access to the Deck fixing methods that this Joker loves, but they do not have a distinct consistency advantage right away like the aforementioned ones do. Poker hands: Focus on these hands in the early game to consistently maximize this Joker's impact: Two Pair Three of a Kind Full House (the best choice, due to having 5 scoring cards while not being substantially harder to find)

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Full House (the best choice, due to having 5 scoring cards while not being substantially harder to find) As you manipulate your Deck to include more 10s and 4s, pivot towards these hands (note that 3 of these 4 are secret hands, meaning you will not be able to level scale them right away): Four of a Kind Five of a Kind Flush House Flush Five

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Four of a Kind Five of a Kind Flush House Flush Five Jokers: Retrigger Jokers (except Mime) will all work remarkably nicely with this Joker. Hanging Chad is the easiest one to find, guaranteeing an extra +28 Chips and +8 Mult at the very least if a 4 is at the start of the hand. Dusk (retriggering all cards when 0 hands remain), Hack (retriggering all 4s), and Seltzer (temporarily retriggering all cards) have much higher ceilings, but are slightly more conditional. Sock and Buskin can also be used, but only if the player has Pareidolia.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Even Steven: Meshes well with this Joker early on, and can do so even later in the presence of a retrigger Joker, essentially doubling the yield of the Additive Mult when scoring. Clever Joker, Sly Joker, and Wily Joker: These Chip Jokers can provide a little bit of a boost, mostly in the early game, to the hands one would be aiming to play anyway. A Full House or Flush House would trigger any (and all) of the three.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Jolly Joker, Mad Joker, and Zany Joker: Similar to the above Jokers, but for Additive Mult. These are even less advisable to keep as the run progresses, as there are far stronger sources of Additive Mult than Chips, but can clear most Blinds early on, especially when combined with this Joker.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Flower Pot: A Multiplicative Mult card that will give a strong X3 Mult benefit as long as the played hand contains at least 1 each of Hearts, Spades, Diamonds, and Clubs. Hands with multiples of the same rank, like the ones Walkie Talkie builds want to play, are generally easier to fit 1 of each suit in. Consider pairing with Wild cards or Smeared Joker for extra ease of use. Seeing Double: Though easier to trigger than the above card, only needing at least 1 Clubs card and 1 of any other suit, it only gives a middling X2 Mult bonus. It is more useful in the early-to-mid-game, but is a potential take when combined with another Multiplicative Mult source.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Shortcut: Most Straights starting with a 10 and having at least two gaps can also include a 4 (Q/J 10 8 6 4 also work). Since Saturn has the highest Planet card scaling of all the non-secret hands (excluding Neptune, which technically also benefits but is much harder to pull off), and the hand also has access to powerful support like The Order, this Joker can pair well with it in a pinch.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Spare Trousers: This scaling Additive Mult Joker complements Walkie Talkie's power incredibly, gaining +2 Mult whenever a Two Pair, Full House, or Flush House is played - all of which would likely be frequently played anyway. If acquired early, it can build up mid-to-high double digits' worth of Mult, and still be kept even when playing stronger hands like Four/Five of a Kind, as its final result still applies to all played hands.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: The Duo, The Trio, and The Family: As hands containing multiple 10s and 4s are the most optimal to play with this Joker, these are the best Multiplicative Mult cards to pair with it. Of notable importance, Four/Five of a Kind and Flush Five will trigger any (and all) of them. Consumables: Tarot cards: The Hierophant and The Empress can be used to boost the Chips and Mult bonus provided by Walkie Talkie. The Hanged Man can be used to thin out the deck and make 4s and 10s easier to find. Death can be used to turn other cards into 4s or 10s.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Death can be used to turn other cards into 4s or 10s. Justice can enhance a 4 or a 10 into a Glass card, granting it a X2 Mult bonus on top of its flat Mult. Strength can be used to upgrade 3s into 4s or 9s into 10s. Spectral cards: Aura can add the Foil, Holographic, or Polychrome effect to a 4 or 10, making the Chips and/or Mult bonus even stronger. Cryptid can be used to create more 4s and 10s. Deja Vu can add a Red Seal to 4s or 10s and allow Walkie Talkie to trigger them multiple times. Immolate can destroy up to five cards, making the 4s and 10s easier to find.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: Immolate can destroy up to five cards, making the 4s and 10s easier to find. Incantation can add 4s and/or 10s at the cost of a random card being destroyed (which can be a 4 or a 10). Anti-Synergies: Mad World doesn't start with any 10s, which makes Walkie Talkie weaker. Trivia: Walkie Talkie is one of only two Jokers to provide both Chips and Mult buff to scored cards, the other being Scholar.

title: Walkie Talkie
text: Walkie Talkie: The affected cards, and score values, are a reference to the phrase "10-4", commonly used by US law enforcement to acknowledge that they have understood a message received over their walkie-talkies. It became more common knowledge among the public around the mid-to-late-1950s, and is now sometimes used in informal conversation in Anglophone countries to show acknowledgement of a statement. The German version of Walkie Talkie's description erroneously states that the Joker gives "X4 Mult" instead of "+4 Mult".

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Wee Joker (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains +8 Chips when each played 2 is scored, (Currently +0 Chips). Rarity: Rare. Unlock Requirement: Win a run in 18 or fewer rounds. Buy Price: $8. Sell Price: $4. Type: Chips. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: ✗ No. Eternal: Yes. Wee Joker is a Rare scaling Chips Joker that adds Chips to played hands. The amount of Chips added begins at +0 and is permanently increased by +8 whenever a 2 is scored. This also works with retriggers, such as the likes of Hack or Red Seal. It will not gain Chips if the played 2 is not scored.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Wee Joker is one of, if not the, strongest Chips Joker there is to offer thanks to its absurd scaling capabilities. Once the player can score 2s consistently, Wee Joker shines as a steady Chips source that can reach Stuntman levels of potency quite quickly and also has the potential to take off into the 4 digits, with some highly proficient scaling reaching 10s of thousands of Chips. To do so, poker hands that use a high number of playing cards are basically required, such as Four of a Kind, Five of a Kind or Flush Five.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Taking Wee Joker late into the run, when deck-fixing is already in the works, may still be worthwhile in case the player severely lacks a source of Chips. The player may have removed 2s beforehand though, which can make Wee Joker way more difficult to use. Instead, it is advised that the player first remove 7s and 8s, since their synergies are often the least impactful. Doing this on a Straight build is a no-go, however. To unlock this Joker, the player must win a run in 18 rounds or less. Decks: Wee Joker synergizes well with all Decks fairly equally, but some have minor advantages over the others.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Decks: Wee Joker synergizes well with all Decks fairly equally, but some have minor advantages over the others. Most decks have the same starting amount of four 2s, making Wee Joker synergize with them fairly equally. However, some decks have features that may make utilizing Wee Joker easier: Red Deck: The extra Discard allows the player to cycle through more cards, which helps with finding and scoring 2s greatly. Blue Deck: The extra Hand lets the player use a "throwaway" hand for extra scaling, and also acts as a pseudo-Discard, again helping with finding and scoring 2s.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Magic Deck: With the help of the two starting copies of The Fool, the player can potentially create a deck centralized around 2s right at the very beginning. This can help with playing into Wee Joker later tremendously, provided the player can find the Joker. Try copying a Death to convert cards into 2s, or The Hanged Man to get rid of many non-2s at once. Ghost Deck: Thanks to its easier access to Spectral cards, the Ghost Deck has great potential to manipulate the deck into being beneficial to Wee Joker. Try looking for Cryptid to create multiple new 2s, or Deja Vu to put a red seal on an existing 2.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Abandoned Deck and Mad World: Due to the small size of the deck, the likelihood of stumbling across 2s on these deck is very much better, and thus allows for more efficient scaling. Painted Deck: The starting +2 Hand size lets the player see more cards, and also allows for more lenient discarding in certain situations. Plasma Deck: Sources of Chips are inherently better on Plasma Deck due to it treating Chips and Mult equally. Before the player gets their +Mult and xMult going, Wee Joker can be an absolute carry, often winning the run by itself. Poker hands: Hands that score large quantities of 2s are preferable to other hands. Focus on these in the early game:

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Pair and Two Pair (mostly for emergencies) Three of a Kind Full House As Deck manipulation access becomes more realistic, pivot to these hands (the final two are the most ideal, as they allow five 2s to score all at once): Four of a Kind Five of a Kind Flush Five

title: Wee Joker
