text: Wee Joker: Four of a Kind Five of a Kind Flush Five Jokers: Any retrigger Jokers work incredibly well with Wee Joker, as rescoring a 2 upgrades Wee Joker another time. In particular, Hack offers unconditional retriggers to 2s, making it very helpful, with one copy providing up to an extra +40 Chips on a hand with five scoring 2s. Hanging Chad is also very strong with Wee Joker, guaranteeing +24 Chips if a 2 can be scored. Sock and Buskin can only retrigger 2s if Pareidolia is owned. Seltzer and Dusk can also be useful, but they have certain limits; Seltzer only lasts for 10 hands, and Dusk only works on the final hand.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Drunkard and Merry Andy: The extra discards provided by these Jokers make finding and scoring 2s much easier. Even Steven and Fibonacci: Giving +4 Mult and +8 Mult, respectively, whenever a 2 is scored, either of these can make playing large quantities of 2s even more rewarding, especially when accounting for retriggers. Trading Card is a source of both money and deck thinning, which helps Wee Joker by making 2s proportionally more common, and making acquiring better scoring easier as the run progresses. DNA: By duplicating 2s, especially 2s with a Red Seal, this Joker can scale much faster, making it a near auto-include when discovered while holding this Joker, even if just temporarily.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Splash allows the player to score 2s without needing to be part of the scoring hand. This is particularly useful if the player only draws one 2, as splash can score the 2 while playing 4 other cards to find more 2s later. The Idol can be an amazing joker to give huge amounts of multiplicative mult if the player has a lot of 2s in their deck. While it requires a massive amount of deck-fixing, it can pay off incredibly well by giving X2 Mult when a 2 is scored, which pairs well with the retriggers that Wee Joker builds often have.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Ancient Joker can potentially be useful if there are a large number of Wild 2s, as this enables the extremely powerful Flush Five - a hand that can guide a run far into Endless Mode in combination with repeated Multiplicative Mult sources and Planet card scaling. Bloodstone can be considered in its absence by creating a large number of 2s of Hearts, albeit its randomness factor makes it a lot less reliable. This isn't an issue if Oops! All 6s is owned. Consumables: Death and Strength can make more 2s. The Hanged Man can remove non-2s allowing you to see 2s easier. Deja Vu can apply Red Seals onto 2s allowing Wee Joker to scale faster.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Deja Vu can apply Red Seals onto 2s allowing Wee Joker to scale faster. Cryptid can create copies of 2s. Incantation can add 2s to the deck but might destroy a 2 in the process. Vouchers: Grabber together with Nacho Tong are very good Vouchers to take, as they allow the player to score more 2s, or use the extra hands as pseudo-discards to find more 2s. Wasteful, as well as its upgraded counterpart Recyclomancy, are good Vouchers to take when using Wee Joker. As scoring non-2s is less ideal, discards can be used in order to locate 2s.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Hieroglyph gives more opportunity to score 2s, but might not be worth it if the player is struggling to score enough points. Its upgraded counterpart, Petroglyph, may also be worth considering if the player has access to extra discards, but it is much less justifiable on the higher Stakes. Boss Blinds: This Joker is easily distinguishable when played against Amber Acorn, as it retains its unique shape even when flipped face-down. Decks: 15 Minute City is not recommended due to lack of 2s by default.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Decks: 15 Minute City is not recommended due to lack of 2s by default. Strategy: As skipping is usually a high-risk strategy, it can be slightly tricky to win a run in 18 or fewer rounds, meaning the player must skip at least 6 Blinds, averaging at 1.25 Blinds per Ante skipped. A basic Deck, such as Red Deck or Blue Deck, is likely the best, as an additional discard/hand makes it more feasible to play more risky as is the case with skipping. Plasma Deck can skip more in the early game due to its balancing ability, making the need to obtain Jokers early less of a priority.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: Anaglyph Deck earns the player a Double Tag upon defeating a Boss Blind, making skipping slightly more viable. Tags in general to look out for are Investment Tag and Speed Tag, as earning Economy is critical since the player sees fewer Shops and Blind payouts overall. Throwback will have scaled to a minimum of X4 Mult by the end of the run, making it a very consistent source of scaling multiplicative mult. The Uncommon Tag may be a quick way to obtain Throwback early, on top of retroactively scaling it.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: The Uncommon Tag may be a quick way to obtain Throwback early, on top of retroactively scaling it. Trivia: The card art is identical to the default Joker, but scaled down to a smaller size. This also makes all Joker Stickers appear at a scaled-down size on the card itself. When duplicating this joker through the use of Ankh or Invisible Joker, the Joker Sticker will appear normal sized, going off the card. This Joker is part of a set that doesn't adhere to the standard joker size, along with Photograph, Half Joker, and Square Joker.

title: Wee Joker
text: Wee Joker: The term "wee" is a Scottish term used to refer to something as small-sized or not at a regular size. This also ties into the Wee Joker's ability to keep building +8 Chips for every scoring card with a rank of 2, the smallest rank in Balatro.

title: Wily Joker
text: Wily Joker: Wily Joker (Joker). Effect: +100 Chips if played hand contains a Three of a Kind. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Chips. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Wily Joker is a Common Chips Joker that provides +100 Chips when playing a hand that contains a Three of a Kind. This includes hands that include any three cards with the same rank, such as a Full House.

title: Wily Joker
text: Wily Joker: Decks: Abandoned Deck and Mad World work best with Wily Joker thanks to their smaller card count. Erratic Deck can synergize with Wily Joker if it's randomized to have lots of cards of the same rank. Plasma Deck benefits from the large amount of chips, which, when balanced, greatly boost the score for the played hand. Poker hands: Playing any hand with three cards of the same rank will trigger Wily Joker. This includes: Three of a Kind Full House Four of a Kind Five of a Kind Flush House Flush Five Jokers: Zany Joker: +12 Mult when played hand contains Three of a kind. The Trio: X3 Mult when played hand contains Three of a kind.

title: Wily Joker
text: Wily Joker: The Trio: X3 Mult when played hand contains Three of a kind. Trivia: This Joker is part of a series that provides a Chips boost for a specific hand. The others are Sly Joker, Clever Joker, Devious Joker, and Crafty Joker. Much like the other Jokers in this series, this Joker has blue face paint over the mouth, indicating that they provide a bonus of Chips and not Mult like the red face paint Jokers.

title: Wrathful Joker
text: Wrathful Joker: Wrathful Joker (Joker). Effect: Played cards with Spade suit give +3 Mult when scored. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $5. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: On Scored. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Wrathful Joker is a Common Joker that provides conditional Additive Mult to played hands. One of the four 'sinful' Jokers made to support specific Card Suits, it gives +3 Mult each time a Spade card is scored. If the played card is retriggered, either by a Joker effect or by its own Red Seal, Wrathful Joker's effect will activate again.

title: Wrathful Joker
text: Wrathful Joker: Decks: Magic Deck's Fool Tarots can be used to mass-convert cards to have Spade suits. Ghost Deck can find a Sigil Spectral card in the shop, which may convert cards into Spades. This Joker is easier to take with Checkered Deck, as the deck starts with 26 Spade playing cards. Poker hands: This Joker works best with Flush hands, if they contain only Spade suit cards. These hands are as follows: Flush Straight Flush (and Royal Flush) Flush House Flush Five Other hands that score more cards are generally better to play with Wrathful Joker, as they allow more Spade cards to be scored.

title: Wrathful Joker
text: Wrathful Joker: Jokers: As Wrathful Joker's effect triggers when a Spade card is scored, retrigger Jokers, that allow cards to be scored multiple times, are very good to combo with Wrathful. Flush Jokers, like Crafty Joker and Droll Joker, work well with Wrathful Joker, as you want to be playing flushes to maximize its effect anyways.

title: Wrathful Joker
text: Wrathful Joker: Arrowhead also triggers off of Spade cards scored, forming a natural synergy with Wrathful Joker. As Arrowhead gives a large amount of Chips, Wrathful Joker's innate synergy with it is higher than other suit-Mult Jokers and their upgrades, as they boost both sides of the spectrum. As a result, Wrathful Joker is best with X Mult Jokers, like The Tribe, Card Sharp, Hologram, Cavendish, etc. that can play off of its +15 Mult, assuming 5 Spades are scored, to balance the Mult it gives with the Chips from Arrowhead.

title: Wrathful Joker
text: Wrathful Joker: Because Wrathful Joker's Mult is applied during the scoring of your played cards, Jokers that focus on creating Tarot cards are helpful to Wrathful Joker's viability. They can both allow more Spades to be created, and create certain Enhancements (particularly Glass and Steel) that work well with high hand-scoring Mult builds. Smeared Joker effectively turns all Club cards into Spades for the purpose of Wrathful Joker's effect. Blinds: When facing The Goad, all Spade cards are debuffed, meaning Wrathful Joker cannot activate. Trivia: Wrath is one of the traditional seven deadly sins. The four basic Jokers that provide +3 Mult for each suit are each based on these. The other Sinful Jokers are Greedy Joker, Lusty Joker and Gluttonous Joker.

title: Wrathful Joker
text: Wrathful Joker: "Wrath" is an less common term for anger, and since Spades are the tips of pikes, which are weapons, the two are associated. Wrathful Joker's uncommon counterpart, Arrowhead, is a weapon that also plays on the themes of violence and wrath.

title: Yorick
text: Yorick: Yorick (Joker). Effect: This Joker gains X1 Mult every 23 [23] cards discarded, (Currently X1 Mult). Rarity: Legendary. Unlock Requirement: Find this Joker from the Soul card. Buy Price: 20 (cannot be found in shop). Sell Price: $10. Type: Multiplicative Mult. Activation: Mixed. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Yorick is one of the five Legendary Jokers that can be generated from using The Soul Spectral card, which in itself has a 3 in 1000 (0.3%) chance to replace any given card in a Spectral Pack or an Arcana Pack.

title: Yorick
text: Yorick: Yorick starts at X1 Mult and gains an extra X1 Mult for every 23 cards discarded. Decks: Red Deck starts with an extra discard, which can help Yorick by allowing up to 5 more cards to be discarded than normally available. Painted Deck starts with a larger Hand size, letting the player get rid of unused cards to their heart's content while still being able to keep the important cards to form poker hands. Five-Card Draw works very well with Yorick, as this deck starts with 6 discards, which means it can consistently gain X1 Mult every blind with the use of 5 discards.

title: Yorick
text: Yorick: Golden Needle may also work with Yorick, as this deck also starts with 6 discards. However, this deck penalizes the player by losing $1 for each discard, which can make it awkward to use Yorick. Poker hands: Yorick can be made to work with all poker hands. Discarding a large amount of cards to form bigger poker hands like Straight or Full House is a viable strategy, while smaller poker hands like High Card and Pair can still be made consistently after discarding for Yorick. Jokers: Drunkard gives 1 extra discard, which is the same as using Red Deck, making scaling Yorick much easier.

title: Yorick
text: Yorick: Jokers: Drunkard gives 1 extra discard, which is the same as using Red Deck, making scaling Yorick much easier. Merry Andy gives 3 extra discards, which drastically helps improving Yorick, almost always giving at least an extra X1 Mult to it every round if all discards are used to their maximum effect. Though, it is important to note that its downside, -1 Hand size, along with it being an Uncommon, makes it more difficult to come by than Drunkard. A large Hand size is typically preferred when discarding for Yorick to keep important cards, which makes Jokers that give more Hand sizes, like Juggler and Troubadour, very helpful when paired with Yorick.

title: Yorick
text: Yorick: Mystic Summit, Faceless Joker, Mail-In Rebate, Castle, Hit the Road, and Burnt Joker all have abilities that activate when using discards. Spectral cards: Medium's Purple Seal generates a Tarot card after discarding a card. If the player is discarding left and right to beef up Yorick, it is helpful to get another bonus out of it. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give 1 extra discard, allowing Yorick to scale faster. Blinds: The Hook's forced discard effect can help with scaling Yorick. Decks: These decks can make Yorick difficult to use: Mad World starts with only 32 cards in deck, which may make it risky to discard more. Blast Off starts with 2 discards.

title: Yorick
text: Yorick: Blast Off starts with 2 discards. Jokers: Burglar shuts down Yorick by removing all discards and is highly recommended to be avoided at all costs when using Yorick, especially when it has the Eternal sticker. Delayed Gratification, Banner, Green Joker, and Ramen all incentivize not discarding, which goes against Yorick. Trading Card has less synergy with Yorick, since it incentivizes only discarding 1 card for the first discard. Blinds: The Water gets rid of all discards, meaning Yorick is unable to scale during the blind. Stakes: Blue Stake and above hinder Yorick's potential because they have 1 less discard by default.

title: Yorick
text: Yorick: Stakes: Blue Stake and above hinder Yorick's potential because they have 1 less discard by default. Trivia: Yorick is an unseen character in William Shakespeare's tragedy Hamlet. He is the dead court jester whose skull is exhumed in Act 5, Scene 1 of the play. The sight of Yorick's skull evokes a reminiscence by Hamlet of the man, who apparently played a role during Hamlet's upbringing: "Alas, poor Yorick! I knew him, Horatio; a fellow of infinite jest."

title: Yorick
text: Yorick: This also seems to be the origin of the 23 cards needed to discard for Yorick's scaling, as in the same Act 5, Scene 1 of the play, the following lines can be found: "This skull has lain in the earth three-and-twenty years... Sir, this skull belonged to Yorick, the king's jester". Yorick's costume in Balatro seems to be based on the jester's appearance in the 1868 painting The Young Lord Hamlet by Philip Hermogenes Calderon, albeit with the primary color altered from red to yellow. This joker is animated, with Yorick hovering just above the gold card face. The other legendary Jokers are Canio, Chicot, Perkeo, and Triboulet.

title: Yorick
text: Yorick: The other legendary Jokers are Canio, Chicot, Perkeo, and Triboulet. In other media: Yorick appears as an artifact in Monster Train 2.

title: Zany Joker
text: Zany Joker: Zany Joker (Joker). Effect: +12 Mult if played hand contains a Three of a Kind. Rarity: Common. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Type: Additive Mult. Activation: Independent. Copyable: Yes. Perishable: Yes. Eternal: Yes. Zany Joker is a Common Additive Mult Joker that provides +12 Mult when playing a hand containing a Three of a Kind. This includes hands that include any three cards with the same rank, such as a Full House.

title: Zany Joker
text: Zany Joker: Decks: Ghost Deck has several spectral cards (namely Ouija) that make deck fixing towards Three of a Kind and above much easier. Abandoned Deck and Mad World both have smaller deck sizes, making Three of a Kinds much more consistent to find. Painted Deck starts with +2 hand size, making a Three of a Kind easier to search for. Erratic Deck can work well with Zany Joker if the seed grants a deck with many cards of the same rank. Poker hands: Playing any hand with three cards of the same rank will trigger Zany Joker. This includes: Three of a Kind Full House Four of a Kind Five of a Kind Flush House Flush Five

title: Zany Joker
text: Zany Joker: Three of a Kind Full House Four of a Kind Five of a Kind Flush House Flush Five Jokers: Wily Joker gives +100 Chips when playing a Three of a Kind. The Trio gives X3 Mult when playing any hand that has a Three of a Kind, synergizing greatly with Zany Joker's flat +12 Mult. Consumables: The Hanged Man and Immolate can cut deck size down on the size of the player's deck and make assembling a Three of a Kind much easier. Death can turn cards into other cards and make Three of a Kinds more consistent to put together.

title: Zany Joker
text: Zany Joker: Death can turn cards into other cards and make Three of a Kinds more consistent to put together. Ouija makes all cards held in hand the same rank at the cost of reducing hand size by -1, making it easier to assemble a Three of a Kind. Trivia: This joker is part of a series which provide a Mult boost for a specific hand. The others are Jolly Joker, Mad Joker, Crazy Joker and Droll Joker. In demo versions of the game, Zany Joker had a different color scheme with yellow and red. The Steam page for Balatro still shows this old art in some screenshots.

title: Death
text: Death: Death (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Select 2 cards, convert the left card into the right card, (Drag to rearrange). Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. Death is a Tarot card that allows the player to convert one card into another by selecting both in a specific order. All properties, such as Enhancements, Editions, and additional chips from Hiker are copied over.

title: Death
text: Death: Usage notes: If Death is used on the automatically-selected card in the Cerulean Bell Boss Blind, the card converted will also stay permanently selected until played or discarded. If Death is used on a debuffed card, the converted card will be debuffed as well. Decks: Magic Deck starts off with 2 copies of The Fool, meaning if found early, the player can create 2 extra copies of Death and give them a major head start in terms of deck fixing. Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of Death.

title: Death
text: Death: Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of Death. Poker Hands: Death is best used to create poker hands that require a lot of deck fixing in order to assemble, especially on a consistent basis. These mainly include the secret hands Five of a Kind, Flush Five and Flush House. Jokers: Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult every time Death is used. Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of Death appearing in the Shop.

title: Death
text: Death: Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of Death appearing in the Shop. Strategies: Death is a utility Tarot that's mainly used to create extra copies of the player's strongest played cards, or just cards that the player wishes to draw more often. Death is best used to create more Gold cards and Steel cards as their respective Tarots (The Devil and The Chariot respectively) can only enhance one card at a time. Death is also incredibly useful if the player wants to create a copy of a card that has a Seal on it, mainly a card that has a Red Seal or a Blue Seal.

title: Death
text: Death: A more niche use of Death is using it in a pinch to create a desired poker hand. For example, if the player wants to assemble a Four of a Kind but is down a card needed to complete it, they can use Death to convert one of their unwanted cards into the card they need in order to complete the hand.

title: Death
text: Death: Trivia: In real life, the Death tarot card is often symbolized as rebirth, and does not typically represent actual death, hence its meaning in Balatro. That idea, that something has to end before something new can take its place, is exactly what the card does mechanically: instead of destroying a card, it lets one card’s identity end so another can take its place. Death is one of the two Tarot cards that appears on the artwork for one of the Jumbo Arcana Packs, the other one is The Emperor

title: Judgement
text: Judgement: Judgement (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Creates a random Joker card, (Must have room). Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. Judgement is a Tarot card that allows the player to create a random Joker.

title: Judgement
text: Judgement: Usage notes: Like other randomly created Jokers, the cards created by this will not be Perishable, Eternal, or Rental (though they may have an Edition). There is a 70% chance of generating a Common Joker, a 25% chance of generating an Uncommon Joker, and a 5% chance of generating a Rare Joker when using this card. Judgement cannot generate a Legendary Joker. You cannot use Judgement if you have no empty Joker slots remaining (the Use button will be greyed out). The Non-Perishable challenge has Judgement create Eternal cards. The Jokerless challenge bans Judgement.

title: Judgement
text: Judgement: The Non-Perishable challenge has Judgement create Eternal cards. The Jokerless challenge bans Judgement. Decks: Magic Deck starts off with 2 copies of The Fool, meaning if found early, the player can create 2 extra copies of Judgement and give themselves more chances to find Jokers at no cost. Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of Judgement. Bram Poker prevents Jokers from appearing in the shop, which makes Judgement more valuable. Jokers: Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult every time Judgement is used. Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of Judgement appearing in the Shop. Decks: Non-Perishable makes it very risky to use Judgement, as it spawns an Eternal Joker on this deck.

title: Judgement
text: Judgement: Decks: Non-Perishable makes it very risky to use Judgement, as it spawns an Eternal Joker on this deck. Strategies: Judgement is best used in the early game when the player doesn't have a strong economy and needs Jokers to keep them afloat. In the earlier antes, sometimes it's better to simply spend the $3 and get a random Joker, rather than using re-rolls and burning through money. Even if the Joker created by Judgement isn't needed or optimal, it can always be sold.

title: Justice
text: Justice: Justice (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Enhances 1 selected card into a Glass Card. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. Justice is a Tarot card that allows the player to enhance one card into a Glass card.

title: Justice
text: Justice: Usage notes: When using Justice on a face-down card, the card will briefly flip over and be revealed. This can be helpful on Boss blinds such as The Fish and The Wheel. When facing The Pillar, using Justice on a debuffed card will make it a "new" card and thus no longer debuffed. Decks: Magic Deck starts off with 2 copies of The Fool, meaning that the player can create 2 extra copies of Justice if found early. Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of Justice in the Shop. Jokers: Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult when Justice is used. Glass Joker gains X0.75 Mult every time a Glass card is destroyed.

title: Justice
text: Justice: Glass Joker gains X0.75 Mult every time a Glass card is destroyed. Oops! All 6s increases the odds into a 1 in 2 chance of breaking. Canio can also gain X1 Mult if a Glass face card is destroyed. Erosion gains +4 Mult whenever your deck loses a card (as long as its smaller than the starting size). Driver's License can potentially have synergy since you need 16 enhanced cards to activate it. However, if the Glass card breaks, this will not help you reach the threshold. Retrigger Jokers like Hack, Sock and Buskin, Hanging Chad, Seltzer and Dusk can reactivate Glass cards, further increasing your score.

title: Justice
text: Justice: Retrigger Jokers like Hack, Sock and Buskin, Hanging Chad, Seltzer and Dusk can reactivate Glass cards, further increasing your score. Seals: Red Seals will retrigger the Glass cards, allowing you to get a X4 Mult in total. Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of Justice appearing in the Shop. Decks: Fragile makes Justice useless since every card is already a Glass card.

title: Strength
text: Strength: Strength (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Increases rank of up to 2 selected cards by 1. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. Strength is a Tarot card that allows the player to increase the rank of two cards by one each. For example, a 4 would become a 5, a 10 would become a Jack, a King would become an Ace, and an Ace would become a 2.

title: Strength
text: Strength: Usage notes: To make many of the same rank for poker hands like Four of a Kind or Flush Five, or to make more of a desired rank for Jokers like Baron or Photograph, Strength is best used at the beginning, with Death becoming far more powerful after a few cards have been Strengthened. This is because, for example, while a 10 only requires 1 Strength card to turn into a Jack, each lower rank requires more Strength cards to make the same rank. Turning two 8s into a Jack requires 3 Strength cards, but only 2 Death cards.

title: Strength
text: Strength: When increasing the rank of face-down cards the cards will be briefly flipped. This can be used in a pinch to find out what a face-down card is. Applying Strength on an Ace (a card rank that normally provides 11 Chips) will weaken it down to a card with a rank of 2 (which normally provides 2 Chips). Poker hands: Poker hands that require 2 different ranks, like Two Pair and Full House, benefit the most from Strength, as there are more targets for it. Hands that require many of 1 rank like Four of a Kind and Flush Five also benefit from Strength, but have less targets for it.

title: Strength
text: Strength: Straight benefits from consolidating lower ranks into higher ranks to make playing Straights more consistent, and from evening out the ranks if many of 1 Modified card was created through Death. However, this does not give many targets for Strength. Jokers: Any Joker that is based around having a certain rank of card in the deck benefits from Strength, but some Jokers benefit more: Odd Todd and Even Steven affect every other rank of Aces and number cards, so Strength can be used on 20 different cards in a standard 52 deck to make them usable for these Jokers.

title: Strength
text: Strength: Fibonacci immediately benefits from Kings, 4s, and 7s being Strengthened into Aces, 5s, and 8s, meaning that 12 different cards in a standard 52 card deck are good targets for Strength. Walkie Talkie makes 3 and 9 good targets for Strength, making it slightly better than Jokers that only affect 1 rank. Trivia: When faced upright, the Strength tarot card is meant to represent "inner strength", "courage", and "willpower", especially through compassion and patience rather than brute strength. This is heavily reflected through the in-game function of increasing the rank of any two cards, even if just by one rank at a time, as increasing the power of a card even slightly can make a huge difference in a run.

title: Temperance
text: Temperance: Temperance (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Gives the total sell value of all current Jokers, (Max of $50). Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. Temperance is a Tarot card that grants the player the total sell value of all their Jokers, up to $50.

title: Temperance
text: Temperance: Usage notes: Using the Vouchers Clearance Sale and Liquidation will lower the total sell value of all Jokers and reduces the amount of money gained from Temperance. Debuffed Jokers still provide their full sell value for Temperance. Players can still use Temperance even if they have no Jokers, though they will receive $0. Synergies: Egg increases its own sell value by $3 after every round. Gift Card increases the sell value of all Jokers by $1 after every round. Although not directly synergistic like the two Jokers mentioned above, if you are playing towards Swashbuckler, you will also benefit more from Temperance. Bull and Bootstraps can gain up to +100 Chips and +20 Mult, respectively, after using Temperance.

title: Temperance
text: Temperance: Bull and Bootstraps can gain up to +100 Chips and +20 Mult, respectively, after using Temperance. Anything that enhances a Joker like The Wheel of Fortune, Hex, or Ectoplasm can increase its sell value, making Temperance more valuable. Vagabond relies heavily on Temperance to make money to use at the shop, as the player will most likely have less than $4 at the end of the round, and Temperance does not require the player to hold money unlike The Hermit. The Black Deck provides an extra Joker slot, which when used will increase Temperance's value. Similarly, Five-Card Draw provides two extra Joker slots, which when used will increases Temperance's value even more.

title: Temperance
text: Temperance: Similarly, Five-Card Draw provides two extra Joker slots, which when used will increases Temperance's value even more. Similarly, Antimatter provides an extra Joker slot, which when used will increase Temperance's value. The Omelette starts with 5 Eggs, which will increase Temperance's value, although it'll reach the limit at some point. Anti-synergies: The Painted Deck and Blast Off have one less Joker slot, which mean Temperance gives less money than usual. Similarly, Cruelty has two less Joker slots, which mean Temperance gives even less money than usual. Jokerless bans all methods of acquiring Jokers, which makes Temperance useless.

title: Temperance
text: Temperance: Jokerless bans all methods of acquiring Jokers, which makes Temperance useless. Clearance Sale and Liquidation are not generally recommended if you are going to be using Temperance frequently, as they reduce the sell price of all Jokers and thus make Temperance give less money. On Gold Stake, Rental Jokers have a sell value of $1. This also makes them effectively free if you sell them immediately, however, and it is always worth buying a Rental Joker (that does not have an Eternal sticker as well) if you are going to be using Temperance immediately afterward, as it will still net you an additional dollar.

title: Temperance
text: Temperance: Credit Card, Joker, Jolly Joker, Sly Joker and Splash all have a sell value of $1, which is not good for Temperance. Trivia: Temperance's ability to give the current sell values of all Jokers in the player's possession mirrors temperance's modern meaning (as a virtue) of abstinence and self restraint. The player is rewarded for restraining themself from selling a high value joker by getting its sell value later in a tarot card instead. Temperance is one of the four Tarot cards that appears on the artwork for one of the normal Arcana Packs. The other Tarot cards are The Fool, The Hierophant and The World.

title: The Chariot
text: The Chariot: The Chariot (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Enhances 1 selected card into a Steel Card. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Chariot is a Tarot card that allows the player to enhance one card into a Steel card.

title: The Chariot
text: The Chariot: Usage Notes: The Fragile challenge bans The Chariot. When using The Chariot on a face-down card, the card will briefly flip over and be revealed. This can be helpful on Boss blinds such as The Fish and The Wheel. When facing The Pillar, using The Chariot on a debuffed card will make it a "new" card and thus no longer debuffed. Decks: Magic Deck has 2 copies of The Fool, allowing the player to create extra copies of The Chariot if found early. Jokers: Mime re-triggers the effect of Steel cards, effectively doubling the score of every Steel card that's being held in hand. Steel Joker adds X0.2 Mult for each Steel card in the player's full deck.

title: The Devil
text: The Devil: The Devil (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Enhances 1 selected card into a Gold Card. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Devil is a Tarot card that allows the player to enhance one card into a Gold card.

title: The Devil
text: The Devil: Usage Notes: The Fragile Challenge bans The Devil. When using The Devil on a face-down card, the card will briefly flip over and be revealed. This can be helpful on Boss blinds such as The Fish and The Wheel. When facing The Pillar, using The Devil on a debuffed card will make it a "new" card and thus no longer debuffed. Decks: Magic Deck has 2 copies of The Fool, allowing the player to create extra copies of the Devil if found early. Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of the Devil in the Shop.

title: The Devil
text: The Devil: Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of the Devil in the Shop. Jokers: Golden Ticket has a chance to spawn as long as the player has one Gold card in their deck. In addition, Golden Ticket gives $4 for every Gold card that scores, incentivizing the player to play them and creating more Gold cards. Mime retriggers the effect of Gold cards, doubling the amount of money given by every Gold card held in hand. Driver's License will gain X3 Mult when 16 enhanced cards are in the player's deck; Gold cards count towards the total. Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult every time the Devil is used.

title: The Devil
text: The Devil: Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult every time the Devil is used. Vagabond benefits from Gold cards, as they generate money at the end of the round without hurting Vagabond. Juggler and Troubadour both increase hand size, allowing for more Gold cards to be utilized. Turtle Bean can also be used, but only temporarily. Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of the Devil appearing in the Shop. Trivia: The Devil enhancing cards into Gold Cards may be a reference to the common association between the devil and greed.

title: The Emperor
text: The Emperor: The Emperor (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Creates up to 2 random Tarot cards, (Must have room). Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Emperor is a Tarot card that creates two random Tarot cards in the player's consumable area (excluding the Emperor itself).

title: The Emperor
text: The Emperor: Usage Notes: The Bram Poker challenge starts the player with a copy of The Emperor. If the Emperor creates Tarot cards that the player doesn't need, keeping them in the consumable slot prevents them from showing up again in the Shop or in Arcana Packs (assuming the player doesn't also have Showman). This makes it easier for the player to find the Tarot cards that the player actually needs. The Emperor will never generate itself, unless the player has Showman.

title: The Emperor
text: The Emperor: The Emperor will never generate itself, unless the player has Showman. Jokers: Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult for every Tarot card used. Given that the Emperor spawns two Tarot cards on top of being consumed itself, that means Fortune Teller will gain +3 Mult if the player has at least two consumable slots free and uses every card spawned by the Emperor. Campfire will gain X0.25 Mult for every Tarot card sold.

title: The Emperor
text: The Emperor: Campfire will gain X0.25 Mult for every Tarot card sold. The Fool, especially if obtained from The Emperor. If The Fool was one of the two cards created by The Emperor, The Fool can be immediately used to create The Emperor again, while retaining the other Tarot card created by the original Emperor Tarot card. If the maximum number of slots for consumables is 2, the other Tarot card can then be used, then have the newer Emperor Tarot card used to spawn in two new Tarot cards. Vouchers: The Crystal Ball voucher gives +1 consumable slot, making it easier to get both Tarot cards from the Emperor by having more room.

title: The Emperor
text: The Emperor: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon will make the Emperor appear in the Shop more often. Anti-Synergies: Nebula Deck will only have one consumable slot without Crystal Ball, making the Emperor only spawn one Tarot card. Trivia: The Emperor can theoretically be infinitely duplicated so long as it creates The Fool when used. The odds of this happening once is only 1 in 10, and the chance of it happening many times in a row is exponentially lower. However, if Perkeo is used to obtain a Negative copy every other Tarot card, this can become a guarantee, and the player can obtain infinite copies of a particular Tarot card.

title: The Emperor
text: The Emperor: The Emperor is one of the two Tarot cards that appears on the artwork for one of the Jumbo Arcana Packs, the other one is Death.

title: The Empress
text: The Empress: The Empress (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Enhances 2 selected cards to Mult Cards. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Empress is a Tarot card that allows the player to enhance two cards into Mult cards.

title: The Empress
text: The Empress: Usage Notes: The Bram Poker challenge starts the player with a copy of The Empress. The Fragile challenge bans The Empress. When using The Empress on a face-down card, the card will briefly flip over and be revealed. This can be helpful on Boss blinds such as The Fish and The Wheel. When facing The Pillar, using The Empress on a debuffed card will make it a "new" card and thus no longer debuffed. Decks: Magic Deck starts off with 2 copies of The Fool, meaning that the player can create 2 extra copies of the Empress. Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of the Empress in the Shop.

title: The Empress
text: The Empress: Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of the Empress in the Shop. Jokers: Driver's License will gain X3 Mult when 16 enhanced cards are in the player's deck; Mult cards count towards the total. Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult every time the Empress is used. Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of the Empress appearing in the Shop. In other media: In Black Mirror, there is a scene in "Hotel Reverie" where a character is seen playing Balatro, and The Empress is a card shown onscreen. Joker, Campfire, Blue Joker, Sixth Sense, and Uranus are shown onscreen as well.

title: The Fool
text: The Fool: The Fool (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Creates the last Tarot or Planet card used during this run, The Fool excluded. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Fool is a Tarot card that allows the player to create another copy of the last Tarot or Planet card used during the current run, excluding The Fool itself.

title: The Fool
text: The Fool: Usage notes: The Fool cannot be used if your consumable area is full. If The Fool was your last used Tarot or Planet card, you cannot use The Fool again until you use a different card. Spectral cards do not affect The Fool at all, thus the player cannot create a copy of the last Spectral card they used before The Fool. This also applies to Spectral cards from Arcana and Celestial Packs (The Soul and Black Hole) and Spectral cards from Omen Globe since they are still Spectral cards. Editions on Tarot/Planet cards, such as the Negative edition from Perkeo, are not copied by The Fool. The Magic Deck starts the player with two copies of The Fool.

title: The Fool
text: The Fool: The Magic Deck starts the player with two copies of The Fool. Trivia: The icon of the final achievement of Balatro, Completionist++, is a golden version of The Fool's drawing. The Fool is one of the four Tarot cards that appears on the artwork for one of the normal Arcana Packs. The other Tarot cards are Temperance, The Hierophant and The World.

title: The Hanged Man
text: The Hanged Man: The Hanged Man (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Destroys up to 2 selected cards. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Hanged Man is a Tarot card that allows the player to permanently destroy two cards from their deck.

title: The Hanged Man
text: The Hanged Man: Usage notes: Destroying a selected card while battling Cerulean Bell will allow the player to freely select other cards for that hand. Decks: All decks benefit from the Hanged Man, as it is generally recommended for the player to thin out their deck as early as possible. But there are two that stand out: Magic Deck starts off with 2 copies of The Fool, meaning if found early, the player can create 2 extra copies of the Hanged Man and give them a major head start in terms of deck fixing. Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant, making it easier to find copies of the Hanged Man in the Shop.

title: The Hanged Man
text: The Hanged Man: Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant, making it easier to find copies of the Hanged Man in the Shop. Jokers: Erosion gains +4 Mult every time a card is destroyed; destroying 2 cards with the Hanged Man means that Erosion will gain +8 Mult, as long as the final result is having less cards than the starting deck. Glass Joker gains X0.75 Mult for every Glass card destroyed, so it can effectively gain X1.5 Mult with 2 Glass cards destroyed. Canio gains X1 Mult for each face card destroyed, so it can effectively gain X2 Mult with 2 Face cards destroyed. Hologram works well with the Hanged Man, as it can destroy cards that were only added to pump Hologram.

title: The Hanged Man
text: The Hanged Man: Hologram works well with the Hanged Man, as it can destroy cards that were only added to pump Hologram. Strategies: The Hanged Man is best used to cut the unwanted cards out of the player's deck in order to make their most desired cards easier to find. For example, if the player intends on playing only face cards, the player can use the Hanged Man to destroy the numbered and Ace cards. The Hanged Man is also useful if the player has a Joker that scales when cards are destroyed, such as Erosion and Canio. Trivia: Destroyed cards will be visually burned, except for Glass cards, which will be visually broken as if they were broken on use.

title: The Hanged Man
text: The Hanged Man: The Hanged Man has meanings that correlate with the concepts of "surrender" and "letting go", emphasizing the card's ability to destroy up to 2 selected cards.

title: The Hermit
text: The Hermit: The Hermit (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Doubles money, (Max of $20). Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Hermit is a Tarot card that doubles the player's current money, up to $20.

title: The Hermit
text: The Hermit: Usage notes: The Hermit will give no money if the player is in debt. Synergies: Bull and Bootstraps can gain up to +40 Chips and +8 Mult, respectively, after using The Hermit. Anti-Synergies: Vagabond requires having low money, which limits The Hermit to be used out of any blind. Credit Card does not make a good combo with The Hermit, since debt makes it do nothing. Trivia: The Hermit is one of the two Tarot cards that appear on the artwork of one of the Mega Arcana Packs. The other one is The Tower.

title: The Hierophant
text: The Hierophant: The Hierophant (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Enhances 2 selected cards to Bonus Cards. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Hierophant is a Tarot card that allows the player to enhance two cards into Bonus cards.

title: The Hierophant
text: The Hierophant: Usage Notes: The Fragile challenge bans The Hierophant. When using The Hierophant on a face-down card, the card will briefly flip over and be revealed. This can be helpful on Boss blinds such as The Fish and The Wheel. When facing The Pillar, using The Hierophant on a debuffed card will make it a "new" card and thus no longer debuffed. Decks: Chips are at their absolute strongest on Plasma Deck due to the balancing gimmick, making Bonus cards a worthwhile investment. Magic Deck starts off with 2 copies of The Fool, meaning that the player can create 2 extra copies of the Hierophant.

title: The Hierophant
text: The Hierophant: Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of the Hierophant in the Shop. Jokers: Driver's License will gain X3 Mult when 16 enhanced cards are in the player's deck; Bonus cards count towards the total. Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult every time the Hierophant is used. Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of the Hierophant appearing in the Shop. Trivia: The Hierophant is one of the four Tarot cards that appears on the artwork for one of the normal Arcana Packs. The other Tarot cards are The Fool, Temperance and The World.

title: The High Priestess
text: The High Priestess: The High Priestess (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Creates up to 2 random Planet cards, (Must have room). Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The High Priestess is a Tarot card that creates two random unlocked Planet cards in the player's consumable area.

title: The High Priestess
text: The High Priestess: Usage notes: The High Priestess is best used if the player has Constellation as it gains X0.1 Mult for every Planet card used, meaning that the Joker will consistently gain X0.2 Mult for every planet spawned the High Priestess if has at least two free slots in their consumable area. Although a more niche strategy, if the Planet cards spawned by the High Priestess are irrelevant to the player, keeping them in the consumable area stops them from showing up again in the Shop and in Celestial Packs (assuming the player doesn't also have Showman). This makes it easier for the player to find their desired Planet card.

title: The High Priestess
text: The High Priestess: Decks: Magic Deck has 2 copies of The Fool, allowing the player to create extra copies of the High Priestess if found early. Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of the High Priestess in the Shop. Jokers: Campfire will gain X0.25 Mult for every Planet card sold. Constellation will gain X0.1 Mult for every Planet card used. Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult every time the High Priestess is used. Satellite will pay out an extra $1 per unique Planet card used in a run. If used early the High Priestess can potentially spawn Planet cards not yet used by the player, boosting Satellite.

title: The High Priestess
text: The High Priestess: Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of the High Priestess appearing in the Shop. Anti-Synergies: Nebula Deck will only have one consumable slot without Crystal Ball, making the High Priestess only spawn one Planet card. Additionally, Nebula Deck already starts with Telescope, meaning that the player will no longer have to try their luck with the High Priestess and can find their most wanted Planet card by opening Celestial Packs. Astronomer makes all Planet cards and Celestial Packs free, but not the High Priestess, making it a worse value option for generating Planet cards.

title: The Lovers
text: The Lovers: The Lovers (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Enhances 1 selected card into a Wild Card. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Lovers is a Tarot card that allows the player to enhance one card into a Wild card.

title: The Lovers
text: The Lovers: Usage Notes: When using The Lovers on a face-down card, the card will briefly flip over and be revealed. This can be helpful on Boss blinds such as The Fish and The Wheel. When facing The Pillar, using The Lovers on a debuffed card will make it a "new" card and thus no longer debuffed. The Fragile challenge bans The Lovers. Decks: Magic Deck has 2 copies of The Fool, allowing the player to create extra copies of the Lovers if found early. Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of the Lovers in the Shop.

title: The Lovers
text: The Lovers: Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of the Lovers in the Shop. Jokers: Since Wild cards count as all suits, any Joker that grants a bonus based on the suit of card, including, but not limited to: Ancient Joker. Castle. Seeing Double. Flower Pot. Blackboard. All Sinful Jokers like Lusty Joker, etc. All Suit-Oriented Jokers like Rough Gem, etc. all benefit from them. Driver's License will gain X3 Mult when 16 enhanced cards are in the player's deck; Wild cards count towards the total. Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult every time the Lovers is used. Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of the Lovers appearing in the Shop.

title: The Lovers
text: The Lovers: Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of the Lovers appearing in the Shop. Blinds: The Head, The Window, The Club, and The Goad all debuff Wild cards, making them useless when playing hands like Flush, Straight Flush/Royal Flush, Flush House, and Flush Five.

title: The Magician
text: The Magician: The Magician (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Enhances 2 selected cards to Lucky Cards. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Magician is a Tarot card that allows the player to enhance two selected cards into Lucky cards.

title: The Magician
text: The Magician: Usage Notes: The Fragile challenge bans The Magician. When using The Magician on a face-down card, the card will briefly flip over and be revealed. This can be helpful on Boss blinds such as The Fish and The Wheel. When facing The Pillar, using The Magician on a debuffed card will make it a "new" card and thus no longer debuffed. Decks: Magic Deck starts off with 2 copies of The Fool, meaning that the player can create 2 extra copies of the Magician. Zodiac Deck has Tarot Merchant making it easier to find copies of the Magician in the Shop. Jokers: Oops! All 6s enhances the chances of triggering the Lucky cards that the Magician creates.

title: The Magician
text: The Magician: Jokers: Oops! All 6s enhances the chances of triggering the Lucky cards that the Magician creates. Lucky Cat continuously builds X0.25 Mult for every successful triggering of Lucky cards. Hanging Chad retriggers the first played card twice, which can benefit Lucky cards for more chances on hitting either the +20 Mult or $20. Seltzer, Sock and Buskin, Hack, and Dusk can all double the amount of Lucky card triggers when a hand is played, which is the best way to increase the odds of getting +20 Mult or $20. Driver's License will gain X3 Mult when 16 enhanced cards are in the player's deck; Lucky cards count towards the total.

title: The Magician
text: The Magician: Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult every time the Magician is used. Seals: Red Seals double the opportunities for the Lucky card to trigger. Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of the Magician appearing in the Shop.

title: The Moon
text: The Moon: The Moon (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Converts up to 3 selected cards to Clubs. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Moon is a Tarot card that allows the player to change the suit of up to three cards to Clubs.

title: The Moon
text: The Moon: Usage notes: When using The Moon on a face-down card, the card will briefly flip over and be revealed. This can be helpful on Boss blinds such as The Fish and The Wheel. Synergies: Jokers that synergize with the Club suit, like Gluttonous Joker and Onyx Agate, benefit from The Moon. The Moon can also help trigger Blackboard and Seeing Double easier. Anti-Synergies: Checkered Deck doesn't start with any Club cards, which can make it very awkward to use The Moon. The Club debuffs Club cards, making them unable to be scored.

title: The Moon
text: The Moon: The Club debuffs Club cards, making them unable to be scored. Trivia: The Moon is part of a group of celestial body themed Tarot cards that change the suit of playing cards. The other Tarot cards in this group are The World, The Sun, and The Star.

title: The Star
text: The Star: The Star (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Converts up to 3 selected cards to Diamonds. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Star is a Tarot card that allows the player to change the suit of up to three cards to Diamonds.

title: The Star
text: The Star: Usage notes: When using The Star on a face-down card, the card will briefly flip over and be revealed. This can be helpful on Boss blinds such as The Fish and The Wheel. Synergies: Jokers that synergize with Diamond suit, like Greedy Joker and Rough Gem, benefit from The Star. text: The Sun: The Sun (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Converts up to 3 selected cards to Hearts. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Sun is a Tarot card that allows the player to change the suit of up to three cards to Hearts.

title: The Sun
text: The Sun: Usage notes: When using The Sun on a face-down card, the card will briefly flip over and be revealed. This can be helpful on Boss blinds such as The Fish and The Wheel. Synergies: Checkered Deck: The Sun can further increase the amount of Hearts this deck starts with. Jokers that synergize with the Heart suit, like Lusty Joker and Bloodstone, benefit from The Sun. Anti-Synergies: The Head debuffs Heart cards, making them unable to be scored. Trivia: The Sun is part of a group of celestial body themed Tarot cards that change the suit of playing cards. The other Tarot cards in this group are The World, The Moon, and The Star.

title: The Tower
text: The Tower: The Tower (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: Enhances 1 selected card into a Stone Card. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Tower is a Tarot card that allows the player to enhance one card into a Stone card.

title: The Tower
text: The Tower: Usage Notes: The Fragile challenge bans The Tower. Jokers: Driver's License will gain X3 Mult when 16 enhanced cards are in the player's deck; Stone cards count towards the total. Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult every time the Tower is used. Stone Joker gains +25 Chips for every Stone card added to the player's deck. The Idol will provide X2 Mult when a card of a specific rank and suit is scored; Stone cards cannot be selected, and so will increase the chance of hitting your preferred card.

title: The Tower
text: The Tower: Poker hands: With the except of five-hand poker hands like Straights and Flushes*, all poker hands work with the Tower as Stone cards can be played in any hand. However, if the player wants to only play Stone cards, then they're better off leveling up High Card. *(Unless the player has Four Fingers) Vouchers: Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon increase the possibility of the Tower appearing in the Shop. Blinds: The Head, The Window, The Club, The Goad, and the The Plant cannot affect Stone cards as they do not have suits or ranks to begin with. Jokers: Ancient Joker depends on having access to all 4 suits, and has no use for Stone cards.

title: The Tower
text: The Tower: Jokers: Ancient Joker depends on having access to all 4 suits, and has no use for Stone cards. Trivia: The Tower is one of the two Tarot cards that appear on the artwork for one of the Mega Arcana Packs. The other one is The Hermit. The Tower is seen missing a pixel from its innermost border near the top left of the card.

title: The Wheel of Fortune
text: The Wheel of Fortune: The Wheel of Fortune (Tarot card). Type: Tarot. Effect: 1 in 4 chance to add Foil, Holographic, or Polychrome edition to a random Joker. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. The Wheel of Fortune is a Tarot that has a 1 in 4 chance to add an Edition to a random Joker.

title: The Wheel of Fortune
text: The Wheel of Fortune: Usage notes: The chosen edition is weighted at a 50% chance of making a Joker Foil, 35% chance of making a Joker Holographic, and a 15% chance of making a Joker Polychrome. When multiplying these with the default 25% chance, the combined odds are a 12.5% chance of making a Joker Foil, 8.75% chance of making a Joker Holographic and a 3.75% chance of making a Joker Polychrome. The number of jokers you have that Wheel could apply to does not change the probability of it working.

title: The Wheel of Fortune
text: The Wheel of Fortune: The number of jokers you have that Wheel could apply to does not change the probability of it working. The Wheel will not apply to any Joker that already has an edition (including Negative). It also cannot be used if all Jokers already have an edition, and its Use button will be disabled. If The Wheel of Fortune misses the chance to apply an edition to a Joker, the card simply says the word, "Nope!" Decks: Fragile starts with two Oops! All 6s, which means Wheel of Fortune will always trigger. Jokers: Oops! All 6s will increase the chance to apply an edition to 2 in 4 (50%).

title: The Wheel of Fortune
text: The Wheel of Fortune: Jokers: Oops! All 6s will increase the chance to apply an edition to 2 in 4 (50%). Fortune Teller gains +1 Mult every time Wheel of Fortune is used, even if the player gets nothing out of it. Decks: Jokerless bans all methods of acquiring Jokers, which makes Wheel of Fortune useless. Ectoplasm has an anti-synergy, as the Wheel of Fortune may apply a different edition to a useful joker that can no longer be made Negative. Trivia: In certain bugged seeds (such as QV1LTNYQ and FAJ8UPYL), due to glitch in random number generation, The Wheel of Fortune can never trigger, unless with two Oops! All 6s.

title: The Wheel of Fortune
text: The Wheel of Fortune: Its classic "Nope!" effect had a pin during a crowdfunded Pin Collection by Makeship along with Jimbo and the Cavendish Joker. Playstack also released a product where the "Nope!" effect appears on a bucket hat. The Wheel of Fortune also had a Youtooz Collectible figurine due to a merchandising collaboration in addition to Jimbo/ Joker and the Vagabond Joker. The Wheel of Fortune's "Nope!" appears on an Ante Up! shirt due to an official merchandise collaboration with Fangamer. The exclamation point of the "Nope!" appears outside of the word to the left.

title: The Wheel of Fortune
text: The Wheel of Fortune: The Wheel of Fortune has straightforward meanings like "good luck" and "a turning point" when faced upright, as well as reversed meanings of "bad luck" and "resistance to change". Both of these sets of meanings refer to the chanceful application of an edition to a random Joker, or rather a lack thereof.

title: The World
text: The World: The World can also help trigger Blackboard easier. Anti-Synergies: The Goad debuffs Spade cards, making them unable to be scored. title: Ceres
text: Ceres: Ceres (Planet card). Type: Planet. Effect: Increases Flush House hand value by +4 Mult and +40 Chips. Unlock Requirement: Play Flush House during the current run. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. Ceres is a Planet that increases the value of Flush House by +4 Mult and +40 Chips (default 14 Mult x 140 Chips).

title: Ceres
text: Ceres: It can only appear during a run after playing at least one Flush House. Trivia: Ceres is labeled "Dwarf Planet" in the card description, along with Pluto and Eris. Ceres is a dwarf planet located in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, as shown at the top of the card. The visible asteroids surrounding the planet in the card's art also reflect this. In other media: This planet card, alongside with the depiction of Ceres and those of the other secret Planet cards, are referenced in Vampire Survivors, specifically in a weapon called the "Negative Space."

title: Ceres
text: Ceres: The Negative depiction of Ceres, alongside all other planets and the rocket from the Rocket joker, are all referenced in that weapon as well.

title: Earth
text: Earth: Earth (Planet card). Type: Planet. Effect: Increases Full House hand value by +2 Mult and +25 Chips. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $3. Sell Price: $1. Earth is a Planet card that increases the value of Full House by +2 Mult and +25 Chips (default 4 Mult x 40 Chips).

title: Earth
text: Earth: Trivia: The Earth's only moon, the Moon, can be seen on its card. Another Planet card with this similar property is Eris. Earth is one of the four Planet cards that appears in the artwork for one of the normal Celestial Packs. The other ones are Mercury, Jupiter and Uranus. On Balatro's Steam Page an early design of Earth appears where the card itself appears to be a cooler blue, while the continents appear to be more brown. In versions before 0.9.0l-DEMO the background of Planet cards were grey instead of the cyan used since.

title: Earth
text: Earth: In versions before 0.9.0l-DEMO the background of Planet cards were grey instead of the cyan used since. In other media: This planet card (along with the planet icon), all of the other non-secret Planet cards, and the Rocket joker, are all referenced in Vampire Survivors, specifically in a weapon called the "Celestial Booster." The Negative depiction of Earth is referenced in another weapon from the game, the Negative Space, which is the evolved version of the Celestial Booster.

title: Eris

title: Planet X

title: Ankh
text: Ankh: Ankh (Spectral card). Type: Spectral. Effect: Create a copy of a random Joker, destroy all other Jokers, (Removes Negative from copy). Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Ankh is a Spectral card that picks a random Joker, and destroys all other Jokers. It then creates a copy of that randomly chosen Joker.

title: Ankh
text: Ankh: Usage notes: The copied Joker will retain almost all the properties of the original, including any scaling, Edition, and Stickers. There is only 1 exception: Negative is removed from the copy. Ankh cannot destroy Eternal Jokers, though this does not impact which Joker can be chosen as target. Ankh cannot be used if the player's Joker slots are all filled, and will show a "No Space!" message. The line "(Removes Negative from copy)" in the card's effect only shows if you already have a Negative Joker.

title: Ankh
text: Ankh: The line "(Removes Negative from copy)" in the card's effect only shows if you already have a Negative Joker. Copying a Joker does not copy the card back - the copied Joker will always be created with the Red Deck's card back and can thus be identified even when turned face down by the Amber Acorn boss blind. This is presumed to be a bug. If the player tries to buy and use Ankh in the shop (only on Ghost Deck) while all Joker slots are filled, the Ankh card will become stuck in place for the rest of the run. The player can actually interact and move the bugged Ankh around. This is likely a bug.

title: Ankh
text: Ankh: Decks: Non-Perishable works well with Ankh, as all Jokers are Eternal, allowing the player to duplicate any Jokers freely without destroying other Jokers. However, it becomes useless once all Jokers slots are filled. Stakes: Playing on Black Stake and above allows Eternal Jokers to appear. Since Eternal Jokers cannot be destroyed, the player can safely use Ankh to duplicate any Jokers if they are Eternal. Decks: Typecast sets Joker slots to 0 after Ante 4, at which point Ankh won't be able to be used anymore. On a Knife's Edge makes it risky to use Ankh as it can duplicate the Eternal, Pinned Ceremonial Dagger, leaving the first copy permanently stuck behind the second copy and thus unable to scale.

title: Ankh
text: Ankh: Jokerless bans all methods of acquiring Jokers, which makes Ankh useless. Jokers: Generally, passive effect Jokers like Four Fingers or Pareidolia do not benefit from being copied by Ankh. There are also some Jokers that might be expected to work well when copied but can behave unexpectedly with multiple copies. This includes: Sixth Sense: Only one Spectral card will be created, even with multiple copies of it. To Do List: Unlike Jokers like Mail-In Rebate, where multiple copies will always choose the same rank, multiple copies of To Do List may want different hands to be played. Vampire: Only the leftmost Vampire will scale when removing enhancements.

title: Ankh
text: Ankh: Vampire: Only the leftmost Vampire will scale when removing enhancements. Strategy: Ankh creates a duplicate of random Joker at the expense of all non- Eternal Jokers, giving the player 2 copies of a Joker, essentially doubling its value. This effect has lots of potential to help the run pivot in multiple different ways depending on the Joker it chooses to copy, but be careful, it can mess up the run as well if not considered carefully.

title: Ankh
text: Ankh: Ankh essentially acts as a one-time use, more dangerous version of Invisible Joker. On higher stakes, particularly from Black Stake onward due to the Eternal sticker appearing from this Stake, it pivots in liability and usage, providing immense value for one's run with a downside that may easily be ignored. Note that Ankh also copies the Perishable and Rental stickers, which can be hugely detrimental. Ankh destroys Jokers, which means it's a good idea to sell all the Jokers that you don't want it to copy, gaining a little bit of money back and leaving a greater chance to hit other Jokers if you have multiple Eternal Jokers and only one of them you want to duplicate.

title: Ankh
text: Ankh: If you leave one Joker that is not Eternal, there is always a chance that Ankh hits it, doubling that Joker which can be helpful for scoring while still keeping the other Jokers that have the Eternal sticker. If your build requires the current Jokers that, while not too beneficial going into the late game, is needed for survival, doesn't function as well with two Jokers of the same type, or suffer greatly if you duplicate a certain Joker and destroy the others, it may not be wise to use Ankh, because the effect may not be beneficial to the run and the Joker destruction effect can in turn be run-killing.

title: Ankh
text: Ankh: Trivia: An "Ankh" (☥) is a symbol of life and immortality in ancient Egyptian culture and is said to be a precursor to the original Christian cross, despite the two being completely separate religious symbols. When Ankh duplicates a Joker, the color of spawning animation changes with the rarity of Joker. For example, if a Rare Joker is duplicated, the animation will be red. Ankh is the only item with this property, as most items do not have a spawning animation (such as Judgement), or can only generate a specific rarity (such as Riff-Raff).

title: Aura
text: Aura: Aura (Spectral card). Type: Spectral. Effect: Add Foil, Holographic, or Polychrome effect to 1 selected card in hand. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Aura is a Spectral card that allows the player to give 1 selected card a randomly chosen edition.

title: Aura
text: Aura: Usage notes: The odds of each edition are weighted, with a 50% chance to make a card Foil, a 35% chance to make a card Holographic, and a 15% chance to make a card Polychrome. These are the same odds that The Wheel of Fortune has when upgrading a Joker when it triggers. When playing against The Pillar, unlike tarot cards that give enhancements, using Aura to add editions to debuffed cards does not make them be considered as not played and recover. Aura cannot be used on a playing card that already has an edition.

title: Aura
text: Aura: Aura cannot be used on a playing card that already has an edition. Strategy: Aura applies a random Edition on one playing card of the player's selection, be it Foil which gives +50 Chips, Holographic giving +10 Mult or Polychrome which is a X1.5 Mult when scored. This effect while being very good early on for easy scoring, needs to be used on specific cards for the best value, and even then rarely provides a large benefit, which may make it not too appealing. Any method of duplicating playing cards buffed by Aura like Death, DNA or Cryptid can help finding them easier, which creates easier scoring opportunities.

title: Aura
text: Aura: Each Edition has a different usage and thus have different availability and usage across multiple builds. The following can be treated as a 'guide' for choosing whether to use Aura or not: Foil works miraculously on the Plasma Deck due to the tendency of Chips-oriented builds on it. A 5-card hand with all Foil gives an extra +250 Chips, equal to Stuntman, which is an amazing source of scoring that's even retriggerable by certain Jokers. Outside of it, Foil tends to fall off, due to Chips not necessarily being needed when on a build heavily favoring Mult. Still, it can be good in certain builds where the lack of a reliable Chips source can make it shine.

title: Aura
text: Aura: Holographic serves as the middle ground when using Aura. Its effect tends to fall off quite a lot, due to most builds requiring lots of XMult to function, and +10 Mult doesn't bring a massive benefit. Still, this Edition has its uses in the early game, if no reliable + Mult Joker are found, and on some builds extra Mult added can go a long way. Such an example would be on a build that has lots of XMult Jokers, but a small base Mult to begin with.

title: Aura
text: Aura: Polychrome is by far the best edition for almost all builds, being an XMult effect that's comparable to Ancient Joker or Baseball Card, provided the player has many of them to play. On the early game where not much access to Planets is available, one might find it a struggle to use Polychrome efficiently, but once a high enough base Mult is reached it fits seamlessly. It is generally recommended to use Aura on cards already improved with Enhancements and Seals, and if not at disposal, at least on viable ranks.

title: Aura
text: Aura: Any kind of retrigger works with Aura, and so the player is incentivized to use it on 2, 3, 4, 5 for Hack, face cards for Sock and Buskin, or cards with Red Seal. Since cards with editions cannot be overwritten by other editions, it can sometimes be beneficial to skip Aura if there is only one copy of the desired card in the deck and one of the editions is undesirable. Trivia: Aura, when referring to spiritualism, is a form of emanation surrounding the body of a person and acts as the most essential part of the individual.

title: Black Hole
text: Black Hole: Black Hole (Spectral card). Type: Spectral. Effect: Upgrade every poker hand by 1 level. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: 4 (cannot be found in shop). Sell Price: $2. Black Hole is a Spectral card that upgrades every poker hand, including hands not yet discovered, by one level.

title: Black Hole
text: Black Hole: Black Hole can only be found in Booster Packs, where it has a chance of replacing each planet or spectral card in the pack with a 0.3% chance. This means Black Hole can be found in Spectral Packs and Celestial Packs, but also in Arcana Packs if the Omen Globe voucher has been claimed. It cannot be created by Sixth Sense and Séance, or found in the shop when using the Ghost Deck. Usage notes: Despite being able to be found in Celestial Packs, Black Hole is strictly considered a Spectral card and not a Planet card. Thus, Black Hole does not trigger the effects for Satellite or Constellation and cannot be copied by The Fool.

title: Black Hole
text: Black Hole: Thus, Black Hole does not trigger the effects for Satellite or Constellation and cannot be copied by The Fool. Black Hole will level up the secret poker hands (Five of a Kind, Flush House, Flush Five) even if they have not been played during the run. Synergies: Black Hole is a powerful card that should almost always be taken when looking in Celestial Packs. It synergizes with every build since it levels up every hand. Obelisk has a great synergy with Black Hole as it encourages a wide variety of hands to be played.

title: Black Hole
text: Black Hole: Obelisk has a great synergy with Black Hole as it encourages a wide variety of hands to be played. Strategy: Black Hole upgrades every poker hand by one level, including the secret hands. This is one of the rarest cards in Balatro, only having a 0.3% chance to replace any card in Celestial Packs and Spectral Packs. With Omen Globe, Black Hole can also spawn in Arcana Packs.

title: Black Hole
text: Black Hole: Black Hole acts as a superior way of upgrading poker hands to Planet cards by giving one level to all poker hands. This effect, while falling short when compared to The Soul, is still generally better than its counterpart, Planet cards, when The Soul can be worse in certain situations against other Tarot cards.

title: Black Hole
text: Black Hole: Using Black Hole may sometimes not be the best move. Extra levels on all poker hands are hard to utilize without using a deck that is not fixed to playing around a certain poker hand, and using the respective Planet card can put it on The Fool while also boosting Constellation and possibly Satellite. So even though it is not recommended, sometimes skipping Black Hole can be a decent choice, although very rarely will the player fall into such a situation.

title: Black Hole
text: Black Hole: Trivia: The art style of Black Hole differs from other Spectral cards and resembles that of Planet cards. It also appears to be pulling in the sides of the card and its own name tag towards the center by the force of its gravity. The Soul is the Tarot-equivalent version of Black Hole despite both being Spectral cards. Both have the same 0.3% chance to replace another card in the packs they appear in. Black Holes themselves aren't a spiritual element but rather an astronomical object of no energy that is spiritually believed to be a portal to another world or to the beyond.

title: Black Hole
text: Black Hole: This and The Soul are the only two spectral cards to feature something on the top part of the card. The Black Hole features the entire solar system, which includes the planets from all of the planet cards, excluding Eris, which is only featured in its own planet card, and Planet X, which isn't in the solar system at all.

title: Cryptid
text: Cryptid: Cryptid (Spectral card). Type: Spectral. Effect: Create 2 copies of 1 selected card in your hand. Unlock Requirement: Available from start. Buy Price: $4. Sell Price: $2. Cryptid is a Spectral card that creates 2 copies of a selected card, allowing the player to easily create copies of a specific card in their deck.

title: Cryptid
text: Cryptid: Usage notes: Similar to Death, the copies are almost completely identical, including Enhancements, Editions and Seals and permanently gained chips (from Hiker). Exceptions and differences with Death include when copying the force-selected card from the Cerulean Bell: though the copies are not force selected by default, they cannot be unselected once selected once, or when copying a face-down card from The Mark: the copies will be face-up, revealing their identity while still keeping the original card face-down. Another difference is that death does not add new cards to the player's deck, and does not scale Hologram unlike cryptid.

title: Cryptid
text: Cryptid: Synergies: Cryptid synergizes very well with deck fixing cards when used correctly, such as The Hanged Man, because it is very effective and efficient in focusing the player's entire deck around multiple copies of a single card. Cryptid also copies enhancements, so it is very easy to make a stupidly strong deck if the player has Perkeo. Baron gives exponentially more scoring when a Cryptid is used to make copies of a Red Seal Steel King. With enough Cryptids and the right Jokers, the elusive naneinf score can be achieved. Hologram gets a free X.5 Mult boost when a Cryptid card is used.

title: Cryptid
text: Cryptid: Hologram gets a free X.5 Mult boost when a Cryptid card is used. Glass Joker and Canio both benefit from Cryptid as it can add more face/glass cards to destroy and scale up. Anti-Synergies: Erosion becomes weaker after using Cryptid. Strategy: Cryptid creates 2 copies of 1 selected card in the player's hand. This effect is very powerful for helping the player find a specific card wanted, as it is basically tripling a specific card in the deck with pretty much no downside with just one use. Cryptid can be used to copy cards that already have a good Enhancement, Edition and/or Seal. ex: Red Seal Glass Polychrome King.

title: Cryptid
text: Cryptid: Using Cryptid is highly beneficial to most builds, ranging from High Card to Flush Five builds. Inversely, it may not work very well for Straight/Straight Flush builds, as the sudden influx of a rank may make it harder to find other ranks. Cryptid bypasses the hand size limit, which can be useful in a High Card build utilizing Steel cards if the player has a way to hold multiple copies of Cryptid at the same time, e.g. by using Perkeo. Even if not attainable, one single Cryptid use will still give the player what is essentially +2 hand sizes, which is immense value.

title: Cryptid
text: Cryptid: Unlike Death, Cryptid does not modify other cards but rather adds more cards, which might worsen its deck-fixing value. Do note that, if there is no good card for Cryptid to copy, it might be best to skip it entirely, as using it can bloat the deck and make it harder to find other cards. Trivia: The term Cryptid is defined as a creature of legend or mythological origins, more accurately found in stories known as folklore told by people who have believed that said creatures exist or have found traces of them but is not actually proven or scientifically documented.

title: Cryptid
text: Cryptid: Cryptid's effect of creating two exact copies of a selected card could reference that there could be more than just one, or perhaps multiple copies, of a certain cryptid in the world. To which stories based on said creatures could differ depending on certain cultures and folklore. The skull in Cryptid's art is based on a Jackalope, a mythological creature of Western North American folklore that is said to be a rabbit with big antler-like horns. It was previously mistaken as a Wendigo, a malevolent winter spirit of Algonquian folklore that was said to be a symbol of cannibalism amongst humans. Wendigos are commonly misinterpreted in popular culture as having deer skulls for heads with antlers on them.

title: Cryptid
text: Cryptid: Both Jackalopes and Wendigos are not true cryptids so much as they are actually mythical creatures fabricated by human imagination and exist only in fiction. Whenever Cryptid creates copies of a selected playing card, the copies have a spawning animation with the color green. There exists a purposefully unbalanced Balatro mod under the same name originally made by programmer MathIsFun0.

title: Deja Vu
