Consumables: The Hanged Man and Immolate: Allows trimming of unwanted cards to make those added by Magic Trick more frequent.

title: Magic Trick
text: Magic Trick: Consumables: The Hanged Man and Immolate: Allows trimming of unwanted cards to make those added by Magic Trick more frequent. Vouchers: Overstock and Overstock Plus: Increases the amount of playing cards seen per reroll. Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut: Makes rerolls cheaper, decreasing the cost to find more playing cards. Decks: Ghost Deck decreases the chance of finding cards from Magic Trick, relative to other decks. Jokers: Erosion: Adding playing cards with magic trick decreases Erosion by +4 Mult. As Magic Trick decreases the chance of finding Jokers and Consumables in the shop, any Jokers that gain value from them are weakened. This includes: Campfire: Gaining X0.25 Mult per Joker or Consumable sold. Astronomer: Making Planet cards free.

title: Magic Trick
text: Magic Trick: Campfire: Gaining X0.25 Mult per Joker or Consumable sold. Astronomer: Making Planet cards free. Fortune Teller: Gains +1 Mult per tarot card used. Constellation: Gains X0.1 Mult per planet card used. Vouchers: Hone and Glow Up: With fewer Jokers seen per shop there are fewer chances for Hone to give them an Edition. Planet Merchant, Planet Tycoon, Tarot Merchant, and Tarot Tycoon all conflict with the chance to find playing cards by increasing the probabilities of Planet cards and Tarot cards respectively. Strategies: It is generally not recommended to take Magic Trick without a specific synergy in mind, as the added playing cards will dilute the shop while providing less value than the Jokers and Consumables they replace.

title: Magic Trick
text: Magic Trick: Trivia: This Voucher's sprite depicts the Top Hat magic trick, which is usually made with rabbits. In this case, the trick is made with a playing card, like if magically, playing cards start to appear in the shop. Card tricks are also a common magic trick used by magicians, which further ties into the nature of the voucher.

title: Money Tree
text: Money Tree: Money Tree (Voucher). Type: Upgraded. Effect: Raise the cap on interest earned in each round to $20. Unlock Requirement: Max out the interest per round earnings for ten consecutive rounds. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades from: Seed Money. Money Tree is a voucher that raises the cap on interest earned in each round to $20.

title: Money Tree
text: Money Tree: Usage Notes: The player must max out the interest per round earnings for ten consecutive rounds to unlock Money Tree. Seed Money must be purchased in the same run for Money Tree to appear. The The Omelette challenge bans Money Tree. The Rich get Richer challenge starts with a copy of Seed Money and Money Tree. Decks: Yellow Deck gives an initial boost to your economy, allowing you to hit the interest cap earlier on. Jokers: To the Moon is the best Joker to pair with Seed Money. Its interactions with interest and Seed Money are listed earlier on this page. Bull: This voucher helps generate more interest each round, scaling Bull faster.

title: Money Tree
text: Money Tree: Bull: This voucher helps generate more interest each round, scaling Bull faster. Bootstraps: This voucher helps generate more interest each round, scaling Bootstraps faster. Decks: Green Deck and Mad World disable interest, making Money Tree useless. Luxury Tax receives little benefit from Money Tree as in order to take advantage of its high interest, the player would want high starting money, which this deck punishes. Jokers: Vagabond encourages playing without earning interest, making Money Tree useless. Credit Card enables going $20 in debt, well below the minimum interest level.

title: Money Tree
text: Money Tree: Credit Card enables going $20 in debt, well below the minimum interest level. Trivia: The name of this voucher could be a reference and inverse of the common idiom, "money doesn't grow on trees," which refers to money being hard-earned and thus should not be wasted on needless things.

title: Nacho Tong
text: Nacho Tong: Nacho Tong (Voucher). Type: Upgraded. Effect: Permanently gain an additional +1 hand per round. Unlock Requirement: Play a total of 2,500 cards. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades from: Grabber. Nacho Tong is a voucher that increases the number of hands per round by 1.

title: Nacho Tong
text: Nacho Tong: Usage Notes: The player must play a total of 2,500 cards across runs to unlock Nacho Tong. This Voucher shares an unlock requirement (as well as art) with the Card Player achievement. Grabber must be purchased in the same run for Nacho Tong to appear. The Blast Off and Golden Needle challenges ban Nacho Tong. Decks: Blue Deck: Since it has +1 hand by default, Nacho Tong gives Blue Deck the most amount of hands out of any deck. Green Deck: Gives $2 at end of round if hand goes unused. Black Deck: Helps make up for Black Deck's lack of Hands.

title: Nacho Tong
text: Nacho Tong: Black Deck: Helps make up for Black Deck's lack of Hands. Jokers: All Jokers that scale upon hand played, such as Green Joker, Square Joker, and Ride the Bus have more opportunities to scale. Troubadour's -1 Hand has less of an effect. Card Sharp: The extra hand allows more possible hands to be played with the X3 Mult active. Loyalty Card becomes easier to activate. Space Joker: The extra hand gives more opportunities for Space Joker to activate. Hiker: Nacho Tong allows more cards to be played and upgraded. Vagabond: Allows for the generation of 1 more Tarot card per Blind. Reserved Parking and Matador: Nacho Tong allows for the generation of more money.

title: Nacho Tong
text: Nacho Tong: Reserved Parking and Matador: Nacho Tong allows for the generation of more money. Tags: Handy Tag will give more money. Vouchers: Hieroglyph: Helps make up for Hieroglyph's -1 Hand downside. Trivia: According to LocalThunk, this name comes from the joke of calling one's hands Nacho Tongs—in which Nacho is a type of Texas-Mexican tortilla chip topped with cheese and often additional savory toppings (as depicted in its art), and tong is a gripping device. Nacho Tong's art is based on the hand of LocalThunk himself.

title: Observatory
text: Observatory: Observatory (Voucher). Type: Upgraded. Effect: Planet cards in your consumable area give X1.5 Mult for their specified poker hand. Unlock Requirement: Use a total of 25 Planet cards from any Celestial Pack. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades from: Telescope. Observatory is a tier 2 voucher that causes Planet cards in your Consumables slots to give X1.5 Mult when their poker hand is played. This bonus is added after Jokers (see Guide: Activation Sequence for detailed information on activation order).

title: Observatory
text: Observatory: Usage notes: The player must use a total of 25 Planet cards from booster packs across runs to unlock Observatory. The corresponding tier 1 voucher Telescope must be purchased in the same run for Observatory to appear. Synergies: Jokerless can greatly benefit from Observatory, with this being one of only a few ways to access multiplicative mult. Perkeo can create negative copies of a planet after each shop, effectively giving X1.5 Mult each shop. This can be paired with a Blueprint or Brainstorm for even more planets. Showman makes it possible to obtain multiple copies of the same planet from The Shop. Crystal Ball increases consumable slot size by 1, allowing one more planet to be held.

title: Observatory
text: Observatory: Crystal Ball increases consumable slot size by 1, allowing one more planet to be held. Blue Seal create planet cards in the consumable slot when held in hand at end of round, and are an easy way to obtain multiple copies of the same planet. Anti-Synergies: Despite being slightly easier to get on Nebula Deck, the smaller consumable slot section can make Observatory somewhat weaker.

title: Omen Globe
text: Omen Globe: Omen Globe (Voucher). Type: Upgraded. Effect: Spectral cards may appear in any of the Arcana Packs. Unlock Requirement: Use a total of 25 Tarot cards from booster packs. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades from: Crystal Ball. Omen Globe is a voucher that has a 20% chance to replace each individual Tarot card in an Arcana Pack with a Spectral card.

title: Omen Globe
text: Omen Globe: Usage notes: The player must use a total of 25 Tarot cards from booster packs across runs to unlock Omen Globe. Crystal Ball must be purchased in the same run for Omen Globe to appear. Showman allows multiple copies of the same Spectral card to appear in the same pack. Below is a chart on the approximate probabilities of receiving each number of Spectral cards from an Arcana pack: Decks: Erratic Deck: The unbalanced starting ranks can give you direction of where to target deck fixing (e.g. taking Grim when starting with an irregular amount of Aces). Abandoned Deck: With fewer starting cards, the effect of deck-altering Spectral cards like Immolate and Grim is increased.

title: Omen Globe
text: Omen Globe: Abandoned Deck: With fewer starting cards, the effect of deck-altering Spectral cards like Immolate and Grim is increased. Zodiac Deck: Because Zodiac deck starts with Tarot Merchant it is easier to gain Tarot cards, which when combined with Spectral cards gained from Omen Globe can provide strong deck fixing. Magic Deck: Omen Globe appears more often in this deck since it starts with Crystal Ball. Poker hands: As Spectral cards provide lots of deck fixing potential (such as card destruction via Immolate and duplication via Cryptid), it is generally much easier to form higher scoring hands like Four of a Kind and Flush Five.

title: Omen Globe
text: Omen Globe: Jokers: Hologram: Omen Globe makes it easier to find the Familiar, Grim, Incantation, and Cryptid Spectral cards, all of which add playing cards into the deck and thus scale Hologram. Erosion: A single Immolate can take Erosion to +20 Mult on its own, making for a potentially large source of mult. Driver's License: As Grim, Familiar, and Incantation all create enhanced cards and Cryptid can also duplicate an enhanced card, Driver's License can potentially reach 16 enhanced cards faster. Mime: Can benefit heavily from the increased amount of Blue Seals (from Trance) and Red Seals (from Deja Vu).

title: Omen Globe
text: Omen Globe: Mime: Can benefit heavily from the increased amount of Blue Seals (from Trance) and Red Seals (from Deja Vu). Any Joker that can retrigger played cards, such as Sock and Buskin or Hanging Chad, can be very powerful, as the modifications Spectral cards like Aura and Talisman apply can be activated multiple times. Jokers that create Spectral cards or Tarot cards such as Sixth Sense, Cartomancer, and Hallucination pair well with the Spectral cards created by Omen Globe. This is because the deck fixing potential Spectral/Tarot cards provide are more powerful in larger quantities, potentially leading to a snowball effect.

title: Omen Globe
text: Omen Globe: Accordingly, any jokers that benefit heavily from deck fixing are also more powerful, such as The Idol, Mail-In Rebate, and Triboulet. Vouchers: Clearance Sale and Liquidation: Reduces the cost of the packs necessary for Omen Globe's effect. Tarot Merchant and Tarot Tycoon: The deck fixing effects of the tarot cards pair well with the effects of spectral cards gained through Omen Globe. Paint Brush and Palette: Can supplement the hand size loss from Ouija and Ectoplasm.

title: Omen Globe
text: Omen Globe: Paint Brush and Palette: Can supplement the hand size loss from Ouija and Ectoplasm. Stakes: Playing on Black Stake and above allows Eternal Jokers to appear. Since Eternal Jokers can't be destroyed, the player can safely use Ankh to duplicate any Jokers or Hex to apply Polychrome to any Jokers if they are Eternal. Omen Globe can help the player to find Ankh and Hex more easily. Jokers: Fortune Teller: Does not increment if you take a Spectral card from an Arcana Pack, although it can still be useful since the player can find Medium easier. Consumables: The Fool's value decreases as it cannot give Spectral cards.

title: Omen Globe
text: Omen Globe: Consumables: The Fool's value decreases as it cannot give Spectral cards. Blinds: The Pillar: As Spectral cards heavily favour deck fixing, this blind can be an issue if playing the same cards repeatedly.

title: Omen Globe
text: Omen Globe: Strategy: As mentioned above, Spectral cards are most useful for their deck fixing potential. With powerful spectral cards such as Deja Vu and Immolate able to alter or destroy cards in a more significant ways than tarot cards. It is generally recommended to pair with as many other sources of spectral or tarot cards to maximise this effect to draw powerful cards as consistently as possible. Also, it is generally better to receive Omen Globe early into the run, giving the most time to deck fix and to gain value out of Hex and Ankh before having multiple powerful jokers.

title: Omen Globe
text: Omen Globe: Trivia: In superstition an omen is a foretelling of the future events through phenomenon. This is the apparent thematic connection with the prior voucher, Crystal Ball, which is tied to fortune-telling as both relate to non-scientific predictions of the future.

title: Overstock
text: Overstock: Overstock (Voucher). Type: Base. Effect: +1 card slot available in shop. Unlock Requirement: Unlocked from the start. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades to: Overstock Plus. Overstock is a voucher that increases the number of card slots available in the Shop from 2 to 3. It also immediately restocks any empty card slots in the Shop when purchased.

title: Overstock
text: Overstock: Reroll Efficiency: The discount for rerolling can be calculating using the following formula, where x is the number of rerolls: Discount={(x+1)(5x+19)8,if x is odd5x2+24x+208,if x is even A calculator for the discounts can be found here. Usage notes: The Zodiac Deck starts with a copy of Overstock, along with Tarot Merchant and Planet Merchant. Coupon Tag does not work with this Voucher restocking cards after purchasing it. For example, the first time you enter the store, the items in the shop will be free. If you then purchase the Overstock Voucher after, the new items in the shop will cost the regular amount.

title: Overstock
text: Overstock: Overstock will pay for itself quickly as it functions effectively as half a reroll when entering the shop while also boosting the strength of subsequent rerolls. Synergies: Chaos the Clown, Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut can make rerolling very lucrative and allow the player to get even more value for less money. Flash Card has a similar want of rerolls, and having more shop slots naturally makes rerolling in general more worth it. One can also consider that more Shop slots means more chances for items that may provide money like The Hermit, which then means more possible rerolls for Flash Card. Having more shop slots allows Jokers such as Campfire, Constellation, and Fortune Teller to scale faster.

title: Overstock
text: Overstock: Having more shop slots allows Jokers such as Campfire, Constellation, and Fortune Teller to scale faster. Trivia: "Overstock" refers to the suppliance of items in a store that goes beyond its original inventory limit. This could also be done to prevent going out of stock until the product is shelved again. The Overstock Voucher appears on an Ante Up! shirt due to an official merchandise collaboration with Fangamer. Overstock is so far the first and only voucher to appear on or as a part of any physical merchandise. There are 2 miscolored pixels in the inner field of the sprite, causing the white dotted line to be slightly thicker on the upper left corner.

title: Overstock Plus
text: Overstock Plus: Overstock Plus (Voucher). Type: Upgraded. Effect: +1 card slot available in shop. Unlock Requirement: Spend a total of $2500 at the shop. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades from: Overstock. Overstock Plus is a voucher that increases the number of card slots available in the shop from 3 to 4. It also immediately restocks any empty card slots in the Shop when purchased.

title: Overstock Plus
text: Overstock Plus: Reroll Efficiency: The discount for rerolling can be calculating using the following formula, where x is the number of rerolls: Discount=32x2+132x+5 A calculator for the discounts can be found here. Usage notes: The player must spend a total of $2500 at shop across runs to unlock Overstock Plus. Overstock must be purchased in the same run for Overstock Plus to appear. Synergies: Chaos the Clown, Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut can make rerolling very lucrative and allow the player to get even more value for less money. Flash Card has a similar want of rerolls, and having more shop slots naturally makes rerolling in general more worth it.

title: Overstock Plus
text: Overstock Plus: One can also consider that more Shop slots means more chances for items that may provide money like The Hermit, which then means more possible rerolls for Flash Card. Having more shop slots allows Jokers such as Campfire, Constellation, and Fortune Teller to scale faster.

title: Paint Brush
text: Paint Brush: Paint Brush (Voucher). Type: Base. Effect: +1 hand size. Unlock Requirement: Unlocked from the start. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades to: Palette. Paint Brush is a voucher that increases hand size by 1.

title: Paint Brush
text: Paint Brush: Decks: Checkered Deck contains 26 Spades and 26 Hearts. By increasing hand size by 1, a Flush can be drawn on every hand. Luxury Tax: Paint Brush can help offset the hand size penalty given by this deck. Five-Card Draw: Paint Brush can partially offset the deck's -3 hand size penalty. Jokers: Any Joker that benefits from held in hand procs will appreciate the extra hand size. Having a bigger hand size will allow you to hold more Kings for Baron, and more Queens for Shoot the Moon. Reserved Parking can proc more if you're able to hold more face cards in hand, allowing you to earn more money.

title: Paint Brush
text: Paint Brush: Mime can retrigger more cards this way as well. This can allow you to retrigger Blue Seals, Gold cards, Steel cards, or the Jokers mentioned above. This also benefits Sixth Sense by making it much easier to find your 6s. However this is not a long term synergy, unless you combine it with DNA, which makes the combination a lot easier, as you are more likely to find what you need. Paint Brush can help offset Jokers that reduce hand size such as Merry Andy and Stuntman. Poker hands: Poker hands that require 5 cards to play like Full House, or Straight can benefit from the large hand size, making it easier to find the cards to make them.

title: Paint Brush
text: Paint Brush: Smaller hands like High Card or Pair also benefit from large hand sizes, by allowing you to hold onto more Steel cards to increase your score. title: Palette
text: Palette: Palette (Voucher). Type: Upgraded. Effect: +1 hand size. Unlock Requirement: Reduce your hand size down to five cards. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades from: Paint Brush. Palette is a voucher that increases hand size by 1.

title: Palette
text: Palette: Usage notes: The player must reduce their hand size to 5 cards in a run to unlock Palette. This can be achieved through a combination of Merry Andy, Stuntman, Ectoplasm, Ouija, and/or The Manacle. Paint Brush must be purchased in the same run for Palette to appear. Decks: Luxury Tax: Palette can help offset the hand size penalty given by this deck. Five-Card Draw: Palette can partially offset the deck's -3 hand size penalty. Jokers: Any Joker that benefits from held in hand procs will appreciate the extra hand size. Having a bigger hand size will allow you to hold more Kings for Baron, and more Queens for Shoot the Moon.

title: Petroglyph
text: Petroglyph: Petroglyph (Voucher). Type: Upgraded. Effect: -1 Ante,, -1 discard each round. Unlock Requirement: Reach Ante 12. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades from: Hieroglyph. Petroglyph is a voucher that decreases the ante by 1, at the cost of 1 discard.

title: Petroglyph
text: Petroglyph: Usage Notes: The player must reach Ante 12 in a run to unlock Petroglyph. Hieroglyph must be purchased in the same run for Petroglyph to appear. Petroglyph can cause certain Boss Blinds or Showdown Blinds to appear on antes they wouldn't normally be able to appear on, since the Boss Blind doesn't change after Petroglyph is purchased. Rerolling the Blind after purchasing Petroglyph will change it back into an expected Boss Blind. Ante 0 can be reached by purchasing a Petroglyph on Ante 1. Ante -1 can be reached via incredibly rare circumstances, involving a voucher tag, very fast reflexes, and the seed to roll both Hieroglyph and Petroglyph. A basic demonstration can be found here.

title: Petroglyph
text: Petroglyph: Petroglyph actually just reduces the Ante value by 1, without ending or starting Antes, so Ante-related effects (such as The Pillar) will still work as usual. If the player obtains Petroglyph in Ante 9, returns to Ante 8 and fails, non-Endless mode game over scenes will be used (i.e., the background turns red and Jimbo appears). This may be a bug. Decks: Red Deck gives +1 discard, which can be helpful by mitigating the -1 discard penalty from Petroglyph. Jokers: Jokers that rely on scaling can benefit from Petroglyph with the extra Ante. By playing more rounds, you give your Jokers more chances to get stronger. For example: Square Joker, Lucky Cat, Castle, etc.

title: Petroglyph
text: Petroglyph: For example: Square Joker, Lucky Cat, Castle, etc. Alternatively, Throwback can gain more XMult by skipping more Blinds. Jokers that can potentially reward you for playing more Blinds. You can get more value from these Jokers this way. Economy Jokers such as Satellite, Golden Joker, Mail-In Rebate, etc. Tarot and Spectral card Jokers such as Vagabond, Superposition, Séance, etc. With up to three more Blinds with the additional Ante, Burnt Joker will get more chances to activate. This also includes Jokers like Trading Card, Marble Joker, Space Joker, etc. Cards with Seals can be activated more with the extra Blind. Drunkard can provide +1 discard, which can be helpful by mitigating the -1 discard penalty from Petroglyph.

title: Petroglyph
text: Petroglyph: Drunkard can provide +1 discard, which can be helpful by mitigating the -1 discard penalty from Petroglyph. Merry Andy can provide +3 discards, mitigating the -1 discard penalty from Petroglyph at the cost of -1 hand size. Burglar removes all discards, making Petroglyph's -1 discard penalty irrelevant. Vouchers: Wasteful and Recyclomancy both give +1 discard, which can be helpful by mitigating the -1 discard penalty from Petroglyph. Decks: Green Deck will give the player $1 less at the end of each blind. Blast Off only starts with 2 discards, which means that redeeming Petroglyph will leave the players with just one discard.

title: Petroglyph
text: Petroglyph: Blast Off only starts with 2 discards, which means that redeeming Petroglyph will leave the players with just one discard. Jokers: Jokers that require discards, such as Banner, Trading Card, Mail-In Rebate, etc. will be weakened due to fewer discards. Tags: Garbage Tag will give less money. Stakes: On Blue Stake or higher, Petroglyph becomes more difficult to use with the -1 discard restriction from the start of the run. This means it may be more difficult to get the poker hand you need before the end of the round.

title: Petroglyph
text: Petroglyph: Trivia: A petroglyph is a rock carving, especially a prehistoric one. Due to petroglyphs being a prehistoric form of art, the effect of the voucher sending the player back another ante can be interpreted as them being sent further backwards in time.

title: Planet Merchant
text: Planet Merchant: Planet Merchant (Voucher). Type: Base. Effect: Planet cards appear 2X more frequently in the shop. Unlock Requirement: Unlocked from the start. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades from: Planet Tycoon. Planet Merchant is a Voucher that increases the rate that Planet cards appear in the Shop by approximately 2x. This can make it harder to find important jokers to increase scoring or earn money if picked up too early.

title: Planet Merchant
text: Planet Merchant: To increase the rate that Planet cards appear, this voucher changes the weight of planets in the shop from 4 to 9.6. If nothing else impacts the shop weights, this changes the planet chance from approximately 14.3% to 28.6%. Usage notes: Planet Merchant does not increase the chance of finding Celestial Packs. The Zodiac Deck starts with a copy of Planet Merchant, along with Tarot Merchant and Overstock. The Blast Off Challenge Deck starts with a copy of Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon. Jokers: Constellation can scale faster with more Planet cards to use. Astronomer allows the player to purchase all Planet cards in The Shop for free.

title: Planet Merchant
text: Planet Merchant: Astronomer allows the player to purchase all Planet cards in The Shop for free. Satellite earns $1 at end of round per unique Planet card used this run, which can be easier to find with more Planet cards in The Shop. Campfire can scale faster with more Planet cards to buy and sell. Vouchers: Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut allow the player to find more Planet cards with cheaper rerolls. Overstock and Overstock Plus allow the player to find even more Planet cards by seeing more cards per reroll. Anti-Synergies: Jokers that have strong synergies with another Joker, like Photograph and Hanging Chad, can be harder to find with more Planet cards diluting the Shop.

title: Planet Merchant
text: Planet Merchant: Cavendish can be harder to find once Gros Michel goes extinct if Planet Merchant was bought, because it dilutes the Shop. Jokers that rely on Tarot cards, like Fortune Teller, can be harder to use with less Tarot cards in the Shop. Trivia: Tarot Merchant is the matching voucher for Tarot cards.

title: Planet Merchant
text: Planet Merchant: Trivia: Tarot Merchant is the matching voucher for Tarot cards. "X Merchant" is slang from sports that implies that a player "trades" solely on one specific thing, e.g., foul merchant, free throw merchant, etc. This means that they make their money from drawing fouls and taking free throws instead of scoring some other way. Planet Merchant means that the run relies on specifically Planet cards to win, because they show up more frequently in the Shop. It also has a double meaning, as the player also buys more Planet cards, as they would from a merchant.

title: Recyclomancy
text: Recyclomancy: Recyclomancy (Voucher). Type: Upgraded. Effect: Permanently gain an additional +1 discard each round. Unlock Requirement: Discard a total of 2500 cards. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades from: Wasteful. Recyclomancy is a voucher that increases the amount of discards each round by 1.

title: Recyclomancy
text: Recyclomancy: Usage notes: The player must discard a total of 2500 cards across runs to unlock Recyclomancy. This Voucher shares an unlock requirement (as well as art) with the Card Discarder achievement. Wasteful must be purchased in the same run for Recyclomancy to appear. Decks: Red Deck: Red Deck has +1 discard by default, meaning that buying Recyclomancy gives Red Deck more discards than any other deck. Green Deck: Gives $1 for every discard that goes unused. Black Deck: An extra discard can potentially save a run on Black Deck, as it gives the player an extra opportunity to search for their desired play without resorting to wasting one of the deck's already minimal amount of hands.

title: Recyclomancy
text: Recyclomancy: Blast Off: Recyclomancy can help offset the deck's -1 discard penalty. Poker hands: All poker hands benefit from an extra discard, but those that require more discards than usual to play, like Flushes, Full Houses, and Straights, will be grateful for Recyclomancy. Joker: Castle and Hit the Road: The extra discard provides more opportunities to discard cards of a suit or Jacks, respectively. Yorick: The extra discard allows for faster scaling each round. Mail-In Rebate and Faceless Joker: The extra discard allows more cards to be discarded for money. Trading Card and Burnt Joker: The extra discard can help offset the discard used for the Jokers' effect. "Remaining discards" Jokers: Banner gives more chips if the player has more discards.

title: Recyclomancy
text: Recyclomancy: "Remaining discards" Jokers: Banner gives more chips if the player has more discards. Delayed Gratification provides $2 per discard if no discards are used. Modifiers: Purple Seal: The extra discard provides more opportunities to generate more Tarot cards. Vouchers: Petroglyph: Recyclomancy can help offset the -1 discard from Petroglyph. Stakes: Blue Stake and above removes a discard, making Recyclomancy extremely beneficial. Jokers: Burglar sets discards to 0, and having more discards will not increase the number of hands obtained. Green Joker as it gets -1 Mult for every discard used. Ramen as any discard reduces its XMult. Blinds: The Water will always set discards to 0.

title: Recyclomancy
text: Recyclomancy: Ramen as any discard reduces its XMult. Blinds: The Water will always set discards to 0. Trivia: Recyclomancy is a coined word composed of recycle and -mancy; the latter is a suffix derived from Greek μαντεία (manteia), meaning "divination by means of" or "prophecy through", and is often used to describe things generally related to magic, such as Necromancy and Cartomancy (Cartomancer is related to this).

title: Reroll Glut
text: Reroll Glut: Reroll Glut (Voucher). Type: Upgraded. Effect: Rerolls cost an additional $2 less. Unlock Requirement: Reroll the shop a total of 100 times. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades from: Reroll Surplus. Reroll Glut is a voucher causing rerolls to cost $4 less than default, making their starting cost $1. This effectively saves $ equal to Rerolls×4.

title: Reroll Glut
text: Reroll Glut: Usage notes: The player must reroll the shop a total of 100 times across runs to unlock Reroll Glut. Reroll Surplus must be purchased in the same run for Reroll Glut to appear. Synergies: Flash Card: Similar to Reroll Surplus, rerolls are cheaper, allowing Flash Card to be scaled at a lower cost. Cheaper rerolls allows more cards to be seen at a lower cost and thus can be useful to scale Jokers such as Campfire, Constellation, and Fortune Teller.

title: Reroll Surplus
text: Reroll Surplus: Reroll Surplus (Voucher). Type: Base. Effect: Rerolls cost $2 less. Unlock Requirement: Unlocked from the start. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades to: Reroll Glut. Reroll Surplus is a voucher causing rerolls to cost $2 less, making their starting cost $3. This effectively saves $ equal to Rerolls×2.

title: Reroll Surplus
text: Reroll Surplus: Synergies: Flash Card: Rerolls are cheaper, allowing Flash Card to be scaled at a lower cost. Cheaper rerolls allows more cards to be seen at a lower cost and thus can be useful to scale Jokers such as Campfire, Constellation, and Fortune Teller.

title: Retcon
text: Retcon: Retcon (Voucher). Type: Upgraded. Effect: Reroll Boss Blind unlimited times, $10 per roll. Unlock Requirement: Discover 25 Blinds. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades from: Director's Cut. Retcon is a voucher that allows the player to reroll the boss blind as much as they want for $10 per roll.

title: Retcon
text: Retcon: Usage notes: The player must discover 25 Blinds to unlock Retcon. Director's Cut must be purchased in the same run for Retcon to appear. Rerolling on Ante 8 (or a multiple of 8) will always roll a Showdown Blind, and other antes will always roll a normal Boss Blind. Decks: Green Deck can allow you to gain more money in order to purchase then use this voucher. Yellow Deck may help you with the cost of this as well.

title: Retcon
text: Retcon: Yellow Deck may help you with the cost of this as well. Poker hands: Any poker hands you have that are countered by the current boss blind can be avoided, by using this voucher. For example, The Plant can be changed into a boss that does not debuff a deck reliant on face cards. Jokers: Matador can benefit depending on what the rerolled boss blind becomes, and your own deck. Having a strong economy with Jokers like To the Moon, Satellite, Mail-In Rebate, etc. may be necessary to keep rerolling the Blinds since it's expensive. Jokers: Chicot and Luchador can disable the current boss effect, making this voucher less useful.

title: Retcon
text: Retcon: Jokers: Chicot and Luchador can disable the current boss effect, making this voucher less useful. However, since Chicot’s ability to disable boss blinds allows you to gain Hand size if you have multiple of that card when facing The Manacle, it can be worth it to reroll for the Manacle. Unfortunately, due to this requiring you to have multiple Chicots, it is unlikely that this strategy can be viable. Trivia: A Retcon, short for retroactive continuity, is when an established narrative is changed or rewritten afterwards. This voucher allows you to reestablish the "narrative" of the run by changing the Boss Blind unlimited times to the one you prefer so long as you have the money for it.

title: Retcon
text: Retcon: In the files of some Beta versions of the game there is a pink variant of the cassette.

title: Seed Money
text: Seed Money: Seed Money (Voucher). Type: Base. Effect: Raise the cap on interest earned in each round to $10. Unlock Requirement: Unlocked from the start. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades to: Money Tree. Seed Money is a voucher that raises the cap on interest earned after defeating a Blind to $10. This means that you can earn interest with up to $50 in reserve. The extra income from Seed Money almost always makes it a worthy investment, especially as it unlocks the Money Tree voucher.

title: Seed Money
text: Seed Money: Usage Notes: The The Omelette challenge bans Seed Money. The Rich get Richer challenge starts with a copy of Seed Money and Money Tree. Decks: Yellow Deck gives an initial boost to your economy, allowing you to hit the interest cap earlier on. Jokers: To the Moon is the best Joker to pair with Seed Money. Its interactions with interest and Seed Money are listed earlier on this page. Bull: This voucher helps generate more interest each round, scaling Bull faster. Bootstraps: This voucher helps generate more interest each round, scaling Bootstraps faster. Decks: Green Deck and Mad World disable interest, making Seed Money useless.

title: Seed Money
text: Seed Money: Decks: Green Deck and Mad World disable interest, making Seed Money useless. Luxury Tax receives little benefit from Seed Money as in order to take advantage of its high interest, the player would want high starting money, which this deck punishes. Jokers: Vagabond encourages playing without earning interest, making Seed Money useless. Credit Card enables going $20 in debt, well below the minimum interest level.

title: Seed Money
text: Seed Money: Credit Card enables going $20 in debt, well below the minimum interest level. Trivia: "Seed money" is a technical term referring to the initial investment of capital that new projects or businesses receive when they are not self-sustaining and need help covering initial expenses such as marketing, research, or office space. The voucher giving extra interest reflects this; the player is given a little extra income to help sustain their run but not enough to the point where they can carelessly spend.

title: Tarot Merchant

title: Tarot Merchant
text: Tarot Merchant: Stone Joker gains more Chips for more Stone cards in the deck from The Tower and Death. Steel Joker gains more XMult for more Steel cards in the deck from The Chariot and Death. Glass Joker gains more XMult when more Glass cards are destroyed, by creating them with Justice and Death, and destroying them by playing or with The Hanged Man. Golden Ticket can provide more money with more Gold cards in the deck from The Devil and Death, and the player can find them more easily by thinning the deck with The Hanged Man.

title: Tarot Merchant

title: Telescope
text: Telescope: Telescope (Voucher). Type: Base. Effect: Celestial Packs always contain the Planet card for your most played poker hand. Unlock Requirement: Unlocked from the start. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades to: Observatory. Telescope is a voucher that causes Celestial Packs to contain the Planet card for the player's currently most played Poker Hand during the run. In case of a tie, Telescope picks the higher-tier hand.

title: Telescope
text: Telescope: Usage notes: Telescope will still function normally if the player already has the designated Planet card in their Consumables slot, even without Showman. Telescope picks the higher-tier hand in case of multiple most played hands. Purchasing Telescope enables Observatory to appear that run (provided that Observatory is unlocked). The Nebula Deck starts with a copy of Telescope. Telescope may unintentionally become a hindrance if the player's most played hand is not the hand they plan to score most of their chips with. For example, if the player is scoring with Flushes but is using hands as discards, then the player's most played hand may end up being High Card instead, and all Celestial Packs will have Pluto instead of Jupiter.

title: Telescope
text: Telescope: Decks: Red Deck: The extra discard can make it easier to get specific hands. Yellow Deck: The extra starting cash makes it easier to buy more packs early on. Painted Deck: The +2 hand size makes it easier to get specific hands. Poker hands: Telescope can synergize with any poker hand because it can be upgraded from every Celestial Pack. But it's more difficult to synergize well with multiple hands, since it only guarantees the most played hand. Jokers: Constellation: Opening Celestial Packs is further rewarded as Constellation gains X0.1 Mult for each planet used. Astronomer: Celestial Packs become free. Jokers: Red Card has anti-synergy because it incentivizes skipping Booster Packs, while taking Telescope incentivizes not skipping Planet Packs.

title: Telescope
text: Telescope: Jokers: Red Card has anti-synergy because it incentivizes skipping Booster Packs, while taking Telescope incentivizes not skipping Planet Packs. Obelisk encourages playing multiple different hands, which does not work well with Telescope focusing on the player's most played hand. Satellite will be harder to scale with Telescope. Trivia: Telescope is associated with space, similar to most other planet-related or poker hand level-related objects such as Constellation or Space Joker respectively. The reason of Telescope's effect to guarantee the planet card for your most played hand may be a reference to how telescopes are used to watch planets from far away.

title: Telescope
text: Telescope: In the demo version of Balatro, Telescope had a completely different effect, where it unlocked a feature called "Planetarium," which allowed you to select one of up to two random Planet cards when a Blind is selected. Also in the demo, the Crystal Ball voucher unlocked "Tarot Reading," which had the same effect except for tarot cards.

title: Wasteful
text: Wasteful: Wasteful (Voucher). Type: Base. Effect: Permanently gain +1 discard each round. Unlock Requirement: Unlocked from the start. Buy Price: $10. Upgrades to: Recyclomancy. Wasteful is a voucher that increases the amount of discards each round by 1.

title: Wasteful
text: Wasteful: Decks: Red Deck: Red Deck has +1 discard by default, meaning that buying Wasteful gives Red Deck more discards than any other deck. Green Deck: Gives $1 for every discard that goes unused. Black Deck: An extra discard can potentially save a run on Black Deck, as it gives the player an extra opportunity to search for their desired play without resorting to wasting one of the deck's already minimal amount of hands. Blast Off: Wasteful can help offset the deck's -1 discard penalty. Poker hands: All poker hands benefit from an extra discard, but those that require more discards than usual to play, like Flushes, Full Houses, and Straights, will be grateful for Wasteful.

title: Wasteful
text: Wasteful: Joker: Castle and Hit the Road: The extra discard provides more opportunities to discard cards of a suit or Jacks, respectively. Yorick: The extra discard allows for faster scaling each round. Mail-In Rebate and Faceless Joker: The extra discard allows more cards to be discarded for money. Trading Card and Burnt Joker: The extra discard can help offset the discard used for the Jokers' effect. "Remaining discards" Jokers: Banner gives more chips if the player has more discards. Delayed Gratification provides $2 per discard if no discards are used. Modifiers: Purple Seal: The extra discard provides more opportunities to generate more Tarot cards. Vouchers: Petroglyph: Wasteful can help offset the -1 discard from Petroglyph.

title: Wasteful
text: Wasteful: Vouchers: Petroglyph: Wasteful can help offset the -1 discard from Petroglyph. Stakes: Blue Stake and above removes a discard, making Wasteful extremely beneficial. Jokers: Burglar sets discards to 0, and having more discards will not increase the number of hands obtained. Green Joker as it gets -1 Mult for every discard used. Ramen as any discard reduces its XMult. Blinds: The Water will always set discards to 0. Trivia: Wasteful means using or expending something of value carelessly, extravagantly, or to no purpose. This comes in handy with its ability of giving an extra discard.

title: Base
text: Base: Base (Edition). Type: Edition. Effect: No extra effects. Base is an edition card modifier that provides no extra effects. It is the default edition for all playing cards, Jokers, and Consumables.

title: Base
text: Base: Notes: Jokers have the Base edition 96% of the time, changing to 92% with Hone and 84% with Glow Up. Playing cards found in Standard Packs have the Base edition 92% of the time, changing to 84% with Hone and 68% with Glow Up. Consumables such as Tarot cards, Planet cards, and Spectral cards always appear with the Base edition, unless generated through Perkeo.

title: Foil
text: Foil: Foil (Edition). Type: Edition. Effect: +50 Chips. Foil is an edition card modifier that makes a Joker or playing card give +50 Chips.

title: Foil
text: Foil: Foil adds +$2 to the buy price of jokers and playing cards. Jokers: Foil Jokers can naturally appear in the Shop with a 2% chance. The chance to get a Foil can be increased with Hone & Glow Up by 2X and 4X respectively. Ankh is able to duplicate Foil Jokers. Invisible Joker can copy a Foil Joker, and the copy will keep the edition. The Wheel of Fortune has a 50% chance of applying Foil to a random Joker if it activates. Foil Tag applies Foil to the next base edition joker in the shop and makes it free. Playing Cards: Foil playing cards can be naturally acquired from Standard Packs with a 4% chance.

title: Foil
text: Foil: Playing Cards: Foil playing cards can be naturally acquired from Standard Packs with a 4% chance. The chance to get a Foil can be increased with Hone & Glow Up by 2X and 4X respectively. Foil playing cards are able to be purchased from the Shop if Illusion is owned. Aura has a 50% chance to apply Foil to a selected playing card in your hand. Death, Cryptid, and DNA can duplicate Foil playing cards.

title: Foil
text: Foil: Death, Cryptid, and DNA can duplicate Foil playing cards. Jokers: Due to being an edition that is often given to playing cards (through Standard Packs, Aura, etc.), Jokers that can retrigger playing cards that may have Foil like Hanging Chad, Sock and Buskin, and Hack have the ability to indirectly provide hundreds of Chips through retriggers. Nearly all Jokers that give a large amount of Mult (namely, ones that are able to give a high amount of +Mult like Ceremonial Dagger or Flash Card) benefit from Chips increasing often much more significantly than Mult.

title: Foil
text: Foil: This is because if a hand is currently at, say, 10 Chips X 100 Mult, +50 Chips would increase the net score by a much higher amount than +50 Mult would. Decks: Plasma Deck balances Chips and Mult, with one Foil card yielding up to 625 Chips (25x25). This is often significantly better than Holographic or even Polychrome, especially in most early to mid-game runs. Ghost Deck makes it much easier to find spectral cards like Aura or Cryptid that are able to either make existing cards Foil or create new Foil cards. Seals: Red Seals are able to be applied to Foil playing cards, causing each one to give +100 Chips.

title: Foil
text: Foil: Seals: Red Seals are able to be applied to Foil playing cards, causing each one to give +100 Chips. Strategies: Due to the fact that +50 Chips is a quite large amount of score, obtaining even just two Foil Jokers can often lead the player into not needing a Joker that provides Chips. This is especially the case if Foil playing cards are utilized, as playing cards can be retriggered and are much more easily able to be duplicated compared to Jokers.

title: Foil
text: Foil: In other media: In the same update where the Ante Chamber DLC was introduced in Vampire Survivors, a game mechanic that mainly gives the player stat bonuses, the Survarot, was introduced. This game mechanic includes card editions, most of which are directly referenced from Balatro, which is the case for Foil.

title: Holographic
text: Holographic: Holographic (Edition). Type: Edition. Effect: +10 Mult. Holographic is an edition card modifier that makes a joker or a playing card give +10 Mult.

title: Holographic
text: Holographic: Holographic adds +$3 to the buy price of jokers and playing cards. Jokers: Holographic Jokers can naturally appear in the Shop with a 1.4% chance. The chance to get a Holographic can be increased with Hone & Glow Up by 2X and 4X respectively. The Wheel of Fortune has a 35% chance to add Holographic to a random Joker if it activates. Holographic Tag applies Holographic to the next base edition joker in the shop and makes it free. Ankh is able to duplicate Holographic Jokers. Invisible Joker can copy a Holographic Joker, and the copy will keep the edition. Playing Cards: Holographic playing cards can be naturally acquired from Standard Packs with a 2.8% chance.

title: Holographic
text: Holographic: Playing Cards: Holographic playing cards can be naturally acquired from Standard Packs with a 2.8% chance. The chance to get a Holographic can be increased with Hone & Glow Up by 2X and 4X respectively. Holographic playing cards are able to be purchased from the Shop if Illusion is owned. Aura has a 35% chance to apply Holographic to a selected playing card in your hand. Death, Cryptid, and DNA can duplicate Holographic playing cards.

title: Holographic
text: Holographic: Death, Cryptid, and DNA can duplicate Holographic playing cards. Jokers: Due to being an edition that is often given to playing cards (through Standard Packs, Aura, etc.), Jokers that can retrigger playing cards that may have Holographic like Hanging Chad, Sock and Buskin, and Hack have the ability to indirectly provide dozens of Mult through retriggers. Nearly all Jokers that give a large number of Chips, like Wee Joker or Runner, benefit from Mult increasing often much more significantly than Chips. Decks: Ghost Deck makes it much easier to find spectral cards like Aura or Cryptid that are able to either make existing cards Holographic or create new Holographic cards.

title: Holographic
text: Holographic: Seals: Red Seals are able to be applied to Holographic playing cards, causing each one to give +20 Mult. Strategies: To maximize Mult, Holographic cards in a hand should be placed to the left of Glass cards and other multiplicative Mult sources (like Bloodstone) so that the XMult is applied after the +10 Mult from the Holographic cards. In other media: In the same update where the Ante Chamber DLC was introduced in Vampire Survivors, a game mechanic that mainly gives the player stat bonuses, the Survarot, was introduced. This game mechanic includes card editions, most of which are directly referenced from Balatro, which is the case for Holographic.

title: Negative
text: Negative: Negative (Edition). Type: Edition. Effect: +1 Joker or Consumable slot. Negative is an edition card modifier that gives +1 Joker slot or Consumable slot, depending on what type of card is Negative. Negative consumables can only be acquired through Perkeo. The Negative edition is the rarest edition in Balatro, having a 0.3% chance to be applied to a Joker in the shop. However, the Negative edition is also the most powerful edition in the game, as the ability to hold an additional Joker has significantly more potential than even Polychrome. The Negative edition inverts the colors of whatever it is applied to, and adds an additional shine on top.

title: Negative
text: Negative: Negative adds +$5 to the buy price of jokers and consumables. Acquisition: There are a few ways of acquiring a Joker with a Negative edition: Jokers in the shop can naturally appear with the Negative edition, with a 0.3% chance of this happening. Ectoplasm applies the Negative edition to a random Joker in the player's Joker slots at the cost of -1 hand size. Negative Tag guarantees that the next Joker (without any other edition) in the shop has the Negative edition.

title: Negative
text: Negative: Negative Tag guarantees that the next Joker (without any other edition) in the shop has the Negative edition. As for Negative consumables, the only way to acquire them is with Perkeo. Perkeo creates Negative copy of a random consumable card, and can do so to any consumable except Black Hole and The Soul, as these 2 consumables cannot be added to your consumable slots. Because Perkeo is a Legendary Joker, however, having Negative consumables is incredibly rare, more so than Negative Jokers. Usage notes: Invisible Joker and Ankh will remove the Negative edition from a Joker it copies, if it has it. This is the only way to remove an edition from a card in Balatro.

title: Negative
text: Negative: If a Negative Joker appears in the Shop, it can be purchased even if there are no extra Joker slots available, unless, in rare cases, the current Jokers exceed the Joker slots (for example, selling Negative Invisible Joker to replicate a Joker or in the Typecast Challenge). Unlike other modifiers, the Negative effect of Joker remains effective even if it gets debuffed; only by selling Negative Joker will the Joker slot decrease. However, if a debuffed Joker (either from Crimson Heart or Perishable sticker) gains Negative enhancement afterwards, the Joker slot will not increase, and selling it will still decrease Joker slot, resulting in permanent Joker slot loss, which is likely a bug.

title: Negative
text: Negative: Strategies: The Negative edition is almost always worth taking, especially if a good Joker appears in the shop with the Negative edition. Even if the Joker is not helpful for your build, it can be worth picking up anyways as it increases the money earned from Temperance and can completely nullify the Verdant Leaf Boss Blind. Trivia: This is the only edition that cannot affect playing cards, since Standard Packs, cards in the shop (with Illusion,) and Aura only offer Foil, Holographic, and Polychrome. The Antimatter voucher always has the Negative filter applied to it when it appears in the shop.

title: Negative
text: Negative: The Antimatter voucher always has the Negative filter applied to it when it appears in the shop. On Balatro's Steam Page an early form of the Negative filter is shown. Though it appears on Mystic Summit, it is most prominent on DNA and Banner. Near the end of the Balatro launch trailer, Mr. Bones appears to have an altered negative.

title: Negative
text: Negative: Near the end of the Balatro launch trailer, Mr. Bones appears to have an altered negative. In other media: In the same update where the Ante Chamber DLC was introduced in Vampire Survivors, a game mechanic that mainly gives the player stat bonuses, the Survarot, was introduced. This game mechanic includes card editions, most of which are directly referenced from Balatro. This is the case for this edition as well, though it is called "Inverted" in Vampire Survivors.

title: Polychrome
text: Polychrome: Polychrome (Edition). Type: Edition. Effect: X1.5 Mult. Polychrome is an edition card modifier that gives X1.5 Mult when on a playing card or Joker. Polychrome playing cards give X1.5 Mult when played or retriggered, and Polychrome Jokers give X1.5 Mult when Jokers are calculated, (after playing cards are scored.)

title: Polychrome
text: Polychrome: Polychrome adds +$5 to the buy price of jokers and playing cards. Acquisition: By default, Jokers in the shop or generated by Judgement have a 0.3% chance to be Polychrome. This becomes 0.9% with Hone and 2.1% with Glow Up. Standard Packs can generate Polychrome playing cards, with a 1.2% chance by default, 2.4% with Hone, and 4.8% with Glow Up. Illusion can generate Polychrome playing cards, but is not affected by Hone or Glow Up. Aura has a 15% chance to add Polychrome to a selected playing card. The Wheel of Fortune has a 15% chance to add Polychrome to a random Joker if it activates.

title: Polychrome
text: Polychrome: The Wheel of Fortune has a 15% chance to add Polychrome to a random Joker if it activates. Hex applies Polychrome to a random Joker and destroys all other non- Eternal Jokers. If only 1 Joker is owned, Hex is guaranteed to apply Polychrome to that specific Joker. The Polychrome Tag applies Polychrome to the next base edition joker in the shop and makes it free. Death, Cryptid, and DNA can duplicate Polychrome playing cards. Ankh and Invisible Joker are able to duplicate Polychrome Jokers.

title: Polychrome
text: Polychrome: Death, Cryptid, and DNA can duplicate Polychrome playing cards. Ankh and Invisible Joker are able to duplicate Polychrome Jokers. Usage notes: If Polychrome is on a card that gives additive Mult, the additive Mult will be added first, then the Polychrome will multiply the result by X1.5 Mult (e.g, Joker would give +4 Mult, then give X1.5 Mult). Seals: Red Seals retrigger playing cards 1 additional time, which gives X2.25 Mult if that card is polychrome. Jokers: Hanging Chad can give X3.375 Mult if your first scored card is Polychrome. While Hanging Chad is best utilized early game when Polychrome cards in your deck are limited, it can still be viable well into endless.

title: Polychrome
text: Polychrome: Sock and Buskin, Dusk, Hack, and Seltzer can retrigger your played Polychrome cards, essentially doubling Polychrome's effect. While all of these are viable, Sock and Buskin and Hack are the best as they can be utilized multiple times per round and are not consumed. Jokers with exponential scaling potential such as Triboulet and The Idol are both ideal Jokers to pair with Polychrome cards, providing a significant amount of extra xMult, especially when retriggered. Photograph is great if you have Polychrome face cards, or have Pareidolia to trigger its effect on a non-face Polychrome card. Invisible Joker can copy a Polychrome Joker, the new Joker will keep the Polychrome edition.

title: Polychrome
text: Polychrome: Invisible Joker can copy a Polychrome Joker, the new Joker will keep the Polychrome edition. Consumables: Ectoplasm allows for an extra Joker to be utilized, and its -1 hand size is not much of a downside if your deck is comprised multiple copies of 1 card. Because Polychrome cards only activate when scored, there is no need to have a large hand size. Ankh can copy a Polychrome Joker. If that Joker is Eternal, then multiple copies of a Polychrome Joker can be made with Ankh.

title: Polychrome
text: Polychrome: Strategies: Polychrome Jokers score at the same time as other Jokers in your Joker slots, including jokers such as Even Steven, who trigger when a card is scored. It's best to move your Polychrome Jokers to the right of any additive Mult Jokers. In other media: In the same update where the Ante Chamber DLC was introduced in Vampire Survivors, a game mechanic that mainly gives the player stat bonuses, the Survarot, was introduced. This game mechanic includes card editions, most of which are directly referenced from Balatro, which is the case for Polychrome. Even Polychrome's effect in Vampire Survivors is similar in vein to Polychrome in Balatro, where both provide multipliers to specific values.

title: Bonus cards
text: Bonus cards: Bonus cards (Enhancement). Type: Enhancement. Effect: +30 extra chips. Bonus cards are playing cards that are Enhanced to give +30 Chips to a played hand when scored.

title: Bonus cards
text: Bonus cards: The Hierophant can make up to 2 cards in your hand Bonus cards. Incantation, Familiar, and Grim can add Bonus Number, Face, and Ace cards, respectively. Standard Packs can contain Bonus cards. Illusion allows for Bonus cards to be purchased in The Shop. Usage notes: Between Jokers that give Mult and Chips, ones that give Chips are far fewer in number, making The Hierophant a good option in a pinch. Retriggering with a Red Seal or the Common Hanging Chad can make it particularly strong in Plasma Deck, but also in all decks' early to mid game. Decks: Chips are at their absolute strongest on Plasma Deck due to the balancing gimmick, making Bonus cards a worthwhile investment.

title: Bonus cards
text: Bonus cards: Poker hands: All poker hands work with Bonus cards, as they provide Chips for the player's base score. However, during the early game, poker hands with low base Chips like High Card and Pair tend to benefit the most from Bonus cards. Conversely, larger hands like Flushes and Straights allow more Bonus cards to be played, increasing the player's score even more.

title: Glass cards
text: Glass cards: Glass cards (Enhancement). Type: Enhancement. Effect: X2 Mult, 1 in 4 chance to destroy card. Glass cards are Enhanced playing cards that give X2 Mult when scored, and have a 1 in 4 chance to be destroyed after all scoring is finished. The XMult from Glass cards is given when playing card effects are calculated, which is the same timing as Jokers like Photograph and Hanging Chad. Because of this, the best way to increase your score with Glass cards is to level up the Poker Hand you are playing the most, and get as many retriggers on your Glass cards as possible (retriggering a Glass card does not reroll the 1 in 4 chance to break.) There are a few different ways to find or create Glass cards, which are:

title: Glass cards
text: Glass cards: Justice is the easiest way to make Glass cards, as it applies the enhancement to a selected card in your hand. Incantation, Familiar, and Grim can add Glass Number, Face, and Ace cards, respectively. Standard Packs can contain Glass cards. Illusion allows for Glass cards to appear in The Shop. Usage notes: Fragile starts with all playing cards in your deck being Glass cards. Having 5 Glass cards in the deck will unlock Glass Joker.

title: Glass cards
text: Glass cards: Having 5 Glass cards in the deck will unlock Glass Joker. Jokers: Glass Joker rewards playing as many Glass cards as possible, as it substitutes the loss of scoring from broken Glass cards for a permanent X0.75 Mult increase each time this happens. If trying to maximize the scaling of Glass Joker, however, it is important to have a reliable way to generate more Glass cards. Glass Joker also scales if a Glass card is destroyed by other means, such as with Trading Card or The Hanged Man. However, due to a bug, when Glass cards are destroyed by Spectral cards like Immolate, Glass Joker will not scale.

title: Glass cards
text: Glass cards: Erosion gains +4 Mult whenever your deck loses a card (as long as its smaller than the starting size). DNA allows for more Glass cards to be made. This is especially important for these cards because of their chance to be destroyed. Hanging Chad will give X8 Mult if your first played card is a Glass card. Hack, Sock and Buskin, Seltzer, and Dusk similarly retrigger all playing cards, each with a different requirement for doing so. If playing 5 Glass cards, this would give X1024 Mult. Canio can be great if your Glass cards are face cards, as it essentially acts as a better Glass Joker.

title: Glass cards
text: Glass cards: Canio can be great if your Glass cards are face cards, as it essentially acts as a better Glass Joker. Card modifiers: Red Seals can retrigger a Glass card 1 time. Playing 5 Red Seal Glass cards would give X1024 Mult. Blue Seals increases the flat Mult on the hand you are playing, which is then multiplied by the Glass card's effect. Polychrome on a Glass card essentially increases its XMult to X3 Mult. Boss Blinds: If a glass card is debuffed by Boss Blinds, it can be played without risk of breaking, but note that it will not grant the X2 Mult.

title: Glass cards
text: Glass cards: Jokers: Oops! All 6s makes Glass cards more likely to break. This is usually a bad combination, unless you have Glass Joker (and Canio and Erosion in specific cases) and are trying to break as many Glass cards as possible. Strategies: It is usually best to move selected Glass cards to the rightmost position prior to playing your hand. Jokers, enhancements, and editions that give + Mult are more effective if played before a Glass card, as adding flat Mult then multiplying it is better than the other way around. However, if using a Hanging Chad, having a Glass card at the leftmost position is usually more effective.

title: Glass cards
text: Glass cards: Trivia: Glass cards are slightly transparent. This effect is not reflected if a Glass card is drawn face down, as it will display the card back texture for the current deck. If a Glass card is destroyed by other means, such as Trading Card, The Hanged Man, or Immolate, the breaking animation and sound effect are still used instead of the common burning ones. There is a small 2-pixel seam on the bottom right corner of the Glass card texture. This is presumably a graphical bug.

title: Gold cards
text: Gold cards: Gold cards (Enhancement). Type: Enhancement. Effect: $3 if this card is held in hand at end of round. Gold cards are Enhanced playing cards that give $3 if held in hand at the end of the round. If utilizing Gold cards, the best way to get the maximum value is to increase hand size. It can also be beneficial to use Jokers that score with cards held in hand, allowing for smaller hands to be played. There are a few ways to get Gold cards, including:

title: Gold cards
text: Gold cards: The Devil can make 1 playing card in your hand a Gold card. Incantation, Familiar, and Grim can add Gold Number, Face, and Ace cards, respectively. Standard Packs can contain Gold cards. Illusion allows for Gold cards to be found in the shop. Midas Mask can add the Gold enhancement to up to 5 cards per hand. Usage notes: If using Mime and a copy Joker (Blueprint and Brainstorm,) it is possible to copy your best scoring Joker when playing a hand, and while the hand is scoring, move your copy Joker to copy Mime and get an extra $3 per Gold card. Playing a 5 card hand that only has Gold cards will unlock Golden Ticket.

title: Gold cards
text: Gold cards: Playing a 5 card hand that only has Gold cards will unlock Golden Ticket. It is not necessary for all cards to score, so playing a High Card with one scoring card four non-scoring cards will still unlock Golden Ticket. However, the cards do need to be Gold before any Joker effects, which means that using Midas Mask to transform the non-gold cards into gold cards will not unlock Golden Ticket. Having a Gold card with a Gold Seal in your deck will unlock Certificate.

title: Gold cards
text: Gold cards: Having a Gold card with a Gold Seal in your deck will unlock Certificate. Poker hands: Smaller hands provide the maximum potential value for Gold cards. High Card is the best hand if you have a lot of Gold cards in your deck, but other small hands like Pair and Three of a Kind can also work. If using Golden Ticket, however, larger hands can actually be better than smaller ones. Decks: Painted Deck allows for more Gold cards to be held in hand at the end of the round, increasing profit. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette both allow for more Gold cards to be held in hand at the end of the round.

title: Gold cards
text: Gold cards: Consumables: Cryptid can create copies 2 copies of a Gold card. Because these cards are added to your hand, these Gold cards can be utilized immediately. Seals: Red Seals retrigger the effect of a Gold card, giving $6 per Gold card instead of $3. Blue Seals activate on the same condition as Gold cards, and can be added to a Gold card to gain a Planet card and $3 at the end of the round. Jokers: Mime retriggers the Gold card's effect. This can be further increased with Blueprint and/or Brainstorm. Golden Ticket awards $4 when a Gold card is scored. This is especially powerful with retriggers.

title: Gold cards
text: Gold cards: Golden Ticket awards $4 when a Gold card is scored. This is especially powerful with retriggers. Midas Mask allows for up to 12 Gold cards to be made without any deck fixing, assuming a standard 52 card deck. Each additional face card added to your deck after can be another Gold card. Juggler and Troubadour both allow for more Gold cards to be held in hand at the end of the round. Turtle Bean similarly increases hand size, albeit not as permanently as the other 2 bonus hand size Jokers.

title: Gold cards
text: Gold cards: Turtle Bean similarly increases hand size, albeit not as permanently as the other 2 bonus hand size Jokers. DNA, if copied with Blueprint or Brainstorm can net 1 Gold card to your hand per time it is copied. This increases the amount of Gold cards in your deck while also providing extra money for that hand, provided hand after using DNA defeats the Blind. Shoot the Moon, Raised Fist, and Baron can provide scoring from cards held in hand, allowing for smaller hands to be played and more Gold cards to be utilized. Economy-based scalers, such as Bull, Bootstraps, and Flash Card, appreciate the extra money brought in by Gold cards.

title: Gold cards
text: Gold cards: Economy-based scalers, such as Bull, Bootstraps, and Flash Card, appreciate the extra money brought in by Gold cards. Blinds: The Serpent gives +2 hand size per discard and hand if only 1 card is played or discarded. Decks: Five-Card Draw does not work well with Gold cards due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers. Poker hands: Generally, large hands like a Straight or Flush Five are not good with Gold cards, as you want to have as many Gold cards in your hand as possible before defeating a Blind. However, if you have a Golden Ticket, large hands can actually be better than small hands.

title: Gold cards
text: Gold cards: Consumables: Ectoplasm reduces hand size by 1, preventing 1 Gold card for being held in hand at the end of the round. This only gets worse the more Ectoplasms are used. However, the +1 Joker slot can outweigh the hand size reduction in some cases. Ouija also permanently reduces hand size by 1, though its upside is significantly less helpful than Ectoplasm's. This Spectral card should be avoided entirely if utilizing Gold cards. Jokers: Merry Andy reduces hand size, and its +3 discards is not very useful unless you only have a few Gold cards in your deck. Stuntman is similar to but more severe than Merry Andy for utilizing Gold cards.

title: Gold cards
text: Gold cards: Stuntman is similar to but more severe than Merry Andy for utilizing Gold cards. Blinds: The Manacle reduces hand size, therefore allowing fewer Gold cards to be utilized. The Hook can discard Gold cards before scoring, allowing less money to be made. The Psychic can be devastating if your score is reliant on held in hand effects.

title: Lucky cards
text: Lucky cards: Lucky cards (Enhancement). Type: Enhancement. Effect: 1 in 5 chance for +20 Mult, 1 in 15 chance to win $20. Lucky cards are Enhanced cards that have a chance to give the following effects when scored:

title: Lucky cards
text: Lucky cards: A 1 in 5 chance to give +20 Mult A 1 in 15 chance to give $20 Both effects are rolled separately, and both can trigger on the same turn. Lucky cards can be a good source of income throughout an entire run, but this is unlikely to happen in the early game. They're far more likely to give +20 Mult, which can be more than enough in the early game. Lucky cards can be acquired in several ways, including: The Magician adds the Lucky enhancement to 2 selected cards. Incantation, Familiar, and Grim can add Lucky Number, Face, and Ace cards, respectively. Standard Packs can contain Lucky cards. Illusion allows Lucky cards to appear in The Shop.

title: Lucky cards
text: Lucky cards: Standard Packs can contain Lucky cards. Illusion allows Lucky cards to appear in The Shop. Usage notes: On average, Lucky cards give +4 Mult and $1 when scored. If Oops! All 6s is owned, scored Lucky cards give +8 Mult and $3 on average. Seals: Gold Seals combined with Lucky cards give $4 on average when scored. Red Seals double the opportunities for the Lucky card to trigger. Jokers: Lucky Cat is the best Joker to utilize when using Lucky cards, as it can scale incredibly fast with the right setup. Because it can be scaled relatively easily and consistently, it is possible to get over X1000 Mult on a single Lucky Cat.

title: Lucky cards
text: Lucky cards: Oops! All 6s makes all probabilities twice as likely, which can be massively beneficial with Lucky cards. While the +20 Mult becomes less important in higher antes, reliably hitting the $20 can make Oops! All 6s your main source of income. In addition, this Joker also makes Lucky Cat scale twice as fast on average, massively increasing score. Hanging Chad retriggers the first played card twice, which can benefit Lucky cards for more chances on hitting either the +20 Mult or $20. Seltzer, Sock and Buskin, Hack, and Dusk can all double the amount of Lucky card triggers when a hand is played, which is the best way to increase the odds of getting +20 Mult or $20.

title: Lucky cards
text: Lucky cards: Trivia: If the Lucky card also has a Gold Seal and hits the chance for money, the pop-up shows the combined amount of $23.

title: Mult cards
text: Mult cards: Mult cards (Enhancement). Type: Enhancement. Effect: +4 Mult. Mult cards are playing cards that are Enhanced to give +4 Mult to a played hand when scored.

title: Mult cards
text: Mult cards: The Empress can give up to 2 cards in your hand the Mult enhancement. Incantation, Familiar, and Grim can add Mult Number, Face, and Ace cards, respectively. Standard Packs can contain Mult cards. Illusion allows for Mult cards to be purchased in The Shop. Usage notes: To maximize Mult, Mult cards in a hand should be placed to the left of Glass cards and other XMult sources (like Bloodstone) so that the XMult is applied after the +4 Mult from the Mult cards.

title: Mult cards
text: Mult cards: Poker hands: All poker hands work with Mult cards as their main purpose is to multiply the score of any hand. However, larger hands like Four of a Kind and Flushes allow more Mult cards to be played, increasing the player's score even more. Jokers: Any Joker that provides XMult based on the suit, rank, or poker hand played synergizes well with Mult cards. These include, but are not limited to: Ancient Joker Bloodstone Triboulet The Idol Consumables: Tarot cards: Death can be used to turn other cards into Mult cards. Justice turns cards into Glass cards which works exceptionally well with Mult cards as long as the Glass card is place to the right after any Mult card.

title: Mult cards
text: Mult cards: The Empress can turn 2 cards into Mult cards. Spectral cards: Deja Vu adds a Red Seal onto Mult cards and retriggers them when played, doubling their Mult. Cryptid can create more copies of Mult cards.

title: Steel cards
text: Steel cards: Steel cards (Enhancement). Type: Enhancement. Effect: X1.5 Mult while this card stays in hand. Steel cards are Enhanced playing cards that give X1.5 Mult to a played hand while held in hand. This enhancement can be obtained or added to cards a few different ways, including:

title: Steel cards
text: Steel cards: The Chariot adds the Steel enhancement to 1 card in your hand. Incantation, Familiar, and Grim can add Steel Number, Face, and Ace cards, respectively. Standard Packs can contain Steel cards. Illusion allows for Steel cards to be purchased in The Shop. Decks: Plasma Deck, while worse for Steel cards than other decks in early antes, will eventually far surpass any other deck in terms of scoring. Because of how score is calculated on the Plasma Deck, your Mult is essentially raised to the 2nd power if its value before balancing is high enough. Painted Deck starts with +2 hand size, making Steel cards more powerful.

title: Steel cards
text: Steel cards: Painted Deck starts with +2 hand size, making Steel cards more powerful. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette both increase hand size, allowing for more Steel cards to be held in hand. Seals: Red Seals retrigger the effect of Steel cards, doubling their effect. Blue Seals similarly activate when held in hand, allowing for Mult and poker hand scaling to be done simultaneously. Poker hands: High Card is the best hand to play when utilizing Steel cards as it allows for the most Steel cards to be held in hand.

title: Steel cards
text: Steel cards: Jokers: Steel Joker directly benefits from Steel cards, increasing by X0.2 Mult per Steel card in your full deck. This can easily be your primary scoring Joker, or be used as a temporary source of scoring while you look for more powerful Jokers. Mime retriggers the effect of Steel cards, essentially doubling the number of Steel cards held in hand. Baron has a similar effect to Mime if your Steel cards are Kings, giving an additional X1.5 Mult per Steel card. Shoot the Moon can benefit from Steel cards if Queens are moved to the left of Steel cards held in hand.

title: Steel cards
text: Steel cards: Raised Fist has a similar interaction with Steel cards, as moving the lowest ranked card in your hand to the left of any Steel cards will increase your score. Juggler allows for 1 additional Steel card to be held in hand. Troubadour allows for 2 additional Steel cards to be held in hand. Turtle Bean allows for a maximum of 5 additional Steel cards to be held in hand, although just temporarily. Tags: Juggle Tag allows for 3 additional Steel cards to be held in hand, although just temporarily. Blinds: The Serpent gives +2 hand size per discard and hand if only 1 card is played or discarded.

title: Steel cards
text: Steel cards: Blinds: The Serpent gives +2 hand size per discard and hand if only 1 card is played or discarded. Decks: Five-Card Draw does not work well with Steel cards due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers. Jokers: Merry Andy gives -1 hand size, which can drastically reduce the scoring potential of Steel cards. Similarly, Stuntman gives -2 hand size, which can drastically reduce the scoring potential of Steel cards even more.

title: Steel cards
text: Steel cards: Similarly, Stuntman gives -2 hand size, which can drastically reduce the scoring potential of Steel cards even more. Consumables: Ectoplasm permanently reduces hand size by 1, and this reduction increases by 1 each time it is taken. The downside of this can be somewhat negated by the +1 Joker slot, but Ectoplasm should still be used with caution if going for a build that utilizes Steel cards. Ouija also permanently reduces hand size by 1, though its upside is significantly less helpful than Ectoplasm's. This Spectral card should be avoided entirely if utilizing Steel cards. Blinds: The Manacle reduces hand size, therefore allowing fewer Steel cards to be utilized. The Hook can discard Steel cards before scoring.

title: Steel cards
text: Steel cards: The Hook can discard Steel cards before scoring. The Psychic can be devastating if your score is reliant on held in hand effects. Strategies: Card order matters! It's always best to put cards that give flat Mult when held in hand before any Steel cards. For example, if you have Shoot the Moon and your hand looks like this: Then the optimal order could look like this: The exact order doesn't matter, only that the Queen is to the left of the Steel card. That way, the +13 Mult from the Queen is multiplied by X1.5 Mult, giving +19.5 Mult.

title: Steel cards
text: Steel cards: To get the most scoring from Steel cards, the best strategy is to play a High Card with a full hand of Steel cards, ideally all with Red Seals. It is also important to increase hand size whenever possible, either with vouchers or Jokers. If going for a deep endless run, Baron, Mime, and Blueprint/ Brainstorm are essential. Steel cards are also an essential element in achieving naneinf, along with the previously mentioned Jokers (see the naneinf guide here).

title: Stone cards
text: Stone cards: Stone cards (Enhancement). Type: Enhancement. Effect: +50 Chips, no rank or suit. Stone cards are Enhanced playing cards that give 50 Chips when scored. Stone cards are not counted as belonging to any suit or rank and cannot be used to form poker hands; however they are always a part of the scoring hand. Stone cards retain their original suit and rank under the enhancement, and it will be returned if their enhancement is changed, for example to a Gold card via The Devil, and it can also be changed (without revealing it) with Strength, The Moon, The World, The Star, The Sun and Sigil.

title: Stone cards
text: Stone cards: Stone cards can be created a few different ways, including: The Tower adds the Stone enhancement to the selected card. Marble Joker adds a Stone card to your deck when a Blind is selected. Standard Packs can contain Stone cards. Illusion allows Stone cards to appear in the shop. Usage notes: If the Stone enhancement is removed by Vampire during a hand, the card will not give +50 Chips or count towards the poker hand condition, but it will still be a part of the scoring hand. Medusa starts with an Eternal Marble Joker and 12 Stone cards in your deck in place of face cards.

title: Stone cards
text: Stone cards: Medusa starts with an Eternal Marble Joker and 12 Stone cards in your deck in place of face cards. When debuffed, Stone cards will still be a part of the scoring hand, which is relevant when using Matador as it will always trigger with a debuffed Stone card. Poker hands: High Card should be leveled up if playing a deck that contains only Stone cards, as playing a hand of 5 Stone cards will be counted as a High Card hand.

title: Stone cards
text: Stone cards: In general, smaller poker hands work better with Stone cards as they allow more to be played in a given hand, and 5-card hands like Straights and Flushes cannot use Stone cards unless the player also has the Four Fingers, in which case 1 Stone card can be used as well. Seals: Gold Seals can be added to give money when a Stone card is played. Red Seals can be added to double the amount of chips given by a Stone card. Decks: Plasma Deck is the best deck to utilize Stone cards with, since they contribute significantly more score thanks to this deck's balancing mechanic.

title: Stone cards
text: Stone cards: Jokers: Half Joker can combine with the 20 Mult with the 50 Chips of Stone cards to give a lot of score value, but will limit the max number of cards that can be played to 3. Stone Joker scales with each Stone card added to your deck, giving a large number of Chips even when playing a hand that does not contain any Stone cards, as long as they exist in your full deck.
