text: Fragile: Any Boss Blind that debuffs cards will allow Glass cards to be played without breaking, giving players a chance to preserve some Glass cards to use at later blinds, be it The Head, The Club, The Plant, Verdant Leaf, etc. This is the only case where Pareidolia can be useful during The Plant, as every card will be debuffed and therefore cannot be destroyed. If a player doesn't mainly rely on Glass cards X2 Mult to beat this blind, it can actually save the run. Crimson Heart can randomly disable one of the two Oops! All 6s, giving Glass cards a 1 in 2 chance to survive.

title: Fragile
text: Fragile: The Pillar will usually have no effect, as all previously played cards will have been destroyed. The Wheel of Fortune has a 4 in 4 chance of applying an Edition to a Joker. This means that there is a 50% chance of applying Foil to a random Joker, a 35% chance of applying Holographic, and a 15% chance of applying Polychrome. Baseball Card will get X2.25 Mult for free. Bloodstone will always trigger, although the number of cards that are usable with it will decline through use. As hands do not really matter in this challenge, Troubadour and Hieroglyph are not so punishing to use.

title: Fragile
text: Fragile: As hands do not really matter in this challenge, Troubadour and Hieroglyph are not so punishing to use. Anti-Synergies: Any scaling Joker that requires playing hands, for example Green Joker and Spare Trousers, will be hard to scale as more Glass cards will break in the process. Similarly, Acrobat, Card Sharp, and Dusk should not be used, as they require playing many hands, when ideally you should be playing as little as possible to conserve your cards. Blue Joker quickly falls off in value in this challenge. Splash can result in cards being broken prematurely. Hologram is far harder to use due to all sources of adding playing cards besides Cryptid and DNA being banned in this challenge.

title: Fragile
text: Fragile: Immolate shouldn't be used more than once, since losing five cards can make it impossible to assemble certain winning hands. Likewise, The Hanged Man and Trading Card shouldn't be used unless to buff Glass Joker, Canio or Erosion. DNA is weaker in this challenge due to the copied card breaking immediately thereafter, unless the player can win with a single High Card. Jokers that rely on specific cards needing to be played, since they will get destroyed afterwards. This includes Fibonacci, Wee Joker, Smiley Face, etc. The ability of The Wheel becomes 4 in 7 cards drawn face down instead of 1 in 7.

title: Fragile
text: Fragile: The ability of The Wheel becomes 4 in 7 cards drawn face down instead of 1 in 7. Justice is nigh-useless, as all playing cards are already Glass. Its only remaining use in this challenge is to scale Fortune Teller. Hiker requires to play cards more than once, which is practically impossible in this challenge. Trivia: To be fragile means to break easily. This challenge mirrors this by making every card get destroyed after it gets played. This is the challenge that bans the most items in the game, with a total of 25 banned items.

title: Ghost Deck
text: Ghost Deck: Ghost Deck (Deck). Effect: Spectral cards may appear in the shop, start with a Hex card. Unlock Requirement: Win a run with the Yellow Deck on any difficulty. The Ghost Deck is an unlockable deck where you start with a Hex spectral card in your consumables, and Spectral cards may appear in The Shop. This deck is unlocked by winning a run with the Yellow Deck on any stake.

title: Ghost Deck
text: Ghost Deck: Starting Contents: It contains the 52 cards of a normal deck: four suits, each with 13 cards (2 to 10, Jack, Queen, King and Ace). You also start with a Hex Spectral card. The Shop: Spectral cards can appear in the Shop when using this deck with a weight of 2, or about 6.67% for each slot in the Shop.

title: Ghost Deck
text: Ghost Deck: There is no way to increase this weight, and buying Vouchers like Tarot Merchant/ Planet Merchant increases the total weight, lowering the chance of Spectral cards. To increase the chance of seeing Spectral cards, get more slots in the Shop using Overstock/ Overstock Plus vouchers, or make rerolls cheaper using Chaos the Clown or Reroll Surplus/ Reroll Glut vouchers for example. All spectral cards have the same chance of appearing in the shop, except for The Soul and Black Hole, as they can only be found in Booster Packs.

title: Ghost Deck
text: Ghost Deck: Synergies: Ghost Deck starts off with Hex card, which applies Polychrome (X1.5 Mult) to a random Joker, at the cost of destroying all others. To avoid accidentally destroying a valuable Joker, especially in the early game, it's best to use the Hex card as soon as a joker you intend to keep is found. The Hex can be sold for $2. This can allow the player to purchase things they would otherwise not be able to.

title: Ghost Deck
text: Ghost Deck: Playing on Black Stake and above allows Joker to have Eternal stickers. Since a Joker with an Eternal sticker can never be destroyed, using Ankh to copy your strongest Joker if it's an Eternal can provide immense value or using Hex to add Polychrome to any Jokers if they are Eternal. In general Ankh and Hex are significantly better on black Stake and above. Poker hands: Spectral cards typically provide "high risk, high reward" effects that can drastically change the player's circumstances. Jokers: Hologram works exceptionally well on Ghost deck since Incantation, Familiar, Grim and Cryptid scale Hologram for +X1, +X0.75, +X0.5, and +X0.5 respectively.

title: Ghost Deck
text: Ghost Deck: Perkeo allows the player to duplicate spectral cards that can easily be found and placed in their consumable slots via the Shop. Trivia: The term "ghost" is defined as the soul or spirit of a dead person or animal, which ties into the supernatural and spooky aspects of Spectral Cards. The Ghost Deck is the second deck to receive merchandise from Tony Kuchar of Fangamer after the Red Deck. Instead of normal cards, the suits are all high contrast, and four new jokers appear as part of the deck, which include Mr. Bones, Séance, Sixth Sense, and Castle.

title: Golden Needle
text: Golden Needle: Golden Needle (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: Discards each cost $1,, 1 hands per round, 6 discards per round, Start with $10. Initial Jokers & Consumables: Credit Card. Deck: Standard 52 card deck. Restrictions: Banned Jokers: Burglar, Banned Vouchers: Grabber, Nacho Tong. Golden Needle is a Challenge Deck. With only one hand per round, the player must play a winning hand every time, and will be penalized financially for discarding too much.

title: Golden Needle
text: Golden Needle: Starting Contents: The starting deck contains the standard 52 cards and a Credit Card. Usage Notes: Getting Troubadour or Hieroglyph during the challenge will not decrease hands count below 1. If the player runs into The Needle after taking either one or both of these cards, the player will get 2 hands instead of 1, and if it is disabled by either Luchador or Chicot, the number of hands will go back to 1. This is presumed to be a bug. Due to how Chicot 'disables' boss blinds, using multiple copies of it will decrease the number of hands to negative amounts, although this will still be counted as having just one hand.

title: Golden Needle
text: Golden Needle: Jokers: Mail-In Rebate and Faceless Joker could help offset the discard penalty. Trading Card may be useful too, but it's limited to the first discard. Faceless Joker works especially well with Pareidolia, allowing the player to obtain a net of $4 for every discard with more than 3 cards. Dusk will trigger on every hand, improving scoring and potentially increasing money through Gold Seal and specific Jokers. Acrobat will provide an additional X3 Mult for every hand. Troubadour cannot reduce hands per round below 1, so it effectively provides +2 hand size without any penalty. Banner supplies up to 180 Chips if no Discards are used.

title: Golden Needle
text: Golden Needle: Banner supplies up to 180 Chips if no Discards are used. Delayed Gratification can be very strong in early games if players can win without using Discards, as it provides a whopping $12 per blind. Any other Joker that benefits from the extra discards, such as Castle, Hit the Road and Burnt Joker are also good. However, the money punishment may make it awkward to use Jokers like these. Mr. Bones can save the player from sticky situations where one hand isn't enough. Luchador and Chicot can be helpful to disable deadly blinds, especially The Water. Blinds: The Needle, The Eye, The Mouth, and The Fish all become trivial due to the 1-hand limit.

title: Golden Needle
text: Golden Needle: Blinds: The Needle, The Eye, The Mouth, and The Fish all become trivial due to the 1-hand limit. The Hook's forced discard does not cost $1 like normal discards. Vouchers: Redeeming Hieroglyph cannot reduce hands per round below 1, making this Voucher free to take. Petroglyph's punishment is also negligible here as even though it takes out a discard, the player would still have 5 discards to work with and they can get that discard back by means like Drunkard, Wasteful, or Recyclomancy vouchers.

title: Golden Needle
text: Golden Needle: However, redeeming Hieroglyph or Petroglyph provides an additional ante to play and thus another Boss Blind to encounter, which has the chance to be a dangerous Boss such as The Water. If the player does not already have a way of rerolling or disabling boss blinds, they should keep this in mind when considering these vouchers. Jokers: Unless the player can win with one hand, Jokers that have effect based on the amount of hands played will be significantly weaker in this challenge, including Green Joker, Ride the Bus, and Supernova. Green Joker is especially bad, as it requires not using discards, which is pretty risky unless the player has Banner or Delayed Gratification.

title: Golden Needle
text: Golden Needle: Card Sharp will never activate under normal circumstances. Loyalty Card becomes extremely hard to activate, as the player might need to defeat 5 blinds to activate it. Jokers with random scoring, like Misprint and Bloodstone (unless with Oops! All 6s) are not advised, because a stable score is crucial for adjusting gameplay during this challenge, and scoring too little at any point will lead to game over. Other chance-based Jokers like Space Joker, Business Card and Reserved Parking (unless with two and one Oops! All 6s, respectively) are also not advised since missing their effect when most needed will lead to game over. Without a strong High Card build, DNA and Sixth Sense are unlikely to be useful purchases.

title: Golden Needle
text: Golden Needle: Without a strong High Card build, DNA and Sixth Sense are unlikely to be useful purchases. Ramen would rarely see it's full value. Mystic Summit costs $6 to activate. Matador becomes very risky to use. Tags: Handy Tag will only give $1 per blind beaten. Blinds: The Water will almost certainly kill any run unless the starting cards contain a winning hand and players aren't relying on Banner for chips. The Wall can be very hard to overcome, especially if encountered early, since players often didn't have time to build up yet and it's hard to win with 1 hand against the 4x score requirement. This also applies with Violet Vessel.

title: Green Deck
text: Green Deck: Green Deck (Deck). Effect: At end of each Round:, $2 per remaining Hand, $1 per remaining Discard, Earn no Interest. Unlock Requirement: Discover at least 75 items from your collection. The Green Deck is an unlockable deck that, at the end of a round, provides $2 per remaining Hand and $1 per remaining Discard, but does not earn interest. This deck is unlocked by discovering 75 items in the collection.

title: Green Deck
text: Green Deck: Starting Contents: It contains the 52 cards of a normal deck: four suits, each with 13 cards (2 to 10, Jack, Queen, King and Ace). Poker hands: High-scoring poker hands, such as Flush, Straight, and Full House help with gaining more money from remaining Hands. Jokers: Some Jokers, such as Merry Andy, Burglar, or Drunkard, can increase the earnings from Green Deck by providing more Discards or Hands. Some Jokers that gain strength from having low money, such as Credit Card and Vagabond, are great combinations with the Green Deck, as you already get $0 in interest regardless. Jokers that depend on avoiding Discards, such as Ramen, Delayed Gratification, or Banner, become even better.

title: Green Deck
text: Green Deck: Jokers that depend on avoiding Discards, such as Ramen, Delayed Gratification, or Banner, become even better. Vouchers: The +Hands vouchers Grabber and Nacho Tong are slightly better than normal. The +Discards vouchers Wasteful and Recyclomancy are also slightly better than normal. Jokers: Avoid To the Moon since the Green Deck does not generate interest. Jokers that depend on using Discards, such as Mystic Summit or Burnt Joker, become worse. Jokers that scale with Hands or Discards used, such as Green Joker, Square Joker, or Castle, are a lot harder to use efficiently with Green Deck, as they also cost you money.

title: Green Deck
text: Green Deck: Jokers that have an effect on the final hand of the round, such as Dusk and Acrobat, become a lot worse, as you lose all the money earned from your Hands. Jokers that actively depend on having large amounts of money to score (Bull and Bootstraps) are harder to use, due to the lack of interest and Green Deck’s incentive to spend money as it is earned. Vouchers: Avoid the interest vouchers Seed Money and Money Tree, as the Green Deck does not generate interest. However, for longer runs, taking these vouchers prevents them from reappearing in later Antes, which makes other vouchers appear more.

title: Green Deck
text: Green Deck: Hieroglyph and Petroglyph can be harder to use, as they give -1 hand and -1 discard, respectively, which means Green Deck will give less money at the end of each blind. Stakes: On Blue Stake difficulty or higher, meaning you will get -1 discard per round, meaning you will get $1 less at the end of each blind. Tips and Tricks: Winning with only 1 Hand becomes very important with this Deck, as this will be your main source of income. Try to avoid using multiple Hands or Discards in a Blind.

title: Green Deck
text: Green Deck: Avoid saving up a lot of money during the first Ante(s). Getting 1 or more strong Jokers at the start is more important and can help you get a lot of money in the subsequent rounds. Also try to get another source of income, like Golden Joker, Gold cards, or Gold Seal. Trivia: The color green is commonly associated with paper money, which is typically used for everyday spending and does not earn interest, unlike money held in a bank account.

title: Inflation
text: Inflation: Inflation (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: Permanently raise prices by $1 on every purchase. Initial Jokers & Consumables: Credit Card. Deck: Standard 52 card deck. Restrictions: Banned Vouchers: Clearance Sale, Liquidation. Inflation is a Challenge Deck. Each time a card is purchased, the prices of all items will be increased by $1. Note that this also includes the base price of held Jokers and Consumables, meaning their sell value will also slowly increase.

title: Inflation
text: Inflation: Usage Notes: Rerolling the shop won't increase prices. Starting Contents: The starting deck contains the standard 52 cards, as well as a Credit Card. Synergies: As each purchase increases the price of future items, it is important to pick up disposable Jokers to clear early Antes, then sell them once better ones are available (preferably scaling Jokers). Egg and Gift Card can inflate selling prices greatly and can recover money after making an expensive purchase. Swashbuckler will provide a high amount of + Mult since it will scale when other Jokers' prices inflate. Riff-Raff is an excellent source of money since the generated common Jokers still inherit the inflated sell prices.

title: Inflation
text: Inflation: Riff-Raff is an excellent source of money since the generated common Jokers still inherit the inflated sell prices. Ceremonial Dagger will scale very fast thanks to Jokers' inflated sell prices. Jokers that create cards such as Cartomancer, Vagabond, 8 Ball, and Certificate (Purple Seals and Blue Seals) can help provide sources of tarots or planets that don't increase shop prices. Uncommon Tag, Rare Tag, Negative Tag, Foil Tag, Holographic Tag, and Polychrome Tag can be valuable to pick up a guaranteed free Joker with editions if players are low on money and desperately need something to fill up their Joker slot.

title: Inflation
text: Inflation: The Coupon Tag is very powerful in the late game, allowing players to have a free shop to pick up and sell stuff for a quick econ recovery. However, prices will not reset back to normal. Anti-Synergies: While not useless during this challenge, do note that free planet cards provided by Astronomer do increase prices in the shop even though they are free (and that they do not have increased sell prices), meaning that it becomes somewhat less helpful. It can be helpful for getting planet cards that aren't absurdly expensive, however.

title: Inflation
text: Inflation: Jokers that require a high amount of purchases to function, like Fortune Teller, Campfire, and Constellation, are considerably harder to make work, although this can be easily mitigated with Jokers like Cartomancer for Fortune Teller, Astronomer for Constellation, or both for Campfire. Bull and Bootstraps can be considerably harder to use in this challenge if the player needs to buy too much. Trivia: The name of this deck references the economic concept of inflation, an increase in the price of goods and services.

title: Jokerless
text:
Jokerless: Jokerless (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: Jokers no longer appear in the shop,, 0 Joker Slots. Initial Jokers & Consumables: None. Deck: Standard 52 card deck. Restrictions: All methods of acquiring Jokers:
 Tarot cards: Judgement 
 Spectral cards: Wraith and The Soul 
 Tags: Uncommon Tag, Rare Tag, Negative Tag, Foil Tag, Holographic Tag, Polychrome Tag, Buffoon Tag, Top-up Tag 
 Blinds: Crimson Heart, Verdant Leaf, Amber Acorn 
 Vouchers: Antimatter 
 Booster Packs: All Buffoon Pack s. Jokerless is a Challenge Deck. The player is unable to acquire Jokers and must rely on Planet cards, card modifications through Tarot cards and Spectral cards, and Vouchers for scoring.

title: Jokerless
text: Jokerless: Starting Contents: The starting deck contains the standard 52 cards. Poker hands: Straight is the most consistent hand to win, as it is both able to be played early game without any deck fixing, and Saturn has great scaling for late game. Consumables: Without Jokers taking up most of the slots in the shop, Tarot cards like Death and The Hanged Man appear far more frequently. This can make deck fixing far easier. Card modifiers: Blue Seals provide the most consistent source of scaling without Jokers. Purple Seals provide a source of Tarot cards without Jokers. Gold cards and Gold Seals provide one of the only ways to gain more money without economy Jokers.

title: Jokerless
text: Jokerless: Gold cards and Gold Seals provide one of the only ways to gain more money without economy Jokers. Steel cards provide a consistent way to score more without Jokers. Polychrome cards similarly provide a consistent way to score more without Jokers. Glass cards provides both a way to deck fix by breaking cards early, a quick way to score more in tough Boss Blinds or when Antes scale too quickly, and an incredibly powerful source of XMult late game. Red Seals synergize with any of: Gold cards, Steel cards, Glass cards, and Polychrome cards. All editions on playing cards, while rare, are far more powerful without scoring Jokers, making Standard Packs and Aura even more valuable.

title: Jokerless
text: Jokerless: Vouchers: Telescope improves the efficiency of shop purchases by ensuring the player will receive a card of their chosen hand type. Observatory provides X1.5 Mult per planet card held in the consumable area, which will greatly increase scoring due to the lack of XMult available. Crystal Ball further synergizes with this by offering an additional consumable slot, allowing the player to hold more planet cards. Due to the ban on 3 of 5 Finisher Blinds, the risk of encountering Violet Vessel is greatly increased (1 in 2) in Jokerless, and its extremely high score requirement may be detrimental. As Jokers are unavailable, Director's Cut (and Retcon) become the only stable way to avoid Boss Blinds.

title: Jokerless
text: Jokerless: Omen Globe can be used to find Spectral cards easier. Anti-Synergies: Several Tarot cards and Spectral cards are still available which have no effect, such as The Wheel of Fortune, Temperance, Ectoplasm, Ankh, and Hex. Blank is still available but does nothing since Antimatter is banned and Jokers can't be purchased anyways. Hone and Glow Up are less useful because Jokers are unobtainable, but the Editioned Playing cards from Standard Packs can still be useful. Since 3 of the 5 finisher Boss Blinds are banned in this challenge, only Violet Vessel and Cerulean Bell can appear, which are both pretty deadly.

title: Jokerless
text: Jokerless: Trivia: After Update 1.0.1f, Jokerless bans Amber Acorn. This is likely because there wouldn't be any Jokers for it to shuffle, meaning its effect would be rendered obsolete, making it just a normal Blind with a 2x base Blind size. In a similar fashion, Crimson Heart is also banned. In Verdant Leaf's case, this is likely banned because its effect requires the player to sell a Joker, which is not possible due to the challenge's constraints. This is the only deck where the first shop will not have a Buffoon Pack as they're banned.

title: Luxury Tax
text: Luxury Tax: Luxury Tax (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: Hold -1 cards in hand for every $5 you have,, 10 hand size. Initial Jokers & Consumables: None. Deck: Standard 52 card deck. Restrictions: None. Luxury Tax is a Challenge Deck. It penalizes owning too much money via reducing the player's hand size. This also means that a player is not allowed to enter a blind with over $50 (assuming they do not have any increased hand size Jokers), as otherwise they would immediately lose the round.

title: Luxury Tax
text: Luxury Tax: Starting Contents: The starting deck contains the standard 52 cards. Synergies: Credit Card can provide up to +4 hand size if players stay $-20 in debt. The Tooth can also make you go into debt. Vagabond will provide a steady supply of Tarot cards for deck enhancing should players opt to stay below $5. Juggler, Troubadour, and Turtle Bean can help offset the hand size penalty given by Luxury Tax. This also applies to Paint Brush and Palette. Golden Joker, Egg, Satellite and Cloud 9 can help as econ Jokers, as they activate after a blind, meaning that the money accumulated by them can be spent in the next shop, with no downside to your hand size.

title: Luxury Tax
text: Luxury Tax: The Devil and Midas Mask can create Gold cards as well, which gives $3 after the round is completed. Having a larger hand size also means you can hold onto more Gold cards. Coupon Tag can be worth the skip, since the next shop will be free. Merry Andy and Stuntman can go either way, since even though their hand size penalties get offset by the extra hand size given, they limit the player to even less money. Jokers that benefit from having a small hand size (such as Blue Joker), and Jokers that benefit from having a big hand size (such as Baron) can also go either way.

title: Luxury Tax
text: Luxury Tax: Anti-Synergies: Be careful when using Lucky cards, as a single $20 produce will reduce hand size by 4, which makes future hands harder to assemble. This also makes it more risky to scale Lucky Cat. Bootstraps and Bull are practically useless, since you're going to want to hold on to very little money. Similarly, To the Moon provides little benefit, as in order to take advantage of its high interest, you'd want high starting money, which this deck punishes. This also includes Seed Money and Money Tree.

title: Luxury Tax
text: Luxury Tax: This also includes Seed Money and Money Tree. Be wary when using econ jokers that provide money in the middle of a blind such as Golden Ticket, Rough Gem, Business Card, etc. as they can reduce your hand size in the middle of said blind. This also applies to Gold Seals, and therefore, it becomes risky to use Talisman. Although not impossible, it is considerably harder to make Jokers that require high monetary cost (such as Flash Card, Constellation and Campfire) function in this challenge.

title: Luxury Tax
text: Luxury Tax: Skipping for Tags that give money can be dangerous. If you have enough money to set your hand size to less than 1 after skipping, upon selecting blind you will be met with the game over screen. Trivia: A tax is a compulsory contribution to state revenue, levied by the government on workers' income and business profits, or added to the cost of some goods, services, and transactions. This is referenced by how the more money you have, the smaller your hand size.

title: Mad World
text: Mad World: Mad World (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: Extra Hands no longer earn money, Earn no Interest at end of round. Initial Jokers & Consumables: Eternal, Negative Pareidolia, Eternal Business Card. Deck: Ranks 2 through 9 only, 32 cards total. Restrictions: Banned Blinds: The Plant. Mad World is a Challenge Deck. It bans most forms of earning money, but supplies an Eternal, Negative Pareidolia and Eternal Business Card to assist with economy.

title: Mad World
text: Mad World: Starting Contents: The starting deck contains 32 cards in total, consisting of ranks 2 through 9 in each suit. Jokers: Because remaining hands no longer earn money, scaling + Chips and + Mult Jokers become considerably stronger here as players can waste all hands to scale them without any penalty. Any Joker that benefits from face cards is useful for this challenge, be it Scary Face, Smiley Face, Photograph, etc. Reserved Parking will provide additional income in addition to Business Card. Oops! All 6s, combined with the Eternal Business Card and Pareidolia, guarantees that every card earns $2 on scoring.

title: Mad World
text: Mad World: Oops! All 6s, combined with the Eternal Business Card and Pareidolia, guarantees that every card earns $2 on scoring. Additionally, with the Reserved Parking synergy stated above, this also guarantees every card held in hand to earn $1 after a hand is played. Splash lets you play five-card hands that don't score very well, if the only thing you are trying to do with the hand is to earn money and not score. Retrigger jokers such as Hanging Chad or Seltzer can help even further when earning money with the Business Card by playing hands. Sock and Buskin in special retriggers face cards, so every card will get retriggered.

title: Mad World
text: Mad World: Sock and Buskin in special retriggers face cards, so every card will get retriggered. Midas Mask works well together with the Pareidolia, being able to give a consistent source of income. This allows Jokers like Golden Ticket, Vampire and Driver's License to be more useful too. Jokers that rely on many number cards such as Fibonacci, Even Steven, and Odd Todd are stronger on this deck, as those three Jokers affect half of the deck rather than only 20/52 cards in a normal deck. Mail-In Rebate picks a random rank in the deck every round, which is considerably easier to find with only 8 ranks in this deck.

title: Mad World
text: Mad World: Just a simple discard joker like Drunkard lets you practically see all of your deck without needing to play throwaway hands. Merry Andy also works, but is usually overkill and comes at the cost of decreased hand size. The Idol has fewer options to choose from, making it more useful without needing to significantly manipulate the deck. Canio gains X1 Mult when any card is destroyed. However, this can be dangerous due to the small deck. Luchador or Chicot can be used to counter The Mark, at least in the absence of Director's Cut. Jokers: Ride the Bus will effectively never gain any mult due to the eternal Pareidolia.

title: Mad World
text: Mad World: Jokers: Ride the Bus will effectively never gain any mult due to the eternal Pareidolia. To the Moon should be avoided as this challenge does not generate interest. Vagabond is hard to use due to Business Card providing lots of money during the blind. Credit Card can loosen the burden of it, however. Due to the small size of the deck, Erosion will have a lower ceiling on its maximum Mult. Similarly, Blue Joker does not work well in this challenge due to the small size of the deck. Scholar and Superposition require Aces, which this deck does not start with. Walkie Talkie requires 10s and 4s, but this deck does not start with any 10s.

title: Mad World
text: Mad World: Walkie Talkie requires 10s and 4s, but this deck does not start with any 10s. Baron, Shoot the Moon, Hit the Road and Triboulet all rely on specific ranks of face cards, but this deck lacks them. Vouchers: Seed Money and Money Tree work towards Interest, which is banned here. Boss Blinds: The Mark is a particularly dangerous boss in this challenge, as it essentially means that all of your cards will be drawn face down. Trivia: The title is likely a reference to the Tears for Fears song Mad World, which begins with the line "All around me are familiar faces", here referring to face cards.

title: Mad World
text: Mad World: This challenge deck in particular has only 32 cards, making it the smallest challenge deck.

title: Magic Deck
text: Magic Deck: Magic Deck (Deck). Effect: Start run with the Crystal Ball voucher and 2 copies of The Fool. Unlock Requirement: Win a run with the Red Deck on any difficulty. The Magic Deck is an unlockable deck that starts the player off with Crystal Ball and 2 copies of The Fool. This deck is unlocked by winning a run with the Red Deck on any any difficulty.

title: Magic Deck
text: Magic Deck: Starting Contents: It contains the 52 cards of a normal deck: four suits, each with 13 cards (2 to 10, Jack, Queen, King and Ace). This deck also starts the player off with Crystal Ball and 2 copies of The Fool. Jokers: Anything that makes Tarot or Spectral cards in general, such as 8 Ball, Cartomancer, Hallucination, Sixth Sense, Superposition, Séance, and Vagabond. Certificate's cards with Purple Seal or Blue Seal get easier to use. Gift Card can add sell value to an additional Consumable per round. Vouchers: Observatory can scale with an additional Planet card, giving a bonus X1.5 Mult if at max capacity.

title: Magic Deck
text: Magic Deck: Vouchers: Observatory can scale with an additional Planet card, giving a bonus X1.5 Mult if at max capacity. Tips and Tricks: Try to use the 2 starting Fools on a good Tarot/Planet card, for example: The Hermit (doubles money, max of $20) Judgement (create a random Joker) The Empress (enhances 2 cards to Mult cards) The World/ The Sun/ The Star/ The Moon (convert 3 cards to specific suit) The Devil (enhances 1 card into a Gold card) Most Planets, as the triple level up can impact score significantly

title: Medusa
text: Medusa: Medusa (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: None. Initial Jokers & Consumables: Eternal Marble Joker. Deck: 52 cards, with all face cards replaced by Stone cards. Restrictions: None. Medusa is a Challenge Deck. The deck begins with twelve Stone cards, and the proportion of Stone cards in the deck will naturally increase while playing because of the Eternal Marble Joker.

title: Medusa
text: Medusa: Starting Contents: The starting deck contains 52 cards, and all face cards are replaced with Stone cards, for a total of 12 starting Stone cards. Synergies: Stone Joker will provide additional Chips, as Stone cards will be added each round and all of the face cards have already been turned into Stone. Burnt Joker can be used to scale High Card or Pair, both poker hands that work well with all of the Stone cards. Hologram gains X0.25 Mult for free each blind. Blue Joker similarly gains +2 Chips for free each blind. Trading Card can help reduce your deck size, as it will be bloated with the added Stone cards.

title: Medusa
text: Medusa: Trading Card can help reduce your deck size, as it will be bloated with the added Stone cards. The Hanged Man and Immolate can also aid with this. As you start with 12 Enhanced cards and get more every round, Jokers like Vampire or Driver's License can quickly improve your score. Ride the Bus becomes trivial to scale due to the lack of face cards. The Plant and The Mark are irrelevant as long as the player doesn't add any face cards or has Pareidolia. Anti-Synergies: Obelisk might be difficult to use once a significant portion of the deck is Stone cards, as they can only be used for High Card hands.

title: Medusa
text: Medusa: Erosion relies on a small deck size, which is more difficult to get when 1 card is added per round from Marble Joker. Any Joker that is triggered from face cards will be useless unless the player has Pareidolia, and those working with particular ranks (such as Shoot the Moon) will never trigger even with it. However, since a joker slot is already occupied by Marble Joker, keeping another effect joker like Pareidolia may be risky, as it will do nothing without Jokers related to face cards (and vice versa), while always fragile to Boss Blinds like The Plant and The Mark. Splash is pretty much useless in this challenge since Stone cards will always score no matter what.

title: Medusa
text: Medusa: Splash is pretty much useless in this challenge since Stone cards will always score no matter what. Trivia: If the Stone Enhancement on the starting Stone cards is removed or replaced, it can be seen that the ranks and suits match the face cards in a normal deck of cards. Medusa is a famous character from Greek mythology, known for turning anyone who looks at her into stone. The face cards being replaced with Stone cards is a reference to this.

title: Monolith
text: Monolith: Monolith (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: None. Initial Jokers & Consumables: Eternal Obelisk, Eternal Negative Marble Joker. Deck: Standard 52 card deck. Restrictions: None. Monolith is a Challenge Deck. Centering around the usage of Obelisk, this deck starts with an Eternal Obelisk, and an Eternal Negative Marble Joker, encouraging players to use the High Card inflation strategy to boost Obelisk in the late game.

title: Monolith
text: Monolith: Starting Contents: The starting deck contains the standard 52 cards. Jokers: Jokers that provide scaling + Mult independent of poker hands like Red Card or Bootstraps are very important with Obelisk, as little Mult will be provided from the hands themselves. Hologram works well alongside Marble Joker, gaining X0.25 Mult every blind. Stone Joker provides additional chip bonus which scales with Marble Joker every blind. Driver's License will become active very quickly with Marble Joker adding an Enhanced card every Blind. Vampire can use Marble Joker as an enhancement generator to scale more easily. With Vampire removing the enhancement from all Stone cards, the player will need to find a replacement source of + Chips like Square Joker or Bull.

title: Monolith
text: Monolith: Poker hands: Higher value poker hands like Straight and Four of a Kind that rely on finding specific cards are much harder to find with many Stone cards in the deck. Jokers: Burglar removes all Discards, and may force the most played hand to be played, resetting Obelisk. All Jokers that rely on playing specific hands, including Superposition, Crazy Joker, and The Order will not be able to be used as much due to Obelisk. Planet cards, and Jokers that upgrade hands like Space Joker and Burnt Joker, are far less effective because the hand can only be used a limited number of times due to Obelisk.

title: Monolith
text: Monolith: Erosion relies on a small deck size, which is more difficult to get when 1 card is added per round from Marble Joker. Trivia: A monolith is a large single upright block of stone, especially one shaped into or serving as a pillar or monument. This is reflected by the starting Obelisk.

title: Nebula Deck
text: Nebula Deck: Nebula Deck (Deck). Effect: Start run with the Telescope voucher, -1 consumable slot. Unlock Requirement: Win a run with the Blue Deck on any difficulty. The Nebula Deck is an unlockable deck that starts the player off with Telescope and -1 consumable slot. This deck is unlocked by winning a run with the Blue Deck on any difficulty.

title: Nebula Deck
text: Nebula Deck: Starting Contents: It contains the 52 cards of a normal deck: four suits, each with 13 cards (2 to 10, Jack, Queen, King and Ace). You also start with the Telescope voucher, but one fewer Consumable slot than usual. Synergies: Nebula Deck is strongest with 5-card hands such as Straights, as the larger hands typically benefit significantly more from planet cards' effects. Jokers: Constellation gains X0.1 Mult each time a Planet card is used, which is already highly encouraged with Telescope. Astronomer makes all Planet cards and Celestial Packs free, allowing for amazing synergy with Telescope as the most played hand can be consistently leveled up for free.

title: Nebula Deck
text: Nebula Deck: Four Fingers and Shortcut allow for 5-card hands such as Straights to be played easier, pairing well with their increased scaling. Vouchers: Crystal Ball will offset the -1 consumable slot penalty. Jokers: Unfortunately, there are far more Jokers which suffer from the -1 Consumable slot, than benefit from the Telescope voucher. For example: Vagabond gets significantly more difficult to use, to the point of being much less valuable when playing this deck.

title: Nebula Deck
text: Nebula Deck: Vagabond gets significantly more difficult to use, to the point of being much less valuable when playing this deck. Anything that makes Tarot cards or Planet cards in general, such as Cartomancer or Superposition, become more difficult to use. Additionally, The Fool, The Emperor, and the The High Priestess become less valuable, making Jokers which give Tarot cards less valuable as a result. Hallucination suffers even more than the others, as there must be an empty consumable slot for Hallucination to function at all. Certificate's cards with Purple Seal or Blue Seal get much more clunky, as you cannot create two consumables at once, while you also need to get rid of any other consumable before obtaining even one.

title: Nebula Deck
text: Nebula Deck: Red Card encourages skipping Celestial Packs, even though they're more valuable than normal. Séance's Spectral cards become much harder to save for a perfect opportunity. This also applies to Sixth Sense. Gift Card can increase the price of one less Consumable per round. Campfire can be harder to hold onto Consumables to sell to increase its effectiveness between antes. Satellite requires unique Planet Cards, which are harder to find with Telescope generating the same Planet Card. Obelisk relies on playing different hands, which does not work well with Telescope's ability to create the planet card for your most played hand.

title: Nebula Deck
text: Nebula Deck: Vouchers: Because of the single consumable slot, Observatory gets significantly worse without Perkeo, even though this deck is the place where this Voucher is seen most often. Trivia: Playing on Yellow Deck and buying Telescope in the first shop is identical to Nebula deck's effect without the downsides that come with the removal of a consumable slot.

title: Non-Perishable
text: Non-Perishable: Non-Perishable (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: All Jokers are Eternal. Initial Jokers & Consumables: None. Deck: Standard 52 card deck. Restrictions: Banned Jokers: Gros Michel, Cavendish Ice Cream; Turtle Bean, Ramen, Diet Cola; Seltzer; Popcorn, Mr. Bones, Invisible Joker and Luchador, Banned Blinds: Verdant Leaf. Non-Perishable is a Challenge Deck. All Jokers found while playing are Eternal.

title: Non-Perishable
text: Non-Perishable: Starting Contents: The starting deck contains the standard 52 cards. Synergies: Since this Challenge prevents the player from selling any kind of Joker once bought, it's important to pick the Jokers that you absolutely want to keep for the rest of the run. Focus on Consumables such as Tarot cards and Planet cards to get through the early Antes until you find a good Joker lineup. Madness works well with this challenge since it cannot destroy any Eternal Jokers but still gains X0.5 Mult. Ankh and Hex can be used to duplicate and add Polychrome freely. However, Ankh becomes useless after all Joker slots are filled.

title: Non-Perishable
text: Non-Perishable: Scaling Jokers like Constellation, Spare Trousers, Square Joker, etc. can be good choices as well since they will become stronger over the course of the run. Getting them as an early commitment may not be as detrimental to your build this way. Anti-Synergies: Ceremonial Dagger doesn't work at all since it can't destroy any Eternal Jokers and doesn't gain + Mult. Riff-Raff normally can't spawn stickered Jokers, but does spawn Eternal Jokers during this challenge, making it an extremely risky pick-up. This also applies to Judgement, Wraith, The Soul and the Top-up Tag. Since Jokers cannot be sold once bought, Egg and Gift Card don't give any value (besides for Swashbuckler and Temperance), making them useless.

title: Non-Perishable
text: Non-Perishable: Unless the player can get an extra Joker slots by either Ectoplasm or Antimatter, Showman is pretty much a waste of a Joker slot. Trivia: Along with Typecast, this is one of the two possible decks where you can have Eternal Legendary Jokers.

title: On a Knife's Edge
text: On a Knife's Edge: On a Knife's Edge (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: None. Initial Jokers & Consumables: Eternal, Pinned Ceremonial Dagger, The Pinned Joker is always in the leftmost position. Deck: Standard 52 card deck. Restrictions: None. On a Knife's Edge is a Challenge Deck. It features an Eternal Ceremonial Dagger with the unique "Pinned" quality, ensuring it cannot be moved from the leftmost position.

title: On a Knife's Edge
text: On a Knife's Edge: Starting Contents: The starting deck contains the standard 52 cards. Synergies: A continuous source of income is important to keep feeding the Dagger, and because it can't be moved, players are forced to always have at least one disposable Joker while using the remaining three Joker slots for scoring Jokers. Egg is incredibly useful to scale Ceremonial Dagger. However, players need to sacrifice yet another Joker slot to scale Egg in the process. Riff-Raff can provide disposable Jokers to feed the dagger. Make sure to keep a disposable Joker in between them so Riff-Raff can be kept after selecting a blind.

title: On a Knife's Edge
text: On a Knife's Edge: Joker Stencil consistently provides at least X2 Mult upon selecting a Blind since Ceremonial Dagger destroys one Joker and thus creates an empty Joker slot. Anti-Synergies: Using Invisible Joker and Ankh carries a high risk as if it duplicates Ceremonial Dagger, the second copy will also be pinned, leaving the first one impossible to scale. While they can still be useful, note that Brainstorm is only able to copy Ceremonial Dagger, and Blueprint cannot copy Ceremonial Dagger (unless indirectly so, by copying Brainstorm), which limits their utility in this challenge.

title: On a Knife's Edge
text: On a Knife's Edge: Be careful when facing Verdant Leaf. If you rely on enhanced cards to score, you'll have to sell another Joker in addition to feeding Ceremonial one, leaving you with only three Jokers to beat this boss blind. Clearance Sale and Liquidation reduce the sell price of Jokers, so the + Mult gained for Ceremonial Dagger will be reduced as well. Other scaling + Mult Jokers such as Ride the Bus or Red Card become obsolete as Ceremonial Dagger grows.

title: On a Knife's Edge
text: On a Knife's Edge: Other scaling + Mult Jokers such as Ride the Bus or Red Card become obsolete as Ceremonial Dagger grows. Trivia: The term "on a knife's edge" is usually used to describe a very tense or dangerous situation. This is referenced by how Jokers at the left of Ceremonial Dagger are "on a knife's edge" and the fact that daggers are a type of knife.

title: Painted Deck
text: Painted Deck: Painted Deck (Deck). Effect: +2 hand size,, -1 Joker slot. Unlock Requirement: Win a run with any deck on the Green Stake difficulty or harder. The Painted Deck is an unlockable deck which provides +2 default Hand Size, but -1 Joker slot. This deck is earned by winning a run on the Green Stake difficulty.

title: Painted Deck
text: Painted Deck: Starting Contents: It contains the 52 cards of a normal deck: four suits, each with 13 cards (2 to 10, Jack, Queen, King and Ace). You have a larger hand size than usual, but one less Joker slot. Poker hands: This deck makes 5-card hands significantly easier to play. In particular: Straight Flush Full House Straight Flush (or Royal Flush) Jokers: Jokers which reduce hand size, such as Stuntman, can have their downsides negated by the deck's +2 hand size bonus. Any joker which cares about having specific cards in your hand are helped by the extra hand size Painted provides, including: Mime Shoot the Moon Baron Reserved Parking Midas Mask Certificate (Which can generate Blue Seals)

title: Painted Deck
text: Painted Deck: Mime Shoot the Moon Baron Reserved Parking Midas Mask Certificate (Which can generate Blue Seals) Spectral cards: Ectoplasm's and Ouija's hand size downside can be offset by the deck's extra hand size. Ectoplasm can be helpful if the player wants more Joker slots. Ouija usually converts 10 cards, instead of 8 cards that Ouija typically does on other decks. Modifiers: The larger hand size allows for more Gold cards, Steel cards, and Blue Seals to be utilized. Vouchers: Antimatter can offset the -1 Joker slot. Jokers: As there are only 4 Joker slots, Joker Stencil can usually only provide a maximum of X4 Mult. Similarly, Abstract Joker and Swashbuckler will be weaker as fewer Jokers can be acquired.

title: Painted Deck
text: Painted Deck: Similarly, Abstract Joker and Swashbuckler will be weaker as fewer Jokers can be acquired. Riff-Raff is more difficult to use with fewer slots free for new Jokers. Gift Card is less powerful with 1 fewer Joker for it to increase the sell value of. Baseball Card is less powerful with 1 fewer possible Uncommon Joker to gain X1.5 Mult. Blackboard can be harder to trigger, as the increased hand size can make it harder to hold only Clubs and Spades in your hand. Raised Fist is slightly weaker as the extra handsize means you are more likely to have a lower ranked card in hand.

title: Painted Deck
text: Painted Deck: Jokers that provide no direct scoring, such as Splash, Shortcut or Luchador, become harder to keep due to the missing Joker Slot. Consumables: Temperance will give less money due to the player only having 4 Jokers slots. Trivia: Using the Painted Deck is an easy method to unlock the Invisible Joker due to the reduced joker slot fitting its unlock requirement, so long as no fifth joker is acquired via being Negative edition or through the Antimatter voucher. Playing on the Painted Deck is essentially equivalent to playing on the Blue Deck while holding a hidden Eternal Troubadour that has no sell value. Painted Deck, Paint Brush, and Palette share the theme of painting and increased hand size.

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Plasma Deck (Deck). Effect: Balance Chips and Mult when calculating score for played hand, X2 base Blind size. Unlock Requirement: Win a run with any deck on the Blue Stake difficulty or harder. The Plasma Deck is an unlockable deck that changes the way score is calculated in exchange for higher base Blind sizes. It is unlocked by winning a run with any deck on Blue Stake or higher.

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Rather than multiplying Chips and Mult for scoring, the game averages out (balances) Chips and Mult before multiplying them, effectively calculating the score as (Chips+Multiplier2)2 rather than the normal Chips×Mult. For example, a Level 1 flush (10,8,7,6,4), would normally be calculated as 70 × 4 = 280 However, with the Plasma deck, the total Chips and total Mult are averaged together (or balanced) before they get multiplied. 70 + 4 = 74 74 / 2 = 37 37 × 37 = 1,369 This is a significantly higher number and is offset by having Blind sizes twice as high when playing this deck. In fact, the hand score will almost always be higher after balancing (see #Mathematical Proofs).

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Note that at higher Antes, the /2 becomes irrelevant, effectively making plasma deck a straight ^2 to your score. Starting Contents: It contains the 52 cards of a normal deck: four suits, each with 13 cards (2 to 10, Jack, Queen, King and Ace).

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Synergies: You want to aim for the highest raw number boosts to Chips and Mult. Since Chips start off at a higher number, most Jokers and Consumables boost Chips with a larger raw number than Mult (e.g Bonus card's +30 Chips vs Mult card's +4 Mult). This is roughly balanced on other decks, but on the Plasma Deck, Chips and Mult equally contribute to the hand score, so using cards with large +Chips will result in a much higher score. 2,4,6,8,10 with Even Steven = 10 Chips and 10 Mult A,3,5,7,9 with Odd Todd = 77.5 Chips and 77.5 Mult

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: 2,4,6,8,10 with Even Steven = 10 Chips and 10 Mult A,3,5,7,9 with Odd Todd = 77.5 Chips and 77.5 Mult In a normal deck, focusing on only XMult leads to a non-optimal distribution, but this is solved by the Plasma Deck's balancing mechanism and can result in much higher final scores, even with identical builds and the same hand. Normal Deck Scoring: 100 × 10,000 = 1,000,000 Plasma Deck Scoring: 5,050 × 5,050 = 25,502,500 Chip boosters: any Jokers that add large +Chips Bonus card enhancement (+30 Chips) Foil edition (+50 Chips) Red Seal will trigger the card twice, so you get twice the Chips

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Foil edition (+50 Chips) Red Seal will trigger the card twice, so you get twice the Chips higher rank cards (Ace card's +11 Chips vs Two card's +2 Chips); this especially matters in the early game However in later Antes, Chips only carry so far since they can only be additive in the base game (i.e. there are no XChips effects in the base game). On the other hand, Mult can be multiplicative. While XMult is slow early on, with a high enough base Mult, this boost can be much greater than +Chips in the late game. In this example, one would need +4000 Chips to match the power of adding a Polychrome:

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: X1.5 Mult Polychrome × 8 Mult = 12 Mult— the Polychrome effectively gives +4 Mult which balances to +2 Chips and +2 Mult X1.5 Mult Polychrome × 8000 Mult = 12000 Mult—the Polychrome effectively gives +4000 Mult which balances to +2000 Chips and +2000 Mult This makes the Plasma Deck one of the best decks for Endless mode, since even though the score requirement per Ante is doubled, by focusing on the XMult, the score one achieves is almost squared from the score achieved in any other deck. An Endless run example: 4 Polychrome Red Seal Glass 2s, Level 20 Four of a Kind, The Idol/ Blueprint/ Hack/ Brainstorm/ Perkeo, and Observatory with 115 Negative Mars cards Chips:

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Chips: Each card gives 2 Chips × 4 triggers (one from card, one from Red Seal, one from Blueprint Hack, one from Hack) = 8 Chips The resulting Chips is 630 (base) + (8 Chips × 4 cards) = 630 + 32 = 662 Chips Mult: Each card gives an XMult of (2 Glass × 1.5 Polychrome × 2 Idol × 2 Brainstorm Idol)^4 retriggers = 12^4 = X20,736 Mult The resulting Mult is 64 (base) × (20,736^4 cards) × (1.5^115 Mars cards) = 64 × 184,884,258,895,036,416 × 178,030,655,708,718,648,266 = 2.106e39 Mult On a regular deck, the resulting score is 662 Chips × 2.106e39 Mult = 1.394e42, which is enough to beat Ante 19 with any Stake difficulty.

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: But on the Plasma Deck, the resulting score is ((662 Chips + 2.106e39 Mult) / 2)2 = (1.053e39)2 = 1.109e78, which is enough to beat Ante 24 with any Stake difficulty. This means, on the Plasma Deck, this build with the current setup has a headstart of 5 Antes. Poker hands: Playing many scoring cards is very efficient in this deck, for example Two Pair: A,A,10,10 = 62 Chips and 2 Mult, which becomes 32 Chips and 32 Mult = 1,024 Jokers: Stuntman is very useful with the Plasma Deck, because it produces an incredible amount of Chips and doesn't need time to scale.

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Wee Joker can also be incredibly useful with the Plasma Deck, however it requires a lot more time and focusing to reach an optimal level.

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Any Endless build can benefit from the Plasma Deck; Perkeo can be used for copying Planet cards for the Observatory voucher, where the amount of Planets needed is less than usual due to each Planet boosting the score by almost the square of the amount as on any other deck. Sixth Sense and Séance can generate a Cryptid in the consumable area, which can also be copied by Perkeo (for Baron/ Mime builds) — the amount of Cryptids needed is also less than usual, since each Cryptid boosts the score by almost the square of the amount as on any other deck.

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Proof that balancing (almost) always increases a hand's score: This is a case of the AM–GM inequality. Let Chips be C and Mult be M. The balanced hand score is given by (C+M2)2, and the normal hand score is given as CM. Expanding the balanced hand score, we get Balanced Hand Score=(C+M2)2,=C2+M2+2CM4,=C2+M2−2CM+4CM4,=C2+M2−2CM4+4CM4,=C2+M2−2CM4+CM. We notice that C2+M2−2CM=(C−M)2, which is always greater than or equal to zero. Since CM is the normal hand score, we have Balanced Hand Score=(C−M)24+Normal Hand Score. Therefore, the balanced hand score will always be greater than or equal to the normal hand score. They will only be equal if C=M, indicating the normal hand score was already balanced. This inequality is expressed as (C+M2)2≥CM

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: (C+M2)2≥CM which is a form of the AM-GM inequality. ◼ However, this assumes no rounding. In reality, balancing rounds half-down, which can in some cases actually reduce the final score. For example, if Chips and Mult differ by exactly 1: Before balancing, score=CM=n(n+1)=n2+n. After balancing, score=floor⁡(2n+12)2=n2, which is less than n2+n.

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Before balancing, score=CM=n(n+1)=n2+n. After balancing, score=floor⁡(2n+12)2=n2, which is less than n2+n. Plasma Deck requires a 5.8x ratio between Chips and Mult to be as effective as other decks: Due to Plasma Deck's doubled Blind size, some hands are less effective at beating a large Blind when played on Plasma Deck. A hand's effectiveness can be measured as its score divided by the Blind size—like the Blind has an HP bar and a hand reduces it by a percentage. At worst, a hand can be twice as ineffective on Plasma Deck if its Chips and Mult are exactly equal, as balancing doesn't increase the score, yet the Blind size is doubled.

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Plasma Deck thus encourages the player to build towards heavily scaling either Chips or Mult—typically Chips in the early game as it's easier to get a decent number of Chips quickly, then pivoting to Mult later as it scales faster in the long run with XMult effects. Otherwise, if the player had built towards having relatively balanced Chips and Mult, balancing again would not provide enough of a buff to overcome the doubled Blind size debuff, and the hand ends up being less effective, especially at larger blinds. Specifically, a hand's Mult has to be around 5.8x its Chips, or its Chips around 5.8x its Mult, for the hand to be as effective on Plasma Deck as on a normal-scoring deck. What follows is a proof:

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: Let Chips be C and Mult be M. The normal hand score is given as CM, while the balanced hand score is given as (C+M2)2. The effectiveness of a given hand is measured as its score divided by the Blind size S. On a normal-scoring deck, this is measured as CMS; on Plasma Deck, it is measured as (C+M)28S where the doubled Blind size 2S is accounted for. To find the Chips–Mult ratio CM where a hand becomes equally effective on both decks, set the two measures equal: CMS=(C+M)28S,8CM=(C+M)2,8CM=C2+M2+2CM,0=C2+M2−6CM. Solve for C using the quadratic formula, treating M as a constant: C=6M±(−6M)2−4M22,=6M±36M2−4M22,=6M±32M22,=6M±42M2,=3M±22M. The two solutions are approximately C≈5.828M and C≈0.172M.

title: Plasma Deck
text: Plasma Deck: C=6M±(−6M)2−4M22,=6M±36M2−4M22,=6M±32M22,=6M±42M2,=3M±22M. The two solutions are approximately C≈5.828M and C≈0.172M. These solutions are reciprocals of each other, which means either CM≈5.828, or MC≈5.828. ◼

title: Red Deck
text: Red Deck: Red Deck (Deck). Effect: +1 discard every round. Unlock Requirement: Unlocked from start. The Red Deck is a deck which provides +1 discard every round. This deck is unlocked by default.

title: Red Deck
text: Red Deck: Starting Contents: It contains the 52 cards of a normal deck: four suits, each with 13 cards (2 to 10, Jack, Queen, King and Ace). Synergies: Being one of the more generic decks, Red Deck pairs nicely with anything, and as such lets the player utilize lots of different strategies centralizing around what the run gives them without much issue. An extra discard means the player can cycle through at most 5 other cards, which helps significantly for playing bigger poker hands while also helping find specific cards, acting as an extra layer of filtering.

title: Red Deck
text: Red Deck: Jokers: Thanks to the prominent feature that Red Deck possesses, Jokers that function off of discards should be of priority when using it. An example would be Banner, which gains +30 Chips per remaining discard. Discard-dependent Jokers such as Mail-in Rebate, Faceless Joker, Castle, Burnt Joker or Yorick are also preferred when using Red Deck. Even though not being directly harmful, the likes of Delayed Gratification, Green Joker or Ramen gives less value when using discards, which hurts Red Deck's potential when paired with them.

title: Red Deck
text: Red Deck: Although notably, Delayed Gratification enjoys a boost to its effect, giving the player an extra $2 in most cases. The risk of using a deck with basically no effect oftentimes outweigh the benefit that this interaction gives, but nonetheless, it can be considered a synergy. Vouchers: Paint Brush and Palette make it easier to search for specific cards or hands in your deck when combined with the extra discard. Blinds: The Serpent benefits from the extra discard because it allows the player to draw an extra 3 cards, making the blind more manageable.

title: Red Deck
text: Red Deck: The Hook benefits from the extra discard because it allows the player to see more cards before the cards are forcefully discarded, making it significantly easier to assemble a 5 cards hand. Modifiers: Purple Seal: The extra discard provides more opportunities to generate more Tarot cards. Tags: Garbage Tag gives more money. Vouchers: Petroglyph: Red Deck can help offset the -1 discard from Petroglyph. Stakes: Red Deck can help offset the -1 discard penalty from playing Blue Stake and above. Jokers: Burglar nullifies red deck's +1 discard. Blinds: The Water also nullifies red deck's +1 discard.

title: Red Deck
text: Red Deck: Jokers: Burglar nullifies red deck's +1 discard. Blinds: The Water also nullifies red deck's +1 discard. Trivia: Red and Blue backed playing card decks are some of the most common colors used in real-world playing card decks, such as Bicycle decks. The Red Deck is the first deck to be featured in a set of real world Balatro Playing Cards by Tony Kuchar of Fangamer. The playing card deck also has four jokers which include Joker, Blueprint, Juggler, and Gros Michel. In other media: This deck is depicted in the cover art of the Ante Chamber DLC of the bullet heaven game Vampire Survivors. Jimbo is seen holding 17 cards from that deck, all of them being face-down.

title: Rich get Richer
text: Rich get Richer: Rich get Richer (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: Chips cannot exceed the current $,, Start with $100. Initial Jokers & Consumables: Seed Money, Money Tree. Deck: Standard 52 card deck. Restrictions: None. Rich get Richer is a Challenge Deck. It prevents Chips from exceeding the current amount of money the player is holding before multiplying Chips and Mult.

title: Rich get Richer
text: Rich get Richer: Starting Contents: The starting deck contains the standard 52 cards. Synergies: Economy Jokers such as Rocket, Mail-In Rebate and especially To the Moon help generate money and increase the cap on Chips. Bootstraps is a great addition during this challenge, since you want to have as much money as possible. While Bull is weaker than usual, due to the challenge preventing chips from exceeding dollars, it does still max out your chip value in this challenge. Using Jokers that rely on + Mult can be a good strategy since Mult is unaffected by the Chips restriction. For example, Green Joker, Spare Trousers, Fortune Teller, etc. Similarly, Jokers that give XMult are unrestricted by the Chip restriction.

title: Rich get Richer
text: Rich get Richer: For example, Green Joker, Spare Trousers, Fortune Teller, etc. Similarly, Jokers that give XMult are unrestricted by the Chip restriction. Lucky Cat can synergize well with this deck since you can potentially gain $20 from Lucky cards, on top of the X0.25 Mult that Lucky Cat gains. Temperance, The Hermit and Immolate will also gain money. Anti-Synergies: Jokers that add a lot of Chips, such as Stuntman and Arrowhead, generally do not get to see their full effect due to the cap on Chips. Wraith should be avoided as it sets money to $0. Credit Card is pretty much useless seeing as going into debt is essentially an immediate loss.

title: Rich get Richer
text: Rich get Richer: Credit Card is pretty much useless seeing as going into debt is essentially an immediate loss. Vagabond would not be useful since you need to have $4 or less during the round to produce tarot cards, limiting the player to 4 Chips. Avoid playing your most played hand against The Ox as it'll set money to $0. The Tooth deducts $1 for each played card, reducing your Chip maximum and potentially losing the game. Trivia: This challenge is the only way in the game that allows the player to score a 0-point hand, which happens when the player lets their money drop to $0 or less.

title: Rich get Richer
text: Rich get Richer: "The rich get richer" (which is often followed up by "and the poor get poorer") is an expression used to describe the widening wealth gap between wealthy individuals and the impoverished. The expression is also used to describe situations where people who have a lot will only ever receive more of it, and those who have little will have even that taken away from them. This ties into the overall challenge; builds with a lot of money will progress through the run faster and faster while builds that lack money will have a tougher and tougher time meeting the score requirements until it becomes impossible to win.

title: The Omelette
text: The Omelette: The Omelette (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: All Blinds give no reward money, Extra Hands no longer earn money, Earn no Interest at end of round. Initial Jokers & Consumables: 5x Egg. Deck: Standard 52 card deck. Restrictions: Banned Vouchers:, Seed Money, Money Tree,, Banned Jokers:, To the Moon, Rocket, Golden Joker, Satellite. The Omelette is a Challenge Deck. It bans any kind of way to earn money at end of round.

title: The Omelette
text: The Omelette: Starting Contents: It contains the standard 52 card deck and 5 Eggs. Synergies: Certain Economy Jokers like Cloud 9, Delayed Gratification or Rough Gem are still allowed, so working your build around them can be a good way to ensure a consistent econ after each round. Scaling + Chips and + Mult Jokers are very strong in this challenge since players can expend all of their hands to scale without penalties. For example, Ride the Bus, Square Joker, Green Joker, etc.. Swashbuckler is powerful in this challenge due to multiple Egg you start with. With 4 Eggs, this Joker will gain +12 Mult on every end of round.

title: The Omelette
text: The Omelette: Tarot card generating Jokers like Cartomancer or Vagabond allowing players to get Tarot cards like The Hermit or Temperance to boost their income without having to sell one of their Eggs. Sixth Sense and Séance can be used to create Immolate. Gift Card, when picked up while players still have 1-2 Eggs left, will boost their sell value significantly. Gold cards and Gold Seal are a good way to earn money after each blind, so look out for The Devil and Talisman. Similarly, Midas Mask can be a consistent way to get Gold cards. Anti-Synergies: Bull and Bootstraps are quite hard to use, due to the majority of ways to earn money being banned.

title: The Omelette
text: The Omelette: Anti-Synergies: Bull and Bootstraps are quite hard to use, due to the majority of ways to earn money being banned. Similarly, Jokers like Constellation, Fortune Teller and especially Campfire require lots of purchases, making them harder to use in this challenge. Wraith may not be worth the risk of getting into $0. Trivia: Omelettes are a common breakfast food that is cooked with eggs being a major ingredient, if not the main one. This ties into the five Egg Jokers in your slots being the only way to earn any money.

title: Typecast
text: Typecast: Typecast (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: When ante 4 boss is defeated:, - all Jokers become eternal, - set Joker slots to 0. Initial Jokers & Consumables: None. Deck: Standard 52 card deck. Restrictions: Banned Blinds: Verdant Leaf. Typecast is a Challenge Deck. After Ante 4's boss is defeated, all Jokers in the player's hand will become Eternal, and Joker slots will be reduced to 0, preventing additional Jokers from being purchased, even if Negative.

title: Typecast
text: Typecast: Jokers that self-destruct like Gros Michel or activate on sell like Luchador (which cannot have Eternal stickers) will not be made Eternal after Ante 4. Note that destroying or selling these Jokers will not free up a slot for another Joker, since the slots are set to 0. For a list of jokers that cannot become Eternal see Eternal#Incompatible_Jokers. Starting Contents: The starting deck contains the standard 52 cards. Synergies: Scaling Jokers are very useful additions to your lineup, giving you another avenue to gain strength past Ante 4 outside of card enhancements and planet cards. These are Jokers like Square Joker, Spare Trousers, Red Card, Constellation, etc.

title: Typecast
text: Typecast: Buffoon Packs will continue to spawn after Ante 4 despite it being impossible to take Jokers from them. This makes Red Card especially desirable, as it can extract value from what would otherwise be a wasted booster slot. Madness in particular is very strong in this challenge due to the forced Eternal. After your Jokers become Eternal, Hex has no downsides to its use. Anti-Synergies: Joker Stencil will no longer function after Ante 4 due to the reduced Joker slots. Invisible Joker can be sold after Ante 4, but it will display "No room!" and cannot replicate any Joker.

title: Typecast
text: Typecast: Invisible Joker can be sold after Ante 4, but it will display "No room!" and cannot replicate any Joker. Gros Michel and Cavendish can both still go extinct after Ante 4, which can lose the run if they were a significant part of scoring. Ceremonial Dagger can no longer scale after Ante 4. It's worse when found too late or when skipping a lot of blinds. Ectoplasm will become useless after Ante 4, as it can only reduce hand size with no upside. Ankh does not work if all Joker slots are full of Eternal jokers, making it useless after Ante 4. Blank may not be worth buying, since Antimatter's extra Joker slot will become irrelevant after Ante 4.

title: Typecast
text: Typecast: Blank may not be worth buying, since Antimatter's extra Joker slot will become irrelevant after Ante 4. Trivia: Along with Non-Perishable, this is one of the two possible decks where you can have Eternal Legendary Jokers. "Typecast" (or "typecasting") usually refers to the act of giving a performer the same roles repeatedly due to the factors out of their control such as their height, ethnicity, or gender. This fits in with the theme of this challenge deck, as after Ante 4, all the Jokers the player currently has will become Eternal, defining their build for the rest of the run.

title: X-ray Vision
text: X-ray Vision: X-ray Vision (Deck). Rules & Modifiers: 1 in 4 cards are drawn face down. Initial Jokers & Consumables: None. Deck: Standard 52 card deck. Restrictions: None. X-ray Vision is a Challenge Deck. During this challenge, there is a 1 in 4, or a 25% chance for cards to be drawn face down.

title: X-ray Vision
text: X-ray Vision: Usage Notes: Using Oops! All 6s will not affect the probabilities of drawing cards face down. Starting Contents: The starting deck contains the standard 52 cards. Synergies: Due to the difficulty of ensuring the player has a certain hand, a High Card or Pair build can be a more reliable way to beat the challenge. As such, Jokers that synergize with easier/smaller hands may be successful, such as: Jokers that rely on playing many hands reliably, such as Green Joker Jokers that rely on in-hand effects, such as Shoot the Moon and Raised Fist Jokers that require the player to discard certain cards, such as Castle and Burnt Joker

title: X-ray Vision
text: X-ray Vision: Jokers that require the player to discard certain cards, such as Castle and Burnt Joker However, if the player still wishes to play bigger hands, Jokers that help the player plays them reliably become much more important. This includes: Jokers that make specific hands easier to play, like Four Fingers, Shortcut, and Smeared Joker Jokers that enable the player to see more of your deck, like Drunkard and Juggler Since Oops! All 6s has no effect on how many cards are drawn face down, it can be safely used alongside chance-based Jokers like Space Joker. Anti-Synergies: Jokers that can reset, like Ride the Bus or Obelisk, can be accidentally reset due to the cards drawn face down.

title: X-ray Vision
text: X-ray Vision: Bosses that already draw cards face down like The Fish or The House can be more deadly than usual. Strategies: The Sort feature at the bottom of the screen can narrow down what the face down cards are. Sorting by rank sorts in descending order, with Aces being the highest rank and 2s being the lowest. Sorting by suit sorts in the order of Spades, Hearts, Clubs, then Diamonds, with each suit being sorted by rank. The player can briefly see face-down cards when using certain Tarot or Spectral cards, e.g., The Empress or Ouija.

title: X-ray Vision
text: X-ray Vision: The player can briefly see face-down cards when using certain Tarot or Spectral cards, e.g., The Empress or Ouija. Trivia: X-ray is an electromagnetic wave of high energy and very short wavelength, which is able to pass through many materials opaque to light. This challenge reflects this by making each card have a 1 in 4 chance of being drawn face down, because the player would need X-ray to see a card that has been drawn face down.

title: Yellow Deck
text: Yellow Deck: Yellow Deck (Deck). Effect: Start with extra $10. Unlock Requirement: Discover at least 50 items from your collection. The Yellow Deck is an unlockable deck that starts the player off with $14, an extra $10 compared to usual. This deck is unlocked by discovering 50 items in the collection.

title: Yellow Deck
text: Yellow Deck: Starting Contents: It contains the 52 cards of a normal deck: four suits, each with 13 cards (2 to 10, Jack, Queen, King and Ace). Jokers: Jokers that rely on Money like Bootstraps, Flash Card and To the Moon can be more powerful on Yellow Deck, especially in earlier Antes, due to the extra starting money. Tags: Skipping for an Economy Tag in ante 1 should usually allow the player to reach the initial Interest cap. Vouchers: Seed Money can be bought earlier in a run, and be used to its full potential earlier.

title: Yellow Deck
text: Yellow Deck: Vouchers: Seed Money can be bought earlier in a run, and be used to its full potential earlier. Strategies: Due to starting with more money than all other decks, the player has more accessible options in early shops, as well as continuing to build towards the Interest cap. For example the player can buy Overstock in Ante 1, and still find scoring options, like opening Buffoon Packs or using Planet cards, whilst still saving some money, which is harder to do on other decks. This headstart on Interest and Money can allow the player to scale something like Red Card faster and earlier in the run, all while staying near or above the Interest cap.

title: Yellow Deck
text: Yellow Deck: Trivia: The color yellow is associated with Money in Balatro.

title: Zodiac Deck
text: Zodiac Deck: Zodiac Deck (Deck). Effect: Start run with Tarot Merchant, Planet Merchant, and Overstock. Unlock Requirement: Win a run with any deck on the Red Stake difficulty or harder. The Zodiac Deck is an unlockable deck that starts the player off with Tarot Merchant, Planet Merchant and Overstock. It is unlocked by winning a run on the Red Stake difficulty. This Deck shares an unlock requirement with the Low Stakes achievement.

title: Zodiac Deck
text: Zodiac Deck: Starting Contents: It contains the 52 cards of a normal deck: four suits, each with 13 cards (2 to 10, Jack, Queen, King and Ace). The Tarot Merchant, Planet Merchant and Overstock vouchers are automatically equipped at the start of a run on this deck. Since players start with Overstock and immediately have a third card slot in the Shop, Zodiac Deck has a slightly higher chance to generate Jokers with reroll; Zodiac Deck generates about 1.53 jokers per shop roll while every other deck without any vouchers generates about 1.43 jokers per reroll. Jokers: Egg and Gift Card, which both increase the sell price of Jokers, become much stronger due to the ease of finding Temperance in the shop.

title: Zodiac Deck
text: Zodiac Deck: Jokers that are centered around Tarot cards or card enhancements, such as Fortune Teller, Driver's License and Vampire become easier to scale and utilize due to the abundance of Tarot cards. Constellation, Satellite, and Astronomer are much more viable since Planet cards are easier to come across. Campfire becomes faster to scale due to the increase in cards available in the Shop. Vouchers: Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut are more powerful due to Zodiac Deck starting with 3 card slots instead of the typical 2, making it easier for players to find their desired cards.

title: Zodiac Deck
text: Zodiac Deck: Trivia: The word "Zodiac" comes from the Greek word ζῳδιακός (zōidiakos), which means "circle of little animals", and is used in both astronomy and astrology, referring to a belt in the sky along which the paths of the sun, the moon, and the planets move. Astronomy is the study of planets, while astrology is linked to fortune telling, similar to tarot cards, explaining why both consumables are more likely to be found on this deck. The circles on the back of Zodiac Deck are not regular circles, and are one pixel wider on width than height.

title: Black Stake
text: Black Stake: Black Stake (Stake). Description: Shop can have Eternal Jokers, (Can't be sold or destroyed). Unlocked Deck on win: Anaglyph Deck. Previous: Green Stake. Next: Blue Stake. The Black Stake is the fourth Stake, being unlocked after winning Green Stake on a specific Deck. This Stake makes the Shop have a 30% chance on selling Jokers with the Eternal sticker on them. It also applies the effects of all preceding Stakes.

title: Black Stake
text: Black Stake: Winning a run on this Stake with a specific Deck will result in unlocking the succeeding Stake on that Deck, the Blue Stake. Winning a run with this Stake for the first time will complete the achievement Mid Stakes and unlock the Anaglyph Deck.

title: Blue Stake
text: Blue Stake: Blue Stake (Stake). Description: -1 Discard. Unlocked Deck on win: Plasma Deck. Previous: Black Stake. Next: Purple Stake. The Blue Stake is the fifth Stake, being unlocked after winning Black Stake on a specific Deck. This Stake decreases the number of Discards per round by 1. It also applies the effects of all preceding Stakes.

title: Blue Stake
text: Blue Stake: Winning a run on this Stake with a specific Deck will result in unlocking the succeeding Stake on that Deck, the Purple Stake. Winning a run with this Stake for the first time will make the player unlock the Plasma Deck. Trivia: In an interview with Bloomberg, LocalThunk has confirmed that he plans to change the blue stake in the 1.1 Update.

title: Gold Stake
text: Gold Stake: Gold Stake (Stake). Description: Shop can have Rental Jokers, (Costs $3 per round). Previous: Orange Stake. The Gold Stake is the eighth and the final Stake, being unlocked after winning Orange Stake on a specific Deck. This Stake makes the Shop have a 30% chance on selling Jokers with the Rental sticker on them. It also applies the effects of all preceding Stakes.

title: Gold Stake
text: Gold Stake: Several Achievements are unlocked through winning Gold Stake runs: Winning a run on this stake once grants the High Stakes achievement Winning a run with every deck at this stake grants the Completionist+ achievement Winning a run with every joker at this stake grants the Completionist++ achievement Trivia: It is one of the three stakes that do not unlock a Deck upon winning, with the other two being the White Stake and the Purple Stake.

title: Green Stake
text: Green Stake: Green Stake (Stake). Description: Required score scales faster for each Ante. Unlocked Deck on win: Painted Deck. Previous: Red Stake. Next: Black Stake. The Green Stake is the third Stake, being unlocked after winning Red Stake on a specific Deck. This Stake scales up the score requirements for defeating Blinds for each Ante and carries the effects of the preceding stake, Red Stake.

title: Green Stake
text: Green Stake: Winning a run on this Stake with a specific Deck will result in unlocking the succeeding Stake on that Deck, the Black Stake. Winning a run with this Stake for the first time will make the player unlock the Painted Deck.

title: Orange Stake
text: Orange Stake: Orange Stake (Stake). Description: Shop can have Perishable Jokers, (Debuffed after 5 Rounds). Unlocked Deck on win: Erratic Deck. Previous: Purple Stake. Next: Gold Stake. The Orange Stake is the seventh Stake, being unlocked after winning Purple Stake on a specific Deck. This Stake makes the Shop have a 30% chance on selling Jokers with the Perishable sticker on them. It also applies the effects of all preceding Stakes.

title: Orange Stake
