The Jokers are also free, meaning that the player can use this Tag even when in debt.

title: Top-up Tag
text: Top-up Tag: Synergies: Black Deck has an extra Joker slot which the player should make use of before the -1 hand downside kills the run, making the Top-up Tag a very enticing option. Anti-synergies: Painted Deck has one fewer Joker slot, making it likely that a Top-up Tag will simply be wasted. Double Tag will be wasted unless there are at least three open Joker slots (ideally four). A second Double Tag is even more likely to be wasted, and three or more are guaranteed to be wasted outside of the extremely improbable scenario of playing exactly Black Deck, with Antimatter already redeemed, and a completely empty Joker tray.

title: Top-up Tag
text: Top-up Tag: Anaglyph Deck's massive supply of Double Tags are very likely to be wasted on a Top-up Tag.

title: Uncommon Tag
text: Uncommon Tag: Uncommon Tag (Tag). Description: Shop has a free Uncommon Joker. Appearing from Ante: Any. The Uncommon Tag makes a free Uncommon Joker available in the next Shop.

title: Uncommon Tag
text: Uncommon Tag: It is a tag that can be acquired either by skipping a Small Blind or a Big Blind. This tag starts to appear at Ante 1. Notes: The Joker is forcefully generated when entering the next Shop, and thus unaffected by Vouchers that lower the probability of Jokers appearing in the Shop, or certain Challenges that prevent Jokers from appearing in the Shop (like Bram Poker). Multiple Uncommon Tags or Rare Tag will take effect in order, until there are no more open slots available in the current shop. Rerolling the shop will let any remaining Uncommon/ Rare Tags take effect.

title: Uncommon Tag
text: Uncommon Tag: If the player has edition Tags (Foil Tag, Holographic Tag, Polychrome Tag, Negative Tag) at the same time, the edition Tag will take effect after the Uncommon Tag, and the edition will be applied to the generated Uncommon Joker if it was generated without edition. The Joker generated by Uncommon Tag can have Edition and in-run Stickers (on Black Stake or higher). The Jokerless challenge bans Uncommon Tag.

title: Voucher Tag
text: Voucher Tag: Voucher Tag (Tag). Description: Adds one Voucher to the next shop. Appearing from Ante: Any. The Voucher Tag makes The Shop have an extra Voucher in stock. The Shop normally only has a single Voucher available. With this tag, another Voucher will appear in the next shop available for purchase.

title: Voucher Tag
text: Voucher Tag: It is a Tag that can be acquired either by skipping a Small Blind or a Big Blind. This tag starts to appear at Ante 1. Notes: The extra Voucher does not remain through the entire ante and is only available for one shop. Multiple Voucher Tags take effect at the same time. For example, if the player has 3 Voucher Tags, there will be 3 extra Vouchers in the shop. Duplicates of the same Voucher are not allowed, so using a Voucher Tag creates a higher probability to find a specific Voucher than finding the Voucher in 2 Antes. If the shop runs out of unique Vouchers to spawn, only Blank will spawn as fallback.

title: Voucher Tag
text: Voucher Tag: If the shop runs out of unique Vouchers to spawn, only Blank will spawn as fallback. If a player manages to buy a base Voucher while there are still Voucher Tags left to redeem, those Voucher tags may generate the upgraded version of that Voucher. Slowing down the game's speed can make it easier to hunt for an specific upgraded Voucher by giving time to buy the corresponding base Voucher.

title: Poker Hands
text: Poker Hands: Poker hands are sets of one to five cards that can be played in Balatro to obtain Chips and Mult for scoring. Each hand also has a level that affects its potency. In general, the more difficult it is to play a certain poker hand, the higher its base score will be. For example, a Pair will score for much less than a Four of a Kind.

title: Poker Hands
text: Poker Hands: At the beginning of a run, all hands start at Level 1, and are generally upgraded through Planet cards. Hands can also be upgraded with the Orbital Tag, the Black Hole Spectral card, Burnt Joker, and Space Joker. The level can also be permanently decreased by The Arm. There is no limit to how many times a poker hand can be leveled up. Furthermore, the poker hand levels are reset back to Level 1 each time when starting a new run.

title: Poker Hands
text: Poker Hands: Higher-tier hands take precedence over lower-tier hands regardless of their level or scoring. For example, if the hand is 9 9 9 9 2, and all of them are diamonds, the hand will always be a Four of a Kind and never a Flush. By selecting the desired cards before playing them, it is possible to check which poker hand it will count as on the left-hand side, over the scoreboard. An exception to this is when playing against a Boss Blind that turns cards in hand face down which, when selected, will make the poker hand name appear as "???" until it is played.

title: Poker Hands
text: Poker Hands: Generally, only the cards relevant to the hand are scored. All others are not scored. For example, if an Ace is played as a High Card with 4 other cards, only the High Card base amount and the Ace's values are used for the hand's score. The other cards (up to 4) are just discarded and have no effect. However, sometimes it can be beneficial to play extra cards as an extra discard while still having the main hand score. This would not work with any hand that requires five cards to be played. The main exceptions to this rule are with Splash, which explicitly allows all played cards to be scored, with Four Fingers, which can be used to score a Straight that contains two cards of matching rank (A A K Q J); and with Stone cards to gain an extra +50 Chips.

title: Poker Hands
text: Poker Hands: Secret Poker Hands: There are three "secret" poker hands that are only possible through adding more playing cards to the deck, or changing existing cards with Consumables or Jokers. These poker hands will not appear in the Run Info screen until they have been played at least once, after which they will show up on the info menu, and their respective Planet cards will be obtainable only during the current run. These poker hands will also be upgraded by Black Hole, even before they are unlocked.

title: Poker Hands
text: Poker Hands: Additional Notes: The exact judgment criteria of a Straight Flush is "any hand which is both a Straight and a Flush". With Four Fingers, it's possible to make a Straight Flush with such cards as 9♠️ 8♠️ 7♥️ 6♠️ 3♠️. Additionally, a Royal Flush is "a Straight Flush with all cards of rank 10 or higher". Similarly, the exact judgment criteria of a Flush House is "any hand which is both a Full House and a Flush". With Four Fingers, it's possible to make a Flush House with such cards as 8♠️ 8♠️ 8♥️ 6♠️ 6♠️.

title: Poker Hands
text: Poker Hands: In much the same way, the exact judgement criteria of Flush Five is "any hand which is both Five of a Kind and a Flush". With Four Fingers, it's possible to make a Flush Five with 5 cards of the same rank, of which only 4 are of the same suit. Two Pair and Full House require that the cards are of different ranks. Thus, Four of a Kind, Five of a Kind, and Flush Five are not considered as containing Two Pair, and Five of a Kind and Flush Five do not contain a Full House.

title: Poker Hands
text: Poker Hands: A poker hand's type is unaffected by the card order. For example, a Straight will still count as one, even if the cards are played as 10, Ace, Queen, King, Jack. This makes it useful with Jokers like Hanging Chad, so certain cards in the scoring order can maximize their potential. In older versions, it was possible for poker hands to be decreased to Level 0, by playing a hand of Level 1 during The Arm. This was changed to a minimum of level 1 in 1.0.0k. Unlike most poker hands that level up through the use of a Planet card, the Royal Flush instead levels up alongside the Straight Flush.

title: Poker Hands
text: Poker Hands: Trivia: X(number) of a kind are sometimes referred as Xoak (for example, 3oak/4oak) for short in the community. In poker terminology, the two types of straight that Ace can form are called Broadway Straight (A K Q J 10) and Wheel Straight (A 2 3 4 5). These names are sometimes used in the community. Each secret poker hand is impossible to encounter when using a standard 52-card deck with 13 cards in each suit. Flush Five used to not exist and was considered as Five of a Kind. The Flush Five (with the corresponding planet card Eris) was later introduced in January 2024.

title: Poker Hands
text: Poker Hands: The "lvl.X" label on the left panel and the background color of the level labels in the "Run Info" feature different colors for each level. For level 1, the color is white. For level 2, the color is blue. For level 3, the color is green. For level 4, the color is yellow. For level 5, the color is orange. For level 6, the color is red. Although only encountered if using third-party tools (or older versions of Balatro), the same color is also used for level 0 hands. For level 7 and onwards, the color is purple.

title: Booster Packs
text: Booster Packs: Two new Booster Packs are always offered in each Shop, often but not always of two different types. Booster Packs do not refresh when rerolling the Shop. They come in five categories: Arcana Packs, containing Tarot cards for immediate use. Celestial Packs, containing Planet cards for immediate use. Standard Packs, containing Playing cards (often with Enhancements, Seals and/or Editions) that are added into your deck. Buffoon Packs, containing Joker cards to add to your run. Spectral Packs, containing Spectral cards for immediate use.

title: Booster Packs
text: Booster Packs: Buffoon Packs, containing Joker cards to add to your run. Spectral Packs, containing Spectral cards for immediate use. Each category of Booster Pack comes in three sizes - Normal, Jumbo and Mega - with each providing more total options than the previous one. The pack will always contain the full amount of cards stated when opened despite the "up to" phrasing, but can in some cases contain duplicate cards. The amount of cards the player can choose depends on the pack size, choosing up to 2 cards from Mega sized packs and up to 1 card from Normal and Jumbo sized packs. Within each size, there is a variety of artwork which can be shown on the Booster Pack; this does not affect the behavior of the Booster Pack.

title: Booster Packs
text: Booster Packs: Purchasing a Booster Pack opens it immediately, taking the player out of the shop, and revealing a set amount of card options for the player to choose from. For Tarot and Spectral Packs, a hand of Playing cards equal to the player's current hand size is dealt for the player to apply effects on while in the pack. The player is able to use any consumables they currently have in their consumable slots while in the pack.

title: Booster Packs
text: Booster Packs: The player is not required to select an option, and can choose to skip at any point if none of the (remaining) cards offered are appealing. Skipping or selecting the final choice from the pack will immediately close the pack and put the player back in the shop. Skipping any booster pack will scale Red Card when held, including skipping a Mega sized pack after having already chosen one of the offered cards.

title: Booster Packs
text: Booster Packs: Booster Pack rates: The Booster Packs offered to the player are determined using different probabilities based on their Type and Size. Each kind of Booster Pack has a weight assigned to it, which determines how likely it is to be drawn; for instance, a Jumbo Arcana Pack has four times the likelihood to be offered than a Mega Arcana Pack, but is half as likely to be offered as a Normal Arcana Pack. It should be noted that (unless playing Jokerless) the first pack in each run is always a Normal Buffoon Pack.

title: Booster Packs
text: Booster Packs: It should be noted that (unless playing Jokerless) the first pack in each run is always a Normal Buffoon Pack. Usage notes: Booster packs follow a set order of consumables specific to each seed. This means if a shop has two of the exact same booster packs, opening both packs in any order will yield the same result.

title: Booster Packs
text: Booster Packs: It is possible to softlock the game during a Arcana/Spectral Pack opening if you have 0 cards left to apply effects to. You can remove cards from the drawn hand using e.g. Immolate or The Hanged Man. Once there are 0 cards left in your hand, the game greys out the skip button and will not allow you to use any consumables that apply effects. Other consumables that do not apply effects to cards like Temperance or The Hermit will still work. The Fragile challenge bans Standard Packs. The Jokerless challenge bans Buffoon Packs. Trivia: Opening an Arcana, Standard, Buffoon, or Spectral Pack triggers the Arcana Theme, while opening a Celestial Pack triggers the Celestial Theme.

title: Booster Packs
text: Booster Packs: The "MEGA" text on Mega Booster Packs mimicks the style of the Metallica logo. In the cover of all of the booster packs, except for all of the Standard Packs and 2 normal Spectral Packs, there is a Joker or a consumable card that is represented. In the order of the Collection, the represented cards are: For the Arcana Packs: The Fool, Temperance, The Hierophant, The World, Death (Jumbo), The Emperor (Jumbo), The Tower (Mega), and The Hermit (Mega). For the Celestial Packs: Mercury, Jupiter, Earth, Uranus, Mars (Jumbo), Pluto (Jumbo), Saturn (Mega), and Venus (Mega). For the Buffoon Packs: Hack, Juggler, Banner (Jumbo), and Brainstorm (Mega). For the Spectral Packs: Incantation (Jumbo) and Ectoplasm (Mega).

title: Booster Packs
text: Booster Packs: For the Buffoon Packs: Hack, Juggler, Banner (Jumbo), and Brainstorm (Mega). For the Spectral Packs: Incantation (Jumbo) and Ectoplasm (Mega). Before Booster Packs were introduced (at 0.8.8), the player obtained cards by purchasing them directly from the store or, with Telescope and Crystal Ball respectively, by entering "Tarot Reading" and "Planetarium", in which the player could select one from two Planet and Tarot cards. Purchasing Observatory or Omen Globe increases the number of available cards to 4. This mechanism later became Booster Packs. At the start of every Shop, Booster Packs have a spawning animation with a dark blue color that matches the color of their label when you hover over them. Their label is shortened to simply say "Booster".

title: Booster Packs
text: Booster Packs: Their label is shortened to simply say "Booster". A Mega Celestial Pack with Venus appears on an Ante Up! shirt due to an official merchandise collaboration with Fangamer. This is the only time a booster pack appears on or as a part of any physical merchandise.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: Playing cards are a set of cards that the player uses to play a certain hand to achieve a certain score, with the help of Jokers and card modifiers. Most decks start with the standard 52-card deck, but the contents of the deck can be modified through the addition, destruction, or modification of playing cards. In most rounds, the default hand size (the number of playing cards per hand) is 8, though this may change under certain conditions.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: The full contents of a deck (all of the currently available playing cards) can be viewed by clicking or tapping on the deck near the bottom right corner of the screen. There, they can see a left panel listing the deck's name and effect as well as the numbers of cards categorized into ranks and suits. To the right, all of the deck's contents can be seen. When a playing card is used (and not discarded or remaining in the player's hand), there are mainly two states for playing cards:

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: Being played: a playing card that is used, but is not included in the overall score (except if Splash is used.) They are the extraneous cards that cannot be picked up through specific poker hands. Those cards are indicated from the lack of a "card pick-up" animation before scoring. Being scored: a playing card that is used and is counted through the overall score, due to it being picked up by a specific Poker Hand. These cards are indicated by a small animation that elevates these cards before they get scored. Items that modify decks: The following is a list of items (including decks) that modify playing cards or add or remove the contents of a standard 52-card deck.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: Jokers: The following Jokers can permanently manipulate the contents of a deck. Most of them only modify a small part of a deck for each time they are used. Marble Joker: adds a Stone card to the deck each time a blind is selected. DNA: adds a copy of a played card into the deck, as long as the first hand has a single card. Sixth Sense: if first hand is a single played card with a rank of 6, it will be destroyed and have a Spectral card created. Hiker: increases number of chips by +5 Chips for every played card. Vampire: if an Enhanced card is played and scored, it will remove the enhancement and gain X0.1 Mult.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: Vampire: if an Enhanced card is played and scored, it will remove the enhancement and gain X0.1 Mult. Midas Mask: every face card becomes a Gold card when scored. Trading Card: as long as the first discard contains a single playing card, that playing card will be destroyed and the player will gain $3. Certificate: at the start of a round, a playing card with a random rank, suit, and seal will be added to a deck. The effects of some jokers, such as the Blue Joker, Hologram, Erosion, Glass Joker, and the Stone Joker, depend on deck manipulation or the contents of a deck. However, these effects by themselves do not add, modify, or remove playing cards by themselves.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: Decks: There are a few decks that do not start as the standard 52-card deck. These decks include: The Abandoned Deck: contains 40 playing cards at the start of the game, since it excludes the 12 face cards. The Checkered Deck: contains 26 playing cards with the Spades suit and another 26 playing cards with the Hearts suit at the start of the game. It also does not start with any playing card with a Diamond or Club suit. The Erratic Deck: the suits and ranks of this deck are randomized.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: The Erratic Deck: the suits and ranks of this deck are randomized. Challenge decks: These challenge decks start with a deck that is not the standard 52-card deck. Furthermore, some of them may also have Jokers or other items that can manipulate the deck: 15 Minute City has a single copy for each face card, but has Aces, 2s, and 3s excluded. Mad World has only 32 cards, consisting only of cards between 2 and 9 (or, in other words, the player starts with no Aces, no face cards, and no cards with a rank of 10).

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: Medusa has the face cards replaced with Stone cards. Furthermore, since this challenge has an Eternal Marble Joker, that Joker would add one Stone card every time a blind is selected, thus it continually manipulates the contents of the deck. Double or Nothing adds a Red Seal on all playing cards, but permanently debuffs a playing card once it is scored. Fragile turns all playing cards into Glass cards while banning Jokers and other items that can help with adding non-glass cards or removing/modifying the Glass enhancement. These challenge decks start with a standard 52-card deck, but have Jokers or other items that can manipulate the deck:

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: These challenge decks start with a standard 52-card deck, but have Jokers or other items that can manipulate the deck: Bram Poker has an Eternal Vampire (which gains X0.1 Mult at the cost of the removal of a scored playing card's enhancement). It also has the Magic Trick and Illusion, which are two vouchers that can help with deck manipulation, since they allow purchasing playing cards from the Shop. Monolith has an Eternal, Negative Marble Joker, which adds one Stone card every time a blind is selected. Vouchers: Magic Trick can make playing cards purchasable from the Shop. Illusion can make playing cards with an enhancement, edition (except Negative), or seal purchasable from the Shop.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: Illusion can make playing cards with an enhancement, edition (except Negative), or seal purchasable from the Shop. Hone and Glow Up can make modified playing cards (with an enhancement, an edition, and/or a seal) show up more often, as long as Illusion is redeemed beforehand. Overstock or Overstock Plus may have a chance to restock the Shop with a playing card, as long as there are empty slots before having either of these vouchers redeemed and at least the Magic Trick is redeemed beforehand. Tarot cards: The Magician: allows up to 2 selected playing cards to be converted into Lucky cards. The Empress: allows up to 2 selected playing cards to be converted into Mult cards.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: The Empress: allows up to 2 selected playing cards to be converted into Mult cards. The Hierophant: allows up to 2 selected playing cards to be converted into Bonus cards. The Lovers: allows a selected playing card to be converted into a Wild card. The Chariot: allows a selected playing card to be converted into a Steel card. Justice: allows a selected playing card to be converted into a Glass card. Strength: allows up to 2 selected playing cards to have their ranks incremented by 1. The Hanged Man: destroys up to 2 selected playing cards.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: The Hanged Man: destroys up to 2 selected playing cards. Death: allows for the selected playing card to the left to have the same rank and suit of the selected playing card to its right. The Devil: allows a selected playing card to be converted into a Gold card. The Tower: allows a selected playing card to be converted into a Stone card. The Star: allows up to 3 selected playing cards to have their suits converted into Diamonds. The Moon: allows up to 3 selected playing cards to have their suits converted into Clubs. The Sun: allows up to 3 selected playing cards to have their suits converted into Hearts.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: The Sun: allows up to 3 selected playing cards to have their suits converted into Hearts. The World: allows up to 3 selected playing cards to have their suits converted into Spades. Spectral cards: Familiar: destroys a random playing card in hand and adds 3 enhanced face cards instead. Grim: destroys a random playing card in hand and adds 2 enhanced Ace cards instead. Incantation: destroys a random playing card in hand and adds 4 enhanced numbered cards instead. Talisman: adds a Gold Seal to the selected playing card in hand. Aura: adds Foil, Holographic, or Polychrome to the selected playing card in hand. Sigil: converts all playing cards in hand to a random suit.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: Sigil: converts all playing cards in hand to a random suit. Ouija: converts all playing cards in hand to a random rank and reduces hand size by 1. Immolate: destroys 5 playing cards in hand to gain $20. Deja Vu: adds a Red Seal to the selected playing card in hand. Trance: adds a Blue Seal to the selected playing card in hand. Medium: adds a Purple Seal to the selected playing card in hand. Cryptid: creates 2 copies of the selected playing card in hand.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: Cryptid: creates 2 copies of the selected playing card in hand. Blinds: It should be noted that there are no blinds that add or destroy playing cards nor any blinds that can permanently affect playing cards, though some blinds can temporarily apply negative effects to playing cards during their particular rounds. This includes: The House: first hand of playing cards are drawn as face-down. The Wheel: 1 in 7 of playing cards are drawn as face-down. The Club: All playing cards with the Club suit are debuffed. The Fish: All playing cards are drawn as face-down after each hand played. The Goad: All playing cards with the Spade suit are debuffed.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: The Goad: All playing cards with the Spade suit are debuffed. The Window: All playing cards with the Diamond suit are debuffed. The Plant: All face cards are debuffed. The Pillar: Playing cards that were played during an Ante are debuffed. The Head: All playing cards with the Heart suit are debuffed. The Mark: All face cards are drawn as face-down. Verdant Leaf: All playing cards are debuffed until one Joker is sold. Cerulean Bell: Makes a random playing card force-selected. Other: All Enhancements and all Seals can be applied only to playing cards. Furthermore, all Editions, except Negative, can be applied to playing cards.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: The contents of a deck can be modified with the addition of playing cards from Standard Packs or from skipping a blind to obtain a Standard Tag (which opens a free Mega Standard Pack). Settings: When a new player starts Balatro, there are two default settings for playing cards: All of the face cards are set to the default face cards; High contrast mode is disabled.

title: Playing Cards
text: Playing Cards: All of the face cards are set to the default face cards; High contrast mode is disabled. Once the player goes to the Options, they can click "Customize Deck" and choose different face cards of characters from other games and IPs, particularly among the ones introduced in the Friends of Jimbo updates. They can also tick the box that makes them have a higher contrast, though they can also modify that option through Settings > Game. It should be noted that these settings apply across all profiles. Further reading: Suits Ranks

title: Shop
text: Shop: The Shop is the location where Jokers, Consumables, and Vouchers can be acquired by spending money. The Shop is only accessible after defeating a Small Blind, Big Blind, or Boss Blind. By default, the shop sells: 2 random cards (usually Jokers, but occasionally Tarot, Planet, and Playing cards if you have purchased the Magic Trick voucher, or Spectral cards if you are playing with Ghost Deck.) 2 random Booster Packs (except for the first visit to any Shop in a run, where one normal Buffoon Pack is guaranteed) 1 Voucher

title: Shop
text: Shop: 1 Voucher Weights: Weights determine how likely a card is to appear in the given set. The higher the weight, the more it appears. The random cards sold are drawn with the default weights: Joker: 20 Tarot: 4 Planet: 4 This can be rewritten to the approximate chances of each card appearing as following (note that these are rounded): Joker: 71.4% Tarot: 14.3% Planet: 14.3% In addition, when a Joker is generated, the different rarities have specific weights as well. The default values for these are: Common: 70% Uncommon: 25% Rare: 5%

title: Shop
text: Shop: Common: 70% Uncommon: 25% Rare: 5% Vouchers: With the Magic Trick Voucher, playing cards are given a weight of 4; the Illusion Voucher makes playing cards enhanced 40% of the time, editioned 20% of the time, and is unaffected by Hone/ Glow Up. The Tarot Merchant Voucher raises the Tarot card weight to 9.6 while the Tarot Tycoon Voucher raises the weight to 32. The Planet Merchant and Planet Tycoon Vouchers work in the same way for their respective Planets. With the Ghost Deck, Spectral cards can appear with a weight of 2.

title: Shop
text: Shop: The number of available random cards can be increased by the Overstock and Overstock Plus Vouchers, which increases the number of sold cards to 3 and 4 respectively.

title: Shop
text: Shop: Reroll: The player may pay money to reroll the shop an unlimited number of times, removing any of the remaining random cards and replacing them with 2 new random cards. Note that because the rerolls are random, cards seen before rerolling can also appear again. The reroll cost starts at $5 and increases by $1 each reroll, resetting to $5 upon entering a new shop. Reroll Surplus and Reroll Glut decrease the initial price to $3 and $1, respectively. Chaos the Clown will make the first reroll free. The D6 Tag starts the rerolls on the next shop to $0.

title: Shop
text: Shop: However, rerolling the shop does not restock Booster Packs or the Voucher. Booster packs only restock upon entering a new shop, and the Voucher restocks after defeating the boss blind. Flash Card has a special synergy with rerolling, as it scales when rerolling the shop. In short: All items have a buy cost (purchase price) and a sell value, which are recalculated every time the player interacts with the item. These follow consistent formulas for calculating them, with some exceptions applied due to other in-game items. Here follows a simplified formula for calculating an item's buy cost and sell value. For more details, see the Calculating buy cost and Calculating sell value sections. buy_cost = (base_cost + edition_cost) * discount_percent

title: Shop
text: Shop: buy_cost = (base_cost + edition_cost) * discount_percent sell_value = floor(buy_cost / 2) Base cost: All items have a base cost, even Legendary Jokers (which can't be found in the shop). Playing cards can only be found in the Shop after purchasing the Magic Trick Voucher, and Spectral cards can only be found when playing with the Ghost Deck. Edition cost: Jokers can have Editions, which raises their price in the shop and their sell value. Consumables can have a Negative Edition when generated by Perkeo, but they can never be found in the shop with an Edition. When Illusion is bought, Playing cards can also have Editions in the shop, increasing their price.

title: Shop
text: Shop: Discounts: After purchasing the Clearance Sale and Liquidation Vouchers, a 25% or 50% discount is applied to the buy cost of all items in the shop. This also indirectly affects the sell value of all items. Clearance Sale (25% off) effectively sets discount_percent = 0.75 Liquidation (50% off) effectively sets discount_percent = 0.5 Special cases: During the Inflation Challenge Deck, every item's price increases by $1 on every purchase. This increase in cost is applied at the same time as the Edition cost, before any discounts from Vouchers. The Astronomer Joker will set the cost of Planets and Celestial Packs to $0.

title: Shop
text: Shop: The Astronomer Joker will set the cost of Planets and Celestial Packs to $0. The Coupon Tag sets the buy cost of all items in the next Shop to $0, except for Vouchers which retain their normal pricing. The Rental sticker sets the buy cost of Jokers with this sticker to $1. If the item is a Booster Pack, and the player is playing the tutorial and is in the first shop, the buy cost increases by $3. This only applies to the first Shop. Subsequent Shops will have the intended price for Booster Packs.

title: Shop
text: Shop: This only applies to the first Shop. Subsequent Shops will have the intended price for Booster Packs. The jokers Egg and Gift Card can add extra sell value to cards. This extra value is only applied to the sell value, and after all other steps. The added value is not influenced by the discount vouchers. Calculating buy cost: Add up the item's: Base cost. Edition cost (if it has an Edition). Inflation costs (if playing the Inflation challenge). Multiply this total by the discount_percent from the discount vouchers. Round half down (for example, 8.5 is rounded to 8). If the buy price after rounding is $0 or lower, set it to $1.

title: Shop
text: Shop: If the buy price after rounding is $0 or lower, set it to $1. Apply any remaining special cases (such as Astronomer, the Rental Sticker, or the Coupon Tag). Calculating sell value: Recalculate the item's total buy cost (applying any vouchers bought in-between, any special case that changes the buy cost, etc.). Divide the total buy cost by 2. Floor the result of the division (for example, 3.75 is rounded to 3). If the sell value after flooring is $0 or lower, set it to $1. Add any additional sell value gained from Egg or Gift Card. Trivia: The Shop's logo appears on an Ante Up! shirt due to an official merch collaboration with Fangamer.

title: Shop
text: Shop: Trivia: The Shop's logo appears on an Ante Up! shirt due to an official merch collaboration with Fangamer. In other media: The Shop's logo appears in the Ante Chamber stage in Vampire Survivors.

title: Ante
text: Ante: Blinds are the main obstacle that the player must overcome during a run in Balatro. For each selected Blind, the player has to meet or surpass the required score to beat it, otherwise they will lose the run. Defeating the Blind may also award some money. An Ante is made up of three Blinds in succession: a Small Blind, a Big Blind, and a random Boss Blind. Special Boss Blinds called Showdown Blinds only appear on the final level of a run, at Ante 8. The player can choose to take on a Small or Big Blind, or to skip one or both and claim one or more Tags instead; Boss Blinds must always be played.

title: Ante
text: Ante: The score required to defeat a Blind is determined by the Ante level and Stake. If playing on the Plasma Deck, the score requirement is doubled. Generally, a run starts at Ante 1 and goes up an Ante level for every Boss Blind defeated. By completing Ante 8 and finishing the Showdown Blind, the run is considered "won". However, the player may continue afterwards in Endless Mode if they wish.

title: Ante
text: Ante: Small Blind and Big Blind: Small and Big Blinds have no other effects and can be skipped to receive a Tag. The score required is 1x base chips for the Small Blind and 1.5x base chips for the Big Blind. On Red Stake or higher, Small Blinds will give no reward money. Boss Blind: Boss Blinds are the last blind of an Ante, most of which require a score of 2x base chips. Boss Blinds have certain special effects that add difficulty to the round, for example: Inflicting negative effects on certain cards, including debuffed, face-down, and force-selected.

title: Ante
text: Ante: Inflicting negative effects on certain cards, including debuffed, face-down, and force-selected. Restricting the size or type of poker hand that can be played. Hands that don't meet the restriction can still be played but will not be scored or activate other effects. Changing other values in the game, like hand/discard counts, hand size, and required score. Boss Blinds are randomly selected. Each Boss Blind has a minimum ante in which it can appear, with Ante 1 (including Antes lesser than 1) having only eight possible bosses. Only the Boss Blinds with the fewest appearances will be selected—this means a Boss Blind will not appear again before all Boss Blinds have appeared once, including being defeated or rerolled.

title: Ante
text: Ante: Boss Blinds cannot be skipped, but there are other ways to avoid them: The vouchers Director's Cut and Retcon enable players to reroll Boss Blinds. Rerolling on Ante 8 (or a multiple of 8) will always roll a Showdown Blind, and other antes will always roll a normal Boss Blind. Luchador and Chicot can disable the effect of Boss Blinds. For blinds with an extremely high score (The Wall and Violet Vessel), the score will return to normal (2x base chips), while The Needle won't have its score increased.

title: Ante
text: Ante: Showdown Blind: Showdown Blinds are a special type of Boss Blind that appear at the end of the game (Ante 8). In endless mode, Showdown Blinds will appear again in Ante 16, 24, and 32. Apart from their timing, they are otherwise identical to regular Boss Blinds (can be rerolled, disabled by Luchador and Chicot, and so on). Antes: An Ante is made up of three rounds, each consisting of a Small Blind, a Big Blind, and a Boss Blind.

title: Ante
text: Ante: A run will always begin at Ante 1. After defeating the Showdown Blind in Ante 8, the run is won, but the player can choose to continue in Endless Mode to set a personal high score. Endless Mode begins from Ante 9 and purports to offer infinite Ante levels to ascend, with additional Showdown Blinds every eight Antes, but Ante score requirements also scale much faster. Under Blinds in the Collection, a list of the base score per Ante is shown up to Ante 16, although the player can reach higher Antes. Ante 0 can be reached by purchasing a Hieroglyph on Ante 1 (or Petroglyph on Ante 1 to reach Ante 0 a second time).

title: Ante
text: Ante: Green Stake and Purple Stake (or higher) will cause chip requirements to be higher. Playing on the Plasma Deck doubles the Ante requirement for all stakes. List of Antes: Before Endless mode (Ante 8 or lower), an Ante's chip requirement is derived from a fixed list. After Endless Mode (Ante 9 or higher), the chip requirement is calculated using the following formula: Chip Requirement=Ante 8 Requirement⋅(1.6+(0.75(Ante−8))1+0.2(Ante−8))Ante−8 The chip requirement is then rounded to two significant digits. A calculator for the score requirements for antes can be found here.

title: Ante
text: Ante: A calculator for the score requirements for antes can be found here. Ante -1: It is possible to reach Ante -1 by utilizing Yellow Deck and a Voucher Tag skip tag. On a seed that has Hieroglyph in Ante 1, skip for the Voucher tag, beat the Big Blind, and then cash out. With slow game speed (recommended 0.5 or 1), quickly buy Hieroglyph before the Voucher tag activates, which will allow Petroglyph to spawn since the game checks for voucher availability after Hieroglyph has been bought. With the bonus econ from Yellow Deck, it is possible to buy both Vouchers, which bring players to Ante -1. A basic demonstration can be found here.

title: Ante
text: Ante: Ante 39: In Ante 39, the score requirement exceeds 21024 (1.8e308), which is the largest number that can be represented in double-precision floating-point format, causing the score to overflow to NaN (not a number). Scoring over 21024 points results in the score showing as naneinf (nan exponent infinity). Since nan is incomparable to any value, scoring even naneinf is not sufficient for beating a score requirement of nan (even with Mr. Bones), meaning that at the current moment, Ante 39 is the highest Ante reachable in Endless mode without the use of glitches to skip antes. A player is considered to have "completed" or "beaten" endless mode if one scores naneinf on Ante 39.

title: Ante
text: Ante: Notes: The scaling in Endless mode is faster than super-exponential, proportional to xx2 (polynomial-exponential), where x denotes the current Ante. The common Endless build of Mime/ Baron with Perkeo/ Cryptid and Red Seal Steel kings can, theoretically, scale at a similar or faster speed (proportional to xx2). However, this would involve the constant addition of (presumably negative) copies of Blueprint or Brainstorm to the joker roster every Ante, a near-impossible feat in a normal game, unless using extremely tedious tarot-based infinite money strategies. (It is also possible to use Mime/Baron with Burglar to get xx3without Perkeo; see Guide: naneinf.) Regardless, in vanilla Balatro, the Ante 39 nan overflow will always end the run, meaning there is never any need to go to such great lengths to scale a build.

title: Ante
text: Ante: Having Mr. Bones is the only way to prevent losing an entire run if the player does not meet the score requirement of a Blind, as long as the player reaches 25% of the required score. Trivia: The names Small Blind, Big Blind, and Ante are based on poker terminology. The symbols and names of most of the Boss Blinds are based on the letters of the Phoenician alphabet. The sole exception is The Flint, which is an original creation by the developer, though it resembles the runic letter jera (ᛃ).

title: Ante
text: Ante: According to LocalThunk, the reason for inventing a new symbol for The Flint was to bring the total number of blinds from 29 to 30 for a neat Collection screen. The symbols and names of the five Showdown Blinds are based on alternate playing card suits: Hearts, Bells (replaces Diamonds in German decks), Acorns (replaces Clubs in German decks), Leaves (replaces Spades in German decks), and Vessels (replaces Hearts in Italian and Spanish decks).

title: Ante
text: Ante: The name "Showdown Blind" for the five Boss Blinds that appear on Ante 8 comes from the game code. As this group is not named in any player-facing text, names "Finisher Blind" or "Final Boss Blind", which have both been referred by LocalThunk, are also commonly used in game community. During public test versions of Balatro, Finisher Boss Blinds appeared on Ante 10, and during demo versions of Balatro, the player can only play 5 Antes plus an Ante 6 containing only a Showdown Blind. The name of every blind contains exactly two words each. The name of every non-showdown Boss Blind starts with the word "The".

title: Ante
text: Ante: The name of every non-showdown Boss Blind starts with the word "The". Balatro developer LocalThunk has given the reasoning behind the design of some Boss Blind effects in the Balatro Discord. The Plant debuffs face cards because plants do not have faces. The Needle requires precision in reference to the phrase "thread the needle". The Wheel has a chance-based effect similarly to The Wheel of Fortune. The Eye bans repeat hand types because it has observed what hands were played. Players can drag the icons of the blinds on the left panel, much like how they can drag jokers, consumables, and playing cards.

title: Ante
text: Ante: When continuing interrupted games, the Blind icon, effects, and score requirements on the game interface may disappear (which is likely a bug). In this case, blind information can be viewed in the run info. It will recover after defeating the current Blind.

title: Card Ranks
text: Card Ranks: Card ranks are the thirteen values that can be found on a playing card in Balatro. These values are Ace, the number cards 2 to 10, and the three face cards: Jacks, Queens and Kings. Each card also has a suit. Aces: In most games with playing cards, an Ace can be treated 'low' or 'high'. If treated low, it usually represents a 1. If treated high, it usually represents a card better than a face card. For example, in Blackjack, an Ace can be valued at 1 or 11, at the player's choice. In Balatro, the Ace can be considered as 'low' or 'high' in a Straight, but it always scores as 'high' to provide 11 Chips.

title: Card Ranks
text: Card Ranks: Jokers: Scholar gives +20 Chips and +4 Mult for every scored Ace. Superposition creates a Tarot card if the played hand contains an Ace and a Straight. Odd Todd gives +31 Chips for every scored Ace. Fibonacci gives +8 Mult for every scored Ace. Consumables: Grim destroys 1 random card in the hand and adds 2 random Enhanced Aces to the hand. Face cards: "Face cards" is a grouping term for Jacks, Queens and Kings. Usually in most games, a King is better than a Queen, a Queen is better than a Jack, and all are better than number cards. It is possible to have number cards and Aces count as face cards if you have Pareidolia.

title: Card Ranks
text: Card Ranks: In Balatro, all face cards provide 10 Chips each when scored. From Update 1.0.1g, it is possible to customize the artwork of face cards with Friends of Jimbo from other games. Jokers: Scary Face gives +30 Chips for every scored face card. Smiley Face gives +5 Mult for every scored face card. Business Card has a 1 in 2 chance to give $2 for every scored face card. Faceless Joker gives $5 for discarding 3 face cards at the same time. Sock and Buskin retriggers all scored face cards. Midas Mask turns all scored face cards into Gold cards. Reserved Parking has a 1 in 2 chance to give $1 for every face card held in hand.

title: Card Ranks
text: Card Ranks: Reserved Parking has a 1 in 2 chance to give $1 for every face card held in hand. Photograph gives X2 Mult for the first scored face card. Canio gains X1 Mult for each destroyed face card. Hit the Road gains X0.5 Mult for every Jack discarded this round. Shoot the Moon gives +13 Mult for every Queen held in hand. Baron gives X1.5 Mult for every King held in hand. Triboulet gives X2 Mult for every scored King and Queen. Pareidolia makes every card count as a face card. Consumables: Familiar destroys 1 random card in the hand and adds 3 random Enhanced face cards to the hand. Jokers: Ride the Bus resets if face cards are scored.

title: Card Ranks
text: Card Ranks: Jokers: Ride the Bus resets if face cards are scored. Boss Blinds: The Plant debuffs all face cards. The Mark draws all face cards face down. Number cards: Number cards usually carry the value of their number, unless modified by tarot cards to add card modifiers or modified by joker effects. They are sometimes called 'pip' cards, as each icon printed on them is a pip. In Balatro, the number cards provide chips equal to their value unless modified, for example, a 7 card provides 7 Chips when scored. Note that cards are not scored when not required for the hand, unless the player has Splash.

title: Card Ranks
text: Card Ranks: Even and Odd cards: "Even cards" are cards with a rank that can be divided by 2 into a whole number. In Balatro, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 are considered even. "Odd cards" are cards with a rank that cannot be divided by 2 into a whole number. In Balatro, Ace, 3, 5, 7, and 9 are considered odd. Jokers: Odd Todd gives +31 Chips for every scored 3, 5, 7, and 9. Even Steven gives +4 Mult for every scored 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. Fibonacci gives +8 Mult for every scored 2, 3, 5, and 8. Hack retriggers all scored 2s, 3s, 4s, and 5s.

title: Card Ranks
text: Card Ranks: Hack retriggers all scored 2s, 3s, 4s, and 5s. Walkie Talkie gives +10 Chips and +4 Mult for every scored 10 and 4. Wee Joker gains +8 Chips for every scored 2. Sixth Sense creates a Spectral card if the first played hand in a round is a single 6, and destroys the 6. 8 Ball has a 1 in 4 chance of creating a Tarot card for every scored 8. Cloud 9 gives $1 for every 9 in the deck. Consumables: Incantation destroys 1 random card in the hand and adds 4 random Enhanced number cards to the hand. Random Rank Jokers: Some Jokers in Balatro act on a random rank each round:

title: Card Ranks
text: Card Ranks: Random Rank Jokers: Some Jokers in Balatro act on a random rank each round: Mail-In Rebate (chooses based on deck composition) The Idol (chooses based on deck composition) Consumables: The following Spectral cards can act on a rank: Ouija (converts all cards in hand to a single, random rank) The following Tarot cards can interact with ranks: Strength (increases rank of up to 2 selected cards by 1) Death (copies the left card into the right card, which copies the rank) Trivia: The basic deck in Balatro is based on the French-suited, 52-card standard deck that is usually the most common deck of cards available in predominantly English-speaking countries.

title: Card Ranks
text: Card Ranks: While Balatro has a plethora of unique Joker cards and is a core part of its identity, traditional decks usually only include a few Joker cards at most and they typically aren't used in most games. When they are utilized, the Joker card can serve as a Wild card that acts as any rank or suit or have unique functions relative to the game. They can also be used as a stand-in card to complete a 52-card deck if a card is missing. Face cards are sometimes called court cards, as the figures represent the highest roles in a royal court.

title: Card Ranks
text: Card Ranks: Face cards are sometimes called court cards, as the figures represent the highest roles in a royal court. The names of Aces and Faces are usually translated in non-English-speaking areas, which includes changing the letter (J/Q/K/A) printed on the card. Unusually though, on French-language decks, the Ace becomes a 1.

title: Card Suits
text: Card Suits: Balatro's core gameplay is based on a standard deck of 52 playing cards. A standard deck consists of 4 suits, with 13 cards of a different rank in each suit. The suits are found in the following order: the Spade suit, the Heart suit, the Club suit, and the Diamond suit, shown from top to bottom in the visual deck display, and left to right in your hand when sorting by suit (while the rank acts as the tiebreaker). This is true even when the cards are drawn face down, allowing you to guess at a card's suit.

title: Card Suits
text: Card Suits: Each suit contains an Ace followed by King, Queen, and Jack, and then 10-2, shown left to right both in the visual deck display and in your hand when sorted by suit. When your hand is sorted by rank, the ranks are ordered from left to right, (A, KQJ, 10-2) while the suits act as the tiebreaker. This is true even when the cards are face down, allowing you to guess at a card's rank. (For example, in rank sort, an Ace of Diamonds will be sorted to the right of an Ace of Spades, but to the left of a King of any suit.)

title: Card Suits
text: Card Suits: Some decks in Balatro (such as the Checkered Deck or the Erratic Deck) use a different distribution of cards, and some consumables and Jokers can manipulate the suits in a deck. Wild cards are considered to be every suit simultaneously, meaning they can benefit from multiple suit-related Jokers (and be penalized by any suit-related Boss Blind). However, for Jokers such as Flower Pot and Seeing Double, each Wild card will only count as one suit at a time. Spade suit: The Spade suit is one of four suits in Balatro. It is one of two black suits, the other being the Club suit. The Spade suit is colored dark blue-black. The World is used to turn cards into Spades.

title: Card Suits

It is one of two red suits, the other being the Diamond suit. The Heart suit is colored bright red. Enabling high contrast in the game's deck customization options darkens the shade of Hearts' color. The Sun is used to turn cards into Hearts. title: Card Suits
text: Card Suits: The Lovers (converts 1 selected card into a Wild card) The Star (converts 3 selected cards to the Diamond suit) The Moon (converts 3 selected cards to the Club suit) The Sun (converts 3 selected cards to the Heart suit) The World (converts 3 selected cards to the Spade suit) Death (copies the left card into the right card, which copies the suit)

title: Challenges
text: Challenges: Challenge Decks are unique decks that contain some condition making them unique from, and often more challenging than, the normal decks. This could manifest in having an altered starting deck, possessing certain Eternal Jokers, restrictions on hands or discards, restrictions on allowed cards, and more. They can only be played on the White Stake.

title: Challenges
text: Challenges: When playing Challenge Decks, achievements and unlocks cannot be obtained, as some would be trivialized by the conditions given by the deck. Statistics such as the number of times a consumable has been used and high scores like Best Hand/Highest Ante still get updated. It is not possible to start a seeded run on Challenge Decks, but the seed generated by each challenge run can still be used on normal decks.

title: Challenges
text: Challenges: Decks: There are twenty different Challenge Decks currently in Balatro, with the first five unlocked after winning on five different decks. Each subsequent deck is unlocked after winning a run with a new Challenge Deck. To unlock all the Challenge Decks, the player needs to win with fifteen of them. Trivia: The card back of the Challenge Deck is a maze. The maze can be started either from the top opening or the bottom one. LocalThunk, the developer of Balatro, has stated that some manner of challenge creator is on his list of things to add, with no timetable.

title: Challenges
text: Challenges: If a Challenge begins with a Voucher, and a saved run is continued from the main menu before the first Blind is selected, any effect the Voucher would have will not be applied.

title: Interest
text: Interest: At the end of each round, $1 of interest is earned for every $5 the player has at the end of the round, with a cap of $5 each round (which means that any money over $25 won't generate interest). This incentivizes the player to save money up to a point. Interactions: To the Moon gives an extra $1 interest for every $5 held at the end of a round. Seed Money and its upgrade Money Tree increase the cap on earned interest to $10 and $20 respectively (which means that any money over $50 and $100 won't generate interest respectively). Large amounts of money can be gained per round by combining these vouchers with To the Moon.

title: Interest
text: Interest: Any economy Joker and Gold cards can help in getting more money and thus win more interest up to the cap. Note that economy Jokers that trigger once the round is already over (like Golden Joker and Rocket) don't count towards interest that round, whereas Gold cards and Jokers that trigger before (like Reserved Parking) do count towards interest in the same round. Green Deck, The Omelette, and Mad World have the property of not being able to gain Interest, making Seed Money, Money Tree, and To The Moon useless. Those cards are banned in The Omelette. Yellow Deck starts with an extra $10, thus earning $2 of interest in the first round.
